name: Cinnamon apple oat porridge with ground flax and sunflower seed butter
inspiredBy: Canadian morning porridge, made with fortified soy drink instead of milk and finished with ground flax, a Canadian crop
about: Creamy rolled oats simmered in fortified soy drink with diced apple and cinnamon, stirred with ground flax and a spoonful of toasted wheat germ, then swirled with sunflower seed butter for a nutty richness, with no nuts in the recipe. The soy drink brings **calcium and vitamin D**, the flax adds plant omega-3, and the wheat germ and seed butter add choline and vitamin E.
steps: Wash the apple, then dice it with the skin on. Shake the carton of soy drink well, because the calcium settles at the bottom.
Put the oats, soy drink, apple, flax, wheat germ, cinnamon and salt in a small pot over medium heat. Stir often until it bubbles gently.
Turn the heat down and cook, stirring, until the oats are thick and creamy and the apple is soft, about 6 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl and swirl the sunflower seed butter over the top while the porridge is hot, so it melts into ribbons.
tip: Cook a double pot and keep the second portion in a shallow container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat with a splash of soy drink until steaming. A fortified oat drink with added calcium works too, with a little less protein; check it for "may contain" nuts too.

name: Tofu scramble a la mexicana with warm corn tortillas
inspiredBy: Mexican huevos a la mexicana, the everyday scramble of tomato, onion and chile, made with tofu
about: Crumbled tofu fried with tomato, onion and spinach, turned golden with turmeric and cumin, and served with black beans, warm corn tortillas and avocado. It is the classic Mexican breakfast flavour with no eggs, and the calcium-set tofu brings **protein, calcium and choline**.
steps: Wash the spinach and cilantro. Pat the tofu dry and crumble it with your fingers into pea-sized pieces.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, turmeric and chili flakes and cook until the juices thicken, about 3 minutes.
Add the tofu, beans and salt and cook, stirring, until hot and lightly golden at the edges, about 5 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or directly over a low flame. Finish the scramble with the lime juice and cilantro and serve with the avocado.
tip: Add more chili flakes if you like heat. A little more tomato makes it saucier. Buy tofu in blocks you will use within 2 days, keep the rest covered in the fridge, or freeze it.
ingredients: buy the calcium-set kind (calcium sulfate on the label) showing about 45% of the daily value for calcium in an 85 g serving; check the "may contain" line for nuts and sesame; opened tofu goes covered in the fridge and is used within 2 days
plain corn tortillas; check the label for "may contain" and for added milk or egg

name: Blueberry overnight oats with soy yogurt, flax and pumpkin seeds
inspiredBy: Canadian overnight oats, with soy yogurt and soy drink in place of dairy
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in soy yogurt and fortified soy drink with ground flax, wheat germ and a spoonful of sunflower seed butter, then topped with blueberries and toasted pumpkin seeds for crunch. It is made the night before and tastes like a bowl of blueberry yogurt. It brings **calcium, fibre and plant omega-3**, with vitamin C from the berries and vitamin E from the seeds.
steps: The night before, stir the oats, soy yogurt, soy drink, flax, wheat germ, sunflower seed butter, maple syrup and cinnamon together in a jar or bowl. Shake the soy drink carton first.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least 4 hours, until the oats are soft and the mixture is thick. It keeps up to 2 days.
In the morning, toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until they puff and pop, about 3 minutes.
Rinse the blueberries. Stir the oats, loosen with a splash of soy drink if it is too thick, and top with the blueberries and warm seeds.
tip: Mix two jars at once. Frozen blueberries thaw into a natural sauce overnight. For children under 4, chop or grind the pumpkin seeds first, since whole seeds are a choking risk.

name: Salmon salad sandwich on rye with dill and cucumber
inspiredBy: Canadian deli salmon salad sandwiches, with a soy yogurt and Dijon dressing instead of mayo
about: Flaked canned salmon, soft bones and all, mixed with crunchy cucumber, onion, dill, creamy mashed avocado and a lemony soy yogurt and Dijon dressing, piled on rye with spinach and carrot sticks. There is no mayo and no egg. The salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D, B12 and calcium**.
steps: Wash the cucumber, spinach, carrot and dill before cutting.
Drain the salmon and flake it into a bowl, mashing in the soft bones, which are edible and carry the calcium.

Stir in the soy yogurt, mashed avocado, Dijon, lemon juice, cucumber, onion, dill and pepper. Taste and add a little more lemon if it needs brightness. The salmon is already salty, so there is no added salt.

Toast the rye in the oven or a dry pan if you like. Pile the salmon salad on half the slices, top with the spinach and cover with the rest. If the filling seems dry, loosen it with a teaspoon of soy drink or an extra squeeze of lemon.
Serve with the carrot sticks. Move any leftover salmon from the opened tin to a covered glass container in the fridge and use it within 2 days, as you would the leftover filling.
tip: To pack it, keep the filling cold with an ice pack and eat it within 2 hours of leaving the fridge. Pack the bread separately so the rye stays crisp.
ingredients: plain tin, not a flavoured one; check the label for "may contain"; move any leftover to a covered glass container
soy only, with no almond or coconut blend; check the label for "may contain" nuts
plain Dijon; check the label for "may contain"
sliced; buy it packaged with a full ingredient list, not from a bakery counter, since breads often carry milk, egg or sesame, and check for "may contain"

name: Ginger-soy tofu and edamame rice bowl with cucumber and carrot
inspiredBy: Japanese donburi-style rice bowls, with a ginger-soy glaze and no sesame
about: Seared tofu and edamame over brown rice with crunchy cucumber and carrot, glazed with a quick ginger, garlic, soy and lime sauce. There is no sesame oil or seeds in the recipe, so just check the soy sauce label. The tofu and edamame bring **protein, calcium, iron and choline**.
steps: Cook the rice ahead if you can. Cook the brown rice in plenty of simmering water until tender, about 30 minutes, drain it well, then spread it in a shallow container and cool it within 1 hour. Keep it up to 3 days.
Wash the cucumber and carrot and cut them into matchsticks. Whisk the soy sauce, lime juice, maple syrup and ginger with a spoonful of water.
Pat the tofu dry and cut it into cubes. Sear in the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat until golden on two sides, about 6 minutes, adding the garlic for the last 30 seconds.
Add the edamame and the sauce to the pan and cook, turning, until the sauce turns glossy and clings, about 2 minutes.
Reheat the rice until steaming hot (74 °C), spoon it into a bowl and top with the tofu and edamame and the cool cucumber and carrot.
tip: Cook the rice on Wednesday night, and this lunch takes 15 minutes. Keep any opened tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
ingredients: buy the calcium-set kind (calcium sulfate on the label) showing about 45% of the daily value for calcium in an 85 g serving; check the "may contain" line for nuts and sesame; opened tofu goes covered in the fridge and is used within 2 days
shelled and already cooked; check the label for "may contain"
check the label for "may contain" sesame

name: Maritime-style salmon cakes with a carrot, cucumber and dill salad
inspiredBy: Maritime Canadian salmon cakes, bound with potato and oats instead of egg
about: Golden pan-fried cakes of canned salmon and mashed potato with onion, Dijon and dill, served with a crisp carrot, cucumber and dill salad and a squeeze of lemon. The potato and oats hold them together, so there is no egg. The salmon, soft bones and all, brings **omega-3, B12, vitamin D and calcium**, and the carrot adds vitamin A.
steps: Boil the potato in unsalted water until a knife slides in easily, about 15 minutes, or use the one you boiled and chilled on Wednesday. Drain well and mash it, leaving a few small lumps. Let it cool for 10 minutes.

Drain the salmon, flake it and mash in the soft bones. Mix it into the potato with the oats, onion, Dijon, half the dill, half the lemon juice, the pepper and the salt. Shape into 2 or 3 firm patties, then chill them for 10 minutes so they hold together.
Wash the cucumber, carrot, spinach and dill. Grate the carrot and toss it with the sliced cucumber, the soy yogurt, the rest of the dill and lemon juice, and a pinch of pepper.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Fry the cakes until deep golden and 74 °C (165 °F) in the centre, about 4 minutes a side. Turn them gently, once.

Serve the cakes on the spinach with the carrot and cucumber salad. Eat the same day, since fried fish cakes don't reheat well, and move any salmon left in the opened tin to a covered glass container in the fridge for up to 2 days.
tip: Boil an extra potato on Wednesday while the salmon roasts, chill it within 2 hours, and these come together in 15 minutes.
ingredients: plain tin, not a flavoured one; check the label for "may contain"; move any leftover to a covered glass container
rolled oats, ground fine in a blender or crushed, to bind
plain Dijon; check the label for "may contain"
soy only, with no almond or coconut blend; check the label for "may contain" nuts

name: Chicken in red pumpkin seed sauce with rice and black beans
inspiredBy: Mexican pipián rojo, the red chile sauce thickened with toasted pepitas, served with beans and rice
about: Tender chicken breast simmered in a smoky red sauce of guajillo chile, tomato and toasted pumpkin seeds, with black beans, wilted spinach and brown rice. The seeds give the sauce body, so it needs no nuts, no cream and no flour. It brings **protein, choline, iron and magnesium**. Make it for two and tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Start the rice. Cook the brown rice in plenty of simmering water until tender, about 30 minutes, then drain it well and keep it covered while you make the sauce.

Tear the guajillo into pieces and toast them in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side, just until fragrant, then cover with hot water and soak 10 minutes. Toast the pumpkin seeds in the same pan, stirring, until they puff and pop, 3 to 4 minutes. Set aside a spoonful for the top.
Blend the drained chiles with the tomatoes, half the onion, the garlic, the toasted seeds, the cumin, oregano, cinnamon and broth until smooth.

Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat and cook the rest of the onion until soft, about 4 minutes. Add the chicken and stir for 2 minutes. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling raw chicken.

Pour in the red sauce and simmer gently, stirring often, until it coats the back of a spoon and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 15 minutes. Keep the heat low, because seed sauces catch on the bottom.

Wash the cilantro. Stir in the beans and the spinach and cook until the spinach wilts, about 2 minutes. Add the lime juice and salt, taste, and serve over the rice with the avocado, cilantro and the reserved seeds on top.

Pack the second portion into a shallow container for tomorrow. Get the chicken and the rice into the fridge within 2 hours (cool the rice within 1 hour) and use within 3 days. Reheat once, until steaming hot at 74 °C.
tip: Skip the rice and serve with warm corn tortillas if you prefer, and add a pinch of chili flakes at the table for heat. It freezes well: thaw it in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.
ingredients: plain, with no added broth or seasoning solution; check the label; cut into bite-size pieces
plain and unsalted; buy them packaged, not from a bulk bin, from a brand made without nuts and sesame if you can, and check for "may contain"
stock and bouillon can carry milk, so check the label for milk and for "may contain"
dried, stemmed and seeded; check the package for "may contain" peanuts and sesame

name: Greek-style chicken and white bean stew with kale, lemon and dill
inspiredBy: Greek braised chicken with beans, in the spirit of fasolada and chicken with celery, brightened with lemon and dill
about: Chicken breast simmered with white beans, tomato, carrot and kale in an oregano and cinnamon-scented sauce, finished with lemon and a handful of dill, with rye bread for the sauce. It is a hearty one-pot supper. It brings **protein, choline, iron and folate**. Make it for two and tomorrow's lunch is ready.
steps: Wash the kale and carrot. Pat the chicken dry and wash your hands and the board after handling it.
Warm the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in a single layer, in two batches, about 4 minutes a batch, then set it aside.

Lower the heat, soften the onion and carrot for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, oregano and cinnamon for 1 minute. Stir in the tomatoes, bay leaf, salt, pepper and 200 ml of water, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes, until the chicken is tender and has reached 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle of a thick chunk.
Add the beans and kale and simmer 8 minutes more, until the kale is silky. Remove the bay leaf and stir in the lemon juice and half the dill.
Serve with the rye bread and the rest of the dill. Put the second portion into a shallow container within 2 hours, keep it up to 3 days and reheat once to 74 °C.
tip: The stew freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw it in the fridge, use it within 2 days and never refreeze it.
ingredients: boneless, trimmed and cut into bite-size chunks
on the side; buy it packaged with a full ingredient list, not from a bakery counter, since breads often carry milk, egg or sesame, and check for "may contain"

name: Maple-mustard salmon with roasted potatoes, carrots and broccoli
inspiredBy: Canadian maple-glazed salmon, with a Dijon edge and roasted vegetables
about: A salmon fillet brushed with maple and Dijon and roasted with crisp-edged potatoes, carrots and broccoli, finished with fresh dill and lemon. It is a classic Canadian supper on one tray. The salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D, B12 and choline**, and the carrots and broccoli add vitamin A, C and K.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Scrub the potatoes and carrots and wash the broccoli. Toss the potatoes and carrots with most of the oil, the garlic, salt and pepper on a large tray.
Roast the potatoes and carrots for 15 minutes, until they are just starting to brown. Add the broccoli to the tray and roast 5 minutes more.
Meanwhile whisk the maple syrup and Dijon in a small bowl. Pat the salmon dry. Wash your hands, the board and anything else the raw fish touched.
Push the vegetables to the sides of the tray, put the salmon in the middle with a little oil and brush it with the maple-mustard glaze.
Roast until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), 10 to 12 minutes. Squeeze the lemon over everything and scatter the dill on top.
tip: Cook it fresh, because fish is best eaten the day it is cooked. Boil an extra potato for Saturday's salmon cakes while the oven is on.
ingredients: plain Dijon; check the label for "may contain"

name: Beef, potato and kale soup with carrot
inspiredBy: Canadian farmhouse beef and vegetable soup, with tomato for depth
about: A thick, savoury soup of tender beef, potato, carrot and onion with tomato and kale stirred in at the end and a slice of rye on the side. It tastes like a Sunday kitchen in a bowl. It brings **iron, zinc, B12 and choline** from the beef, and potassium and fibre from the vegetables.
steps: Wash the carrot, potato and kale. Pat the beef dry, wash your hands and board after handling it, and brown it in the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat until deeply coloured, about 6 minutes.
Add the onion and carrot and cook until the onion softens, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, broth, bay leaf and about 500 ml of water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 50 minutes, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potato and simmer 20 minutes more, until the beef melts at the touch of a fork and the potato is tender. The beef will be well past 71 °C (160 °F) by then.
Stir in the kale and simmer 5 minutes more. Remove the bay leaf, add the salt and pepper, and taste. For a thicker soup, mash a few potato pieces against the side of the pot.
Serve with the rye. Cool the second portion in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours. Keep up to 3 days and reheat once to 74 °C, adding a splash of water.
tip: It takes about 1½ hours on the stove, so start early. A pressure cooker makes it in about 25 minutes of cooking, or use a slow cooker all day. Freeze single portions for up to 3 months, thaw them in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.
ingredients: trimmed and cut into small cubes

name: Sardine pasta with broccoli, tomato, lemon and toasted breadcrumbs
inspiredBy: Sicilian pasta con le sarde and pasta with broccoli, without the pine nuts and with a crisp breadcrumb topping
about: Whole-wheat spaghetti tossed with canned sardines, tender broccoli, tomato, garlic and chili, topped with golden breadcrumbs, dill and lemon. It is quick, bright and not the least bit fishy. The sardines, soft bones and all, bring **calcium, omega-3 and vitamin B12**.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Wash the broccoli and dill. Tear or crush the rye into crumbs and toast them in a dry pan, or with a drop of the oil, over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes, then tip them out.
Cook the pasta in the boiling water until almost al dente, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Save a cup of the pasta water, then drain.

Meanwhile warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and chili flakes for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes, the salt and a splash of pasta water. Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly, about 6 minutes.
Break the sardines into the sauce and heat through for 2 minutes. Toss in the pasta and broccoli with a splash more pasta water, crushing the broccoli a little so it melts into the sauce.

Finish with the lemon juice, pepper and half the dill. Top with the breadcrumbs and the rest of the dill. Eat it fresh, and move any sardines left in the opened tin to a covered glass container in the fridge, for up to 2 days.
tip: If your family dislikes sardines, mash them into the sauce so they melt away. The crumbs keep crisp if you add them at the table.
ingredients: plain dry pasta, not fresh or filled (those often have egg); check the label for "may contain"
plain tin in oil, not one in sauce; check the label for "may contain"; move any leftover to a covered glass container

name: Chicken pozole rojo with hominy, spinach and baked tortilla strips
inspiredBy: Mexican pozole rojo from Jalisco, a red chile and hominy stew with fresh toppings, here made with chicken breast
about: A deep red stew of tender chicken and hominy in a guajillo and ancho chile broth, with thin ribbons of raw spinach, lime, avocado and baked tortilla strips on top. The broth does the work while you do other things. The chicken brings **protein, choline and niacin**, and the lime and spinach add vitamin C and folate.
steps: Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Toast the chiles 20 to 30 seconds a side, just until fragrant (burnt chiles turn bitter). Cover with hot water and soak 15 minutes.
Blend the soaked chiles with half the onion, the garlic, the cumin, the oregano, the broth and a ladle of the soaking water until smooth.

Put the bay leaf, the chile sauce and 600 ml of water in a heavy pot, bring to a simmer and cook, partly covered, for 20 minutes so the broth deepens. Add the chicken and simmer gently until it is cooked through and tender, about 20 minutes. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Add the rinsed hominy and salt and simmer 10 minutes more. The chicken must reach at least 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle of a thick chunk.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Toss the tortilla strips with the oil, spread them on a tray and bake until crisp, about 8 minutes.
Wash the spinach and cilantro. Ladle the pozole into bowls and top with the spinach ribbons, onion, avocado, cilantro, a squeeze of lime and the tortilla strips.
Cool the second portion of the stew in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours. Keep up to 3 days, reheat once to 74 °C, and add the toppings fresh.
tip: The stew freezes well without the toppings. Thaw it in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.

dried, stemmed and seeded; check the package for "may contain" peanuts and sesame

name: Japanese-style tofu and vegetable curry with brown rice
inspiredBy: Japanese kare raisu, the mild, slightly sweet curry, here made from scratch rather than from a boxed roux
about: A mild, glossy Japanese-style curry of golden tofu, carrot, broccoli and edamame over brown rice. The sauce gets its body and a gentle sweetness from grated potato and apple, so there is no boxed roux (which often carries milk). The calcium-set tofu brings **protein, calcium, iron and choline**.
steps: Wash the carrot, potato, apple and broccoli before cutting. Start the rice: cook the brown rice in plenty of simmering water until tender, about 30 minutes, then drain it well.
Pat the tofu dry and cut it into cubes. Fry it in half the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat until golden on all sides, about 8 minutes. Set it aside.
In a pot, heat the rest of the oil and cook the onion until soft and golden, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and cook 1 minute, until it smells toasty.

Stir in the tomatoes, the grated potato and apple and about 350 ml of water, scraping the bottom. Add the carrot, cover and simmer until the carrot is just tender and the potato has melted into the sauce, about 12 minutes.
Add the broccoli, edamame, tofu, soy sauce, maple syrup and salt. Simmer 5 minutes, until the sauce is glossy and thick enough to coat the rice.
Serve over the rice. Cool any leftover rice within 1 hour and any leftover curry within 2 hours, refrigerate, keep up to 3 days, and reheat once to 74 °C.
tip: Japanese curry is mild by design. Add a pinch of chili flakes at the table for heat. Keep any opened tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

Spoon the soy yogurt into a bowl and stir in the flax.
Top with the blueberries and drizzle with the maple syrup.

about: Crisp apple slices with a creamy, nutty-tasting sunflower seed butter dip loosened with a little soy drink. It is a simple snack with **fibre, vitamin E and magnesium**.

Stir the sunflower seed butter, soy drink and cinnamon together until it makes a smooth, thick dip.

name: Smoky roasted white beans
about: White beans roasted until crunchy outside and creamy inside, with smoked paprika and a squeeze of lemon. They bring **fibre, folate and plant protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Dry the beans very well in a clean towel, because dry beans crisp.
Toss with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt and spread on a tray.
Roast, shaking the tray once, until crisp and golden, about 25 minutes. Finish with the lemon juice and eat the same day.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and chili
about: Warm edamame tossed with lemon juice, a pinch of salt and a few chili flakes, the way a Japanese izakaya serves it. They bring **protein, folate, iron and choline**.
steps: Heat the edamame in a microwave or steam them for 2 to 3 minutes, until steaming hot all the way through.
Toss with the lemon juice, salt and chili flakes while still warm.
Eat with a spoon, or with your fingers.

name: Blueberry, spinach and ginger soy smoothie
about: A creamy smoothie of blueberries, spinach and fortified soy drink with ground flax, a spoonful of wheat germ and a little ginger. It is sweet enough that you taste only the berries, and a glass brings **calcium, vitamin D, B12 and plant omega-3**.
steps: Shake the soy drink carton well and wash the blueberries (if fresh) and spinach.
Blend everything until smooth, about 1 minute.
Drink right away, or keep in the fridge up to a day and shake before drinking.

name: Cucumber with lime, chili and pumpkin seeds
about: Cool cucumber spears with lime, a pinch of chili and salt and toasted pumpkin seeds, the way Mexican street stands serve it. It is a crisp, refreshing snack with **magnesium and vitamin K**.

Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they pop, about 3 minutes.

name: Baked tofu bites with a lime-soy dip
about: Cubes of calcium-set tofu baked until the edges turn chewy and crisp, with a quick lime and soy dip. They bring **protein, calcium and choline**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Pat the tofu very dry and cut it into cubes.
Toss with the oil, paprika and garlic powder and bake on a tray, turning once, until golden and chewy at the edges, about 25 minutes.
Stir the soy sauce and lime juice together for the dip. Toss the hot tofu with half of it as it leaves the oven, and serve the rest on the side.

name: Lime and paprika toasted pumpkin seeds
about: Pumpkin seeds toasted until they puff, tossed with lime and smoked paprika. A small handful brings **magnesium, zinc and iron**, and the crunch is very satisfying.
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they puff and pop, about 4 minutes.
Toss with the lime juice, paprika and salt in the hot pan so the lime dries onto the seeds.
Cool before eating, and keep any extra in a jar for up to a week.
tip: For children under 4, chop or grind the pumpkin seeds first, since whole seeds are a choking risk.

name: No-bake oat bites with sunflower seed butter
about: Soft, chewy bites of oats, sunflower seed butter, pumpkin seeds and maple, rolled by hand and chilled. They are made without nuts and bring **fibre, vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Stir the oats, sunflower seed butter, pumpkin seeds, maple syrup and cinnamon together in a bowl. Add a splash of soy drink, a teaspoon at a time, until it holds when squeezed, then rest the mix for 5 minutes so the oats soften.
Roll into small balls with damp hands.
Chill for 20 minutes. They keep in a covered container in the fridge up to 5 days.
tip: For children under 4, chop or grind the pumpkin seeds first, since whole seeds are a choking risk.
ingredients: look for plain rolled oats, packaged and not from a bulk bin; check the label for "may contain" nuts and sesame
plain or unsweetened, with calcium, vitamin D and B12 on the label (a carton giving about 25 to 30% of the daily value for calcium per cup); check it for "may contain" nuts
plain; look for a brand made in a nut-free and sesame-free facility, and check the label for "may contain" peanuts, tree nuts and sesame, since many seed butters share a line
plain and unsalted; buy them packaged, not from a bulk bin, from a brand made without nuts and sesame if you can, and check for "may contain"

name: Baked apple with maple oat crumble
about: A soft, warm baked apple topped with a crisp crumble of oats, pumpkin seeds, maple and cinnamon. It tastes like dessert and is the week's sweet treat, with **fibre and magnesium**.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Wash the apple, halve it and scoop out the core.
Stir the oats, pumpkin seeds, maple syrup, oil and cinnamon together into a crumble. Put the apple cut side up in a small dish and pile the crumble into the hollows and over the top.
Bake until the apple is soft and the crumble is golden, about 25 minutes. Eat warm.
tip: For children under 4, chop or grind the pumpkin seeds first, since whole seeds are a choking risk.
ingredients: look for plain rolled oats, packaged and not from a bulk bin; check the label for "may contain" nuts and sesame
plain and unsalted; buy them packaged, not from a bulk bin, from a brand made without nuts and sesame if you can, and check for "may contain"

name: Rye toast with sunflower seed butter and blueberries
about: Toasted rye bread spread with sunflower seed butter and topped with juicy blueberries. It is a filling snack with **fibre, vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Rinse the blueberries and toast the bread in the oven or a dry pan until golden.
Spread with the sunflower seed butter.
Top with the blueberries, pressing a few in so they stay put.
ingredients: sliced; buy it packaged with a full ingredient list, not from a bakery counter, since breads often carry milk, egg or sesame, and check for "may contain"
plain; look for a brand made in a nut-free and sesame-free facility, and check the label for "may contain" peanuts, tree nuts and sesame, since many seed butters share a line

name: Black bean salsa with baked tortilla chips
about: A chunky salsa of black beans, canned tomato, onion, lime and cilantro, scooped with homemade baked corn tortilla chips. It brings **fibre, folate and iron**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Cut the tortillas into wedges and bake on a tray until crisp, about 8 minutes.
Wash the cilantro. Stir the beans, tomatoes, onion, lime juice, cilantro and salt together.
Scoop the salsa with the warm chips.
ingredients: plain corn tortillas; check the label for "may contain" and for added milk or egg; cut into wedges

name: Overnight oats with berries and almonds
about: Creamy rolled oats soaked in milk overnight with cinnamon, swirled with berries and topped with toasted almonds. The oats bring **slow, steady fibre**, and the almonds bring vitamin E and a little calcium.
steps: Stir the oats, milk and cinnamon together in a jar or container with a lid, then fold in the frozen berries. Cover and chill overnight, or at least 6 hours.
In the morning, stir well. Eat it cold, or warm it in the microwave for 1 to 2 minutes until just steaming. Add a splash of milk if it has thickened.
Top with the almonds just before eating so they stay crunchy.
tip: Mix two jars at once and eat the second within 3 days. Keep soaked oats covered in the fridge, never on the counter. Frozen berries are fine for most people. If you are pregnant, over 65 or have a weakened immune system, heat them until steaming hot first or use fresh.
ingredients: frozen, no need to thaw first

name: Cardamom millet porridge with apple and walnuts
about: Creamy, golden millet simmered in milk with cardamom and cinnamon, topped with warm apple slices and toasted walnuts. Millet is a **gluten-free grain** with magnesium and manganese, and the apple adds sweetness without any added sugar.
steps: Rinse the millet in a sieve under cold water. Toast it in a small dry pot over medium heat, stirring, until it smells nutty, about 2 minutes.

Add the milk, an equal amount of water, the cardamom and the cinnamon. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cook with the lid ajar, stirring often, until the millet is soft and the porridge is thick, about 15 minutes.
Add the diced apple for the last 4 minutes so it softens but keeps a little bite. Spoon into a bowl and top with the walnuts.
tip: For a quicker morning, simmer the millet in the water the night before, cool it within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep it covered in the fridge. In the morning, warm it with the milk and spices until steaming, about 5 minutes, then add the apple.

name: Savoury quinoa breakfast bowl with kale, tomato and a firm egg
about: Fluffy quinoa warmed with cumin, wilted kale and blistered tomatoes, topped with firm-cooked eggs and a squeeze of lemon, with a glass of milk on the side. The **eggs and quinoa** bring choline and complete protein, and the kale and tomato add calcium, iron and vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume with a pinch of salt, covered, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender, about 14 minutes. Rest it, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Meanwhile, wash the kale and tomatoes and halve the tomatoes. Warm half the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat and cook the tomatoes until they blister, about 3 minutes. Add the kale, cumin and a splash of water and stir until tender, about 3 minutes. Tip it onto the quinoa.
Wipe the pan, warm the rest of the oil and cook the eggs, turning once, until the whites are set and the yolks are completely firm, about 5 minutes.
Top the bowl with the eggs and the walnuts, finish with the lemon juice and serve with a glass of milk.
tip: When the bowl is on two mornings in a row, cook a double pot of quinoa on the first, cool the extra within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep it covered in the fridge. Warm it in the pan until steaming. Otherwise cook a fresh pot, which takes about 14 minutes.

name: Quinoa, tuna and chickpea salad with kale, tomato and dill
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mediterranean tuna and chickpea salads, made with quinoa and kale
about: Fluffy quinoa tossed with light tuna, chickpeas, finely sliced kale, juicy tomatoes and a good handful of dill and parsley in a bright lemon dressing. The **tuna and chickpeas** make it properly filling, and the kale and tomato bring calcium and vitamin C to help absorb the iron.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume with a pinch of salt, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 14 minutes. Rest it, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Spread the quinoa in a shallow container to cool. Cool it within 1 hour, then chill it. Meanwhile, wash the kale, tomatoes, parsley and dill, then slice, halve and chop them.

Whisk the lemon juice and olive oil with a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss the kale with half the dressing and rub it with your fingers for a minute to soften it. Add the cooled quinoa, tuna, chickpeas, tomatoes, onion and herbs and toss with the rest.
Eat half now. Pack the second portion in a covered container in the fridge for Wednesday. Keep any opened tin of tuna covered in the fridge and use within 2 days.
tip: Eat the second portion within 3 days of cooking. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
ingredients: washed, stems removed, very finely sliced

name: Smoky chickpea and tomato stew with barley and kale
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish and North African chickpea stews, with barley
about: A smoky stew of chickpeas, sweet cherry tomatoes and chewy barley, with kale stirred in and a spoonful of cool yogurt on top. The chickpeas and kale bring **fibre, folate and calcium**, and the barley keeps it hearty.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion with the garlic, smoked paprika and cumin, about 5 minutes.

Add the tomatoes and cook, pressing them with the back of a spoon, until they collapse, about 5 minutes. Add the barley and broth, then enough hot water to just cover. Simmer with the lid ajar, topping up with a splash of water if it gets dry, until the barley is tender, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and kale and simmer until the kale is tender, about 5 minutes. Add the lemon juice and a pinch of salt and pepper, and serve with the yogurt on top.
tip: Cool leftovers within 1 hour and use within 3 days, reheated until steaming. Add the yogurt cold.

name: Creamy barley and mushroom risotto with chicken and peas
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian mushroom risotto, made with pearled barley
about: Pearled barley simmered slowly in chicken broth until creamy like risotto, with golden mushrooms, seared chicken breast, sweet peas and spinach, finished with a little parmesan and lemon. The barley gives **soluble fibre and a creamy bite**, and the chicken and mushrooms bring B vitamins and protein.
steps: Wash the mushrooms, spinach and carrot. Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and season with a pinch of salt, pepper and the thyme.

Warm half the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken until golden, about 4 minutes, then lift it out onto a plate. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw chicken.
Add the rest of the oil, then the mushrooms, and cook until golden, about 5 minutes. Stir in the onion, garlic and carrot for 2 minutes, then the barley for 1 minute.
Add the broth, then hot water by the ladleful as it is absorbed, stirring now and then, until the barley is tender and creamy, about 22 minutes.
Return the chicken with the peas and cook until the peas are steaming hot and the chicken is cooked through, to 74 °C (165 °F). Fold in the spinach until wilted, then the parmesan and lemon juice.
Spoon half into a bowl. Cool the other portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill it for tomorrow. Reheat it once, until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F), with a splash of water.
tip: Pearled barley has had some of its bran polished off, which makes it creamy. For more chew, use hulled barley, the whole grain: soak it overnight and simmer about 25 minutes longer, adding hot water as needed. Keep the leftover risotto no more than 3 days.

name: Quinoa tabbouleh-style salad with roast salmon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine tabbouleh, with quinoa in place of bulgur
about: A very green, lemony tabbouleh made with quinoa instead of bulgur, packed with parsley, cucumber and tomato, with chickpeas for body and a warm salmon fillet on top. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and all that parsley adds vitamin K and vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume with a pinch of salt, covered, until tender, about 14 minutes. Fluff it with a fork and spread it on a plate to cool for 10 minutes.

Pat the salmon dry, rub it with a little of the oil, the allspice and a pinch of salt and pepper, and roast on a lined tray until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily, about 12 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Wash the parsley, cucumber and tomatoes. Chop the parsley very finely, and dice the cucumber and onion.
Toss the quinoa with the parsley, vegetables, chickpeas, lemon juice and the rest of the oil. Taste for salt and lemon. Top with the salmon.
tip: Use salmon bought and cooked within a day, or thawed overnight in the fridge. If you cook extra quinoa, cool it within 1 hour and use it within 3 days.

name: Buckwheat with roasted vegetables, chickpeas, a firm egg and lemon yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European kasha and Middle Eastern roast vegetable trays
about: Nutty buckwheat under a tray of roasted carrots, broccoli, red pepper and red onion, with crisp spiced chickpeas, a firm-cooked egg and a cool lemon-garlic yogurt. **Buckwheat, chickpeas and egg** make a satisfying plate with lots of fibre, protein and choline, and the carrots and broccoli add vitamin A and C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the vegetables. Toss the carrots, broccoli, pepper and onion on a tray with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Roast for 12 minutes.
Add the chickpeas to the tray, stir, and roast until the vegetables are browned at the edges and the chickpeas are crisp, about 15 minutes more.

Meanwhile, rinse the buckwheat, toast it in a dry pot for 1 minute, then add 2 parts water to 1 part buckwheat by volume and a pinch of salt. Simmer, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes. Rest it for 5 minutes, covered, then fluff.

Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water, peel one and halve it. Stir the yogurt with half the lemon juice, a very small grated clove of garlic and a pinch of salt.
Pile the buckwheat on a plate, top with the roast vegetables and chickpeas and the halved egg, then add the yogurt, the rest of the lemon and the parsley.

Cool the second portion of buckwheat and vegetables within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill. Keep the second egg in its shell, and the yogurt and parsley separate, and add them cold. Eat within 3 days.
tip: Tomorrow the second portion is great cold as a salad, or warm the grain and vegetables until steaming hot before adding the yogurt. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
ingredients: boiled until the yolk is completely firm

name: Farro with lemon-herb chicken, chickpeas and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by freekeh dishes, made with farro
about: Chewy farro with seared lemon-garlic chicken, chickpeas, tender broccoli, juicy tomatoes and a big handful of parsley, lightly spiced with allspice and cinnamon and finished with toasted walnuts. It is **protein-rich and high in fibre**, and the herbs and lemon keep it fresh.
steps: Rinse the farro and simmer it in plenty of lightly salted water until tender but chewy, about 20 minutes. Drain well.
Meanwhile, toss the chicken with half the lemon juice, the garlic, allspice, cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken, turning, until golden and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 8 minutes. Lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli with a splash of water and cook, covered, until tender but still bright, about 5 minutes. Add the chickpeas and tomatoes for the last 2 minutes, until the chickpeas are hot.
Toss the farro with the broccoli, tomatoes, the rest of the lemon juice and the parsley. Top with the chicken and walnuts.
Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill it. Reheat it once for the next lunch until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F), adding the walnuts after.
tip: Farro is wheat, so it is not gluten-free. Freekeh, if you can find it, can go in its place. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.

name: Lemon-dill trout with barley, roasted beets and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian fish with beets and dill, served on barley
about: Pan-roasted trout on lemony barley with sweet roasted beets and carrots, steamed broccoli and a cool dill-yogurt sauce. The trout brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the beets and broccoli add folate and fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the beet and carrot cubes with half the oil and a pinch of salt and roast on a tray until tender at the edges, about 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the barley and simmer it in plenty of lightly salted water until tender, about 25 minutes. Drain well.
Stir the yogurt with the dill, half the lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of salt. Cover and chill.

Pat the trout dry and season with salt and pepper. Warm the rest of the oil in a heavy pan and cook the trout skin side down for 4 minutes, then turn and cook until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily, about 3 minutes more. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.

Steam the broccoli in a splash of water in a covered pot until tender but bright, about 5 minutes. Toss the barley with the broccoli, the roast beets and carrots and the rest of the lemon juice. Top with the trout and the dill-yogurt sauce.
tip: Use fresh trout bought and cooked within a day, or thawed overnight in the fridge. Leftover plain barley must be cooled within 1 hour and used within 3 days.
ingredients: washed, peeled and cut into small cubes
washed and cut into small cubes

name: Stuffed butternut squash with turkey, quinoa, kale and apple
inspiredBy: Inspired by North American harvest-style stuffed squash
about: Roasted butternut squash halves piled with sage-spiced turkey, quinoa, kale and diced apple, with toasted walnuts on top. The squash brings **vitamin A and potassium**, and the turkey and quinoa make it a full meal.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the squash, halve it lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Brush with a little of the oil and a pinch of salt and roast cut side down until a knife slides in easily, about 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume, covered, until tender, about 14 minutes. Fluff it. Wash the kale and chop it finely.

Warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan. Soften the onion with the garlic, sage and cinnamon, about 5 minutes. Add the turkey, break it up and cook until browned and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Stir in the kale, apple and broth until the kale wilts, then the quinoa. Season with salt and pepper.
Turn the squash cut side up, pile in the filling and return to the oven for 8 minutes. Top with the walnuts.
Cool the second portion within 1 hour, then chill it. Reheat it once for the next lunch until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: The filling also works in roasted peppers, or on its own as a quick quinoa and turkey hash.

name: Ginger beef and broccoli with toasty buckwheat
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese beef and broccoli, over buckwheat
about: Quick-seared beef strips with broccoli, carrot, kale and edamame in a ginger-garlic sauce, over toasty buckwheat. The beef and edamame bring **iron and protein**, and the broccoli and lemon add vitamin C, which helps your body absorb the iron from the edamame and greens.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat, toast it in a dry pot for 1 minute, then add 2 parts water to 1 part buckwheat by volume and a pinch of salt. Simmer, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes. Rest it for 5 minutes, covered, then fluff.
Meanwhile, mix the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of water. Toss the sliced beef with a third of it. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer until browned, about 2 minutes, and lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil, the broccoli, carrot and a splash of water, cover and steam for 4 minutes. Add the kale and edamame and stir until the kale wilts and the edamame is steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes.
Return the beef, pour in the rest of the sauce and toss until hot and cooked through, to 71 °C (160 °F), about 1 minute. Serve over the buckwheat.
tip: Slice the beef thinly while it is partly frozen, and cook it in a very hot pan so it sears instead of steaming.

name: Carrot and red pepper sticks with sumac yogurt dip
about: Crunchy sticks with a cool, garlicky yogurt dip dusted with tangy sumac. The carrot brings **vitamin A**, the pepper vitamin C and the yogurt calcium.
steps: Wash and cut the vegetables into sticks. Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice, a very small grated clove of garlic and a pinch of salt, then dust it with the sumac. Dip away.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A banana and a few walnuts with a shake of cinnamon. The banana brings **potassium**.
steps: Peel the banana, dust with the cinnamon and eat it with the walnuts.

name: Canned salmon in red pepper boats
about: Canned salmon with the bones, piled into red pepper halves with lemon. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats, vitamin D, B12 and calcium**.
steps: Wash the pepper, halve it lengthwise and remove the seeds. Flake the salmon into the pepper halves and squeeze over the lemon. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use within 2 days.

name: Apple with almonds and cinnamon
about: A crisp apple and a small handful of almonds with a shake of cinnamon. The apple brings **fibre** and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it, dust with the cinnamon and eat it with the almonds.

name: Orange with almonds
about: A juicy orange and a small handful of almonds. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the orange, peel it and eat it with the almonds.

name: Crunchy cumin chickpeas
about: Oven-crisped chickpeas with cumin and smoked paprika. They bring **fibre, folate and plant protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the very dry chickpeas with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt.
Roast on a tray, shaking once, until crisp, about 20 minutes. Cool for 5 minutes, then eat.
ingredients: drained, rinsed and patted very dry

name: Apple with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A crisp apple and walnut halves with a shake of cinnamon. The apple brings **fibre**.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it, dust with the cinnamon and eat it with the walnuts.

name: Warm edamame with ginger and lemon
about: A bowl of warm edamame with lemon and a little fresh ginger. Edamame brings **protein, folate and fibre**.
steps: Cover the frozen edamame with boiling water for 3 minutes until steaming hot all the way through, then drain. Toss with the lemon juice, ginger and a pinch of salt.

name: Yogurt with berries and walnuts
about: Thick yogurt with berries and a few walnuts. It brings **calcium, protein and plant omega-3 fats**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, stir in the berries and top with the walnuts. Frozen berries are fine for most people. If you are pregnant, over 65 or have a weakened immune system, heat them until steaming hot first, let them cool, or use fresh.

name: Sardines on tomato with lemon
about: Canned sardines piled on juicy tomatoes with lemon. The sardines bring **omega-3 fats, calcium and vitamin D**.
steps: Wash the tomatoes and slice them onto a plate. Lay the sardines over the tomatoes and squeeze over the lemon. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use within 2 days.

name: Firm-boiled egg with cucumber, tomato and dill
about: A firm-boiled egg with crunchy cucumber, sweet cherry tomatoes and a scatter of fresh dill. The egg brings **choline and protein**.
steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water, peel and halve. Serve with the washed tomatoes and cucumber, the dill and a pinch of pepper.
ingredients: boiled until the yolk is completely firm

name: Orange segments with yogurt and walnuts
about: Orange segments with creamy yogurt and chopped walnuts. The orange brings **vitamin C**, the yogurt calcium and the walnuts plant omega-3 fats.
steps: Wash and peel the orange and separate the segments. Spoon the yogurt over and top with the walnuts.

Add the broth, then hot water by the ladleful as it is absorbed, stirring now and then, until the barley is tender and creamy, about 22 minutes.
Return the chicken with the peas and cook until the peas are steaming hot and the chicken is cooked through, to 74 °C (165 °F). Fold in the spinach until wilted, then the parmesan and lemon juice.
Spoon half into a bowl. Cool the other portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill it for tomorrow. Reheat it once, until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F), with a splash of water.
tip: Pearled barley has had some of its bran polished off, which makes it creamy. For more chew, use hulled barley, the whole grain: soak it overnight and simmer about 25 minutes longer, adding hot water as needed. Keep the leftover risotto no more than 3 days.

name: Quinoa tabbouleh-style salad with roast salmon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine tabbouleh, with quinoa in place of bulgur
about: A very green, lemony tabbouleh made with quinoa instead of bulgur, packed with parsley, cucumber and tomato, with chickpeas for body and a warm salmon fillet on top. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and all that parsley adds vitamin K and vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume with a pinch of salt, covered, until tender, about 14 minutes. Fluff it with a fork and spread it on a plate to cool for 10 minutes.

Pat the salmon dry, rub it with a little of the oil, the allspice and a pinch of salt and pepper, and roast on a lined tray until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily, about 12 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Wash the parsley, cucumber and tomatoes. Chop the parsley very finely, and dice the cucumber and onion.
Toss the quinoa with the parsley, vegetables, chickpeas, lemon juice and the rest of the oil. Taste for salt and lemon. Top with the salmon.
tip: Use salmon bought and cooked within a day, or thawed overnight in the fridge. If you cook extra quinoa, cool it within 1 hour and use it within 3 days.

name: Buckwheat with roasted vegetables, chickpeas, a firm egg and lemon yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European kasha and Middle Eastern roast vegetable trays
about: Nutty buckwheat under a tray of roasted carrots, broccoli, red pepper and red onion, with crisp spiced chickpeas, a firm-cooked egg and a cool lemon-garlic yogurt. **Buckwheat, chickpeas and egg** make a satisfying plate with lots of fibre, protein and choline, and the carrots and broccoli add vitamin A and C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the vegetables. Toss the carrots, broccoli, pepper and onion on a tray with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Roast for 12 minutes.
Add the chickpeas to the tray, stir, and roast until the vegetables are browned at the edges and the chickpeas are crisp, about 15 minutes more.

Meanwhile, rinse the buckwheat, toast it in a dry pot for 1 minute, then add 2 parts water to 1 part buckwheat by volume and a pinch of salt. Simmer, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes. Rest it for 5 minutes, covered, then fluff.

Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water, peel one and halve it. Stir the yogurt with half the lemon juice, a very small grated clove of garlic and a pinch of salt.
Pile the buckwheat on a plate, top with the roast vegetables and chickpeas and the halved egg, then add the yogurt, the rest of the lemon and the parsley.

Cool the second portion of buckwheat and vegetables within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill. Keep the second egg in its shell, and the yogurt and parsley separate, and add them cold. Eat within 3 days.
tip: Tomorrow the second portion is great cold as a salad, or warm the grain and vegetables until steaming hot before adding the yogurt. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
ingredients: boiled until the yolk is completely firm

name: Farro with lemon-herb chicken, chickpeas and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by freekeh dishes, made with farro
about: Chewy farro with seared lemon-garlic chicken, chickpeas, tender broccoli, juicy tomatoes and a big handful of parsley, lightly spiced with allspice and cinnamon and finished with toasted walnuts. It is **protein-rich and high in fibre**, and the herbs and lemon keep it fresh.
steps: Rinse the farro and simmer it in plenty of lightly salted water until tender but chewy, about 20 minutes. Drain well.
Meanwhile, toss the chicken with half the lemon juice, the garlic, allspice, cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken, turning, until golden and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 8 minutes. Lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli with a splash of water and cook, covered, until tender but still bright, about 5 minutes. Add the chickpeas and tomatoes for the last 2 minutes, until the chickpeas are hot.
Toss the farro with the broccoli, tomatoes, the rest of the lemon juice and the parsley. Top with the chicken and walnuts.
Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill it. Reheat it once for the next lunch until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F), adding the walnuts after.
tip: Farro is wheat, so it is not gluten-free. Freekeh, if you can find it, can go in its place. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.

name: Lemon-dill trout with barley, roasted beets and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian fish with beets and dill, served on barley
about: Pan-roasted trout on lemony barley with sweet roasted beets and carrots, steamed broccoli and a cool dill-yogurt sauce. The trout brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the beets and broccoli add folate and fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the beet and carrot cubes with half the oil and a pinch of salt and roast on a tray until tender at the edges, about 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the barley and simmer it in plenty of lightly salted water until tender, about 25 minutes. Drain well.
Stir the yogurt with the dill, half the lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of salt. Cover and chill.

Pat the trout dry and season with salt and pepper. Warm the rest of the oil in a heavy pan and cook the trout skin side down for 4 minutes, then turn and cook until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily, about 3 minutes more. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.

Steam the broccoli in a splash of water in a covered pot until tender but bright, about 5 minutes. Toss the barley with the broccoli, the roast beets and carrots and the rest of the lemon juice. Top with the trout and the dill-yogurt sauce.
tip: Use fresh trout bought and cooked within a day, or thawed overnight in the fridge. Leftover plain barley must be cooled within 1 hour and used within 3 days.
ingredients: washed, peeled and cut into small cubes
washed and cut into small cubes

name: Stuffed butternut squash with turkey, quinoa, kale and apple
inspiredBy: Inspired by North American harvest-style stuffed squash
about: Roasted butternut squash halves piled with sage-spiced turkey, quinoa, kale and diced apple, with toasted walnuts on top. The squash brings **vitamin A and potassium**, and the turkey and quinoa make it a full meal.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the squash, halve it lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Brush with a little of the oil and a pinch of salt and roast cut side down until a knife slides in easily, about 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume, covered, until tender, about 14 minutes. Fluff it. Wash the kale and chop it finely.

Warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan. Soften the onion with the garlic, sage and cinnamon, about 5 minutes. Add the turkey, break it up and cook until browned and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Stir in the kale, apple and broth until the kale wilts, then the quinoa. Season with salt and pepper.
Turn the squash cut side up, pile in the filling and return to the oven for 8 minutes. Top with the walnuts.
Cool the second portion within 1 hour, then chill it. Reheat it once for the next lunch until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: The filling also works in roasted peppers, or on its own as a quick quinoa and turkey hash.

name: Ginger beef and broccoli with toasty buckwheat
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese beef and broccoli, over buckwheat
about: Quick-seared beef strips with broccoli, carrot, kale and edamame in a ginger-garlic sauce, over toasty buckwheat. The beef and edamame bring **iron and protein**, and the broccoli and lemon add vitamin C, which helps your body absorb the iron from the edamame and greens.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat, toast it in a dry pot for 1 minute, then add 2 parts water to 1 part buckwheat by volume and a pinch of salt. Simmer, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes. Rest it for 5 minutes, covered, then fluff.
Meanwhile, mix the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of water. Toss the sliced beef with a third of it. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer until browned, about 2 minutes, and lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil, the broccoli, carrot and a splash of water, cover and steam for 4 minutes. Add the kale and edamame and stir until the kale wilts and the edamame is steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes.
Return the beef, pour in the rest of the sauce and toss until hot and cooked through, to 71 °C (160 °F), about 1 minute. Serve over the buckwheat.
tip: Slice the beef thinly while it is partly frozen, and cook it in a very hot pan so it sears instead of steaming.

name: Firm egg scramble with chickpeas, kale and tomato
about: A quick pan of firm-cooked eggs with chickpeas, wilted kale and blistered tomatoes, with a glass of milk on the side. The **eggs and chickpeas** bring choline and protein, and the kale adds calcium and vitamin K.
steps: Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat and cook the tomatoes until they blister, about 3 minutes. Add the kale, cumin and a splash of water and stir until tender, about 3 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and stir until hot, about 2 minutes. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour them in and stir until completely set and firm, about 3 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl and serve with a glass of milk.
tip: Make it your own with baby spinach in place of the kale, or a pinch of chili flakes with the cumin.

name: Berry yogurt bowl with apple and almonds
about: Thick yogurt with berries, diced apple, almonds and cinnamon. It brings **calcium, protein and vitamin E** with fruit for fibre.
steps: Wash and dice the apple.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and stir in the berries and apple.
Top with the almonds and a dusting of cinnamon, and eat straight away while the almonds are crunchy.
tip: Frozen berries are fine for most people. If you are pregnant, over 65 or have a weakened immune system, heat them until steaming hot first, let them cool, or use fresh.

name: Gingerbread pear overnight oats with walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by gingerbread and Bircher muesli, with grated pear in place of the usual apple
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight with grated pear, ginger, cinnamon and a little nutmeg, so it tastes like gingerbread without the sugar. The oats bring **slow fibre**, the milk adds protein and calcium, and the walnuts and pumpkin seeds give it a crunch.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, ginger, cinnamon and nutmeg together in a jar or container with a lid.
Wash the pear, grate it on the coarse side of a grater and fold it in. Cover and chill overnight, or at least 6 hours.
In the morning, stir well. Eat it cold, or warm it in the microwave until just steaming. Loosen with a splash of milk if it has thickened.
Top with the walnuts and pumpkin seeds just before eating so they stay crunchy.
tip: Soaked oats keep up to 3 days covered in the fridge, never on the counter. Mix a jar the night before and eat it the next morning, or mix two jars at once and eat the second within 3 days.

name: Warm cranberry-orange compote yogurt bowl with oat crunch
inspiredBy: Inspired by the cranberry sauce on a harvest table, made lighter and served over yogurt
about: Tart cranberries simmered with chopped orange, a little honey and cinnamon until they burst, spooned over cool Greek yogurt with toasted oats, walnuts and pumpkin seeds. Cranberries and orange bring **vitamin C**, and the yogurt carries the protein.
steps: Rinse fresh cranberries, and wash, peel and chop the orange. Put the cranberries, chopped orange with its juice, honey and cinnamon in a small pot over medium heat. Simmer 6 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until the berries burst and the juice turns syrupy. Let it cool a few minutes.
While it simmers, toast the oats in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden and nutty. Add the chopped walnuts and pumpkin seeds for the last minute.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, pour the warm compote over and scatter the oat crunch on top.
tip: Make a double batch of compote and use the second half within 3 days, covered in the fridge. Frozen cranberries need no thawing.
ingredients: peeled and chopped, with any juice

name: Beet and potato breakfast hash with firm eggs
inspiredBy: Inspired by New England red flannel hash, without the corned beef
about: Crisp-edged potato and ruby beet with soft onion and two eggs cooked until the yolks are firm, finished with parsley and a splash of vinegar. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, and the beets bring folate.
steps: Put the diced potato in a microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water, cover and microwave 4 to 5 minutes, until nearly tender.

Warm the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potato and the finely chopped onion and cook 6 minutes, turning now and then, until golden. Add the beets, paprika, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper and cook 3 minutes more.
Make a well in the hash for each egg and crack them in. Cover and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are completely firm. Break the yolks up with a fork if you like.
Finish with the vinegar and the chopped parsley.
tip: Make it quicker by boiling extra potatoes at dinner the night before. Cool them within 1 hour in a shallow container, refrigerate, use within 3 days and skip the microwave step.

name: Baked apples stuffed with oats, walnuts and cinnamon
inspiredBy: Inspired by the old-fashioned baked apple, with an oat and walnut filling and a spoon of yogurt
about: A whole apple baked until soft, filled with cinnamon oats, honey and walnuts, with cool Greek yogurt on the side. The oats and apple skin give you **fibre that keeps you full**, and the whole kitchen smells like autumn.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Wash the apples, slice a thin lid off the top and scoop out the core with a spoon, keeping the base and sides intact.
Stir the oats, walnuts, honey, cinnamon and a splash of water together into a thick, damp filling. Pack it into the apples and set the lids back on.
Stand the apples in a small baking dish with a splash of water in the bottom. Cover loosely with foil and bake 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 5 minutes more, until the apples are soft when pierced and the oats are lightly crisp on top.
Serve warm with the cool yogurt.
tip: The oven does all the work, so put them in and make your coffee. Bake as many apples as you have people.

name: Beet, apple and white bean salad with canned salmon, a firm egg and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian beet, apple and fish salads, with white beans to make it a lunch
about: Sweet beet, crisp apple and creamy white beans over peppery arugula with flaked canned salmon, a firm egg and a sharp mustard-lemon dressing. The salmon brings **omega-3 and calcium from its soft bones**, the egg adds choline, and the beans bring iron, with lemon to help absorb it.
steps: Put the egg in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 to 11 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water, then peel.
Whisk the mustard, lemon juice, olive oil, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper with a spoonful of water.
Wash the arugula and apple. Slice the apple thinly and cut the beets into wedges.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes.
Toss the beans, beets and apple with half the dressing. Pile onto the arugula, flake the salmon over the top, add the quartered egg and the walnuts and spoon over the rest of the dressing.
tip: Beets stain, so use a board you do not mind. Keep an opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Packing it? Keep the dressing separate and use a cold bag with an ice pack, and eat it the same day.
ingredients: cooked, vacuum-packed or boiled at home
drained, skin and soft bones left in

name: Roast squash with green lentils, kale and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by French-style warm lentil salads, with sage-roasted butternut
about: Sage-roasted butternut squash on warm lentils with garlicky kale, a mustard and cider vinegar dressing and toasted walnuts and pumpkin seeds. The lentils and squash give you **iron, folate and plenty of fibre**, and the second portion is even better the next day.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash, peel and cube the squash, then toss it on a tray with half the oil, the sage, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Roast about 25 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized at the edges.
Meanwhile, rinse the lentils and simmer them with the thyme in plenty of water for 18 to 20 minutes, until tender with a little bite. Drain well.

Slice the onion and soften it in the rest of the oil in a wide skillet for 4 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the washed, stemmed and chopped kale with a splash of water. Cook 4 minutes until tender.
Fold the drained lentils into the kale and stir in the mustard and cider vinegar. Taste and add a pinch more iodized salt if it needs it.
Toast the walnuts and pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes. Pile the lentils onto plates and top with the squash and nuts.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container and refrigerate it for tomorrow's lunch. Reheat the lentils and squash once, until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F), and add the walnuts and seeds cold.
tip: Keep the second portion up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat it only once.
ingredients: peeled and cut in 2 cm cubes

name: Horseradish salmon with roasted Brussels sprouts, carrots and buckwheat
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian salmon with horseradish and dill, with autumn vegetables roasted alongside
about: A salmon fillet roasted beside caramelized Brussels sprouts and carrots, with nutty buckwheat and a sharp horseradish and parsley yogurt sauce. The salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D and choline**, and the sprouts bring vitamin K and vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the Brussels sprouts and carrots on a large tray with most of the oil, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Roast 25 minutes, turning once, until browned at the edges and tender.
Meanwhile, rinse the buckwheat and simmer it in about twice its volume of water with a lid on for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and let it steam 5 minutes.
Stir the yogurt, horseradish, chopped parsley and lemon juice together. Add a spoonful of water if it is too thick.

About 12 minutes before the vegetables are done, pat the salmon dry, rub with the last of the oil, salt and pepper, and set it skin side down on a second small tray. Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily.
Wash your hands, board and knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw fish.
Fluff the buckwheat with a fork. Serve the salmon on the buckwheat with the vegetables and the sauce.
tip: Buy the salmon the day you cook it, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight.
ingredients: washed, peeled and cut in thick batons

name: Apple-mustard chicken with red cabbage, white beans and buckwheat
inspiredBy: Inspired by Polish and German braised cabbage with apple, and Eastern European kasha
about: Tender chicken thigh pieces simmered with red cabbage, apple, white beans, caraway and mustard, served over nutty buckwheat. The cabbage and apple bring **vitamin C and fibre**, and the chicken and beans bring protein, iron and zinc.
steps: Toss the chicken pieces with the mustard, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Rinse the buckwheat, then simmer it in about twice its volume of water with a lid on for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and let it steam 5 minutes.

Warm half the oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 minutes, turning, until golden. It will not be cooked through yet. Move it to a clean plate, and wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

In the same skillet, soften the onion in the rest of the oil for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and caraway for 30 seconds. Stir in the washed cabbage, the apple, vinegar and broth, cover and cook 10 minutes until the cabbage is soft.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan, add the drained beans and simmer uncovered 5 to 6 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the sauce has thickened.
Fluff the buckwheat with a fork and stir in the chopped parsley. Serve the chicken and cabbage over it.
This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container and refrigerate it for tomorrow's lunch. Reheat it once, until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Keep the second portion up to 3 days in the fridge and reheat it only once.

name: Creamy mushroom, barley and white bean soup with spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Polish and Russian mushroom and barley soups, thickened with mashed white beans and a splash of milk instead of cream
about: Deeply browned mushrooms, chewy barley and white beans, seasoned with thyme and a little caraway. Half the beans are mashed in and a splash of milk makes the broth creamy, then spinach and a squeeze of lemon finish it. The mushrooms bring **B vitamins and copper**, the milk brings calcium, and the beans and barley bring fibre.
steps: Heat a large pot over medium-high heat, add the mushrooms and cook 5 minutes without much stirring, until the water has gone and they are well browned.
Add the oil, chopped onion and carrot and cook 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic, thyme and caraway for 30 seconds.

Add the rinsed barley, a pinch of iodized salt and enough broth and boiling water from the kettle to cover by about 3 cm. Bring back to a boil, then simmer with a lid on 20 minutes, until the barley is tender with a little chew.

Stir in the beans. Mash about half of them against the side of the pot to make the soup creamy. Add the spinach and cook 2 minutes until wilted. Pour in the milk and warm gently for 2 minutes without boiling, then take the pot off the heat and stir in the lemon juice and pepper.
Ladle into bowls, swirl in the yogurt and scatter the chopped walnuts and almonds on top.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container (barley keeps absorbing broth, so loosen it with water when you reheat). Refrigerate for tomorrow's lunch and reheat gently, without a hard boil, until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Put the kettle on before you start. The soup keeps up to 3 days in the fridge. Swirl in the yogurt and scatter the nuts on after reheating.

name: Sage beef strips with sweet potato, kale and white beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Tuscan-style skillet of beans and greens, with sweet potato and sage for autumn
about: Quick-seared beef strips in one skillet with crisp-edged sweet potato, wilted kale and creamy white beans, all pulled together with sage and a little mustard. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, and the sweet potato brings vitamin A.
steps: Warm half the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sweet potato with a splash of water, cover and cook 8 minutes until nearly tender, then uncover and cook 6 minutes more, stirring, until browned at the edges. Move it to a plate.

Pat the beef dry and toss with the sage, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Add the rest of the oil to the hot skillet and sear the beef in a single layer for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until browned, with no pink left and at least 71 °C (160 °F) in the thickest strip. Move it to a clean plate, and wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw beef.

Add the sliced onion to the skillet for 2 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the washed, stemmed and chopped kale, the broth, vinegar and mustard and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the kale is tender.
Stir in the beans, sweet potato and beef and heat through for 2 minutes until steaming. Taste and add a little more vinegar if it needs brightness.
tip: Put the beef in the freezer for 20 minutes before slicing for thin, even strips. If it was frozen, thaw it in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
ingredients: sliced across the grain in thin strips

name: Roast squash and chickpea bowl with arugula, firm eggs and tahini-lemon sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern roast pumpkin and chickpea salads with tahini
about: Cumin and paprika roast butternut and chickpeas on a bed of peppery arugula with firm eggs, a lemony tahini sauce and crunchy walnuts and pumpkin seeds. The chickpeas, eggs and tahini bring **protein, choline, calcium and magnesium** to a bowl that is mostly squash.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash, peel and cube the squash. Toss it and the drained chickpeas on a tray with the oil, cumin, paprika and a pinch of iodized salt. Roast 25 minutes, turning once, until the squash is tender and the chickpeas are crisp at the edges.
Meanwhile, put the eggs in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 to 11 minutes until the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, grated garlic and a few spoonfuls of water into a smooth, pourable sauce. Thinly slice the onion, wash the arugula and chop the walnuts and pumpkin seeds.
Pile the arugula into bowls, top with the warm squash and chickpeas, the onion and the halved eggs, then drizzle with the sauce and scatter the walnuts and pumpkin seeds over.
tip: Roast the chickpeas on the same tray as the squash, then eat the bowl warm or at room temperature. Packing it? Keep the eggs and sauce in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
ingredients: peeled and cut in 2 cm cubes

name: Walnut-crusted trout with roasted Brussels sprouts, crisp kale and crushed potatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by nut-crusted fish plates, with a mustard and parsley walnut crust
about: A rainbow trout fillet under a mustard, parsley and walnut crust, roasted alongside caramelized Brussels sprouts, crisp kale and golden potatoes. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the walnuts add more omega-3 and a good crunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Toss the potatoes on a large tray with half the oil, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Roast 8 minutes.
Add the Brussels sprouts and garlic to the tray, toss and roast 17 minutes more, turning once.
Mix the walnuts, chopped parsley and a little oil into a crumbly crust. Pat the trout dry and brush the top with the mustard. Press the crust on firmly and set it on a lined tray.
Wash your hands, board and knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw fish.

Put the trout in the oven for the last 12 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily. Add the washed, torn kale to the vegetables for the last 6 minutes, until crisp at the edges.
Squeeze the lemon over the trout and vegetables and serve.
tip: Buy the trout the day you cook it, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight.

name: Canned salmon and chickpea salad with apple, red cabbage, spinach and sunflower seeds
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian fish and apple salads, with chickpeas for body
about: Flaked canned salmon and chickpeas with crisp red cabbage, carrot and apple on a big bed of spinach, topped with walnuts and sunflower seeds, in a cider vinegar and mustard dressing. Canned salmon with its soft bones brings **omega-3 and calcium**, and the chickpeas bring iron and fibre.
steps: Whisk the vinegar, mustard and olive oil with a spoonful of water and the pepper.

Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Wash the apple, cabbage, carrot, spinach and parsley, then shred the cabbage, grate the carrot, cut the apple into matchsticks, thinly slice the onion and chop the parsley.
Toss the chickpeas, cabbage, carrot, apple, onion and parsley with most of the dressing. Toss the spinach with the rest and spread it in a wide bowl as a bed.
Pile the chickpea slaw onto the spinach, flake the salmon over the top and scatter the walnuts and sunflower seeds.
tip: Keep an opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Packing it? Use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
ingredients: drained, skin and soft bones left in
