name: Warm mushroom, buckwheat and chickpea salad with kale and a firm egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European kasha with mushrooms, served as a warm salad
about: Browned mushrooms, nutty buckwheat and chickpeas with a firm egg, tossed with massaged kale, parsley and a mustard-lemon dressing. The chickpeas and egg bring **protein and choline**, and the mushrooms bring B vitamins.
steps: Put the egg in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 to 11 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.

Rinse the buckwheat and simmer it in about twice its volume of water with a lid on for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat, let it steam 5 minutes, then spread it in a shallow container to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, sear the mushrooms in a hot dry skillet for 5 minutes until browned, then add a little of the oil and the garlic for 30 seconds.
Whisk the lemon juice, mustard, the rest of the oil, a pinch of iodized salt and pepper. Wash, stem and finely slice the kale and rub it with a spoonful of the dressing for a minute to soften it.

Toss the buckwheat, mushrooms, drained chickpeas, kale, onion and parsley with the rest of the dressing and scatter the chopped walnuts and almonds on top. Quarter the egg and add it cold. Eat warm or at room temperature.
tip: Cook the buckwheat the night before, cool it within 1 hour in a shallow container and refrigerate. Use it within 3 days. Packing it? Keep the egg in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

name: Chicken, chickpea and mushroom masala with sweet potato and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian chole and chicken masala, with mushrooms, sweet potato and spinach
about: Chicken, chickpeas and mushrooms simmered with sweet potato in a tomato, ginger and garam masala sauce, with spinach stirred in at the end and a spoon of cool yogurt. The chickpeas and spinach bring **iron and folate**, the sweet potato brings vitamin A, and the lemon helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken pieces for 4 minutes, turning, then move them to a clean plate. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
In the same pot, cook the chopped onion 4 minutes, then the mushrooms 5 minutes more until browned. Stir in the grated garlic, garam masala, turmeric, cumin and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, the sweet potato, a pinch of iodized salt and enough water to nearly cover. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 12 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the drained chickpeas and simmer, uncovered, 6 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the sweet potato is tender.
Stir in the washed spinach until wilted, then the lemon juice. Serve topped with the yogurt and chopped parsley.
tip: For heat, add a pinch of chili powder or a slit green chili with the spices.

name: Orange with sunflower seeds
about: Juicy orange segments with sunflower seeds. Sunflower seeds bring **vitamin E**, which is one of the harder vitamins to reach.
steps: Wash and peel the orange and split it into segments.
Serve with the sunflower seeds.

name: Greek yogurt with orange and almonds
about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy orange pieces and chopped almonds. It brings **protein and calcium**, and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash and peel the orange, then chop it into pieces.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the orange and chopped almonds.

name: Pear with almonds
about: A juicy pear with almonds. The pear skin brings **fibre**, and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the pear and slice it.
Serve with the almonds.

name: Pear with walnuts
about: A juicy pear with crunchy walnuts. The walnuts add **omega-3 fats** and a good bite to the sweet fruit.
steps: Wash the pear and slice it.
Serve with the walnuts.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A ripe banana with walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The banana brings **potassium** and the walnuts bring omega-3 fats.
steps: Slice the banana into a bowl.
Top with the walnuts and cinnamon.

name: Greek yogurt with cinnamon and walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt with a dusting of cinnamon and chopped walnuts. It brings **protein and calcium** with a little crunch.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Top with the cinnamon and the chopped walnuts.

name: Apple slices with walnuts and cinnamon
about: Crisp apple slices with walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The apple skin brings **fibre**, and the walnuts bring omega-3 fats.
steps: Wash the apple, cut it into slices and dust with the cinnamon.
Serve with the walnuts.

name: Banana with almonds
about: A ripe banana with a small handful of almonds. The banana brings **potassium** and the almonds bring vitamin E and magnesium.
steps: Slice the banana into a bowl.
Top with the almonds.

name: Smoky roasted chickpeas
about: Crunchy chickpeas roasted with smoked paprika and cumin, ready in 25 minutes. A handful gives you **plant protein and fibre**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Drain the chickpeas, rinse and pat them very dry with a clean towel.
Toss with the oil, paprika, cumin and a pinch of iodized salt on a tray.
Roast 25 minutes, shaking the tray once or twice, until crisp. They crisp more as they cool.
tip: Best the day they are made. Cool completely before storing in a loosely covered container.

name: Carrot sticks with white bean and sage dip
about: Creamy white beans mashed with lemon, garlic and a little sage for dipping crunchy carrot. It is a snack with **fibre and plant protein** in it.
steps: Mash the beans with the lemon juice, olive oil, grated garlic, sage, a pinch of iodized salt and a spoonful of water until fairly smooth.
Wash and peel the carrots and cut them into sticks. Serve with the dip.
tip: Make a small batch of dip and keep it covered in the fridge up to 3 days.

name: Walnut, almond and seed mix
about: A small handful of walnuts, almonds, pumpkin seeds and sunflower seeds. Together they bring **vitamin E, omega-3, iron and magnesium**.
steps: Stir the walnuts, almonds, pumpkin seeds and sunflower seeds together.
Keep a small portion in a jar or bag.

name: Overnight oats with berries, walnuts and chia
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss bircher muesli
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight with Greek yogurt and milk until creamy, with frozen berries that thaw into a sweet swirl, a spoonful of chia and crunchy walnuts. Five minutes the night before, and it brings **fibre, protein and plant omega-3** to the first meal.
steps: Wash your hands, then stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia and cinnamon together in a jar until no dry oats are left.
Spoon the frozen berries on top, put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. The berries thaw and bleed into the oats, which is exactly what you want.
In the morning, stir it up and loosen it with a splash of milk if it is thick. Scatter the walnuts over the top so they stay crunchy.
Keep it in the fridge and eat within 2 days of making it.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, simmer the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

name: Apple cinnamon oatmeal with walnuts
about: Creamy stovetop oats cooked in milk with grated apple and cinnamon, topped with toasted walnuts. It is warm, filling and ready in 10 minutes, with **fibre, calcium and a little plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the apple, then grate it. Put the oats, grated apple, cinnamon and salt in a small pot with just enough of the milk to cover them.
Cook over medium heat, stirring often, for about 5 minutes until thick and creamy, adding a splash more milk if it catches.
Spoon into a bowl, pour the rest of the milk around it and scatter over the walnuts.
tip: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes for extra flavour.

name: Turkish-style potato and chickpea skillet with eggs
inspiredBy: Inspired by Turkish patatesli yumurta (potatoes with eggs)
about: Crisp-edged potatoes and chickpeas with onion, spinach, cumin and mild, fruity Aleppo pepper, with eggs cooked right in the pan until the yolks are firm, then finished with lemon, parsley and a pinch of dried mint. A slow Saturday breakfast with **protein, iron and folate**.
steps: Wash the potatoes and spinach before cutting. Dice the potatoes small, about 1 cm, so they cook quickly.
Heat the oil in a wide nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the potatoes, cover and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until they are tender and starting to brown.
Add the onion, Aleppo pepper, cumin and salt and cook for 4 minutes. Stir in the chickpeas and cook another 3 minutes so they crisp at the edges, then fold in the spinach until just wilted.

Make wells in the pan and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook for about 8 minutes, until the whites and yolks are completely firm. Finish with the lemon juice, parsley and the mint, rubbed between your fingers. Wash your hands after handling the raw eggs.
tip: Dice the potatoes the night before to cut the morning time.

name: Sweet potato and pinto bean breakfast bowl
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex breakfast bowls
about: A soft baked sweet potato piled with warm, cumin-scented pinto beans mashed until creamy, plus avocado, a spoonful of yogurt and lime. Filling, sweet and savoury at once, with **fibre, potassium and vitamin A** to start the day.
steps: Wash the sweet potato and prick it all over with a fork. Microwave on high for 6 to 8 minutes, turning once, until soft all the way through. In the oven it takes about 45 minutes at 200 °C (400 °F): bake it the night before, refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).
Meanwhile, warm the pinto beans in a small pot with the cumin, salt and 2 tablespoons of water for about 4 minutes, mashing about half so they turn creamy, like quick refried beans.
Split the sweet potato open, spoon over the beans, then top with the avocado, yogurt, lime juice and pumpkin seeds.
tip: Add a pinch of chili flakes to the beans for heat.

name: Hummus plate with herby lentil salad and egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine hummus plates
about: Creamy homemade hummus with a cool lentil, cucumber and tomato salad, a firm hard-boiled egg and carrot sticks to scoop. The chickpeas and lentils bring **plenty of protein, iron and folate**, and the lemon helps your body absorb the iron.
steps: Wash the cucumber, tomatoes, parsley and carrot. Put the egg in a small pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water, then peel and halve.

Blend the chickpeas, tahini, half the lemon juice, the garlic, half the olive oil, the cumin, half the salt and 2 to 3 tablespoons of cold water until smooth and creamy. Add more water if it is thick.
Toss the lentils with the cucumber, tomatoes, onion, parsley, the rest of the lemon juice, the rest of the oil and the remaining salt.
Spread the hummus on a plate, make a dip in the middle and pile the lentil salad beside it. Arrange the egg and carrot sticks around the edge.
tip: Make the hummus and boil the egg the night before and it is a 5-minute lunch.

name: White bean and tuna salad with potatoes and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Tuscan tonno e fagioli
about: A Tuscan-style salad of creamy white beans, flaked tuna, a firm hard-boiled egg, warm boiled potatoes, tomatoes and baby spinach in a bright lemon dressing. The beans and tuna bring **protein, folate and iron**, and the potatoes make it a full lunch.
steps: Wash the potatoes and produce. Cut the potatoes into bite-sized chunks, put them in a pot with the egg, cover with cold water, bring to a boil and cook for about 12 minutes, until a knife slides in easily and the egg yolk is completely firm. Drain, then cool the egg in cold water, peel it and cut it into quarters.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a large bowl. Add the warm potatoes and onion and toss, so they soak up the dressing.
Fold in the white beans, tuna, tomatoes and parsley, flaking the tuna with a fork. Top with the egg.
Add the spinach just before serving so it stays fresh and bright.
tip: Canned light tuna is low in mercury; keep fresh or frozen tuna out of the week. For a packed lunch, boil the potatoes and egg the night before, keep them in the fridge and add the spinach in the morning.

name: Three-bean beef chili
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex chili con carne
about: A thick, smoky chili with kidney, black and pinto beans, lean beef, carrot, tomatoes and sweet peppers, topped with avocado, a spoonful of yogurt and lime. The three beans bring **fibre, folate and iron**, and the spices are bloomed in the oil for depth.
steps: Wash the carrot, pepper and parsley. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and pepper for about 7 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 71 °C (160 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, all three beans, the salt and about 150 ml of water. Simmer, partly covered, for 18 to 20 minutes until thick, adding a splash of water if it catches.
Stir in the lime juice. Serve topped with the avocado, yogurt and parsley.

Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool it in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours. Keep up to 3 days and reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F), until steaming. To freeze, cool within 2 hours and freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F) until steaming.
tip: Easing into beans? Rinse canned beans well and start with a smaller bowl, then build up over a week or two. Keep the rest of the pinto beans covered in the fridge for Thursday's breakfast bowl, and freeze the leftover black and kidney beans for Friday's stew or another chili. Skip the beef for a fully vegetarian pot.

name: Ginger-soy salmon with edamame, spinach and roasted sweet potato
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese teriyaki-style salmon
about: Salmon fillets glazed with ginger, garlic, lime and reduced-sodium soy, served over garlicky wilted spinach and edamame with caramelized roasted sweet potato. It is the first fish night, with **omega-3 and some vitamin D** from the salmon and plant protein from the edamame.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potato and spinach. Cut the sweet potato into thin wedges. Toss them with half the olive oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Whisk the soy sauce, lime juice, ginger and half the garlic. Pour half over the salmon in a dish and marinate in the fridge for 10 minutes. Never reuse the marinade that touched raw fish.
Move the sweet potato aside and put the salmon on the tray. Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling raw fish.

Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a pan, add the remaining garlic, the edamame and the spinach and cook for about 4 minutes, until the spinach is wilted and the edamame is hot. Splash in the reserved sauce.
Serve the salmon over the spinach and edamame with the sweet potato.
tip: Eat the fish fresh: salmon is one of the two dinners this week that is not a leftover.
ingredients: skin on or off, pin bones removed

name: Lentil and squash dal
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian dal
about: Red lentils melt into a golden, gently spiced dal with sweet butternut squash and carrot, served with a cool cucumber and tomato salad and brightened with lemon and parsley. It brings **iron, folate and vitamin A**, and the lemon helps your body absorb the iron.
steps: Wash the squash, carrot, cucumber, tomatoes and parsley. Rinse the lentils under cold water until it runs clear.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric and coriander and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Add the lentils, squash, carrot, crushed tomatoes, salt and about 600 ml of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have broken down and the squash is tender.
Stir in the garam masala and half the lemon juice and cook for 1 minute. Scatter with parsley.
While the dal finishes, toss the cucumber and tomatoes with the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of the salt. Serve this cool, crunchy salad next to the dal.

Pack the second portion for lunch: cool it in a shallow container, refrigerate within 2 hours, keep up to 3 days and reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F). To freeze, cool within 2 hours and freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F) until steaming.
tip: Add a pinch of chili flakes with the cumin for heat, and spoon it over a little cooked millet or quinoa if you have some.

name: Tuscan white beans with spinach, potatoes and baked eggs
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan fagioli all'uccelletto
about: Creamy cannellini-style beans simmered with rosemary, tomato, carrot and spinach, with diced potato for body and eggs baked firm on top. It is rustic and deeply savoury, with **fibre, plant iron and folate** from the beans and greens.
steps: Wash the potato, carrot and spinach. Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, rosemary and chili flakes and cook 1 minute.
Add the potato, crushed tomatoes, salt and about 300 ml of water. Simmer, covered, for 10 minutes, until the potato is almost tender.
Stir in the beans and simmer for 8 minutes more. Mash a few beans against the side of the pot to make the broth creamy, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Make a small well for each egg and crack them in. Cover and cook gently for about 8 minutes, until the white and yolk are completely firm. Wash your hands after handling the raw eggs.
Finish with lemon juice. Pack the second portion for lunch: cool it in a shallow container, refrigerate within 2 hours, keep up to 3 days and reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Add the rind of a hard cheese to the pot while it simmers if you have one.

name: Black bean and sweet potato stew
inspiredBy: Inspired by Caribbean and Latin American black bean stews
about: A smoky, lime-bright stew of black beans and sweet potato with peppers, cumin and smoked paprika, finished with creamy avocado and toasted pumpkin seeds. It brings **fibre, potassium and vitamin A**, and it is even better the next day.
steps: Wash the sweet potato, pepper and parsley. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and chili powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the sweet potato, crushed tomatoes, salt and about 300 ml of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, for 12 minutes.
Stir in the black beans and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes more, until the sweet potato is tender and the stew is thick. Mash a few beans against the pot to thicken it.
Stir in the lime juice. Serve topped with the avocado, pumpkin seeds and parsley.

Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool it in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours. Keep up to 3 days and reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F). To freeze, cool within 2 hours and freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F) until steaming.
tip: Leave out the chili powder for a mild pot.

name: Spanish-style chicken, chickpea and potato stew
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish chicken and chickpea stews
about: Tender chicken thighs simmered with chickpeas, potatoes, peppers and smoked paprika in a garlicky tomato broth, finished with spinach and lemon. It is the weekend project: the stew gets better overnight and brings **protein, iron and zinc**.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach and parsley. Pat the chicken dry and season with half the salt and half the smoked paprika. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for about 5 minutes. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling raw chicken.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, cumin and the rest of the paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes, crushed tomatoes, the remaining salt and about 300 ml of water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender, the sauce is thick and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
Fold in the spinach until wilted, then add the lemon juice and parsley.

Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool it in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours. Keep up to 3 days and reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F). To freeze, cool within 2 hours and freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F) until steaming.
tip: A strip of orange peel simmered in the pot adds a classic Spanish note.

name: Lemon trout on warm lentils with roasted tomatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by French lentilles with fish
about: Trout fillets roasted with lemon over earthy lentils warmed with carrot, onion and garlic, with blistered cherry tomatoes and a handful of spinach. It is the second fish night, with **omega-3, protein and some vitamin D**, plus the lentils' iron and folate.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the tomatoes, carrot, spinach and parsley. Put the tomatoes on a lined tray with a little of the oil and roast for 10 minutes.

Push the tomatoes aside, lay the trout on the tray, brush with a little oil, top with lemon slices and a pinch of the salt. Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling raw fish.

Meanwhile, warm most of the remaining oil in a pan and cook the carrot and onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin, then the lentils and a splash of water and warm through for 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the lemon juice, parsley, pepper and the rest of the salt. Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Serve the trout over the lentils with the roasted tomatoes, scattered with the toasted almonds.
tip: Salmon works in place of trout if you prefer.

name: Orange with pumpkin seeds
about: A juicy orange with a small handful of pumpkin seeds, sweet and crunchy at once. It brings **vitamin C, magnesium and zinc**, and the vitamin C helps your body absorb the iron in the beans.
steps: Wash the orange before peeling it. Peel, segment and eat with the pumpkin seeds.

name: Pear with walnuts
about: A ripe pear and a small handful of walnuts, soft and crunchy together. It brings **fibre and a little plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it and serve with the walnuts.

name: Greek yogurt with berries, walnuts and chia
about: Thick Greek yogurt with frozen berries that thaw into a sauce, a sprinkle of walnuts and a spoonful of chia. It brings **protein, calcium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the berries and let them thaw for a few minutes, then add the walnuts and chia.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, simmer the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

name: Apple with almonds
about: A crisp apple with a small handful of almonds for crunch. It brings **fibre, vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

name: Carrot and cucumber sticks with lemon tahini
about: Crunchy carrot and cucumber sticks with a quick lemon tahini dip that takes a minute to stir. It brings **fibre, vitamin A and some calcium**.
steps: Wash the carrot and cucumber and cut into sticks. Stir the tahini, lemon juice, salt and a splash of cold water until smooth and pourable, then serve for dipping.

name: Edamame with lime and chili
about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with lime and a pinch of chili, salty and bright. It brings **plant protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain. Toss with the lime juice, chili flakes and salt and eat warm.

name: Edamame with lemon and cumin
about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with lemon juice, a little ground cumin and a pinch of salt. It brings **plant protein, folate and iron**, and the lemon helps your body absorb the iron.
steps: Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain. Toss with the lemon juice, cumin and salt and eat warm.

name: Sardines with tomato, cucumber and lemon
about: Canned sardines with their soft bones, fresh tomato and cucumber and a squeeze of lemon, ready in two minutes. They bring **omega-3, calcium, vitamin B12 and some vitamin D**.
steps: Wash the tomatoes, cucumber and parsley. Arrange the cucumber and tomatoes on a plate, lay the sardines on top, then finish with the lemon juice, parsley and pepper.
tip: Buy two tins for Thursday and Friday. Sardines are packed in oil; drain them well and keep the soft bones in for the calcium. Keep any opened tin in a covered container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

name: Greek yogurt with pear and walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt with diced pear, cinnamon and a few walnuts, a protein-rich extra at the bigger sizes. It brings **protein, calcium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the pear, then dice it. Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the pear, walnuts and cinnamon.

name: Greek yogurt with apple and walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt with diced apple, cinnamon and a few walnuts, a protein-rich extra at the bigger sizes. It brings **protein, calcium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the apple, then dice it. Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the apple, walnuts and cinnamon.

name: Almond, walnut and pumpkin seed mix
about: A small handful of almonds, walnuts and pumpkin seeds, an easy extra at the bigger sizes. It brings **vitamin E, magnesium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Mix the almonds, walnuts and pumpkin seeds in a small bowl.

name: Orange with almonds
about: A juicy orange and a handful of almonds, fresh and crunchy. It brings **vitamin C, vitamin E and some calcium**.
steps: Wash the orange before peeling it. Peel, segment and eat with the almonds.

name: Apple with walnuts
about: A crisp apple with a handful of walnuts, an easy extra at the bigger sizes. It brings **fibre and plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the walnuts.

name: Overnight oats with blueberries and almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss bircher and North American overnight oats
about: Oats soaked in milk and Greek yogurt with chia until spoonable, then topped with fresh blueberries, a drizzle of honey and crunchy almonds. It is made the night before, and the oats and chia bring **fibre and plant omega-3**, and the almonds bring vitamin E, to keep you going till lunch.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia, cinnamon and salt together in a jar or bowl. Cover and chill overnight, or at least 4 hours.
In the morning, stir well. If it has thickened too much, loosen it with a splash of milk.
Wash the blueberries and spoon them on top, then add the honey and the almonds for crunch.
Keep any extra jar covered in the fridge and eat it within 3 days.
tip: Mix each jar the night before, or mix Monday's on Sunday night and Wednesday's and Friday's together on Tuesday night, so none waits more than 3 days. Swap in any berry or chopped fruit.

name: Warm apple and cinnamon quinoa bowl
inspiredBy: Inspired by quinoa breakfast porridge from the Andes
about: Quinoa simmered in milk until soft and creamy, with diced apple, cinnamon, a spoonful of Greek yogurt, toasted almonds and chia on top. It is warm and comforting, and the quinoa and yogurt bring **protein and magnesium** to a quick weekday breakfast.
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under cold water for 30 seconds. This removes its bitter coating.

Put the quinoa, milk, cinnamon and salt in a small pot. Bring to a gentle boil, then turn the heat to low, cover and simmer until the quinoa is soft and most of the milk is absorbed, about 15 minutes. Stir once or twice.
Meanwhile, wash and dice the apple, and toast the almonds in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Spoon the quinoa into a bowl and top with the apple, the yogurt, the almonds, the chia and the honey.
tip: Cook a double pot, chill the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, and eat it within 3 days. Reheat the quinoa with a splash of milk until steaming (74 °C), then add the yogurt, apple and almonds cold.

name: Sweet potato and black bean breakfast hash with firm eggs
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex breakfast skillets
about: Crisp-edged sweet potato cubes, onion, black beans and wilted spinach in a smoky skillet, with eggs cooked until the yolks are firm, a little avocado and a cool spoonful of yogurt on top. It is a proper weekend breakfast, and the sweet potato and spinach bring **vitamin A and folate**.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Microwave the sweet potato cubes in a covered bowl with a splash of water until just tender, about 4 minutes.

Heat the oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sweet potato in a single layer and cook without stirring for 3 minutes, then stir and cook until golden at the edges, about 5 minutes more.
Add the onion, smoked paprika, cumin and salt. Cook until the onion softens, about 4 minutes. Stir in the black beans and spinach until the spinach wilts.

Make gaps in the hash and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook over medium-low heat until the whites are set and the yolks are firm all the way through, about 6 minutes. Break each yolk gently with a spatula to be sure it is cooked through.
Slide onto a plate and top with the sliced avocado, a spoonful of yogurt and the pepper. Wash your hands and the pan after handling raw eggs.
ingredients: scrubbed and cut in small cubes
cooked until the yolks are firm

name: Apple slices with walnuts
about: Crisp apple slices with a handful of walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. It is sweet and crunchy, with **fibre and plant omega-3** in a snack that takes a minute.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and scatter the cinnamon over the slices. Serve with the walnuts.

name: Carrot and cucumber sticks with quick hummus
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine hummus
about: A small bowl of lemony, garlicky chickpea hummus with crisp carrot and cucumber sticks for dipping. The chickpeas and tahini bring **fibre, folate and copper**, and it is blended in two minutes.
steps: Blend or mash the chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt and a spoonful of cold water until smooth and creamy, adding a little more water if it is thick.
Wash the carrot and cucumber, cut them into sticks and serve with the hummus.
tip: Make a double batch of hummus and keep it in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

name: Crunchy smoky roasted chickpeas
about: Chickpeas dried well and roasted until crunchy, tossed with smoked paprika, cumin and a squeeze of lemon. They are a salty-crunchy snack with **plant protein and fibre**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Rinse the chickpeas, then pat them completely dry in a clean towel. Dry chickpeas get crunchy.
Toss them with the oil, smoked paprika, cumin and salt on a baking tray and spread in one layer.
Roast, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp, about 25 minutes. Squeeze over the lemon juice and let them cool on the tray, where they keep crisping.
tip: Roast a double tray, cool completely, and keep in a jar for up to 3 days. They soften after that.

name: Apple slices with almonds
about: Crisp apple slices with a small handful of almonds and a pinch of cinnamon: sweet, crunchy and quick. The apple brings **fibre and vitamin C** and the almonds bring vitamin E and magnesium.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and scatter the cinnamon over the slices. Serve with the almonds.

name: Warm edamame with lime and chili
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese izakaya edamame
about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with lime juice, chili flakes and a few sesame seeds. They are a protein-rich snack with **folate and iron**, ready in five minutes.
steps: Heat the edamame in a microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water, covered, until steaming hot, about 2 minutes.
Drain, then toss with the lime juice, chili flakes, salt and sesame seeds.

name: Hard-cooked eggs with cherry tomatoes and cucumber
about: Firm hard-cooked eggs with sweet cherry tomatoes, cool cucumber and a pinch of smoked paprika. It is a simple plate with **protein and choline**.
steps: Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and cook for 11 minutes, so the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Wash and slice the tomatoes and cucumber. Halve the eggs and serve with the vegetables, sprinkled with the smoked paprika, salt and pepper.
tip: Cook a few extra eggs and keep them peeled in the fridge in a covered container for up to 3 days.
ingredients: hard-cooked until the yolks are firm

name: Lemony tuna and white bean bowl with spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan tonno e fagioli
about: Creamy white beans and flaked light tuna tossed in a lemon and garlic dressing over a big bed of spinach, with juicy cherry tomatoes, cucumber and pumpkin seeds. It needs no cooking at all, and the beans, tuna and spinach bring **protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomatoes, cucumber and parsley. Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, salt and pepper together in a bowl.
Add the beans, tuna, red onion, tomatoes and cucumber to the dressing and toss gently so the beans soak it up.
Pile the spinach into a bowl, spoon the bean and tuna mix on top and finish with the parsley and pumpkin seeds.
tip: Eat it the day it is made; to pack it for work, keep the spinach separate until lunch. Canned light tuna is a low-mercury choice. Keep any leftover tuna covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

name: Quinoa bowl with roast sweet potato, black beans and lime crema
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican and Tex-Mex burrito bowls
about: Fluffy quinoa under smoky roasted sweet potato and black beans, with a firm hard-cooked egg, crunchy red cabbage, creamy avocado, pumpkin seeds and a cool lime and cilantro crema. It makes **two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done**, and the sweet potato and beans bring vitamin A, fibre and iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the vegetables. Toss the sweet potato cubes on a tray with half the oil, the cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder and half the salt. Roast, turning once, until tender and browned at the edges, about 25 minutes.

Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa under cold water. Simmer it in a pot of water with a pinch of salt, covered, until the grains are tender and the little tails have popped, about 15 minutes. Drain and fluff with a fork.
Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 11 minutes, so the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water, then peel and halve them.
Stir the beans into the tray for the last 5 minutes so they warm through and pick up the spices.
Make the crema: stir the yogurt with the lime juice, half the cilantro and a pinch of salt. Toss the red cabbage and onion with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt.

Spoon half the quinoa into a bowl for tonight. Top with half the sweet potato and beans, an egg, half the cabbage and crema and the pumpkin seeds. Slice the avocado just before eating and scatter on with the rest of the cilantro.

Pack the rest for tomorrow with the egg, cabbage, crema and avocado kept separate. Cool the quinoa, sweet potato and beans within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep everything in the fridge up to 3 days. Reheat only the quinoa, sweet potato and beans, once, until steaming at 74 °C (165 °F), then add the cold toppings.
tip: Slice fresh avocado and add a squeeze of lime to the leftover bowl so it tastes freshly made.
ingredients: hard-cooked until the yolk is firm

name: Teriyaki-style salmon bowl with edamame, spinach and barley
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese teriyaki
about: Salmon glazed in a sticky ginger, soy and honey sauce over chewy barley, edamame, wilted spinach and carrot ribbons. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the edamame brings protein and folate.
steps: Rinse the barley and simmer it in plenty of water until tender but still chewy, about 25 minutes. Drain. Start this first.

Stir the soy sauce, honey, lemon juice, ginger and garlic together. Pour a spoonful over the salmon and leave it in the fridge while the barley cooks. Do not reuse that marinade; the rest is your sauce.

Heat the oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the salmon about 4 minutes on the first side and 3 on the other, until the centre reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and it flakes easily. Wash your hands, the board and the plate that held the raw fish.
Pour the sauce into the pan and let it bubble for 1 minute until it thickens and coats the salmon.
Heat the edamame with a splash of water in a covered pan until steaming, about 2 minutes, then add the spinach and wilt it for 1 minute.
Spoon the barley into a bowl, add the spinach, edamame and carrot ribbons, and lay the salmon on top. Finish with the sesame seeds.
tip: If you cook the barley the night before, chill it within 1 hour in a shallow container, use it the next day, and reheat it until steaming (74 °C).

name: Sesame-lime chicken and buckwheat bowl
inspiredBy: Inspired by Asian sesame noodle sauces
about: Seared chicken breast strips on nutty buckwheat with spinach, shredded red cabbage, carrot and cucumber, all coated in a creamy tahini, lime and ginger sauce. The chicken brings **protein** and the tahini brings **calcium and iron**, and the bowl is crunchy and bright.
steps: Simmer the buckwheat in water until tender, about 12 minutes. Drain and let the steam escape.
Meanwhile, whisk the tahini, lime juice, soy sauce, honey and ginger with a splash of warm water until creamy and pourable.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken strips, turning, until golden and cooked through at 74 °C (165 °F), about 7 minutes. Wash your hands, the knife and the board after the raw chicken.
Wash the vegetables. Toss the cabbage, carrot and cucumber with a spoonful of the sauce.
Spoon the buckwheat into a bowl over the spinach so it wilts a little, top with the vegetables and chicken, and drizzle with the rest of the sauce. Finish with the cilantro and sesame seeds.
tip: Swap the chicken for edamame or a hard-cooked egg if you like.

name: Lentil and roasted beet bowl with walnuts and yogurt-parsley sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European and Middle Eastern beet and lentil salads
about: Earthy green-brown lentils and sweet roasted beets over spinach, with a firm-cooked egg, toasted walnuts and a cool yogurt and parsley sauce. It makes **two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done**, and the lentils and beets bring iron and folate.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash and scrub the beets and cut them into small cubes so they cook quickly. Toss with half the oil and a pinch of salt and roast on a tray until tender and caramelised at the edges, about 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the lentils. Simmer them in plenty of water until tender but not mushy, about 22 minutes. Drain well.
Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 11 minutes, so the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water, then peel.

Whisk the rest of the oil with half the lemon juice, the garlic, a pinch of salt and the pepper. Toss the warm lentils and red onion in it. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Stir the yogurt with the parsley, the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Pile half the spinach into a bowl for tonight, top with half the lentils and beets and a halved egg, and finish with walnuts and yogurt sauce.

Pack the rest with the egg, spinach, sauce and walnuts kept separate. Cool the lentils and beets within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep everything in the fridge up to 3 days. Reheat only the lentils and beets, once, until steaming at 74 °C (165 °F), then add the cold toppings. They are also good cold.
tip: Beets stain, so use a tray you do not mind. Pre-cooked beets from the produce aisle also work and save the roasting.
ingredients: scrubbed and cut in small cubes
hard-cooked until the yolk is firm

name: Chicken shawarma-spiced bowl with chickpeas, roast carrots, barley and tahini sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine chicken shawarma
about: Chicken breast, chickpeas and carrots roasted together on one tray in warm shawarma spices, over chewy barley with a crunchy red cabbage and parsley slaw and a lemony tahini sauce. It makes **two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done**, and the chickpeas and tahini bring fibre, iron and copper.
steps: Wash your hands, then toss the chicken strips with a third of the oil, the garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, allspice, cinnamon, a splash of the lemon juice and half the salt in a bowl. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 15 minutes. Never reuse the marinade.
Rinse the barley and simmer it in plenty of water until tender but chewy, about 25 minutes. Drain.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the carrots and chickpeas with the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt on a lined tray and roast for 10 minutes. Add the chicken, spread everything in a single layer and roast, turning once, until the chicken is cooked through at 74 °C (165 °F) and the chickpeas are crisp at the edges, about 15 minutes more. Wash the bowl, board and your hands after the raw chicken.
Wash the cabbage, spinach and parsley. Toss the cabbage, onion, spinach and parsley with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Whisk the tahini with the rest of the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and enough cold water to make a pourable sauce.
Spoon half the barley into a bowl for tonight, top with half the chicken, chickpeas and carrots and some slaw, and drizzle with tahini sauce.

Pack the rest with the slaw and sauce kept separate. Cool the barley, chicken, chickpeas and carrots within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep everything in the fridge up to 3 days. Reheat only the barley, chicken, chickpeas and carrots, once, until steaming at 74 °C (165 °F), then add the cold slaw and sauce.
tip: Add a pinch of chili flakes to the tahini sauce for heat.

name: Lemon-herb trout bowl with roast squash, white beans and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian salsa verde
about: Flaky rainbow trout with a bright parsley, lemon and garlic sauce, over roasted butternut squash, quinoa, white beans and garlicky spinach with pumpkin seeds. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the squash and spinach bring vitamins A and K.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the vegetables. Toss the squash with a little of the oil and a pinch of salt and roast on a tray until tender and browned, about 25 minutes.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in water, covered, until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and fluff.
Make the sauce: stir the parsley, half the garlic, half the lemon juice and half the remaining oil together with a pinch of salt.

Pat the trout dry and season with salt and pepper. Add it to the oven tray for the last 8 to 10 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board after raw fish.

Meanwhile, heat the last of the oil in a skillet, add the rest of the garlic and the spinach with a splash of water and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes. Stir in the white beans to warm through, and the last of the lemon juice.
Spoon the quinoa into a bowl, top with the squash, spinach and beans and the trout, and spoon the sauce over. Finish with the pumpkin seeds.
tip: Cook a little extra quinoa and chill it within 1 hour for tomorrow's salmon bowl. Salmon or arctic char work in place of the trout.

name: Salmon and avocado bowl with quinoa, edamame and lime-ginger dressing
inspiredBy: Inspired by Hawaiian poke bowls, made with canned salmon
about: Flaked canned salmon on quinoa with creamy avocado, cool cucumber, grated carrot and edamame, under a bright lime and ginger dressing, with sesame seeds on top. The salmon brings **omega-3 and calcium from its soft bones**, and nothing needs cooking except the quinoa.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in water with a pinch of salt, covered, until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain, fluff and cool it for 5 minutes.
Whisk the lime juice, honey, ginger, oil and salt together. Heat the edamame in a covered bowl with a splash of water until steaming hot, about 2 minutes, then let it cool a little.
Wash the cucumber, carrot and cilantro. Spoon the quinoa into a bowl and arrange the salmon, edamame, cucumber, carrot and avocado on top.
Drizzle with the dressing and finish with the sesame seeds and cilantro.
tip: Use the extra quinoa from Friday's trout bowl, chilled within 1 hour and kept in the fridge. Keep the rest of an opened can of salmon covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days, for Sunday's cakes. Canned salmon with its soft bones is a good calcium source, and you will not taste them.

name: Gochujang beef and vegetable barley bowl
inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean bibimbap, with barley in place of rice
about: Savoury ground beef and quickly sautéed spinach, carrot and cabbage over chewy barley with edamame and a sweet-hot gochujang sauce. It makes **two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done**, and the spinach and edamame bring iron and folate while the beef brings zinc and B12.
steps: Rinse the barley and simmer it in plenty of water until tender but chewy, about 25 minutes. Drain and keep it covered.
Stir the gochujang with the honey and a spoonful of water to make the sauce.
Heat half the oil in a large skillet over high heat. Stir-fry the carrot and cabbage for 3 minutes, then add the spinach until just wilted. Tip onto a plate and season with a little of the sauce.

Add the rest of the oil to the pan, then the beef and garlic. Break up the beef and cook, stirring, until browned and no pink remains, about 6 minutes, reaching 71 °C (160 °F). Stir in the soy sauce. Wash your hands and the bowl that held the raw beef.

Add the edamame to the pan and stir until steaming hot, about 2 minutes. Spoon half the barley into a bowl for tonight and arrange half the vegetables, edamame and beef on top. Spoon over some gochujang sauce, add the cucumber and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

Pack the rest for tomorrow with the cucumber and gochujang sauce kept separate. Cool the barley, beef and cooked vegetables within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep them in the fridge up to 3 days. Reheat only those, once, until steaming at 74 °C (165 °F), then add the cucumber and sauce.
tip: Use less gochujang if you like it milder, and add more at the table.

name: Moroccan-spiced salmon cakes with buckwheat, roast carrots and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by North African spiced fish cakes
about: Golden baked cakes of canned salmon, oats and parsley with cumin, coriander and smoked paprika, served over nutty buckwheat and spinach with roast carrots, toasted walnuts and a lemon-garlic tahini sauce. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D** along with calcium from its soft bones, and the carrots bring vitamin A.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the carrot batons with half the oil and a pinch of salt on a large tray and roast for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, mix the salmon with the egg, oats, parsley, half the garlic, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, chili powder, cinnamon, salt, pepper and a squeeze of lemon. Let it sit for 5 minutes so the oats soak up the moisture, then shape into firm patties. Wash your hands after handling the raw egg.
Brush the patties with the rest of the oil and set them on the tray beside the carrots. Bake, turning once, until golden and cooked through at 74 °C (165 °F) in the centre, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the buckwheat in water until tender, about 12 minutes. Drain and stir in the spinach so it wilts in the heat.

Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes. Whisk the tahini with the rest of the garlic, the remaining lemon juice, a pinch of salt and enough cold water to make a pourable sauce.
Spoon the buckwheat and spinach into a bowl, add the carrots, salmon cakes and cucumber, and spoon the tahini sauce over. Finish with the walnuts.
tip: Pan-fry the cakes in a little oil instead if you want a crisper crust.

name: Oat and banana pancakes with warm strawberries and yogurt
about: Fluffy whole-wheat and oat pancakes, sweetened mostly by mashed banana (no egg), stacked with warm strawberries, Greek yogurt and sliced almonds. The oats and strawberries bring **fibre and vitamin C**, the yogurt brings protein, the almonds bring vitamin E and the chia brings plant omega-3.
steps: Mash the banana in a bowl. Stir in about 100 ml of water per portion, then the flour, oats, chia, baking powder and cinnamon until just combined, with a few small lumps. Rest the batter 5 minutes while the oats and chia soften.
Warm the strawberries with the maple syrup in a small pot over medium heat, stirring now and then, until they are soft and juicy and steaming, about 4 minutes. Keep them warm.

Brush a non-stick pan with the oil and heat over medium. Spoon in the batter in rounds and cook until bubbles form and the edges look set, about 2 minutes, then flip and cook another 2 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Stack the pancakes, spoon over the warm berries and the yogurt, and scatter the almonds on top.
tip: Mix the dry ingredients the night before and the batter takes 2 minutes in the morning.

name: Avocado and firm egg on whole-grain toast with tomato and spinach
about: Mashed avocado with lemon and chili flakes on whole-wheat toast, topped with a fried egg cooked until the yolk is completely firm, tomato and baby spinach. The avocado brings **healthy fats and vitamin E**, and the egg brings protein and choline.
steps: Wash the avocado, tomato and spinach. Halve and stone the avocado, scoop it into a bowl and mash it with the lemon juice, the chili flakes and the salt. Slice the tomato.

Toast the bread. Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, crack in the eggs and cook, covered, until the whites are set and the yolks are completely firm, about 5 minutes, turning them once if you like. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Spread the avocado on the toast, lay on the spinach and tomato, top with the firm eggs and scatter the feta over.
tip: Add a squeeze of lime and a little chopped cilantro for a fresher bite.

name: Savoury oats with garlicky spinach, tomatoes and a yogurt swirl
about: Creamy oats simmered in low-sodium broth with garlic and oregano, folded with wilted spinach and tomatoes and finished with a swirl of Greek yogurt and toasted walnuts. The oats and spinach bring **iron, magnesium and fibre**, and no eggs are needed.
steps: Wash the spinach and tomato. Dice the tomato.
Warm the oil in a small pot over medium heat and cook the garlic and oregano for 30 seconds, then add the tomato and cook until it starts to break down, about 3 minutes.
Add the broth and oats. Simmer, stirring often, until the oats are creamy, about 6 minutes, adding a splash of water if they get too thick. Stir in the spinach for the last minute, until wilted.
Spoon into a bowl, swirl in the yogurt, and top with the walnuts and a grind of pepper.
tip: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.

name: White bean and wilted greens toast with lemon, tomato and walnuts
about: Warm, garlicky smashed white beans and wilted spinach piled on whole-wheat toast with fresh tomato, lemon and toasted walnuts and a little feta. The beans bring **fibre, folate and protein** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3, so there is plenty of substance without an egg.
steps: Wash the spinach and tomato, and dice the tomato.

Warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and chili flakes for 30 seconds, then add the beans, tomato and salt. Cook, mashing about half the beans with the back of a spoon, until hot and thick, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook until just wilted, about 1 minute, then add the lemon juice.
Toast the bread, pile the warm beans and greens on top, and scatter the feta and walnuts over.
tip: Mash the beans with a little lemon zest for a brighter flavour.

name: Ranchero tofu scramble with black beans on corn tortillas
inspiredBy: Mexican huevos rancheros, with tofu and beans in place of the eggs
about: Crumbled tofu simmered with a quick ranchero sauce of tomato, red pepper, onion, garlic, oregano and a little chili, with black beans, spooned onto warm corn tortillas with lime and cilantro. The tofu and beans bring **protein and some calcium** with no eggs.
steps: Wash the tomato, pepper and cilantro. Dice the tomato, onion and pepper, and chop the cilantro.
Warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, oregano and chili flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato, the crumbled tofu, the beans and the salt. Cook, stirring, until the tomato breaks down and the tofu is hot and lightly golden, about 6 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, about 20 seconds a side. Spoon the scramble onto them and finish with the lime juice and cilantro.
tip: Add a spoonful of salsa or a little more chili for more heat.

name: Turkish-style menemen with firm eggs, peppers and whole-grain toast
inspiredBy: Turkish menemen, with the eggs cooked fully firm
about: Eggs stirred into slowly cooked tomatoes, red pepper and onion until completely set, with parsley, feta and Aleppo pepper, scooped up with whole-wheat toast and a handful of spinach. The egg and tomato bring **choline and vitamin C**.
steps: Wash the tomato, pepper, spinach and parsley. Dice the tomato, pepper and onion.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 6 minutes. Add the tomato, Aleppo pepper and salt and simmer until thick and glossy, about 8 minutes, stirring in the spinach for the last minute.
Beat the eggs lightly and stir them in. Cook, stirring gently, until the eggs are completely set and the yolks are firm, with no liquid left, about 4 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Scatter with the feta and parsley and serve straight from the pan with the toast.
tip: Serve from the pan with extra bread for scooping.
ingredients: or a pinch of chili flakes

name: Canned salmon and egg toast with cucumber, parsley and strawberries
about: Flaked canned salmon (bones and all) mashed with Greek yogurt, lemon and parsley on whole-wheat toast, topped with sliced hard-cooked egg and crisp cucumber, with a few strawberries on the side. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, its soft bones bring calcium and the egg brings choline.
steps: Boil the egg in its shell for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it under cold water, peel it and slice it. Wash your hands after handling the raw egg. Wash the cucumber, parsley and strawberries, slice the cucumber thinly and chop the parsley.
In a bowl, mash the salmon with the yogurt, lemon juice, parsley and pepper. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
Toast the bread. Spread with the salmon mixture and top with the cucumber and the sliced egg. Serve with the strawberries.
tip: Rub the toast with half a garlic clove for extra flavour.

name: Warm red lentil and roasted tomato bowl with canned salmon, spinach and a firm egg
about: Red lentils simmered with onion, garlic and cumin until thick and spoonable, piled in a bowl with oven-roasted tomatoes, wilted spinach, flaked canned salmon and a chopped firm hard-cooked egg, finished with lemon and almonds. The salmon and egg bring **omega-3, B12 and choline**, the lentils bring iron and folate, and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the tomatoes, spinach, carrot and parsley. Halve the tomatoes, toss them on a tray with half the oil and a pinch of the salt, and roast until soft and browned at the edges, about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute, then the lentils and about 3 times their volume of water. Simmer, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and thick, about 15 minutes, adding the rest of the salt at the end.
Boil the egg in its shell for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it under cold water, peel it and chop it. Wash your hands after handling the raw egg.

Stir the spinach into the hot lentils until wilted. Spoon into a bowl, top with the roasted tomatoes, the grated carrot, the flaked salmon and the egg, then finish with the lemon juice, parsley and almonds. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
If packing it, keep the lentils and toppings in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Cook the lentils the night before; cool within 1 hour in a shallow container and reheat until steaming.

name: Chicken and black bean chilaquiles bake with lime kale slaw
inspiredBy: Mexican chilaquiles, baked with chicken and beans instead of fried with eggs
about: Crisp-baked corn tortilla wedges tossed in a smoky chicken, black bean and tomato sauce, then topped with a lime-cilantro kale and carrot slaw. A brunch classic turned into an easy weeknight dinner. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done. The beans and chicken bring **protein and iron**, the lime and kale bring vitamin C and some calcium.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the kale, carrot and cilantro. Slice the kale very thinly, grate the carrot and massage both with the lime juice, half the cilantro and a pinch of the salt until the kale softens. Keep the slaw in the fridge.
Cut all the tortillas into wedges, toss with a little of the oil and bake on a tray until crisp, about 8 minutes. Once cool, keep half in a sealed container for tomorrow.
Warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and chili flakes for 1 minute.

Add the chicken, the tomatoes and a splash of water, and simmer, stirring now and then, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the sauce is thick, about 12 minutes. Stir in the beans and the rest of the salt and cook 3 minutes. Wash your hands, knife and board after handling the raw chicken.
Toss half the sauce with the warm tortilla wedges so they soften at the edges but keep some crunch, top with the slaw and the rest of the cilantro, and eat right away.

Cool the second portion of sauce within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep it in the fridge with the slaw separate. Tomorrow, reheat the sauce until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F), and toss it with the saved wedges.
tip: Leave out the chili flakes for a milder version.
ingredients: crushed by hand, with its juice
washed, stems removed, very thinly sliced

name: Maple-lime salmon with roasted broccoli, carrots, kale and lemony bulgur
about: A salmon fillet glazed with maple, lime, garlic and smoked paprika, roasted on the same tray as garlicky broccoli, carrots and crisp kale and served over fluffy bulgur. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, the carrots bring vitamin A and the kale brings some calcium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the broccoli, carrots and kale. Cut the broccoli and carrots up and tear the kale off its stems. Toss the broccoli and carrots on a tray with half the oil, half the garlic and a pinch of the salt, and start roasting.

Stir the maple syrup, lime juice, smoked paprika, the rest of the garlic and a pinch of salt in a small bowl. After 8 minutes, pat the salmon dry, set it on the tray with the vegetables, scatter the kale around it and brush the fish with the glaze. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Roast for 12 to 14 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and the vegetable edges are browned.
Meanwhile, rinse the bulgur and simmer it in twice its volume of water with a pinch of salt, covered, for about 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Fluff with the lemon juice and the parsley.
Serve the salmon and vegetables over the bulgur. Buy fresh salmon the day you cook it, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge.
tip: Spoon any glaze left on the tray over the bulgur.
ingredients: skin-on or skinless fillet, bought fresh

name: Roasted pepper, broccoli and tofu toasts with hummus, feta and a firm egg
about: Two slices of whole-wheat toast spread with hummus and piled with roasted red pepper, onion and broccoli, golden roasted tofu, baby spinach, feta and sliced hard-cooked egg. The tofu, egg and hummus bring **protein, choline and some calcium**, with a squeeze of lemon to brighten it.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the pepper, broccoli and spinach. Slice the pepper and onion and cut the broccoli into small florets.

Toss the vegetables and the tofu cubes on a tray with the oil, cumin and salt. Roast, shaking once, until the vegetables are browned at the edges and the tofu is golden, about 22 minutes. Meanwhile, boil the egg in its shell for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it under cold water, peel it and slice it. Wash your hands after handling the raw egg.
Toast the bread and spread with the hummus. Top with the spinach, the roasted vegetables and tofu, the sliced egg, the feta and a squeeze of lemon.
tip: Roast a double tray on Sunday and use half in a bowl later in the week.

name: Baked egg and spinach strata with red pepper and feta, and a crisp cucumber salad
inspiredBy: a North American breakfast strata, with a yogurt custard, spinach, red pepper and feta
about: Cubes of whole-wheat bread soaked in an egg and yogurt custard with spinach, red pepper and feta, baked until the centre is completely set and the eggs are firm all the way through, served with a cucumber and tomato salad. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, the spinach and pepper bring vitamins A and C.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and oil a baking dish with a little of the oil. Wash the pepper, spinach, cucumber, tomato and parsley. Cut the bread into small cubes.

Warm the rest of the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in the spinach until wilted. Tip everything into the dish with the bread cubes and the feta.
Whisk the eggs with the yogurt, salt and pepper and pour over, pressing the bread down so it soaks. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.

Bake until the centre is completely set, a knife comes out clean and the middle reaches 74 °C (165 °F), about 25 minutes (30 to 35 in a deeper dish). The eggs must be firm all the way through, with no wet egg left.
Toss the cucumber, tomato and parsley with the lemon juice and serve alongside slices of the strata.
Cool the second portion within 1 hour, wrap it and keep it in the fridge with the salad separate. Eat it tomorrow, cold or warmed until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F). Do not freeze.
tip: Assemble it in the morning, keep it covered in the fridge and bake it straight from the fridge after work, adding about 10 minutes.

name: Smoky black bean and sweet potato burgers on toast with kale slaw
about: Pan-seared patties of black beans, sweet potato, oats and walnuts in smoked paprika and cumin, served open-face on toasted whole-wheat bread with feta and a lime-yogurt kale slaw. The beans and sweet potato bring **fibre and vitamin A**, with protein from the beans, walnuts and feta.
steps: Wash the sweet potato and prick it all over. Microwave until very soft, about 6 minutes, then scoop the flesh into a bowl. Wash the kale and carrot.
Mash the sweet potato with the black beans, leaving some texture. Stir in the oats, walnuts, onion, paprika, cumin and salt, then shape into patties and chill for 10 minutes.
Massage the thinly sliced kale and the carrot with the lime juice and a little of the oil until the kale softens, then stir in the yogurt for the slaw.
Warm the rest of the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the patties until crisp and golden and hot through, about 5 minutes a side.
Toast the bread, set a patty on each slice, and top with the feta and slaw. Cool any extra patties within 1 hour and use them within 2 days, reheated until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Chill the patties longer if the mixture feels soft.
ingredients: for the pan and the slaw
washed, stems removed, very thinly sliced

name: Carrot, red lentil and ginger soup with walnuts and whole-grain toast
about: A silky soup of carrots, red lentils, ginger and cumin, finished with lemon, a yogurt swirl and toasted walnuts, with a slice of whole-wheat toast on the side. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done. The lentils bring **iron, folate and protein**, and the carrots bring vitamin A.
steps: Wash the carrots and chop them. Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the carrots, lentils, broth and enough water to cover everything. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, until the lentils and carrots are completely soft, about 22 minutes.
Blend until smooth with a stick blender (or leave it a little chunky). Stir in the lemon juice and the salt.
Serve in a bowl with a swirl of yogurt and the walnuts on top, with the toast on the side.

Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep it in the fridge without the toast or yogurt, and use it tomorrow. Reheat the soup to 74 °C (165 °F) and add the yogurt cold. It also freezes: cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze.
tip: A pinch of chili flakes on top gives it a little heat.

name: Braised beef with white beans, potatoes, carrots and spinach
about: Beef chuck and onions braised slowly with tomato and thyme until tender, with white beans, small potatoes, carrots and spinach stirred in at the end. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's dinner is done. The beef and beans bring **iron and zinc**, with vitamin C from the tomato.
steps: Pat the beef dry. Warm the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, about 6 minutes, moving it to a clean plate. Wash your hands, knife and board after handling the raw beef.
In the same pot, cook the onion until golden, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.

Return the beef, add the tomatoes, broth and enough water to just cover, plus the bay leaf and salt. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently until the beef is tender and reaches at least 71 °C (160 °F), about 75 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrots and cook until tender, about 15 minutes, then the beans for 5 minutes and the spinach for the last 2 minutes. Remove the bay leaf and finish with the lemon juice.

Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep it in the fridge. Use it tomorrow, reheated to 74 °C (165 °F). It also freezes: cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze.
tip: In a pressure cooker the beef is tender in 35 minutes.
ingredients: crushed by hand, with its juice

name: Hummus with cucumber, carrot and red pepper sticks
about: A scoop of hummus with crunchy cucumber, carrot and red pepper for dipping. The chickpeas bring **fibre and protein**.
steps: Wash the vegetables, cut them into sticks and serve with the hummus. If packing it, keep it chilled and eat it the same day.
ingredients: washed, seeded and cut in sticks

name: Strawberry and almond yogurt bowl with toasted oats and chia
about: Thick Greek yogurt with sliced strawberries, chopped almonds, toasted oats and a pinch of chia. A fruit-and-nut bowl that brings **protein and calcium**.
steps: Wash, hull and slice the strawberries. Toast the oats in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the strawberries, then the almonds, oats and chia.

name: Orange and almonds
about: A juicy orange with a small handful of almonds. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Serve with the almonds.

name: Sliced banana with cinnamon-toasted walnuts
about: A sliced banana with walnuts toasted in a dry pan with a pinch of cinnamon. It brings **potassium** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Toast the walnuts with the cinnamon in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes, until fragrant. Peel and slice the banana and scatter the warm walnuts over.

name: Strawberries with almonds
about: Fresh strawberries with a small handful of almonds. The strawberries bring **vitamin C** and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash and hull the strawberries and serve them with the almonds.

name: Paprika roasted chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crunchy with smoked paprika and a little olive oil. They bring **fibre, protein and iron**.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Toss the dried chickpeas with the oil, paprika and salt.
Roast on a tray, shaking once, until crisp, about 25 minutes. Cool a few minutes before eating.

name: Tomato, cucumber and feta cup with olive oil
about: Diced tomato and cucumber with crumbled feta, a drizzle of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon. It brings **vitamin C and some calcium**.
steps: Wash the tomato and cucumber and dice them. Toss with the feta, oil and lemon juice.

name: Hummus and tomato toast
about: A slice of whole-wheat toast with hummus and sliced tomato. The hummus brings **fibre and protein**.
steps: Toast the bread, spread with the hummus and top with the sliced tomato.

name: Walnut and almond mix with cinnamon
about: A small handful of walnuts and almonds with a pinch of cinnamon. The walnuts bring plant omega-3 and the almonds bring **vitamin E**.
steps: Mix the nuts with the cinnamon and serve.

name: Greek yogurt with banana, walnuts and cinnamon
about: Thick Greek yogurt with sliced banana, chopped walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. It brings **protein and calcium**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Slice the banana into a bowl, spoon the yogurt over and top with the walnuts and cinnamon.

name: Oat and banana pancakes with warm strawberries and yogurt
about: Fluffy whole-wheat and oat pancakes, sweetened mostly by mashed banana (no egg), stacked with warm strawberries, Greek yogurt and sliced almonds. The oats and strawberries bring **fibre and vitamin C**, the yogurt brings protein, the almonds bring vitamin E and the chia brings plant omega-3.
steps: Mash the banana in a bowl. Stir in about 100 ml of water per portion, then the flour, oats, chia, baking powder and cinnamon until just combined, with a few small lumps. Rest the batter 5 minutes while the oats and chia soften.
Warm the strawberries with the maple syrup in a small pot over medium heat, stirring now and then, until they are soft and juicy and steaming, about 4 minutes. Keep them warm.

Brush a non-stick pan with the oil and heat over medium. Spoon in the batter in rounds and cook until bubbles form and the edges look set, about 2 minutes, then flip and cook another 2 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Stack the pancakes, spoon over the warm berries and the yogurt, and scatter the almonds on top.
tip: Mix the dry ingredients the night before and the batter takes 2 minutes in the morning.

name: Avocado and firm egg on whole-grain toast with tomato and spinach
about: Mashed avocado with lemon and chili flakes on whole-wheat toast, topped with a fried egg cooked until the yolk is completely firm, tomato and baby spinach. The avocado brings **healthy fats and vitamin E**, and the egg brings protein and choline.
steps: Wash the avocado, tomato and spinach. Halve and stone the avocado, scoop it into a bowl and mash it with the lemon juice, the chili flakes and the salt. Slice the tomato.

Toast the bread. Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, crack in the eggs and cook, covered, until the whites are set and the yolks are completely firm, about 5 minutes, turning them once if you like. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Spread the avocado on the toast, lay on the spinach and tomato, top with the firm eggs and scatter the feta over.
tip: Add a squeeze of lime and a little chopped cilantro for a fresher bite.

name: Turkish-style menemen with firm eggs, peppers and whole-grain toast
inspiredBy: Turkish menemen, with the eggs cooked fully firm
about: Eggs stirred into slowly cooked tomatoes, red pepper and onion until completely set, with parsley, feta and Aleppo pepper, scooped up with whole-wheat toast and a handful of spinach. The egg and tomato bring **choline and vitamin C**.
steps: Wash the tomato, pepper, spinach and parsley. Dice the tomato, pepper and onion.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 6 minutes. Add the tomato, Aleppo pepper and salt and simmer until thick and glossy, about 8 minutes, stirring in the spinach for the last minute.
Beat the eggs lightly and stir them in. Cook, stirring gently, until the eggs are completely set and the yolks are firm, with no liquid left, about 4 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Scatter with the feta and parsley and serve straight from the pan with the toast.
tip: Serve from the pan with extra bread for scooping.
ingredients: or a pinch of chili flakes

name: Smoky black bean and sweet potato burgers on toast with kale slaw
about: Pan-seared patties of black beans, sweet potato, oats and walnuts in smoked paprika and cumin, served open-face on toasted whole-wheat bread with feta and a lime-yogurt kale slaw. The beans and sweet potato bring **fibre and vitamin A**, with protein from the beans, walnuts and feta.
steps: Wash the sweet potato and prick it all over. Microwave until very soft, about 6 minutes, then scoop the flesh into a bowl. Wash the kale and carrot.
Mash the sweet potato with the black beans, leaving some texture. Stir in the oats, walnuts, onion, paprika, cumin and salt, then shape into patties and chill for 10 minutes.
Massage the thinly sliced kale and the carrot with the lime juice and a little of the oil until the kale softens, then stir in the yogurt for the slaw.
Warm the rest of the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the patties until crisp and golden and hot through, about 5 minutes a side.
Toast the bread, set a patty on each slice, and top with the feta and slaw. Cool any extra patties within 1 hour and use them within 2 days, reheated until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Chill the patties longer if the mixture feels soft.
ingredients: for the pan and the slaw
washed, stems removed, very thinly sliced

name: Chicken and black bean chilaquiles bake with lime kale slaw
inspiredBy: Mexican chilaquiles, baked with chicken and beans instead of fried with eggs
about: Crisp-baked corn tortilla wedges tossed in a smoky chicken, black bean and tomato sauce, then topped with a lime-cilantro kale and carrot slaw. A brunch classic turned into an easy weeknight dinner. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done. The beans and chicken bring **protein and iron**, the lime and kale bring vitamin C and some calcium.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the kale, carrot and cilantro. Slice the kale very thinly, grate the carrot and massage both with the lime juice, half the cilantro and a pinch of the salt until the kale softens. Keep the slaw in the fridge.
Cut all the tortillas into wedges, toss with a little of the oil and bake on a tray until crisp, about 8 minutes. Once cool, keep half in a sealed container for tomorrow.
Warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and chili flakes for 1 minute.

Add the chicken, the tomatoes and a splash of water, and simmer, stirring now and then, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the sauce is thick, about 12 minutes. Stir in the beans and the rest of the salt and cook 3 minutes. Wash your hands, knife and board after handling the raw chicken.
Toss half the sauce with the warm tortilla wedges so they soften at the edges but keep some crunch, top with the slaw and the rest of the cilantro, and eat right away.

Cool the second portion of sauce within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep it in the fridge with the slaw separate. Tomorrow, reheat the sauce until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F), and toss it with the saved wedges.
tip: Leave out the chili flakes for a milder version.
ingredients: crushed by hand, with its juice
washed, stems removed, very thinly sliced

name: Chicken and red lentil dhansak with onion bulgur and a cucumber salad
inspiredBy: Parsi chicken dhansak, with lime and a little maple in place of tamarind and jaggery, and bulgur in place of brown rice
about: Chicken thighs simmered with red lentils, tomato, ginger and warm spices until the lentils melt into a thick, gently sweet and sour sauce, with spinach and fenugreek stirred through. It comes with golden-onion bulgur and a crunchy cucumber salad. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done. The lentils and spinach bring **iron, folate and fibre**, and the lime and tomato help your body absorb the iron.
steps: Wash the spinach, cucumber and cilantro. Rinse the lentils and the bulgur. Thinly slice the onion and set a small handful aside for the salad.

Warm half the oil in a small pot over medium heat and cook a third of the sliced onion until deep golden, about 8 minutes. Add the bulgur, a pinch of the salt and twice its volume of water, cover and simmer until the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes.

Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the rest of the onion until soft and golden, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, cardamom and chili flakes and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the tomatoes, the chicken, the lentils, the rest of the salt and about 3 times the lentils' volume of water. Simmer, stirring often so the lentils don't catch, until they collapse into a thick sauce and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F), about 20 minutes. Wash your hands, knife and board after handling the raw chicken.
Stir in the spinach and the crumbled fenugreek leaves until the spinach wilts, then the maple syrup and most of the lime juice. Taste: it should be gently sweet, sour and warm.
Toss the cucumber with the reserved onion, the cilantro and the last of the lime juice. Serve the dhansak over the onion bulgur with the cucumber salad on the side.

Cool the second portion of dhansak and bulgur within 1 hour in separate shallow containers, keep them in the fridge with the salad separate, and use them tomorrow. Reheat the dhansak and bulgur until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F), adding a splash of water.
tip: Freeze the dhansak without the bulgur: cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).
ingredients: crushed by hand, with its juice

name: Lemony canned salmon with Aleppo pepper on tomato and cucumber slices
