Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until the barley is tender and the chicken is 74 °C (165 °F) at the thickest part, near the bone.
Lift out the drumsticks, pull the meat off the bones in chunks and return it to the pot with the washed spinach. Simmer for 2 minutes more. Add the lemon juice and the dill.

Cool the second portion within 1 hour, since it holds cooked barley, in a shallow container in the fridge. Eat within 3 days, reheated until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F); add a splash of water, since the barley thickens it. To carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
tip: To freeze, cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Chicken thighs work as well as drumsticks.
ingredients: weight of the meat off the bone; buy about 1.4 times this in bone-in drumsticks, skin removed

name: Ginger-mustard salmon with crispy chickpeas, potatoes and broccoli
about: A salmon fillet brushed with Dijon, ginger and lemon and roasted on one tray with golden chickpeas, baby potatoes, broccoli and wilted spinach, with a fresh cilantro and lemon drizzle. Quick and bright, with **omega-3 and vitamin D** from the salmon and **iron and fibre** from the chickpeas.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the vegetables. Toss the potatoes with half the oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan and roast for 10 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and the smoked paprika to the tray with a pinch of salt and roast 5 minutes more. Stir the mustard, garlic, ginger, half the lemon juice and the pepper together.

Add the broccoli to the tray, push everything aside and lay the salmon on it. Brush the salmon with the mustard glaze. Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw fish.
Meanwhile, stir the cilantro with a squeeze of the remaining lemon and a pinch of salt.
Toss the vegetables with the rest of the oil and lemon and fold in the washed spinach so it wilts in the heat. Serve the salmon on top and spoon the cilantro and lemon over it.
tip: Green beans work in place of the broccoli too.

name: Chicken, sweet potato and lentil curry
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian chicken curries and East African coconut curries
about: Diced chicken breast in a gently spiced coconut and tomato sauce with sweet potato, lentils, spinach and kale, finished with lemon and cilantro. Creamy without being heavy, it makes tomorrow's lunch and brings **vitamin A, fibre and iron**.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and cumin and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes. Wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken.

Add the sweet potato, tomatoes, coconut milk, salt and 150 ml water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sweet potato is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F).

Stir in the lentils, the washed spinach and the kale and cook for 4 minutes, until the lentils are hot and the greens are wilted. Stir in the garam masala and finish with the lemon juice and cilantro.

Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container and refrigerate. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). To carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack and reheat it before eating.
tip: Add a pinch of chili for more heat. To freeze, cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Roast chicken legs with carrots, parsnips and potatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by a British Sunday roast
about: Chicken drumsticks and thighs roasted over carrots, parsnips and potatoes with garlic, thyme and lemon until the juices run into the vegetables, with broccoli and kale added for the last minutes. The Sunday-style roast, with **vitamin A, potassium and protein**. It makes tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the vegetables. Toss the carrots, parsnips, potatoes, onion and garlic on a large pan, or two, with half the oil, the thyme and half the salt. Roast for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, pull the skin off the drumsticks and thighs. Rub them with the mustard, the rest of the oil, the lemon juice, pepper and the remaining salt. Wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water.

Nestle the chicken among the vegetables, not on top of them, and roast for 25 minutes. Add the broccoli and kale, turn the vegetables over and roast 10 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) at the thickest part, near the bone, and the juices run clear.
Rest for 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over everything.

Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). To carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack and reheat it before eating.
tip: Use two pans so nothing steams. A spoonful of plain yogurt with the pan juices is good on the side.
ingredients: weight of the meat off the bone; buy about 1.3 times this in bone-in thighs, skin pulled off
weight of the meat off the bone; buy about 1.4 times this in bone-in drumsticks, skin pulled off

name: Za'atar trout with lentil, cucumber and tomato salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine flavours
about: Rainbow trout fillet rubbed with za'atar and lemon and roasted, served over a cool lentil salad with cucumber, tomato and dill and a lemony yogurt drizzle. Fresh and light, with **omega-3, protein and fibre**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Rub the trout with half the oil, half the lemon juice and the za'atar and set it on a lined pan. Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw fish.
Meanwhile, wash the cucumber, tomatoes and dill. Toss the lentils with the cucumber, tomatoes, onion, most of the dill, the rest of the oil, a little lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Whisk the yogurt with the remaining lemon juice and a spoonful of water until pourable.
Serve the trout on the lentil salad and drizzle with the yogurt. Scatter the last of the dill over.

name: Apple slices with almonds
about: Crisp apple slices with a small handful of almonds: sweet, crunchy and quick. The apple brings **fibre and vitamin C** and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

name: Apple slices with walnuts and cinnamon
about: Apple slices with walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon. The apple brings **fibre and vitamin C**, and the walnuts bring omega-3 fats and crunch.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and sprinkle with the cinnamon. Serve with the walnuts.

name: Edamame with lemon and chili
about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with lemon juice, a pinch of chili and a little salt. A savoury snack with **plant protein, folate, iron and choline**.
steps: Put the frozen edamame in a pot of boiling water or a covered bowl in the microwave for 3 to 4 minutes, until heated through and steaming hot.
Drain and toss with the lemon juice, chili and salt. Serve warm.

name: Orange and banana with cinnamon
about: Juicy orange segments and banana slices with a pinch of cinnamon, a light fruit snack. The fruit brings **vitamin C, folate and potassium**.
steps: Peel the orange and break it into segments. Peel and slice the banana, and sprinkle both with the cinnamon.

name: Dried apricots and almonds
about: A small chewy and crunchy mix of dried apricots and almonds. The apricots bring **vitamin A and potassium**, and the almonds bring magnesium and vitamin E.
steps: Slice the apricots, toss with the almonds and eat from a small bowl.

name: Banana with walnuts
about: A banana with a small handful of walnuts: filling, sweet and crunchy. The banana brings **potassium and fibre**, and the walnuts bring omega-3 fats.
steps: Peel the banana and serve with the walnuts.

name: Orange and almonds
about: A juicy orange with a small handful of almonds. The orange brings **vitamin C and folate**, and the almonds bring vitamin E and some calcium.
steps: Peel the orange, break it into segments and serve with the almonds.

name: Smoky roasted chickpeas
about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with smoked paprika and a squeeze of lemon. A savoury snack with **fibre and plant protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the chickpeas with the oil, smoked paprika and salt on a pan.
Roast for 20 minutes, shaking once, until golden and crisp. Squeeze the lemon over and let them cool for 5 minutes; they crisp more as they cool.
They are best within a couple of hours. Once cool, keep any leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 3 days, and crisp them again in a hot oven or dry pan for 3 to 4 minutes.

name: Greek yogurt with berries and walnuts
about: Thick yogurt with thawed berries and toasted walnuts. Protein, **calcium and omega-3 fats** in a few minutes.
steps: Thaw the berries in a bowl in the fridge or in the microwave for 30 seconds.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the berries and scatter the walnuts over.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first.

name: Brown rice and barley congee with shrimp, bok choy and crushed peanuts
inspiredBy: Cantonese shrimp congee (har juk), made quickly from cooked grains and topped with crushed peanuts as in peanut congee
about: A soft and creamy rice porridge with sweet shrimp, ginger and bok choy, topped with crushed roasted peanuts, scallion and a few drops of sesame oil. It is built from the rice and barley you cooked on Sunday: simmer the base the night before, and in the morning it takes 5 minutes. The **shrimp carry the protein** and the peanuts add vitamin E and crunch.
steps: The night before, while dinner cooks, put the rice and barley in a small pot with the sliced ginger and about 3 parts water to 1 part cooked grain by volume. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to a steady simmer.

Simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then and pressing some of the grains against the side of the pot, until the grains have broken down and the congee is soft and creamy. Cool it and keep it in the fridge.
In the morning, reheat the base with a splash of water until it bubbles. Crush the peanuts roughly with the flat of a knife. Slice the scallion.
Toss the shrimp with the soy sauce and a pinch of white pepper and stir them into the congee. Cook for 2 minutes, until pink and curled.
Stir in the bok choy and the salt and cook for 1 minute, just until the leaves are bright green.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the scallion, the peanuts and a few drops of sesame oil.
tip: Congee is the great leftover rescuer. Any cooked rice and a handful of greens will do, and a spoon of rinsed zha cai on top is very Cantonese.
ingredients: peeled and deveined, cut into pieces
about a 2 cm piece, thinly sliced

name: Whole-wheat scallion egg pancake with cucumber and warm soy milk
inspiredBy: Chinese street-cart egg pancakes (jianbing), made with whole-wheat flour and sweet bean sauce
about: A thin, chewy whole-wheat crepe with scallion in the batter, two eggs spread over the top and a smear of sweet bean sauce, rolled up around crunchy cucumber. A glass of warm soy milk goes alongside, the way it is sold at breakfast stands. The **whole wheat and eggs keep you full**, and the soy milk adds calcium.
steps: Whisk the flour with about twice as much water as flour by weight and the salt, until you have a thin, pourable batter like cream. Stir in half the scallion, finely sliced, and let it rest for 5 minutes while you get everything else ready.
Cut the cucumber into thin matchsticks. Stir the sweet bean sauce with a spoonful of water to loosen it into a spreadable sauce.

Warm a non-stick pan over medium heat and brush it with a little of the oil. Pour in the batter and tilt the pan to spread it as thin as a crepe. Cook for about 2 minutes, until the top looks dry and the edges lift. Flip it over.

Crack the eggs onto the pancake, break the yolks with your spatula and spread the egg out in a thin layer. Scatter on the rest of the scallion and the sesame seeds, and cook for another minute, until the egg is just set.
Spread the sweet bean sauce over the egg, lay the cucumber along one side and roll the pancake up tightly. Cut it in half.
Warm the soy milk in a small pot or in the microwave and serve it alongside.
tip: Add a few drops of chili oil under the cucumber if you like jianbing hot.

name: Millet and sweet potato porridge with a soy-simmered egg and tofu
inspiredBy: Northern Chinese xiaomi zhou, the millet porridge eaten with an egg and a crisp pickle on the side
about: A golden, creamy millet porridge cooked with chunks of sweet potato, topped with toasted walnuts and served with a firm soy-simmered egg, tofu and a tangy quick pickle of daikon. It is a slow weekend breakfast that makes two bowls, so Sunday morning is just a reheat. The millet and sweet potato bring **fibre and vitamin A**.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, until the whites and yolks are both firm. Cool them under cold water and peel.

In a small pot, bring the soy sauce, about 150 ml (⅔ cup) of water and the ginger to a gentle simmer. Add the tofu and simmer for 10 minutes. Slip the peeled eggs into the warm liquid and leave them there while the porridge cooks.
While the eggs and tofu sit, rinse the millet in a sieve until the water runs clear. Put it in a pot with the sweet potato and about 8 times as much water as millet by volume. Bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low and simmer, partly covered, for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the millet is soft and the porridge is thick and creamy. The sweet potato will mostly melt into it.
Toss the daikon sticks with the black vinegar and a few drops of sesame oil, and let them sit while the porridge cooks. They should be crisp and tangy. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Serve a portion of porridge with a halved egg, some of the tofu and a spoonful of the soy liquid, the pickle on the side and the walnuts on top.
Keep the second portion of porridge in the fridge. It thickens overnight, so loosen it with a splash of water when you reheat it. The eggs and tofu keep well in their liquid.
tip: A strip of mandarin peel in the tofu's liquid is lovely.
ingredients: calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate, cubed

name: Tomato and egg stir-fry over brown rice and barley
inspiredBy: Chinese tomato and egg stir-fry (fanqie chao dan)
about: The most-loved home dish in China: three tender egg curds, cooked through, folded into a jammy, sweet-sharp tomato sauce, spooned over rice. It is ready in about 20 minutes and is wonderful hot or at room temperature. The **tomatoes bring vitamin C and potassium**, and the eggs make it a proper lunch.
steps: Cut the tomatoes into wedges, slice the scallion whites and greens separately and mince the garlic. Beat the eggs with the salt and a few drops of sesame oil. Reheat the rice and barley.

Heat half the oil in a wok or wide pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Pour in the eggs and let them puff for about 15 seconds, then push them gently from the edges into the middle in big curds. Keep going for about 1 minute, until no runny egg is left, then take them out.
Add the rest of the oil to the same pan, then stir-fry the garlic and scallion whites for 10 seconds. Add the tomatoes, the soy sauce and the sugar, which balances the acid.
Cook, pressing the tomatoes now and then, for 3 to 4 minutes, until they collapse into a thick, jammy sauce. Splash in a little water if it gets dry.
Fold the eggs back in for 1 minute, so the curds soak up the sauce. Scatter with the scallion greens and serve over the rice and barley.
tip: Very ripe, sweet tomatoes? Cut the sugar to a pinch. Pale winter ones need all of it.

name: Egg fried brown rice with tofu, edamame and scallion
inspiredBy: Chinese egg fried rice, packed with tofu and edamame
about: Fried rice only works with cold, day-old rice, which is exactly what your batch in the fridge is. Fluffy egg, golden tofu and bright edamame are tossed over high heat until the grains jump and smell toasty. The **tofu and edamame add plant protein** and the tofu brings calcium.
steps: Break up the cold rice and barley with wet hands so there are no clumps. Pat the tofu dry and cut it into small cubes. Mince the ginger and garlic, slice the scallion whites and greens separately, and beat the eggs.

Heat a wok or your widest pan over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once. Add half the oil, then the tofu, and fry for 3 minutes, turning now and then, until golden on a few sides. Slide it onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, pour in the eggs and scramble them in a few seconds, breaking it into small pieces.

Add the ginger, garlic and scallion whites and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Tip in the rice and barley, press it flat against the pan for a few seconds, then toss. Keep going for 3 minutes, until the grains separate and you hear them popping.

Return the tofu, add the edamame, and drizzle the soy sauce and broth around the edge of the pan so they sizzle. Toss for another minute, then finish with the scallion greens and a pinch of white pepper.
tip: The pan has to be hot and the rice has to be cold. If you cook for two, fry in two batches so the rice fries instead of steams.
ingredients: calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate, cut into small cubes

name: Whole-wheat noodles with beef and mushroom sauce, cucumber, carrot and daikon
inspiredBy: Beijing zhajiangmian, with whole-wheat noodles, extra mushrooms and tofu in the sauce
about: Chewy noodles under a dark, glossy sauce of lean minced beef, shiitake and tofu simmered with sweet bean paste, topped with a pile of raw cucumber, carrot and daikon matchsticks. Hot, savoury sauce meets cold, crunchy vegetables in every bite, which is the whole point of the dish. The **raw vegetable strips and whole-wheat noodles add fibre**.
steps: Cut the cucumber, carrot and daikon into thin matchsticks and keep them in separate piles. Finely dice the shiitake, mince the ginger and garlic, and slice the scallion whites and greens separately.

Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, for about 4 minutes, until it is no longer pink and starting to brown (71 °C / 160 °F inside). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef. Add the ginger, garlic and scallion whites and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the shiitake and the crumbled tofu and cook for about 3 minutes, until the mushrooms soften and give up their liquid.

Push everything to one side and fry the sweet bean sauce in the oil that collects, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes, until it smells deep and toasty and the oil separates. Stir it through the beef, add the soy sauce and pour in enough water to come about halfway up the mixture.
Simmer on low for 8 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is dark, thick and glossy and clings to the spoon.
Cook the noodles in plenty of boiling water for the time on the package, then drain and toss with the black vinegar.
Pile the noodles in a bowl, spoon the hot sauce over and top with the cucumber, carrot, daikon and scallion greens. Toss everything together at the table.
tip: The sauce keeps for 4 days in the fridge. Make a double batch and you have a 10-minute lunch waiting.
ingredients: whole-wheat spaghetti stands in for whole-wheat noodles
calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate, crumbled

name: Mapo tofu with beef and shiitake, with oyster-sauce gai lan and mixed rice
inspiredBy: Sichuan mapo doufu, with lean beef, mushrooms mixed in and a bowl of greens to go with it
about: Soft tofu in a spicy, savoury sauce built on doubanjiang, with a little lean beef (the traditional Sichuan way) and a lot of diced shiitake that melt into the sauce. Toasted, ground Sichuan pepper brings the numbing tingle, and gai lan with oyster sauce cools it down. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done, and the **tofu and gai lan carry calcium**.
steps: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan over medium heat for about a minute, until they smell citrusy, then grind them to a coarse powder. Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes. Slide them into a pot of hot water with a good pinch of salt, steaming but not boiling, and leave them for 2 minutes, then drain gently. This seasons the tofu and firms it so it does not break apart in the sauce.
Finely dice the shiitake so it is about the size of the minced beef. Mince the garlic and ginger and slice the scallion. Stir the cornstarch with a few tablespoons of cold water until smooth.

Heat the oil in a wok or wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the beef and shiitake together, breaking the beef up, for 4 to 5 minutes, until the beef is browned all the way through (71 °C / 160 °F) and the mushroom liquid has cooked off. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.

Push the meat to one side and add the doubanjiang. Fry it for about a minute, until the oil turns red and it smells toasty and deep. This is the heart of the dish. Add the garlic and ginger for 15 seconds, then pour in enough water that the tofu will sit about half-submerged.
Slide in the tofu and gently nudge it with the back of the spoon rather than stirring, so the cubes stay whole. Simmer for 5 minutes.

Stir the cornstarch again and pour it in in three goes, nudging the pan after each, until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the tofu. Simmer 1 minute more, then sprinkle with the Sichuan pepper and the scallion.
Boil the gai lan in a pot of water for 2 minutes, until the stems are crisp-tender and bright green. Drain and toss with the oyster sauce.
Reheat the rice and barley and serve the mapo tofu over it with the gai lan on the side. Pack only the second portion of mapo tofu and rice for tomorrow's lunch, and boil fresh gai lan to go with it.
tip: Want it milder? Use half the doubanjiang and taste before you add more.
ingredients: soft or medium-firm, calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate

name: Pan-seared salmon with ginger scallion oil, garlic bok choy and mixed rice
inspiredBy: the Cantonese and Shanghainese habit of pouring sizzling oil over ginger and scallion, here on pan-seared salmon
about: A crisp-skinned salmon fillet with a sharp, fragrant sauce of ginger and scallion that sizzles when hot oil hits it, with black vinegar and soy stirred in. Garlicky bok choy and rice and barley complete the plate in about 25 minutes. **Salmon is rich in omega-3 fats** and vitamin D, and the vinegar cuts through the richness.
steps: Take the salmon out of the fridge 10 minutes ahead and pat it very dry. Season both sides with a pinch of the salt. Reheat the rice and barley.
Finely chop the ginger and scallion and put them in a small heatproof bowl with a tiny pinch of salt. Thinly slice the garlic.

Warm a third of the oil in a non-stick or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Lay the salmon in, skin side down, and press it gently for 10 seconds so the skin makes full contact. Cook without moving it for 4 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the flesh has turned opaque two thirds of the way up. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until it just flakes. Move it to a plate.
Wipe the pan, add the rest of the oil and heat it until it shimmers, about a minute. Carefully pour it over the ginger and scallion. It will sizzle and spit. Stir in the soy sauce and black vinegar.
Return the pan to the heat with the bok choy, the garlic and a splash of water. Cover and steam for 2 minutes, until the stems are just tender, then drizzle with the sesame oil.
Serve the salmon on the rice and barley with the sauce spooned over and the bok choy beside it.
tip: No bok choy? Any leafy green steamed the same way works, and the sauce is excellent on plain steamed fish, too.

name: Stir-fried chicken with snow peas, shiitake, carrot and almonds, over mixed rice
inspiredBy: Cantonese stir-fried chicken with snow peas and carrot, in a light oyster sauce, with toasted almonds as in almond chicken
about: Tender strips of chicken thigh with crunchy snow peas, sweet carrot and meaty shiitake in a light oyster sauce, tossed in a very hot wok so everything stays crisp, with toasted almonds scattered on top. It makes two portions and packs well into a lunch box. The almonds bring **vitamin E and crunch**, and the snow peas add vitamin C.
steps: Toss the chicken with the broth and half the cornstarch and leave it for 10 minutes. This light coating keeps it juicy in the hot pan.

Meanwhile, toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty. Slice the carrot into thin coins, slice the shiitake, mince the ginger and garlic, and slice the scallion. Stir the oyster sauce and the rest of the cornstarch into a few tablespoons of water.

Heat a wok or wide pan over high heat until it is almost smoking. Add half the oil and the chicken, in two batches because two portions crowd a home wok. Spread it out and leave it alone for 30 seconds so it browns, then stir-fry for 2 minutes, until cooked through. Move it to a plate.

Add the rest of the oil, then the ginger, garlic, shiitake and carrot and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the mushrooms are golden and the carrot is just tender. Add the snow peas and stir-fry for 1 minute more. Keep everything moving and the vegetables will stay crisp.
Return the chicken, stir the oyster sauce mixture again and pour it in, then toss for 30 seconds, until glossy. Finish with the scallion and the almonds.

Reheat the rice and barley and serve the chicken over it. Pack the second portion, rice and all, for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat it in a hot pan rather than the microwave so the vegetables stay crisp.
tip: Snow peas can swap for sugar snaps, and toasted cashews work in place of the almonds.

name: Sichuan-style braised mackerel and tofu in doubanjiang sauce, with garlic gai lan
inspiredBy: Sichuan doubanyu, fish braised in chili bean paste, made with mackerel and tofu
about: Mackerel pieces seared until golden, then braised in a spicy, savoury doubanjiang sauce with ginger, garlic, a touch of sugar and black vinegar, with cubes of tofu soaking up the sauce. Cold garlic gai lan on the side cools things down. **Mackerel is rich in omega-3 fats** and vitamin D, and the strong sauce suits it perfectly.
steps: Cut the mackerel into 3 cm chunks and pat them very dry. Sprinkle them with a pinch of white pepper. Cut the tofu into thick slabs. Mince the ginger and half the garlic, and slice the scallion. Reheat the rice and barley.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Lay in the mackerel, skin side down, and sear for 2 minutes without moving it, then turn and sear 1 minute more, until golden. Take it out and set it on a plate.

Turn the heat down to medium. Add the doubanjiang to the oil left in the pan and fry for about a minute, until the oil turns red. Add the ginger and the garlic for 15 seconds, then pour in enough water to come about halfway up where the fish will sit, along with the broth, the sugar and the black vinegar.

Bring it to a simmer and slide in the tofu. Put the fish back in, skin side up, and simmer gently for 6 minutes, spooning the sauce over the top now and then instead of stirring, so the fish stays whole.
Meanwhile, boil the gai lan for 2 minutes, until the stems are crisp-tender, then drain and rinse under cold water. Toss it with the rest of the garlic, finely minced, and the sesame oil.
Spoon the fish, tofu and plenty of sauce over the rice and barley. Sprinkle with the scallion and serve with the cold gai lan.
tip: Not a fan of mackerel? Salmon steaks are good in the same sauce.
ingredients: fillets or steaks, cut into chunks
calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate

name: Red-braised beef shank with daikon, carrots, eggs and napa cabbage
inspiredBy: Shanghainese red-braising (hong shao), the soy sauce and caramelized sugar braise used for beef and chicken
about: Beef shank simmered slowly in soy sauce, a splash of chicken broth, caramelized sugar, ginger and star anise until the meat is fork-tender and the sauce turns dark and glossy, with daikon, carrot and a braised egg soaking up all of it and napa cabbage wilted in at the end. It takes patience but very little work, and it tastes even better tomorrow. The **beef gives you iron and zinc**.
steps: Put the beef in a pot of cold water, bring it to a boil and cook for 3 minutes, until grey scum rises. Drain and rinse the beef. This gives you a clean, clear sauce. Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel.

Warm the oil in a heavy pot over medium-low heat, add the sugar and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until it melts into an amber syrup. This is what gives red-braised dishes their colour and gloss. Add the sliced ginger and the scallion whites and stir for 30 seconds, then add the beef and stir for 2 minutes to coat it.
Pour in the broth and soy sauce, add the star anise and pour in enough water to just cover the beef. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down low, cover and simmer for 90 minutes.
Add the daikon, carrot and peeled eggs, cover again and simmer for 25 minutes more, until the beef is fork-tender and the daikon looks translucent.

Stir in the napa cabbage and simmer for 5 minutes with the lid off. If the sauce is thin, turn the heat up for the last couple of minutes and let it bubble down until it is glossy and clings to the beef.
Reheat the rice and barley and serve the beef, vegetables and a halved egg over it with the scallion greens. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Start it as soon as you walk in, or use a pressure cooker, where the beef is tender in 35 minutes. A double batch is no more work and freezes very well.

name: Homemade beef, shrimp and napa dumplings in whole-wheat wrappers, with black vinegar and smashed cucumber
inspiredBy: Northern Chinese jiaozi, with a hot-water whole-wheat dough and plenty of cabbage in the filling
about: Plump boiled dumplings filled with lean beef, sweet shrimp, napa cabbage, ginger and scallion, wrapped in a tender hot-water dough made with whole-wheat flour, and served with a sharp black vinegar dip and a garlicky smashed cucumber. It is the weekend project: put on music and fold with someone. The **whole-wheat wrappers and cabbage add fibre**.
steps: Make the dough. Put the flour in a bowl and stir in just-boiled water a splash at a time (about 60% as much water as flour by weight) with chopsticks until it looks shaggy. When it is cool enough to touch, knead for 5 minutes, until smooth. Cover and rest it for 30 minutes. The hot water softens the whole-wheat bran, so the wrappers stay tender.

Make the filling. Toss the shredded napa with the salt and leave it for 10 minutes, then squeeze it very dry in a clean towel. Mix it with the beef, the finely chopped shrimp, minced ginger, finely chopped scallion, soy sauce, broth, about half the canola oil and half the sesame oil. Stir in one direction for a minute, then stir in cold water a spoonful at a time, until the lean filling is moist and sticky. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef and shrimp.

Roll the dough into a long rope and cut it into pieces about the size of a large grape. Flatten each piece and roll it into a thin round about 7 cm wide, a little thinner at the edge than in the middle.
Put a generous tablespoon of filling in each wrapper, fold it in half and pinch the edge shut. Set the finished dumplings on a floured tray, not touching.

Boil them in a big pot of water, in batches, stirring gently so they do not stick. When they float, add a splash of cold water, and repeat that once more. They are done about 1 minute after the second splash, about 6 minutes in all. Cut one open to check: the filling should be 71 °C (160 °F) and no longer pink.

For the dip, stir the black vinegar with a few drops of sesame oil. Smash only half the cucumber with the flat of a knife, chop it roughly and toss it with the minced garlic and a few drops of vinegar and sesame oil. Smash the rest fresh tomorrow, because it turns watery overnight.

Eat half the dumplings with the dip and the cucumber. Cool the rest for tomorrow's lunch, then pan-fry them in the rest of the canola oil with a splash of water and the lid on for 3 minutes, until crisp on the bottom and hot through.
tip: Fold double and freeze the raw dumplings on a tray, then bag them. They boil straight from frozen in 7 to 8 minutes.

name: Whole steamed sea bass with ginger, scallion and hot oil, gai lan and mixed rice
inspiredBy: the Cantonese steamed fish served at family dinners, with ginger, scallion and sizzling oil
about: A whole sea bass steamed for just 8 to 10 minutes over soft tofu until the flesh is silky, topped with fine threads of ginger and scallion and a splash of sizzling oil and soy sauce. Gai lan and rice make it a full Sunday dinner, and it is much easier than it looks. The steamed fish is a **very lean protein**, and the tofu and gai lan add calcium.
steps: Ask the fishmonger to scale and gut the fish. Pat it dry and cut two or three slashes into each side. Rub it inside and out with the salt, and a pinch of white pepper.

Cut half the ginger into slices and half the scallion into lengths. Tuck some inside the fish. Lay the rest on a heatproof plate with the tofu slabs, then set the fish on top so the fish sits off the plate and the tofu soaks up the juices.

Set up a steamer: a wok or wide pot with a rack and a lid. Bring about 4 cm of water to a rolling boil, lower in the plate, cover and steam on high for 8 to 10 minutes. The fish is done when the flesh at the thickest part is opaque and pulls easily from the bone.
While it steams, cut the rest of the ginger and the green parts of the scallion into very fine threads. Warm the soy sauce with the broth and 2 tablespoons of hot water.
Lift the plate out and pour off the cloudy liquid. Pick off the cooked ginger and scallion and discard them. Pile the fresh threads on top of the fish, with the tofu alongside.

Heat the oil in a small pot until it shimmers. Spoon a teaspoon of it into a bowl and set it aside, then pour the rest over the threads, which sizzle and release their smell. Pour most of the warm soy sauce around the fish.
Boil the gai lan for 2 minutes, drain and toss with the sliced garlic, the reserved hot oil and the rest of the soy sauce. Reheat the rice and barley and serve everything together.
tip: No steamer? Set the plate on a bowl placed upside-down in a big pot with a lid. The steaming time stays the same.
ingredients: one whole sea bass or branzino, about 400 g cleaned; this is the edible weight
calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate, cut into thick slabs

name: Mandarin and roasted peanuts
about: A juicy mandarin with a small handful of roasted peanuts, a snack you will find at any Chinese market stall. It is sweet, salty and crunchy. The **peanuts bring protein and vitamin E**, and the mandarin adds vitamin C.
steps: Peel the mandarin and eat it with the peanuts.

name: Mandarin and toasted almonds
about: A juicy mandarin with a handful of toasted almonds, sweet and crunchy together. The almonds are the **best vitamin E source** in the week's snacks, and the mandarin adds vitamin C.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty. Peel the mandarin and eat it with the almonds.

name: Roasted sweet potato (kao hongshu)
inspiredBy: Chinese street-cart roasted sweet potato
about: A whole sweet potato roasted until the skin crackles and the inside turns jammy and caramelized, the way it is sold from street carts all over northern China in winter. Nothing is added. It is full of **vitamin A and fibre**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Pierce the sweet potato a few times with a fork, set it on a tray and roast for 45 to 50 minutes, until it feels very soft and some syrup oozes out.
Let it cool for a few minutes and eat it with the skin on.
tip: Roast a whole tray on Sunday and rewarm one in a toaster oven. They keep for 4 days in the fridge.

name: Warm walnut soy milk
inspiredBy: Chinese walnut drinks (hetao lu)
about: Warm, plain soy milk blended with toasted walnuts until it is creamy and nutty, a cousin of the walnut drinks sold across China. It is comforting and filling without being sweet. The soy milk brings **calcium and protein**, and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Warm the soy milk until steaming, then blend it with the walnuts for 30 seconds, until smooth. Drink it warm.

name: Warm almond soy milk
inspiredBy: Chinese almond soy drinks (xingren dou jiang)
about: Warm, plain soy milk blended with toasted almonds until it is creamy and fragrant, in the spirit of the almond drinks sold across southern China. It is comforting and not too sweet. The soy milk brings **calcium and protein**, and the almonds add vitamin E.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Warm the soy milk until steaming, then blend it with the almonds for 30 seconds, until smooth. Drink it warm.

name: Mandarins
about: Two juicy mandarins, the fruit that sits in a bowl in every Chinese home from autumn on. They are sweet, easy and refreshing. The mandarins bring **vitamin C and fibre** for almost no effort.
steps: Peel the mandarins and eat them in segments.

name: Asian pear with toasted almonds
about: Crisp, juicy Asian pear slices with toasted almonds. Pear is a very Chinese fruit to snack on, and it is cool and refreshing. The **almonds bring vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Slice the pear and eat it with the almonds.

name: Asian pear with walnuts
about: Crisp Asian pear with a handful of walnuts, sweet and crunchy together. It is quick, filling and travels well. The **walnuts add plant omega-3 fats**, and the pear adds fibre.
steps: Slice the pear and eat it with the walnuts. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes first if you like.

name: Cold tofu with scallion, soy and sesame oil
inspiredBy: xiaocong ban doufu, Chinese tofu tossed with scallion
about: A block of cool, soft tofu with finely sliced scallion, a few drops of soy sauce and sesame oil, one of the simplest and most loved cold dishes (xiaocong ban doufu) in China. It is savoury and fresh. The tofu brings **calcium and plant protein**.
steps: Drain the tofu and set it on a plate. Slice it into big squares, or leave it whole and break it up with a spoon.
Scatter on the finely sliced scallion and the sesame seeds, then dribble over the soy sauce and the sesame oil.
ingredients: calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate

name: Warm edamame with Sichuan pepper salt
inspiredBy: Sichuan-style salted edamame
about: Warm, steamy edamame tossed with a pinch of salt and toasted, ground Sichuan pepper for a numbing tingle, in the spirit of Sichuan snack tables. It is a fun thing to nibble on. Edamame brings **plant protein, folate and fibre**.
steps: Boil the edamame in water for 4 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan for 1 minute, until fragrant, then grind them. Toss the edamame with the salt and the pepper and eat while warm.

name: Smashed cucumber with garlic, black vinegar and peanuts
inspiredBy: Sichuan and northern Chinese smashed cucumber (pai huanggua)
about: Cucumber smashed with the flat of a knife so it soaks up a sharp, garlicky dressing, with crushed roasted peanuts on top. It is cool, tangy and crunchy, and takes five minutes. The **peanuts bring vitamin E and protein** to a very light snack.
steps: Smash the cucumber with the flat of a knife until it splits, then chop it into bite-size pieces.
Toss it with the minced garlic, black vinegar, sesame oil and salt. Top with the crushed peanuts.

name: Pumpkin pie oatmeal
about: Rolled oats simmered in milk with pumpkin, a mashed banana, ground flaxseed, cinnamon and nutmeg, topped with toasted walnuts and sunflower seeds. It tastes like a slice of pie and takes ten minutes from the pot, and the pumpkin and oats bring **fibre and vitamin A**, with the flax adding some omega-3.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, pumpkin, mashed banana, ground flaxseed, cinnamon and nutmeg together in a small pot over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy and the pumpkin has melted into the oats.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the walnuts and sunflower seeds. Eat right away.
tip: Keep what is left of the tin of pumpkin covered in the fridge and use it within 4 days, or freeze it in spoonfuls. It also goes into the pumpkin pie yogurt snack. At the smallest sizes there are only a few spoonfuls of oats: cook them in just enough of the milk to cover, and drink the rest of the milk alongside.

name: Cherry pie oatmeal
inspiredBy: Inspired by a bowl of warm cherry pie
about: Creamy rolled oats with frozen cherries that cook down to a jammy sauce, a pinch of cinnamon and a scatter of toasted almonds and walnuts. It is dessert for breakfast that happens to bring **fibre, protein and vitamin E**.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, cherries and cinnamon together in a small pot over medium heat.
Simmer gently for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring often and pressing a few cherries with the spoon, until the oats are creamy and the milk has turned pink.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the almonds and walnuts.
tip: Frozen blueberries or a diced apple work the same way. At the smallest sizes there are only a few spoonfuls of oats: cook them with the cherries in just enough of the milk to cover, and drink the rest of the milk alongside.

name: Spinach and mushroom scramble on a sweet potato
inspiredBy: Inspired by a diner breakfast plate
about: Eggs scrambled until completely set with mushrooms and spinach, spooned onto a microwaved sweet potato split open like a baked potato. It is a quick, hearty breakfast with **protein, choline and vitamin A**.
steps: Wash the sweet potato, spinach and parsley. Prick the sweet potato all over with a fork and microwave it for 6 to 8 minutes, turning once, until a knife slides in easily.
Meanwhile, warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms for 4 minutes, until browned and the water has cooked off.
Add the spinach and stir for 1 minute, until it wilts. Beat the eggs with the salt, pepper and paprika and pour them in.
Stir gently for 3 to 4 minutes, until the eggs are completely set and no liquid egg is left.
Split the sweet potato, spoon the scramble on top and scatter with the cheddar and parsley.
tip: Bake the sweet potato in the oven when you have the time and the skin goes crisp.

name: Sage turkey patties and potato hash with a firm egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic diner breakfast of patties and hash, made with turkey
about: Savoury turkey patties with sage, thyme and grated apple, on a crisp-edged hash of potato, onion and spinach, with an egg cooked on top until the yolk is firm. It is the slow weekend breakfast, with **protein, choline and iron**.
steps: Wash the potatoes, spinach and apple. Mix the turkey with the grated apple, sage, thyme, half the salt and the pepper. Shape into small flat patties, then wash your hands, the board and the bowl with hot soapy water.

Warm half the oil in a large nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes, onion and paprika, cover for 5 minutes, then uncover and cook for 8 minutes more, turning now and then, until golden and tender.
Push the potatoes to one side. Add the rest of the oil and the patties and cook for 4 to 5 minutes a side, until browned and the middle reaches 74 °C (165 °F).

Stir the spinach and the rest of the salt into the hash for 1 to 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts. Make a well, crack in the egg, add a spoonful of water to the pan and cover for 5 to 6 minutes, until the white is set and the yolk is fully firm all the way through.
Slide the hash onto a plate and serve with the patties.
tip: Make the patties the night before so they hold together better in the pan. Keep the raw patties covered on the bottom shelf of the fridge and cook them within a day.
ingredients: scrubbed and cut in 1 cm dice

name: Chicken Waldorf salad with white beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by the classic Waldorf salad, with a yogurt dressing
about: Poached chicken, crisp apple and celery in a creamy lemon-yogurt dressing with walnuts and sunflower seeds, folded with white beans and piled on baby spinach. It is the deli salad you remember, with **protein, fibre and vitamin C**.
steps: Cover the chicken with cold water in a small pot, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 12 to 14 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Lift it out, slice it, spread it in a shallow container and refrigerate it within 2 hours.
Wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water. Wash the apple, celery, spinach and parsley.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Dice the cold chicken and fold it into the dressing with the apple, celery, beans and parsley.
Pile onto the spinach and scatter with the toasted walnuts and sunflower seeds.
tip: Poach the chicken the night before and the salad takes five minutes. Packed for lunch, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

name: Loaded baked potato soup with smoky turkey crumbles
inspiredBy: Inspired by loaded baked potato soup
about: A thick, creamy soup of potato and white beans that gets its body from blending part of the pot, not from flour or cream, with green beans stirred in at the end. It is "loaded" with smoky turkey crumbles, a little cheddar, yogurt and parsley, and it brings **protein, fibre and potassium**.
steps: Wash the potatoes, green beans and parsley. Warm half the oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the potatoes, thyme and broth and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 12 minutes, until the potatoes are very tender. Add the white beans and milk and bring back to a simmer.

Meanwhile, crumble the turkey into a small pan with the rest of the oil and the paprika. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until browned and crisp and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Wash your hands and the pan with hot soapy water.

Blend about half the soup, with a stick blender or in a blender, and stir it back in, so it is thick and creamy but still has chunks. Add the green beans and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, until they are tender and the soup is steaming hot. Season with the salt and pepper, and loosen with a splash of water if it is too thick.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the turkey, yogurt, cheddar and parsley.
tip: Careful when blending hot soup: fill the blender halfway and hold the lid down with a towel.

name: Broccoli cheddar soup with crisp sweet potato rounds
inspiredBy: Inspired by American broccoli cheddar soup
about: A thick, green, cheesy-tasting soup of broccoli, onion and white beans, made creamy by blending most of the pot rather than with flour or cream, with a little sharp cheddar and a swirl of yogurt. Roasted sweet potato rounds go alongside for dunking. The broccoli and beans bring **vitamin C, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potato and broccoli. Toss the sweet potato rounds with half the oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 20 minutes, turning once, until tender with browned edges.
Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion, carrot and garlic for 6 minutes. Add the broth, beans and broccoli and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes, until the broccoli is very tender and the soup is steaming hot. Add the milk, mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Blend about two thirds of the soup, with a stick blender or in a blender, and stir it back in, so it is thick and creamy but still has green flecks. Stir in half the cheddar.
Scatter the rest of the cheddar over the hot sweet potato rounds and return them to the oven for 2 minutes, until melted.
Ladle the soup into a bowl, swirl in the yogurt, scatter with the sunflower seeds and serve the cheesy rounds alongside for dunking.
tip: Careful when blending hot soup: fill the blender halfway and hold the lid down with a towel.
ingredients: sharp, grated, half for the soup and half for the rounds

name: Lentil and beef shepherd's pie with cauliflower mash
inspiredBy: Inspired by British shepherd's pie, with lentils in half the meat's place
about: Lean beef and lentils simmered with carrot, celery, mushrooms and peas in a thick herby gravy, under a golden mash of potato and cauliflower. The lentils bring **iron, folate and fibre**, and they thicken the gravy, so there is no flour.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Boil the potatoes and cauliflower in salted water for 15 minutes, until very tender. Heat the grill (broiler) to high.

While they cook, warm half the oil in a deep ovenproof pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion, carrot, celery and mushrooms for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the beef and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink is left. Wash your hands, the board and the spoon with hot soapy water.

Stir in the tomato paste, thyme, rosemary, paprika and broth. Mash a third of the lentils with a fork, then stir in all the lentils, mashed and whole, with the peas. Simmer for 8 minutes, until a spoon drawn through the gravy leaves a trail, the peas are steaming hot and the beef has reached 71 °C (160 °F).
Drain the potatoes and cauliflower and mash them with the milk, the rest of the oil and the salt until smooth.
Spoon the mash over the filling and fork it into ridges. Scatter with the cheddar and grill for 5 to 6 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Eat half now. Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it tomorrow, reheated until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Drain the cauliflower well and let it steam dry for a minute before mashing so the top can brown. To freeze the pie, cool it within 2 hours and freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw it in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Salmon fish pie with spinach and peas
inspiredBy: Inspired by British fish pie
about: Chunks of salmon gently poached in milk with onion, spinach and peas, in a creamy sauce thickened with blended white beans, under a lightly browned mash of potato and cauliflower, with a chopped firm-cooked egg folded in the way the classic has it. The salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D and protein**.
steps: Wash the vegetables and parsley. Bring a pot of salted water to the boil, lower in the egg in its shell, add the potatoes and cauliflower and boil for 10 minutes, then lift out the egg and cool it under cold water. Keep the vegetables boiling 4 minutes more, until very tender, then mash them with half the oil and a pinch of salt. Heat the grill (broiler) to high.
Meanwhile, soften the onion in a wide ovenproof pan with the rest of the oil for 4 minutes. Blend the beans with the milk, mustard and nutmeg until smooth and pour it in.

Simmer gently for 2 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon, then add the salmon and poach for 4 to 5 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw fish.
Peel and chop the firm egg. Fold it in with the spinach, peas, lemon juice, parsley and the rest of the salt and pepper for 1 minute, until the spinach wilts and the peas are steaming hot.
Spoon the mash over the top and rough it up with a fork. Scatter with the cheddar and grill for 5 to 6 minutes, until golden.
tip: Cooked fish keeps only 2 days, so this is one to eat fresh rather than plan as a leftover.

name: White chicken and bean chili with all the toppings
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex white chicken chili
about: A mild, lime-bright chili of chicken, white beans and green chiles, thickened with a few mashed beans, then piled with avocado, cilantro, yogurt, a little cheddar and crunchy pumpkin seeds. It makes two bowls, and the beans and toppings bring **protein, fibre and healthy fats**.
steps: Wash the cilantro and avocado. Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat and soften the onion and garlic for 5 minutes. Add the cumin, oregano and chili powder and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes, until the outside turns white. Wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water.
Add the green chiles, broth and half the beans. Simmer for 12 minutes, until the chicken is tender and reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
Mash the rest of the beans with a fork, or blend them with a splash of the broth, and stir them in. Simmer for 5 minutes more, until thick. Season with the lime juice, salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with the avocado, cilantro, yogurt, cheddar and pumpkin seeds. Eat half now.
Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate without the toppings. Eat it tomorrow, reheated until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), with fresh toppings.
tip: Add a pinch of cayenne for heat. To freeze the chili, cool it within 2 hours, freeze for up to 2 months, thaw it in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Turkey meatballs with mushroom gravy and squash mash
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swedish meatballs and Sunday-dinner gravy
about: Tender baked turkey meatballs with a savoury mushroom gravy thickened by blended white beans, a sweet mash of butternut squash and green beans on the side. It is the cosy plate of meatballs and gravy, with **protein, vitamin A and fibre**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray. Wash the vegetables and parsley. Boil the squash in salted water for 15 minutes, until very tender.

Mix the turkey with the egg, oats, grated onion, garlic, parsley, thyme, half the salt and the pepper. Shape into small balls and set on the tray. Wash your hands and the bowl with hot soapy water. Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until browned and the middle reaches 74 °C (165 °F).

Meanwhile, brown the sliced onion and mushrooms in half the oil in a wide pan for 6 minutes. Spoon a third of them into a blender with the beans, broth and mustard, blend until smooth and pour it back into the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes, until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
Steam the green beans in a basket over the squash pot for the last 6 minutes, until tender but still bright green.
Drain the squash and mash it with the milk, the rest of the oil, the nutmeg and the rest of the salt. Roll the meatballs in the gravy and serve with the mash and green beans. Eat half now.
Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it tomorrow, reheated until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: The meatballs keep 3 days in the fridge. Leftover squash mash is lovely stirred into oatmeal.
ingredients: peeled and cut in 3 cm cubes

name: Roast salmon with creamed spinach and crispy smashed potatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by a steakhouse plate of creamed spinach and smashed potatoes
about: A salmon fillet roasted with lemon and parsley, a bowl of creamed spinach made creamy with blended white beans, milk and a little nutmeg, and golden smashed baby potatoes. The salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D and protein**, and the spinach brings **folate and vitamin K**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the potatoes, spinach and parsley. Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then drain.
Flatten each potato with the bottom of a glass on an oiled tray, brush with a third of the oil and a pinch of salt and roast for 18 minutes, until crisp and golden.

Pat the salmon dry, rub with a little oil, half the lemon juice, half the parsley, salt and pepper and add it to the tray for the last 10 minutes, until it flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water.
Meanwhile, soften the onion and garlic in the rest of the oil in a large pan for 3 minutes. Add the spinach in handfuls and stir for 3 minutes, until it wilts.
Blend the beans with the milk, nutmeg and a pinch of salt until smooth, stir it into the spinach and simmer for 3 minutes, until creamy.
Squeeze the rest of the lemon over the salmon, scatter with parsley and serve with the spinach and potatoes.
tip: Trout works the same way if you prefer it.

name: Chicken pot pie with a crispy potato crust
inspiredBy: Inspired by classic chicken pot pie, with a potato crust instead of pastry
about: Chicken, carrot, celery, peas and mushrooms in a creamy thyme and sage sauce thickened with blended cauliflower and white beans, under an overlapping crust of thinly sliced potato baked golden. It is the Sunday pie without the pastry, with **protein, vitamin A and fibre**, and it makes two portions.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the vegetables. Simmer the cauliflower in the broth for 8 minutes, until very soft, then blend it with the beans, milk and mustard until smooth. Fill the blender no more than half full and hold the lid down with a towel.

Meanwhile, warm half the oil in a deep ovenproof pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion, carrot, celery and mushrooms for 6 minutes. Add the chicken, thyme and sage and stir for 4 minutes, until the chicken turns white. Wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water.

Pour in the blended sauce, add the peas and half the salt and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, until it bubbles and coats the back of a spoon. At the bigger sizes there is more liquid, so give it a few minutes longer.
Toss the potato slices with the rest of the oil and salt and the pepper, and lay them in overlapping circles over the filling, like roof tiles.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and golden at the edges and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Scatter with the cheddar for the last 5 minutes.
Let it stand for 5 minutes. Eat half now. Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it tomorrow, reheated until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: A mandoline or the slicing blade of a food processor makes the potato layer quick. Keep the slices thin so they cook through.
ingredients: scrubbed, sliced as thin as a coin

name: Glazed beef and lentil meatloaf with roasted potatoes and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic diner meatloaf dinner
about: Two small, tender, lean loaves with grated carrot and mashed lentils for moisture, brushed with a tangy tomato and mustard glaze, served with crisp roasted potatoes and broccoli. The beef and lentils bring **iron, zinc and protein**, and the vitamin C in the broccoli helps you absorb the lentils' iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the potatoes, broccoli and parsley. Toss the potato wedges with half the oil, the paprika and a pinch of salt on a large tray and roast for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, mix the beef with the lentils, oats, egg, onion, carrot, garlic, parsley, thyme, half the salt and the pepper. Shape into 2 small, flat loaves about 3 cm high on a second small tray. Wash your hands and the bowl with hot soapy water.
Stir the tomato paste, mustard and half the lemon juice together with a spoonful of water and brush half over the loaves.
Slide the loaves into the oven beside the potatoes and bake for 15 minutes. Give the wedges a turn.

Add the broccoli, tossed in the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt, to the potato tray. Brush the loaves with the rest of the glaze and bake for 12 minutes more, until the loaves reach 71 °C (160 °F) in the middle and the potatoes and broccoli are crisp and browned.
Rest the loaves for 5 minutes and serve with the vegetables, with the rest of the lemon juice squeezed over the broccoli.
tip: Mix the meatloaf in the morning, keep it covered in the fridge and it only needs shaping and baking.

name: Baked cinnamon apple with walnuts
about: A warm apple cooked soft with cinnamon and topped with toasted walnuts, like a little apple crisp. It brings **fibre, vitamin C and healthy fats**.
steps: Wash the apple. Put the apple chunks, cinnamon and a spoonful of water in a microwave-safe bowl, cover and microwave for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft.
Top with the walnuts and eat warm.
ingredients: washed, cored and cut in chunks

name: Veggie sticks with white bean ranch dip
about: Crunchy carrot, celery and broccoli with a creamy herb dip of blended white beans, lemon and parsley. It is the ranch you love, with **fibre and plant protein**.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut them into sticks.
Blend the beans, oil, lemon juice, garlic powder, salt and 2 spoonfuls of water until smooth, then stir in the parsley. Serve with the vegetables.
Keep leftover dip covered in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

name: Clementines with almonds and walnuts
about: Two easy-peel clementines with a small handful of almonds and walnuts. It is sweet, juicy and crunchy, with **vitamin C, vitamin E and omega-3**.
steps: Wash the clementines, peel them and eat with the almonds and walnuts.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A sliced banana with chopped walnuts and a shake of cinnamon, a little like banana bread without the loaf. It brings **potassium and omega-3**.
steps: Slice the banana into a bowl and scatter with the walnuts and cinnamon.

name: Cherry yogurt with walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt with cherries that thaw to a juicy sauce, a little cinnamon and chopped walnuts. It brings **protein, calcium and omega-3**.
steps: Thaw the cherries in the fridge. Stir the cherries and cinnamon into the yogurt and top with the walnuts.
tip: If you are pregnant, over 60, or have a weakened immune system, heat the cherries until steaming and cool them first.

name: Pumpkin pie yogurt with walnuts
about: Greek yogurt swirled with pumpkin, cinnamon and nutmeg, topped with a few walnuts. It tastes like pumpkin pie filling and brings **protein, calcium and vitamin A**.
steps: Stir the yogurt, pumpkin, cinnamon and nutmeg together and top with the walnuts.
Keep the rest of the pumpkin tin covered in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

name: Apple slices with walnuts and sunflower seeds
about: A crisp apple with a handful of walnuts and sunflower seeds and a shake of cinnamon. It is sweet and crunchy, with **fibre, vitamin E and omega-3**.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the walnuts, sunflower seeds and a shake of cinnamon.

name: Guacamole with carrot and celery sticks
about: Mashed avocado with lime, cilantro and a pinch of garlic, scooped up with crunchy carrot and celery. It is creamy and filling, with **healthy fats, potassium and fibre**.
steps: Wash the avocado, carrot, celery and cilantro. Halve the avocado, scoop it into a bowl and mash it with a fork with the lime juice, garlic powder and salt.
Stir in the cilantro and serve with the carrot and celery sticks.
Eat it the day you make it, or press cling film onto the surface and keep it in the fridge for up to 1 day.

name: Creamy banana oats with peanut butter and walnuts
inspiredBy: a classic hot oatmeal with banana and peanut butter
about: Creamy stovetop oats with mashed banana, a spoonful of peanut butter and toasted walnuts. The oats bring **slow-burning fibre**, and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Wash your hands. Stir the oats, milk and the mashed half of the banana in a small pot over medium heat.
Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the sliced banana, the peanut butter and the walnuts. Dust with cinnamon.
ingredients: 1% milk or any milk you like
ripe, half mashed and half sliced
roughly chopped and toasted in a dry pan

name: Blueberry yogurt bowl with toasted oats and walnuts
inspiredBy: a parfait-style yogurt bowl
about: Thick Greek yogurt under juicy blueberries, with oats toasted in a pan for crunch and walnuts on top. It is quick, cool and **high in protein**, with plant omega-3 from the walnuts.
steps: Wash fresh blueberries. If using frozen, thaw them in a bowl in the fridge overnight or for 30 minutes on the counter.
Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden and fragrant, then let them cool.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, pile on the berries, and scatter over the oats and walnuts. Dust with cinnamon.
tip: For anyone pregnant, over 65, under 5 or with a weak immune system, boil frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first.

name: Spinach, mushroom and white bean scramble with firm-cooked eggs
inspiredBy: Tuscan-style beans and greens with eggs
about: Mushrooms, spinach and tomatoes cooked down with white beans, then eggs stirred through until fully firm. Served with an orange on the side, the beans and eggs together give **protein, choline and fibre** before 9 a.m.
steps: Wash the mushrooms, spinach, orange and tomatoes. Slice the mushrooms, halve the tomatoes and mince the garlic.
Warm the oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms for 4 minutes until browned, then add the garlic and tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and spinach and stir until the spinach wilts and the beans are hot.

Beat the eggs with the iodized salt, pour them in, and stir gently for 3 to 4 minutes until completely firm all the way through, with no liquid left. Serve with the orange. Keep the rest of an opened tin of beans covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days: the next scramble or the bean dip can take it.

name: Braised lentils with carrots, thyme, sardines and lemon yogurt
inspiredBy: French-style lentils with carrots and thyme
about: Green-brown lentils simmered with carrot, onion, tomato paste and thyme, wilted with spinach and finished with sardines and lemon yogurt. This is **the big lentil pot** for the week: one portion for lunch today, plus the lentils the soup and the bowl will need later.
steps: Wash the carrot, spinach and lemon. Dice the carrot and onion small and mince the garlic. Zest the lemon, then juice it.
Warm the oil in a large pot and soften the onion and carrot for 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and thyme for 1 minute.

Add the rinsed lentils for all three meals: today's lunch, the Day 2 soup and the Day 3 bowl (add up the dry lentils in those recipes, or check the Prep tab), then the bay leaf and water to cover by two fingers. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes in a roomy pot until tender but still holding their shape.

Now, before the spinach goes in, scoop out the lentils for the soup and the bowl (cooked lentils weigh about 2½ times their dry weight, so each meal's share is its dry amount times 2½). Spread them in a shallow container, cool within 1 hour and refrigerate. Use within 3 days, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F) when used hot.
Stir the spinach into the pot for 2 minutes, then the salt and half the lemon juice. Remove the bay leaf.

Stir the lemon zest and remaining juice into the yogurt. Serve the lentils topped with the yogurt, the sardines broken into chunks and the sunflower seeds. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
tip: Day 1 is the big cook. To do it all in one session, roast the chicken tray while the lentils simmer, cool tonight's portion with the rest and reheat it to 74 °C (165 °F) at dinner. Cooked lentils also freeze well if you will not use them within 3 days.
ingredients: from a lemon; zest it first

name: Roast chicken thighs with carrots, sweet potato and lemony barley
inspiredBy: a big-batch roast tray with roots and a grain
about: Chicken thighs roast next to a tray of carrots, sweet potato, onion and broccoli while a pot of barley simmers. Cook extra and it feeds **four meals**: tonight's dinner, the Day 2 lunch, the chicken in the Day 2 soup and the base of the Day 3 skillet.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). This is the big cook of the week. The list here is one portion, so make twice everything on it (tonight and the Day 2 lunch). Also weigh out the raw chicken listed in the Day 2 soup and in the Day 3 skillet, and the carrots, sweet potato and dry barley listed in the skillet. Together that is all the chicken and barley on the week's shopping list.
Wash the vegetables and herbs. Cut the carrots, sweet potato and onion into chunky pieces, and the broccoli into florets.

Rub all the chicken with half the oil, the paprika, thyme, garlic, half the lemon juice and half the salt. Wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken.

Use two trays so nothing is crowded. Toss the vegetables (not the broccoli yet) with the remaining oil and a pinch of the salt on one tray, with the skillet's carrots and sweet potato at one end. Lay the chicken on the other tray in its groups. Roast the vegetables for 40 minutes and the chicken for 35 to 40 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part. Add the broccoli to the vegetable tray for the last 15 minutes.

Meanwhile simmer all the barley in plenty of water for 25 to 30 minutes until tender, then drain. Cooked barley weighs about 3 times its dry weight, so scoop out the skillet's share (its dry amount times 3), then toss the rest with the remaining lemon juice, salt and the chopped parsley.

Serve one portion now with the barley. Pack the second portion for the Day 2 lunch, the soup's chicken in its own container, and the skillet's chicken, carrots, sweet potato and barley in another, all in shallow containers.
Cool everything within 1 hour, then refrigerate. Eat it all within 3 days of cooking (the Day 3 skillet finishes it), reheated to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Mushroom, lentil and chicken soup with thyme and spinach
inspiredBy: rustic European mushroom and lentil soup
about: Browned mushrooms and tomato paste give this soup a deep, savoury flavour, and the lentils bring **iron and folate**. It is made for lentils and chicken cooked ahead, like the big pot and tray in this plan, so it is ready in about half an hour; cooking them from scratch adds about 40 minutes.
steps: If the lentils and chicken are not cooked yet, simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 20 to 25 minutes, and roast the chicken until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part, then shred it. If you cooked them ahead, take your portion from the fridge. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after raw chicken.
Wash the mushrooms, carrot and spinach. Slice the mushrooms, dice the onion and carrot and mince the garlic.
Warm the oil in a pot over medium-high heat and brown the mushrooms for 5 minutes. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and thyme for 1 minute, then add the cooked lentils, the shredded chicken and enough water to cover generously.
Simmer for 10 minutes, until the chicken is steaming hot and reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the lemon juice and salt.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the yogurt and toasted sunflower seeds. Use cooked lentils and chicken within 3 days of cooking.
tip: Blend a third of the soup for a creamier texture.
ingredients: dry weight; cooked ahead in the big lentil pot, or simmered first
raw weight; roasted ahead on the tray, or cooked first, then shredded

name: Lentil and tuna bowl with cucumber, feta and red pepper
inspiredBy: a Greek-leaning lentil salad with tuna
about: Cooked lentils (made ahead in the big pot, or simmered first and cooled) tossed cold with flaked tuna, crunchy cucumber, sweet pepper, tomatoes, feta and plenty of parsley in a lemon dressing. It is assembled in five minutes and is **high in fibre and protein**, with B12 from the tuna.
steps: If the lentils are not cooked yet, simmer them in plenty of water for 20 to 25 minutes, drain, spread in a shallow container and cool within 1 hour. Wash the cucumber, pepper, tomatoes, spinach and parsley. Dice the cucumber and pepper, halve the tomatoes, thinly slice the onion and chop the parsley.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and salt in a bowl. Add the lentils, vegetables, spinach and parsley and toss.

Flake in the tuna, then crumble over the feta and add the walnuts. Keep any opened tin of tuna covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Pack in a cold bag with an ice pack if taking it to work, and eat the same day. Use cooked lentils within 3 days of cooking.
ingredients: dry weight; cooked ahead in the big lentil pot, or simmered first and cooled

name: Lemony chicken, barley and broccoli skillet with spinach
inspiredBy: a fast skillet supper from tray leftovers
about: Roast chicken, roots and barley, reheated with garlic, spinach, broccoli and lemon so it tastes like a new dish. Made for tray leftovers, like the big tray in this plan, it keeps **protein and fibre high** with almost no new cooking. From scratch, roast the chicken and vegetables and cook the barley first.
steps: If the chicken, vegetables and barley are not cooked yet, roast the chicken and vegetables at 220 °C (425 °F) for 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F), and simmer the barley for 25 to 30 minutes. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after raw chicken. Wash the spinach, broccoli, parsley and lemon. Chop the spinach and parsley, cut the broccoli into small florets and mince the garlic.
Warm the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and chili flakes for 30 seconds, then the broccoli with a splash of water. Cover and steam for 3 minutes.
Add the roasted vegetables, barley, chicken and spinach with a splash of water. Cover and heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until everything is steaming hot and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley. Cooked chicken is good for 3 days in the fridge, so finish every bit of this skillet today.
ingredients: raw weight; roasted ahead on the tray, or cooked first, then sliced
dry weight; cooked ahead with the tray, or simmered first
roasted ahead on the tray, or roasted first
roasted ahead on the tray, or roasted first

name: Edamame, tofu and egg slaw bowl with tahini-ginger dressing
inspiredBy: Asian-style slaws with a sesame dressing
about: Edamame, firm tofu and chopped firm-cooked eggs on a crunchy red cabbage, carrot and pepper slaw in a tahini-ginger-lemon dressing, topped with sunflower seeds. It brings **protein, choline, some calcium and vitamin C**, and nothing here needs a long cook.
steps: Cook the frozen edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes until steaming hot, then drain and cool under cold water.
Boil the eggs in a pot of simmering water for 10 minutes until the yolks are completely firm, then cool them under cold water and peel. Eggs boiled ahead are fine too.
Wash the cabbage, spinach, carrot, pepper and lemon. Shred the cabbage and carrot, slice the pepper and grate the ginger.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, ginger and salt with a spoonful of warm water until smooth.

Cube the tofu (it is ready to eat, so keep it chilled). Toss the edamame, tofu, spinach and vegetables with the dressing, top with the quartered eggs and the sunflower seeds. Eat it the same day, packed in a cold bag with an ice pack if it travels.
tip: Boil the eggs ahead, while the lentils simmer on Day 1 or any evening: in their shells they keep up to 1 week in the fridge, and lunch then takes about 15 minutes.

name: Chermoula salmon with lemony millet, cucumber and tomato salad
inspiredBy: Moroccan chermoula, with a millet salad on the side
about: Salmon baked under a bright herb, garlic and cumin paste, served on lemony millet with cucumber and tomato. It is **the week's fish cook**: eat one portion warm, and pack the second cold for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: The list is one portion, so make twice everything on it (tonight and tomorrow's lunch). Cook fresh salmon the day you buy it, or thaw frozen fillets overnight in the fridge. Wash the herbs, cucumber, tomatoes and lemons. Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Rinse the millet.

Blend or finely chop most of the parsley, the garlic, cumin, paprika, half the lemon juice and half the oil into a paste. Rub it over the salmon and rest it in the fridge while the oven heats, 30 minutes at most. Never reuse the raw paste.
Simmer the millet in plenty of water for 15 minutes, drain, and toss with the remaining lemon juice, oil and salt. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw salmon.
Bake the salmon on a lined tray for 12 to 14 minutes until it flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Dice the cucumber, tomato and onion and toss with the millet. Serve a portion of salmon on top with the almonds.
This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour, refrigerate it covered, and eat it cold tomorrow. Use it within 2 days; if you take it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.

name: Tofu and spinach saag-style curry with tomatoes and quinoa
inspiredBy: Indian saag paneer, with tofu doing the work of the cheese
about: Cubes of tofu in a spiced spinach, tomato and ginger sauce finished with yogurt, over fluffy quinoa. Spinach and tofu make this **rich in iron, folate and some calcium**. The second portion is tomorrow's lunch, and the pot of quinoa also feeds the Day 6 shrimp.
steps: Wash the spinach and tomatoes. Dice the onion and mince the garlic and ginger. Rinse the quinoa. The list is one portion, so make twice everything on it (tonight and tomorrow's lunch).

Simmer the quinoa in about double its volume of water for 15 minutes, then fluff and set aside, covered. Cook the quinoa for the Day 6 shrimp in the same pot (its dry weight is listed in that recipe, or check the Prep tab).
Warm the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, garam masala, cumin and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste and tofu and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in the spinach until it wilts down. Take off the heat and stir in the yogurt and salt.

This makes two portions. Serve one over quinoa. Cool the second portion and the rest of the quinoa in shallow containers within 1 hour and refrigerate. Eat the curry tomorrow, reheated to 74 °C (165 °F), and use the quinoa within 3 days.

name: Lemon-chili shrimp with broccoli, edamame and quinoa
inspiredBy: a quick garlicky shrimp pilaf
about: Garlic shrimp tossed with broccoli, edamame and fluffy quinoa, brightened with lemon and a pinch of chili. With quinoa cooked ahead, like the saag night in this plan, it is on the table in about 20 minutes (30 from scratch), and it brings **iodine, zinc and lean protein**.
steps: Wash the broccoli and parsley. Cut the broccoli into small florets, thinly slice the onion and mince the garlic. Pat the shrimp dry.
If the quinoa is not cooked yet, simmer it in about double its volume of water for 15 minutes, then fluff. If you cooked it ahead, take it from the fridge.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan. Cook the broccoli and frozen edamame with a splash of water for 5 minutes until tender and steaming hot.

Push the vegetables aside, add the remaining oil, garlic and chili flakes for 30 seconds, then the shrimp for 3 minutes until pink and opaque (70 °C, 158 °F). Wash your hands, the board and the knife after the raw shrimp.
Toss in the quinoa and stir for 2 minutes until it is steaming hot, then add the onion, lemon juice, parsley and salt.
ingredients: peeled, thawed in the fridge if frozen
dry weight, rinsed; cooked ahead with the saag, or simmered first

name: Sardine and new potato salad with cucumber, orange and parsley
