about: Creamy oats simmered in milk with grated carrot, grated apple, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg, topped with cool Greek yogurt, toasted almonds and pumpkin seeds. It tastes like carrot cake with the frosting, and the carrot brings **vitamin A as carotenoids** alongside protein from the yogurt and fibre from the oats and apple.
steps: Wash the carrot and apple and grate them on the large holes of a box grater.
Put the oats, milk, carrot, apple, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg in a small pot with a splash of water.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until the oats are thick and the carrot is soft.
Spoon into a bowl, add the yogurt and scatter over the toasted almonds and pumpkin seeds.
tip: Grate the carrot the night before and keep it covered in the fridge to make this a 10-minute breakfast.

name: Blueberry overnight oats with yogurt and chia
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss bircher muesli, soaked the night before
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt, with chia stirred through, then topped with blueberries. It is ready when you wake up, with **fibre, protein and plant omega-3** and the deep blue of the berries.
steps: The night before, stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia and cinnamon together in a jar or small bowl until smooth.
Cover and put it in the fridge to soak for at least 6 hours, or overnight.
In the morning, wash the blueberries and spoon them on top. Eat it cold, straight from the jar.
tip: Make it fresh the night before and eat it within 2 days. Never keep soaked oats longer than 3 days.

name: Golden sweet potato and corn hash with a firm egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by a diner breakfast hash
about: Golden sweet potato cubes with sweet corn, yellow pepper and onion with smoked paprika, topped with an egg cooked until the yolk is firm, a squeeze of lemon and cool yogurt. A sunny, hearty plate with **vitamin A as carotenoids, potassium and protein**.
steps: Wash the sweet potato, pepper and cilantro. Put the sweet potato cubes in a bowl with a splash of water, cover with a plate and microwave for 4 minutes, until just tender.
Heat the oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the sweet potatoes, smoked paprika and salt and cook for 6 minutes, turning now and then, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 3 minutes, then the frozen corn for 2 minutes, until the corn is steaming hot.
Push the hash to the sides, crack the egg into the middle and cover the pan. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the white is set and the yolk is completely firm.
Finish with the lemon, black pepper, cilantro and a pinch of chili flakes if you like, then serve straight from the pan with the cold yogurt on the side.
tip: Microwave the sweet potato cubes the night before and this is a 15-minute breakfast.

name: Banana and cinnamon quinoa porridge with almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by creamy breakfast porridge, made with quinoa and milk
about: Quinoa simmered in milk with cinnamon until soft and creamy, topped with sliced banana, toasted almonds and pumpkin seeds. A slow, cosy weekend bowl with **potassium, calcium and iron**.
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under cold water for 30 seconds.
Put the quinoa, milk, cinnamon and a splash of water in a small pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cook for 14 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the quinoa is tender and the porridge is thick and creamy. Add a splash of milk if it gets stiff.
Spoon into a bowl, lay the banana slices on top and scatter over the almonds and pumpkin seeds.
tip: Mash half the banana into the pot for a naturally sweet porridge.

name: Rainbow fruit bowl with yogurt and toasted oats
inspiredBy: Inspired by a fruit-and-yogurt parfait, with a stripe of every colour
about: Thick Greek yogurt topped with mango, green apple, blueberries and strawberries in a row of colour, then a crunch of toasted oats, walnuts and a spoonful of chia. It is bright, quick and gives you **vitamin C, protein and calcium** in one bowl.
steps: Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until they smell nutty. Tip them into a bowl to cool.
Wash the blueberries, strawberries and apple. Use mango thawed overnight in a covered bowl in the fridge, or fresh mango.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and arrange the mango, apple, blueberries and strawberries in rows on top.
Scatter over the toasted oats, the walnuts and the chia just before eating so the oats stay crisp.
tip: Toast a few days of oats at once and keep them in a jar.

name: Sardine and quinoa herb salad with chickpeas, kale and cucumber
inspiredBy: Inspired by lemony chickpea and herb salads from the eastern Mediterranean
about: A herby, lemony salad of quinoa, chickpeas, kale, cucumber and cilantro, with sardines folded through. Sardines bring **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas and greens bring iron and folate, with the lemon to help absorb the iron.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and cook it in about twice its volume of water for 14 minutes, until tender. Spread it on a plate to cool, then chill it within 1 hour.
Wash the kale, cucumber and cilantro. Slice the kale very thinly, put it in a bowl with the lemon juice, the oil and the salt, and rub it with your fingers for 1 minute, until it softens.
Add the chickpeas, quinoa, cucumber, onion, cilantro, cumin and pepper and toss well.
Flake the sardines over the top and fold them in gently so they stay in chunks.

Taste and add a little more lemon if you like. If you pack it, put it in a container with an ice pack and eat it the same day. Keep an opened tin of sardines covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
tip: Cook the quinoa the evening before and this is a 10-minute lunch. Squeeze a little extra lemon over the sardines just before eating.

name: Carrot, lentil and kale slaw with a firm egg and cumin-lemon yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Moroccan carrot salad, with lentils and greens added
about: Grated carrot and shredded kale tossed with lentils and pumpkin seeds in a cumin and lemon yogurt dressing, with a firm hard-cooked egg on top. Orange from the carrot, green from the kale, and **fibre, vitamin A (as carotenoids) and protein** all in one bowl.
steps: Put the egg in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool it under cold water and peel it.
Wash the carrot, kale and cilantro. Grate the carrot and slice the kale as thinly as you can.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, oil, cumin, paprika and salt together in a bowl.
Add the carrot, kale and lentils and toss until everything is coated. Let it sit for 5 minutes so the kale softens.
Halve the egg and lay it on top with the pumpkin seeds and cilantro. If you pack it, put it in a container with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Keep the dressing in a separate small jar if you are packing it, and stir it in at lunch.
ingredients: hard-cooked until the yolk is firm

name: Purple cabbage, beet and shrimp bowl with black beans and quinoa
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Tex-Mex bean and slaw bowl, in purple, with paprika shrimp
about: Shredded red cabbage and beet with black beans, fluffy quinoa and quick paprika shrimp, tossed in a lemony cilantro dressing and finished with toasted almonds. It is **high in fibre and protein**, and the red cabbage and beet turn the whole bowl a deep purple.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and cook it in about twice its volume of water for 14 minutes, until the little tails pop out. Spread it on a plate to cool for 10 minutes, then chill it within 1 hour.
Wash the cabbage and cilantro. Shred the cabbage finely and dice the beet.

Pat the shrimp dry and toss with the paprika and a pinch of the salt. Heat half the oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until pink, opaque and firm all the way through. Cool them on a plate, then wash your hands, the pan and the board with hot soapy water.
Whisk the lemon juice, the rest of the oil, cumin, the rest of the salt, half the cilantro and a splash of water together.
Toss the cooled quinoa with the cabbage, beans and beet, then stir through the dressing. Lay the shrimp on top with the almonds and the rest of the cilantro.
Pack it in a container with an ice pack and eat it the same day. Keep the shrimp cold until you eat.
tip: Cook the quinoa the evening before, cool it fast in a shallow container, and use it within 3 days. Swap the shrimp for chicken if you prefer.
ingredients: peeled, thawed in the fridge if frozen
vacuum-packed cooked beet or home-roasted, diced

name: Rainbow chopped salad with chickpeas, millet, a firm egg and lemon dressing
inspiredBy: Inspired by an Israeli chopped salad, with every colour in the bowl
about: Finely chopped red cabbage, carrot, yellow pepper, cucumber and sweet corn with kale, chickpeas, millet and a firm egg, in a bright lemon and olive oil dressing. A crunchy bowl with **fibre, vitamin C and plant protein**.
steps: Rinse the millet and cook it in about 2½ times its volume of water for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender, adding the frozen corn for the last 2 minutes so it is steaming hot. Spread both on a plate and cool quickly, then chill within 1 hour. Hard-cook the egg in boiling water for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool and peel it.
Wash all the vegetables and cilantro. Chop the cabbage, kale, carrot, pepper and cucumber into small, even pieces.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, paprika, salt and pepper together in a large bowl.
Add the chickpeas, millet and corn, the vegetables and the cilantro and toss well.
Chop the egg and scatter it over with the walnuts. Eat it right away, or cover it and chill it and eat it the same day.
tip: The smaller you chop, the better it tastes: every forkful gets every colour.
ingredients: hard-cooked until the yolk is firm

name: Green herb chicken curry with kale and quinoa
inspiredBy: Inspired by Thai green curry, with a fresh cilantro, ginger and lemon paste
about: Chicken simmered in a bright green paste of cilantro, garlic, ginger and chili with light coconut milk and plenty of kale, over quinoa. The kale brings **calcium, vitamin K and folate**, and the lemon at the end lifts the whole pot.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and cook it in about twice its volume of water for 14 minutes, until tender, then fluff it with a fork.
Wash the kale and cilantro. Roughly chop half the onion and blitz it with the garlic, cilantro, ginger, coriander, cumin, chili, half the lemon juice and a splash of water to a loose green paste.
Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Dice the rest of the onion and cook it for 4 minutes, then add the paste and cook for 2 minutes, until it smells fragrant.

Add the chicken and stir to coat, then wash your hands, the knife and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken. Pour in the coconut milk and about a cup of water, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 12 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
Add the kale and cook for 4 minutes, until it is soft and bright green. Stir in the salt and the rest of the lemon juice.

Serve over the quinoa. Pack the second portion for tomorrow: put the curry and quinoa in a shallow container, cool and chill within 1 hour, keep it up to 3 days and reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Freezer: cool within 1 hour in a shallow container and freeze up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Add more chili if you like heat.

name: Quick beef and red pepper goulash with potatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by Hungarian goulash, made quick with tender steak cubes
about: Small cubes of sirloin simmered with sweet paprika, tomato, red pepper and potatoes until the sauce is rich and red, with a spoonful of cool yogurt. A beefy red bowl with **iron, zinc and vitamin C** from the peppers and tomato.
steps: Wash the pepper, potatoes and cilantro. Pat the beef dry and season it with half the salt.

Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in a single layer for 4 minutes, turning once. Lift it onto a plate. Wash your hands, the knife and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw beef.
Add the onion to the pot and cook for 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the garlic, paprika, smoked paprika and caraway for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomato, about 1 cup of water, the potatoes and the beef with its juices. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 15 minutes.

Add the red pepper and cook uncovered for 8 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender, the beef is cooked through at 71 °C (160 °F) and the sauce is thick. Season with the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Spoon into a bowl, top with the yogurt and the cilantro.
tip: The goulash tastes even better the next day. Chill it within 1 hour and eat it within 3 days, reheated until steaming hot. To make it a faster weeknight dinner, cut the beef, potatoes and pepper the night before, or cook it in a pressure cooker for 15 minutes at high pressure.

name: Orange-ginger salmon with roasted sweet potato and garlicky spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by orange-glazed salmon, with a ginger and garlic glaze
about: Salmon brushed with a sticky orange and ginger glaze, roasted beside crisp sweet potato wedges, with garlicky spinach on the side. Salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the sweet potato brings vitamin A as carotenoids and potassium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potatoes, spinach and orange. Toss the wedges on a tray with half the oil, the paprika and half the salt and roast for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the orange juice, zest, ginger and half the garlic in a small pan for 4 to 5 minutes, until it is reduced and syrupy.

Turn the sweet potatoes, push them to one side and lay the salmon on the tray. Brush the fish with half the glaze and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Use fresh salmon the day you buy it, or thaw frozen salmon in the fridge. Wash your hands, the knife and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw fish.
While the fish roasts, heat the rest of the oil in a pan, add the rest of the garlic and the spinach and cook for 2 minutes, until wilted. Season with the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Serve the salmon and wedges with the spinach and brush on the last of the glaze.
tip: Orange zest is where the flavour is, so wash the orange well before zesting.

name: Beef and eggplant stew with sweet potato, chickpeas and red cabbage slaw
inspiredBy: Inspired by Persian khoresht bademjan, a beef and eggplant stew with tomato and cinnamon
about: Small cubes of sirloin simmered with eggplant, sweet potato and chickpeas in a cinnamon-scented tomato sauce, with cool yogurt and a crunchy purple cabbage slaw. The eggplant and cabbage give the plate its colour, and the beef, chickpeas and yogurt bring **protein, iron and calcium**.
steps: Wash the eggplant, sweet potato, cabbage and cilantro. Heat half the oil in a wide, deep pot over medium-high heat, add the eggplant and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until it starts to brown. Lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil and brown the beef in a single layer for 4 minutes, turning once. Wash your hands, the knife and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw beef. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, then the garlic, cinnamon, turmeric and cumin for 30 seconds.
Pour in the tomato and about a cup of water, add the sweet potato and the salt, cover and simmer for 12 minutes.
Return the eggplant, add the chickpeas and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes more, until the sweet potato is tender, the beef is cooked through at 71 °C (160 °F) and the sauce is thick.
Toss the cabbage with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt and pepper. Spoon the stew into bowls, top with the yogurt and cilantro and serve with the slaw.

Pack the second portion for tomorrow: cool and chill the stew within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep the slaw and the yogurt apart, and reheat the stew until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). Keep it up to 3 days.
tip: Salt the eggplant cubes for 10 minutes and pat them dry if you want less oil to soak in. For a faster weeknight dinner, cut everything the night before and keep it covered in the fridge, or use a pressure cooker for 15 minutes at high pressure.

name: Golden turmeric chicken and chickpea skillet with corn and yellow pepper
inspiredBy: Inspired by an Indian-style turmeric chicken, with lemon and sweet corn
about: Chicken and chickpeas simmered in turmeric, cumin and ginger with yellow pepper and sweet corn, finished with lemon and cilantro. A warm, golden skillet with **protein, fibre and iron**, and the lemon helps your body absorb the iron.
steps: Wash the pepper and cilantro. Season the chicken with half the salt, the turmeric, cumin, coriander and ginger and toss to coat.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 minutes, stirring now and then. Wash your hands, the knife and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 4 minutes, until soft, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chickpeas, the frozen corn and about three-quarters of a cup of water. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through at 74 °C (165 °F) and the corn is steaming hot.
Stir in the lemon juice, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Serve in bowls, spoon the cold yogurt on top and scatter with the cilantro.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow: cool and chill it within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep the yogurt separate, keep it up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Swap the chicken breast for thigh if you like it richer, and add 3 minutes.

name: Cumin-lemon salmon on cauliflower and chickpea mash with garlicky spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern spiced fish with a hummus-style mash
about: A cumin-and-paprika seared salmon fillet with a garlicky lemon pan sauce, on a creamy mash of cauliflower, potato and chickpeas, with garlicky spinach. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas and cauliflower bring fibre, iron and choline.
steps: Wash the cauliflower, potatoes, spinach and cilantro. Put the potato chunks in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 8 minutes. Add the cauliflower and the chickpeas and cook for 8 minutes more, until the vegetables are very tender.

Pat the salmon dry and season with half the salt, the pepper, the cumin and the paprika, then wash your hands, the knife and the board with hot soapy water. Heat half the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the fillet for 4 minutes, until golden. Flip it and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Use fresh salmon the day you buy it, or thaw frozen salmon in the fridge.
In the last minute, add the garlic and the lemon juice to the pan and spoon it over the fish.
Drain the potato, cauliflower and chickpeas and mash them with the milk, the rest of the oil and the rest of the salt until creamy.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan with the garlic left in the pan and a splash of water for 2 minutes, until soft. Serve the salmon on the mash with the spinach and cilantro.
tip: No skin on the fillet? Cook it a minute less on the second side.

name: Red and yellow peppers stuffed with turkey and millet in paprika tomato sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Hungarian stuffed peppers (töltött paprika)
about: Red and yellow pepper halves filled with ground turkey, millet and kale, baked in a sweet paprika tomato sauce until soft and topped with cool yogurt and cilantro. The weekend project of the week, with **protein, fibre and vitamin C** in two colours of pepper.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Rinse the millet and cook it in about 2½ times its volume of water for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender, then spread it on a plate to cool for 10 minutes. Chill it within 1 hour if you are not filling the peppers right away.
Wash the peppers, kale and cilantro. Cut the peppers in half through the stem, remove the seeds and set them cut-side up in a baking dish.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes. Add the garlic, caraway, paprika and smoked paprika for 30 seconds, then the turkey. Cook for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Wash your hands, the spoon and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw turkey.
Stir in half the tomato, the kale, the millet and the salt and cook for 3 minutes, until the kale wilts.

Spoon the filling into the pepper halves. Pour the rest of the tomato around them in the dish with a splash of water and cover with foil. Bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 minutes more, until the peppers are soft and the filling reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
Top with the yogurt, the cilantro and a grind of black pepper. Chill any leftovers within 1 hour in a shallow container and eat within 3 days, reheated until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Stuff the peppers the day before, cover them and bake straight from the fridge, adding 5 minutes.

name: Crispy kale chips with pumpkin seeds
about: Kale roasted until crisp with a little oil, paprika and salt, with a spoonful of pumpkin seeds. A crunchy green snack with **vitamin K, iron and magnesium**.
steps: Heat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). Wash the kale and dry it very well, because wet kale steams instead of crisping.
Toss the kale with the oil, paprika and salt on a tray, spread in a single layer, and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the edges are crisp.
Serve with the pumpkin seeds. Best eaten the same day.
ingredients: washed, dried very well, torn in pieces

name: Green apple slices with almonds
about: Crisp green apple with a handful of almonds. A tart and crunchy snack with **fibre and vitamin E**.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds on the side.

name: Beet and chickpea dip with rainbow veggie sticks
inspiredBy: Inspired by beet hummus, made with pumpkin seeds instead of tahini
about: A magenta dip of chickpeas, cooked beet, lemon and garlic, with red pepper, carrot and cucumber sticks for dunking. It gives you **fibre, folate and a bit of iron**, and the sticks bring vitamin C.
steps: Blend the chickpeas, beet, pumpkin seeds, lemon juice, oil, garlic powder, cumin and salt with 2 tablespoons of water until smooth, adding a little more water if it is stiff.
Wash the pepper, carrot and cucumber and cut them into sticks.
Spoon the dip into a small bowl and serve with the sticks. Keep leftover dip covered in the fridge and use within 3 days.
tip: Make a double batch of the dip, keep it covered in the fridge and use it within 3 days.
ingredients: vacuum-packed cooked beet or home-roasted, roughly chopped

name: Red apple slices with walnuts
about: Crisp red-skinned apple slices with a handful of walnuts. Sweet and crunchy, with **fibre and plant omega-3** from the walnuts.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve it with the walnuts.

name: Mango with almonds
about: Sweet golden mango with a handful of almonds. A tropical snack with **vitamin C, vitamin E and fibre**.
steps: Thaw the mango in a covered bowl in the fridge overnight, or use fresh mango, and serve it in a bowl with the almonds.

name: Orange wedges with pumpkin seeds
about: Juicy orange wedges with toasted pumpkin seeds. Bright and crunchy, with **vitamin C and magnesium**.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Serve with the pumpkin seeds.

name: Blueberries with almonds
about: Plump blueberries with a handful of almonds. Deep blue-purple, sweet and crunchy, with **fibre, vitamin C and vitamin E**.
steps: Rinse the blueberries and serve them with the almonds.

name: Banana with almonds and cinnamon
about: A sliced banana with chopped almonds and a shake of cinnamon. Sweet, soft and crunchy, with **potassium and vitamin E**.
steps: Slice the banana, scatter over the almonds and dust with cinnamon.

name: Golden turmeric roasted chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with turmeric, cumin and a little salt. A crunchy golden snack with **fibre, iron and plant protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Pat the chickpeas very dry with a clean towel.
Toss them on a tray with the oil, turmeric, cumin and salt and roast for 25 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and golden.
Cool on the tray for 10 minutes. They keep best in a jar, up to 3 days.
ingredients: drained, rinsed and patted very dry

name: Golden chia pudding with mango and almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by golden milk, set into a chia pudding
about: Chia seeds soaked overnight in milk with turmeric, cinnamon and ginger until thick like pudding, topped with sweet mango and almonds. A cool golden snack with **plant omega-3, calcium and fibre**.
steps: Stir the milk, chia, turmeric, cinnamon and ginger together in a jar. Wait 5 minutes and stir again so the chia does not clump.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight, until thick and spoonable. Put the mango in a covered bowl in the fridge to thaw at the same time, or use fresh mango.
Top with the mango and the almonds just before eating. Keep it covered in the fridge and eat within 3 days.
tip: Make it the night before. A splash more milk loosens it if it sets too firm.

name: A handful of almonds and walnuts
about: A small handful of almonds and walnuts. Simple and filling, with **vitamin E, plant omega-3 and magnesium**.
steps: Measure out a small handful of each and eat them plain, or toast them in a dry pan for 3 minutes for extra flavour.

name: Cauliflower, carrot and cucumber sticks with lemon-garlic chickpea dip
inspiredBy: Inspired by hummus, made without tahini
about: A creamy, pale dip of chickpeas, lemon and garlic with raw cauliflower, carrot and cucumber for dunking. Crunchy and fresh, with **fibre, iron and plant protein**, and carrot for a little vitamin A.
steps: Blend the chickpeas, lemon juice, oil, garlic powder, cumin and salt with 2 tablespoons of water until smooth, adding a little more water if it is stiff.
Wash the cauliflower, carrot and cucumber and cut them into small florets and sticks.
Serve the vegetables with the dip. Keep the dip covered in the fridge and use it within 3 days.

name: Apple slices with cinnamon and pumpkin seeds
about: Crisp apple slices dusted with cinnamon, with pumpkin seeds on the side. Sweet and crunchy, with **fibre and magnesium**.
steps: Wash and slice the apple, dust it with the cinnamon and serve with the pumpkin seeds.

name: Maple flax oat porridge with yogurt and orange juice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Canadian flax porridge with maple
about: Creamy oats cooked in milk with cinnamon and a spoon of ground flax, in the spirit of Canadian flax porridge, topped with cold Greek yogurt and a drizzle of maple, with a glass of orange juice alongside. It is a **carb-first start with real protein** from the milk and yogurt, and it sits easily before a session.
steps: Put the oats, milk, a splash of water, the cinnamon, the ground flax and the salt in a small pot over medium heat. Stir often until the porridge is thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, add the Greek yogurt in a cold spoonful on top and drizzle with the maple syrup.
Serve with the glass of orange juice.
tip: Stir the yogurt in only at the end so you get hot and cool in the same spoonful.

name: Egg rice bowl with spinach and miso soup
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Japanese teishoku breakfast
about: A Japanese-style breakfast: scrambled eggs and soy-dressed spinach over steamed rice, with a small bowl of miso soup and a glass of orange juice. It gives you **plenty of rice for the day ahead** and a good share of protein from the eggs.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear. Cook it covered in a rice cooker or a small pot with a little more than its own volume of water, about 15 minutes, then rest it 5 minutes with the lid on.

While the rice cooks, wash the spinach and scallion, then wilt half the spinach in a dry hot pan for 1 minute, press out the water and toss it with a few drops of the soy sauce. Keep the other half raw for the soup.
Heat 250 ml of water until steaming, not boiling. Whisk the miso into a ladle of it, pour it back in, then add the raw spinach and half the scallion. Keep it just below a simmer for 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the rest of the soy sauce. Scramble them gently in the canola oil over medium heat until no runny egg is left and they are fully set, about 3 minutes.
Pile the rice in a bowl, top with the spinach and eggs, and scatter over the rest of the scallion. Serve with the miso soup and the orange juice.
tip: Set the rice cooker on a timer the night before.

name: Huevos rancheros with black beans on corn tortillas
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos rancheros
about: Fried eggs on warm corn tortillas under a quick cooked tomato and chili sauce, with black beans on the side. It is a **carbs, protein and fibre** breakfast, with tomato and lime in the sauce for vitamin C.
steps: Wash the tomato and cilantro. Warm the canola oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion with the chili powder and cumin until soft, about 3 minutes, then add the chopped tomato and the salt. Simmer 6 minutes until thick, then stir in the lime juice.
Warm the black beans in a small pot with a splash of water until steaming. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, about 30 seconds a side.
Make a well in the sauce for each egg, crack them in, cover and cook until the whites and yolks are set, about 6 minutes.
Lay the tortillas on a plate, spoon over the beans, slide the eggs and sauce on top and finish with the cilantro.
tip: Make the sauce the night before if you like. It keeps up to 3 days in the fridge, so make it fresh for each of the two mornings.

name: Tuna, white bean and tomato pasta salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian insalata di pasta al tonno
about: A cool Italian-style pasta salad of tuna, creamy white beans, juicy tomato and spinach in a lemon and olive oil dressing. It packs **plenty of carbs and protein**, and keeps well in a lunch box.
steps: Boil the pasta in plenty of water until just tender, about 10 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool, which stops it going gluey.
Wash the tomato, spinach and onion. Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, dried basil, pepper and salt in a bowl. Add the onion and leave it for a few minutes to soften.
Add the pasta, beans, tomato, spinach and tuna and toss until everything is coated.
Eat it cold. Cool the pasta fast and refrigerate it within 1 hour. If you carry the salad, keep it cold and eat it within 2 hours.
tip: Cook the pasta the night before and dress it just before you eat. Keep the rest of the tuna tin in a lidded container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
ingredients: short pasta such as penne or fusilli

name: Maple white beans on toast with a glass of milk
inspiredBy: Inspired by Quebec baked beans
about: Soft white beans simmered in a tomato, maple and mustard sauce piled onto thick whole wheat toast. It is quick Canadian comfort food, and the beans, toast and milk give you **carbs, fibre and plenty of protein**.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a small pot and soften the onion, about 4 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes, beans, maple syrup, mustard, a splash of water, the salt and the pepper. Simmer gently, stirring now and then, for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Toast the bread and spoon the beans over it. Serve with the glass of milk.
tip: Make a double batch of the beans, cool it within 2 hours and keep it up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Tuna and black bean tostadas with fresh pico
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican tostadas de atun
about: Crisp baked corn tortillas piled with chili and lime tuna, black beans and a fresh tomato, onion and cilantro pico. It is crunchy, tangy and **carb-rich with lots of protein**.
steps: Wash the tomato and cilantro. Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Brush the tortillas with the olive oil, lay them on a tray and bake 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until crisp and lightly golden. If you have more than 4 tortillas on your plate, keep 3 or 4 whole as tostadas and break the rest into chips for scooping.
Make the pico by mixing the tomato, onion, cilantro, half the lime juice and a pinch of the salt.
Warm the beans in a small pot with the cumin and a splash of water, mashing a few, for 3 minutes.
Mix the tuna with the chili powder, the rest of the lime juice, the salt and a spoon of the pico juice for moisture.
Spread the beans on the tostadas, then top with the tuna and the pico. Eat straight away so they stay crisp.
tip: Open a fresh tin for this one. Keep any spare tuna in a lidded container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

name: Beef and potato stew with ugali and sukuma wiki
inspiredBy: Inspired by Kenyan beef stew with ugali and sukuma wiki
about: A Kenyan-style home stew of tender beef, potato and carrot in a tomato and ginger sauce, served with firm white ugali and sukuma wiki, collard greens cooked with onion and tomato. It is **a big, carb-rich plate with iron** from the beef and greens, and a squeeze of lemon helps your body absorb it.
steps: Wash all the vegetables. Pat the beef dry and season with half the salt, the pepper and the cumin. Brown it in half the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat, about 6 minutes, then lift it out. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
In the same pot, cook half the onion, the garlic and the ginger until soft, about 4 minutes. Add half the tomato and the turmeric and cook down for 4 minutes.
Return the beef, add enough water to just cover it, cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes. Add the potato and carrot and simmer 20 minutes more, until the beef is tender and the potatoes are soft.

For the sukuma wiki, cook the rest of the onion in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, add the rest of the tomato and the collards and cook 6 to 8 minutes until wilted and tender. Add the rest of the salt and half the lemon juice.

For the ugali, bring water to a boil, about 2 cups for every cup of cornmeal. Pour in the cornmeal in a steady stream, stirring hard with a wooden spoon, and keep pressing and turning for 6 minutes until it pulls away from the pot as a firm mound.

Finish the stew with the rest of the lemon juice and the cilantro. Serve the ugali with the stew and greens. Put the second portion in a shallow container, refrigerate within 1 hour (the ugali is a cooked grain) and use it within 3 days. Reheat once, covered, with a splash of water, until steaming hot (74 °C).
tip: A pressure cooker does the beef in 25 minutes. Use white maize meal (unga) from an African or Latin grocer if you can; a fine cornmeal makes a smoother ugali than a coarse polenta grind.

name: Ginger soy salmon rice bowl with spinach and carrot
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese salmon teriyaki donburi
about: Pan-seared salmon glazed with soy, ginger and maple on short-grain rice, with garlicky spinach and shredded carrot. It is a Japanese-style bowl with **omega-3 fats and plenty of rice** after a long day.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it covered in a rice cooker or small pot, about 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes with the lid on.
Stir the soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger and half the lime juice in a small pot and simmer for 1 minute until slightly syrupy. This glaze only touches cooked fish.
Wash the spinach, carrot and scallion. Wilt the spinach with the garlic in a hot dry pan, about 1 minute. Squeeze out the water and toss with the rest of the lime juice.

Pat the salmon dry. Sear it in the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat, about 4 minutes a side, until the centre reaches 70 °C and flakes easily. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Pile the rice in a bowl and add the spinach and carrot. Lay the salmon on top, spoon over the glaze and finish with the scallion.
tip: Eat the salmon the day you cook it. Fish is best fresh.

name: Chicken in salsa verde with Mexican carrot rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican pollo en salsa verde and arroz con zanahoria
about: Chicken thighs simmered in a tangy tomatillo and cilantro sauce, served over fluffy rice cooked with carrot and onion. It is a Mexican home classic with **rice for the carbs and lean protein**, and it tastes even better the next day.
steps: Wash the tomatillos, carrot and cilantro. Put the tomatillos, half the onion and the garlic in a pot with water to cover and boil for 8 minutes until the tomatillos turn olive green and soft. Drain, and blend with the cilantro, lime juice and half the salt into a sauce.
Season the chicken with the cumin and a pinch of the salt. Brown it in half the oil in a wide pan for 5 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes until the chicken reaches 74 °C and the sauce has thickened.

Meanwhile dice the rest of the onion and cook it with the carrot in the remaining oil for 3 minutes. Stir in the rice for 1 minute, add about twice its volume of water and the rest of the salt, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes, then fluff.

Serve the chicken and sauce over the rice. Cool the second portion of rice within 1 hour, then refrigerate it and the chicken in shallow containers and reheat once to steaming hot (74 °C) for tomorrow.
tip: Canned tomatillos work if you cannot find fresh.

name: Maple mustard turkey with mashed potatoes and garlicky spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Canadian maple and mustard roasts
about: Turkey breast roasted with a sticky maple and Dijon glaze and carrots on the tray, with a big pile of creamy skin-on mashed potatoes and garlicky spinach. It is a Canadian Sunday dinner that works on a weeknight, with **potatoes for carbs** and lean protein from the turkey.
steps: Wash the carrots, potatoes and spinach. Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Stir the mustard, maple syrup, half the garlic and the thyme together.

Toss the carrots with a third of the canola oil and a little of the salt on a tray. Rub the turkey with the glaze and set it in the middle. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Roast for 18 to 22 minutes, until the thickest part of the turkey reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the carrots are tender. Rest the turkey 5 minutes.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in water for 15 to 18 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain and mash with half the remaining oil, the warm milk, most of the remaining salt and the pepper.
Wilt the spinach with the rest of the garlic in the last of the oil in a hot pan, about 1 minute, and season with the last pinch of salt.

Serve the turkey over the mash with the carrots, spinach and the bread on the side. Put the second portion in a shallow container, refrigerate within 2 hours. Tomorrow, slice the turkey and reheat it covered in a pan with a splash of water, so it stays moist, until steaming hot (74 °C).
tip: Dijon mustard, soy sauce and miso are used in small amounts for flavour; swap in any you like.
ingredients: a whole wheat roll or slice

name: Spaghetti with sardines, tomato, lemon and garlic breadcrumbs
inspiredBy: Inspired by Sicilian spaghetti with sardines and toasted breadcrumbs
about: Spaghetti in a quick garlicky tomato sauce with sardines, wilted spinach, lemon and crisp toasted breadcrumbs. It is a southern Italian-style pasta night with **carbs and omega-3 fats**, and the sardine bones add calcium.
steps: Wash the spinach. Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook the spaghetti until just tender, about 10 minutes. Save a mug of the pasta water, then drain.
While it cooks, toast the bread crumbs with a third of the olive oil in a pan over medium heat until golden, 3 to 4 minutes. Tip them out and wipe the pan.
Warm the rest of the oil in the pan and cook the garlic and cayenne for 30 seconds. Add the crushed tomatoes, dried basil and a splash of pasta water and simmer 8 minutes.
Stir in the sardines, breaking them up, and the spinach. Cook until the spinach wilts, 2 minutes.
Toss in the pasta with the lemon juice, a splash of pasta water and the salt. Top with the toasted breadcrumbs.
tip: Keep a tin of sardines in the cupboard for this one.

name: Slow beef and white bean ragu on soft polenta
inspiredBy: Inspired by northern Italian ragu on polenta
about: A slow-cooked tomato ragu of tender shredded beef and white beans with carrot and collards, spooned over creamy polenta. It is **a rich weekend pot** that makes two portions, with corn for carbs and beef and beans for iron.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Pat the beef dry and brown it in the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat, about 6 minutes, then lift it out. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
In the same pot, cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic and rosemary for 1 minute.

Return the beef, add the crushed tomatoes, bay leaf, half the salt and a cup of water. Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the beef is very tender and falls apart. Stir in the beans and the collards for the last 10 minutes, until the collards are tender, then break up the beef with a spoon.

For the polenta, bring water to a boil, about 4 cups for every cup of cornmeal, with the rest of the salt. Whisk in the cornmeal in a thin stream, turn the heat low and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until thick and creamy. Add water if it gets stiff.

Stir the pepper into the polenta. Spoon the ragu over it. Put the second portion in shallow containers, refrigerate within 1 hour (the polenta is a cooked grain) and reheat once with a splash of water to steaming hot (74 °C).
tip: The pressure cooker does the beef in 35 minutes. To freeze, cool the ragu within 1 hour and freeze it the same day. Thaw it in the fridge, use it within 2 days and reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F). Eat the polenta fresh or reheat it with a splash of water.

name: Chicken pilau with kachumbari
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swahili pilau and kachumbari
about: A Kenyan coastal-style pilau: rice cooked with browned onion, chicken and warm spices, with a fresh tomato and onion kachumbari on the side. It is a **one-pot rice dinner** that is mild and rich in carbs, and the kachumbari brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the rice and let it drain, and wash the onion, tomato and cilantro. Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook two thirds of the sliced onion over medium heat until deep golden, about 12 minutes.

Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, cardamom, cinnamon, clove and pepper and stir for 1 minute. Add the chicken and brown it for 5 minutes, then about a third of the chopped tomato. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Stir in the rice and the salt, then pour in enough water to sit about 1 cm above the rice. Bring to a boil, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes.
Leave it covered for 10 minutes, then check that the chicken is at 74 °C and fluff gently.
For the kachumbari, mix the rest of the tomato, diced, with the remaining raw onion, the cilantro, lime juice and a pinch of salt. Serve it alongside the pilau.
Cool any extra rice within 1 hour and refrigerate.
ingredients: chopped, some for the pilau and some for the kachumbari

name: Banana and maple toast
about: Whole wheat toast with sliced banana and a drizzle of maple syrup. It is quick, easy on the stomach and **steady carbs before you head out**.
steps: Toast the bread until lightly golden.
Lay the banana slices on top, drizzle with the maple syrup and finish with the tiniest pinch of salt.
tip: Eat it 30 to 60 minutes before a session.

name: Rice cakes with almond butter and maple
about: Crisp rice cakes spread with almond butter and a thin drizzle of maple. It is **light, easy carbs** for a pre-session snack, with a little vitamin E from the almonds, and it travels well in a jersey pocket or bag.
steps: Spread the almond butter on the rice cakes.
Drizzle with the maple syrup and eat straight away, or wrap them for the bag.

name: Salted baby potatoes with olive oil and lemon
about: Small potatoes boiled until tender, tossed in olive oil and lemon with a good pinch of salt. It is a savoury **carb and salt snack** that is easy to eat before a long session, and it is a favourite on long rides.
steps: Scrub the potatoes. Put them in a pot of cold water with a pinch of salt, bring to a boil and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Drain and let them steam dry for a minute. Toss with the olive oil, lemon juice and the rest of the salt.
Eat them warm or at room temperature. Refrigerate any that are left within 2 hours, in a lidded container.
tip: Boil a double batch and keep half in the fridge for up to 3 days. For a long ride or run, pack them with an ice pack, or eat them within 2 hours of leaving the fridge (1 hour on a hot day).

name: Almond butter oat bites
about: No-bake bites of rolled oats, almond butter, maple and cinnamon rolled into small balls. They give you **slow carbs and a little vitamin E** and fit in a pocket.
steps: Mix the oats, almond butter, maple syrup, cinnamon and salt with a teaspoon of water until it holds together.
Roll into 4 or 5 small balls. Eat straight away or chill for 20 minutes to firm up.

name: Homemade chocolate milk with a banana
about: Cold milk whisked with cocoa and a little maple syrup, with a banana on the side. It is the classic recovery pairing of **carbs and protein**, with no powders needed.
steps: Whisk the cocoa and maple syrup with a splash of warm milk until smooth, then stir in the rest of the cold milk.
Drink it with the banana.
tip: Shake it in a bottle and keep it cold in a cooler bag with an ice pack until you drink it.

name: Greek yogurt with mango and toasted oats
about: Thick Greek yogurt with sweet mango, maple and a crunch of toasted oats. It brings **protein and carbs together** after a session.
steps: Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, shaking, until they smell nutty. Let them cool.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the mango, the toasted oats, the maple syrup and a pinch of cinnamon.

name: Egg, tomato and yogurt sandwich
about: Chopped hard-boiled eggs mixed with Greek yogurt, mustard and lemon, with tomato and spinach in whole wheat bread. It is a savoury, **protein and carb recovery snack** that holds up in a lunchbox.
steps: Wash the tomato and spinach. Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil, then cover and leave off the heat for 11 minutes. Cool in cold water and peel.
Chop the eggs and mash them with the yogurt, mustard, lemon juice, pepper and salt.
Pile onto one slice of bread, add the tomato and spinach, and top with the second slice. Keep it cold if you are carrying it, and eat within 2 hours.

name: Mango banana oat smoothie
about: Milk, Greek yogurt, banana, mango and a spoonful of oats blended thick. It is **an easy drink of carbs and protein** when you do not feel like chewing after a session.
steps: Put everything in a blender and blend for about a minute until smooth and thick.
Add a splash of milk if it is too thick. Drink it straight away.

name: Arroz con leche with cinnamon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican arroz con leche
about: Creamy rice simmered slowly in milk with cinnamon and a strip of lemon peel, sweetened with a little maple syrup and eaten warm or chilled. It is a Mexican-style rice pudding that gives you **easy carbs plus the protein of milk**, and it is the extra snack on the bigger days.
steps: Wash the lemon and pare off one wide strip of peel, leaving the white pith behind. Put the rinsed rice, milk, cinnamon, lemon peel and salt in a small heavy pot over medium-low heat. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often so it does not catch.
Cook uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice is very soft and the milk has thickened to a creamy pudding.
Fish out the lemon peel and stir in the maple syrup. Eat it warm, or cool it within 1 hour, chill it in a lidded container and eat it within 2 days.
tip: Make it the day you eat it, or the night before: it is lovely cold. Many Mexican cooks use a strip of lime peel instead of lemon, so use whichever you have.
ingredients: one wide strip, no white pith

name: Banana and date oat porridge with skyr and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic Canadian oatmeal breakfast, with skyr for protein
about: Oats simmered in milk with cinnamon and mashed banana, sweetened by chopped dates and topped with a cold spoonful of skyr and crunchy walnuts. It is an easy **slow-burning carb start**, with plenty of protein, so have it 2 to 3 hours before a hard morning session. If you train soon after waking, have a pre-session snack first and the porridge after.
steps: Put the oats, milk, a splash of water, the cinnamon, the salt and the chopped dates in a small pot over medium heat. Stir often until the porridge is thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the mashed banana for the last minute so it melts into the porridge.
Spoon into a bowl, add the cold skyr on top and scatter over the walnuts.
tip: Chop the dates the night before so the morning takes five minutes.

name: Warm buckwheat porridge with apple, skyr and sunflower seeds
inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European kasha porridge
about: Toasted buckwheat groats simmered in milk until soft, with sliced apple, cinnamon and a drizzle of honey, finished with skyr and toasted sunflower seeds. A warm, nutty Eastern European-style porridge that gives you **steady carbs** and good protein.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat in a sieve. Toast it in a dry small pot over medium heat for 2 minutes until it smells nutty.
Add the milk, a splash of water, the cinnamon and the salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 12 minutes, stirring once, until the groats are soft and the porridge is thick.
Stir in most of the sliced apple for the last 2 minutes so it softens.
Spoon into a bowl, top with the skyr, the last of the apple and the sunflower seeds, and drizzle with the honey.
tip: Cook it the evening before: cool within 1 hour in a shallow covered container, chill, and reheat with a splash of milk until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). Honey is not for babies under 1.

name: Spanish potato and spinach omelette with an orange
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish tortilla de patatas, with spinach added
about: A thick Spanish-style omelette of tender potato, sweet onion and spinach, cooked through until the eggs are fully set and golden, with a juicy orange alongside. A **hearty, savoury weekend breakfast** with plenty of carbs and good protein from the eggs.
steps: Wash and scrub the potatoes, then slice them very thinly. Warm the olive oil in a 20 cm non-stick pan over medium-low heat, add the potato and onion with a pinch of the iodized salt, cover and cook for 12 minutes, turning once or twice, until the potato is tender.
Add the washed spinach and stir for 1 minute until wilted. Spread the vegetables evenly in the pan.
Beat the eggs with the rest of the salt and the pepper and pour them over the vegetables. Cook over low heat for 6 minutes until the bottom is set and golden.

Finish the top under a hot broiler for 3 minutes if the pan handle is ovenproof (or flip the omelette onto a plate and slide it back into the pan for 3 minutes) until the eggs are completely firm, with no runny egg left in the centre.
Serve in wedges with the peeled orange.
tip: Slice the potatoes the evening before and keep them in the fridge in a covered bowl of water; drain and pat dry before cooking. Use a 24 cm pan at the bigger sizes.

name: Smashed sweet potato with smoky beans, firm eggs and an orange
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican breakfast beans and eggs
about: Soft chunks of sweet potato smashed with cumin and lemon, topped with warm kidney beans, firm-scrambled eggs and scallion, with an orange alongside. A **savoury, dairy-free breakfast** with slow carbs, plant protein and eggs, ready in about 25 minutes.
steps: Wash the sweet potato and scallion. Microwave the sweet potato chunks covered for 6 minutes, or boil for 12 minutes, until very tender. Smash roughly with a fork with the lemon juice, half the cumin and a pinch of the iodized salt.
Warm the rinsed kidney beans with the rest of the cumin, the smoked paprika and a splash of water in a small pan for 4 minutes until steaming hot.
Beat the eggs with the pepper. Warm the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and scramble the eggs for 3 minutes, stirring, until completely firm with no liquid egg left.
Pile the sweet potato on a plate, top with the beans and eggs and the scallion, and serve with the peeled orange.
tip: Cook the sweet potato the night before, cool it within 2 hours, keep it covered in the fridge and reheat until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Salmon and potato cakes with dill skyr and a crunchy carrot salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian fish cakes and Canadian salmon patties
about: Golden pan-seared cakes of canned salmon, mashed potato and oats, served with a cool dill skyr sauce and a quick carrot, cucumber and sunflower seed salad. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats and a solid hit of protein**, and the potato and oats keep the carbs coming.
steps: Boil the potato cubes in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes until very tender. Drain well, return them to the pot for a minute to steam dry, then mash roughly and let cool for 10 minutes.

Wash the scallion, dill, carrot and cucumber. Mash the drained salmon (soft bones and all) into the potato with the oats, beaten egg, scallion, half the dill, half the lemon juice and the pepper. Shape into 2 or 3 thick patties.
Heat the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the cakes for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden and hot through, 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle.
While they cook, toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then toss them with the grated carrot, sliced cucumber, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of the iodized salt.
Stir the rest of the dill and lemon into the skyr and spoon it beside the cakes and salad.
tip: Shape the patties the evening before and keep them covered in the fridge, then fry at lunch. Cool any cooked cakes within 1 hour; keep up to 2 days and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). If you pack them, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.

name: Greek-style lemon chickpeas with potatoes, spinach and a firm egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek revithada, with potatoes added
about: Chickpeas and potatoes simmered with onion, garlic, rosemary and plenty of lemon until the sauce turns silky, with spinach wilted in and a quartered firm egg on top, a bit like the Greek baked chickpeas called revithada. It is **cosy, lemony and filling**, with chickpeas and egg for protein and potatoes for carbs.
steps: Cover the egg with cold water, bring to a boil and cook 10 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water, peel and quarter it.
Meanwhile, wash the potatoes and spinach. Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and rosemary for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes, chickpeas, salt, pepper and enough water to just cover. Simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, crushing a few potato chunks to thicken the sauce, until the potatoes are tender.
Fold in the spinach and half the lemon juice and cook 2 minutes until wilted.
Spoon into a bowl, top with the egg and a dollop of skyr stirred with the rest of the lemon juice.
tip: Make the stew the evening before without the egg or skyr: cool within 1 hour, keep covered in the fridge up to 3 days and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Add a freshly boiled egg.

name: Beef and kidney bean beet soup with cabbage, dill skyr and an apple
inspiredBy: Inspired by Ukrainian borscht, without the potato and the rye bread
about: A ruby beet and cabbage soup with browned beef, kidney beans, carrot and a squeeze of lemon, finished with a spoon of dill skyr. The beans and beef make it **filling and high in protein**, and the beets add natural sweetness and potassium. An apple on the side rounds out the carbs.
steps: Wash and prepare the vegetables. Warm the canola oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the ground beef with the onion for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 71 °C (160 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the beet, carrot, cabbage, bay leaf, salt, pepper and enough water to cover by a thumb-width.
Simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes until the beets are tender. Add the rinsed kidney beans and simmer 5 more minutes, then add the lemon juice. Remove the bay leaf.
Stir half the dill into the skyr. Ladle the borscht into a bowl, add a spoonful of the dill skyr, scatter over the rest of the dill and eat the washed apple on the side.
tip: Make it the evening before; it tastes better the next day. Cool within 1 hour, chill, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). The beets stain, so use a dark cutting board.

name: Jerk chicken and sweet potato traybake with coconut spinach and lemon onions
inspiredBy: Inspired by Jamaican jerk chicken, as a one-tray dinner with sweet potato and coconut spinach
about: Chicken thighs rubbed with a quick jerk paste of allspice, thyme, scallion, garlic and cayenne, roasted on one tray with sweet potato wedges, then served with creamy coconut spinach and sharp lemon-pickled onions. A **big tray of slow carbs** with lots of protein, and enough left for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Mix the sliced onion with half the lemon juice and a pinch of the iodized salt in a small bowl and leave it to pickle while you cook.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Mix half the scallion, the garlic, ginger, cayenne, the rest of the lemon juice, half the canola oil, the allspice, thyme, pepper and half the salt into a paste. Rub it all over the raw chicken, cover and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes to 4 hours. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken, and never reuse the marinade.

Toss the sweet potato wedges with the rest of the oil on a tray and roast for 10 minutes. Add the chicken to the tray and roast 20 to 25 minutes more, turning the wedges once, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the wedges are tender and browned.
While the tray roasts, warm the coconut milk with the rest of the scallion and a splash of water in a pan for 3 minutes. Add the washed spinach and stir 2 minutes until just wilted.
Rest the chicken on a clean plate for 5 minutes, then slice it. Serve with the wedges, the coconut spinach and the drained onions.
Put the second portion in a shallow container, cool within 1 hour and chill; eat it tomorrow, reheated to 74 °C (165 °F), with the onions kept cold.
tip: No scotch bonnet needed: cayenne gives the heat. Mix the paste the night before and marinate for up to 4 hours on the day. Leave out the cayenne for a milder, kid-friendly version.

name: Berbere beef and red lentil stew with spinach and millet
inspiredBy: Inspired by Ethiopian minchet abish and misir wot, without injera
about: Lean beef simmered with red lentils, onion, ginger, garlic and warming berbere until thick and saucy, with spinach folded in and a mound of fluffy millet underneath. It is a **rich, hearty stew** with plenty of protein, and it tastes even better the next day.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Cook the millet: toast the rinsed millet in a dry pot for 2 minutes, add about twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes with the lid on and fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, warm the oil in a wide pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and berbere and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and brown it for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.

Stir in the tomato paste, lentils, carrot, the salt and enough water to cover by a thumb-width. Simmer, stirring now and then, for 18 minutes until the lentils have melted into a thick stew and the beef is at 71 °C (160 °F).
Fold in the washed spinach and cook 2 minutes until wilted, then finish with the lemon juice. Spoon over the millet.
Put the second portion, with its millet, in a shallow container, cool within 1 hour and chill. Use it tomorrow, reheated to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: No berbere? Mix paprika, a little cayenne, cumin, ginger, allspice and cinnamon. Cool within 1 hour; freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Salmon and potato chowder with carrot, dill and lemon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Canadian fish chowders and Scandinavian laxsoppa
about: A creamy, chunky chowder of tender potato, carrot and onion, with flaked salmon, milk and plenty of fresh dill and lemon, with crunchy sunflower seeds on top. It is **comfort food that fuels recovery**: salmon brings omega-3 fats and protein, and the potatoes bring the carbs.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes and set aside. Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion and carrot with the thyme for 6 minutes.
Add the potatoes, the salt and enough water to just cover. Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender. Crush a few pieces against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.
Stir in the milk and warm gently for 3 minutes without boiling. The crushed potato gives the chowder its body.
Flake in the drained salmon, bones and all (they mash in easily), and warm through for 3 minutes until steaming hot. Add the lemon juice, pepper and most of the dill.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the rest of the dill and the toasted sunflower seeds. Tip any leftover canned salmon into a covered container, chill it and use it within 2 days.
tip: Eat the chowder the same day; if you have extra, cool it within 1 hour and use it within 2 days, reheated to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Turkey picadillo with carrots, raisins and quinoa
inspiredBy: Inspired by Cuban and Mexican picadillo, served over quinoa
about: A Cuban- and Mexican-style picadillo: ground turkey simmered with tomato, carrot, raisins, garlic and cumin, finished with lemon and cilantro and spooned over fluffy quinoa. The sweet raisins and bright lemon make it a **lean, savoury-sweet plate** with plenty of lean protein, and it is even better the next day.
steps: Cook the quinoa: simmer the rinsed quinoa in about twice its volume of water with a pinch of the iodized salt, covered, for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Meanwhile, wash the vegetables. Warm the canola oil in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the onion and carrot for 7 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and cinnamon and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the ground turkey and cook for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Add the crushed tomatoes, raisins, salt and pepper. Simmer for 12 minutes until thick and glossy and the turkey has reached 74 °C (165 °F). Stir in the lemon juice and half the cilantro.

Serve the picadillo over the quinoa with the rest of the cilantro. Put the second portion, with its quinoa, in a shallow container, cool within 1 hour and chill. Use it tomorrow, reheated to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Paprika mackerel with crushed potatoes and green beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish and Portuguese grilled mackerel with potatoes
about: Atlantic mackerel fillets pan-seared with smoked paprika and garlic, on a bed of olive oil crushed potatoes and bright green beans, finished with lemon and scallion. Mackerel is one of the richest fish for **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the potatoes carry the carbs.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily, adding the green beans for the last 4 minutes. Drain well.
Crush the potatoes lightly with a fork in the pot, then toss with half the olive oil, half the lemon juice, the pepper and half the scallion. Keep warm with the green beans.
Pat the mackerel dry and season with the smoked paprika and a pinch of the iodized salt. Heat the rest of the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.

Cook the mackerel skin-side down for 4 minutes until crisp, then flip, add the sliced garlic and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until the garlic is golden and the fish flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Serve the fish on the potatoes and green beans with the rest of the lemon juice and scallion.
tip: Ask the fishmonger to remove the pin bones. Buy the fish the day you cook it, or thaw frozen fillets overnight in the fridge. Eat the same day.

name: Chickpea and spinach masala with cucumber raita and millet
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian chana masala and cucumber raita, over millet
about: Chickpeas simmered in an onion, tomato, ginger and garam masala sauce with spinach, spooned over fluffy millet and cooled by a creamy cucumber and skyr raita. A **plant-forward dinner** with plenty of protein from chickpeas, skyr and millet.
steps: Cook the millet: toast the rinsed millet in a dry pot for 2 minutes, add about twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes with the lid on and fluff with a fork.

Meanwhile, wash the vegetables and cilantro. Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 7 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric and cayenne and stir for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and the salt and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the chickpeas and 100 ml of water and simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Fold in the spinach and the garam masala and cook for 2 minutes until wilted. Finish with the lemon juice and half the cilantro.
Stir the grated cucumber into the skyr with a pinch of salt for the raita. Serve the masala over the millet with the raita on the side and the rest of the cilantro on top.

Put the second portion, with its millet, in a shallow container, cool within 1 hour and chill; keep the raita covered in its own container. Use both tomorrow, reheating the masala and millet to 74 °C (165 °F) and serving the raita cold.
tip: Skyr is easy to find in most supermarkets, but plain Greek yogurt works too, and hulled millet from the bulk section is fine. Freeze the masala without the raita: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Piri-piri chicken with tomato quinoa and green beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by Portuguese piri-piri chicken, served with tomato quinoa
about: Chicken thighs marinated in a fiery lemon, garlic, cayenne and smoked paprika paste, roasted until sticky and served over a soft tomato quinoa cooked like Portuguese tomato rice, with green beans. A **weekend favourite** with lots of protein and a bright, hot kick you can dial up or down.
steps: Mix half the garlic with the lemon juice, half the olive oil, the smoked paprika, cayenne, pepper and a third of the salt. Add the raw chicken, turn to coat, cover and marinate in the fridge for 1 to 4 hours. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken, and never reuse the marinade.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Lift the chicken onto a tray, discard the marinade and roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is browned and reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Rest it on a clean plate.

Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the rest of the garlic, then the rinsed quinoa and crushed tomatoes, a splash of water and the rest of the salt. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Steam or boil the washed green beans for 4 minutes until tender but still bright.
Serve the sliced chicken over the tomato quinoa with the green beans.
tip: Eat it the same day, or cool within 1 hour, keep up to 2 days and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Use half the cayenne for a milder version.

name: Peanut butter stuffed dates
about: Soft medjool dates split and filled with smooth peanut butter and a tiny pinch of salt. Quick **natural sugars to top up** your fuel before a session, with a little fat and protein to keep the stomach happy.
steps: Slit each date open along one side and take out the pit.
Fill each one with peanut butter, add the tiniest pinch of the iodized salt and press closed.
Eat 30 to 60 minutes before training.

name: Peanut butter banana halves with honey
about: A ripe banana sliced in half lengthwise, spread with peanut butter and drizzled with honey. An old athlete favourite that gives you **fast carbs and potassium** and sits lightly before a workout.
steps: Peel the banana and slice it in half lengthwise.
Spread the peanut butter over the cut sides and drizzle with the honey.
Eat 30 to 60 minutes before training.
tip: Honey is not for babies under 1.

name: Oat and date energy bites
about: No-bake bites of rolled oats, mashed dates and peanut butter with a pinch of cinnamon. They give **slow oat carbs and quick date sugars** in one portable snack, ideal for a jersey pocket.
steps: Mash the pitted dates with a fork, or pulse them in a food processor, until sticky.
Mix in the oats, peanut butter, cinnamon and salt until it holds together; add a teaspoon of water if it is dry.
Roll into small balls. They keep in a covered container in the fridge for up to 5 days.

name: Apple slices with raisins, walnuts and cinnamon
about: Crisp apple slices tossed with plump raisins, chopped walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. A **light, juicy pre-session snack** with quick fruit carbs and a little crunch.
steps: Wash the apple, core it and cut it into slices.
Toss with the raisins, walnuts and cinnamon in a bowl.
Eat 30 to 60 minutes before training.

name: Cinnamon sweet potato rounds with honey
about: Thick rounds of sweet potato cooked until soft, dusted with cinnamon and a little salt and drizzled with honey. Gentle on the stomach and **a slow, easy carb top-up**, a favourite with long-distance riders.
steps: Wash the sweet potato and cut it into rounds about 2 cm thick.
Microwave them covered for 5 to 6 minutes, or roast at 200 °C (400 °F) for 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Dust with the cinnamon and the iodized salt and drizzle with the honey. Eat warm, 60 to 90 minutes before training.
tip: Honey is not for babies under 1.

name: Orange segments with medjool dates
about: Juicy orange segments with soft medjool dates. Simple, sweet and **easy on the stomach**, with quick carbs and vitamin C before you head out.
steps: Wash and peel the orange and break it into segments.
Serve with the pitted dates. Eat 30 to 60 minutes before training.

name: Skyr with warm cinnamon apple and toasted oats
about: Cold, thick skyr over warm cinnamon apple and crunchy toasted oats, like a quick apple crisp. A **recovery snack with plenty of protein** and fruit carbs to refill.
steps: Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden and fragrant, then tip them out.
Cook the diced apple in the same pan with a splash of water, the cinnamon and the honey for 4 minutes until soft.
Spoon the skyr into a bowl, top with the warm apple and the toasted oats.
tip: Honey is not for babies under 1.

name: Peanut butter banana smoothie with skyr
about: A thick blender smoothie of milk, skyr, banana and peanut butter. Drink it within an hour or two of finishing a session for **plenty of protein** and quick carbs in a form you can finish even when you are not hungry.
steps: Put the milk, skyr, banana, peanut butter and cinnamon in a blender.
Blend until smooth, about 30 seconds, and drink right away.

name: Skyr with chopped dates, walnuts, sunflower seeds and cinnamon
about: Thick skyr stirred with chopped dates and cinnamon, topped with walnuts and sunflower seeds. A **recovery snack with plenty of protein**, plus quick date sugars and a little omega-3 fat from the walnuts.
steps: Stir the chopped dates and cinnamon into the skyr.
Top with the walnuts and sunflower seeds.

name: Salted baby potatoes with firm-boiled eggs and an orange
about: Small potatoes boiled until tender and tossed with olive oil and a good pinch of salt, with two firm-boiled eggs and a juicy orange. A **salty, savoury recovery snack** with real protein, as welcome after a long sweaty session as it is simple.
steps: Cover the eggs with cold water in a pot, bring to a boil and cook 10 minutes until the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in a separate pot of water for 15 to 18 minutes until tender, then drain and toss with the olive oil, the iodized salt and the pepper.
Serve the warm potatoes with the halved eggs and the orange segments. Eat within an hour or two of finishing a session.
tip: Make it ahead: boil the eggs and potatoes the day before, cool within 2 hours and chill. Eggs in their shells keep up to 1 week, the potatoes up to 3 days; eat them cold, or warm the potatoes until steaming hot. After a long, sweaty session, a little extra salt is fine.

name: Crispy spiced chickpeas with a firm egg and raisins
about: Rinsed chickpeas roasted until crunchy with garam masala and a little salt, like a roasted chana snack, served with a firm-boiled egg and sweet raisins. A **salty-sweet recovery snack** with plant and egg protein.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Toss the dry chickpeas with the olive oil, garam masala and salt on a tray and roast 25 minutes, shaking once, until crisp.
Meanwhile, cover the egg with cold water, bring to a boil and cook 10 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Serve the warm chickpeas with the halved egg and the raisins. Eat within an hour or two of finishing a session.
tip: Make it ahead: roast the chickpeas before you head out, or the day before (cool within 2 hours, keep covered in the fridge up to 3 days and re-crisp in a hot oven for 5 minutes). Firm-boiled eggs keep in their shells in the fridge for up to 1 week.

name: Apple cinnamon oatmeal with walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by an old-fashioned Canadian porridge
about: Creamy rolled oats cooked in milk with chopped apple and cinnamon, finished with a big dollop of Greek yogurt, toasted walnuts and sunflower seeds. The oats bring **slow-burning fibre**, and the yogurt and milk add protein and calcium.
steps: Wash the apple, then chop it into small pieces, skin on. Toast the walnuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes.
Put the oats, milk, apple, cinnamon and salt in a small pot over medium heat. Stir often until the oats are thick and creamy and the apple is just soft, about 6 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl, top with the yogurt, walnuts and sunflower seeds.
tip: Cook a double batch on Wednesday, spread the second bowl in a shallow container and refrigerate it within 1 hour, then reheat it on Thursday with a splash of milk until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
ingredients: washed, chopped with the skin on

name: Scrambled eggs with tomato and spinach on whole-wheat toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian diner scramble
about: Firm, fluffy scrambled eggs folded with wilted spinach and tomato, on whole-wheat toast with orange wedges. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, and the orange helps your body absorb the iron in the spinach.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomato and orange. Chop the tomato, beat the eggs with the salt and pepper, and put the bread in the toaster.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the tomato and cook until it softens, about 2 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until it wilts, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the eggs and keep folding gently until they are completely set with no liquid egg left and the yolk is firm, about 3 minutes. They should reach 71 °C (160 °F).
Pile the eggs on the toast and serve with the orange wedges.

name: Yogurt bowl with blueberries, banana and oat crunch
inspiredBy: Inspired by the North American yogurt parfait
about: Thick Greek yogurt topped with blueberries, sliced banana and a toasty crunch of oats and walnuts. It has **plenty of protein**, plus plant omega-3 from the walnuts, and takes 10 minutes.
steps: Wash the blueberries. Toast the oats and walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the blueberries and banana.
Scatter the oat crunch and the cinnamon over the top just before eating so it stays crisp.
tip: Toast a jar of the oat and walnut crunch on Sunday and keep it in the cupboard for the week.

name: Salmon salad sandwich on rye
inspiredBy: Inspired by the classic Canadian salmon sandwich
about: Canned salmon mashed with yogurt, Dijon, celery and dill, piled on rye with crisp cucumber, with carrot sticks on the side. It is **omega-3 rich** and the soft bones in canned salmon add calcium.
steps: Wash the celery, dill, cucumber and carrot. Chop the celery and dill, slice the cucumber and cut the carrot into sticks.
Mash the salmon in a bowl with the yogurt, Dijon, celery, dill, lemon juice and pepper until it holds together.
Pile the salmon onto one slice of rye with the cucumber and top with the other slice. Serve with the carrot sticks.

If you are packing it, keep the filling in a container in the fridge and assemble at lunch so the bread stays crisp. Pack it with an ice pack, or keep it in the fridge until you leave, and eat it the same day. Refrigerate the rest of an opened can of salmon in a covered container and use it within 2 days, on the salmon toast.

name: Smashed chickpea and crunchy veg sandwich with yogurt sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by the café smashed-chickpea sandwich
about: Whole-wheat toast piled with smashed chickpeas and walnuts, cucumber, tomato and red pepper, with a lemony yogurt sauce and parsley. The chickpeas bring **fibre, folate and plant iron**, and the lemon helps you absorb it.
steps: Wash the cucumber, tomato, red pepper, spinach, parsley and apple. Dice the vegetables and chop the parsley.
Mash about half the chickpeas roughly with a fork, with the walnuts, the olive oil, half the lemon juice, the cumin, salt and pepper. Stir in the remaining whole chickpeas.
Stir the yogurt with the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of pepper.

Toast the bread dark so it holds together. Spread the yogurt sauce on both slices, pile the chickpeas, spinach and diced vegetables on one, scatter over the parsley and close the sandwich. Serve the apple on the side.

name: Hearty white bean and vegetable soup with rye
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian minestrone and a Canadian bean soup
about: A big, comforting pot of white beans, carrot, celery, spinach and tomato in a thyme-scented broth, finished with lemon and a little Parmesan, with a slice of rye on the side. The beans and spinach bring **fibre, iron and folate**, and it tastes even better the next day.
steps: Wash the carrot, celery, onion and spinach. Dice the carrot, celery and onion, and mince the garlic.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery with the salt until they begin to soften, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic and thyme for 30 seconds.
