Add the tomatoes, broth, bay leaf and the beans. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the spinach and cook until it just wilts, about 2 minutes. Remove the bay leaf, then stir in the lemon juice and pepper.
Ladle into bowls, top with the Parmesan and serve with the rye.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate it. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Mash a ladleful of the beans against the side of the pot for a thicker soup. It freezes well for up to 3 months.

name: Lemon herb chicken with broccoli and brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by a family-dinner roast chicken and rice
about: Juicy chicken thigh pan-roasted with lemon, oregano and garlic, served over a fist of nutty brown rice with garlicky broccoli and carrots. It is a **weeknight classic** that makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Rinse the brown rice and cook it in plenty of boiling water for 30 minutes, or follow the packet, then drain. Spread the portion for tomorrow on a plate to cool within 1 hour, then refrigerate.

Meanwhile, wash the broccoli and carrot, and trim the chicken and cut it into 2 or 3 flat pieces. Mix the oregano, paprika, half the salt and half the garlic with half the lemon juice and half the oil, and rub it over the chicken. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

Warm a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 6 to 7 minutes on each side, until golden and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part. Rest it on a board for 5 minutes, then slice.

In the same pan, cook the onion and carrot in the remaining oil for 4 minutes. Add the broccoli, the rest of the garlic, the rest of the salt, the pepper and a splash of water, cover, and steam for 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Serve the chicken over the rice with the vegetables and squeeze over the rest of the lemon juice.
Pack the second portion of chicken and vegetables into a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate it with the rice. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Squeeze a little extra lemon over the leftover portion when you reheat it. Quick-cooking brown rice takes about 10 minutes and gets dinner nearer 35.

name: Whole-wheat spaghetti with lentil tomato sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian spaghetti bolognese, with lentils doing the work of the meat
about: A thick, savoury tomato sauce packed with lentils, carrot, celery and spinach over whole-wheat spaghetti, with Parmesan on top. The lentils make it taste like a bolognese and bring **protein, fibre and iron**.
steps: Wash the carrot, celery, onion and spinach, then dice the carrot, celery and onion finely and mince the garlic. Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the pasta.
Warm the oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of the salt until soft, about 7 minutes. Stir in the garlic and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, lentils and the rest of the salt with a splash of water. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick. Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in the boiling water until just tender, about 10 minutes. Drain, saving a cup of the water.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce, loosening it with a splash of the pasta water. Season with pepper and top with the Parmesan.
Spread the second portion in a shallow container so it cools fast, and refrigerate it within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Beef and bean chili
inspiredBy: Inspired by the classic North American bean chili
about: A weeknight chili with a little ground beef stretched with kidney beans and plenty of peppers, spiced with chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika. The beans bring **fibre and plant protein** and the beef adds iron and zinc.
steps: Wash the pepper and onion, then dice them and mince the garlic.

Warm the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef and break it up, cooking until it is browned with no pink left, about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Add the onion and pepper and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin and paprika for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, beans, salt and a splash of water. Simmer for 20 minutes, until thick. The beef should reach 71 °C (160 °F).
Ladle into bowls, top with the Parmesan and serve with the toast.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Leave out the chili powder for a milder pot, and add a squeeze of lemon at the end. A pack of ground beef is more than this pot needs: freeze the rest flat in pot-sized bags, then thaw one in the fridge and cook it within 2 days.

name: Lemon dill salmon with roasted potatoes and green beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic baked salmon dinner
about: Salmon baked with a Dijon, lemon and dill topping, beside crisp roasted baby potatoes and carrots with garlicky green beans. The salmon is a **rich source of omega-3 and vitamin D**, and it is on the table in about 45 minutes.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the potatoes, carrots, green beans and dill, then cut the potatoes and carrots into bite-size chunks.
Toss the potatoes and carrots on a large tray with half the oil and half the salt. Roast for 15 minutes.
Mix the Dijon, half the lemon juice, the dill and the pepper. Pat the salmon dry and spread the mixture over the top. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.

Push the vegetables to one side, add the green beans tossed with the rest of the oil, the garlic and the rest of the salt, and nestle in the salmon. Roast for 12 to 14 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Squeeze the rest of the lemon over everything and serve.

name: Mustard roast chicken with sweet potato and carrots
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Sunday roast chicken
about: Chicken thighs roasted on one tray with sweet potato, carrots and broccoli, with Dijon, rosemary and garlic. The sweet potato and carrot bring **vitamin A and fibre**, and it makes two portions for Sunday's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potato, carrots, broccoli and onion, then cut them into even chunks.
Toss the sweet potato, carrot, onion and garlic on a large tray with half the oil and half the salt. Roast for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix the Dijon, rosemary, the rest of the oil and the rest of the salt, and rub it over the chicken. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

Push the vegetables aside, add the chicken, and roast for 10 minutes, then add the broccoli and roast 15 to 20 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the edges of the vegetables are browned.
Squeeze the lemon over the tray and toss the juices through.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Eat the second portion cold from the fridge on Sunday, or reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Herby baked trout with white beans and tomatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Tuscan white-bean and fish supper
about: Trout fillet baked with lemon and parsley over a warm skillet of white beans, tomatoes and spinach. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the beans add fibre and iron to a light Sunday supper.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the tomatoes, spinach and parsley. Cut the tomatoes into wedges and chop the parsley.

Pat the trout dry and rub it with a little of the oil, half the lemon juice, half the parsley, half the salt and the pepper. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish. Bake on a lined tray for 12 to 15 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and cook until they burst, about 4 minutes.
Add the beans and the rest of the salt and heat through for 3 minutes. Stir in the spinach until wilted, then add the rest of the lemon juice.
Spoon the beans onto a plate, lay the trout on top and finish with the rest of the parsley.

name: Apple with almonds
about: A crisp apple with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and healthy fats**.
steps: Wash the apple and slice it. Serve with the almonds.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A banana sliced over a handful of walnuts with a dash of cinnamon. It gives you **potassium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Slice the banana into a bowl, scatter over the walnuts and dust with the cinnamon.

name: Orange with sunflower seeds
about: A juicy orange with a spoonful of sunflower seeds. The seeds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the orange adds vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Serve with the sunflower seeds.

name: Yogurt with walnuts and cinnamon
about: Thick Greek yogurt with walnuts and a shake of cinnamon. A quick snack of **protein and omega-3**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl. Top with the walnuts and cinnamon.

name: Smoky roasted chickpeas
about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with smoked paprika and garlic powder. A snack with **fibre, iron and plant protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Pat the chickpeas very dry with a clean towel.
Toss them on a tray with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt. Roast, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and golden, 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool on the tray for 10 minutes so they crisp up. Keep leftovers in an open container at room temperature and eat within 2 days.
tip: Roast a double tray and keep the rest in an open jar for up to 2 days.
ingredients: rinsed, drained and patted very dry

name: Blueberries with walnuts
about: A bowl of fresh blueberries with a handful of walnuts. A snack of **antioxidant-rich berries and plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the blueberries. Serve in a bowl with the walnuts scattered over.

name: Blueberry yogurt with almonds
about: Thick Greek yogurt with blueberries and chopped almonds. A snack with **protein, calcium and vitamin E**.
steps: Wash the blueberries. Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the blueberries and almonds.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and chili
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese izakaya edamame
about: Shelled edamame steamed until tender, with lemon, a pinch of salt and chili flakes. A snack with **plant protein, folate and choline**.
steps: Cook the edamame in boiling water until tender and hot, about 4 minutes, then drain well.
Toss with the lemon juice, chili and salt and eat warm.

name: Canned salmon on rye toast with cucumber
about: Flaked canned salmon on rye toast with cucumber, lemon and black pepper. A quick snack that brings **omega-3, protein and choline**, and the soft bones add calcium.
steps: Wash the cucumber and slice it. Toast the rye.

Mash the salmon with the lemon juice and pepper, pile it on the toast and top with the cucumber. Eat it the same day, and refrigerate the rest of an opened can in a covered container to use within 2 days.

name: Canned salmon and tomato on whole-wheat toast
about: Flaked canned salmon on whole-wheat toast with sliced tomato, lemon and black pepper. A quick snack that brings **omega-3, protein and choline**.
steps: Wash the tomato and slice it. Toast the bread.

Mash the salmon with the lemon juice and pepper, pile it on the toast and top with the tomato. Eat it the same day, and refrigerate the rest of an opened can in a covered container to use within 2 days.

name: Hard-boiled egg with tomato on rye toast
about: A firm hard-boiled egg sliced over rye toast with juicy tomato and pepper. It brings **protein and choline** in a few minutes.
steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and cook for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool it in cold water, then peel.
Wash the tomato and slice it. Toast the rye, top with the tomato and the sliced egg, and season with the salt and pepper.

name: Carrot cake oatmeal with yogurt
inspiredBy: North American carrot cake, turned into a quick oatmeal
about: Creamy rolled oats simmered with finely grated carrot, cinnamon and a little maple, topped with a spoonful of yogurt and a thin swirl of sunflower seed butter. It tastes like carrot cake for breakfast, and the carrot melts into the oats. The oats bring **fibre** and the carrot brings vitamin A.
steps: Wash and peel the carrot and grate it on the fine holes.
Stir the oats, milk, an equal splash of water, the carrot, ground flax, cinnamon and salt together in a small pot.
Bring to a gentle bubble over medium heat, then turn it down and cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy and the carrot is soft, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the maple syrup and spoon into a bowl.
Top with the yogurt and a thin swirl of sunflower seed butter.
tip: Serves the family: multiply the oats, milk and carrot and cook one big pot. Spread the sunflower seed butter thinly for little ones, or leave it off and stir in extra yogurt. For children under 2, use whole milk and whole-milk yogurt instead of the 1% milk and 2% yogurt here.

name: Zucchini and banana pancakes with blueberries
inspiredBy: North American weekend pancakes, with zucchini in the batter
about: Fluffy whole-wheat pancakes with grated zucchini and ripe banana folded into the batter, piled with blueberries, yogurt and a drizzle of maple. The zucchini melts into the batter and keeps the pancakes moist. The whole-wheat flour and oats bring **fibre**, and the egg brings choline.
steps: Wash the zucchini, grate it and squeeze it dry in a clean tea towel. Mash it with the banana in a big bowl.
Whisk the flour, oats, baking powder, cinnamon and salt in a second bowl.
Beat the egg and milk into the banana mixture, then fold in the dry mix until just combined. A few lumps are fine. Let it sit for 5 minutes.

Heat a non-stick pan over medium with a little of the oil. Spoon in small rounds and cook until bubbles pop and the edges look set, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook 2 minutes more, until the middle is cooked through with no wet batter.
Stack the pancakes and top with the blueberries, yogurt, a drizzle of the warmed seed butter and the maple syrup.
tip: Serves the family: multiply the batter and keep finished pancakes warm in a 100 °C (200 °F) oven. Cooled extras freeze between sheets of parchment and warm up in the toaster. Leave the maple off a baby's pancakes and top them with fruit, and no honey under 1. Do not taste raw batter and keep little hands out of it, as raw flour and raw egg can carry bacteria. Cut the blueberries in half for the very small.

name: Cheesy spinach and zucchini egg muffins with toast
about: Soft, golden egg muffins studded with grated zucchini, spinach and a little melted cheddar, served with whole-wheat toast and a few cherry tomatoes. They bake while you pack school bags, and the second portion reheats well for tomorrow's breakfast. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, and the spinach and tomatoes bring vitamins K and C.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and lightly oil a muffin tin. Wash the zucchini, spinach and tomatoes before cutting.
Grate the zucchini and squeeze it dry in a clean tea towel. Chop the spinach finely.
Whisk the eggs, milk and salt in a jug, then stir in the zucchini, spinach and cheese.

Pour into the muffin cups until about three-quarters full. Bake until puffed, golden and set right through with no wobble, about 20 minutes. The muffins must be firm and reach 74 °C (165 °F) in the centre.
Toast the bread, cut the tomatoes in quarters and serve the muffins warm with them.
Cool the second portion of muffins quickly, put them in a shallow container and into the fridge within 2 hours. Keep up to 3 days and reheat once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Serves the family: a dozen muffins uses about 6 eggs, and they freeze well. Thaw overnight in the fridge, eat within 2 days and never refreeze.

name: Veggie fried rice with egg and edamame
inspiredBy: Chinese-Canadian fried rice, with the vegetables chopped small
about: Brown basmati rice stir-fried with diced chicken, scrambled egg, edamame, sweet corn and tiny broccoli florets, finished with a little reduced-sodium soy sauce. It is the fried rice the kids ask for, with the vegetables chopped small enough to blend in. The chicken and egg bring **protein and choline**, and the broccoli brings vitamin C.
steps: Cook the rice the night before if you can. Rinse it and cook it in plenty of water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain and spread it on a tray so it cools within 1 hour. Chilled rice from the fridge fries best.
Wash the broccoli. Chop it into tiny florets and chop the onion small.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and stir-fry until cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes, then wash your hands and the board after the raw chicken.
Add the onion, broccoli, corn and edamame and stir-fry until bright and hot, about 5 minutes.
Push the vegetables aside, pour in the beaten egg and scramble it until fully set with no runny bits, about 2 minutes.
Add the cooled rice and ginger and stir-fry until steaming and lightly toasted, about 4 minutes. Splash in the soy sauce and toss to coat.
tip: Serves the family: cook a big pot of rice the night before and chill it within 1 hour. Fridge rice keeps up to 3 days, and fried rice should be reheated until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F). For under-4s, mash or crush the edamame lightly, as whole firm beans and corn can be a choking risk.

name: Loaded baked potato with broccoli, cheddar and white beans
about: A fluffy baked potato split open and piled with tender broccoli, creamy mashed white beans, melted cheddar and a cool spoonful of yogurt. It is a cosy, filling lunch that kids love to build themselves. The potato and beans bring **potassium and fibre**, and the broccoli brings vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Scrub the potato, prick it all over and microwave it for 7 to 9 minutes, turning once, until nearly soft.
Rub the skin with a little oil and finish in the oven for 10 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the middle is fluffy.
Steam the broccoli until tender and bright green, about 5 minutes, then chop it small.
Warm the beans in a small pan with the garlic powder, salt and a splash of water, mashing about half of them.
Split the potato, fluff the inside with a fork and pile on the beans, broccoli and cheddar. Return it to the oven for 2 minutes to melt the cheese, then top with the yogurt and dill.
tip: Serves the family: bake a whole tray of potatoes and set out the toppings so everyone builds their own. Chop the broccoli very small for little ones.
ingredients: washed and cut into small florets

name: Creamy egg salad sandwich with veggie sticks and grapes
about: Firm-cooked egg mashed with yogurt, cucumber and a little dill, piled between slices of whole-wheat bread, with carrot and red pepper sticks and a handful of grapes on the side. It is a lunchbox classic with a lighter yogurt dressing. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, and the peppers bring vitamin C.
steps: Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and cook for 10 to 12 minutes so the yolks are firm all the way through. Cool them in cold water and peel.
Wash the cucumber, carrot, pepper and grapes. Dice the cucumber finely, cut the carrot and pepper into sticks, and cut the grapes into quarters lengthwise.
Mash the eggs in a bowl with the yogurt, cucumber, lemon juice, dill and salt until creamy but still a bit chunky.
Spread the egg salad on a slice of bread, top with the second slice and cut into fingers.
Serve with the carrot and pepper sticks and the grapes.
tip: Serves the family: boil a dozen eggs at once and keep them in the shell in the fridge up to 5 days. If it goes in a lunchbox, pack it in an insulated bag with an ice pack so it stays cold until lunch. Without an ice pack, eat it within 2 hours of leaving the fridge (1 hour in hot weather). Throw away any that comes home. For under-4s, steam the carrot sticks until soft and keep the grapes in quarters.
ingredients: boiled in the shell until the yolk is firm

name: Taco night with turkey and veggie-packed filling
inspiredBy: Mexican-style tacos, kept mild for the family
about: A mild, savoury turkey and black bean filling with finely grated zucchini melted into it, spooned into warm corn tortillas, with all the toppings set out on the table so everyone builds their own. The heat goes on the table, not in the pot, so kids and grown-ups both get what they like. The beans bring **iron and fibre**, and the toppings add vitamin C.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Grate the zucchini on the fine holes and squeeze it dry in a clean tea towel. Chop the onion very small.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the onion and zucchini for about 5 minutes.
Add the turkey and break it up as it cooks until no pink remains and it reaches 71 °C (160 °F), about 7 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.

Stir in the paprika, cumin, oregano, garlic powder and salt for 1 minute, then add the tomato sauce and black beans. Simmer for 8 minutes, mashing some of the beans, until the filling is thick and spoonable.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or wrapped in foil in the oven.
Put the lettuce, tomatoes, corn, avocado, cheddar and yogurt in small bowls on the table with the filling and tortillas, and let everyone build their own.

Pack the second portion of filling into a shallow container and into the fridge within 2 hours, keeping the toppings separate and making a fresh bowl of toppings for the leftover filling. Keep up to 3 days and reheat once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Serves the family: multiply the filling and set out a bowl of hot sauce, pickled jalapeños or chili flakes for the adults, so nothing spicy goes in the pot. For under-4s, quarter the cherry tomatoes and serve it as a taco bowl.

name: Crispy baked salmon fish fingers with potato wedges and peas
inspiredBy: British fish fingers, baked with salmon
about: Strips of salmon coated in crunchy whole-wheat crumbs and baked until golden, with crispy oven potato wedges, sweet green peas and a lemony yogurt dip. Salmon is naturally mild and soft, which makes it a great first fish finger. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the peas bring fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Scrub the potato, cut it into wedges, toss with half the oil and a pinch of the salt on a tray and roast, turning once, for about 25 minutes.
Toast the bread and blitz it into crumbs in a food processor. Mix the crumbs with the paprika and a pinch of salt on a plate.
Pat the salmon dry. Run your fingertips along the fillet and pull out any pin bones with tweezers. Cut the salmon into finger-sized strips.

Dip each strip in the flour, then the egg, then the crumbs, pressing so they stick, and set them on an oiled tray. Drizzle with the rest of the oil. Wash your hands, the board and the knife in hot soapy water now, after the raw fish and egg.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp and the salmon reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily. The egg coating will be cooked firm.
Simmer the peas for 3 minutes. Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice, dill and a pinch of salt for the dip.
tip: Serves the family: double the batch on two trays. If your kids want a milder finger, use cod or haddock for some of the strips now and then, but you will get less omega-3 that night, so keep Thursday's salmon bowls as written. Check every finger for bones again before serving little ones, and break them up for the very small.

name: Veggie-packed pasta bake with turkey, white beans and mozzarella
inspiredBy: Italian baked pasta, with the vegetables blended into the sauce
about: Whole-wheat pasta in a rich tomato sauce that has carrot, zucchini, red pepper and spinach blitzed right into it, with lean turkey and white beans for protein and a golden mozzarella top. The sauce is blended smooth, which kids who dislike chunks will happily eat, so tell them what is in it and let them help grate. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done, and it brings **iron, fibre and vitamin A**.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Boil the pasta in a big pot of water until just shy of tender, about 2 minutes less than the package says, and drain.

Wash the vegetables. Warm the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion, carrot, pepper and zucchini for 8 minutes. Add the tomato sauce, beans, basil, oregano and garlic powder and simmer 10 minutes, then stir in the spinach until wilted.
Blitz the sauce with a stick blender until smooth, keeping the blade under the surface so the hot sauce does not spit.
Brown the turkey in a separate small pan, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 71 °C (160 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Stir the turkey, salt and pasta into the sauce, tip into a baking dish and top with the mozzarella.
Bake until bubbling and golden on top, about 20 minutes, with the middle steaming hot at 74 °C (165 °F).
Pack the second portion into a shallow container and into the fridge within 2 hours. Keep up to 3 days and reheat once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Serves the family: multiply everything and bake in a bigger dish. It freezes well: thaw it overnight in the fridge, use it within 2 days, reheat to 74 °C (165 °F) and never refreeze. Chili flakes at the table for the adults.

name: Salmon rice bowls with soy-maple glaze, egg ribbons and edamame
inspiredBy: a Japanese-style teriyaki salmon bowl, kept mild for the family
about: Flaky baked salmon brushed with a gentle soy and maple glaze over fluffy brown rice, with egg ribbons, edamame, cucumber and carrot and a few slices of avocado. It is a mild, sweet-salty bowl that kids tend to love, and it is on the table in about 45 minutes. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the edamame brings iron and fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Rinse the rice and cook it in plenty of water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain.
Stir the soy sauce, maple syrup, lemon juice and ginger together. Pour about a third into a small dish and keep it for the bowl, away from the raw fish.

Pat the salmon dry, feel along it for pin bones and pull any out. Set it on a lined tray and brush with the rest of the glaze, and throw away what is left on the brush. Wash your hands and the board now, after the raw fish, before touching anything else.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the salmon reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily.
Beat the egg with a splash of water and cook it as a thin omelette in a lightly oiled pan until completely set, about 2 minutes a side. Roll it up and slice into ribbons.
Boil the edamame for 4 minutes and drain. Wash the cucumber and carrot, then slice and grate them.
Pile the rice into a bowl with the edamame, cucumber, carrot, egg and avocado, flake the salmon on top and drizzle with the reserved glaze.
tip: Serves the family: if you cook extra rice, spread it on a tray so it cools within 1 hour, and keep it in the fridge up to 3 days. For under-4s, flake the salmon, double-check for bones, and mash or crush the edamame lightly.

name: Mild chicken and vegetable noodle soup
inspiredBy: Canadian chicken noodle soup, with extra vegetables
about: A gentle, golden soup with tender shredded chicken, carrot, zucchini and small whole-wheat pasta shapes, creamy white beans, peas and a little spinach, finished with lemon. It is the soup you want on a tired Friday night, and it makes enough for tomorrow's lunch. The chicken and white beans bring **protein and iron**, and the carrot and peas bring vitamin A and fibre.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Warm the oil in a big pot and soften the onion and carrot for 6 minutes.

Pour in the broth and about as much water as broth, to taste, add the bay leaf, onion powder, garlic powder and pepper, and slip in the chicken thighs whole. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook until the chicken is cooked through, 74 °C (165 °F), about 15 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after the raw chicken.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks, and set it aside. Remove the bay leaf.
Add the pasta, white beans and zucchini and simmer until the pasta is tender, about 8 minutes. Add the peas and spinach for the last 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts.
Return the chicken to the pot with the salt and lemon juice and ladle into bowls.

Cool the second portion quickly in a shallow container and put it in the fridge within 2 hours. Keep up to 3 days and reheat once until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F), adding a splash of water as the pasta thickens it.
tip: Serves the family: double the pot and freeze portions without the pasta. Thaw overnight in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze. Hot pepper at the table for the grown-ups.

name: Pizza night on whole-wheat dough with chicken, peppers and corn
inspiredBy: a North American pizza night, on whole-wheat dough
about: Homemade whole-wheat pizza dough rolled thin and topped with a tomato and white bean sauce, a little mozzarella, cooked chicken, sweet red pepper, corn and spinach, with a crunchy avocado salad on the side. Let the kids add their own toppings, and make a plain cheese one for the fussy ones. It brings **protein, calcium and iron**, and the whole-wheat dough and beans add fibre.
steps: Stir the yeast into comfortably warm water, about 70 ml for every 100 g of flour (the dough makes two portions, so that is twice the flour in the list), and leave it 5 minutes. Mix with the flour, salt and half the oil, adding a splash more water if it is dry, and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky. Cover and let it rise in a warm spot until doubled, about 1 hour. Do not taste the raw dough, and keep little hands out of it, as raw flour can carry bacteria.
Heat the oven to 250 °C (480 °F) with a tray inside. Wash the vegetables.
Dice the chicken small and cook it in a pan over medium-high heat until cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after the raw chicken.

Roll the dough out thin on a sheet of baking parchment. Spread with the tomato sauce stirred with the mashed white beans, oregano and garlic powder, then scatter on the mozzarella, chicken, pepper, corn and spinach.
Slide it, on its parchment, onto the hot tray and bake until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling, 10 to 12 minutes.
Toss the lettuce, cucumber and avocado with the lemon juice and a drizzle of the rest of the oil and serve alongside.
Cool the second portion within 2 hours, put it in a shallow container in the fridge for up to 3 days, and reheat until steaming, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Serves the family: make the dough in the morning or the night before and keep it in the fridge, and bake two pizzas on two trays. Plan on a 1 hour rise on top of the prep and cook time. Hot sauce and chili flakes stay on the table. For little ones, cut the slices into small strips.

name: Sheet-pan maple-lemon chicken with carrots, broccoli and crisp white beans
inspiredBy: a North American sheet-pan supper
about: Juicy chicken thighs brushed with a mild maple, lemon and paprika glaze, roasted on one tray with sweet caramelized carrots, broccoli and crisp white beans. One tray, no fuss, and everything finishes at the same time. The chicken and beans bring **protein and iron**, and the broccoli and carrots bring vitamins C and A.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the vegetables. Toss the carrots and onion with half the oil and a pinch of salt on a large tray and roast for 15 minutes.

Stir the maple syrup, lemon juice, paprika, garlic powder, mustard powder and a spoonful of the remaining oil into a glaze. Brush it over the chicken in a separate dish and use all of it on the chicken, never saving any that touched the raw meat.

Push the vegetables aside and lay the chicken on the tray, then wash your hands and the board. Toss the broccoli and white beans with the last of the oil, add them to the tray and roast for 20 minutes more, until the beans are crisp at the edges.
Check that the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part and the juices run clear.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice the chicken and serve it with the vegetables.
tip: Serves the family: use two trays so nothing crowds and steams. For little ones, cut the chicken, carrots and broccoli small and mash their beans, as crisp, crunchy beans can be a choking risk under 4. Add baby potatoes if you want them. Hot sauce or grainy mustard at the table for the grown-ups.

name: Apple slices with a thin spread of sunflower seed butter
about: Crisp apple slices with a thin spread of sunflower seed butter, a snack that lasts all afternoon. The sunflower seed butter brings **protein and vitamin E**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, core it and cut it into thin slices.
Spread a thin layer of sunflower seed butter on each slice, or serve it as a dip, and dust with cinnamon.
tip: Spread sunflower seed butter thinly, never in a thick spoonful, for little ones. Grate or lightly steam the apple for under-4s.

name: Berry yogurt parfait with toasted oat crunch
about: Creamy Greek yogurt layered with juicy blueberries and a crunchy toasted oat topping, with a little maple. It is an easy snack that tastes like dessert, and it brings **protein and calcium**.
steps: Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and smelling nutty, about 3 minutes, and let them cool.
Wash the blueberries. Layer the yogurt, blueberries and oats in a glass and drizzle with the maple syrup.
tip: Cut blueberries in half for the very small. No honey for babies under 1.

name: Veggie sticks with lemon-dill yogurt dip
about: Crunchy cucumber, carrot and red pepper sticks with a cool lemony yogurt dip. It is a bright, easy snack for after school, and it brings **vitamin C and calcium**.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut them into sticks.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice and dill and serve alongside for dipping.
tip: For under-4s, grate the carrot or steam the sticks until soft, as small, hard pieces of raw vegetable are a choking risk.

name: Blueberry banana smoothie with a handful of spinach
about: A creamy smoothie of blueberries, banana and milk with a handful of spinach blended in, which turns it a deep purple. It brings **calcium and fibre**, and a little ground flax adds plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the spinach and blueberries.
Blend everything with a few ice cubes until completely smooth, about 1 minute, and pour into a glass.
tip: Serves the family: double it and pour into small cups. Use frozen blueberries for a thicker shake.

name: Cheddar toast fingers with apple slices
about: Warm whole-wheat toast fingers with melted cheddar and crisp apple slices on the side, a snack plate in a few minutes. The cheddar brings **calcium** and the apple brings fibre. Cheese stays a small portion to keep the salt down.
steps: Heat the grill. Lay the bread on a tray, scatter with the cheddar and grill until melted and bubbling, about 2 minutes. Cut into fingers.
Wash the apple, slice it thin and serve alongside.
tip: Grate or steam the apple for under-4s.

name: Grapes and mozzarella
about: Sweet grapes with soft part-skim mozzarella, a fresh and filling snack. The mozzarella brings **calcium** and the grapes bring plenty of water.
steps: Wash the grapes and cut each in quarters lengthwise.
Serve with the mozzarella.
tip: Always cut grapes into quarters for under-4s, as whole grapes are a choking risk.
ingredients: cut in thin sticks or tiny pieces

name: Oat and sunflower seed butter bites
about: No-bake little balls of oats, sunflower seed butter, mashed banana and ground flax, a lunchbox treat. The oats bring **fibre** and the sunflower seed butter brings protein and vitamin E.
steps: Mash the banana in a bowl and stir in the sunflower seed butter, maple syrup and cinnamon.
Mix in the oats and ground flax.
Roll into small balls and chill for 20 minutes. Keep in the fridge up to 3 days.
tip: Made with seed butter, so it is peanut-free for school lunchboxes, but check the label for traces. For under-4s, press each ball flat with a fork, as small, round, sticky balls can be a choking risk, and keep them cold in the lunchbox.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and a pinch of salt
about: Shelled edamame warmed through and tossed with lemon juice, a little salt and a pinch of garlic powder. It is a bright, easy snack that brings **protein, iron and folate**, and little hands can scoop it up.
steps: Warm the edamame in a small pot of simmering water for 3 minutes until hot, then drain well.
Toss with the lemon juice, salt and garlic powder and serve warm or cool.
tip: Serve the shelled beans in a small bowl and keep an eye on the youngest, as small beans can be a choking risk under 4. Mash lightly for little ones.

name: Firm-boiled egg with cherry tomatoes and cucumber
about: A firm-boiled egg with sweet cherry tomatoes and crunchy cucumber half-moons, a simple protein snack for after school. The egg brings **protein and choline**, and the tomatoes bring vitamin C.
steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk is firm all the way through. Cool in cold water and peel.
Wash the tomatoes and cucumber, quarter the tomatoes and cut the cucumber into thin half-moons, quartered for under-4s. Serve with the egg, cut in wedges, and a pinch of salt.
tip: Boil a batch of eggs and keep them in the shell in the fridge up to 5 days. Keep the cherry tomatoes cut in quarters and the cucumber in small pieces for under-4s.
ingredients: boiled in the shell until the yolk is firm

name: Apple slices with cinnamon yogurt dip
about: Crisp apple slices with a creamy cinnamon and maple yogurt for dipping. It tastes like apple pie in a bowl, and brings **protein, calcium and fibre**.
steps: Wash the apple, core it and slice it thin.
Stir the yogurt with the cinnamon and maple syrup and serve as a dip.
tip: Grate or lightly steam the apple for under-4s. Leave the maple out of a baby's dip, and no honey under 1.

name: Blueberry banana yogurt cup
about: Cool Greek yogurt with sliced banana and juicy blueberries. It brings **protein, calcium and potassium**.
steps: Wash the blueberries.
Layer the yogurt, banana and blueberries in a cup.
tip: Cut blueberries in half for the very small. No honey for babies under 1.

name: Overnight oats with raspberries and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss bircher and North American overnight oats
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt, spooned over juicy raspberries with chopped walnuts for crunch. The oats and raspberries bring **plenty of fibre**, and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, cinnamon and salt together in a jar or bowl. Cover and chill overnight, or at least 4 hours.
In the morning, stir well and loosen with a splash of milk if it has thickened.
Wash the raspberries and roughly chop the walnuts.
Spoon the raspberries on top and scatter with the walnuts.
Keep any spare jar covered in the fridge and eat it within 3 days.
tip: Mix each jar the night before: Tuesday night for Wednesday and Thursday night for Friday. Any berry works. If you use frozen berries and you are pregnant, 60 or older, feeding a child 5 or under, or have a weakened immune system, boil them for 1 minute and cool them first.

name: Warm quinoa porridge with pear and hazelnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Andean quinoa porridge
about: Quinoa simmered in milk until creamy and soft, then topped with diced pear and toasted hazelnuts. It is a gentle, cosy start, and the hazelnuts bring **vitamin E** while the quinoa adds magnesium.
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under cold water for 30 seconds to remove its bitter coating.

Put the quinoa, milk, cinnamon and salt in a small pot. Bring to a gentle boil, then cover and simmer on low until the quinoa is soft and creamy, about 15 minutes, stirring once or twice. If it still looks thin, simmer it uncovered for a few minutes more.
Meanwhile, wash and dice the pear, and toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the pear and the hazelnuts.
tip: Cook it the night before, cool it in a shallow container within 1 hour and keep it in the fridge. Reheat it with a splash of milk until steaming (74 °C) and add the pear and nuts cold. Use within 3 days.

name: Lemon and chili edamame
about: Warm edamame tossed with lemon juice, a pinch of chili flakes and a little salt. A **plant-protein** snack that brings folate and iron.
steps: Heat the edamame in a pot of simmering water or in the microwave until steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the lemon juice, chili flakes and salt.

name: Lemony chickpea and herb salad with feta
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek and Levantine chickpea salads
about: A crunchy salad of chickpeas, edamame, cucumber, tomato, red pepper and a big handful of parsley, with a little feta, a lemony yogurt dressing and toasted pumpkin seeds. The chickpeas and parsley bring **fibre, iron and folate**, and the lemon helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Simmer the edamame in water until steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes, then drain and cool under cold water. Rinse the chickpeas well and drain them. Wash all the vegetables and the parsley.
Dice the cucumber and red pepper, halve the tomatoes, slice the onion very thinly and chop the parsley.
Whisk the yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, oregano and pepper in a large bowl. Add the chickpeas, edamame and vegetables and toss to coat.
Top with the feta and the pumpkin seeds. If you are packing it, keep it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: A spoonful of leftover quinoa or a handful of baby spinach makes it bigger. The feta is a garnish, so a little goes a long way.

name: Sheet-pan lemon-parsley salmon with potatoes, carrots and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by sheet-pan suppers from North American home kitchens
about: Baby potatoes, carrots and broccoli roast on one tray while a mustard-glazed salmon fillet finishes on top, with lemon and fresh parsley. The salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, and the carrots and broccoli add vitamin A, vitamin C and choline.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the potatoes, carrots and broccoli. Cut the potatoes into bite-sized pieces and the carrots into thick sticks.
Toss the potatoes and carrots on a large tray with half the olive oil, the garlic, salt and pepper. Roast for 15 minutes.
Toss the broccoli with the rest of the oil. Push the potatoes aside, add the broccoli, and nestle the salmon fillets among the vegetables. Brush the salmon with the mustard.
Roast until the salmon flakes easily and reads 70 °C (158 °F) in the thickest part, and the potatoes and carrots are golden, about 12 to 14 minutes.
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley. Wash your hands, the knife and the board after handling the raw fish.
Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 1 hour, because it holds cooked potato and fish, and keep it in the fridge for tomorrow. Eat it within 2 days and reheat it only once.
tip: Tomorrow the second portion is lunch: eat it cold on a bed of greens, or reheat it until steaming (74 °C). In a packed lunch, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
ingredients: skin on or off, patted dry
washed and cut in thick sticks

name: Pan-seared trout with warm mustard lentils and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by French lentilles du Puy with fish
about: A crisp-skinned trout fillet over earthy green lentils tossed with carrot, spinach, kale, mustard and lemon, finished with toasted hazelnuts. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the lentils bring iron and folate.
steps: Put the lentils in a pot with plenty of water and bring to a boil. Simmer until tender but not mushy, about 22 minutes, then drain.

Meanwhile, heat half the oil in a pan. Cook the carrot and onion until soft, about 6 minutes. Stir in the lentils, mustard, half the lemon juice, half the salt, the chili flakes, the spinach and the kale. Stir until both wilt, about 3 minutes.
Pat the trout dry and season with the remaining salt and the pepper. Heat the rest of the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the trout skin-side down until crisp, about 4 minutes.
Flip and cook until the fish flakes easily and reads 70 °C (158 °F), about 3 minutes more. Squeeze the rest of the lemon juice over it.
Spoon the lentils onto a plate, lay the trout on top and scatter with the hazelnuts and parsley. Wash your hands, the pan and the board after handling the raw fish.
tip: Cook a double batch of lentils on a quiet evening and keep them chilled within 1 hour in a shallow container; use within 3 days.

name: Garlicky shrimp and white bean skillet with kale
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish alubias con gambas and gambas al ajillo
about: Plump shrimp in a smoky garlic, paprika and tomato pan with creamy white beans, sweet carrot, browned mushrooms and wilted kale, finished with lemon, parsley and toasted walnuts. The shrimp bring **protein, iodine and selenium**, and the beans, kale and carrot add iron, calcium, folate and vitamin A.
steps: Wash the kale, tomatoes and parsley. Pat the shrimp dry.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and mushrooms until the mushrooms are browned and the carrot is soft, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic, smoked paprika and chili flakes and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they slump and turn saucy, about 5 minutes. Stir in the beans, the kale and a splash of water, cover and cook until the kale is tender, about 4 minutes.

Nestle in the shrimp. Cook, turning once, until they are pink and opaque all the way through and curled into a loose C, about 3 to 4 minutes (74 °C if you check with a thermometer). Do not eat shrimp that are still grey or translucent.
Season with the salt, then finish with the lemon juice, parsley and toasted walnuts. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling raw shrimp.
tip: Serve with a few spoonfuls of cooked quinoa if you want it bigger. Thaw frozen shrimp in the fridge overnight, cook them the same day and never refreeze them.
ingredients: thawed in the fridge overnight if frozen, patted dry

name: Seared mackerel on a warm mustard potato salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by German warm potato salad and Scandinavian mackerel
about: A seared Atlantic mackerel fillet over warm baby potatoes, green beans, cucumber and red onion in a tangy yogurt and mustard dressing. The mackerel brings **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, and the potatoes and beans add potassium and fibre.
steps: Put the potatoes in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes. Add the green beans for the last 4 minutes, then drain.
Whisk the yogurt, mustard, lemon juice, half the salt and the pepper in a large bowl. Add the warm potatoes, beans, onion, cucumber and parsley and toss gently.
Pat the mackerel dry and season with the rest of the salt. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook skin-side down until crisp, about 4 minutes.
Flip and cook until the flesh flakes easily and reads 70 °C (158 °F), about 3 minutes more.
Serve the mackerel on top of the potato salad. Wash your hands, the pan and the board after handling the raw fish.
Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 1 hour, because it holds cooked potato and fish, and keep it in the fridge. Eat it tomorrow, cold, and within 2 days.
tip: Buy the mackerel very fresh, keep it in the fridge and cook it the day you buy it or the next. Tomorrow the cold salad and mackerel make a packed lunch: use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
ingredients: scrubbed and cut in bite-sized pieces

name: Cod and chickpea stew with fennel and saffron
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish and Moroccan fish and chickpea stews
about: Flaky cod simmered in a saffron and smoked paprika tomato broth with chickpeas, fennel, carrot, mushrooms and spinach, with lemon and parsley at the end. The cod brings **lean protein and iodine**, and the chickpeas and spinach bring iron and folate, and the carrot adds vitamin A.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the fennel, carrot, mushrooms and onion until soft, about 10 minutes. Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika and saffron for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon, the chickpeas and a cup of water. Simmer for 10 minutes, until the broth thickens a little.
Season the cod with the salt and nestle it into the stew with the spinach. Cover and simmer gently until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, 70 °C (158 °F), about 6 minutes.
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw fish.
Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and keep it in the fridge. Tomorrow, reheat it only once, until steaming (74 °C). Eat it within 2 days.
tip: Serve with a spoonful of cooked quinoa if you want it bigger. Do not freeze the leftover.

name: Mussels in tomato broth with garlic potatoes and fennel salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Belgian moules and Provençal fish broths
about: Mussels steamed open in a garlicky tomato and fennel broth, with tender potatoes to mop it up and a crunchy fennel and spinach salad. The mussels bring **iron, B12, zinc and selenium** in one pot, and the tomato broth is a pleasure to dip into.
steps: Put the potatoes in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and toss with a little of the oil, the salt and half the garlic.
Scrub the mussels under cold running water and pull off any beards. Tap any open mussel on the counter: if it does not close within a minute, throw it away, along with any with cracked shells.

Heat the rest of the oil in a wide pot. Cook the onion and sliced fennel until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the remaining garlic and the chili flakes for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes, crushing them, and a splash of water. Simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the mussels, cover tightly and cook over high heat, shaking the pot once, until the shells open, about 5 to 6 minutes. Throw away any mussel that stays closed after cooking.
Toss the shaved fennel and baby spinach with the lemon juice. Spoon the mussels and broth over the potatoes, scatter with the parsley and hazelnuts and serve the salad alongside.
Wash your hands, the board and the pot after handling the raw mussels. Eat them the day you cook them and do not keep the leftovers.
tip: Buy mussels from a trusted fishmonger, keep them cold and cook them the same day. At home, keep them in the fridge in an open bowl under a damp cloth, never in water or a sealed bag.
ingredients: meat weight, so buy about four times as much in the shell
scrubbed and cut in bite-sized pieces
washed, half sliced for the broth and half shaved for the salad

name: Black bean and sweet potato chili with lemon and avocado
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex and Southwestern bean chili
about: A thick, smoky chili of black beans, sweet potato, peppers and kale with a little quinoa, finished with lemon, avocado and toasted pumpkin seeds. The beans and sweet potato bring **fibre, iron and vitamin A**, and the lemon helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and red pepper until soft, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.

Add the sweet potato, tomatoes (crushed with a spoon), the quinoa, the beans, salt and a cup of water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the sweet potato and quinoa are tender, about 22 minutes.
Stir in the kale and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Finish with the lemon juice. Ladle into a bowl and top with the avocado, pumpkin seeds and parsley.
Chill any extra within 1 hour (it holds cooked quinoa) in a shallow container and eat it within 3 days, reheated until steaming (74 °C).
tip: Leave out the chili powder for a milder pot. To freeze a double batch, cool it within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze and reheat to 74 °C. Add the avocado and seeds fresh.
ingredients: scrubbed and cut in small cubes

name: Mushroom, spinach and tomato scramble with avocado and orange
inspiredBy: Inspired by classic North American scrambled eggs
about: Eggs scrambled until completely set with browned mushrooms, wilted spinach and sweet cherry tomatoes, topped with creamy avocado and served with orange segments. It is ready in about 15 minutes, and the eggs bring **choline and B12** while the orange adds vitamin C.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomatoes, avocado and orange, and wipe the mushrooms clean. Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper in a bowl.

Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and cook until they are browned, about 4 minutes, then add the tomatoes and cook 2 minutes more. Add the spinach and stir until it wilts.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently until they are completely set, with no runny egg left, about 3 minutes. The eggs should be firm all the way through.
Peel and segment the orange. Serve the scramble with the sliced avocado, the pumpkin seeds and the orange on the side.
Wash your hands, the pan and the bowl after handling raw eggs.

name: Lentil, kale and tomato soup with lemon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern and Mediterranean lentil soups
about: A hearty soup of green lentils, carrot, kale and tomato, flavoured with garlic, cumin and a squeeze of lemon, with toasted pumpkin seeds on top. The lentils bring **protein, iron and folate**, and the lemon helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook until the onion is soft, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the lentils, the tomatoes (crushed with a spoon) and plenty of water to cover by 3 cm. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered until the lentils are tender, about 22 minutes.
Stir in the kale and salt and cook until the kale is tender, about 3 minutes. Add the lemon juice.
Serve topped with the pumpkin seeds. Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours, keep it in the fridge and reheat it only once, until steaming (74 °C), tomorrow.
tip: This is a long weekday lunch, so make it the evening before while dinner cooks. To freeze the second portion, cool it within 2 hours and freeze up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C. Add the seeds fresh.

name: Canned salmon and white bean salad with cucumber and parsley
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan tuna and bean salad
about: Flaked canned salmon and creamy white beans tossed with crisp cucumber, red onion, parsley and a lemony yogurt dressing. The salmon, bones and all, brings **omega-3 and calcium**, and it takes no cooking at all.
steps: Rinse the white beans and drain the salmon. Wash the cucumber, spinach and parsley.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil and pepper in a bowl. Add the beans, cucumber, onion and parsley and toss.
Flake in the salmon, mashing the soft bones in, and fold gently.
Pile onto the spinach and scatter the walnuts over the top.
Move any leftover salmon out of the tin into a covered container, keep it in the fridge and use it within 2 days. If you pack the salad, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Add a handful of cherry tomatoes if you have them.
ingredients: drained, bones left in and mashed

name: Apple with walnuts
about: A crisp apple with a small handful of walnuts. The apple brings **fibre**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3 and vitamin E.
steps: Wash and slice the apple.
Eat with the walnuts.

name: Pear with toasted hazelnuts
about: A ripe pear with a small handful of toasted hazelnuts. The pear brings **fibre**, and the hazelnuts bring vitamin E and magnesium.
steps: Wash and slice the pear.
Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes, and eat them with the pear.

name: Raspberries with Greek yogurt and pumpkin seeds
about: Cool Greek yogurt topped with juicy raspberries and a spoonful of toasted pumpkin seeds. The yogurt brings **protein and calcium**, and the raspberries add fibre.
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they pop, about 2 minutes.
Wash the raspberries.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the raspberries and seeds.

name: Veg sticks with lemon-garlic yogurt dip
about: Crunchy carrot, cucumber and red pepper sticks with a thick yogurt dip brightened with lemon, garlic and oregano. The vegetables bring **vitamin A and fibre**, and the yogurt adds protein and calcium.
steps: Wash the carrot, cucumber and pepper, then cut them into sticks.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice, garlic, oregano and salt.
Serve the sticks with the dip. Keep any extra dip covered in the fridge and use it within 3 days.

name: Apple with peanut butter
about: Crisp apple slices with a spoonful of peanut butter. The apple brings **fibre**, and the peanut butter adds protein, niacin and vitamin E.
steps: Wash and slice the apple.
Dip the slices in the peanut butter or spread it on top.

name: Firm-boiled egg with tomato and cucumber
about: A firm-boiled egg with juicy cherry tomatoes and crisp cucumber, drizzled with olive oil and a pinch of oregano. A **light, protein-rich** snack where the egg brings choline and the tomatoes add vitamin C.
steps: Lower the egg into a pot of boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water, then peel.
Wash the tomatoes and cucumber, then halve the tomatoes and slice the cucumber.
Arrange on a plate with the egg, then drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with the oregano and salt. Wash your hands after handling the raw egg.
ingredients: boiled until the yolk is firm, then peeled

name: Greek yogurt with pear and walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt topped with diced pear, chopped walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon. The yogurt brings **protein and calcium**, and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Wash and dice the pear.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the pear, the walnuts and the cinnamon.

name: Pear with walnuts
about: A ripe pear with a handful of walnuts. The pear brings **fibre**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3 and a good crunch.
steps: Wash and slice the pear.
Eat with the walnuts.

name: Arepas with huevos pericos and black beans
inspiredBy: Colombian and Venezuelan arepas with huevos pericos, the everyday scramble of eggs, tomato and scallion
about: Golden corn arepas with a soft scramble of eggs, tomato, scallion and wilted spinach, warm black beans and a squeeze of lime. Arepas are made from precooked corn flour, so they are naturally gluten-free and cook in a dry pan. The eggs, beans and spinach bring **protein, choline, iron and folate**, and the lime keeps it bright.
steps: Use black beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed. Warm them with a splash of water.

Stir the masarepa with a pinch of the salt and enough warm water to make a soft dough, a bit firmer than play dough. Let it rest for 5 minutes, then shape it into two discs (one at the Light size) about 1.5 cm thick, pinching any cracks closed.

Cook the arepas in a dry nonstick or cast-iron pan over medium heat until they have a golden crust and sound hollow when tapped, about 7 minutes a side. Or brown them for 4 minutes a side and finish them in a 200°C (400°F) oven for 8 minutes.
While they cook, warm the oil in a second pan and soften the scallion for 2 minutes. Add the tomato and cook for about 4 minutes, until it turns jammy, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Beat the eggs with the rest of the salt, pour them in and stir gently until just set and still glossy, about 2 minutes. Stir in half the cilantro.
Split the arepas and fill them with the eggs, or serve them alongside. Add the beans, a squeeze of lime and the rest of the cilantro.
tip: Cook the arepas the night before and re-crisp them in a dry pan or toaster for 3 minutes, and breakfast takes 10. At the Light size, make one arepa. Check the label on the masarepa: it should say precooked corn, nothing else (buy a gluten-free line if you are celiac).
ingredients: precooked cornmeal for arepas, not masa harina

name: Tapioca crepes with queijo coalho, a fried egg and linhaça mango yogurt
inspiredBy: Brazilian tapioca, the cassava-starch crepe sold at breakfast stands in the northeast, with a fried egg and iogurte com linhaça (yogurt with ground flaxseed) on the side
about: A lacy, chewy crepe made from cassava starch, folded around golden queijo coalho that goes soft and spotty in the pan, with a fried egg alongside. Cool yogurt with mango and a spoon of ground flaxseed makes it a proper breakfast. It is **gluten-free by nature**, and the egg, cheese and yogurt bring protein, choline and calcium.
steps: Stir the tapioca starch and salt with just enough water to make it feel like damp sand that holds together when squeezed. Leave it for 10 minutes, then rub it through a sieve so it turns into fine, fluffy crumbs.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat. Scatter the crumbs in an even round about 18 cm wide, with no oil. After about a minute they fuse into a pale, lacy crepe.
Lay the coalho on one half, press lightly and let it soften for 1 to 2 minutes, until the cheese is spotty and the crepe is just set. Fold the crepe over and slide it onto a plate.
Fry the egg in the same pan, without oil, until the white and the yolk are firm, about 3 minutes, flipping it for the last minute. Tuck it next to the crepe, or inside it, as many Brazilians do.
Stir the ground flaxseed into the yogurt, toss the mango with the lime juice and spoon it over the yogurt.
tip: Brazilian shops sell tapioca already hydrated (goma), which skips the first step. Or hydrate and sieve the starch the night before; it keeps in a sealed tub in the fridge, and breakfast takes 8 minutes. If you are celiac, buy the starch from a gluten-free line. Queijo coalho is sold at Brazilian shops, and halloumi grills the same way.
ingredients: ground flaxseed, stirred into the yogurt

name: Quinoa con leche with banana and cinnamon
inspiredBy: Peruvian quinua con leche, the warm breakfast quinoa simmered in milk with cinnamon and clove
about: Quinoa simmered slowly in milk with cinnamon and clove until creamy, sweetened with mashed banana and topped with a few slices. It is the kind of breakfast Lima sells in a cup on cold mornings. Quinoa and milk together bring **complete protein, magnesium and calcium**.
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under cold running water for a minute, until the water runs clear. This washes off the bitter coating.
Put the quinoa, milk, cinnamon, clove and salt in a pot (enough for both bowls) and bring it to a gentle simmer. A cinnamon stick, if you have one, is even better.
Cook uncovered on low heat for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains have popped open and the porridge is creamy. Add a splash of milk or water if it gets too thick.
Mash half the banana into the pot for sweetness.
Spoon one portion into a bowl and slice half of the remaining banana on top.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow. It sets firm in the fridge, so loosen it with a splash of milk when you reheat it, and slice the last of the banana on top.
tip: Cook it on Wednesday evening while dinner is on, then reheat one bowl on Thursday and the other on Friday, about 3 minutes each. Stir in a spoon of raisins or a little honey if you like it sweeter.
ingredients: half mashed in, the rest sliced on top

name: Rice and black beans with garlicky couve, orange and grilled queijo coalho
inspiredBy: the Brazilian everyday plate of arroz e feijão with couve refogada, laranja and queijo coalho grelhado
about: Rice and black beans with thin ribbons of garlicky couve (kale or collards), sweet orange slices and squares of golden grilled queijo coalho. It is the Brazilian lunch plate found in every kitchen, and the orange is there to cut through the beans. The beans, greens and cheese bring **iron, folate and calcium**, and the orange helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Use a few spoons of leftover rice, or cook it fresh: rinse it and simmer it covered in twice its volume of water for about 15 minutes, then let it rest off the heat for 5. Use the beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed, and warm them with a splash of water.
Soften the onion in half the oil for about 6 minutes, until soft and golden, then stir it through the beans.

In the same pan, warm the rest of the oil with the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the couve and toss over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until bright green and still a little crisp. Season with salt and the lime juice.
Slice the coalho into thick squares and cook in a dry nonstick pan over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes a side, until golden and spotty.
Pile the rice and beans on a plate. Add the couve, cheese and orange.
tip: Queijo coalho is sold at Brazilian shops; halloumi grills the same way.
ingredients: cook it fresh, see the steps
couve: collard greens or kale, about half a bunch, stems out, rolled and sliced into thin ribbons

name: Caldo tlalpeño with chicken, chickpeas and chipotle
inspiredBy: Mexico City caldo tlalpeño, the smoky chicken and chickpea soup
about: A brothy, smoky Mexico City soup of shredded chicken, chickpeas and carrot in a tomato and chipotle broth, finished with avocado, cilantro and lime. The sauce is fried first, which is what gives it that sweet, deep red base. Chicken and chickpeas bring **protein, iron and folate**.
steps: Blend the tomato, chipotle, garlic, half the onion, the cumin and oregano with a splash of water until smooth.
Warm the oil in a pot, add the sauce and fry it for 5 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and thickens.

Add the chicken thigh, the carrot, the cilantro stems (chop the leaves for the end), the salt and enough water to cover by 3 cm. Simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through. Lift it out and shred it.
Add the chickpeas to the pot and simmer for 5 minutes. Return the chicken.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the rest of the onion, finely chopped, plus the avocado, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
tip: Check the label on the canned chipotles and on any boxed broth you use. Half a chipotle gives a gentle heat; add a whole one if you like it hot.

name: Causa with sardines, egg and avocado
inspiredBy: causa limeña, the cold layered potato terrine from Lima, here with canned sardines and avocado in the middle
about: A cool, lime-bright layer of golden mashed potato spiked with ají amarillo, filled with mashed sardines and creamy avocado, and finished with sliced egg, tomato and cilantro. It is a Lima lunch staple and a lunchbox hero because it is served cold. The sardines bring **omega-3, calcium and vitamin B12**, and the potato brings potassium.
steps: Lower the egg into a pot of boiling water with the potato chunks. Boil for 10 minutes, then lift the egg into cold water. Keep the potatoes going until very tender, about 15 minutes in all. Drain them, and let them steam dry in the pot for a minute.
Mash the warm potatoes until smooth with the ají amarillo paste, most of the lime juice, the oil and a pinch of salt. You want a smooth, bright yellow dough. Chill it for 10 minutes.
Mash the sardines (bones and all, they melt in) with the avocado, the rest of the lime juice, the sliced scallion and a pinch of salt.
Press half the potato into a flat layer on a plate, spread the sardine and avocado filling over it and top with the rest of the potato, smoothing the surface.
Garnish with the sliced egg, tomato wedges and cilantro. Eat it cold or at room temperature.
tip: Boil the potatoes the night before and lunch is a 10 minute assembly. Canned tuna or chicken are the classic fillings, and both work here. Buy sardines in oil or water, not in a sauce, and check the label on the ají paste.
ingredients: canned in oil, drained, with the bones

name: Chicken in hogao with black beans and baked maduros
inspiredBy: Colombian hogao, the tomato and scallion sofrito, over chicken thigh, with black beans in place of red, ripe plantain and avocado from the bandeja paisa plate
about: Chicken thigh simmered in hogao, the Colombian tomato and scallion base, with spinach wilted in, next to warm black beans, sweet caramelized baked plantain and a few slices of avocado. The sweet plantain with the savoury, tangy chicken is the classic Colombian pairing. The chicken, beans and spinach bring **protein, iron and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Peel the plantain and slice it on a long diagonal into thick pieces. Toss with a third of the oil and a pinch of salt and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and caramelized at the edges.
For the hogao, warm half the remaining oil in a pan and soften the scallion and garlic for 2 minutes. Add the tomato and cumin and cook for 8 minutes, until it turns jammy. Scoop out a third.

Use black beans from your Sunday pot (frozen, if you stashed a tub), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed. Warm them in a small pot with the scooped-out hogao and a splash of water.

Brown the chicken pieces in a pan with the rest of the oil for about 6 minutes. Stir in the rest of the hogao and the salt, cover and simmer for 8 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) inside, then fold in the spinach until it wilts. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Serve the chicken with the beans, maduros and avocado, with the cilantro and lime juice over everything.
tip: The plantain should be properly ripe, with a mostly black skin, for real sweetness.

name: Peruvian quinoa soup with beef and vegetables
inspiredBy: Peruvian sopa de quinua, the everyday Andean quinoa soup, with lean ground beef and greens for a fuller meal
about: A bright, herby soup of lean beef, potato, carrot and quinoa, finished with kale, peas, a fistful of cilantro and lime. It is an Andean home classic on cold evenings and it reheats beautifully. The quinoa and beef bring **protein, iron and zinc**, and the lime helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, garlic, ají amarillo paste and cumin until the onion is soft and sweet, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef and stir for 4 minutes, breaking it up, until it loses its raw colour. Add the carrot, potato, oregano and salt, then pour in enough water to cover everything by 3 cm.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer for 12 minutes. Rinse the quinoa in a sieve, stir it in and simmer for 12 minutes more, until the grains look translucent and have popped their tails.
Stir in the peas and kale for the last 3 minutes. Switch off the heat and stir in the cilantro and lime juice.
Eat one portion now. Pack the second for tomorrow's lunch, and loosen it with a splash of water when you reheat it, because the quinoa keeps drinking.
tip: Rinse the quinoa well, and skip bulk bins if you are celiac, since cross-contact is common there. If you use boxed broth in place of water, check the label for wheat.

name: Roasted salmon in ají amarillo glaze with crisp potatoes and salsa criolla
inspiredBy: Peruvian flavours: the ají amarillo of every Lima kitchen, and the lime-and-onion salsa criolla that goes with fish
about: Salmon roasted with a fruity, gently hot ají amarillo and garlic glaze, next to crisp-edged potatoes and roasted red pepper with a sharp onion salsa. The glaze caramelizes while the fish stays tender. Salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the potatoes and red pepper with half the oil and a pinch of the salt on a tray. Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the potatoes are crisp and golden at the edges.

Meanwhile make the salsa criolla. Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 2 minutes to soften its bite, drain, then toss with half the lime juice, half the cilantro and a pinch of salt. Leave it to sit.
Stir the ají amarillo paste with the grated garlic, the rest of the lime juice and a spoon of the oil. Pat the salmon dry, season it with salt and spread the glaze over the top.
Push the vegetables over, put the salmon on the tray skin-side down and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until it just flakes and the glaze has darkened at the edges.
Serve the salmon with the potatoes and pepper, drizzle with the last of the oil, and spoon the salsa criolla on top with the rest of the cilantro.
tip: Ají amarillo paste is sold at Latin grocers and online; check the label, since a few brands add fillers.
ingredients: half for the glaze, half for the salsa
sliced very thin, red onion if you have it

name: Beef picadillo tacos with carrot, peas and cabbage slaw
inspiredBy: Mexican picadillo, the home-style ground beef with tomato, carrot and peas, served in corn tortillas
about: Lean ground beef simmered with tomato, onion, carrot and peas and a little ancho and cumin, spooned into warm corn tortillas with crunchy lime cabbage and a little grated queijo coalho. Picadillo is an everyday Mexican supper and it is on the table in about 35 minutes. The beef brings **iron, zinc and vitamin B12**, and the carrots bring vitamin A.
steps: Toast the ancho in a dry pan for 20 seconds each side, then soak it in hot water for 10 minutes, until soft. Blend it with the tomato, garlic, cumin and oregano until smooth.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion and carrot for 5 minutes. Add the beef and brown it for about 5 minutes, breaking it up.
Pour in the blended sauce and the salt and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick and clinging. Stir in the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Toss the cabbage with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Fill the tortillas with the picadillo and top with the grated coalho (queso fresco or cotija if you have it), the cilantro and the rest of the lime juice. Serve the slaw alongside.
tip: Queso fresco is the Mexican choice if you can find it. Check the tortillas say 100% corn, nothing else, and check the label on the ancho powder if you use it. Picadillo keeps 3 days and is good over rice or in a baked potato.
ingredients: stemmed and seeded, toasted and ground, or 1 tsp ancho powder

name: Galinhada with chicken, corn and peas
inspiredBy: Brazilian galinhada from Goiás, the one-pot chicken and rice coloured with urucum, with a little chicken liver the way many home cooks add giblets
about: Chicken thighs and a little chicken liver cooked with rice in one pot with tomato, sweet pepper and golden urucum, with corn and peas scattered on top and spinach folded through at the end. It is Brazilian Sunday comfort food on a Thursday, and it is even better the next day. The liver is a small amount with a big payoff: it brings **iron, vitamin B12 and folate**.
steps: Toss the chicken with the lime juice, half the salt and the pepper. Warm the oil in a wide heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for about 3 minutes a side. Set it aside.

In the same pot, cook the onion, red pepper and garlic with the colorau for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the tomato and the raw chopped liver and cook for 4 minutes more, stirring, until the tomato is jammy and the liver melts in.
Stir in the rinsed rice for a minute so every grain gets coated. Return the chicken and pour in hot water, about twice the volume of the rice. Add the rest of the salt.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes. Scatter the corn and peas on top, cover again and cook for 5 minutes more. Switch off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and fold in the spinach, scallion and cilantro, so the spinach wilts in the steam. Eat one portion now and pack the second for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: The liver disappears into the rice and just adds depth; leave it out if you prefer. Colorau is sold at Brazilian and Latin shops. Check the label, because some brands cut it with wheat flour; plain sweet paprika plus a pinch of turmeric is a safe stand-in.
ingredients: chicken liver, trimmed and chopped small
or sweet paprika with a pinch of turmeric

name: Salmon moqueca capixaba-style with peppers, tomato and mashed cassava
inspiredBy: moqueca capixaba from Espírito Santo, the coconut-free moqueca cooked with tomato, peppers, cilantro and urucum, with salmon and a mash of cassava where the coast would serve pirão
about: Salmon gently stewed with ripe tomato, sweet pepper, onion, cilantro and golden urucum, spooned over a soft mash of cassava that soaks up the juices, with quick garlicky kale (couve) on the side. The capixaba style skips the coconut and lets the tomato and lime do the work. Salmon brings **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, and the kale brings calcium.
steps: Put the cassava in a pot of salted water, bring it to a boil and cook for about 20 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance.

Meanwhile, rub the salmon with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Layer the onion, pepper and tomato in a wide pan with the garlic, half the oil, the colorau and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and have made a juicy sauce.
Nestle the salmon into the vegetables, cover and simmer gently for 8 minutes, until the fish flakes. Do not stir, or the fish will break up.
Drain the cassava, keeping a splash of its water. Mash it with a spoon of the oil, the rest of the lime juice, a pinch of salt and enough cooking water to make it creamy.
Warm the rest of the oil in a pan with a pinch of salt and toss the kale over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until bright green and still a little crisp.
Spoon the mash into a bowl, lay the fish and stew over it, and scatter with the cilantro. Serve the garlicky kale alongside.
tip: Frozen peeled cassava is sold at most Latin and Caribbean shops and saves the peeling. Any firm fish works, and shrimp is classic. Check the label on the colorau.
ingredients: skinless fillet, or pull the skin off
peeled, cut in chunks, woody core removed
couve: stems out, sliced into thin ribbons

name: Beef tamales in red chile salsa with lime cabbage slaw
inspiredBy: Mexican tamales rojos de res, with olive oil in the masa
about: Soft, tender masa wrapped around shredded beef in a deep guajillo and ancho salsa, steamed in corn husks until the masa pulls away clean. It is the weekend project: put on some music and fold a batch. The masa is corn, so it is **naturally gluten-free**, and the beef brings protein, iron and zinc.
steps: Soak about eight dried corn husks (they are a wrapper, not on the list) in a big bowl of hot water for 30 minutes, weighed down with a plate, until soft and pliable.

Cut the beef into big chunks and simmer it in a pot of salted water with a quarter of the onion and garlic for 75 minutes, until it is fork-tender and shreds easily (well past 71 °C / 160 °F). Lift it out, shred it, and keep about 2 cups of the broth. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
