steps: Toss the chicken with half the lemon juice, half the garlic (crushed), half the oil, the oregano, paprika and a pinch of the salt. Cover, and marinate in the fridge for at least 15 minutes. Never reuse the marinade.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Spread it in a shallow container and cool within 1 hour.

Wash the parsley, spinach, kale, tomatoes and cucumber. Chop the kale fine with the parsley and spinach and massage it with a squeeze of the lemon juice for a minute to soften it. For the tabbouleh, toss the cooled quinoa with the greens, tomatoes, onion, the rest of the lemon juice and oil and a pinch of salt.
Whisk the tahini with a squeeze of lemon, the rest of the garlic and 2 to 3 tablespoons of water until pourable, and dice the cucumber for the plate.

Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken pieces for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until golden and a thermometer reads 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw chicken.

Plate one portion of chicken with the tabbouleh, diced cucumber and a drizzle of the tahini sauce. Cool the second portion of chicken and tabbouleh within 1 hour, keep them and the sauce in separate shallow containers in the fridge and use them tomorrow. Tomorrow, reheat the chicken until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and serve the tabbouleh and sauce cold.
tip: Marinate the chicken in the morning and it only needs 10 minutes in the pan at dinner.

name: Baked chickpea and edamame bites with lemon-tahini sauce and crunchy salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by baked falafel, with edamame for a green centre
about: Herby baked bites made from chickpeas, edamame and oats, served with a lemony tahini sauce and a cucumber, carrot and spinach salad. They bring **plant protein, fibre and folate**, the carrot adds vitamin A, and the tahini adds some calcium and vitamin E.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray with parchment. Heat the frozen edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, until steaming hot, and drain.

Pulse the chickpeas, edamame, oats, onion, parsley, cilantro, garlic, cumin, half the lemon juice, half the salt and half the oil in a food processor until it holds together when pressed but still has some texture.
Shape the mix into small patties, about 5 per portion, and set them on the tray. Brush the tops with a little oil and bake for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Whisk the tahini with the rest of the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and 2 to 3 tablespoons of water until pourable.

Wash the cucumber, carrot, spinach and kale. Shred the kale and rub it with a squeeze of the lemon juice for a minute to soften it, then slice the cucumber, grate the carrot and toss everything together with the spinach. Plate one portion of bites with the salad and a drizzle of sauce.

Cool the second portion of bites within 1 hour on a plate, then keep them and the sauce covered in the fridge. Tomorrow, reheat the bites in a hot oven for 10 minutes until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and toss a fresh portion of the salad rather than keeping the dressed one.
tip: The bites are firmer if the mix rests in the fridge for 10 minutes before shaping.

name: Baked salmon with dill potatoes, broccoli and a crunchy kale and cucumber salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Scandinavian-style salmon and new potato supper
about: A baked salmon fillet with mustard and lemon, dill potatoes and tender broccoli, with a crisp kale and cucumber salad on the side. The salmon is the **omega-3 and vitamin D** star of the plate, and the kale adds calcium and vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes, until almost tender, then drain.
Toss the potatoes with half the oil on a tray and roast for 10 minutes. Add the salmon, brushed with the mustard, and the broccoli, tossed with a little oil.

Roast for 12 to 15 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily and a thermometer reads 70 °C (158 °F) in the thickest part. Use the salmon the day you buy it or thaw it overnight in the fridge. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Wash the cucumber and kale. Shred the kale and rub it with half the lemon juice for a minute to soften it, then slice the cucumber and toss it with the kale, the pepper and a pinch of salt.
Toss the hot potatoes with the dill and the rest of the lemon juice. Plate everything together.

name: Edamame and quinoa plate with egg, crunchy veg and a cilantro-lime dressing
about: Edamame and fluffy quinoa with a firm-boiled egg, carrot, cucumber, spinach and kale, tossed in a garlicky cilantro-lime dressing. It is a packable plate with **plant protein, iron and choline**, and the lime helps your body absorb the iron.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Spread it in a shallow container and cool within 1 hour.
Put the egg in a small pot of cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes so the yolk is completely firm. Cool under cold water, peel and quarter it.
Heat the frozen edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, until steaming hot all the way through, then drain and cool under cold water.
Wash and chop the cilantro, then whisk it with the olive oil, lime juice, crushed garlic and salt.

Wash the carrot, cucumber, spinach and kale, then grate, dice and shred them, rubbing the kale with a squeeze of the dressing for a minute to soften it. Toss them with the quinoa, edamame, onion and most of the dressing.
Top with the egg and drizzle with the rest of the dressing. For a packed lunch, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Cook the quinoa the evening before, cool it within 1 hour and keep it covered in the fridge for no more than 3 days.

name: Chimichurri beef bites with crispy potatoes and a white bean salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Argentinian steak with chimichurri
about: Seared beef bites in a punchy parsley and garlic chimichurri with crispy roasted potatoes and a lemony white bean and tomato salad. A small portion of lean beef plus beans brings **iron, zinc and B12**, with vitamin C from the parsley and lemon to help absorb the iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the potatoes with a third of the oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, make the chimichurri. Stir the parsley, garlic, oregano, chili, half the lemon juice, the rest of the oil but a little for the pan and a pinch of salt together.

Toss the beef with a spoonful of the chimichurri. Heat a heavy pan over high heat with the little oil and sear the beef pieces for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until browned and a thermometer reads 71 °C (160 °F). Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw beef. Never reuse the raw marinade.

Wash the tomatoes, spinach and kale. Shred the kale and rub it with a squeeze of the lemon juice for a minute to soften it. Toss the white beans with the tomatoes, onion, spinach, kale, the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.

Plate one portion of beef, potatoes and salad with a spoonful of chimichurri. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in shallow containers and keep it in the fridge for tomorrow, when you reheat the beef and potatoes until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Dice the potatoes small so they crisp in 25 minutes.

name: Seared salmon with garlicky white beans, tomatoes and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Tuscan-style white bean and greens supper
about: A crisp-edged salmon fillet on a pan of garlicky white beans, burst tomatoes and wilted spinach, with a cool cucumber and parsley salad. It brings **omega-3, vitamin D, iron and folate** in one pan, and it is on the table in about 30 minutes.
steps: Pat the salmon dry and season with a pinch of salt. Heat a third of the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the salmon for 4 minutes, skin side down if it has skin.

Flip the salmon and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more, until it flakes and a thermometer reads 70 °C (158 °F) in the thickest part. Use the salmon the day you buy it, or thaw it overnight in the fridge. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish. Lift it onto a plate.
In the same pan, warm the rest of the oil over medium heat. Cook the garlic and smoked paprika for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes, until they begin to burst.

Stir in the white beans and a splash of water and cook for 3 minutes, until hot. Stir in the shredded kale and the spinach and cook for 1 minute more, until just wilted, then add half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Wash and slice the cucumber and toss it with the onion, parsley and the rest of the lemon juice. Plate the salmon on the beans with the salad on the side.

name: Herby potato salad plate with egg, white beans and crunchy veg
inspiredBy: Inspired by a northern European warm potato salad
about: Warm potatoes tossed in a mustard, lemon and yogurt dressing with dill and parsley, plated with creamy white beans, a firm-boiled egg and crisp vegetables. It brings **protein, choline, potassium and fibre**, and it is just as good cold.
steps: Put the potatoes and the egg in a pot of cold salted water and bring to the boil. Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender, and the egg for 10 minutes so the yolk is completely firm.
Lift out the egg, cool it under cold water, then peel and quarter it. Drain the potatoes and let them steam for 2 minutes.
Stir the yogurt, mustard, lemon juice, dill, parsley, onion and salt together for the dressing.

Toss the warm potatoes with the dressing and the white beans. Wash the cucumber, tomatoes, spinach and kale. Shred the kale and rub it with a squeeze of lemon juice for a minute to soften it, then arrange the vegetables on the plate with the egg and the potato salad.
If packing it, cool the potatoes and the egg within 1 hour before adding the yogurt dressing, keep it cold in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

name: Chili-lime shrimp with roasted sweet potato, black beans and avocado salsa
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Mexican-style shrimp and black bean plate
about: Quick-seared chili-lime shrimp beside crisp roasted sweet potato, warm black beans and a chunky avocado and pepper salsa. The sweet potato brings **vitamin A**, the beans fibre and folate, and the shrimp lean protein and iodine.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the sweet potato cubes with half the oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 22 to 25 minutes, turning once, until the edges are crisp.

Cook fresh shrimp the day you buy them. If they are frozen, thaw them overnight in the fridge and cook them the same day. Keep raw shrimp cold until the pan. Toss the shrimp with half the lime juice, the chili powder, cumin, garlic, a pinch of salt and a little oil. Marinate in the fridge for 10 minutes. Never reuse the marinade.
Wash the avocado, pepper, tomatoes and cilantro. Dice the avocado, pepper and tomatoes and stir them with the onion, cilantro, the rest of the lime juice and a pinch of salt for the salsa.
Warm the black beans in a small pan with a splash of water for 3 minutes, until steaming hot. Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes and scatter them over the salsa.
Heat a pan over high heat and cook the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until they are pink, opaque and curled, 70 °C (158 °F) inside. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw shrimp.
Plate the shrimp with the sweet potato, the black beans and a spoonful of salsa.

name: Marinated chickpea plate with egg, feta, red pepper, cucumber and tomato
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Greek-style mezze plate
about: Chickpeas soaked in a lemony oregano dressing, plated with a firm-boiled egg, a little feta, crisp pepper, cucumber and tomato and a scatter of pumpkin seeds. The chickpeas bring **protein, folate and iron**, and the lemon and red pepper add vitamin C to help absorb the iron.
steps: Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, cumin and salt in a bowl. Stir in the chickpeas and onion and leave to marinate for at least 10 minutes, or up to a few hours in the fridge.
Put the egg in a small pot of cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes so the yolk is completely firm. Cool under cold water, peel and quarter it.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they pop.
Wash the pepper, cucumber, tomatoes and parsley, then slice and halve them as needed.
Spoon the marinated chickpeas onto a plate and arrange the vegetables, egg and feta around them. Scatter the parsley and seeds over the top.
For a packed lunch, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: The marinated chickpeas keep 3 days in the fridge, so make a double batch to snack on.

name: Spiced red lentil and carrot patties with roasted broccoli and tahini-yogurt sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian-style lentil tikkis
about: Pan-crisped patties of red lentils, grated carrot and oats with cumin and turmeric, served with roasted broccoli and a cool tahini-yogurt sauce. Lentils bring **plant protein, iron and folate**, and the broccoli adds vitamin C to help absorb that iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the broccoli with a third of the oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 18 to 20 minutes, until the tips are charred. Wash and shred the kale, toss it with a little of the oil and add it to the tray for the last 6 minutes so the edges crisp.
Simmer the lentils in just enough water to cover them by 1 cm for 10 to 12 minutes, until very soft and the water is absorbed. Add a splash more water if they catch. Mash them roughly in a bowl.
Stir in the carrot, oats, onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, turmeric and salt. Let the mix sit for 5 minutes, then shape it into 4 patties.
Heat the rest of the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and hot all the way through.
Squeeze the grated cucumber dry and stir it into the yogurt with the tahini and lemon juice for the sauce.
Plate the patties with the broccoli and a spoonful of the sauce.

name: Kiwi with toasted pumpkin seeds
about: Juicy kiwi with a handful of toasted pumpkin seeds. It brings **vitamin C and magnesium** in two minutes.
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until they pop. Peel and slice the kiwi and sprinkle the seeds over it.

name: Roasted red pepper and walnut dip with carrot and cucumber sticks
inspiredBy: Inspired by Syrian muhammara
about: A smoky red pepper and walnut dip with a little lemon and cumin, for scooping with crisp carrot and cucumber. The walnuts bring **omega-3 and vitamin E**.
steps: Heat the grill to high. Grill the whole pepper for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until the skin blackens. Cool it in a covered bowl for 5 minutes, then peel and deseed it.
Blend the pepper with the walnuts, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, paprika, cumin and salt until chunky-smooth.
Wash and cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks and serve them with the dip.
tip: Make a double batch of dip: it keeps 3 days in the fridge.

name: Apple slices with almonds
about: Crisp apple with a handful of almonds. It brings **fibre and vitamin E**.
steps: Wash and slice the apple and serve it with the almonds.

name: Blueberries with walnuts
about: Sweet blueberries with a handful of walnuts. Together they bring **omega-3, vitamin E and fibre**.
steps: Rinse the blueberries and serve them with the walnuts.

name: Warm smoky edamame with lemon
about: Warm edamame tossed with smoked paprika, lemon and a drizzle of olive oil. It brings **plant protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Heat the frozen edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, until steaming hot all the way through, then drain. Toss with the olive oil, lemon juice, smoked paprika and salt and serve warm.

name: White bean and herb cucumber cups
inspiredBy: Inspired by a bruschetta topping, served on cucumber
about: Thick cucumber rounds topped with a lemony mashed white bean, tomato and parsley mix. It is crunchy, cool and brings **fibre and folate**.
steps: Mash the white beans roughly with the lemon juice, olive oil and salt. Stir in the tomato and parsley.
Wash the cucumber and cut it into thick rounds. Scoop a little out of the centre of each round if you like.
Pile the bean mix on the rounds and scatter the walnuts over the top.

name: Cucumber and tomato with feta and oregano
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Greek horiatiki, without the lettuce
about: Chunky cucumber and tomato with a little crumbled feta, olive oil and oregano. Light, fresh and brings **calcium and vitamin C**.
steps: Wash the cucumber and tomatoes and chunk them onto a plate. Scatter the feta and walnuts over them, drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with the oregano.

name: Lemon-tahini dip with pepper, carrot and cucumber sticks
about: A creamy lemon and garlic tahini dip for scooping with crunchy pepper, carrot and cucumber. The tahini brings **calcium, copper and vitamin E**.
steps: Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice, crushed garlic, salt and 2 to 3 tablespoons of water until smooth and pourable. Wash and cut the pepper, carrot and cucumber into sticks and serve them with the dip.

name: Kiwi with walnuts
about: Juicy kiwi with a handful of walnuts. It brings **vitamin C and omega-3** in two minutes.
steps: Peel and slice the kiwi and serve it with the walnuts.

name: Apple slices with walnuts and cinnamon
about: Crisp apple with a handful of walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. It brings **fibre and omega-3**.
steps: Wash and slice the apple, dust it with the cinnamon and serve it with the walnuts.

name: Lemony marinated chickpeas with cucumber and parsley
about: Chickpeas soaked in lemon, olive oil and cumin with crunchy cucumber and fresh parsley. A small cup brings **plant protein, folate and fibre**.
steps: Stir the lemon juice, olive oil, cumin and salt together. Toss in the chickpeas, cucumber and parsley and leave for at least 10 minutes. Keep covered in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

name: Greek yogurt with blueberries and cinnamon
about: A small cup of thick Greek yogurt with blueberries and a dusting of cinnamon. It brings **protein and calcium**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a cup, top with the rinsed blueberries and dust with the cinnamon.

name: Sardines on warm lemony lentils with tomato, egg, kale and crunchy veg
inspiredBy: Inspired by a French warm lentil salad
about: Canned sardines laid over warm garlicky lentils with softened tomatoes, lemon and parsley, plus a firm-boiled egg, a lemony kale salad and cucumber and carrot sticks. The sardines bring **omega-3 and calcium from their soft bones**, the egg adds choline, and the lentils add fibre, folate and iron.
steps: Put the egg in a small pot of cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes so the yolk is completely firm. Cool under cold water, peel and quarter it.
Warm the olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Cook the crushed garlic for 30 seconds, then add the rinsed lentils and a splash of water and heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until steaming hot.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, until they just soften. Take the pan off the heat and stir in half the lemon juice, the parsley, the salt and a good grind of pepper.
Wash the kale, cucumber and carrot. Shred the kale and rub it with the rest of the lemon juice for a minute to soften it, then cut the cucumber and carrot into sticks.
Drain the sardines and lay them over the warm lentils. Plate with the egg, the kale and the sticks.

Keep any opened tin of sardines covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. For a packed lunch, spread the lentils in a shallow container to cool, refrigerate them within 2 hours, then pack everything in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day. The lentils are good cold.
tip: Keep the rest of an opened can of lentils covered in the fridge and use it within 3 days.

name: Cherry and walnut overnight oats
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss bircher muesli
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt, with frozen cherries that thaw into a ruby swirl, and a crunch of walnuts. Five minutes the night before gives you **protein and fibre** before the day starts.
steps: Wash your hands. Stir the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon together in a jar until there are no dry patches.
Spoon the frozen cherries on top, put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. They thaw into the oats and turn them pink.
In the morning, stir it up. If it is too thick, loosen it with a splash of milk. Scatter the walnuts on just before eating so they stay crisp.
Keep the jar in the fridge and eat it within 2 days of making it.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, simmer the frozen cherries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

name: Toasted oat and quinoa porridge with skillet-seared banana
inspiredBy: Inspired by a skillet-toasted oatmeal, with quinoa for a nutty bite
about: Oats and a little quinoa toasted in the pan, simmered in milk until creamy, then topped with banana slices seared until caramelised and crunchy sunflower seeds. The banana brings **potassium, and the seeds vitamin E**, so it needs no sugar.
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve under cold water for 30 seconds. Warm a small saucepan over medium heat, add the oats and quinoa and toast them, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 2 minutes.

Pour in the milk and a splash of water, add the cinnamon and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 14 minutes, stirring now and then and adding a little more water if it gets thick, until the quinoa is tender and the porridge is creamy.
While it simmers, heat a dry nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and sear the banana slices for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until golden and caramelised.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the banana and sunflower seeds.
tip: Short on time? Use only rolled oats and simmer for 5 minutes.

name: Black bean, pepper and kale skillet scramble
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos con frijoles
about: Eggs scrambled firm in a hot skillet with smoky black beans, sweet red pepper and a handful of kale, finished with feta. The beans and kale add **fibre, folate and iron**, so it fills you up without needing toast.
steps: Wash the pepper and kale. Warm the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the pepper and cook for 3 minutes until just soft.
Stir in the beans, cumin and paprika and cook for 2 minutes. Add the kale and a splash of water and cook for 1 minute until it wilts.
Crack the eggs in, add the salt and stir gently. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the eggs are completely set with no liquid and the yolks are firm.
Spoon onto a plate and crumble the feta over the top.
tip: A squeeze of lime at the end brightens it.

name: Chili-lime grilled chicken with charred corn and black bean salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican elote and a Tex-Mex grill supper
about: Chicken breast marinated in lime, chili and cumin, grilled until golden, on a bright salad of skillet-charred sweet corn, black beans, tomatoes and avocado. The beans and corn bring **fibre and folate**, the kale and carrot add calcium and vitamin A, and the lime on top helps you absorb the iron from the beans.
steps: Make the marinade in a shallow dish: half the lime juice, half the oil, the chili powder, paprika, cumin, garlic and half the salt. Trim any visible fat from the chicken, add it and turn to coat. Cover and marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes or up to 4 hours. Never reuse the marinade. Wash your hands, the knife and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken.

Heat the grill to medium-high, or use a grill pan, or a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element. Lift the chicken out, wipe off the extra marinade and discard it. Grill for 6 to 7 minutes per side, until golden with a few dark grill marks (never black; trim off any black bits) and 74 °C (165 °F) on a thermometer in the thickest part. Rest 5 minutes on a clean plate.
While the chicken cooks, heat a dry skillet over high heat. Add the corn and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring only now and then, until the kernels are speckled golden at the edges.

Wash the tomatoes, kale, carrot, onion and cilantro. In a big bowl massage the kale with a pinch of the salt and a squeeze of the lime for a minute, then toss in the warm corn, beans, tomatoes, carrot, onion, cilantro, the rest of the lime juice, oil and salt.

Slice the chicken and serve it over the salad with the avocado, feta and sunflower seeds on top. Put the second portion in a shallow container, without the avocado, within 1 hour. It keeps up to 3 days in the fridge; add fresh avocado at lunch. If you pack it for lunch, carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Eat the leftover cold on the salad, or warm the chicken slices to 74 °C and keep the salad cold.
ingredients: kernels, thawed if frozen and patted dry

name: Skillet salmon with crisp garlic potatoes and asparagus
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic pan-seared salmon supper
about: Salmon seared skin-side down until the skin crackles, with golden garlicky potatoes and asparagus cooked in the same pan, finished with a lemon-parsley yogurt. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the asparagus adds folate.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes until nearly tender, then drain and let them steam dry for 2 minutes. Buy the salmon the day you cook it and keep it in the fridge until then.

Heat half the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes cut-side down with the paprika and cook for 8 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Add the garlic for the last minute so it does not burn. Move them to the side of the pan.

Pat the salmon dry and season with salt and pepper. Add the rest of the oil to the free half of the pan and lay the salmon in skin-side down. Cook for 5 minutes until the skin is crisp, flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, until it flakes and reads 70 °C (158 °F) in the thickest part.
Add the asparagus to the pan for the last 3 minutes, turning, until bright green and just tender. Wash your hands, the board and the plate that held the raw fish.

Stir the yogurt with half the lemon juice and half the parsley and a pinch of salt. Squeeze the rest of the lemon over the salmon, potatoes and asparagus, spoon the yogurt alongside and scatter with the rest of the parsley.
tip: Salmon is cooked fresh and not saved for later; eat it the same day.

name: Lean beef kebabs with herby quinoa and cucumber-tomato salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern shish kebab and tabbouleh, with quinoa for the grain
about: Cubes of lean sirloin and red pepper marinated in lemon, garlic and cumin, grilled on skewers and served on a lemony quinoa salad packed with parsley and mint. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, and the lemon and parsley help you absorb the iron in the quinoa.
steps: If you use wooden skewers, put them in water to soak for 30 minutes before you start. Mix half the lemon juice, half the oil, the garlic, cumin, paprika and a pinch of the salt in a dish. Trim any visible fat from the beef, add the cubes, turn to coat, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 20 minutes and up to 4 hours. Never reuse the marinade. Wash your hands, the knife and the board after handling the raw beef.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes until the germ ring pops out. Drain well, spread it on a tray to cool, and fluff it with a fork.

Thread the beef, pepper and onion onto skewers. Grill over medium-high heat, or in a grill pan, or under a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element, for 8 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned with a few dark grill marks. Push the thermometer in from the side into the centre of the largest cube: it should read 71 °C (160 °F). Rest for 3 minutes on a clean plate.
Toss the cooled quinoa with the parsley, mint, cucumber, tomatoes, the rest of the lemon juice and oil and the walnuts.

Serve the kebabs on the quinoa. Put the second portion in a shallow container in the fridge within 1 hour, and keep it up to 3 days. Reheat the beef to 74 °C (165 °F) and eat the quinoa salad cold. If you pack it for lunch, carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Cut the beef into cubes of the same size so they all cook at once.
ingredients: trimmed of all visible fat, cut in 3 cm cubes

name: Grilled vegetable plate with crisp chickpeas and garlic-yogurt sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine mezze, eaten as a main
about: Asparagus, carrot, red pepper and onion grilled until tender and golden, with chickpeas crisped in the skillet and a cool garlic-mint yogurt sauce. Chickpeas, feta and walnuts make it a **proper, protein-rich meal**, and the carrots bring vitamin A.
steps: Put the carrot halves in a bowl with a splash of water, cover and microwave for 3 minutes (or simmer them for 4 minutes) until they start to soften, then pat dry. Brush all the vegetables with half the oil and sprinkle with half the salt. Heat the grill to medium-high, or use a grill pan or a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element.

Grill the vegetables in batches, 4 to 5 minutes per side, until tender with a few dark grill marks (never black; trim off any black bits). Start the carrot and onion first, then the pepper and asparagus.

While the vegetables cook, heat the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chickpeas with the cumin and paprika and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden and a little crisp.
Stir the yogurt with the garlic, lemon juice, mint and a pinch of salt.

Pile the vegetables on a plate, spoon over the chickpeas and the sauce, and finish with the feta and walnuts. Put the second portion in a shallow container, sauce on the side, within 1 hour. Keep up to 3 days and eat it cold or at room temperature. If you pack it for lunch, carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Eat the leftover cold with the sauce spooned on, or warm only the chickpeas to 74 °C.

name: Smoky skillet trout with sweet potato wedges, blistered tomatoes and avocado-lime yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Southern-style pan-fried fish supper, with a Tex-Mex avocado crema
about: Trout fillets rubbed with smoked paprika and cumin, seared until crisp, with roasted sweet potato wedges, cherry tomatoes blistered in the same pan and a cool avocado-lime yogurt. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the sweet potato and tomatoes bring vitamin A and C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the sweet potato wedges with a third of the oil, half the paprika and half the salt on a tray. Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and browned at the edges.
Mash the avocado with the yogurt, lime juice, garlic and a pinch of salt until creamy, then stir in half the cilantro. Buy the trout the day you cook it and keep it in the fridge until then.

Pat the trout dry and rub the flesh with the cumin, the rest of the paprika and a little oil. Heat the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the trout skin-side down for 4 minutes until crisp, flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it flakes and reads 70 °C (158 °F) in the thickest part. Wash your hands, the board and the plate that held the raw fish.
Lift the trout onto a clean plate. Add the whole tomatoes to the hot pan and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking, until they blister and just burst.
Serve the trout with the wedges and tomatoes, spoon over the avocado-lime yogurt and scatter with the rest of the cilantro.
tip: Salmon works in place of the trout.

name: Lemon-garlic shrimp skewers with warm lentil and herb salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mediterranean grilled prawns on a warm lentil salad
about: Shrimp tossed in lemon, garlic and smoked paprika, grilled in minutes, on a warm lentil salad with softened red pepper, red onion, parsley and mint. The lentils bring **iron, folate and fibre**, and the shrimp bring iodine.
steps: If you use wooden skewers, put them in water to soak for 30 minutes before you start. Mix half the lemon juice, the garlic, paprika, chili flakes, half the oil and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Add the shrimp, toss and marinate in the fridge for 15 minutes. Never reuse the marinade. Wash your hands, the bowl and the board after handling the raw shrimp.

Warm the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the pepper and onion for 4 minutes, add the lentils and warm them through for 3 minutes. Take off the heat and stir in the rest of the lemon juice, the parsley, mint, cucumber and a pinch of salt.

Thread the shrimp onto the skewers. Lift them from the marinade and discard it. Grill over high heat, or in a grill pan, or under a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element, for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque, lightly browned (never black) and 70 °C (158 °F) in the thickest part.
Spoon the lentil salad onto a plate, lay the skewers on top and scatter with the walnuts.
tip: Cook shrimp the day you thaw them and do not save them.
ingredients: peeled and deveined, thawed in the fridge if frozen

name: Tandoori-style grilled chicken with spiced sweet potato, chickpeas and cucumber raita
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian tandoori chicken, cooked on a grill or broiler instead of in a clay oven
about: Chicken breast marinated in yogurt, ginger, garlic and garam masala, grilled until golden, with a tray of cumin-roasted sweet potato and chickpeas and a cooling cucumber raita. The yogurt marinade keeps the lean breast tender, and the sweet potato brings **vitamin A and potassium**.
steps: Stir half the yogurt with the ginger, garlic, garam masala, turmeric, lemon juice and half the salt in a dish. Trim any visible fat from the chicken, add it, turn to coat, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour and up to overnight. Never reuse the marinade. Wash your hands, the knife and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the sweet potato and chickpeas with half the oil, the cumin and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until the sweet potato is tender and browned at the edges.

Heat the grill to medium-high, or use a grill pan, or a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element. Lift the chicken out of the marinade, wipe off the extra and discard it. Brush with the rest of the oil and grill for 6 to 7 minutes per side, until golden with a few dark grill marks (never black; trim off any black bits) and 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part. Rest for 5 minutes on a clean plate.
Wash the cucumber and mint. Stir the grated cucumber (squeezed dry), the rest of the yogurt, the mint and a pinch of salt into a raita.
Slice the chicken and serve with the sweet potato, chickpeas and raita.
tip: Marinate in the morning for the best flavour. If your broiler is in the same oven, roast the tray first and keep it warm while the chicken cooks. Cook only what you will eat that day.
ingredients: half for the marinade, half for the raita

name: Garlicky lentil and tomato skillet with firm-set eggs
inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern lentils with tomato and eggs
about: Lentils simmered with garlic, tomato and smoked paprika with eggs set firm on top, all in one skillet. The lentils bring **iron, folate and fibre**, and the lemon at the end helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic, paprika, cumin and chili flakes and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for 5 minutes until they collapse into a sauce. Stir in the lentils and 3 tablespoons of water and simmer for 3 minutes.
Make a well in the lentils for each egg and crack them in. Cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are firm all the way through.
Finish with the lemon juice, parsley and feta.
tip: Eat it straight away; eggs are not saved for later.

name: Skillet buckwheat with crisp tofu, red pepper and kale
inspiredBy: Inspired by a ginger-sesame tofu stir-fry, over buckwheat groats
about: Nutty buckwheat groats under golden tofu, red pepper and kale tossed in ginger and garlic, with a lime-tahini drizzle. It is a **meat-free, protein-rich** lunch, with magnesium from the buckwheat and some calcium from the calcium-set tofu.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat, then simmer it in twice its volume of water with a pinch of salt for 12 minutes, until tender and the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Heat half the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil and the pepper and cook for 4 minutes until soft and a little browned. Add the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then the kale, a splash of water and the salt and toss for 2 minutes until the kale wilts.
Whisk the tahini with the lime juice and 1 tablespoon of water. Return the tofu to the pan, spoon everything over the buckwheat, drizzle with the tahini and top with the grated carrot.
tip: To pack it, make it the evening before: cool it in a shallow container within 1 hour, keep it in the fridge and carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack. Eat it cold or warmed to 74 °C.

name: Smoky black bean and sweet potato skillet with red pepper and avocado
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Tex-Mex bean and sweet potato taco filling, without the tortilla
about: Diced sweet potato browned in a skillet with cumin and smoked paprika, then black beans and red pepper, with creamy avocado and feta on top. The sweet potato brings **vitamin A**, and the beans bring fibre, folate and plant protein.
steps: Warm the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sweet potato and a splash of water, cover and cook for 8 minutes, stirring once, until nearly tender. Uncover and cook for 4 minutes more until browned at the edges.
Add the pepper, onion, cumin, paprika, chili powder and salt and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the beans and cook for 3 minutes until hot.
Finish with the lime juice. Top with the avocado, feta and cilantro.

name: Canned salmon bowl with charred corn, seared broccoli and lemon-tahini
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Mediterranean-style salad bowl, with skillet-charred corn
about: Flaked canned salmon on skillet-charred sweet corn with broccoli seared in a hot skillet until tender and a little browned, crunchy cucumber and carrot and a lemon-tahini sauce. The salmon, with its soft bones, brings **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D**.
steps: Heat a dry skillet over high heat. Add the corn and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring only now and then, until the kernels are speckled golden at the edges. Tip it onto a plate.
Add the oil and the broccoli with a splash of water, cover for 2 minutes, then uncover and sear for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until bright green with golden edges.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, 1 tablespoon of water and the salt into a smooth sauce.
Fill a bowl with the corn, broccoli, cucumber, carrot, onion and parsley. Flake the salmon on top and drizzle with the sauce.
Keep any opened tin of fish covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. If you pack this, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
ingredients: kernels, thawed if frozen and patted dry

name: Orange with walnuts
about: A juicy orange with a handful of walnuts. The orange gives **vitamin C** and the walnuts plant omega-3 and crunch.
steps: Wash the orange before peeling it, then peel and segment it. Eat it with the walnuts.

name: Kiwi with walnuts
about: Sweet-tart kiwi with crunchy walnuts. Together they bring **vitamin C and plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the kiwi, slice it in half and scoop with a spoon. Eat with the walnuts.

name: Carrot and pepper sticks with lemon-tahini dip
about: Crunchy carrot and red pepper sticks for dunking in a creamy lemon-tahini dip. A snack with **vitamin A, vitamin C and some calcium**.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut them into sticks. Stir the tahini, lemon juice, salt and about 1 tablespoon of water into a smooth dip and serve it alongside.

name: Skillet-toasted spiced chickpeas
about: Chickpeas crisped in a hot skillet with cumin and smoked paprika. Crunchy, savoury and full of **fibre and plant protein**.
steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chickpeas and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden and crisp. Toss with the cumin, paprika and salt and let them cool for a few minutes before eating.

name: Skillet-charred edamame with lime and chili
about: Edamame charred in a hot dry skillet with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of chili. A snack with **plant protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Heat a dry skillet over high heat. Add the frozen edamame and a splash of water, cover for 2 minutes, then uncover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing, until the water is gone, they are hot all the way through and blistered in spots. Toss with the lime juice, chili flakes and salt and let them cool for a minute.

name: Skillet-warmed cinnamon apple with tahini
about: Apple slices warmed in a skillet until just soft, with a swirl of tahini. Sweet, nutty and filling, with **fibre and a little calcium**.
steps: Wash and slice the apple. Warm a nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the apple and the cinnamon and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until just soft and golden at the edges. Drizzle with the tahini.

name: Greek yogurt with kiwi and walnuts
about: Thick yogurt with chopped kiwi and crunchy walnuts. It brings **calcium, protein and vitamin C**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, add the chopped kiwi and scatter with the walnuts.

name: Cherries with walnuts
about: Sweet cherries with crunchy walnuts. It brings **vitamin C and plant omega-3**.
steps: Thaw the cherries in the fridge, then drain any extra juice and eat them with the walnuts.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, simmer the frozen cherries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A banana with walnuts and a shake of cinnamon. It brings **potassium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Slice the banana, scatter with the walnuts and cinnamon.

name: Gulf foul with lemon, cumin and khubz
inspiredBy: Saudi and Emirati foul, the fava bean breakfast every Gulf family knows, with a boiled egg
about: Warm fava beans mashed with garlic, cumin and lemon, then piled with fresh tomato, onion, parsley and a little green chili, with a spoon of tahini, a boiled egg and hot whole-wheat khubz for scooping. A proper Gulf breakfast that keeps you going until lunch. The fava beans bring **folate, iron and fibre**, and the tahini adds calcium.
steps: Lower the egg into a pot of boiling water and cook it for 10 minutes, then cool it under cold water and peel. Do this first so it is ready when the beans are.
Warm half the oil in a small pan, add the garlic and cumin for 20 seconds, then tip in the fava beans with a splash of water and the salt.
Warm over medium heat for 5 minutes, then mash about half of the beans with a fork so it is chunky and creamy.
Warm the khubz in a dry pan or the toaster until it is soft with a few toasty spots.
Spoon the foul into a shallow bowl and top it with the tomato, onion, parsley and green chili.
Squeeze over the lemon, drizzle with the rest of the oil and the tahini, and serve with the halved egg and the khubz.
tip: Fresh chopped mint is a common addition. Cook a double batch of fava, or open a tin with no salt added, and a second breakfast is quick.
ingredients: cooked from dried, or a tin with no salt added, drained

name: Balaleet-inspired saffron vermicelli with a cardamom omelette
inspiredBy: Emirati balaleet, the sweet-savoury vermicelli with a thin omelette on top, made here with whole wheat pasta and much less sugar
about: Thin strands of whole wheat pasta fried in a little ghee, then simmered with saffron, cardamom and a chopped date for just enough sweetness, and topped with a soft, lightly spiced omelette and toasted almonds. It's the sweet and salty breakfast of the Emirates and Qatar. The two eggs bring **protein and choline**, and the almonds add vitamin E.
steps: Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water. Melt the ghee in a small pan and stir-fry the broken pasta for 2 to 3 minutes until it smells toasty and turns a shade darker.

Add about a third of a cup (80 ml) of hot water, the chopped date, half the cardamom and half the salt. Simmer, stirring now and then, adding a splash more water only if the pasta is still hard, until it is tender and has soaked up nearly all the liquid, about 8 minutes. Stir in most of the saffron water and let it finish drying.

Beat the eggs with the rest of the cardamom, a teaspoon of the saffron water and the rest of the salt. Warm the oil in a non-stick pan and pour in the eggs, tilting the pan so they spread thin. Cook until no runny egg is left, about 2 minutes, then fold or roll the omelette.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden. Pile the vermicelli on a plate, lay the omelette over it and scatter with the almonds. Serve with the orange segments on the side.
tip: Rose water is traditional if you have a bottle: a few drops in the saffron water. A little date syrup (dibs) or honey over the omelette is a common finish. On a weekday, cook the vermicelli the night before. It reheats in a minute with a splash of water while the omelette cooks.
ingredients: thin spaghetti, snapped into short pieces
a small date, pitted and finely chopped

name: Eggs with tomato and green chili, with cucumber and khubz
inspiredBy: Gulf beid wa tamatem, the everyday tomato and egg skillet
about: Eggs set gently into a juicy skillet of tomato, onion, garlic and green chili, with crunchy cucumber and warm khubz. Quick and homey, and very Gulf. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, and cooked tomato is a good source of lycopene.
steps: Warm the oil in a small skillet and soften the onion with the garlic and green chili until golden at the edges, about 4 minutes. Stir in the turmeric and black pepper for a few seconds.
Add the tomato and the salt. Cook over medium heat, mashing the tomato with your spoon, until it has collapsed into a thick, jammy sauce, about 7 minutes.

Make two wells in the sauce and crack the eggs into them. Cover and cook gently for 4 to 6 minutes, until the whites and yolks are both firm. If you prefer them scrambled, stir the eggs in instead and cook until no runny egg is left.
Scatter with the cilantro. Serve straight from the pan with the cucumber and warm khubz.
tip: The tomato base keeps for three days in the fridge, so cook a double batch on Wednesday and reheat it on Saturday morning.

name: Gulf lentil soup with lemon and khubz
inspiredBy: Shorbat adas, the red lentil soup of Gulf kitchens, brightened with lemon
about: A smooth, golden red lentil soup with carrot, onion and cumin, finished with lots of lemon and fresh herbs. A crisp cucumber and khubz on the side make it a full lunch. The lentils bring **iron, folate and plenty of fibre**, and the lemon helps your body use that iron.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot and soften the onion and carrot for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils, the salt and about 2½ cups (600 ml) of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 20 minutes, until the lentils have fallen apart and the carrot is tender.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth, or leave it a little rustic. Add a splash of water if it is thicker than you like.
Stir in the lemon juice, taste and add more salt or lemon if it needs it.
Ladle into a bowl and scatter with the cilantro and parsley. Serve with the khubz, the cucumber and an extra squeeze of lemon.
tip: Make it Sunday evening. It keeps three days and thickens as it sits, so loosen it with a splash of water. Double it and freeze a portion if you like. A pinch of chili flakes on top is common.

name: Spiced chickpeas (nakhi) with labneh, radish and khubz
inspiredBy: the Gulf street-side boiled chickpeas, nakhi, here served over labneh with a fresh salad
about: Warm chickpeas tossed with garlic, cumin and lemon, spooned over thick labneh with crunchy radish, cucumber, mint and parsley, and eaten with khubz. It comes together in 15 minutes and tastes fresh and tangy. Chickpeas and labneh together give you **protein, fibre and calcium** in one plate.
steps: Warm half the oil in a small pan, add the garlic and cumin and stir for 20 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of water and the salt. Warm them through for 4 to 5 minutes, crushing a few with the back of the spoon, then take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.
Spread the labneh across a plate and spoon the warm chickpeas over it. Drizzle with the rest of the oil.
Toss the radish, cucumber, mint and parsley together and pile them on top. Dust with the sumac.
Warm the khubz and tear it up to scoop everything.
tip: A teaspoon of toasted sesame seeds over the top is a nice touch. Warm the chickpeas gently so they stay soft.

name: Gulf-style chicken shawarma plate with garlic labneh sauce and salata
inspiredBy: Gulf chicken shawarma, pan-seared at home with baharat instead of on a spit
about: Chicken marinated in labneh, garlic, lemon and baharat, seared until browned, with a cool garlic-labneh sauce, a crisp cucumber and tomato salata, quick-pickled radish and carrot and warm khubz. It tastes like a shawarma shop but sits on a plate. The chicken brings **protein and niacin**, and the carrot, herbs and tomato add vitamins A and C.
steps: Mix half the labneh with half the garlic, half the lemon juice, the baharat, half the oil and a pinch of the salt. Toss the chicken strips in it and leave for 15 minutes, or up to a day in the fridge.
Toss the radish and grated carrot with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt and leave them to pickle while the chicken marinates.
For the sauce, whisk the rest of the labneh with the remaining garlic, a squeeze of lemon and a splash of water until it pours like thick cream.
Warm the remaining oil in a heavy pan over high heat and sear the chicken in a single layer, turning once, until browned at the edges and cooked through, about 6 minutes.
Toss the cucumber, tomato and parsley with the last of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the khubz. Pile the chicken, salata and pickled radish and carrot on a plate or into the bread and spoon the garlic sauce over.
tip: Roll everything into the khubz for a handheld wrap, or use chicken breast if you prefer it leaner.
ingredients: for the marinade and the sauce

name: Chicken machboos with brown basmati, almonds and raisins
inspiredBy: Kuwaiti, Emirati and Bahraini chicken machboos, made with brown basmati and less oil
about: Chicken browned with onion and tomato, then simmered with baharat, saffron and sour dried loomi into a fragrant pot of brown basmati rice, finished with toasted almonds and sweet raisins. A Friday lunch favourite in homes across the Gulf. The brown rice and almonds add **fibre and vitamin E**, and tomorrow's lunch is already made.
steps: Soak the rinsed rice in cold water for 20 minutes if you have time, then drain. Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water. Pierce the loomi a few times with a knife.
Melt the ghee with the oil in a wide, heavy pot and fry the onion over medium heat until deep golden, about 10 minutes. Stir in the garlic, baharat and tomato paste for a minute.
Add the chicken and brown it for 5 minutes, turning, then add the tomato and the salt. Cook until the tomato breaks down and the pot smells rich, about 6 minutes.
Pour in enough hot water to cover the chicken by a finger, add the loomi, then bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.

Add the rice, pressing it just under the liquid, and top up with hot water if needed so it is covered by about 1 cm. Simmer, covered, over low heat for 30 to 35 minutes, until the rice is tender and the water is gone. Drizzle over the saffron water and rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
While the rice rests, toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden, then scatter them over the rice with the raisins.
Fluff gently and serve, nudging the loomi aside or squeezing it over your plate. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Dried black limes (loomi) are sold whole at Middle Eastern grocers. Add a cinnamon stick and a few cardamom pods with the water for a more traditional pot, and a handful of chopped cilantro on top.
ingredients: 1 whole for the pot of 2 servings, pierced

name: Grilled kanaad (Spanish mackerel) with dakkous and khubz
inspiredBy: Gulf samak mashwi with dakkous, the garlicky tomato and chili sauce served beside grilled fish across the Emirates, Qatar and Bahrain
about: A thick steak of kanaad, the Spanish mackerel the Gulf loves, rubbed with turmeric and grilled, with a punchy dakkous of crushed tomato, garlic, green chili, cumin and lemon, and a crunchy cucumber and carrot salad. It gives you **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, the carrot adds vitamin A and the sauce adds vitamin C.
steps: Pat the fish dry and rub it with the turmeric and half the salt. Leave it on the counter while you make the sauce.

For the dakkous, warm half the vegetable oil in a small pan and cook the garlic and green chili for 30 seconds. Add the tomato, cumin and a pinch of salt and cook, crushing the tomato with a spoon, until thick and saucy, about 8 minutes. Off the heat, stir in half the lemon juice and the parsley.

Heat a heavy pan or a grill until very hot. Brush the fish with the rest of the vegetable oil and cook for 5 to 6 minutes on each side, until the skin is crisp and the flesh just flakes at the thickest part.
Toss the cucumber and carrot with the rest of the lemon juice, the olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Warm the khubz. Serve the fish with a generous spoonful of dakkous on top, the salad alongside and the bread for mopping.
tip: Frozen Spanish mackerel from an Asian or Middle Eastern market is the usual source. King mackerel, Atlantic mackerel or hammour also work if you want a milder fish. Dakkous is great on rice and eggs too, so a double batch will not go to waste.

name: Lamb saloona with eggplant and pumpkin
inspiredBy: Emirati saloona, the everyday tomato and vegetable stew eaten with rice or bread, made with extra vegetables, less meat and no potato
about: Tender lamb simmered with tomato, onion, eggplant and sweet pumpkin in a turmeric and baharat sauce with a whole chili and a tang of loomi, thick enough to scoop with khubz. An everyday Emirati stew. The pumpkin and eggplant bring **vitamin A, potassium and fibre**, and the lamb adds iron and zinc.
steps: Warm the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in batches, about 5 minutes, then lift it out.
Soften the onion in the same pot for 6 minutes, then stir in the garlic, turmeric, half the baharat and the tomato paste until fragrant.
Return the lamb with the tomato, the loomi, the whole green chili, the salt and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes, until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the eggplant and pumpkin and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until everything is soft and the sauce has thickened. Add a splash of water if it gets dry.
Stir in the rest of the baharat, taste and adjust the salt. Fish out the chili and loomi, or leave them in for the table.
Serve with warm khubz. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch, with its bread wrapped separately.
tip: Saloona is even better the next day. Chicken, fish or just vegetables with chickpeas all make good saloona too.
ingredients: in large cubes, butternut or kabocha squash works
1 whole for the pot of 2 servings, pierced

name: Beef and okra marag with chickpeas and a little brown basmati
inspiredBy: Kuwaiti and Emirati marag bamia, the tomato and okra stew eaten over rice
about: Beef and okra simmered in a bright, garlicky tomato broth with crushed coriander, a good squeeze of lemon and chickpeas, ladled over a small portion of brown basmati. Homely and tangy, and not slimy when the okra is cooked whole and gently. The okra and chickpeas bring **folate, fibre and vitamin K**, and it makes tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Warm the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches, about 5 minutes. Lift it out, then soften the onion in the same pot for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, coriander and tomato paste, then the tomato. Cook for 6 minutes, until the tomato starts to break down.
Return the beef with the salt and 2 cups of water. Cover and simmer for about 1 hour and 15 minutes, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the chickpeas and the whole okra. Simmer gently, without stirring too much, for 15 minutes, until the okra is soft but holds its shape. Stir in the lemon juice.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in plenty of boiling salted water for about 35 to 40 minutes until tender, then drain.
Serve the marag over the rice with the cilantro scattered on top. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Frozen whole okra works well and is easy to find. Trimming the cap without cutting into the pod, and adding lemon or tomato, keeps it from turning slimy.

name: Roasted sardines with cumin sweet potatoes and a cucumber and radish salata
inspiredBy: Omani and Gulf grilled sardines with garlic and coriander, with a crisp salata in the style of salata Arabiya
about: Fresh sardines marinated in garlic, lemon, cumin and cilantro, then roasted until the skin crackles, with cumin-roasted sweet potato wedges and a crisp salata of cucumber, radish, onion, parsley and lemon. Quick and bright. Sardines give you **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**, and the sweet potato gives you vitamin A.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the sweet potato wedges with half the vegetable oil, half the cumin and a pinch of salt on a baking tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Mash the garlic with a pinch of salt and mix it with the cilantro, the rest of the cumin, half the lemon juice and the rest of the vegetable oil. Rub it over the sardines inside and out.
Turn the wedges and push them to one side. Lay the sardines on the tray and roast for 8 to 10 minutes, until the skin is blistered and the flesh flakes easily.
Toss the cucumber, radish, onion and parsley with the rest of the lemon juice, the olive oil, the sumac and a pinch of salt.
Serve the sardines and sweet potatoes with the salata on the side and a lemon wedge if you like.
tip: Frozen sardines work well once thawed. Open the window or use the exhaust fan, since sardines are fragrant. Mackerel can stand in for the sardines.

name: Lamb harees with ghee and cinnamon, laban and cucumber
inspiredBy: Emirati, Qatari and Saudi harees, the slow wheat and meat porridge of Ramadan and celebrations
about: Cracked wheat and tender lamb cooked slowly with onion and cardamom until they melt into a thick, silky porridge, finished with a spoon of melted ghee and a dusting of cinnamon. Cold laban and a cucumber, mint and parsley salad cut the richness. The cracked wheat brings **fibre, magnesium and B vitamins**, and the laban adds calcium. It makes two portions, so Sunday's lunch is done.
steps: Rinse the cracked wheat and cover it with plenty of cold water. Leave it to soak while the lamb cooks, at least an hour.

Put the lamb, the onion, the cardamom and the salt in a heavy pot with about 5 cups of water. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then cover and simmer for 1 and a half hours, until the lamb is very tender.

Lift out the onion and discard it. Drain the wheat and add it to the pot with the black pepper. Simmer, covered, over the lowest heat for 1 hour, stirring from time to time and adding hot water whenever it looks dry, until the wheat is very soft and has broken down.

Take the pot off the heat and beat the porridge hard with a wooden spoon or a masher for 5 to 10 minutes, until the lamb shreds into the wheat and it turns smooth and stretchy. Add a little hot water if it is too stiff; it should fall from a spoon in a thick ribbon.
Melt the ghee in a small pan until it just starts to smell nutty.
Spoon the harees into shallow bowls and make a small well in the middle. Pour the hot ghee into the well and dust with the cinnamon.

Toss the cucumber with the mint, parsley and lemon juice and serve it alongside with a glass of cold laban. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch; loosen it with a splash of water when you reheat it.
tip: A drizzle of date syrup (dibs) is a real Saudi finish. Whole wheat berries soaked overnight make a more traditional, silkier harees, but they need about 2 more hours. A pressure cooker does the wheat and lamb together in about 50 minutes. Chicken works well in place of the lamb, and some families add a pinch of sugar with the ghee.

name: Shrimp with tamarind and tomato over brown basmati, with carrot salad
inspiredBy: Kuwaiti and Bahraini robyan, the shrimp cooked in a tangy tamarind and chili sauce and served over rice
about: Plump shrimp cooked in a sour-spicy sauce of tamarind, tomato, chili and coriander, spooned over fragrant brown basmati with a crunchy carrot salad. Quick, bright and very Gulf. The shrimp give you lean **protein, selenium and iodine**, the carrot brings vitamin A and the tomato vitamin C.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of boiling salted water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain and keep covered.
Whisk the tamarind into 3 tablespoons of warm water until smooth.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, coriander and dried chili for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato and the salt and cook until it has broken down into a sauce, about 7 minutes. Stir in the tamarind.
Add the shrimp and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until they are pink and curled. Take off the heat and fold in most of the cilantro.
Toss the carrot with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Spoon the shrimp over the rice and serve with the carrot salad and the rest of the cilantro.
tip: Start the rice first and the rest comes together while it cooks. Fresh lime is an easy swap for the lemon.
ingredients: peeled and deveined, no added salt or phosphate on the label

name: Dates with cold laban and cardamom
inspiredBy: Tamr w laban, dates with laban, a classic Gulf pairing
about: A couple of soft dates with a large glass of cold, lightly salted laban and a pinch of cardamom, the way many Gulf families break a fast or end an afternoon. Dates give quick energy and the laban brings **calcium and protein**.
steps: Stir the cardamom into the cold laban and drink it with the dates on the side.
tip: Khalas, sukkari or ajwa are the traditional dates and are worth looking for at a Middle Eastern grocer. Medjool works fine if that is what you can find.

name: Cold cucumber and mint laban
about: Cold laban with grated cucumber, mint and a pinch of salt, a thin, sippable salad that Gulf families have with hot meals and on hot afternoons. Cooling and tangy, and the laban brings **calcium and protein**.
steps: Stir the cucumber, mint and salt into the cold laban.
Chill it for 10 minutes if you have time, then drink it or eat it with a spoon.

name: Warm saffron and cardamom milk with a date and almonds
inspiredBy: the saffron and cardamom milk of Gulf evenings, with the sugar swapped for a date
about: Milk warmed with cardamom and a thread of saffron, with a date and a few almonds on the side instead of sugar. Soothing and fragrant. The milk adds **calcium** and the almonds add vitamin E.
steps: Warm the milk with the cardamom and saffron until steaming, about 3 minutes, and let it sit for a minute so the saffron blooms.
Pour into a glass and sip it with the date and almonds.

name: Orange and pistachios
about: Juicy orange segments with a small handful of pistachios, a fresh and crunchy pairing. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the pistachios add vitamin E and B6.
steps: Peel the orange and eat it with the pistachios.
ingredients: unsalted, in the shell or shelled

name: Pomegranate seeds with pistachios and mint
about: Ruby pomegranate seeds with chopped pistachios and torn mint, a juicy and crunchy bowl. Sweet, tart and refreshing. Pomegranate brings **vitamin C and potassium** and the pistachios add vitamin E.
steps: Scatter the pomegranate seeds in a bowl with the pistachios and mint and eat.

name: Roasted chickpeas with lemon and cumin
about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with cumin, paprika and a squeeze of lemon, a crunchy snack to nibble on. They are crunchy, tangy and lightly salted. Chickpeas bring **protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Toss the dry chickpeas with the oil, cumin and paprika and spread on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp. Toss them straight away with the salt and the lemon, so the salt clings, and eat them warm.
ingredients: no salt added, drained and patted very dry

name: Dates stuffed with almonds
about: A date split open and tucked with an almond and a pinch of cardamom, with a few more almonds on the side, chewy and crunchy together. A small, sweet snack for the afternoon. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Split the dates and remove the pits.
Tuck one or two almonds into each date, dust with the cardamom and press closed. Eat the rest of the almonds alongside.
tip: Khalas, sukkari or ajwa dates are traditional. Medjool works fine too.

name: Dates with pistachios and cardamom
about: Chopped dates pressed with crushed pistachios and a pinch of cardamom, rolled into small bites. They are sweet and a little green. The pistachios bring **vitamin B6 and vitamin E**.
steps: Mash the dates with the cardamom and half the pistachios until sticky.
Roll into two small balls, then roll them in the remaining pistachios.

name: Almonds, pistachios and raisins
about: A small bowl of toasted almonds, pistachios and sweet raisins, the kind of mix that sits out for guests all over the Gulf. Salty-sweet and crunchy. The nuts bring **vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then toss with the pistachios and raisins in a bowl.

name: Khubz with tahini and date
about: A warm piece of whole-wheat khubz spread with tahini and topped with chopped date, the same sweet-and-nutty pairing as tahini with date syrup. Chewy and gently sweet. The tahini adds **calcium and copper**.
steps: Warm the khubz in a dry pan for a minute.
Spread with the tahini, scatter over the chopped date and fold in half.

name: Kefir bircher muesli with apple, raspberries and toasted nuts
inspiredBy: Swiss birchermuesli, made the way many German households do it with kefir
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in tangy kefir and a little thick yogurt with grated apple, cinnamon and a spoonful of ground flax, then topped with raspberries and toasted walnuts and hazelnuts. It is cold, creamy and ready the moment you wake up. The oats, fruit, flax and walnuts bring **plenty of fibre**, and kefir and yogurt are fermented dairy foods.
steps: The night before, wash the apple and grate it, skin and all, into a jar or bowl.
Stir in the oats, kefir, yogurt, ground flax, lemon juice and cinnamon, cover and refrigerate overnight, at least 6 hours. It keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days.
In the morning, toast the walnuts and hazelnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes, then roughly chop them.
Give the muesli a good stir and loosen it with a splash of water if it has gone stiff. Top with the raspberries and the warm nuts.
tip: Make a jar the night before: Sunday for Monday, Tuesday for Wednesday and Friday for Saturday. A jar keeps in the fridge up to 2 days. Kefir that has been open a few days gets tangier, which many people like.
ingredients: fresh and rinsed just before eating, or frozen and thawed in the fridge

name: Savoury oat upma with carrot, spinach and yogurt
inspiredBy: south Indian rava upma, made with oats
about: A south Indian upma made with toasted rolled oats instead of semolina: mustard seeds, ginger, onion, carrot and tomato in a golden, spoonable porridge with spinach folded through. A bowl of cool yogurt on the side and some toasted pumpkin seeds finish it. The **oats and vegetables bring fibre** and the yogurt brings a fermented food to the morning.
steps: Wash the carrot, tomato and spinach, then dice the carrot and tomato and chop the spinach. Toast the oats in a wide dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 4 minutes. Tip them out and wipe the pan.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in the same pan for 2 minutes until they pop, then set them aside.
Warm the oil over medium heat, add the mustard seeds and cover until they stop popping, about 30 seconds. Stir in the ginger and onion and cook until the onion is soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the carrot, tomato and turmeric and cook until the tomato has collapsed, about 3 minutes. Pour in about 150 ml (⅔ cup) of hot water and the salt and bring to a boil.
Stir in the oats and cook, stirring, until thick and fluffy, about 2 minutes. Fold in the spinach until wilted, then add the lemon juice.
Serve warm with the pumpkin seeds on top and the yogurt alongside.
tip: No time on a weekday? Chop the onion, carrot and tomato the night before and keep them in one container.

name: Miso soup bowl with barley, tofu, kale and a boiled egg
inspiredBy: a Japanese morning miso soup set, made as one bowl with barley
about: A savoury Japanese-style breakfast soup: shiitake and ginger simmered into a quick broth, barley and tofu to make it hearty, kale, a boiled egg, toasted walnuts for crunch and miso stirred in at the end. It is warm, salty-sweet and filling. The **barley and kale bring fibre**, and miso is a fermented food.
steps: Wash the shiitake and kale. Put the egg in a small pot of boiling water and cook for 9 minutes so the yolk is set. Cool it under cold running water, then peel and halve it.
Meanwhile, simmer the shiitake and ginger in about 300 ml (1¼ cups) of water for 5 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the broth tastes savoury.
Add the barley from your batch and the tofu and heat until steaming hot, about 3 minutes. Stir in the kale and simmer until tender, about 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat. Whisk the miso with a ladle of the hot broth in a small bowl until smooth, then stir it back into the pot. Do not boil the soup after the miso goes in.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes. Ladle the soup into a bowl and top with the egg, scallion, walnuts for crunch and a few drops of sesame oil.
tip: Barley from your Sunday batch is a minute of reheating. See the batch note on the jjigae.

name: German-style lentil salad with egg, sauerkraut and rye bread
inspiredBy: Linsensalat, the lentil salad served across southern Germany
about: A Linsensalat of tender whole lentils in a lemony vinaigrette with carrot, cucumber, onion and a lot of parsley and dill, served with a halved egg, a spoonful of sauerkraut and a slice of dark rye. It is sharp, fresh and filling. **Lentils and rye bring fibre**, and the refrigerated, unpasteurised sauerkraut adds a live fermented food.
steps: Rinse the lentils and simmer them in plenty of unsalted water until tender but still holding their shape, 20 to 25 minutes. Drain well.
While they cook, boil the egg for 9 minutes, then cool it under cold water and peel it. Wash the carrot, cucumber, parsley and dill, then dice the vegetables and chop the herbs.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, ground mustard, salt and a grind of pepper in a bowl. Toss the warm lentils and the onion in the dressing so the onion softens a little.
Fold in the carrot, cucumber, parsley and dill.
Serve with the halved egg, the sauerkraut and the rye bread alongside.
tip: Cook the lentils on Sunday and keep them in a shallow container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Then this lunch takes 10 minutes.

name: Seared tofu rice bowl with miso-ginger glaze, shiitake and spinach
inspiredBy: Japanese tofu donburi, with a miso-ginger glaze
about: Golden pan-seared tofu over brown rice with shiitake, carrot, spinach and a fried egg, brushed with a glossy miso, ginger and rice vinegar glaze and finished with sesame seeds. It is quick, savoury and tangy. Tofu and the egg bring **plant and egg protein**, and the miso is a fermented food.
steps: Wash the shiitake, spinach and carrot. Press the tofu between paper towels for 5 minutes, then cut it into slabs about 1.5 cm (½ inch) thick. Reheat the rice from your batch until steaming hot.
Whisk the miso, soy sauce, ginger, rice vinegar and 2 tablespoons of water into a glaze.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the tofu until golden, about 4 minutes a side. Lift it out.
Add the shiitake and carrot to the same pan and cook until the mushrooms are browned, about 4 minutes. Add the spinach and cook 1 minute until wilted.

Return the tofu to the pan, pour in the glaze and turn everything for 1 minute so it glazes. Do not boil it hard. Push everything to one side, crack the eggs into the empty space and fry until the whites are set and the yolks are no longer runny, about 3 minutes.
Spoon over the rice and finish with the scallion, sesame seeds and a few drops of sesame oil.
tip: Press the tofu and slice the vegetables the night before and the bowl is 10 minutes.

name: Chickpea chaat bowl with potato, tomato and yogurt
inspiredBy: Indian chana chaat, with yogurt dressing and no tamarind chutney
about: A tangy Indian-style chaat of chickpeas, warm potato, tomato, cucumber and onion, tossed with a lemony yogurt and chaat masala and scattered with toasted pumpkin seeds and parsley. It is cool, crunchy and sharp. The **chickpeas and potato bring fibre and potassium**, and the yogurt is a fermented food.
steps: Wash the potato, cut it into 2 cm (¾ inch) cubes and boil in water until just tender, about 10 minutes. Drain and let the steam go.
Toast the cumin seeds and pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant, then crush the cumin lightly.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, chaat masala and olive oil together.
Wash the tomato, cucumber and parsley before cutting. Toss the chickpeas, warm potato, onion, tomato and cucumber with the yogurt dressing.
Top with the parsley, the crushed cumin and the pumpkin seeds.
tip: Boil the potatoes the night before and the bowl takes 5 minutes. Cold potatoes work too.

name: Kimchi, chicken and tofu jjigae with brown rice and barley
inspiredBy: Korean kimchi jjigae, made with chicken and tofu
about: A fiery-tangy Korean kimchi stew with tender chicken thigh, tofu, shiitake, a handful of spinach and an egg poached in the pot, spooned over brown rice and barley. It is one pot, takes about 30 minutes and tastes even better the next day. **Kimchi is a fermented food**, bought refrigerated and live, and the tofu and egg add protein. Kimchi often contains fish sauce or shrimp, so check the label.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Cut the raw chicken, then wash your hands and the board. Warm the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the chicken with the garlic and ginger until the outside turns white, about 4 minutes.
Add the kimchi and onion and cook, stirring, until the kimchi softens and smells sweetly sour, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the gochugaru and soy sauce, then pour in about 600 ml (2½ cups) of water for the two portions. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes.
Add the shiitake and tofu and simmer 8 minutes more. Check that the chicken has reached 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece.
Stir in the spinach and the scallion. Crack an egg into tonight's portion only, cover and simmer until the whites and yolk are set, about 3 minutes.

Reheat tonight's rice and barley from your batch until steaming and spoon the stew over them. Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Tomorrow, reheat the stew to 74 °C (165 °F) and crack in a fresh egg until set.
tip: Older, sourer kimchi makes the best jjigae. Sunday grain batch, Standard: rinse 270 g (about 1½ cups) dry brown rice and simmer about 40 minutes, and simmer 90 g (a scant ½ cup) dry pearl barley about 30 minutes. Light needs about 200 g and 60 g, Big about 420 g and 135 g. Spread both on trays and refrigerate within 1 hour. Keep Monday to Wednesday's portions in the fridge (up to 3 days) and freeze the rest in single portions the same day. Thaw them in the fridge overnight, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F) until steaming.
ingredients: refrigerated, live; check the label for fish sauce or shrimp; with some of its juice

name: Roasted trout with caraway potatoes, kale and warm sauerkraut with apple
inspiredBy: German Forelle with roast potatoes, with kale and sauerkraut as sides
about: A German-inspired plate: trout roasted with dill and lemon, crisp caraway potatoes, kale braised with onion, and sauerkraut warmed gently with apple. It is rustic, tangy and satisfying. Trout is an **oily fish with omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the sauerkraut is a refrigerated, live fermented food. Warming it briefly keeps it mostly raw.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the potatoes, kale and apple. Cut the potatoes into 3 cm (1 inch) cubes and toss with half the olive oil, the caraway and the salt. Roast on a tray for 25 minutes, turning once.
Warm the remaining oil in a wide pan and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the kale with a splash of water, cover, and cook until tender, about 8 minutes.
Stir the apple and sauerkraut into the kale and warm them for 2 minutes. Keep it brief so the sauerkraut stays bright.

Pat the trout dry, lay it skin-side down on the tray for the last 10 to 12 minutes, pushing the potatoes to one side so the fish is not steamed, until it flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Drizzle the lemon juice over the trout, scatter the dill and serve with the potatoes, kale and sauerkraut.

name: Whole masoor dal with spinach and tomato, cucumber raita and brown rice
inspiredBy: north Indian sabut masoor dal, with spinach and a quick raita
about: A comforting Indian dal of whole brown lentils simmered soft, then finished with a spiced tadka of cumin, mustard seed, onion, garlic, ginger and tomato, with spinach folded in. A cooling cucumber raita and brown rice complete it. **Lentils bring fibre, iron and folate**, and the raita is a fermented food.
steps: Rinse the lentils, then simmer them in about 600 ml (2½ cups) of water with the turmeric for the two portions until soft, 25 to 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the cumin and mustard seeds and cover until the popping slows, about 30 seconds.
Stir in the onion, garlic and ginger and cook until soft and golden, about 7 minutes. Add the washed, chopped tomato and the garam masala and cook until it breaks down, 4 minutes.
Add the washed spinach and a splash of water, cover and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Tip the tomato and spinach mixture into the lentils, add the salt and simmer together for 5 minutes. Finish with the lemon juice.

Stir the yogurt with the grated cucumber and a pinch of salt for the raita. Reheat the rice from your batch until steaming and serve all together. Cool the second portion of dal in a shallow container within 2 hours; tomorrow reheat it to 74 °C (165 °F).
