tip: Make a batch and keep the balls in a container in the fridge for the week.

name: Orange and toasted almonds
about: A juicy orange with a handful of warm toasted almonds. The **vitamin C and the crunch of the nuts** make a snack that keeps you going, and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden, about 3 minutes. Peel the orange and eat it with the warm almonds.

name: Quick lemony hummus with fennel and cucumber sticks
about: Creamy lemon and garlic hummus with crunchy fennel and cucumber sticks for dipping. The chickpeas and tahini add **iron and fibre**, and tahini adds calcium.
steps: Use a portion of Sunday night's hummus (the batch is a whole can of no-salt-added chickpeas with 1 tbsp of tahini, garlic, lemon and salt). The ingredient list shows this snack's portion. If you are starting fresh, blitz that amount with a few spoonfuls of ice-cold water until pale and silky.
Cut the fennel and cucumber into sticks and dip away.
tip: Thursday is the last day the Sunday batch is at its best.

name: Dried figs and almonds
about: A few soft dried figs with a handful of warm toasted almonds. It is a sweet, chewy and crunchy snack, with **fibre, calcium and vitamin E**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden, about 3 minutes, and eat them with the figs.

name: Garlic mushrooms with lemon and parsley
inspiredBy: Spanish champiñones al ajillo
about: Mushrooms sizzled in a hot pan with garlic until golden, then finished with lemon and a handful of parsley. They work as a **small savoury snack or a starter**, they are meaty and savoury, and they are a good source of niacin and B vitamins.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms until golden and their water has cooked off, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, then finish with the lemon juice, salt and parsley.

name: Garlic mushrooms with hard-boiled eggs and parsley
inspiredBy: Spanish champiñones al ajillo, with eggs on top
about: Mushrooms sizzled with garlic, lemon and parsley, with two hard-boiled eggs to slice over the top. It works as a **small savoury snack or a starter**, and it gives you protein, choline and niacin.
steps: Lower the eggs gently into boiling water for 10 minutes, until the white and yolk are firm, then cool and peel them.
Warm the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms until golden and their water has cooked off, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Finish with the lemon juice, salt and parsley and serve with the halved eggs on top.

name: Orange and toasted walnuts
about: A juicy orange with a handful of warm toasted walnuts. The vitamin C and the crunch of the nuts make a snack that keeps you going, and the walnuts bring **plant omega-3**.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes, and eat them with the peeled orange.

name: Greek yogurt with orange and honey
about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy orange pieces and a drizzle of honey. It is a bright, simple snack with protein, calcium and **plenty of vitamin C**.
steps: Peel the orange, cut it into pieces over the bowl so the juice falls in, spoon over the yogurt and drizzle with the honey.

name: Sardine tapa with lemon, cucumber and olives
inspiredBy: Spanish and Portuguese tinned fish tapas
about:
A few canned sardines on cool cucumber rounds with a squeeze of lemon, a few olives and a pinch of smoked paprika. It is the kind of thing you would be served with a drink in a Spanish bar, and a hungry-day extra on the larger plans.

Sardines bring omega-3, vitamin D and **calcium from their soft bones**.
steps: Slice the cucumber into thick rounds, top each with a piece of sardine, and finish with the lemon juice, olives, a dusting of smoked paprika and chopped parsley.
ingredients: canned in olive oil, with bones

name: Tzatziki with cucumber and fennel dippers
about: A quick garlicky yogurt and cucumber dip with a drizzle of olive oil, with cucumber rounds and fennel strips for scooping. It is **cool and fresh**, with plenty of protein.
steps: Grate a third of the cucumber, squeeze out the water, and stir it into the yogurt with the finely grated garlic, lemon juice, chopped parsley, salt and the olive oil.
Slice the rest of the cucumber into rounds, cut the fennel into strips and dip away.
tip: Chopped mint or dill is lovely in the dip if you have some.

name: Natto and tamagoyaki rice bowl with tofu miso soup
inspiredBy: Japanese asa-gohan, the classic breakfast tray
about: Warm rice topped with sticky natto, a soft rolled omelette and a small bowl of tofu miso soup. It is a proper Japanese breakfast that takes under 20 minutes. The **natto, egg and tofu** give you a solid hit of protein before you leave the house.
steps: Cook the rice and barley ahead (see the tip) and reheat a portion until steaming hot, 74 °C.
Put the bonito flakes in a small pot with a cup of water. Bring to a simmer for 2 minutes, strain, and return the broth to the pot.
Add the tofu to the broth and warm for 2 minutes. Take the pot off the heat, stir the miso in through a small sieve, and add half the scallion. Do not boil the soup once the miso is in.

Beat the egg with a few drops of the soy sauce and the iodized salt. Pour a thin layer into an oiled small pan over medium-low heat, roll it up as it sets, then pour in the rest and roll again until the omelette is firm all the way through. Slice it.

Spoon the rice into a bowl. Stir the natto briskly with the rest of the soy sauce and a few drops of egoma oil until it is sticky and spoon it on top with the omelette and the remaining scallion. Serve with the soup.
tip: On Sunday, cook about 2 cups (370 g) of brown rice and 1⅓ cups (280 g) of pearled barley together, a little less at Light. That is every rice bowl of the week except the okayu. Simmer them in a big pot of water, like pasta, for 35 to 40 minutes until tender, then drain. Cool within 1 hour in shallow containers, keep 3 days' worth in the fridge and freeze the rest in portions. Reheat from frozen, or thaw in the fridge overnight, until steaming hot, 74 °C, and only once. On warfarin? Skip the natto and add a second egg to the omelette.
ingredients: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

name: Egg, tofu and shirasu okayu with komatsuna
inspiredBy: Japanese okayu, the gentle rice porridge
about: A soft, savoury rice porridge with silky tofu, a set egg, tiny shirasu fish and bright greens. It is comforting, and quick if you start from cooked rice (see the tip). **Shirasu are eaten whole, bones and all**, and the tofu is calcium-set, so it starts the day with calcium.
steps: Rinse the rice and put it in a pot with about six times its volume of water and the ginger. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for about 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the grains are very soft and the porridge is thick. Rinse and chop the komatsuna while it cooks.
Add the shirasu and the tofu and simmer for 3 minutes so the fish are cooked through and hot.
Stir in the komatsuna, then pour in the beaten egg in a thin stream and stir gently. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the egg is completely set.
Ladle into a bowl, season with the salt, drizzle with the soy sauce and top with the scallion and sesame.
tip: Use 120 g of cooked rice with 300 ml of water and it is ready in 15 minutes. If you use dried chirimen jako instead of shirasu, pour boiling water over it and drain first: it is salty. Opened tofu keeps in fresh water in the fridge for up to 2 days.
ingredients: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

name: Kinako soy milk oatmeal with mikan
inspiredBy: Japanese kinako (roasted soybean flour) sweets
about: Creamy oats cooked in soy milk with nutty kinako, walnuts and juicy mikan. It tastes a little like a Japanese sweet. The **soy milk and kinako** carry the protein, and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Put the oats and soy milk in a pot over medium heat. Stir often for about 5 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Whisk the kinako into the porridge off the heat so it does not clump.
Spoon into a bowl, top with the mikan segments and walnuts and drizzle with the honey.

name: Canned salmon, edamame and sesame rice bowl
inspiredBy: Japanese salmon-flake rice bowls
about: Flaked canned salmon with its soft bones, sweet edamame and crisp cucumber over barley rice, dressed with ginger, rice vinegar and sesame. It is cold-friendly and comes together in 15 minutes if the rice is ready. The **soft salmon bones add calcium**, and the salmon brings vitamin D.
steps: Boil the frozen edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain, cool and shell them. Warm the cooked rice and barley until steaming hot, 74 °C, then let it cool a little.
Rinse the cucumber and scrub the carrot. Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce and ginger together in a small bowl. Toss the cucumber and carrot with half of it and leave for 5 minutes.
Mash the salmon with a fork, bones included, and stir in the rest of the dressing.
Pile the rice into a bowl. Top with the salmon, edamame, cucumber and carrot, and scatter over the scallion and sesame.
tip: Taking it to work? Skip the reheating, use rice straight from the fridge, and pack it with an ice pack until lunch.

name: Hiyashi soba with chilled tofu and edamame
inspiredBy: Japanese hiyashi soba and zaru soba
about: Cold buckwheat noodles with creamy tofu, edamame and cucumber with a light bonito sauce poured over. It is refreshing and filling. The **tofu, egg and edamame give the protein**, and the noodles are boiled in unsalted water to keep the sodium down.
steps: Simmer the bonito flakes in half a cup of water for 2 minutes, strain, and stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar and honey. Set the pan in a bowl of cold water to cool the sauce while you do the rest.

Boil the frozen edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain, cool and shell. Boil the soba in plenty of unsalted water as the packet says, then rinse well under cold water, rubbing gently, and drain. Choose a soba with little or no added salt.
Rinse the spinach and cucumber. Plunge the spinach into boiling unsalted water for 1 minute, cool in cold water, squeeze dry and cut into short lengths.
Beat the egg and cook it in a thin layer in a lightly oiled non-stick pan until completely set, then slice into ribbons.
Put the noodles in a bowl and arrange the tofu, edamame, spinach, egg ribbons and cucumber on top.
Pour over the cold sauce, drizzle with the egoma oil and finish with the ginger, scallion and sesame.
tip: Egoma (perilla) oil is sold at Korean grocers as deulgireum; flaxseed oil is used the same way. Keep either in the fridge and never heat it. At smaller sizes the noodles shrink to a small nest, and the tofu and edamame carry the bowl.
ingredients: dried, check the label for salt
calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

name: Shrimp and egg donburi with komatsuna
inspiredBy: Japanese tamago-toji donburi (the oyakodon style)
about: Plump shrimp and set egg simmered in a light bonito and soy broth over barley rice, with a handful of greens. It is quick and warming. The **shrimp and egg** carry the protein.
steps: Rinse the komatsuna before cutting it. Reheat the cooked rice and barley until steaming hot, 74 °C, and spoon into a bowl.
Simmer the bonito in half a cup of water for 2 minutes, strain, and return it to the pan with the soy sauce, honey and onion. Cook for 3 minutes until the onion is soft.
Add the shrimp and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until they are pink and opaque all the way through. Add the komatsuna for the last minute.
Pour the egg over in a thin stream. Cover and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the egg is completely set.
Slide everything over the rice with the broth.
ingredients: peeled and deveined; if frozen, thaw in the fridge overnight and cook within 2 days

name: Tofu and chicken hambagu with grated daikon and komatsuna
inspiredBy: Japanese tofu hambagu (washoku-style hamburg steak)
about: Tender patties of minced chicken thigh and calcium-set tofu, served with refreshing grated daikon, a vinegar-soy sauce and sesame komatsuna. The tofu keeps them light and moist. The **tofu and komatsuna bring calcium** and the patties carry plenty of protein.
steps: Cook the rice and barley (see the breakfast tip) and keep warm. This recipe makes two portions. Scrub and rinse the daikon and komatsuna, then grate the daikon.

Squeeze the tofu in a clean cloth until it is firm and crumbly, then mash it in a bowl. Add the chicken, onion, egg, ginger, the iodized salt and a third of the soy sauce and mix with your hand until sticky. Shape into two oval patties, pressing the centre thin. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the patties for 4 minutes on each side, then cover and cook for another 5 minutes, until a thermometer in the centre reads 74 °C, with no pink and clear juices.
Boil the komatsuna in unsalted water for 1 minute, cool in cold water, squeeze dry and toss with half the sesame and a little soy sauce.

Squeeze the grated daikon lightly. Mix the rice vinegar with the remaining soy sauce. Serve the patties with daikon on top, the sauce spooned over, the greens and the rice. Cool the second portion and refrigerate within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch, then reheat until steaming hot throughout, 74 °C.
tip: No komatsuna? Baby bok choy works the same way.
ingredients: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), squeezed in a cloth

name: Grilled salmon with spinach goma-ae and daikon miso soup
inspiredBy: Japanese shioyaki salmon teishoku
about: A simple grilled salmon fillet with sesame-dressed spinach, a small bowl of daikon miso soup and mugi-gohan. It is the classic Japanese dinner in one tray. The **salmon brings omega-3 and vitamin D**.
steps: Cook the rice and barley ahead if you have not (see the breakfast tip) and reheat a portion until steaming hot, 74 °C.

Pat the salmon dry and rub it with the salt, then wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish. Grill or broil it, skin side up, for about 5 minutes, turn and cook for another 4 to 5 minutes, until the fish reaches 70 °C and flakes easily.
Rinse the spinach well. Plunge the spinach into boiling unsalted water for 1 minute, cool in cold water and squeeze dry. Toss with the ground sesame, soy sauce, rice vinegar and honey.

Simmer the bonito in a cup of water for 2 minutes and strain. Add the daikon and simmer for 5 minutes, until it turns translucent. Off the heat, stir the miso in through a small sieve and add the scallion.
Serve the salmon with the spinach, the soup and the rice.
ingredients: scrubbed and cut into thin matchsticks

name: Chikuzen-ni, simmered chicken with root vegetables
inspiredBy: Kyushu chikuzen-ni (iridori)
about: Chicken thigh simmered with lotus root, kabocha, carrot, shiitake and edamame in a light soy and ginger broth, glossy and not too sweet. It is even better the next day. It is a **fibre-rich simmered dish** with plenty of protein.
steps: Cook the rice and barley (see the breakfast tip) and keep warm. This recipe makes two portions.

Soak the dried shiitake in 250 ml of warm water for 30 minutes and keep the soaking water. Scrub and rinse the lotus root, kabocha and carrot. Soak the lotus root slices in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.

Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat and brown the chicken for 4 minutes. Wash your hands and board after cutting the raw chicken. Add the lotus root, carrot, shiitake and ginger and stir for 2 minutes.

Add about 200 ml of the shiitake soaking water, the soy sauce, the salt and the honey. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 10 minutes, then lay the kabocha on top, cover again and cook for another 10 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C with no pink.
Add the edamame, then uncover and simmer for 5 minutes, spooning the broth over, until it has reduced to a glaze.
Serve over the rice. Cool the second portion and refrigerate within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat until steaming hot throughout, 74 °C.
ingredients: kabocha or buttercup squash, seeded, cut into chunks
soaked until soft, stems removed, quartered

name: Mackerel simmered in miso and ginger with spinach
inspiredBy: Japanese saba no miso-ni
about: Mackerel fillets simmered gently with ginger and a spoonful of miso, with cubes of tofu in the same pot and a bright spinach ohitashi. The miso sauce is thin and savoury, not heavy. The **mackerel is rich in omega-3**, and the tofu adds calcium.
steps: Cook the rice and barley ahead if you have not (see the breakfast tip) and reheat a portion until steaming hot, 74 °C.
Pour boiling water over the mackerel in a sieve for a few seconds to rinse away any fishy smell, and pat dry. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish.

In a small wide pan, bring 100 ml of water, the ginger, honey and half the miso to a simmer. Lay in the mackerel, skin side up, and the tofu. Cover loosely and simmer for 8 minutes, spooning the liquid over.

Stir the remaining miso with a ladle of the hot liquid and stir it back into the pan with the soy sauce. Simmer for 2 more minutes, until the fish reaches 70 °C and flakes easily and the sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile rinse the spinach well and boil it in unsalted water for 1 minute, cool in cold water, squeeze dry, cut into short lengths and top with the bonito flakes and sesame.
Serve the mackerel and tofu with the sauce, the spinach, scallion and rice.
ingredients: fillet, cut in two; Atlantic or Pacific, never king mackerel
calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

name: Beef and tofu sukiyaki-style nabe
inspiredBy: Japanese sukiyaki
about: A shallow pot of lean beef, tofu, cabbage, carrot, shiitake and komatsuna in a gently sweet soy and bonito broth. Everything cooks in one pan and the broth soaks into the rice. It is a **calcium-rich, one-pot dinner**, with the tofu and greens doing most of the work.
steps: Cook the rice and barley (see the breakfast tip) and keep warm. This recipe makes two portions.

Soak the dried shiitake in 150 ml of warm water for 30 minutes. Simmer the bonito in 200 ml of water for 2 minutes and strain. Add the shiitake and its soaking water, the soy sauce, honey and salt to make the broth.
Rinse the cabbage, carrot and komatsuna. Put the tofu, cabbage, carrot and scallion in a wide shallow pan with the broth. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the soaked shiitake and cook for 3 minutes. Lay the beef slices on top and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until no pink remains and the beef is cooked through. Add the komatsuna in the last minute.
Serve over or beside the rice with some of the broth. Cool the second portion and refrigerate within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat until steaming hot throughout, 74 °C.
ingredients: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cut into slabs

name: Turkey and tofu gyoza with simmered kabocha
inspiredBy: Japanese pan-fried gyoza
about: Juicy gyoza filled with lean turkey, tofu and cabbage, pan-fried until crisp underneath and steamed until tender, with a vinegar-soy dip and soft simmered kabocha (or buttercup squash). It is a fun weekend project. The **tofu keeps the filling tender** and adds a little calcium.
steps: Cook the brown rice and barley (see the breakfast tip). This recipe makes two portions.
Scrub and rinse the kabocha. Simmer the chunks in a small covered pot with 100 ml of water and a splash of the soy sauce for 12 minutes, until tender but not falling apart.

Squeeze the tofu in a clean cloth until crumbly. Mix the turkey, tofu, beaten egg, cabbage, scallion, ginger and half the soy sauce by hand until sticky. Fry a small spoonful until cooked through and taste to check the seasoning.

Put a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle of each wrapper, wet the edge, and fold and pleat to seal. If filling is left when the wrappers run out, shape it into small flat patties and fry them in the pan with the gyoza. Wash your hands and board when the gyoza are folded.

Heat the canola oil in a non-stick pan with a lid. Arrange the gyoza flat side down and fry for 2 minutes, until golden underneath. Add 80 ml of water, cover and steam over medium heat for 6 minutes, then uncover and cook until the water is gone. Cut one open, and a patty if you made them, to check: the turkey must reach 74 °C with no pink. Wash your hands and board after the raw turkey and egg.
Mix the vinegar and the rest of the soy sauce for the dip.

Serve the gyoza with the dip, the kabocha drizzled with the egoma oil, and the rice. Cool the second portion and refrigerate within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat in a covered pan with a splash of water until steaming hot throughout, 74 °C.
tip: Freeze uncooked gyoza on a tray, then bag them; cook from frozen with a little more water.
ingredients: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), squeezed in a cloth
kabocha or buttercup squash, seeded, cut into chunks

name: Salmon chanchan-yaki with cabbage and mushrooms
inspiredBy: Hokkaido chanchan-yaki
about: Salmon steamed on a bed of cabbage, carrot and shiitake with a thin miso glaze, all in one pan. It is sweet, savoury and very easy. The **salmon brings omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the vegetables add fibre.
steps: Cook the rice and barley ahead if you have not (see the breakfast tip) and reheat a portion until steaming hot, 74 °C.
Soak the dried shiitake in warm water for 30 minutes, then slice them and keep 3 tablespoons of the water. Whisk the miso, honey and the soaking water into a smooth glaze.
Rinse the cabbage and scrub the carrot. Heat the oil in a wide pan with a lid. Spread the onion, carrot, cabbage and shiitake in a layer.

Lay the salmon and the tofu on top and spoon over the glaze. Cover and steam over medium-low heat for 12 minutes, until the salmon reaches 70 °C and flakes easily and the vegetables are tender. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish.
Scatter with the sesame and serve with the rice, spooning the juices over.
ingredients: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

name: Steamed kabocha with sesame
about: Soft steamed kabocha (or buttercup squash), naturally sweet, with a sprinkle of toasted sesame and a few drops of soy sauce, a very Japanese way to eat squash. It brings **vitamin A and fibre** to the afternoon.
steps: Scrub and rinse the kabocha. Steam the chunks over simmering water for 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Toss with the sesame and soy sauce and serve warm.
ingredients: kabocha or buttercup squash, seeded, cut into chunks

name: Warm kinako soy milk
about: A warm mug of soy milk whisked with nutty kinako and a little honey. It is **calcium and soy protein** in a cup.
steps: Warm the soy milk in a small pot until steaming, not boiling.
Whisk in the kinako and honey until smooth and pour into a mug.

name: Persimmon and almonds
about: Sweet autumn persimmon with a small handful of almonds for crunch. Almonds are a modern snack here rather than a traditional one, but they are an easy way to get **vitamin E**.
steps: Slice the persimmon and serve with the almonds.

name: Mikan and almonds
about: A juicy mikan with a handful of almonds. Almonds are a modern addition, there for **vitamin E**, and the mikan brings vitamin C.
steps: Peel the mikan and serve with the almonds.

name: Plain yogurt with kinako and almonds
about: Tangy yogurt with nutty kinako, chopped almonds and a spoonful of honey. Almonds are a modern touch, there for **vitamin E**, and the yogurt adds calcium.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, dust with the kinako, scatter over the almonds and drizzle with the honey.

name: Edamame with sesame salt
about: Edamame tossed with toasted sesame and a pinch of iodized salt, like the sesame salt (goma-jio) served at home. It is a **plant protein and calcium** snack.
steps: Boil the frozen edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain and let them cool a little.
Toss with the sesame and iodized salt.

name: Warm almond kinako soy milk
about: Warm soy milk whisked with kinako and finely ground almonds, lightly sweet and nutty. Almonds are a modern touch, there for **vitamin E**, and the soy milk adds calcium.
steps: Grind the almonds finely in a clean spice grinder or with a mortar.
Warm the soy milk in a small pot until steaming, not boiling.
Whisk in the kinako, almonds and honey until smooth and pour into a mug.

name: Edamame with a pinch of salt
about: A bowl of warm edamame, a favourite Japanese snack. They are a **plant protein and fibre** snack.
steps: Boil the frozen edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain and let them cool a little.
Toss with the iodized salt.

name: Soy-marinated egg
about: A hard-boiled egg marinated in diluted soy sauce, the kind found in every bento. It is a **small bite of protein**.
steps: Boil the egg in water for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely set. Cool in cold water and peel. Boiling for Tuesday? Boil a second egg for Sunday and keep it in its shell in the fridge.
Mix the soy sauce, honey and 2 tablespoons of water in a small bowl, add the egg and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours, turning once. Eat within 2 days.

name: Greek yogurt with almonds, walnuts and figs
inspiredBy: Greek breakfast yogurt with honey and nuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt with chopped dried figs, toasted almonds, walnuts and oats, and a drizzle of honey. It is creamy with a good crunch, and the **yogurt and almonds bring calcium** and plenty of protein to start the day.
steps: Toast the oats, almonds and walnuts together in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they smell nutty and the oats turn pale gold, about 3 minutes. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and scatter the chopped figs over it.
Top with the toasted oats and nuts, drizzle with honey and dust with cinnamon.
tip: Toast a few days of oats and almonds at once and keep them in a jar.

name: Baked eggs with white beans, tomato and spinach
inspiredBy: Spanish huevos a la flamenca
about: Eggs set in a bubbling tomato, pepper and white bean sauce with a little spinach, finished with smoked paprika and parsley, with toast for the sauce. The **eggs and beans together bring plenty of protein**, and the tomato and pepper add vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water.
Warm the olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 6 minutes, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the paprika, then the tomato and the beans. Simmer until thick, about 6 minutes.
Fold in the spinach until it wilts. Make two wells and crack in the eggs. Season with a pinch of iodized salt.
Cover and cook gently for 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites and yolks are firm all the way through.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the toast.
tip: Cook the sauce the night before and just add the eggs in the morning.
ingredients: crushed by hand with its juice

name: Tomato tostada with sardines and lemon
inspiredBy: Spanish pan con tomate with sardines
about: Crisp toast rubbed with garlic and ripe tomato, piled with canned sardines, red onion, parsley and lemon. Eating the soft sardine bones gives you **calcium and vitamin D** in one quick breakfast.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water.
Toast the bread until crisp. Rub one side with the garlic clove while it is hot.
Rub the cut side of the tomato over the toast, squeezing so the pulp soaks in, and discard the skin.
Break the sardines into big pieces and lay them on the toast with the onion.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon, scatter with parsley and pepper.
tip: Rinse the onion slices under cold water for a milder bite.

name: Tuscan white beans and garlicky greens on toast
inspiredBy: Tuscan fettunta with cannellini and cavolo nero
about: Soft white beans and kale cooked in garlic and rosemary, spooned over thick toast with fried eggs, a little Parmesan and lemon. A slower Sunday breakfast where **white beans and greens carry calcium and fibre**.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water.
Warm the oil with the garlic, rosemary and chili flakes over medium heat until the garlic smells sweet, about 1 minute.
Add the kale with a splash of water and cook, covered, until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the beans and crush a few against the pan. Heat through for 3 minutes. Add a pinch of iodized salt.
Fry the eggs in a nonstick pan with a few drops of oil, covered, until the whites and yolks are set, about 3 minutes.
Pile the beans onto the toast, top with the eggs, then add the lemon and Parmesan.
tip: Swap the kale for chard or spinach.
ingredients: fried until the whites and yolks are set

name: Tuscan white bean and kale soup with Parmesan toast
inspiredBy: Tuscan ribollita
about: A thick, soft soup of white beans, kale and tomato with rosemary, ladled over a slice of toast with Parmesan. **White beans, kale and Parmesan all bring calcium**, and the beans give plenty of protein. Made for two, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water.
Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 8 minutes, adding the garlic and rosemary for the last minute.
Add the tomato, broth, beans and enough water to cover the beans by a finger. Simmer for 15 minutes. Season with iodized salt.
Stir in the kale and simmer until tender, about 8 minutes. Crush some beans against the pot to thicken the soup.
Put the toast in a bowl, ladle the soup over it and top with Parmesan.

Cool the second portion within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate it and eat it tomorrow, or freeze it (thaw it in the fridge and eat it within 2 days). Reheat until steaming hot all through, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Make it the evening before. 50 minutes is a lot at lunch. A pinch of chili and a squeeze of lemon wake it up when reheated.

name: Garlic chicken with chickpeas and kale
inspiredBy: Spanish pollo al ajillo, with lemon and broth
about: Chicken thighs browned with plenty of garlic and smoked paprika, then simmered in lemon and broth with potatoes, chickpeas and kale. It is a one-pot supper with **iron from the chickpeas and kale**, and the lemon helps you absorb it.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water. Use a separate board for the raw chicken, and wash your hands, the board and the knife in hot soapy water before moving on to the vegetables.
Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on both sides, about 6 minutes. Move it to a plate.
Lower the heat. Cook the onion and garlic until soft and just golden, about 5 minutes. Stir in the paprika. Season with iodized salt.
Add the potato, broth and a splash of water. Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and kale. Simmer until the kale is tender, about 8 minutes.
Check that the chicken is cooked through with no pink, 74 °C (165 °F). Finish with lemon and parsley.

Cool the second portion within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate it and eat it tomorrow, or freeze it (thaw it in the fridge and eat it within 2 days). Reheat until steaming hot all through, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Brown the chicken without moving it so the crust builds.
ingredients: trimmed of fat, cut into large pieces

name: Salmon keftedes with tzatziki and a lemony tomato and spinach salad
inspiredBy: Greek keftedes, made with canned salmon
about: Crisp-edged patties of canned salmon, oats, dill and lemon, with a cool tzatziki and a fresh tomato and spinach salad. Canned salmon is mashed with its soft bones, so you get **calcium and vitamin D** as well as omega-3.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water.
Mash the salmon with its bones in a bowl. Mix in the egg, oats, onion, half the dill, the lemon zest, half the lemon juice and a pinch of iodized salt. Shape into patties and rest 5 minutes.
Stir the yogurt with the cucumber, garlic, remaining dill and a little lemon juice for the tzatziki.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Fry the patties until golden and hot through to 74 °C (165 °F), because of the raw egg, about 4 minutes a side.
Toss the spinach and tomatoes with the last of the lemon juice. Serve the patties with the salad, tzatziki and warm pita.
tip: Chill the patties for 20 minutes first if you want them to hold their shape better.

name: Whole-wheat pasta with sardines, fennel and lemon
inspiredBy: Sicilian pasta con le sarde
about: Whole-wheat spaghetti with canned sardines, softened fennel, dried fig and toasted almonds, with a handful of spinach and crisp breadcrumbs. It follows the Sicilian classic, with figs in place of raisins, and the **sardine bones bring calcium and vitamin D**.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water.
Toast the breadcrumbs and almonds in a dry pan until golden, 2 to 3 minutes. Set aside.
Warm the oil and soften the fennel and onion over medium heat until sweet and golden, about 10 minutes. Add the garlic, fig and chili flakes for 1 minute.
Cook the pasta in plenty of boiling water with the pinch of iodized salt until al dente. Save a mug of cooking water and drain.
Add the sardines to the pan, breaking them up, with the pasta, spinach and a splash of cooking water. Toss until the spinach wilts and the sardines are hot.
Finish with lemon, parsley and fennel fronds, and scatter the crumbs and almonds over.
tip: Season at the table with a little black pepper rather than salt, because sardines are already savoury.

name: Spanish lentil and mackerel salad with sherry vinegar
inspiredBy: Spanish ensalada de lentejas con caballa
about: Tender lentils tossed with canned mackerel, sweet peppers, onion, tomatoes and parsley in a sherry vinegar dressing, with toast on the side. The **lentils bring iron and fibre** and the mackerel brings protein and omega-3, and the lentils taste even better after an hour in the fridge.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water.
Whisk the sherry vinegar, olive oil and pepper in a bowl. Add a pinch of iodized salt.
Add the lentils, pepper, onion and tomatoes and toss. Let it sit for 10 minutes so the onion mellows.
Fold in the mackerel and parsley gently so the pieces stay whole.
Pile onto the spinach and serve with the toast.
tip: Mix the lentil salad the night before and fold in the mackerel in the morning. Pack it with an ice pack, or keep it in a fridge at work, and don't leave it out of the cold for more than 2 hours.
ingredients: Atlantic or chub, with soft bones (not king mackerel, which is high in mercury)

name: Turkey albondigas in tomato sauce with chickpeas and spinach
inspiredBy: Spanish albondigas en salsa
about: Turkey meatballs with garlic, parsley and cumin, simmered in a smoky tomato sauce with chickpeas and wilted spinach. Very **high in protein, with iron and folate** from the chickpeas and spinach. Makes two portions.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water. Use a separate board for the raw turkey, and wash your hands, the board and the knife in hot soapy water before moving on to the vegetables.

Soak the oats in 2 tablespoons of water for 5 minutes first. Mix the turkey, soaked oats, egg, half the onion, half the garlic, the parsley, the cumin and a little iodized salt. Shape into small meatballs.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and brown the meatballs all over, about 6 minutes. Move them to a plate.
In the same pan soften the rest of the onion and garlic, then stir in the paprika and tomato. Simmer for 8 minutes.
Return the meatballs with the chickpeas and a splash of water. Cover and simmer gently, never boiling hard, for 15 minutes, until no pink remains and they reach 74 °C (165 °F) in the centre.
Stir in the spinach until wilted.

Cool the second portion within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate it and eat it tomorrow, or freeze it (thaw it in the fridge and eat it within 2 days). Reheat until steaming hot all through, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Finish with a squeeze of lemon.

name: Shrimp saganaki with tomato, feta and warm pita
inspiredBy: Greek garides saganaki, without the ouzo
about: Shrimp simmered in a rich tomato and garlic sauce with a little oregano and chili, finished with crumbled feta and lemon, with warm pita for scooping. A fast supper where the shrimp bring **lean protein and iodine**.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water. Use a separate board for the raw shrimp, and wash your hands, the board and the knife in hot soapy water before moving on to the vegetables.
Warm the oil and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, oregano and chili for 1 minute.
Add the tomato and simmer until it thickens, about 8 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink and opaque all the way through, 3 to 4 minutes. Season with a pinch of iodized salt.
Take off the heat, sprinkle with feta, parsley and lemon, and serve with the warm pita for scooping.
tip: Using frozen shrimp? Thaw them in the fridge overnight and cook them within 2 days. Heat the feta in the sauce for a minute if you like it creamy.

name: Lemon-oregano trout pita with tzatziki and tomato
inspiredBy: Greek grilled fish, souvlaki style
about: Trout fillet marinated in lemon, oregano and garlic, grilled until it flakes and tucked into a warm whole-wheat pita with tzatziki, tomato and onion. **Trout brings omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the yogurt sauce adds calcium.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water. Use a separate board for the raw trout, and wash your hands, the board and the knife in hot soapy water before moving on to the vegetables.
Toss the trout with the lemon juice, half the garlic, the oregano, the oil and a pinch of iodized salt. Marinate in the fridge for 15 minutes.
Stir the yogurt with the grated cucumber, remaining garlic and dill for the tzatziki.
Cook the trout in a hot nonstick pan or under the broiler, about 4 minutes a side, until it flakes easily and is opaque, 70 °C (158 °F).
Fill the warm pita with the trout, tomato, diced cucumber and onion, and top with tzatziki.
tip: Salmon works the same way if trout is hard to find.
ingredients: skinless fillet, cut in large pieces
half diced, half grated for the sauce

name: Crustless spinach, tofu and feta bake
inspiredBy: Greek spanakopita, with calcium-set tofu
about: A golden spinach pie in the spirit of spanakopita, with onion, dill, a little feta and crumbled tofu set with calcium, and a crunchy breadcrumb top instead of pastry. Each portion brings **plenty of calcium** with more than 25 g of protein. Cook once, eat twice.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water.
Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Oil a small baking dish.
Warm half the oil and cook the onion and mushrooms until soft, about 8 minutes. Add the spinach in handfuls until wilted, 3 minutes. Tip into a colander and press out the liquid.
Mix the spinach with the tofu, feta, egg, dill, parsley, lemon, nutmeg and a pinch of iodized salt. Spread in the dish.
Toss the crumbs with the remaining oil and scatter over the top.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until golden and set in the centre, 74 °C (165 °F).

Cool the second portion within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate it and eat it tomorrow, or freeze it (thaw it in the fridge and eat it within 2 days). Reheat until steaming hot all through, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: A salad of tomato and cucumber with lemon is all it needs.
ingredients: set with calcium sulfate (check the label), crumbled
sliced; labelled high in vitamin D (UV-exposed), ordinary mushrooms work but give less vitamin D

name: Lemon salmon with oregano potatoes and green beans
inspiredBy: Greek psari lemonato with patates lemonates
about: Salmon fillet baked on lemony oregano potatoes with tender green beans. It is a Sunday dinner with **omega-3 and vitamin D from the salmon**, and the potatoes soak up all the juices.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water. Use a separate board for the raw salmon, and wash your hands, the board and the knife in hot soapy water before moving on to the vegetables.
Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the potatoes with half the oil, half the lemon juice, the garlic, oregano, pepper and a pinch of iodized salt, and add a splash of water. Roast for 25 minutes.
Add the green beans to the tray and roast for 10 more minutes.
Rub the salmon with the remaining oil and lemon. Nestle it on the tray and bake for about 10 minutes, until it flakes easily and is opaque, 70 °C (158 °F).
Scatter with parsley and serve from the tray.
tip: A squeeze of fresh lemon at the table finishes it.

name: Soy café con leche with an orange and almonds
inspiredBy: Spanish café con leche
about: Strong coffee with warm fortified soy drink, with a juicy orange and a few almonds on the side. The **fortified soy drink brings calcium and vitamin D**. This is the day's one cup of coffee.
steps: Brew the coffee strong, and rinse the orange before peeling it.
Warm the soy drink gently in a small pot or microwave until steaming, and whisk until foamy.
Pour the coffee into a mug, add the soy drink and serve with the orange and almonds.
tip: Use decaf and the plan stays the same.

name: Hummus with pepper and cucumber sticks
inspiredBy: Greek-Levantine hummus
about: Creamy hummus blended with tahini, lemon and garlic, with crunchy vegetables for dipping. The **chickpeas and tahini bring fibre and protein**.
steps: Rinse the vegetables and herbs under running water.
Blend the chickpeas with the tahini, lemon, garlic, a spoonful of water and half the oil until smooth. Add water if it is too thick. Add a pinch of iodized salt.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with the rest of the oil and dust with paprika.
Serve with the vegetables.
tip: Make a bigger batch and keep it in the fridge up to 3 days.

name: White bean and rosemary crostini
inspiredBy: Tuscan crostini di fagioli
about: Whole-wheat toast with a smashed white bean spread scented with garlic, rosemary and lemon. **White beans bring fibre and protein**.
steps: Toast the bread until crisp.
Mash the beans with the garlic, rosemary, lemon and oil, adding water for a spreadable texture.
Spread the mash on the toast.

name: Egg, tomato and oregano plate
inspiredBy: Spanish huevo duro with tomato
about: Hard-boiled eggs with sweet tomato wedges, lemon and oregano. An easy savoury snack with **protein and choline**.
steps: Boil the eggs in the shell for 10 minutes, until the yolks are fully set. Cool in cold water and peel.
Rinse the tomato, cut it in wedges and arrange it on a plate with the eggs.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon and sprinkle with oregano.
tip: Boil several eggs at once and keep them in the fridge in the shell for up to 1 week.

name: Greek yogurt with walnuts and honey
inspiredBy: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, the classic
about: Thick yogurt with crunchy toasted walnuts, a drizzle of honey and a pinch of cinnamon. A classic Greek sweet with **yogurt calcium and walnut omega-3**.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the walnuts.
Drizzle with honey and dust with cinnamon.

name: Warm cinnamon soy drink with figs
inspiredBy: Greek warm milk with honey
about: A cosy bedtime mug in the spirit of Greek warm milk with honey: fortified soy drink with cinnamon, chopped dried figs and a few walnuts. The **soy drink brings calcium and vitamin D**.
steps: Warm the soy drink with the cinnamon until steaming; do not boil.
Whisk to a froth and pour into a mug.
Stir in the chopped figs and scatter the walnuts on top.

name: Chilaquiles verdes with fried eggs and baked tortillas
inspiredBy: Chilaquiles verdes from Mexico City and central Mexico, with the tortillas baked instead of fried and lime-thinned yogurt in place of Mexican crema
about: Crisp baked tortilla wedges tossed in a bright, tangy tomatillo and epazote salsa, then topped with fried eggs, queso fresco, a spoon of lime-thinned yogurt and ripe avocado. Baking the tortillas instead of frying them keeps the crunch and saves most of the oil. The eggs bring protein and **choline**, and the tomatillo brings vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cut the tortillas into wedges, spread them on a tray and bake until crisp and pale gold, about 12 minutes, turning them once.
While they bake, simmer the tomatillos, jalapeño and garlic in a small pot of water until the tomatillos turn olive green and soft, about 8 minutes. Drain.
Blend them with the epazote, cilantro, half the onion and the salt until smooth and bright green.

Warm half the oil in a wide pan, pour in the salsa and let it bubble for 3 minutes, until it thickens a little. Toss in the baked tortillas for less than a minute, just until they are coated, so they keep their bite.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the oil in a second pan, covering the pan and flipping them for the last minute, until the whites and yolks are firm, about 4 minutes.

Stir the yogurt with the lime juice to make a quick crema. Pile the chilaquiles on a plate and top with the eggs, the sliced raw onion, queso fresco, crema and avocado. Eat right away, before they go soft.
tip: On Sunday, bake a double tray of tortilla wedges and blend a double batch of salsa; they keep 4 days, so Monday and Thursday take 10 minutes. Shredded chicken from the tinga is the classic add-in. Epazote is sold fresh or dried at Latin grocers; leave it out if you cannot find it. Use a mild poblano instead of the jalapeño for kids.
ingredients: a day or two old is best
5 or 6 fresh leaves, or a pinch of dried
half in the salsa, half sliced thin for the top
stirred with a squeeze of lime, standing in for Mexican crema

name: Huevos rancheros with salsa ranchera and pinto beans
inspiredBy: Huevos rancheros, with a little oil and a side of beans instead of fried potatoes
about: Two fried eggs on crisped corn tortillas, under a smoky roasted tomato and jalapeño salsa, with warm mashed pinto beans, a little queso fresco and avocado. It is the classic ranch breakfast, and it is filling without being heavy. The beans and eggs bring **protein, iron and folate** before the day has started.
steps: Use the beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed. Warm them with a splash of water and mash roughly with a fork.
Set a dry skillet over high heat and char the tomato, jalapeño and onion, turning them now and then, until blistered and blackened in spots, about 8 minutes.

Blend them with the garlic, half the cilantro, the cumin, oregano and salt into a chunky salsa. Pour it back into the skillet with a splash of water and simmer for 5 minutes, until it thickens and darkens.
Heat a little of the oil in a pan and crisp the tortillas for about a minute on each side. Move them to a plate.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the oil. Set them on the tortillas, spoon the salsa around them and add the beans.
Finish with the queso fresco, avocado and the rest of the cilantro.
tip: The salsa keeps for 4 days, so a double batch covers both mornings. Char and blend it the night before. Chopped serrano makes it hotter.

name: Huevos a la mexicana with pinto beans and warm tortillas
inspiredBy: Huevos a la mexicana, the everyday scrambled eggs with tomato, onion and chile
about: Scrambled eggs cooked with tomato, onion, jalapeño and tender nopalitos, the red, white and green of the Mexican flag, served with warm mashed pinto beans, avocado and warm tortillas. It is one of the most common breakfasts in the country, and it is ready in about 20 minutes. The eggs and beans bring **protein, choline and folate**.
steps: Use the beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed. Warm them with a splash of water and mash roughly with a fork.
Finely chop the tomato, onion and jalapeño. Warm the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion and jalapeño until soft, about 3 minutes.
Rinse the nopalitos well and add them with the tomato, the oregano and a pinch of the salt. Cook until the tomato softens and the juices thicken, about 4 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the rest of the salt, pour them into the pan and stir until no runny egg is left and the eggs are firm, about 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Serve the eggs with the beans, tortillas, avocado, queso fresco and the cilantro.
tip: A chopped serrano or a spoon of salsa makes it hotter. Leave the jalapeño out for kids.

name: Ensalada de nopales with pinto beans, queso fresco and pepitas
inspiredBy: Ensalada de nopales from central Mexico, with pinto beans and pepitas added to make it a full lunch
about: Tender cactus paddles tossed with tomato, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro and lime, folded through pinto beans and finished with queso fresco, toasted pepitas and avocado. It is cool, tangy and fresh, with warm tortillas to scoop it up. The beans and cactus bring **fibre and potassium**, and the pepitas bring zinc and magnesium.
steps: Use the beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed.
Rinse the nopalitos in a colander under cold water until the slippery coating is gone, then drain well.
Toast the pepitas in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until they puff and pop. Tip them out to cool.
Chop the tomato, red onion and jalapeño. Toss them in a big bowl with the nopales, beans, lime juice, oil, oregano, salt and most of the cilantro.
Top with the queso fresco, pepitas, sliced avocado and the rest of the cilantro.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or directly over a gas flame for a few seconds a side and serve them with the salad.
tip: Fresh nopales are worth trying: boil the diced paddles with a piece of onion for 10 minutes, then rinse. It packs well; keep the avocado and tortillas separate.
ingredients: jarred nopalitos, rinsed well under cold water

name: Quesadillas de rajas with corn, pinto beans and raw tomatillo salsa
inspiredBy: Quesadillas de rajas con elote, a street and home favourite across central and southern Mexico
about: Corn tortillas folded around melted Oaxaca cheese, charred poblano strips and sweet corn, served with warm pinto beans, a spoonful of lime crema and a sharp raw tomatillo salsa. Blackening the poblanos is what gives rajas their smoky flavour. The cheese and beans carry **protein and calcium**.
steps: Use the beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed.

Blacken the poblanos directly over a gas flame or under a very hot broiler, turning them until the skin is charred all over, about 10 minutes. Drop them into a covered bowl for 10 minutes to sweat, then peel off the skin, pull out the seeds and slice into strips (rajas).

Warm half the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion over medium-high heat until soft and speckled with brown, about 5 minutes. Add the rajas, corn and a pinch of salt and cook 2 minutes more. Tip into a bowl.

Make the salsa: blend the raw tomatillo, jalapeño, most of the cilantro, half the lime juice and a pinch of salt until almost smooth. Warm the beans with a splash of water and a pinch of salt, mashing a few as they heat.

Wipe out the pan. Lay the tortillas in it a couple at a time, scatter cheese and the filling over one half and fold them over. Cook in the rest of the oil until the cheese melts and the tortillas are golden and crisp at the edges, about 3 minutes a side.
Stir the yogurt with the rest of the lime juice to make a quick crema. Serve the quesadillas with the crema, beans and salsa, and the rest of the cilantro.
tip: Real Oaxaca cheese (quesillo) is stringy and mild. If you cannot find it, mozzarella is the best swap. Char, peel and cook the rajas on Tuesday night, so lunch is 15 minutes.
ingredients: stirred with a squeeze of lime, standing in for crema

name: Tlayuda-inspired tostadas with black beans, guajillo beef and quesillo
inspiredBy: Oaxacan tlayuda with tasajo (thin dried-style beef), usually one large toasted tortilla; this is a smaller, lighter version
about: Crisp baked tortillas spread with garlicky black beans and topped with thin guajillo-rubbed beef in the style of Oaxacan tasajo, melted Oaxaca cheese, shredded cabbage, grated carrot, sliced tomato and avocado. A real tlayuda is one huge toasted tortilla, and this is the same idea in a smaller, lighter size. The black beans and beef bring **iron, zinc and folate**.
steps: Use the beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed.

Soak the guajillo in hot water for 10 minutes. Blend it with half the garlic, half the lime juice, the oregano and a pinch of salt into a thick red paste, adding a spoon of the soaking water if you need it. Rub it all over the beef.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Brush the tortillas lightly with a little of the oil, lay them on a tray and bake until crisp and pale gold, about 8 minutes.
Heat the rest of the oil in a hot pan and sear the beef for about 1 minute a side, until browned at the edges. Rest it for a minute, then slice it thinner still.
Warm the beans in a small pot with the rest of the garlic, minced, the rest of the salt and a splash of water. Mash roughly.

Spread the beans over the crisp tortillas, scatter on the cheese and return the tray to the oven for 3 to 4 minutes, until it melts. Top with the beef, cabbage, grated carrot, tomato and avocado, and squeeze over the rest of the lime.
tip: A large tortilla from a Latin grocery makes it closer to the real thing. A dab of salsa on top is never wrong.
ingredients: round or flank steak, sliced against the grain as thin as you can
1 to 2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded

name: Pollo en tinga with black beans
inspiredBy: Tinga poblana from Puebla, served with black beans on warm tortillas
about: Shredded chicken simmered in a smoky tomato and chipotle sauce with soft onion, piled onto warm tortillas with black beans, a crunchy cabbage and carrot slaw and a sprinkle of queso fresco. It is a Puebla favourite, and it tastes even better the next day. Chicken and black beans bring **protein, folate and niacin**.
steps: Use the beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed.

Put the chicken in a pot with a quarter of the onion, a clove of the garlic, a pinch of salt and enough water to cover. Simmer gently until cooked through and tender, about 18 minutes. Lift it out, save a cup of the broth and shred the meat with two forks.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotles with their sauce, the rest of the garlic, the oregano, cumin, the rest of the salt and the cup of broth until smooth.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and cook the rest of the onion, sliced, until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Pour in the sauce and simmer for 8 minutes until it thickens and darkens.
Stir in the chicken and cook for 5 minutes so it soaks up the sauce. Warm the beans with a splash of water.
Serve on warm tortillas with the beans, cabbage, carrot and queso fresco. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch; tinga keeps well for 4 days.
tip: A small can of chipotles in adobo lasts a while: freeze the rest flat in a bag and snap off a chile when you need one. Tinga is great on a crisp tostada too.
ingredients: chipotles in adobo, about 1 chile and a spoonful of sauce per portion

name: Baja-style salmon tacos with cabbage slaw and lime crema
inspiredBy: Tacos de pescado estilo Baja, made with salmon and a yogurt crema in place of fried fish
about: Ancho-rubbed seared salmon flaked into warm corn tortillas with a crunchy lime cabbage and carrot slaw, cool lime crema and avocado, with a spoonful of black beans on the side. It borrows the Baja fish taco and swaps in salmon for a richer, oilier bite. One serving gives you **omega-3 and B12**, and helps with vitamin D.
steps: Use the beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed. Warm a spoonful per plate with a splash of water.
Soak the ancho in hot water for 10 minutes. Blend it with the garlic, half the lime juice and half the salt into a smooth red paste. Rub it over the salmon and let it sit while you make the slaw.
Toss the cabbage with the carrot, red onion, jalapeño, most of the cilantro and a pinch of salt.
Stir the yogurt with the rest of the lime juice and salt to make a thin, tangy crema.

Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and sear the salmon, skin side down first, until the crust is deep red and it flakes easily, about 4 minutes a side. It releases its own fat, so you do not need oil.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Flake the salmon into them, add the slaw, avocado and a drizzle of crema, and finish with the rest of the cilantro. Serve the warm black beans on the side.
tip: Not a salmon fan? Use any firm fish like cod or tilapia. A little diced mango in the slaw is lovely.
ingredients: 1 dried ancho chile, stemmed and seeded

name: Caldo de res with chickpeas, chayote and corn
inspiredBy: Caldo de res from northern and central Mexico, with chickpeas the way many home cooks add them
about: A big, comforting beef and vegetable soup made on bone-in beef short rib or shank, with cabbage, carrot, chayote, corn and potato in a clear, savoury broth and plenty of cilantro. Chickpeas are a normal addition in many homes, and a squeeze of lime goes in the bowl. It is a full meal in a bowl, rich in **zinc, iron and potassium**.
steps: The night before, cover the chickpeas with plenty of cold water and leave them to soak. Drain before using.

Put the beef and chickpeas in a large pot with the onion, garlic, tomato, salt and enough water to cover well. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes, until the meat is nearly tender.
Add the potato, carrot and corn and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the cabbage and chayote and simmer for 10 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Taste the broth and add salt if you need it. Stir in the cilantro.
Ladle into deep bowls with a piece of everything, with lime wedges to squeeze over and warm tortillas to dip in. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch; the broth gets better overnight.
tip: Most of the simmering is hands-off. In an olla exprés (pressure cooker), the beef and chickpeas take 35 minutes. A chopped serrano and a few drops of lime at the table make it feel like the real thing.
ingredients: bone-in beef shank or short rib; buy about 200 g with the bone
peeled and cut into wedges; zucchini works
about half an ear, cut into rounds

name: Sardine tostadas with beans, jícama slaw and salsa
inspiredBy: Tostadas de sardina, the coastal Mexican tostada made with canned sardines, with a spread of beans added for fibre and iron
about: Crisp baked tortillas spread with warm pinto beans, topped with flaked sardines, a crunchy jícama and carrot slaw, a spoon of fresh tomato salsa and creamy avocado. It is quick, fresh and a little spicy, in the style of seaside tostadas on the Pacific coast. The sardines bring **omega-3 and calcium from the soft bones**.
steps: Use the beans from your Sunday pot (see the plan notes), or canned beans at about three times the dry weight, drained and rinsed.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Lay the tortillas on a tray and bake until crisp and pale gold, about 8 minutes, turning once. These are your tostadas.
Warm the beans in a small pot with a splash of water and a pinch of salt, mashing them roughly.

Toss the jícama, cabbage, carrot, red onion, half the jalapeño and half the cilantro with half the lime juice and half the salt. Stir the chopped tomato with the rest of the jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice and salt for a quick salsa.
Flake the sardines into big pieces with a fork.
Assemble right away: spread beans over each tostada, add the sardines and a pile of the slaw, then a spoon of salsa and sliced avocado. Eat them while the base is still crisp.
tip: Pick sardines packed in olive oil if you like a richer taste. A dash of hot sauce on top never hurts.
ingredients: canned in oil or water, with the bones, drained; sardines in tomato sauce are common in Mexico too

name: Pozole verde with chicken, hominy and pepitas
inspiredBy: Pozole verde from Guerrero, made with chicken and canned hominy for a weeknight
about: A bright green, tangy soup of chicken and chewy hominy in a tomatillo, epazote and toasted pepita sauce, topped with queso fresco, oregano and lime. It comes from Guerrero on the Pacific side, where Thursday is pozole day. The pepitas bring **magnesium and zinc**, and the tomatillo brings vitamin C.
steps: Put the chicken in a pot with half the onion, half the garlic, a pinch of salt and about 5 cups of water. Simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through, about 20 minutes. Lift it out and shred it. Keep the broth.
Toast the pepitas in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until they puff and pop.
Simmer the tomatillos and jalapeño in a little of the broth for 8 minutes. Blend them with the toasted pepitas, epazote, cilantro, the rest of the onion and garlic, and a ladle of broth until smooth.
Warm the oil in the soup pot and fry the green sauce, stirring, for 5 minutes, until it darkens and thickens. Pour in the broth, add the hominy and the rest of the salt and simmer for 20 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pot and heat through for 5 minutes. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with the queso fresco, a pinch of ground oregano and a lime wedge. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Radish slices and a few baked tortilla strips are traditional at the table. Leave the epazote out if you cannot find it and add a little more cilantro.
ingredients: canned white hominy, drained and rinsed; one large 29 oz can makes two portions
3 fresh leaves, or a pinch of dried

name: Pollo pibil with pickled red onion
inspiredBy: Pollo pibil from the Yucatán, normally slow-roasted in a pit; this is the oven version with chicken thigh
about: Chicken thigh marinated in a bright achiote, orange and lime rub, wrapped up and baked low and slow until it falls apart, then piled into warm tortillas with sharp pink pickled onion and carrot, a slice of fresh chile and avocado. It comes from the Yucatán, where it is a weekend feast. The chicken is a good source of **niacin and B12**.
steps: The night before, mash the achiote paste with the orange juice and half the lime juice until it dissolves, then blend with the garlic, oregano, pepper, cumin and most of the salt into a red marinade.

Cut the chicken into big chunks. Rub the marinade all over it, cover and chill overnight, or at least 2 hours. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw chicken, and never reuse the marinade on cooked food.

Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Put the chicken and every drop of marinade on a big piece of foil or parchment, fold it into a tight parcel and set it in a baking dish. A banana leaf is traditional if you can find one.
Bake for about 1½ hours, until the chicken shreds easily with a fork and reads at least 74°C (165°F) in the thickest piece.
While it finishes, make the pickle: cover the red onion, jalapeño and carrot with the rest of the lime juice and a pinch of salt and leave for 30 minutes, until the onion is bright pink.

Shred the chicken right in its juices. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill the tacos with chicken, the pickle and sliced avocado. Pack the second portion into a shallow container and into the fridge within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat it once until steaming hot (74°C).
tip: Achiote paste (recado rojo) comes in small blocks or jars at Latin grocers and many supermarkets, and it is what gives pollo pibil its colour and earthy flavour. Sour orange is the usual juice; orange plus extra lime is the close swap.
ingredients: boneless, skinless, trimmed of any extra fat

name: Frijoles charros with lean beef, tomato and jalapeño
inspiredBy: Frijoles charros from Jalisco and the north, made with a little lean ground beef instead of the usual cured meats
about: A cowboy-style pot of pinto beans simmered with a little lean beef, tomato, onion, ancho chile and epazote, finished with cilantro and queso fresco and served with warm tortillas. It is hearty, smoky and very much northern Mexico. The beans and beef bring **iron, zinc and fibre**.
steps: Cover the beans with water in a pot, add a quarter of the onion and the epazote and simmer until very tender, about 1 hour 15 minutes, topping up the water if you need to. Or use about three times the dry weight in cooked Sunday beans or canned, drained, and simmer them for 20 minutes only.
Toast the ancho in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side, then soak it in hot water for 10 minutes and blend it with the tomato into a smoky sauce.

Warm the oil in a second pot and brown the ground beef with the smoked paprika over medium-high heat, breaking it up, about 5 minutes, until no pink is left and it reads at least 71°C (160°F). Wash your hands after handling the raw beef.

Add most of the rest of the onion, chopped, with the jalapeño and garlic and cook, stirring, until soft and fragrant, about 4 minutes. Pour in the tomato and ancho sauce and cook until thick, about 5 minutes.
Tip in the beans with a cup of their cooking liquid and the salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few of the beans against the side of the pot, until it is thick and stew-like.
Stir in most of the cilantro, then serve with the queso fresco, the rest of the cilantro, the last of the onion, raw, a squeeze of lime and the warm tortillas.
tip: A pinch of smoked paprika with the beef gives the pot a deep, smoky flavour. Make a double pot and freeze half.
ingredients: dried; cooked in the pot, see the steps
a pinch, cooked with the beef
1 dried ancho or pasilla chile, stemmed and seeded
a sprig, or a pinch of dried

name: Papaya and almond licuado with yogurt
about: A thick, cold blend of yogurt and sweet papaya and a spoonful of almonds with a pinch of cinnamon, the way a juice stand would make it. It is creamy and refreshing, and quick. The yogurt and almonds bring **protein, calcium and vitamin E**, and the papaya brings vitamin C.
steps: Blend everything with a splash of cold water and a few ice cubes until thick and smooth.
Pour into a tall glass and eat it with a spoon if it is very thick.

name: Chía fresca with lime
inspiredBy: Chía fresca, the traditional chia agua fresca of Mexico, lightly sweetened with orange juice instead of sugar
about: Chia seeds soaked in water with lime juice and a splash of orange juice until they turn plump and jelly-like, a classic Mexican agua fresca. It is cool, tangy and slightly sweet. Chia brings **omega-3, calcium and magnesium** in a very Mexican way.
steps: Stir the chia into a tall glass of cold water (about 250 ml) and leave it for 10 minutes, stirring once or twice, until it plumps up.
Add the lime juice, orange juice, a tiny pinch of salt and ice, and stir well.

name: Yogurt with orange and toasted pepitas
about: Cold yogurt with juicy orange segments and a handful of toasted pepitas. It is simple, creamy and crunchy, and a very easy snack. The yogurt and pepitas bring **protein, calcium and zinc**.
steps: Toast the pepitas in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes, until they puff and pop.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the orange segments and the pepitas.

name: Jícama sticks with lime and chile
about: Crunchy jícama sticks tossed with lime juice, ground guajillo and a pinch of salt, the way it is sold at street stalls in Mexico. It is juicy, sharp and refreshing. Jícama brings **fibre and vitamin C**, with very few calories.
steps: Peel the jícama and cut it into sticks. Toss with the lime juice, ground guajillo and salt, and eat it cold.
ingredients: toasted and ground guajillo, or chile powder

name: Orange with chile and lime
about: Juicy orange segments sprinkled with ground guajillo, a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt, an everyday Mexican fruit snack. It is sweet, sour and a little spicy. Orange brings **vitamin C and folate**.
steps: Peel the orange and cut it into segments or slices.
Sprinkle with the ground guajillo and lime juice.
ingredients: toasted and ground guajillo, or chile powder

name: Papaya with lime and chile
about: Cold papaya cubes with a squeeze of lime and a dusting of ground guajillo, a popular fruit cup in Mexico. The lime makes the sweetness taste brighter. Papaya brings **vitamin C and vitamin A**.
steps: Scoop out the seeds, peel the papaya and cut it into cubes.
Toss with the lime juice and ground guajillo.
ingredients: toasted and ground guajillo, or chile powder

name: Esquites, warm corn in a cup with lime and queso fresco
inspiredBy: Esquites, the warm corn cup sold at street stalls across central Mexico, with lime yogurt in place of mayonnaise and crema
about: Sweet corn kernels sautéed until a little charred, tossed with lime juice, ground guajillo, queso fresco and a spoonful of lime yogurt, served in a cup. It is warm, sweet and salty, and a Mexican street classic. Corn brings **fibre and B vitamins**, and the queso fresco brings calcium.
steps: Warm the oil in a pan over high heat and cook the corn, stirring now and then, until it is hot and some kernels are browned, about 6 minutes.
Tip into a cup and stir in the yogurt, lime juice and ground guajillo. Top with queso fresco and cilantro.
ingredients: frozen kernels, no need to thaw
toasted and ground guajillo, or chile powder

name: Baked sweet potato with cinnamon
about: A sweet potato baked until soft and caramelized, split open and dusted with cinnamon. Camotes are sold hot by street vendors in the evening in Mexico City. Sweet potato brings **vitamin A and potassium**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Prick the sweet potato with a fork, put it on a tray and bake until very soft and oozing, about 45 minutes.
Split it open and dust with the cinnamon.
tip: Bake two or three at once and keep them in the fridge; reheat a few minutes in a hot oven or microwave.

name: Guacamole with baked tostadas
about: Chunky avocado mashed with lime, red onion, cilantro and a little tomato, scooped up with crisp baked tortilla chips. It is creamy and fresh. Avocado brings **vitamin E, potassium and healthy fat**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Spread the tortilla triangles on a tray and bake until crisp, about 8 minutes.
Mash the avocado roughly with the lime juice and salt, then fold in the tomato, red onion and cilantro, all finely chopped.
Scoop with the warm chips.

name: Chía fresca with orange
inspiredBy: Chía fresca, the traditional chia agua fresca of Mexico, made with orange instead of sugar
about: Chia seeds plumped in cold water with fresh orange juice and a squeeze of lime, a sweeter take on the classic agua fresca. It is bright and refreshing, and the seeds give it a pearly, jelly-like texture. Chia brings **omega-3, calcium and magnesium**.
steps: Stir the chia into a tall glass of cold water (about 200 ml) and leave it for 10 minutes, stirring once or twice, until it plumps up.
Add the orange juice, lime juice and ice, and stir well.

name: Yogurt with orange and toasted almonds
about: Cold yogurt with juicy orange segments and a handful of toasted almonds. It is simple, creamy and crunchy, and a very easy snack. The yogurt and almonds bring **protein, calcium and vitamin E**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 4 to 5 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the orange segments and the almonds.

name: Almonds with lime and chile
about: Almonds toasted in a dry pan and tossed with lime juice, ground guajillo and a pinch of salt, in the style of the spiced nuts sold by Mexican street vendors. They are crunchy, warm and tangy. Almonds bring **vitamin E, magnesium and calcium**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until they smell nutty.
Toss with the lime juice, ground guajillo and salt while still warm.
ingredients: toasted and ground guajillo, or chile powder

name: Cardamom berry porridge with walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian spiced porridge
about: Oats simmered in fortified soy milk with frozen berries, chia and cardamom until thick and creamy, then topped with toasted walnuts. Warm, gently sweet and ready in ten minutes, it brings **fibre, omega-3 and B12** (the B12 comes from the fortified soy milk).
steps: Put the oats, soy milk, frozen berries, chia, cardamom, cinnamon and salt in a small pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until thick and the berries have melted into purple swirls.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until they smell nutty.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and scatter the walnuts over the top so they stay crunchy.
ingredients: choose a soy milk fortified with B12 and calcium (check the label)

name: Turmeric tofu scramble with peppers, spinach and avocado
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian-style tofu bhurji
about: Crumbled calcium-set tofu fried with turmeric, pepper and onion until golden, then wilted spinach, with sliced avocado on the side. It eats like a scramble and brings **plant protein, iron and some calcium** before eight o'clock.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach and avocado. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and soften the onion and pepper for 4 minutes.
Crumble in the tofu with the turmeric, cumin, smoked paprika and salt. Fry for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tofu is hot and golden at the edges.
Add the spinach and stir for 1 minute until it has wilted.
Squeeze over the lime juice and serve with the sliced avocado alongside.

name: Chocolate tahini banana overnight oats
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss overnight oats
about: Oats soaked overnight in fortified soy milk with cocoa, mashed banana, chia and a spoonful of tahini, so it tastes like dessert and eats like a proper breakfast. Five minutes the night before gives you **fibre, calcium and omega-3**, plus B12 from the fortified soy milk.
steps: Wash your hands. Mash the banana in a jar or bowl, then stir in the cocoa, tahini, soy milk, cinnamon and salt until smooth.
Stir in the oats and chia until no dry oats are left. Put the lid on and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, stir well and loosen with a splash of soy milk if it is thick. Eat it cold, or warm it in the microwave for 1 minute.
Keep it in the fridge and eat within 2 days of making it.
tip: Never keep soaked oats more than 2 days; make a fresh jar on Tuesday night for Wednesday and Thursday night for Friday.
ingredients: choose a soy milk fortified with B12 and calcium (check the label)

name: Mushroom, spinach and white bean omelette with blistered tomatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Spanish tortilla and a Tuscan egg and bean skillet
about: A fully set omelette filled with browned mushrooms, wilted spinach and white beans, with cherry tomatoes blistered in the pan. The eggs bring **choline and B12**, and the beans and spinach add iron, with the tomatoes' vitamin C to help absorb it.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomatoes and cilantro. Heat half the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and brown the mushrooms for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes until their skins blister, then add the spinach and white beans and cook for 1 minute until the spinach has wilted. Tip everything onto a plate.

Wipe the pan, add the rest of the oil and pour in the whisked eggs with the salt. Cook over medium heat, lifting the edges, for 3 minutes until the base is set. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Spoon half the filling over one side, fold the other side over and cook for 2 minutes more, until the eggs are completely firm all the way through.
Slide onto a plate, spoon the rest of the filling alongside and scatter the cilantro over.
tip: On a busy weekday, cook the mushroom, tomato and bean filling the night before, keep it in the fridge and reheat it until steaming hot while the eggs cook.

name: Peanut-lime quinoa salad with edamame, cabbage and egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indonesian gado-gado and a Thai-style peanut slaw
about: Fluffy quinoa tossed with edamame, green cabbage and carrot in a creamy peanut and lime dressing, topped with firm-boiled egg. It packs well, tastes better after an hour in the fridge, and gives you **plant protein, folate, fibre and choline**.
steps: Put the egg in a pot of cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool under cold water, peel and quarter.
Rinse the quinoa, then simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Spread it in a shallow container and cool within 1 hour.
Cook the frozen edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, until steaming hot all the way through, then drain and cool under cold water.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, ginger and chili powder with 2 to 3 tablespoons of warm water until smooth and pourable.
Wash the cabbage, carrot and cilantro, then shred the cabbage, grate the carrot and chop the cilantro. Toss them with the quinoa, edamame and dressing, then top with the egg.
For a packed lunch, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day. Keep cooked quinoa no more than 3 days.
tip: Cook the quinoa for this salad on Sunday evening or Monday morning, cool it within 1 hour and keep it covered in the fridge for no more than 3 days.

name: Warm curried lentil and kale salad with apple, eggs and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by an Indian lentil salad and a French lentil and apple salad
about: No-salt-added lentils warmed with curry powder and onion, folded through softened kale and crisp apple, then topped with firm-boiled eggs, lemon and walnuts. Ready in about twenty minutes, it gives you **iron, folate and choline**, with the lemon helping you absorb the iron.
steps: Put the eggs in a pot of cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the yolks are completely firm. Cool under cold water, peel and quarter.
Wash the kale, apple and cilantro. Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the onion for 4 minutes.

Stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the lentils, kale, a splash of water and the salt. Cook, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes until the kale is tender and the lentils are hot.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the lemon juice and the diced apple, so the apple stays crisp.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the eggs, walnuts and cilantro. For a packed lunch, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

name: Smoky black bean, corn and avocado salad with egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican ensalada de frijoles
about: Black beans, sweet corn, red pepper and tomatoes in a smoky lime dressing, with creamy avocado, a firm-boiled egg and toasted pumpkin seeds. It brings **fibre, folate, magnesium and choline**.
steps: Put the egg in a pot of cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool under cold water, peel and quarter.
Cook the frozen corn in boiling water for 3 minutes until steaming hot, then drain and cool under cold water.
Whisk the oil, lime juice, smoked paprika, cumin and salt in a bowl.
Wash the pepper, tomatoes, avocado and cilantro. Add the beans, corn, pepper, tomatoes, onion and cilantro to the bowl and toss well.
Fold in the avocado gently and top with the egg. Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes and scatter them over just before eating.
