For a packed lunch, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

name: Mushroom, lentil and tofu cottage pie with sweet potato top
inspiredBy: Inspired by British shepherd's and cottage pie, with lentils and mushrooms doing the meat's job
about: A rich filling of lentils, crumbled tofu, mushrooms, carrot, peas and spinach with tomato and thyme, under a golden mash of sweet potato and a crunch of walnuts, with no meat at all. It is proper comfort food, it makes tomorrow's lunch, and it brings **iron, folate and vitamin A**.
steps: Put the sweet potato in a pot of cold water with a pinch of the salt, bring to the boil and simmer for 12 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Heat the grill to high.
Meanwhile, warm the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion, carrot and mushrooms for 6 minutes until the water has cooked off and they begin to brown. Add the garlic and thyme and stir for 30 seconds.

Add the tofu, breaking it into small crumbs, and cook for 2 minutes. Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, peas, soy sauce, bay leaf and 100 ml water. Simmer for 6 minutes until thick, then stir in the washed spinach until wilted and remove the bay leaf.
Drain the sweet potato, return it to the pot with the soy milk and the rest of the salt and mash until smooth.
Spoon the filling into an ovenproof dish and spread the mash over the top, rough it up with a fork and scatter the walnuts over. Grill for 5 to 6 minutes until the peaks are golden.
Serve one portion now.

Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days and reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). To carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack and reheat it before eating. To freeze, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).
ingredients: for the mash; choose a soy milk fortified with B12 and calcium (check the label)

name: Ginger-lime salmon with broccoli, garlicky kale and quinoa
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese-style ginger and soy glazed salmon
about: A salmon fillet roasted under a glaze of ginger, soy and lime beside broccoli florets, with garlicky kale and a bed of quinoa. Twenty-five minutes, and the salmon brings **omega-3, B12 and vitamin D**, while the kale adds calcium and vitamin K.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes. Drain any extra water, fluff and keep covered.

Whisk half the soy sauce with the ginger, half the garlic and the lime juice. Wash the broccoli. Put the salmon and the broccoli on a lined tray, spoon the glaze over the salmon and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Meanwhile, wash the kale. Warm the oil in a wide pan, add the rest of the garlic and the kale and stir for 3 minutes until bright green.
Add the rest of the soy sauce and 3 tablespoons of water, cover and steam for 3 minutes until tender.
Serve the salmon and broccoli on the quinoa with the kale, and scatter the cilantro over the top.

name: Chickpea and spinach stew with potatoes and toasted walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish espinacas con garbanzos
about: A smoky tomato stew of chickpeas, potato and a lot of spinach, finished with lemon, cool yogurt and a handful of toasted walnuts. It makes tomorrow's lunch, and the chickpeas, spinach and walnuts bring **folate, iron, magnesium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, smoked paprika and cumin and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the potato, crushed tomatoes, salt and 200 ml water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 12 minutes until the potato is almost tender.
Stir in the chickpeas and cook, uncovered, for 5 minutes. Add the washed spinach in handfuls and stir until it has wilted.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes. Finish the stew with the lemon juice and cilantro.
Serve with a spoonful of cold yogurt and the walnuts scattered on top. Keep the yogurt separate for the second portion; add it cold after reheating.

Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days and reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). To carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack and reheat it before eating. To freeze, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Crispy tofu traybake with broccoli, sweet potato and ginger-lime yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by crisp-fried tofu from Japan and Indonesia, roasted on one tray
about: Cubes of calcium-set tofu roasted until crisp at the edges with broccoli, sweet potato, mushrooms and onion, then drizzled with a cool ginger-lime yogurt sauce. It is one tray, and it brings **plant protein, some calcium, vitamin C and potassium**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the broccoli and cilantro. Toss the sweet potato, mushrooms and onion with half the oil and the chili powder on a large tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Press the tofu dry between clean towels. Toss it with the rest of the oil and a third of the soy sauce until evenly coated.
Push the vegetables aside and add the tofu and broccoli to the tray in a single layer. Roast for 15 minutes more, turning once, until the tofu is crisp at the edges and the sweet potato is tender.
Stir the yogurt with the rest of the soy sauce, the lime juice, ginger, garlic and half the cilantro into a sauce.
Serve the traybake hot, with the cold sauce spooned over and the rest of the cilantro scattered on top.
ingredients: pressed dry, cut in 2 cm cubes

name: Paprika chicken and cabbage stew with potatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by Hungarian paprikás and cabbage stews
about: The week's only chicken goes into a mild paprika stew with cabbage, potato, carrot, kale and mushrooms, with a pinch of caraway and a squeeze of lemon. It makes tomorrow's lunch and brings **protein, vitamin A, vitamin C and fibre**.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the mushrooms with the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika and caraway and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes. Wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken.

Add the crushed tomatoes, potato, carrot, cabbage, kale, salt, bay leaf and 300 ml water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 18 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is soft, the cabbage is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
Remove the bay leaf and stir in the lemon juice. Serve one portion now.

Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days and reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). To carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack and reheat it before eating. To freeze, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Bean-stuffed peppers with quinoa, mint and lemon yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Turkish biber dolma, filled with beans
about: Roasted red pepper halves filled with black beans, quinoa, spinach and a warm tomato sauce spiced Turkish-style with cinnamon, allspice and mint, finished with a spoonful of cool lemon yogurt. A relaxed weekend dish that makes tomorrow's lunch and brings **vitamin C, fibre, folate and iron**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes. Cool a little.
Put the pepper halves cut side up in a baking dish and roast for 15 minutes while you make the filling.
Warm the oil in a pan and soften the onion for 4 minutes. Add the garlic, cinnamon, allspice and dried mint and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the crushed tomatoes and salt and simmer for 5 minutes, then stir in the beans, quinoa and the washed spinach and cook for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts. Add half the lemon juice.

Spoon the filling into the pepper halves and bake for 20 minutes until the peppers are tender and the filling is steaming hot. Stir the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of dried mint into the yogurt.
Serve with the cold yogurt on top. For the second portion, keep the yogurt separate.

Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days and reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). To carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack and reheat it before eating. To freeze, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Roast trout with lemon, quinoa, peas and a yogurt-cilantro sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by lemon-and-herb roast trout
about: Rainbow trout roasted with lemon, served over fluffy quinoa and sweet peas with a cool yogurt-cilantro sauce and a bright cherry tomato salad. The trout brings **omega-3, B12 and vitamin D**, and the peas and edamame bring fibre and folate.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in twice its volume of water with a pinch of the salt, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes. Add the peas and edamame for the last 3 minutes so they are steaming hot, then fluff.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Put the trout on a lined tray, rub with half the oil, a little lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of salt, and roast for 10 to 12 minutes until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Wash the tomatoes and cilantro. Stir the yogurt, half the cilantro and a squeeze of lemon into a sauce.
Toss the tomatoes with the onion, the rest of the oil, the rest of the lemon juice, the rest of the cilantro and the salt.
Spoon the quinoa and peas onto plates, top with the trout, and serve with the yogurt sauce and the tomato salad.

name: Apple slices with peanut butter
about: Crisp apple with a spoonful of peanut butter. A simple snack that brings **fibre and vitamin E**.
steps: Wash the apple and slice it. Serve with the peanut butter for dipping.

name: Warm edamame with lime and sea salt
about: A bowl of steaming edamame with lime. Quick plant protein, **folate and iron**.
steps: Cook the frozen edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes until steaming hot, then drain.
Toss with the lime juice and salt and eat warm.

name: Carrot and pepper sticks with tahini-yogurt dip
about: Crunchy sticks of carrot and red pepper with a lemony tahini and yogurt dip. It brings **vitamin A, vitamin C and some calcium**.
steps: Wash the carrot and pepper and cut them in sticks.
Stir the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice and salt together with a splash of water until smooth. Serve the dip with the sticks, and keep any left over in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Crunchy cumin-lime roasted chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with cumin and a squeeze of lime. They bring **protein, fibre and zinc**.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Pat the chickpeas very dry and toss with the oil, cumin and salt.
Roast on a tray for 25 minutes, shaking once, until crisp. Squeeze the lime over and eat warm or cool. Store in an open container for up to 2 days.
ingredients: rinsed, drained and patted very dry

name: Greek yogurt with berries and chia
about: Thick yogurt over thawed berries with a spoonful of chia for crunch. **Protein, calcium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the thawed berries and scatter the chia over.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, simmer the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

name: Apple with walnuts
about: A crisp apple with a few walnuts for crunch. **Fibre and plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and eat with the walnuts.

name: Banana and peanut butter on cinnamon oats
about: A small bowl of oats made with fortified soy milk, topped with banana and peanut butter. **Fibre, calcium and B12 from the soy milk**.
steps: Stir the oats, chia and soy milk in a bowl and microwave for 90 seconds, stirring once, until hot. Let it stand for 3 minutes so the chia thickens it; it should be soft and spoonable, not stiff.
Top with the banana, peanut butter and cinnamon.
ingredients: choose a soy milk fortified with B12 and calcium (check the label)

name: Firm-boiled egg with apple slices and cherry tomatoes
about: A firm-boiled egg with crisp apple and sweet cherry tomatoes. A simple plate that brings **choline, protein and vitamin C**.
steps: Put the egg in a pot of cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the yolk is completely firm. Cool under cold water and peel.

Wash the apple and tomatoes. Slice the egg and eat with the apple, the tomatoes and a pinch of salt. If you boil it ahead, keep it in the fridge in its shell and eat it within 1 week; for a packed snack, use a cold bag with an ice pack.

name: Cinnamon soy chia pudding with berries
about: Chia seeds soaked in fortified soy milk until spoonable, with cinnamon and berries on top. **Plant omega-3, calcium and B12** from the soy milk.
steps: Stir the chia and cinnamon into the soy milk in a jar. Wait 5 minutes, stir again to break up any clumps, then cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Top with the thawed berries. Keep it in the fridge and eat within 2 days of making it.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, simmer the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.
ingredients: choose a soy milk fortified with B12 and calcium (check the label)

name: Berry banana soy smoothie
about: A thick smoothie of fortified soy milk, banana, berries, oats and chia. **Fibre, calcium, omega-3 and B12** from the soy milk.
steps: Put the soy milk, banana, frozen berries, oats, chia and cinnamon in a blender and blend for 1 minute until completely smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink straight away, or keep it in the fridge and drink within 1 day.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, simmer the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.
ingredients: choose a soy milk fortified with B12 and calcium (check the label)

name: Greek yogurt with banana and walnuts
about: Thick yogurt with sliced banana, walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon. **Protein, calcium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the sliced banana and walnuts and dust with the cinnamon.

name: Chili-garlic edamame
about: Edamame tossed in a hot pan with garlic, chili and a splash of soy sauce. **Plant protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Cook the frozen edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes until steaming hot, then drain well.
Warm the oil in a pan, stir the garlic and chili for 20 seconds, add the edamame and soy sauce and toss for 1 minute. Finish with the lime juice and eat warm.

name: Banana with peanut butter and cinnamon
about: A ripe banana with a spoonful of peanut butter and a dust of cinnamon. **Potassium, B6 and magnesium**.
steps: Slice the banana, spread or drizzle the peanut butter over it and dust with the cinnamon.

name: Japanese breakfast tray with grilled cod, natto and tofu miso soup
inspiredBy: a classic Japanese asa-gohan set
about: The classic Japanese morning tray: grilled cod, a tub of natto, a bowl of miso soup with tofu and scallion, rice, and spinach dressed with soy and sesame. It looks like a lot of small things, but it all comes together in about 20 minutes. The cod, natto and tofu give you **a big, steady dose of protein** before you train, and natto is also a good source of iron.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it with a little more than its own volume of water, covered, until tender, about 18 minutes, then rest it for 10 minutes. A rice cooker does this without watching.
Pat the cod dry, sprinkle it with the salt and let it sit while the grill heats. Broil or grill it skin side up for 6 to 8 minutes, until the skin blisters and the flesh flakes.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 40 seconds, cool it under cold water and squeeze it dry. Cut it into short lengths and dress with the soy sauce, rice vinegar and sesame seeds.
Warm a small mug of water, add the tofu and half the scallion and heat it through. Turn off the heat and stir in the miso until it dissolves. Do not boil it after the miso goes in.
Stir the natto briskly for about 20 turns until it turns stringy and pale, and top it with the rest of the scallion. Serve everything together on a tray with the rice.
tip: Cook the rice the night before, or set a rice cooker timer. Natto is sold frozen in most Asian grocers and thaws in the fridge overnight. A strip of kombu or a pinch of dashi granules in the soup water helps.
ingredients: or Pacific cod or haddock; skin on if you can, patted dry

name: Dan bing egg crepe with turkey and scallion, with edamame on the side
inspiredBy: Taiwanese dan bing
about: A thin wheat crepe with eggs cooked right onto it, rolled up around savoury ground turkey and scallion and brushed with a little soy sauce and fresh chili. It is a Taiwanese street breakfast, and a warm bowl of edamame with a little vinegared daikon turns it into a proper meal. The eggs, turkey and edamame together bring **plenty of protein**.
steps: Whisk the flour with a pinch of the salt and about twice its weight in water until it is a thin, smooth batter like cream. Let it stand for 5 minutes.

Brush a nonstick pan with part of the canola oil over medium heat. Pour in the batter and swirl it into a thin round. Cook for about a minute, until the edges lift and it is just set. Slide it onto a plate.

Add the rest of the canola oil to the pan and cook the turkey for 3 minutes, stirring and breaking it up, until no pink is left and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Add the beaten eggs and egg whites with the scallion. When the eggs are nearly set, lay the crepe on top and press down so it sticks. Cover for 30 seconds, then flip the whole round with a wide spatula: the set egg holds the crepe together. Cook 30 seconds more and roll it up with the egg inside.
Slide onto a board, brush the outside with the soy sauce and sesame oil, scatter on the chili, then cut into thick slices.
Warm the edamame in a splash of hot water and drain. Toss the daikon with the rice vinegar and serve both beside the crepe.
tip: Make the batter the night before and it pours even thinner. Scallion is the classic; a handful of chopped garlic chives makes a good change.

name: Ginger congee with egg, cod and bok choy
inspiredBy: Cantonese fish congee (yu jook)
about: A pot of rice cooked down until it is silky, then topped with thin slices of cod, a firm-cooked egg with silky ribbons of egg white, bok choy and shiitake, plenty of ginger and scallion, toasted sesame and white pepper. It is the Saturday breakfast that takes care of you. The cod and egg give **a big serving of protein**, and a bowl of congee is easy on the stomach after a hard week of training.
steps: Rinse the rice, then simmer it with about seven times its volume of water, the ginger coins and the salt, partly covered, for 45 minutes. Stir now and then so it does not stick, until the grains break down and the porridge is thick and creamy. Add hot water if it gets too thick.
Toss the cod slices with half the soy sauce, the sesame oil and the white pepper, and keep them cold while the congee finishes.

For the first portion, ladle half the congee into a small pot over medium heat, add the bok choy, shiitake and cod, and simmer for 3 minutes, until the cod turns opaque and the bok choy wilts. Turn the heat to low.

Stir in the egg whites in a thin stream so they set in soft ribbons. Crack the whole egg on top, cover and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the white and the yolk are both firm (poke the yolk to check). Slide it into a bowl and add the rest of the soy sauce, the ginger matchsticks, scallion, cilantro and sesame seeds.
Chill the second portion of congee, with its cod, bok choy, shiitake and egg kept raw in the fridge. Tomorrow, loosen it with a splash of water, reheat it and finish it the same way.
tip: A pressure cooker makes the congee in 20 minutes. Rice that has been frozen first breaks down faster.
ingredients: sliced, some cut into fine matchsticks

name: Salmon onigiri bento with edamame and miso tofu soup
inspiredBy: Japanese onigiri and a bento lunch
about: Rice balls wrapped in nori and filled with flaked baked salmon, scallion and sesame, packed with a cool cucumber pickle and edamame, and a mug of miso soup with tofu. This is the lunch you can make the night before. The salmon gives you **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the rice refuels you.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it with a little more than its own volume of water, covered, for about 18 minutes, then rest it for 10 minutes. Spread it on a plate to cool for 10 minutes so you can handle it.
Bake the salmon at 200 C (400 F) for 10 to 12 minutes, until it flakes. Flake it with a fork and mix with half the soy sauce, half the scallion and half the sesame seeds.

Wet your hands, rub them with a little of the salt, and press a handful of rice into a thick triangle around a spoonful of salmon, then cover it with more rice. Shape a few balls in this way and wrap each with a strip of nori.
Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar, a pinch of salt and the remaining sesame seeds. Set it aside for 10 minutes.

Warm a small mug of water, add the tofu and the rest of the scallion and heat through, then off the heat stir in the miso. Serve with the onigiri, cucumber and edamame, with the rest of the soy sauce for dipping.
tip: Cook the salmon and rice the night before, cool the rice fast, and the morning is only shaping. Warm the rice until soft first: fridge-cold rice will not hold together. Wrap onigiri in nori just before eating if you want it crisp.

name: Chicken teriyaki rice bowl with green beans and carrot
inspiredBy: Japanese chicken teriyaki
about: Seared chicken thigh glazed in a quick teriyaki of soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger and garlic with a spoonful of sugar, over brown rice with blistered green beans, carrot and edamame. It is glossy, savoury and not too sweet. It makes **two big portions**, so tomorrow's lunch is done, and the thigh stays juicy even when reheated.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook enough for two portions in about twice its volume of water, covered, for 35 to 40 minutes, then rest it for 10 minutes.
Stir the soy sauce, sugar, ginger, garlic and rice vinegar together with a few spoonfuls of water.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and sear the chicken in two batches so it browns instead of steaming, 3 to 4 minutes a side, until golden and cooked through. Lift it out.
Add the green beans and carrot with a splash of water, cover for 2 minutes, then uncover and cook until the beans are bright and blistered at the edges. Add the edamame for the last minute.

Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and stir for a minute or two until it reduces and turns glossy. Spoon over the rice and finish with the sesame seeds and scallion. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Start the brown rice first, or use a rice cooker. Teri means shine and yaki means grilled, and the sugar is only a spoonful. Pack the rice and chicken apart for lunch so the rice does not go soggy.

name: Shrimp, tofu and edamame stir-fry with bok choy and brown rice
inspiredBy: Chinese home-style stir-fried tofu and shrimp
about: Tofu seared until golden, then tossed with shrimp, edamame, bok choy and shiitake in a hot pan with garlic, ginger and a squeeze of rice vinegar. Only a little soy sauce and a squeeze of vinegar keep it bright instead of salty. The shrimp, tofu and soy beans together bring **a lot of protein**, and it makes two portions.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook enough for two portions in about twice its volume of water, covered, for 35 to 40 minutes, then rest it for 10 minutes.
Pat the shrimp dry and toss them with a little of the soy sauce and a few drops of the rice vinegar. Leave them for 10 minutes.
Heat the canola oil in a wok or large pan over high heat and sear the tofu for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Lift it out.
Add the garlic, ginger, chili and mushrooms and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the shrimp and cook for 2 minutes, until pink and curled.

Tip in the edamame, bok choy and tofu with the rest of the soy sauce and the rice vinegar. Toss for 2 minutes, in two batches if your wok is small, until the bok choy stems are just crisp. Finish with the scallion.
Serve over the rice. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Start the brown rice first, or use a rice cooker. Frozen shrimp are best: thaw them in cold water in 10 minutes. Swap the bok choy for green beans or broccoli if that is what you have.
ingredients: firm, not soft (soft will not sear); pressed dry and cut in squares

name: Beef bibimbap with namul, fried egg and gochujang
inspiredBy: Korean bibimbap
about: Warm rice with sesame-garlic beef, a colourful ring of seasoned spinach, carrot, mushrooms and cucumber, fried eggs and a spoonful of gochujang. Mix it all together at the table. The beef, egg and rice together bring **plenty of protein, iron and zinc**, and it makes two portions.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook enough for two portions with a little more than its own volume of water, about 18 minutes, then rest 10 minutes.
Mix the beef with half the soy sauce, half the garlic and half the sesame oil. Leave it for 20 minutes.
Blanch the spinach for 40 seconds, squeeze it dry and toss with a pinch of garlic and the rest of the sesame oil. Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar.
Stir-fry the carrot and shiitake separately in a little of the canola oil, 1 to 2 minutes each, until just tender and bright.
Cook the beef in a hot pan for 2 to 3 minutes, until browned. Fry today's eggs in the rest of the oil until the whites are set and the yolks are firm, flipping the eggs for the last minute.

Spoon the rice into bowls, arrange the beef and vegetables in sections, add the egg, gochujang and sesame seeds, and stir it all together. For the second portion, keep the beef and vegetables cold and fry the egg fresh tomorrow.
tip: Use a pan with a lid to crisp the bottom of the rice for dolsot-style bibimbap. Gochujang is salty and brands vary, so stir in half, taste, then add the rest.
ingredients: sliced very thin against the grain

name: Grilled saba with grated daikon, miso tofu soup and rice
inspiredBy: Japanese saba shioyaki
about: Mackerel fillets lightly salted and grilled until the skin crackles, with a cool heap of grated daikon, a squeeze of lime, bok choy in sesame and soy, and a bowl of tofu miso soup. The daikon and lime cut the richness of the fish. Mackerel is one of the best sources of **omega-3 and vitamin D** you can eat.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it with a little more than its own volume of water, about 18 minutes, then rest it for 10 minutes.
Rub the mackerel with the salt and leave it for 10 minutes. Pat it dry again. Broil or grill it skin side up for 6 to 8 minutes, until the skin is blistered and the flesh flakes. No turning needed.
Squeeze the grated daikon lightly. Mix the lime juice, ginger and soy sauce and spoon some over the daikon.
Steam the bok choy in a covered pan with a splash of water for 3 minutes until just tender. Toss with the sesame oil and sesame seeds.
Warm a small mug of water, add the tofu and scallion and heat through, then turn off the heat and stir in the miso.
Serve the fish with the daikon, rice, bok choy and soup.
tip: Ask the fishmonger for saba fillets with the skin on. Frozen saba from a Japanese grocer works, and fresh sardines or herring grill the same way. A strip of kombu in the soup water helps.

name: Cold beef shabu soba with sesame, cucumber and edamame
inspiredBy: Japanese reishabu salad over cold soba
about: Thin slices of lean beef quickly poached and chilled, laid over cold buckwheat noodles with cucumber, carrot and edamame under a sesame, rice vinegar and lime dressing. It is a summer lunch in Japan and works any day. The beef and soba together carry **a lot of protein and B vitamins**.
steps: Grind the sesame seeds to a rough paste with a mortar or a spice grinder. Whisk in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, lime juice, ginger and sesame oil with a spoonful of water to make a pourable dressing.

Slice the beef as thin as you can and drop it into a pot of barely simmering water for 1 to 2 minutes, until no pink is left and it reaches 71 °C (160 °F). Wash your hands and the board after the raw beef. Lift it out into a bowl of ice water, then drain and pat dry.
Cook the soba in plenty of boiling water for 4 to 5 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water, rubbing the noodles to remove the starch, and shake them dry.
Pile the noodles into a wide bowl. Top with the beef, cucumber, carrot, edamame and scallion.
Pour over the dressing and toss at the table.
tip: Beef round slices much more easily if it spends 20 minutes in the freezer first.
ingredients: sliced against the grain as thin as you can

name: Thai basil chicken with fried egg, green beans and brown rice
inspiredBy: Thai pad kra pao gai
about: Chopped chicken thigh stir-fried hot and fast with garlic, chilies and a fistful of basil, over rice with a crisp-edged fried egg. A little fish sauce and soy sauce are the salt here, with lime to finish. It makes **two big portions with plenty of protein**.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook enough for two portions in about twice its volume of water, covered, for 35 to 40 minutes, then rest it for 10 minutes.
Pound or finely chop the garlic and chili together into a rough paste. Mix the soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and a splash of water in a small bowl.

Heat two thirds of the oil in a wok or large pan over high heat. Add the garlic and chili paste for 15 seconds, then the chicken, and stir-fry for 3 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains. If your pan is small, cook it in two batches and put it all back together.
Add the green beans and scallion and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then pour in the sauce and toss for a minute. Take it off the heat and stir in the basil until it wilts. Finish with the lime juice.
Heat the rest of the oil in a small pan until shimmering, crack in today's eggs and fry until the edges are lacy and brown and the yolks are firm, flipping the eggs for the last minute.
Serve the chicken over rice with the egg on top. For the second portion, keep the chicken cold and fry the egg fresh tomorrow.
tip: Start the brown rice first, or use a rice cooker. Holy basil is the real thing, but Thai sweet basil is easier to find and works well. Ease off the chili for a milder plate.

name: Red-braised beef with daikon, egg, bok choy and rice
inspiredBy: Chinese hong shao niu rou
about: A weekend pot of lean beef braised slowly with ginger, star anise, cinnamon, reduced-sodium soy sauce and a splash of rice vinegar until it is tender and the sauce is glossy, with daikon, carrot, shiitake and a braised egg that soak up all the flavour. Served over rice with garlicky bok choy. It makes **two big portions**, and tastes even better the next day.
steps: Cover the beef with cold water, bring to a boil and simmer for 3 minutes. Drain and rinse off the grey scum. Boil the eggs for 8 minutes while you wait, cool them in cold water and peel them.
Heat half the oil in a heavy pot, add the ginger, scallion, half the garlic and the star anise and fry for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the sugar and let it melt for 30 seconds.

Add the beef, rice vinegar and soy sauce, turn the meat to coat, then pour in enough hot water to just cover. Add the cinnamon, cover and simmer very gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, then check; if a chunk resists a fork, give it 15 more.

Add the daikon, carrot, shiitake and eggs, cover and simmer for 30 minutes more, until the beef is tender and the sauce clings to the spoon. Uncover and boil for the last few minutes if it is too thin.

Meanwhile, cook the rice with a little more than its own volume of water, covered, for about 18 minutes. Stir-fry the bok choy in the rest of the oil with the last garlic for 2 minutes, with a splash of water.
Serve the beef, daikon and an egg over rice, with the bok choy. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: A pressure cooker does the beef in 40 minutes, and a cinnamon stick beats ground. The braise freezes well in its sauce for up to 3 months.

name: Ginger-scallion steamed salmon with silky tofu, bok choy and brown rice
inspiredBy: Cantonese steamed fish with ginger and scallion
about: A salmon fillet steamed over tofu with slivers of ginger and scallion, then finished with a spoonful of hot oil and a splash of soy sauce. It is the quickest of Chinese home dinners and keeps the fish silky. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the bok choy is steamed right on top.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in about twice its volume of water, covered, for 35 to 40 minutes, then rest it for 10 minutes.
Lay the tofu slices on a heatproof plate, set the salmon on top and scatter over half the ginger and half the scallion.
Steam the plate over boiling water, covered, for 8 to 10 minutes, until the salmon is just opaque and flakes. Put the bok choy in a steamer basket above the fish for the last 4 minutes.
Pour off the liquid from the plate. Top the fish with the rest of the ginger and scallion, the chili and the cilantro.

Heat the canola and sesame oils in a small pan until they shimmer and pour them over the scallion, so they sizzle. Stir the soy sauce and rice vinegar together, spoon it over the fish and serve with the bok choy and rice.
tip: Start the brown rice first, or use a rice cooker. No steamer? A lidded pan with a rack, or a plate set on three balls of foil, works. Sea bass or cod steams the same way.

name: Edamame with lime, chili and a pinch of salt
inspiredBy: Japanese izakaya edamame
about: A bowl of warm edamame tossed with lime, a pinch of chili flakes and a little salt. It is simple, salty-sharp and hard to stop eating. A bowl gives you **a solid serving of protein and fibre**.
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the edamame for 4 minutes, or steam them. Drain.
Toss while hot with the salt, lime juice, chili flakes and sesame seeds, and eat warm or cold.
tip: Frozen shelled edamame goes straight into the water. Pods work too, but the weight on the list is for the shelled beans.

name: Soy-braised eggs with star anise and cucumber
inspiredBy: Chinese tea eggs (cha ye dan), without the tea
about: Boiled eggs cracked and steeped in a fragrant soy, star anise and cinnamon bath until the whites are lightly marbled and savoury. Cool cucumber with a little rice vinegar keeps them fresh. The eggs bring **protein and choline**.
steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool under cold water and tap them all over with the back of a spoon to crack the shells without peeling.

Simmer the soy sauce, star anise, cinnamon and ginger with just enough water to come halfway up the eggs for 5 minutes. Add the cracked eggs, cover and simmer gently for 10 minutes, turning once, then turn off the heat and steep for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Peel the eggs. Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar and sesame seeds, and serve alongside.
tip: Start them the night before so they steep overnight; they keep 3 days in their liquid in the fridge. A black tea bag in the pot makes them proper tea eggs.

name: Thick yogurt with mango, lime and toasted sesame
inspiredBy: Vietnamese sua chua trai cay
about: Thick, tangy yogurt with ripe mango, a squeeze of lime and a scatter of toasted sesame seeds. It tastes like a Vietnamese dessert but holds **a big serving of protein**. Frozen mango works just as well as fresh.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and stir in the lime juice.
Top with the mango and the toasted sesame seeds.
tip: Thaw frozen mango in the fridge overnight.

name: Hiyayakko, chilled tofu with ginger, scallion and edamame
inspiredBy: Japanese hiyayakko
about: A big slab of chilled tofu dressed with grated ginger, scallion, sesame seeds and a few drops of soy sauce and sesame oil, with a handful of edamame for bite. It is cold, silky and savoury. A plate gives you **a solid serving of protein**.
steps: Drain the tofu on a towel for 5 minutes and slide it onto a plate.
Top with the ginger, scallion and edamame, drizzle with the soy sauce and sesame oil, and scatter on the sesame seeds.
tip: A squeeze of lime or a dab of wasabi works in place of the ginger.

name: Chicken and scallion yakitori skewers with daikon
inspiredBy: Japanese negima yakitori
about: Bite-sized chicken thigh and scallion skewers, grilled until charred and brushed with a light tare of soy sauce, a little sugar and ginger, with crisp daikon and a squeeze of lime. They are quick to cook, good cold and **properly high in protein**.
steps: Bring the soy sauce, sugar, ginger and a spoonful of water to a bubble in a small pan and cook for 30 seconds to a minute, until it turns slightly syrupy. It is only a few spoonfuls, so watch it.
Thread the chicken and scallion pieces alternately onto skewers (soak wooden ones for 20 minutes) and brush with the oil.
Grill or broil on high for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, and brushing with the tare in the last few minutes, until cooked through and charred in spots.
Toss the daikon with the rice vinegar. Squeeze the lime over the skewers and serve with the daikon.
tip: Grill a double batch for the two days they appear. They are good cold or gently reheated.

name: Poached shrimp with mango, cucumber and nuoc cham
inspiredBy: Vietnamese tom luoc, poached shrimp with nuoc cham
about: Plump poached shrimp with sweet mango, cool cucumber and a bright dipping sauce of lime, fish sauce, garlic and chili. It is fresh, fast and light but carries **a good serving of protein**.
steps: Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, garlic and chili with a spoonful of warm water until the sugar dissolves.
Drop the shrimp into boiling water for 2 minutes, until pink and curled. Cool them in cold water and drain.
Arrange the shrimp, mango, cucumber and carrot on a plate, scatter on the cilantro, and spoon over the sauce.
tip: Poach the shrimp the night before and they are cold and ready.

name: Canned mackerel onigiri with ginger and scallion
inspiredBy: Japanese saba soboro onigiri
about: Two rice balls filled with canned mackerel cooked down with ginger and soy sauce into savoury flakes, wrapped in nori. A quick, salty-sharp snack that carries **omega-3 and vitamin D** and turns pantry fish into a proper bite before or after training.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it with a little more than its own volume of water, covered, for about 18 minutes, then cool it for 10 minutes.
Warm the mackerel in a dry pan with the ginger and soy sauce, breaking it up with a fork, until it is dry and crumbly, about 3 minutes. Stir in the scallion.
Wet your hands, press the rice around a spoonful of the filling into two triangles, roll in the sesame seeds and wrap in nori.
tip: Cook a double batch of rice the night before and cool it fast; it keeps 3 days in the fridge. Warm it until soft before shaping, since cold rice will not hold together. Canned sardines work too.
ingredients: canned Atlantic mackerel, not king mackerel; drained

name: Tamagoyaki rolled omelette with grated daikon
inspiredBy: Japanese tamagoyaki
about: A rolled Japanese omelette, lightly sweetened with a pinch of sugar and seasoned with soy sauce and scallion, with a little pile of grated daikon. Soft, savoury and quick. It brings **protein and choline** without any bread, and the extra whites keep it light.
steps: Beat the eggs and egg whites with the sugar, soy sauce and scallion.
Brush a small nonstick pan with a little of the oil over medium-low heat. Pour in a thin layer of egg, and when it is almost set roll it up to one side.
Oil the pan again, pour in more egg under and around the roll, and roll again. Repeat until the egg is used up.
Rest the omelette for a minute, slice it into thick pieces and serve with the grated daikon.
tip: Squeeze the grated daikon lightly and add a drop of soy sauce.

name: Cold sesame-ginger chicken with cucumber
inspiredBy: Sichuan bang bang chicken, lightened
about: Tender poached chicken thigh shredded over cool cucumber with a sesame, ginger, rice vinegar and chili dressing. It is a Sichuan cold dish made lighter, good straight from the fridge. It brings **plenty of protein** with almost no effort.
steps: Simmer the chicken with the sliced ginger and half the scallion in barely bubbling water for 12 to 15 minutes, until cooked through. Cool it in its liquid, then shred it by hand.
Grind the sesame seeds to a rough paste. Stir in the grated ginger, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, chili and a spoonful of the poaching liquid.
Pile the cucumber on a plate, top with the chicken and the rest of the scallion, and spoon over the dressing.
tip: Poach the chicken the night before and it only needs shredding. Keep the dressing separate until serving.

name: Ginger-lime mackerel with cucumber and scallion
inspiredBy: Japanese saba-kan, canned mackerel dressed at the table
about: Flaked canned mackerel dressed with fresh ginger, lime, chili and scallion over cool cucumber with toasted sesame. It takes five minutes and tastes bright and clean. Canned mackerel is a cheap source of **omega-3, vitamin D and plenty of protein**.
steps: Flake the mackerel into a bowl and mix with the ginger, lime juice, chili, scallion and soy sauce.
Pile the cucumber on a plate, spoon the mackerel over and scatter on the sesame seeds.
tip: Eat it with a few rice crackers or spoon it over a small scoop of leftover rice.
ingredients: canned Atlantic mackerel, not king mackerel; drained

name: Overnight skyr oats with blueberries and walnuts
about: Thick, creamy overnight oats made with skyr, so a jar is more like a custard than a porridge. Blueberries bring brightness and walnuts bring crunch. The skyr gives you **a real protein head start** before the day has begun.
steps: Stir the oats, skyr, cinnamon and a good splash of water together in a jar or bowl until smooth and thick.
Fold in half the blueberries, cover and chill overnight, or at least 4 hours.
In the morning, loosen with a splash of water or milk if it has set too firm, then top with the rest of the blueberries, the chopped walnuts and a thin drizzle of maple syrup.
tip: Mix a jar the night before. They keep 3 days, so you can mix Monday's on Sunday night, then Thursday's and Saturday's together on Wednesday night.

name: Creamy cottage cheese scramble with spinach, tomato and toast
about: Eggs and egg whites scrambled with a scoop of cottage cheese turn out creamy and extra filling, with wilted spinach, sweet cherry tomatoes and a little cheddar on toast. It takes 10 minutes and gives you **a big hit of protein** with plenty of vitamin K and folate.
steps: Put the bread in the toaster. Warm the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Cook the cherry tomatoes until they just start to burst, about 2 minutes, then add the spinach and cook until the pan is nearly dry.

Beat the eggs and egg whites with the pepper and salt, pour them in and stir slowly with a spatula until set firm with no runny egg left. Take the pan off the heat and fold in the cottage cheese so it stays creamy.
Scatter over the grated cheddar and sliced scallion, and serve on the toast.
tip: Carton egg whites work well here.

name: Blueberry walnut cottage cheese bowl with toasted oats
about: Cool, creamy cottage cheese with blueberries, a little maple syrup and a toasted oat and walnut crunch, like a quick granola bowl. It is sweet, tangy and ready in minutes, and the cottage cheese gives you **a slow-digesting protein** to carry you through the morning.
steps: Toast the oats and chopped walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes. Shake the pan so they do not catch.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and pile on the blueberries.
Scatter over the toasted oats and walnuts, drizzle with the maple syrup and finish with a pinch of cinnamon.

name: Tuscan tuna and white bean salad with garlic toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan tonno e fagioli
about: A classic Tuscan pairing: tender white beans, flaked tuna, baby spinach and sweet tomatoes in a lemony olive oil dressing, with garlic-rubbed toast on the side. It needs no cooking and is **packed with protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Slice the red onion very thin and let it sit in the lemon juice while you get everything else ready. It softens and loses its bite.
Drain and rinse the beans and tip them into a bowl with the olive oil, halved tomatoes, diced avocado, chopped parsley, pepper and the salt, then season to taste.
Drain the tuna, flake it in with the onion and its lemony juices, and fold everything together gently.
Toast the bread and rub it with the cut side of the garlic clove. Serve the salad over the spinach with the toast on the side.

name: Chicken and egg rice bowl with spinach and scallion
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese oyakodon, with chicken breast and a little maple syrup for the sweetness
about: A quick, savoury Japanese-style donburi: chicken and onion simmered in a gingery soy broth, set with firm, fluffy egg and piled over rice with wilted spinach. It is cosy and fast, and the chicken and egg together give you **plenty of protein** in one bowl.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in a covered pot with about one and a half times its volume of water until tender, about 15 minutes. Start this first.

Slice the onion thin and the chicken into thin strips. Stir the soy sauce, maple syrup, grated ginger and about 1/3 cup (80 mL) of water, a little more at bigger sizes, together in a wide frying pan with a lid and bring it to a simmer.
Add the onion and chicken and cook gently for about 6 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the onion is soft.
Add the spinach and let it wilt. Beat the eggs and egg whites lightly and pour them over in a thin stream, then cover and cook for about a minute, until the egg is set firm with no runny egg left.
Spoon the rice into a bowl, slide the chicken and egg on top with all the juices, and finish with the sliced scallion.
tip: Cook the rice a night ahead and the bowl takes 15 minutes.

name: Turkey, black bean and egg brunch burritos
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Tex-Mex breakfast burrito, with spiced ground turkey in place of sausage
about: Smoky, spiced ground turkey with black beans, spinach and fluffy scrambled eggs, rolled into warm flour tortillas with a little melted cheddar. It is a proper weekend brunch with **eggs, turkey and beans in every bite**, and it goes together in about 25 minutes.
steps: Warm the tortillas wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave, then keep them covered.
Soften the finely chopped onion in the oil for 3 minutes. Add the turkey, smoked paprika and cumin and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it smells toasty.
Stir in the black beans, halved tomatoes and spinach and cook until the spinach wilts.
Pour in the beaten eggs and egg whites and stir gently until set firm with no runny egg left.

Fill two small tortillas loosely with the eggs, cheddar, cilantro and sliced avocado, fold in the sides and roll up. Spoon any extra filling beside them. For a crisp outside, toast the burritos seam-side down in the pan for a minute or two.
tip: To get ahead, cook a double batch of the turkey and bean filling and freeze half. Add the eggs, cheddar and avocado fresh.

name: Chicken tinga rice bowls with black beans and avocado
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican tinga de pollo
about: Shredded chicken simmered in smoky chipotle tomato sauce, served over rice and black beans with creamy avocado and lime. It is smoky, a little spicy and tangy, and it **makes two portions**, so tomorrow's lunch is ready. The chicken and beans together carry a big protein load.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in a covered pot with about one and a half times its volume of water until tender, about 15 minutes. Cook enough for both portions.
Meanwhile, simmer the chicken breasts in lightly salted water for 15 to 18 minutes, until cooked through. Lift out and shred with two forks. Keep a mug of the poaching water.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil for about 6 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and stir for a minute.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes and finely chopped chipotle with a spoonful of its sauce. Simmer for 8 minutes, until thick, then stir in the chicken with a good splash of the poaching water, more at bigger sizes, so the sauce stays saucy.
Warm the black beans in a small pan. Build bowls with rice, beans and tinga, then top with sliced avocado, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
Pack the second portion, kept separate from the avocado, for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Reheat day 2 with a splash of water.

name: Maple Dijon sockeye salmon with roasted sweet potatoes and garlic spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by West Coast maple-glazed salmon
about: Sockeye is the deep red salmon of the Pacific coast, lean and full-flavoured, and it loves a sweet and tangy maple Dijon glaze. Caramelized roasted sweet potatoes and garlicky spinach make it a full plate. It is a great source of **omega-3 and vitamin D**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the sweet potatoes with half the olive oil and a pinch of the salt, and roast on a tray for about 25 minutes.
Whisk the Dijon, maple syrup, lemon juice and pepper together.

Push the sweet potatoes over, add the salmon to the tray, season it with the rest of the salt, brush it with the glaze and roast for 8 to 10 minutes, until it just flakes. Sockeye is lean, so do not overcook it.
Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a pan with the sliced garlic until it smells sweet, then add the spinach and cook for about 2 minutes, until wilted.
Scatter the parsley over everything and squeeze over any leftover lemon.

name: Lean beef and kidney bean chili over a baked sweet potato
inspiredBy: Inspired by American beef and bean chili
about: A thick, smoky chili with lean beef, kidney beans and sweet red pepper, spooned over a split baked sweet potato with a squeeze of lime. It is the kind of bowl that **makes a perfect next-day lunch**, because the flavour deepens overnight. Beans and beef give you iron, zinc and fibre in one pot, and the sweet potato adds vitamin A.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Prick the sweet potatoes and bake them for 45 to 50 minutes, until soft all the way through.
Warm the oil in a heavy pot and soften the chopped onion, grated carrot and pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for a minute.
Add the beef and break it up, cooking until no pink remains. Stir in the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano for a minute so they bloom in the fat.
Add the crushed tomatoes and a splash of water, then the beans. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until thick, and season with the salt.
Split the sweet potatoes, spoon the chili over and finish with cilantro and lime. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Microwave the sweet potatoes for 8 minutes, then crisp them in the oven for 10.

name: Turkey and white bean ragù with rigatoni
inspiredBy: Inspired by Bolognese ragù
about: A simmered Italian-style ragù made with very lean turkey and creamy white beans, with finely chopped carrot and onion and plenty of garlic. Tossed with chewy rigatoni and finished with parmesan and parsley, it is real comfort food with **a big dose of protein and fibre** on every plate.
steps: Finely chop the carrot and onion. Soften them in the olive oil over medium heat for about 8 minutes, until sweet and golden. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Add the turkey, let it sit for 3 to 4 minutes so it browns, then break it up and cook until no pink remains. Stir in the fennel seed and oregano and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes, the beans and a splash of water. Simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring now and then and crushing a few of the beans against the side, until thick and glossy.
Boil enough rigatoni for both portions in salted water until just al dente, reserving a cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the pasta with the ragù, loosening with a splash of the pasta water, and finish with the grated parmesan and chopped parsley.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Reheat the leftover with a splash of water or pasta water.

name: Ginger soy salmon rice bowl with spinach and quick pickles
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese salmon teriyaki, with little sugar
about: Pan-seared salmon glazed with ginger and soy, over rice with wilted spinach and cucumber and carrot pickled in rice vinegar. Savoury, sharp and rich in all the right places, it is a Friday-night bowl with **omega-3 and plenty of protein**.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it in a covered pot with about one and a half times its volume of water until tender, about 15 minutes, then keep it warm.
Slice the cucumber and carrot very thin and toss with the rice vinegar, a pinch of salt and a pinch of ginger. Leave them for 10 minutes, then squeeze them dry.

Mix the soy sauce, maple syrup and the rest of the finely grated ginger. Sear the salmon in a hot non-stick pan for 3 minutes, flip, then pour in the glaze off the heat, return the pan and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, spooning it over and watching it so it does not scorch, until the fish just flakes.
Wilt the spinach in the same pan with a splash of water and a drop of soy sauce, about 1 minute.
Build bowls with rice, salmon, spinach, sliced avocado and the pickles, and scatter with sliced scallion.

name: Chicken souvlaki wraps with lemon potatoes and skyr tzatziki
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek souvlaki
about: Lemony, garlicky chicken skewers with oregano, roasted lemon potatoes, a cool cucumber tzatziki made with skyr, and warm wraps. It is a relaxed weekend cook, and the second portion makes **a very good wrap** the next day.
steps: Cut the chicken into chunks. Mix half the lemon juice with half the oil, half the garlic and the oregano, and toss the chicken in it. Marinate for 1 to 4 hours, no longer.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Cut the potatoes into wedges, toss with the rest of the oil, lemon juice and a little salt, and roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until golden at the edges.
For the tzatziki, grate the cucumber and squeeze out the water. Stir it into the skyr with the rest of the garlic, chopped parsley and a pinch of salt.
Thread the chicken on skewers and grill or broil for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Halve the tomatoes and slice the red onion for a quick salad. Warm the wraps and fill them with chicken, tzatziki and salad, with the potatoes on the side.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch, with the tzatziki kept separate. Eat it cold, sliced into the wrap, or warm it for 30 seconds.

name: Lean beef cottage pie with olive oil mash, spinach and carrots
inspiredBy: Inspired by British cottage pie and Québec pâté chinois
about: A proper weekend comfort dish: lean beef, carrots, red pepper, kidney beans and spinach in a rich tomato gravy, under a golden olive oil mash with no butter or cream needed. It is hearty, deeply savoury and **packed with iron, zinc and protein**.
steps: Peel the potatoes if you like, cut them into chunks and boil in water until a knife slips in easily, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm half the olive oil in a wide pan and soften the chopped onion, diced carrot and pepper for about 8 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme for the last minute.

Add the beef and break it up, cooking until no pink remains. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, the beans and a splash of water and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick, and season with two thirds of the salt. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then tip the filling into a baking dish.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with the rest of the olive oil, the pepper, the rest of the salt and a splash of the cooking water until smooth and creamy.
Heat the broiler. Spoon the mash over the filling in the baking dish, rough it up with a fork so the peaks catch, and broil for 5 to 8 minutes, until golden at the edges.
tip: Double it and freeze the second pie. It reheats well in the oven.

name: Blueberry maple skyr with walnuts
about: Thick skyr with blueberries, a drizzle of maple syrup and a few crunchy walnuts. It is cool, a little sweet and **a serious protein hit** for a few minutes of effort.
steps: Spoon the skyr into a bowl and top with the blueberries, chopped walnuts and maple syrup.

name: Spinach and cheddar egg white cups
about: Little baked egg cups made mostly with egg whites, spinach, tomato and a bit of sharp cheddar. They are fluffy, savoury and **very lean protein**, and they reheat in the microwave in under a minute.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and use a silicone muffin tin or line a few cups with parchment cases.
Beat the egg whites and egg with the pepper and salt, and season to taste. Divide the chopped spinach, tomatoes and scallion between the cups, pour in the eggs and top with the cheddar.
Bake for about 15 minutes, until puffed and set in the middle.
tip: Bake a fresh tin on Wednesday night for Thursday, and another on Saturday for Sunday.

name: Tuna and white bean toast with cucumber
about: Crisp toast piled with a lemony Dijon tuna and white bean mash and cool cucumber slices. It is light, crunchy and gives you **protein and fibre** for few calories.
steps: Toast the bread. Mash the tuna and beans together with the lemon juice, Dijon, pepper and salt, and season to taste.
Spread over the toast and top with thin cucumber slices.

name: Cottage cheese, tomato and parsley toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian bruschetta
about: Creamy cottage cheese on toast with sweet cherry tomatoes, fresh parsley and a thread of olive oil, like a bruschetta that actually fills you up. It brings **a good dose of protein**.
steps: Toast the bread and rub it with the cut side of the garlic. Halve the tomatoes and toss with the olive oil, chopped parsley and pepper.
Spread the cottage cheese on the toast and pile the tomatoes on top. At bigger sizes, serve the cottage cheese in a bowl with the toast on the side.

name: Skyr herb dip with crunchy vegetables
about: A cool, garlicky dip of skyr, lemon and parsley with carrot, cucumber and sweet pepper sticks. It is crisp and fresh, and **very high in protein for the calories**.
steps: Stir the skyr with the lemon juice, chopped parsley, finely grated garlic and the salt, and season to taste.
Cut the carrot, cucumber and pepper into sticks and serve with the dip.

name: Lemon Dijon chicken salad cucumber boats
about: Shredded poached chicken folded with Dijon, lemon, olive oil and parsley, spooned into crisp cucumber halves. It is fresh and zingy, and **lean protein with almost no starch**.
steps: Simmer the chicken in lightly salted water for 12 to 15 minutes, until cooked through. Cool a little and shred.
Stir the Dijon, lemon juice, olive oil and chopped parsley together and fold in the chicken.
Halve the cucumber lengthwise, scoop out the seeds with a spoon and fill the hollows with the chicken salad.
tip: Poach the chicken when you cook dinner and the snack takes 5 minutes.

name: Mini turkey meatballs with tomato dip
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian polpette
about: Little baked meatballs of lean turkey with parmesan, parsley and garlic, served with warm crushed tomato for dipping. They are tender, savoury and **a lean protein snack that reheats well**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Soak the oats in half the crushed tomato for 5 minutes, then mix in the turkey, parmesan, chopped parsley, finely grated garlic, oregano and salt, and roll into small balls.
Bake on a lined tray for 12 to 14 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Warm the rest of the crushed tomato with the olive oil in a small pan and serve alongside for dipping.
tip: Ground turkey breast (99% lean) or extra lean ground turkey both work. Bake a double batch and they keep for 4 days.

name: Black bean and cheddar tortilla wedges with fresh tomato salsa
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican quesadillas
about: Crisp pan-toasted tortilla folded around black beans and melted cheddar, cut into wedges and served with a quick lime and cilantro tomato salsa. It is **a filling snack with protein and fibre**.
steps: Mash the beans roughly with a fork. Spread them over one half of the tortilla (at bigger sizes use a large tortilla, or two small ones), scatter over the cheddar and fold it over.
Toast in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes a side, until golden and the cheese has melted. Cut into wedges.
Chop the tomatoes and toss with the lime juice and cilantro for a quick salsa to spoon over.

name: Mexican shrimp cocktail with lime and avocado
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican coctel de camarón
about: Chilled poached shrimp with tomato, cucumber, red onion, lime and cilantro, in the style of a coctel de camarón. It is bright and refreshing and **one of the leanest protein snacks there is**.
steps: Simmer the shrimp in lightly salted water for 2 to 3 minutes, until pink and curled. Drain, rinse in cold water and chill.
Dice the tomatoes, cucumber and red onion and toss with the lime juice, cilantro and a pinch of salt.
Fold in the shrimp so it picks up all the lime and tomato juices in the bowl, then top with diced avocado.

name: Huevos rancheros with pinto beans and avocado
inspiredBy: Mexican huevos rancheros
about: Fried eggs on warm corn tortillas, under a spicy tomato and jalapeño sauce, with garlicky mashed pinto beans, a little crumbled queso fresco and slices of avocado. The eggs and beans together bring **plenty of protein and fibre** to the first meal of the day.
steps: Warm half the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, jalapeño and half the garlic for 3 minutes until soft and fragrant.

Stir in the cumin, then the tomato with a splash of water. Simmer 8 minutes, pressing it down with a spoon, until it thickens into a spoonable sauce. Season with part of the salt and half the lime juice.
Meanwhile, warm the pinto beans in a small pot with the rest of the garlic and a splash of water, mashing them roughly until creamy. Season with a pinch of salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan until they have a few toasty spots, then lay them on the plate.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a nonstick pan until the whites are set and the yolks are firm, flipping them for the last minute.

Spoon the beans onto the tortillas, set the eggs on top, and ladle the sauce over the whites. Taste the sauce and beans and add a pinch more salt if they need it. Stir the rest of the lime juice into the yogurt, and finish with a spoonful of that crema, the avocado, queso fresco and cilantro.
tip: Make the sauce on Sunday and it keeps four days in the fridge, so breakfast takes about 10 minutes.

name: Huevos pericos with a cheese arepa and beans
inspiredBy: Colombian huevos pericos and arepa con queso
about: Colombia's morning scramble with tomato and onion (the colours of the parrot, perico), served with a griddled corn arepa stuffed with a little queso fresco and a spoonful of warm beans. Extra egg whites keep the plate **high in protein** without making it heavy.
steps: Stir the corn flour with a pinch of the salt and enough warm water to make a soft, smooth dough. Rest it 5 minutes, then shape into a thick patty and press the queso fresco into the middle, closing the dough around it.
Cook the arepa in a lightly oiled nonstick skillet over medium heat, about 5 minutes a side, until golden outside and firm when tapped.

Warm a little oil in a pan and cook the onion, garlic and tomato with the cumin for 4 minutes, until the tomato is soft and saucy. Spoon a quarter of it into a small pot with the pinto beans and a splash of water and warm through.
Beat the whole eggs with the egg whites and a pinch of salt, pour them into the tomato pan and stir gently over medium-low heat until just set and creamy, about 2 minutes.
Season the beans and eggs to taste, then serve the eggs beside the arepa and the beans.
tip: On a weekday, griddle the arepa the night before and warm it in a dry pan while the eggs cook, so breakfast is quick. Split it and pile the eggs inside to eat on the go.

name: Yogurt bowl with mango, toasted oats and pepitas
inspiredBy: a tropical-fruit yogurt breakfast, with Brazilian and Mexican touches
about: Thick yogurt with ripe mango and lime, topped with oats toasted in a dry pan and a spoonful of toasted pepitas. The yogurt does the heavy lifting here: a big bowl of it carries **more than 25 g of protein** before you add the oats and seeds.
steps: Toast the oats and pepitas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until they smell nutty. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the mango. Squeeze over the lime juice, which brings out the mango's sweetness.
Scatter on the toasted oats and pepitas and finish with a pinch of cinnamon.
tip: Toast a big batch of oats and pepitas on Sunday and keep them in a jar. At larger sizes use a deep bowl.

name: Turkey burrito bowl with black beans and lime rice
inspiredBy: the Tex-Mex burrito bowl
about: Taco-spiced turkey over lime-cilantro rice with black beans, charred corn, crunchy cucumber, tomato, avocado and a spoonful of chipotle crema. It is a Tex-Mex lunch bowl, built to be big: **lean turkey and beans** carry the protein and the rice carries your training.
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook it in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt for about 15 minutes, until tender. Fluff it with half the lime juice and half the cilantro.
Warm the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 2 minutes, then add the turkey and break it up as it browns, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, oregano and the rest of the salt with a splash of water, and cook 2 more minutes until the turkey is coated and a little saucy.
Warm the black beans in a small pot, and char the corn in a hot dry pan for 3 to 4 minutes until it has brown spots.
Stir the yogurt with the chipotle, a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt to make the crema.
Build the bowls with rice, turkey, beans, corn, cucumber, tomato and avocado. Spoon on the crema and the rest of the cilantro.
tip: Cook a double batch of rice and turkey on Monday and chill half in a covered container. Thursday's bowl then takes 5 minutes; cooked rice and meat keep 3 days in the fridge.

name: Lomo saltado with crisp potatoes and rice
inspiredBy: Peruvian lomo saltado
about: Peru's famous stir-fry, born where Chinese and Peruvian cooking meet: strips of beef seared hot with red onion and tomato, splashed with soy sauce and vinegar and tossed with golden potatoes, served over rice. Lean sirloin and a mound of potatoes make it **high in protein and in training carbs**. It makes two portions.
steps: Cover the potato wedges with cold water in a pot, bring to a boil and simmer 8 minutes until just tender. Drain well and let them steam dry.
Cook the rice in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water for about 15 minutes, until tender.

Toss the beef with the garlic, cumin, pepper and the soy sauce. Heat half the oil in a large skillet over high heat and crisp the potatoes until golden, 6 to 8 minutes, in two batches if they crowd the pan. Set them aside on a plate.

Add the remaining oil to the very hot pan and sear the beef in a single layer, in batches, for 1 to 2 minutes, until browned but still pink inside. A crowded pan steams the beef instead of searing it.
Add the onion and tomato wedges and toss over high heat for 2 minutes, so they stay a little firm. Stir in the ají amarillo paste, the vinegar and the salt.
Fold the potatoes back in, scatter on the cilantro and serve over the rice. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: For a crisper potato, reheat leftovers in a hot dry pan, not the microwave.

name: Peruvian green arroz con pollo with corn
inspiredBy: Peruvian arroz con pollo
about: Chicken and rice cooked in a blended cilantro and ají sauce until the grains turn vivid green and fragrant, with sweet corn and red pepper stirred in. It is a pot you make once and reheat well, with **lean chicken breast** for protein and the rice for energy. It makes two portions.
steps: Blend the cilantro and ají amarillo paste with water, a few spoonfuls at a time, until smooth, pourable and bright green, about a third of a cup at Standard and Big and a little more at XL.
Warm the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes. Lift it onto a plate.
In the same pot, cook the onion, garlic, cumin and oregano for 4 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the green purée and cook 3 minutes, until it darkens and smells herby.

Add the rice, red pepper and salt with a little under twice the rice's volume of water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, then nestle the chicken back in, scatter the corn on top and cover again.
Cook 10 minutes more, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through, then rest off the heat for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and finish with the lime juice.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Reheat leftovers with a splash of water so the chicken stays moist.

name: Trout ceviche with sweet potato, corn and toasted corn
inspiredBy: Peruvian ceviche de trucha, as it is made around Lake Titicaca, with camote and choclo
about: Fresh trout cured briefly in lime juice with red onion, chili and cilantro, served the Peruvian way with boiled sweet potato and sweet corn, and a handful of pan-toasted corn for a nutty bite. Trout is a **fatty fish rich in omega-3**, and the sweet potato brings the carbs.
steps: Rinse the onion slices in cold water for a minute, then drain; this softens their bite and keeps them crisp.

Cover the sweet potato with water, bring to a boil and cook about 12 minutes until tender but not mushy. Lift it out with a slotted spoon, then simmer most of the corn in the same water for 4 minutes and drain.
Pat the rest of the corn very dry and toast it in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking the pan, until golden and nutty in spots, 6 to 8 minutes. It will be chewy rather than crunchy.

Stir the lime juice with the ají amarillo paste, garlic and salt. Toss the trout with this leche de tigre and the onion, and leave it for 3 to 5 minutes, until the edges just turn opaque and the centre is still glossy.
Fold in the cilantro. Serve the ceviche right away with its juices, the warm sweet potato and boiled corn alongside, and the toasted corn on top.
tip: Ask your fishmonger for trout that is safe to eat raw, and keep it cold until you cut it. If you are pregnant or have a weakened immune system, skip the raw version: cook the trout cubes in a hot pan until opaque all the way through, 3 to 4 minutes, then dress them. Ceviche is always made fresh and is not a leftover.
ingredients: safe to eat raw, skinned and cut into 2 cm cubes
peeled and cut into thick rounds

name: Arroz, feijão and grilled lime chicken with collards and vinagrete
inspiredBy: Brazilian prato feito
about: The everyday Brazilian plate: garlicky grilled chicken, white rice, pinto beans simmered with onion and bay, quick sautéed collards (couve) and a fresh tomato vinagrete, with orange slices to finish. It is **big on protein**, and the orange's vitamin C helps your body absorb the iron from the beans and collards. It makes two portions.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the lime juice, half the garlic, the paprika and a pinch of salt for 15 minutes while you start the rice.
Cook the rice with a little under twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt in a covered pot, about 15 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Warm a third of the oil in a pot and cook half the onion and the remaining garlic for 3 minutes. Add the beans, bay leaf and enough water to just cover them, and simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side to thicken the broth. Season with a pinch of salt.
Stir the tomato, the remaining raw onion, the cilantro and the vinegar with a pinch of salt for the vinagrete.
Sear the chicken in the second third of the oil in a very hot pan, in batches if it crowds, for 4 to 5 minutes a side, until browned and cooked through. Rest it for 3 minutes, then slice.
Cook the collards in the last third of the oil in a wide pan over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Plate the rice, beans, chicken, collards and vinagrete with orange slices on the side. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Slice the chicken before packing the leftover so it reheats evenly.
ingredients: butterflied or sliced into thin cutlets
stems removed, sliced into thin ribbons

name: Cuban picadillo with black beans, rice and sweet plantain
inspiredBy: Cuban picadillo a la habanera
about: Lean beef simmered in a sofrito of onion, sweet pepper and garlic with tomato, olives and a splash of vinegar, with black beans stirred in and spooned over rice with sweet fried plantain. The plantain and beans bring the **energy for training**, and the beef the protein. It makes two portions.
steps: Cook the rice in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt, about 15 minutes.
Warm two thirds of the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, pepper and garlic with the cumin and oregano for 6 minutes, until soft and sweet. This is the sofrito.
Add the beef and break it up, cooking 6 minutes until no longer pink. Stir in the tomato, bay leaf, vinegar, a splash of water and the rest of the salt, and simmer 12 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the black beans and the olives and simmer 3 minutes more.
Fry the plantain in the remaining oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until deeply golden and caramelized at the edges.
Serve the picadillo over the rice with the plantain alongside. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Add a spoonful of raisins with the olives if you like the sweet and salty Cuban way.

name: Lighter feijoada with chicken thighs, black beans, collards and orange
inspiredBy: Brazilian feijoada completa, lightened
about: Brazil's Saturday pot, lightened: skinless chicken thighs simmered until tender, then black beans, garlic, bay and a little chicken linguiça for smoke, served over rice with sautéed collards and orange slices. It is a **weekend project** that fills the house with its smell and makes two portions, one for Sunday's lunch.
steps: Put the chicken in a heavy pot with the bay leaf, a pinch of the salt and enough water to cover by 5 cm. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam, then turn it down to a few lazy bubbles, partly cover and cook for 30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and 74 °C (165 °F) inside. A hard boil makes it stringy.
In a skillet, warm half the oil and cook the onion and garlic with the smoked paprika for 6 minutes until golden and sweet.

Stir the sofrito, the black beans and the linguiça slices into the pot. Simmer, uncovered, 20 minutes, until the broth is thick and glossy. Mash a ladleful of beans against the side of the pot to thicken it more, and season with the rest of the salt.
Cook the rice in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water, about 15 minutes.
Sauté the collards in the remaining oil in a wide pan over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until bright green.

Serve the feijoada over rice, with the collards and orange slices, which cut the richness. Wash your hands and board after the raw chicken. Pack the second portion into a shallow container for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat it to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: A pressure cooker does the chicken in 10 minutes at high pressure. Release it, add the sofrito, beans and linguiça, and simmer 15 minutes, uncovered.
ingredients: stems removed, sliced into thin ribbons

name: Salmon moqueca with coconut, tomato and rice
inspiredBy: Brazilian moqueca baiana, with colorau in place of dendê oil
about: A Bahian-style fish stew: salmon simmered gently with tomato, peppers, onion, cilantro and a little coconut milk, golden with urucum, and spooned over fluffy rice. Salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the coconut milk is just a splash, enough for silkiness without much saturated fat.
steps: Marinate the salmon with the lime juice, half the garlic and a pinch of the salt while you start the rice.
Rinse the rice, then cook it in a covered pot with a little under twice its volume of water and a pinch of salt for about 15 minutes, until tender.
Warm the oil in a wide, shallow pan. Layer in half the onion, tomato and red pepper, then the salmon, then the rest of the vegetables. Scatter on the remaining garlic and the colorau.

Pour the coconut milk, loosened with a splash of water, around the edges. Cover and simmer gently for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes and the sauce has thickened. Do not stir; spoon the liquid over the fish instead.
Season with the remaining salt, scatter on the cilantro and serve over the rice, with plenty of sauce.
tip: In Bahia, moqueca comes with rice and pirão, the broth thickened with cassava flour. If you have some, whisk a spoonful into a ladle of the sauce and simmer for a minute.
ingredients: skin removed, cut into large chunks

name: Chile-lime boiled eggs with cucumber
inspiredBy: Mexican street snacks of cucumber with chile and lime
about: Boiled eggs with crunchy cucumber sticks, dressed the Mexican street way with lime, chili and salt. The eggs give you **high-quality protein and choline**, and the crunch makes it feel like a snack.
steps: Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and cook 9 minutes. Cool them under cold water, peel and halve.
Toss the cucumber with the lime juice, chili and half the salt.
Sprinkle the remaining salt over the eggs and serve them with the cucumber.
tip: Boil a batch of eggs on Sunday; they keep five days in the shell.

name: Chicken tostadas with cucumber, lime and chipotle crema
inspiredBy: Mexican tostadas de pollo, with a nod to tinga
about: Poached shredded chicken tossed in a smoky chipotle crema and piled on crisp baked tostadas with lime-dressed cucumber and avocado. A **high-protein snack** without the frying, with the chipotle as a nod to tinga.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and bake the tortillas on a tray for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp.
Stir the yogurt with the chipotle and half the lime juice for the crema. Toss the cucumber with the rest of the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Simmer the chicken in a small pot of lightly salted water with the cilantro stems for 12 to 14 minutes, until cooked through. Cool slightly, shred with two forks, and toss with half the crema.
Pile the chicken on the tostadas, top with cucumber, avocado, the rest of the crema and the cilantro leaves.
tip: Poach double the chicken when you are cooking dinner and the tostadas take 5 minutes.
ingredients: cut into wedges or left whole
stems for the pot, leaves chopped

name: Requesón-style cottage cheese with pineapple and cinnamon
inspiredBy: Mexican requesón with fruit
about: Soft, creamy cottage cheese, close to Mexico's requesón, with sweet pineapple, lime and cinnamon. A **cool, high-protein snack** that takes two minutes.
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and top with the pineapple.
