Grate over a little lime zest, squeeze on the juice, and dust with cinnamon.
Scatter on the pepitas.

name: Cottage cheese with pico de gallo and baked totopos
inspiredBy: Mexican pico de gallo
about: Creamy cottage cheese topped with a fresh pico de gallo of tomato, onion, jalapeño and cilantro, with crisp baked corn totopos for scooping. **Cool, tangy and high in protein**, it is a savoury answer to a sweet snack.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C. Lay the tortilla wedges on a tray and bake 8 to 10 minutes until crisp and lightly golden.
Stir the tomato, onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice and salt together for the pico de gallo.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl, top with the pico and serve with the totopos.

name: Pineapple yogurt with chile, lime and pepitas
inspiredBy: Mexican fruit with chile and lime
about: Thick yogurt with sweet pineapple, a squeeze of lime, a pinch of chili and toasted pepitas, the way fruit is eaten with chile and lime across Mexico. The yogurt keeps it **protein-forward**, the pineapple keeps it a treat.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the pineapple.
Squeeze on the lime and sprinkle with a pinch of chili.
Finish with the toasted pepitas.

name: Sardine tostadas with cucumber, lime and avocado
inspiredBy: Mexican tostadas de sardina
about: Canned sardines, with their soft bones, mashed gently onto crisp corn tostadas with cucumber, red onion, avocado and a squeeze of lime. Sardines bring **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D** in one snack, and tostadas de sardina are a real Mexican favourite.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and bake the tortillas on a tray for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp.
Toss the cucumber, red onion, jalapeño and cilantro with half the lime juice.
Mash the sardines lightly with the rest of the lime, then spread over the tostadas and top with the cucumber mix and avocado.
tip: If there is sardine left in the can, keep it covered in the fridge and eat it within 2 days, mashed with lime on a tostada.
ingredients: cut into wedges or left whole

name: Black bean and egg white tostadas with salsa
inspiredBy: Mexican tostadas with frijoles
about: Crisp corn tostadas topped with mashed black beans, scrambled egg whites and a quick fresh salsa. A savoury, **high-protein snack** with the beans for fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and bake the tortillas on a tray for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp.
Toss the tomato, onion, jalapeño and cilantro with the lime juice and a pinch of salt to make the salsa.
Warm the beans in a small pot with a splash of water, mashing them until spreadable.
Scramble the egg whites in the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat until no runny egg is left, about 3 minutes, and season with a pinch of salt.
Spread the beans over the tostadas, top with the eggs and finish with the salsa.
ingredients: cut into wedges or left whole

name: Egg white tacos with tomato, onion and chile
inspiredBy: Mexican huevos a la mexicana
about: Egg whites scrambled the way Mexico does huevos a la mexicana, with tomato, onion and jalapeño, folded into warm corn tortillas with a squeeze of lime. A **light, very high-protein snack** that is quick and lean.
steps: Warm a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and cook the onion and jalapeño for 2 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomato and cook 2 minutes more, until it has softened and lost its raw edge.
Pour in the egg whites with a pinch of salt and stir gently over medium-low heat, taking the pan off the heat while they are still glossy; the pan finishes them. Overcooked whites go rubbery.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, fill them with the eggs and finish with cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
tip: Buy egg whites by the carton. This week uses a lot of them, and you won't be left with a bowl of yolks.

name: Griddled arepa with scrambled egg whites and tomato hogao
inspiredBy: Colombian arepa with hogao
about: A golden Colombian arepa split open and filled with scrambled egg whites and a warm tomato and onion hogao. The corn arepa gives you **carbs for training** and the egg whites add protein without much fat.
steps: Stir the corn flour with a pinch of the salt and enough warm water to make a soft dough. Rest it 5 minutes, then shape into a thick patty.
Cook the arepa in a lightly oiled nonstick skillet over medium heat, about 5 minutes a side, until golden and firm when tapped.
In a small pan, soften the onion and garlic in a little oil for 2 minutes. Add the tomato and cumin and cook 4 minutes into a thick hogao. Spoon a little out for the top.
Pour the egg whites into the rest of the hogao with the rest of the salt and stir gently until no runny egg is left, about 3 minutes.
Split the arepa, fill it with the eggs and spoon the saved hogao on top.

name: Ful medames with boiled eggs, tomato and warm pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian ful medames
about: Egypt's breakfast of creamy fava beans, warmed with garlic and cumin, mashed a little and finished with lemon, a spoonful of tahini and a little olive oil. Boiled eggs and warm pita make it a proper plate. The beans and eggs together give you **plenty of protein and fibre** before the day starts.
steps: Lower the eggs into a small pot of boiling water and simmer for 8 minutes, then cool them under cold water and peel.
Warm the olive oil in a saucepan, add the garlic and cumin and stir for 30 seconds until it smells toasty.

Tip in the fava beans with a splash of water (or their cooking liquid, if you cooked them from dried), add the salt and simmer for 5 minutes, mashing about a third of the beans with a fork so it goes thick and creamy. Stir in the tahini and half the lemon juice.
Toss the tomato and parsley with the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of Aleppo pepper.
Spoon the ful into a bowl, top with the halved eggs and the tomato salad, and serve with warm pita.
tip: Canned ful medames is what many Egyptian homes use: rinse it very well and taste before you salt, as it usually needs little or none. Boil the eggs the night before and breakfast takes about 6 minutes.
ingredients: small brown ful beans, canned and well rinsed, or cooked from dried

name: Shakshuka with chickpeas and warm pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian and Levantine shakshuka
about: Eggs baked in a bubbling pan of tomato, red pepper and cumin, with chickpeas for body and warm pita for scooping up every last bit. The peppers and tomato bring plenty of vitamin C, and the eggs and chickpeas give it **a solid dose of protein** before the day gets going.
steps: Warm the oil in a wide, deep pan over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, cumin and Aleppo pepper and cook for a minute until fragrant.
Add the grated tomatoes, chickpeas and salt and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to hold a dent.
Make little wells with a spoon, crack the eggs in, cover and cook on low for 5 to 6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble.
Scatter the parsley over the top and eat straight from the pan with warm pita.
tip: Make the sauce the night before and keep it 2 days. Warm it, then crack in the eggs.

name: Thick yogurt bowl with dates, walnuts and toasted oats
inspiredBy: Gulf and Levantine yogurt with dates
about: Thick, tangy yogurt topped with chewy chopped dates, toasted walnuts and oats, with a hint of cardamom. Dates, yogurt and walnuts are an old Levantine and Gulf combination. The yogurt brings **a big dose of protein and calcium**, and the walnuts add omega-3.
steps: Toast the oats and walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until they smell nutty. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Mash the dates into the yogurt with the cardamom so the sweetness runs through, then spoon it into a bowl.
Top with the toasted oats and walnuts and a pinch of cinnamon.
tip: At larger sizes, use a deep bowl. Toast a few days' worth of oats and walnuts at once and keep them in a jar.

name: Chicken and chickpea fatteh with garlic yogurt
inspiredBy: Syrian and Lebanese fatteh
about: A Levantine layered dish: crisp toasted pita, warm spiced chickpeas and shredded chicken, all under a cool garlicky yogurt and tahini sauce with toasted almonds. It is crunchy, creamy and lemony all at once. The chicken and yogurt give you **plenty of protein for the afternoon**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 C. Tear the pita into bite-size pieces, toss with half the oil and bake for 8 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Cover the chicken with water in a small pot, add a pinch of salt and simmer gently for 14 minutes, until cooked through. Lift it out and shred it with two forks.
Warm the chickpeas in a little of the chicken cooking water with the cumin, cinnamon and paprika until hot.
Stir the yogurt with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.

Toast the almonds in the rest of the oil in a small pan until golden. Pile the crisp pita in a shallow bowl, top with the chickpeas and chicken, spoon over the yogurt and finish with the almonds and parsley.
tip: Bake the pita bits ahead and assemble just before eating, so they stay crisp.

name: Shish tawook with garlicky rice and tomato cucumber salad
inspiredBy: Lebanese and Turkish chicken skewers
about: Chicken breast marinated in lemon, garlic, tomato paste and warm spices, grilled until browned at the edges, with fluffy garlicky rice and a crisp tomato, cucumber and carrot salad. A little olive oil and a good marinade keep lean chicken juicy. It makes **two big, high-protein portions**, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Mix the tomato paste, half the lemon juice, half the garlic, the paprika, baharat, pepper, a little salt and half the oil in a bowl. Add the chicken, turn to coat and marinate for at least 30 minutes.

Rinse the rice. Warm the remaining oil in a pot, stir in the rest of the garlic for 30 seconds, add the rice, a pinch of salt and a little less than twice its volume of water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for about 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Rest it, covered, for 5 minutes.
Thread the chicken onto skewers, or spread it on a tray. Grill or broil on high for 12 to 14 minutes, turning once, until browned in places and cooked through.
Toss the tomato, cucumber, carrot, onion and parsley with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Serve the chicken over the rice with the salad. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Marinate 30 minutes to 8 hours. Longer and the lemon turns breast chalky. Cook enough rice for two portions and the leftover lunch is ready.

name: Lean beef and lamb kofta in tomato and pepper sauce with pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian kofta bil salsa and Lebanese kafta bi banadoura
about: Little kofta made with lean beef and a smaller share of lean lamb, grated onion, parsley and baharat, simmered in a garlicky tomato and pepper sauce and served with warm pita. Mixing the two meats keeps the flavour but **keeps saturated fat low**. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Squeeze the grated onion over a bowl and keep the juice. Mix the beef, lamb, squeezed onion, half the parsley, half the garlic, the baharat, cinnamon, a little salt and a spoonful of the onion juice with your hands, squeezing until it holds together. Shape into small ovals and chill them for 20 minutes so they hold.
Warm the oil in a wide, deep pan and brown the kofta for about 6 minutes, turning, then lift them out.
In the same pan, soften the diced onion and pepper for 6 minutes. Stir in the rest of the garlic, the cumin and the tomato paste for a minute.

Add the grated tomatoes and a pinch of salt, return the kofta and simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the kofta are cooked through. Add a splash of water only if the sauce catches.
Scatter the sumac and the rest of the parsley over the top and serve with warm pita. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Shape the kofta the night before. They hold together better after a night in the fridge.
ingredients: ask the butcher to mince lean leg, or use the leanest ground lamb

name: Grilled mackerel with sumac onions and herby bulgur pilaf
inspiredBy: Turkish uskumru izgara with pilav
about: Rich, oily mackerel fillets, broiled until the skin crackles, with a sharp pile of sumac onions and a Turkish-style bulgur pilaf with chickpeas, lots of parsley and a squeeze of lemon. The acid cuts the richness beautifully. Mackerel is a big source of **omega-3 and vitamin D**.
steps: Toss the red onion with the sumac, a squeeze of the lemon juice, half the parsley and a pinch of salt. Set it aside so it softens.
Warm half the oil in a pot and cook the diced onion until soft and golden, about 6 minutes. Stir in the cinnamon and Aleppo pepper for 30 seconds.

Add the bulgur, chickpeas, salt and a little over its volume of water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes. Rest, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff and fold in the rest of the parsley.
Heat the broiler to high. Rub the mackerel with the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt, lay it skin side up on a tray and broil for 5 to 6 minutes, until the skin blisters and the flesh flakes.
Serve the fish over the pilaf with the sumac onions and the rest of the lemon juice squeezed over.
tip: Ask the fishmonger to fillet the mackerel and pull out the pin bones.

name: Turkish tuna and white bean piyaz with boiled egg
inspiredBy: Turkish piyaz, with tuna
about: A cool Turkish bean salad with sumac-bright red onion, grated carrot, tomato, plenty of parsley and chunks of tuna and boiled egg, dressed with lemon and olive oil. Warm pita is on the side. It is easy, filling and **high in protein and fibre** with nothing to cook but an egg.
steps: Boil the egg, or eggs, for 8 minutes, cool under cold water and peel.
Rub the red onion with the sumac and a pinch of salt for a minute to soften and sharpen it.
Toss the beans with the onion, carrot, parsley, tomato, lemon juice, olive oil and Aleppo pepper, and season to taste.
Flake the tuna over the top, add the egg, cut into quarters, and eat with warm pita.
tip: Boil the egg, or eggs, the night before and the whole lunch comes together in 5 minutes.

name: Beef and okra stew (bamia) with rice
inspiredBy: Egyptian bamia
about: A tomatoey Egyptian and Levantine stew of tender lean beef and okra with garlic and parsley, spooned over rice. Lemon at the end keeps it bright. Beef and okra together bring **iron, magnesium and a lot of fibre**, and it tastes even better the next day.
steps: Warm most of the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in two batches, about 5 minutes a batch. Lift it out.
Cook the onion in the same pot until soft and golden, about 6 minutes. Stir in half the garlic, the allspice, cinnamon and tomato paste for a minute.
Return the beef, add the passata, some water to just cover, the salt and pepper. Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the okra whole, cover again and cook for 15 minutes more, until the okra is soft but not falling apart. Stir as little as you can.
Meanwhile, cook the rice with a pinch of salt and a little less than twice its volume of water, covered, on low for 15 minutes.

Warm the last of the oil in a small pan and fry the rest of the garlic with the ground coriander for a minute, until fragrant. Stir this ta'leya into the stew with the lemon juice and parsley, and serve over the rice. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Frozen whole okra works, straight from the freezer. A pressure cooker does the beef in 20 minutes; add the okra after pressure is released.
ingredients: passata or crushed tomatoes, no salt added (not paste)

name: Baharat salmon with saffron rice, roasted cauliflower and carrots, and lemon tahini
inspiredBy: Gulf spiced fish and rice
about: Salmon rubbed with baharat and roasted until just flaking, on saffron-scented rice with charred cauliflower, carrots and tomatoes and a lemony tahini drizzle. It borrows the spices and the fish-and-rice idea of Gulf kitchens. Salmon delivers **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C. Toss the cauliflower, carrots and tomatoes with half the oil, the cumin and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.

Steep the saffron in a few spoonfuls of hot water. Warm the rest of the oil in a pot and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the rinsed rice, stir for a minute, then pour in a little less than twice its volume of water with the saffron and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, then rest for 5.
Rub the salmon with the baharat and ground dried lime. Nestle it among the vegetables and roast for 10 to 12 minutes more, until it just flakes.
Whisk the tahini with half the lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of salt, adding only a spoonful of cold water until it pours like thick cream. Squeeze the rest of the lemon over the salmon.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan. Fluff the rice, fold in the parsley, and serve with the salmon, vegetables, the almonds and a big drizzle of tahini.
tip: If you can't find dried lime, use a little extra lemon and a pinch of sumac.

name: Hummus with warm spiced beef and almonds
inspiredBy: Lebanese hummus bil lahme
about: A big swoop of creamy, lemony hummus topped with sizzling lean beef spiced with allspice and cinnamon, toasted almonds and parsley, with pita and cucumber to scoop. It is a Levantine mezze turned into a proper lunch. The beef and chickpeas together give you **protein and iron**.
steps: Blend the chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, a pinch of salt and 3 or 4 spoonfuls of ice-cold water until smooth and fluffy. Taste and add more lemon or salt if it needs it.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden, then set them aside.

Warm the oil in the same pan and cook the onion for 3 minutes. Add the beef, allspice, cinnamon and a pinch of salt and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and crumbly. Add a splash of water and let it bubble for a minute so the beef stays juicy.
Swoop the hummus into a wide bowl, pile the warm beef on top and scatter the almonds and parsley.
Serve with warm pita and cucumber.
tip: Hummus is best made fresh, but it keeps 3 days in a covered container in the fridge.

name: Maqluba-style chicken and rice with cauliflower and eggplant
inspiredBy: Palestinian and Syrian maqluba
about: The upside-down pot of Palestine, Jordan and Syria: spiced chicken, roasted eggplant, cauliflower, carrot and tomato layered under rice, then turned out like a cake. It is the weekend project, with a cool cucumber yogurt on the side. The chicken and yogurt carry **plenty of protein**, and it makes two portions.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C. Toss the eggplant, cauliflower and carrot coins with half the oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 20 minutes, until browned at the edges.

Rub the chicken with the baharat, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice and a little salt. Brown it in the rest of the oil in a wide, heavy pot for 3 to 4 minutes a side, then lift it out. Soften the onion and garlic in the same pot for 3 minutes and scoop them onto a plate.

Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Layer the tomato slices and the softened onion on the bottom of the pot, then the chicken, then the roasted vegetables and the bay leaf. Pour the rice over the top and press it down.
Pour in enough hot water to cover the rice by about a finger's width, add a pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes, covered.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan. Run a knife around the pot, put a large plate on top and flip it in one confident move. Scatter with almonds.
Stir the yogurt with the cucumber and a pinch of salt and serve alongside. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
tip: Cut the chicken in thick pieces and tuck it under the vegetables so it stays moist. If flipping the pot feels scary, serve it straight from the pot.

name: Lean lamb and white bean stew (kuru fasulye) with bulgur pilaf
inspiredBy: Turkish kuru fasulye with pilav
about: A Turkish favourite: creamy white beans simmered with lean lamb, tomato and a spoonful of paprika-spiked tomato paste, served over a bulgur pilaf with a sharp parsley and onion salad. The beans and lamb give you **iron, zinc and slow-burning fuel** for training.
steps: Warm half the oil in a pot and brown the lamb for about 5 minutes. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, paprika and Aleppo pepper for a minute, then add the passata, salt, pepper and enough water to just cover.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the lamb is tender. Add the beans and cook for 10 more minutes so the sauce goes thick.
Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a small pot, stir in the bulgur for a minute, then add a little over its volume of water and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer for 12 minutes, then rest for 5.
Toss the red onion with the sumac and parsley.
Spoon the stew over the bulgur and pile the onion salad on top.
tip: Canned beans keep this quick. Make a double pot and freeze the second portion; it keeps 3 months.
ingredients: passata or crushed tomatoes, no salt added (not paste)

name: Lupini beans with lemon, cumin and tomato
inspiredBy: Egyptian termis
about: Egypt's street snack: firm, nutty lupini beans tossed with lemon, cumin and olive oil, with juicy tomato wedges. Squeeze each bean out of its thin skin, as people do in Egypt. They are a surprisingly **high-protein, high-fibre** bean you can eat with your fingers.
steps: Rinse the lupini beans well under cold water, because they are salty.
Toss them with the lemon juice, olive oil, cumin and Aleppo pepper.
Serve with the tomato wedges. Squeeze each bean out of its thin skin and eat the inside.

name: Thick yogurt with walnuts, pomegranate and mint
inspiredBy: Levantine yogurt
about: Cool, thick yogurt scattered with juicy pomegranate seeds, toasted walnuts and a pinch of dried mint. Sweet, sharp and crunchy, and **a quick hit of protein and calcium**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until they smell nutty.
Scatter the pomegranate seeds and walnuts over the yogurt and finish with the dried mint.

name: Boiled eggs with dukkah, tomato and warm pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian eggs and dukkah
about: Jammy boiled eggs, split and dusted with dukkah, with sweet ripe tomato, a squeeze of lemon and a little warm pita. The nuts and spices make plain eggs taste like an Egyptian breakfast mezze, and it is **an easy, high-protein snack**.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and simmer for 7 minutes, then cool under cold water and peel.
Arrange the tomato wedges on a plate, squeeze over the lemon and drizzle with the olive oil.
Halve the eggs, dip the cut sides in the dukkah and eat with the tomato and warm pita.

name: Hummus with garlic lemon chicken strips and carrot sticks
inspiredBy: Levantine hummus with shawarma-style chicken
about: Quick hummus with strips of garlicky, lemony chicken breast seared in a hot pan, and crunchy carrot sticks to scoop. It is like a shawarma plate in snack form, and **keeps your protein topped up through the afternoon**.
steps: Blend the chickpeas with the tahini, half the lemon juice, half the garlic, half the cumin, a pinch of salt and a few spoonfuls of cold water until smooth, using a stick blender in a tall jar, or mash very well with a fork for a rustic hummus.
Toss the chicken with the rest of the garlic and cumin, the paprika and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a pan over high heat and sear the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Squeeze over the rest of the lemon.
Spoon the hummus into a bowl, lay the chicken on top and serve with the carrot sticks.

name: Labneh with za'atar, cucumber, mint and carrot sticks
inspiredBy: Levantine labneh and za'atar
about: Thick, tangy labneh swirled with olive oil and za'atar, with cool cucumber, mint and carrot sticks to scoop it up. A classic Levantine breakfast, brought in as a snack, with **protein and a little calcium** in a few minutes.
steps: Spread the labneh in a shallow bowl and make a swirl with the back of a spoon.
Drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with the za'atar.
Scatter the cucumber and mint over the top and scoop it up with the carrot sticks.

name: White cheese with tomato, olives and mint
inspiredBy: Egyptian gebna beida
about: Salty, creamy Egyptian-style white cheese with ripe tomato, a few olives and fresh mint. It is the sort of plate you'd find on the table at any meal, and it gives you **protein and calcium** with very little effort.
steps: Slice the cheese and lay it on a plate with the tomato.
Scatter the olives and mint over the top and eat with a fork.
tip: No gebna beida nearby? Any mild white brined cheese works, such as Bulgarian white cheese or a mild feta. Rinse it if it tastes very salty.

name: Smashed sardines on toasted pita with sumac onion and tomato
inspiredBy: Egyptian sardine sandwich
about: Oily sardines smashed with lemon and sumac onto crisp toasted pita, with sweet tomato and a pile of fresh parsley. It is a classic Egyptian and Mediterranean quick bite, sharp and crunchy. Sardines bring **omega-3 and calcium from the soft bones**.
steps: Toast the pita until crisp and golden. Rub the red onion with the sumac and a squeeze of the lemon juice and let it sit for a few minutes.
Mash the sardines roughly with the rest of the lemon juice and the olive oil.
Pile the tomato and the sardines on the pita and top with the sumac onion, the parsley and a pinch of Aleppo pepper.
tip: Opened sardines keep 2 days in a covered container in the fridge. Mash the rest with lemon and parsley for tomorrow's toast.

name: Tuna, red pepper and parsley pita pocket
inspiredBy: Egyptian and Levantine tuna sandwich
about: Flaked tuna with crunchy red pepper, tomato, parsley, lemon and cumin stuffed into a warm pita pocket. It is a light bite you can eat on the go, with **lean protein** and not much else to wash up.
steps: Flake the tuna into a bowl with the lemon juice, olive oil and cumin.
Warm the pita and open the pocket.
Stuff it with the red pepper, tomato, parsley and tuna.

name: Thick cacik with cucumber, garlic and mint
inspiredBy: Turkish cacik
about: Turkish cacik made thick enough to eat with a spoon: strained-style Greek yogurt with grated cucumber, garlic, mint and a thread of olive oil. It is cool and sharp, and a big bowl is **a lean, calcium-rich hit of protein**.
steps: Squeeze the grated cucumber in your hands to get rid of the extra water.
Stir it into the yogurt with the garlic, fresh mint, lemon juice and salt.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with the olive oil and rub the dried mint over the top.

name: Herb eggah with extra egg whites, tomato and pita
inspiredBy: Egyptian eggah and Levantine ijjeh
about: Eggah, called ijjeh in Lebanon and Syria, is a thick, herby omelette cut into wedges. This one leans on egg whites so it stays light and high in protein, with a whole egg for flavour and colour. Parsley, onion and a pinch of baharat do the work, and it gives you **over 30 g of protein**, warm or cold.
steps: Warm the oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Beat the whole egg and the egg whites with the parsley, baharat, pepper and salt.
Pour the eggs into the pan, cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 minutes, until the top is just set. Slide it onto a plate and cut into wedges.
Serve warm or cold with the tomato and warm pita.

name: Blueberry overnight oats with soy drink, silken tofu and hemp
about: Creamy overnight oats where silken tofu is blended into fortified soy drink, so the jar is creamy and loose, a porridge you can spoon or sip, with no tofu taste at all. Blueberries, walnuts, almonds, chia and hemp hearts add colour, crunch and plant omega-3. It brings **at least 28 g of protein** and a glass of fortified soy drink before you leave the house.
steps: Blend the silken tofu with the soy drink and the cinnamon for about 30 seconds, until completely smooth and pourable.
In a jar or bowl, stir together the oats, chia and hemp hearts. Pour the blended tofu drink over and stir well, so no dry pockets are left.
Rinse the blueberries and fold in about half. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least 4 hours. The jar keeps up to 2 days in the fridge.
In the morning, loosen with a splash of soy drink if it has set too firm. Top with the rest of the blueberries, the chopped walnuts and the sliced almonds.
tip: Mix one jar on Sunday night and one on Thursday night, and breakfast is done. Once opened, keep silken tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Swap in thawed frozen blueberries when fresh are out of season.

name: Tofu scramble with black beans, peppers and a warm corn tortilla
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos a la mexicana, with tofu in place of the eggs
about: Golden crumbled tofu scrambled with onion, red pepper and spinach, with black beans stirred in and a warm corn tortilla and avocado on the side. Turmeric gives the colour, cumin and smoked paprika the savoury depth, and a squeeze of lime lifts it. The tofu and soy drink bring **about 25 g of protein**, and the beans add fibre.
steps: Rinse the pepper, spinach and cilantro under cold water before cutting. Press the tofu between clean towels for a few minutes, then crumble it into small pieces with your hands.
Warm the oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the crumbled tofu, cumin, turmeric, smoked paprika and salt. Stir and cook for 5 minutes, until the tofu is hot and golden at the edges.
Fold in the black beans and spinach and warm through for 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts. Squeeze in the lime juice and stir through the cilantro.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side. Serve the scramble with the tortilla and sliced avocado, and a glass of cold soy drink.
tip: Add a pinch of chili flakes for heat, and rinse canned beans well; it washes away much of what causes gas. Buy a regular firm tofu with about 10% of the daily value for calcium per serving on the label; a high-calcium (calcium-set) tofu would add more calcium than this week needs.
ingredients: a glass of fortified soy drink on the side

name: Soy yogurt bowl with blueberries, hemp and crunchy roasted soybeans
about: Cool, tangy soy yogurt with a handful of crushed roasted soybeans and toasted almonds for crunch, hemp hearts, chia and blueberries, with a glass of fortified soy drink on the side. It is the quick breakfast for mornings with no time, and it brings **protein from soy and hemp** with plant omega-3 from the chia.
steps: Whisk the silken tofu into the soy yogurt in a bowl until smooth, then stir in the chia, maple syrup and cinnamon. Let it sit for 5 minutes so the chia swells a little.
Rinse the blueberries and scatter most of them over the top.
Sprinkle with the hemp hearts, toasted almonds and crushed roasted soybeans just before eating, so they stay crunchy.
Finish with the last blueberries and pour a glass of cold soy drink to go with it. Use soy yogurt by the date on the tub, and silken tofu within 2 days of opening.
tip: Crush the soybeans with the bottom of a glass in a zip bag. Frozen blueberries thaw in the bowl while you stir.
ingredients: ready-to-eat roasted soy nuts, never raw dried soybeans
a glass of fortified soy drink on the side

name: Spiced tempeh and sweet potato hash with spinach and lime
about: A weekend skillet of crisp-edged tempeh and sweet potato with onion, red pepper and spinach, warmed with garam masala and cumin and finished with lime and a handful of walnuts. It is slow enough to enjoy and hearty enough to carry a training day, with a glass of fortified soy drink alongside. The breakfast brings **about 35 g of protein**, and the sweet potato adds vitamin A.
steps: Rinse the spinach, pepper and sweet potato, then chop everything before you light the stove. Scrub the sweet potato; the skin can stay on.
Steam the tempeh cubes over simmering water for 8 minutes. This softens the flavour and helps them brown.
Heat half the oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the sweet potato, covered, for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender.
Push the sweet potato aside, add the remaining oil and the tempeh, and cook for 5 minutes, until golden. Add the onion, pepper, garlic, garam masala, cumin and salt and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until wilted. Finish with the lime juice and the toasted walnuts, and serve with a glass of cold soy drink.
tip: Cube the sweet potato smaller to cut the cooking time. Keep tempeh in the fridge and cook it until hot all the way through. Throw it away if it is slimy or smells of ammonia.
ingredients: a glass of fortified soy drink on the side

name: Black bean and edamame bowl with taco-spiced tempeh crumble
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican burrito bowls
about: A colourful bowl of black beans and edamame over a small scoop of brown rice, topped with a chili-cumin tempeh crumble, tomato, red pepper, carrot, avocado and lime. It is crunchy, fresh and a little smoky. The beans, edamame and tempeh crumble together bring **plenty of protein and iron**, and the lime helps you absorb it.
steps: Rinse the brown rice, then simmer it covered in plenty of water for about 30 minutes, until tender. Drain and keep warm. Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 4 minutes, drain, and rinse the black beans well.
Rinse the tomato, pepper, carrot and cilantro, then dice, grate or chop them. Toss the onion with half the lime juice and the salt, and set aside for the flavours to mingle.

Heat the oil in a pan, add the crumbled tempeh, chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika, and cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until browned and crisp at the edges. Add the soy sauce and cook for 30 seconds.

Warm the black beans for 2 minutes with a splash of water. Build the bowl with rice, beans, edamame, tomato, pepper and carrot, spoon the crumble on top, and finish with the onion, avocado, cilantro and the rest of the lime.
tip: Cook the rice a day ahead: spread it on a tray, cool it within 1 hour and refrigerate. Start with a smaller scoop of beans if you are building up to this size.

name: Red lentil dal tadka with spinach, spiced seitan, tempeh and brown basmati
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian masoor dal tadka
about: Soft red lentils, cauliflower and spinach finished with a sizzling cumin, garlic and chili tadka, served with pan-seared seitan and tempeh in a tikka-style spice rub and a little brown basmati. It is cozy, bright with lemon, and **makes two portions**, so tomorrow's lunch is ready. The lentils, seitan and tempeh together carry the protein, and the lemon helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Rinse the brown basmati and simmer it covered in plenty of water for 30 to 35 minutes, until tender. Cook enough for both portions. Drain.

Rinse the lentils and put them in a pot with 4 times their volume of water, the turmeric, the ginger, the cauliflower florets and half the onion. Simmer for 15 to 18 minutes, skimming any foam, until the lentils and cauliflower are completely soft.

Meanwhile, rinse the spinach, tomato, cauliflower and cilantro. Pat the seitan and tempeh dry so they brown instead of steaming, then toss the cubes with half the garam masala, half the Kashmiri chili and a pinch of salt. Sear them in a non-stick pan with a third of the oil for 8 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides.
Stir the chopped tomato and spinach into the dal and cook 4 minutes, until the spinach is wilted. Season with the salt and the lemon juice.

For the tadka, heat the rest of the oil in a small pan. Add the cumin seeds, then the remaining onion, the garlic and the asafoetida (hing). Cook for 3 minutes, until golden, then stir in the rest of the garam masala and Kashmiri chili. Pour it, sizzling, over the dal.

Serve the dal with the seitan and tempeh, rice and a handful of cilantro. Cool the second portion, rice included, in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Soak the lentils for 30 minutes first and discard the water; the dal is gentler on the stomach and cooks faster. Thaw a frozen portion overnight in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Gochujang tempeh, seitan and edamame stir-fry with bok choy
inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean tempeh and vegetable bokkeum
about: Seared tempeh, seitan and edamame tossed with bok choy and carrot in a sticky gochujang, soy and ginger sauce, over a small bed of brown rice. It is spicy-sweet and savoury, and it **makes two portions**. Tempeh, seitan and edamame together give over 50 g of protein, and the bok choy adds calcium.
steps: Rinse the brown rice and simmer it covered for about 30 minutes, until tender. Cook enough for both portions.
Rinse the bok choy, carrot and scallions, then chop or cut into matchsticks. Steam the tempeh strips over simmering water for 8 minutes. Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 4 minutes, then drain.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce and lemon juice with a splash of water into a smooth sauce.

Pat the seitan dry so it browns instead of steaming. Heat the canola oil in a wide pan or wok over medium-high heat and sear the tempeh and seitan for 5 minutes, until golden. Add the carrot and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, bok choy and edamame and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the bok choy is just wilted. Pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute, until glossy and coating everything.

Finish with the sesame oil and scallions and serve over the rice. Cool the second portion, rice included, in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Gochujang varies in heat. Start with a little less and add more at the end. Pick a seitan near 450 mg sodium per 100 g; brands vary a lot.

name: Lemon-oregano seitan with chickpea Greek salad, soy tzatziki and lemon rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek souvlaki and horiatiki, with seitan and chickpeas
about: Golden strips of seitan marinated in lemon, garlic and oregano, served with a chunky salad of chickpeas, tomato, cucumber, pepper and onion, a cool soy-yogurt tzatziki and a little lemony rice. It is bright, fresh and satisfying, and it **makes two portions**. Seitan brings a lot of protein, and the chickpeas add folate and iron.
steps: Stir half the lemon juice, half the olive oil, the garlic, oregano and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Add the seitan strips and marinate in the fridge for at least 20 minutes. Do not reuse the marinade as a sauce.

Rinse the brown rice and simmer it covered for about 30 minutes, until tender. Cook enough for both portions, then stir in a spoonful of the lemon juice. Rinse the cucumber, tomato, pepper and parsley.
Make the tzatziki by squeezing the grated cucumber dry, then stirring it with the soy yogurt, a squeeze of lemon juice, a little chopped parsley, a little garlic and a pinch of salt.
Toss the chickpeas, diced cucumber, tomato, pepper, onion and parsley with the remaining lemon juice and olive oil.
Lift the seitan from the marinade and pat it dry. Sear it hard in a hot non-stick pan for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until golden and hot all the way through.

Serve the seitan over the rice and salad with the tzatziki. Keep the second portion of seitan, the rice and the salad in separate shallow containers, in the fridge within 1 hour. They keep up to 3 days, but eat the salad within 2 days; reheat the seitan and rice once to 74 °C (165 °F) and eat the salad cold.
tip: Pack the seitan cold into a wrap or a pita for lunch. It is good that way too. Pick a seitan near 450 mg sodium per 100 g; brands vary a lot.
ingredients: grated for the sauce and diced for the salad

name: Chickpea, cauliflower and spinach curry with seared tofu and seitan
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian chana saag, with tofu in place of paneer
about: A thick, tangy curry of chickpeas, cauliflower and spinach in an onion, tomato and ginger masala, with golden seared tofu and chewy seitan that soak up the sauce. A squeeze of lemon and a little brown basmati round it out. It **makes two portions** and tastes even better the next day, and the tofu and seitan keep the protein high.
steps: Rinse the brown basmati and simmer it covered for 30 to 35 minutes, until tender. Cook enough for both portions. Drain.
Rinse the spinach, tomatoes, cauliflower and cilantro, and pat the seitan dry, then cut it into small chunks.
Sear the tofu cubes in a non-stick pan with a third of the oil for 8 minutes, until golden on most sides. Set aside.

Heat the rest of the oil in a wide pot. Add the cumin seeds for 20 seconds, then the onion and cook 8 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, coriander, turmeric and Kashmiri chili and stir for 1 minute.

Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes, until they break down into a thick sauce. Add the cauliflower, chickpeas, seitan and 100 ml of water and simmer, covered, for 12 minutes, until the cauliflower is tender and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the spinach, garam masala, amchur, salt and the seared tofu for 3 minutes, until the spinach wilts. Finish with the lemon juice and cilantro and serve with the rice.
Cool the second portion, rice included, in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Use a pressure cooker for dried chickpeas, or stay with rinsed canned chickpeas for speed. If your stomach is still getting used to beans, start with fewer chickpeas and more tofu. Thaw a frozen portion overnight in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Do not simmer seitan longer than the recipe says; it turns spongy. Buy a regular firm tofu with about 10% of the daily value for calcium per serving on the label; a high-calcium (calcium-set) tofu would add more calcium than this week needs.

name: Smoky black bean, tempeh and seitan chili over baked sweet potato
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex bean chili
about: A thick, smoky chili of crumbled tempeh, chopped seitan, black beans, red pepper and tomato, spooned over a split baked sweet potato with lime and cilantro. The chili is **even better on day two**, so this makes two portions. Tempeh and seitan give it a meaty bite, and the beans add iron, folate and fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Scrub and prick the sweet potatoes and bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until soft right through.
Rinse the pepper, tomatoes and cilantro, and rinse the beans well.
Warm the oil in a heavy pot and soften the onion and pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for a minute. Crumble in the tempeh and add the seitan and cook for 5 minutes, until browned.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano for 30 seconds so they bloom in the hot pot. Add the chopped tomatoes and 100 ml of water.
Add the beans and simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until thick and saucy. Season with the salt and lime juice.

Split the sweet potatoes, spoon the chili over and top with cilantro. Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Microwave the sweet potatoes for 8 minutes, then crisp them in the oven for 10. The chili freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw a frozen portion overnight in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Rather skip the seitan tonight? Use half as much again tempeh and a few more beans; the day's protein dips just under 30%.

name: Mapo-style tofu with seitan mince, bok choy and brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Sichuan mapo doufu, with seitan mince as the savoury, meaty crumble
about: Soft cubes of tofu and savoury seitan mince in a glossy, numbing-and-spicy sauce of doubanjiang, garlic and Sichuan pepper, with bok choy and a little brown rice. It is the comfort dish of a cold night and **makes two portions**. Tofu and seitan mince bring a large dose of protein, and the bok choy adds calcium.
steps: Rinse the brown rice and simmer it covered for about 30 minutes. Cook enough for both portions.

Mince the seitan finely with a knife, or pulse it in a food processor, so it looks like ground meat. Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer and slip the tofu cubes in for 3 minutes; this firms them so they hold together. Lift out gently.

Rinse the bok choy and scallions, then chop. Heat the canola oil in a wok or wide pan over medium heat. Fry the minced seitan for 4 minutes, until browned. Add the doubanjiang, garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute, until the oil turns red.

Add 200 ml of water and simmer for 3 minutes. Add the bok choy and tofu and nudge gently so the cubes stay whole. Simmer uncovered for 4 minutes, until the sauce reduces by about a third and turns glossy.

Finish with the ground Sichuan pepper, black pepper, sesame oil and scallions and serve over the rice. Cool the second portion, rice included, in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Doubanjiang is salty and hot, so taste the sauce before adding more. Skip the Sichuan pepper for a milder plate. Buy a regular firm tofu with about 10% of the daily value for calcium per serving on the label; a high-calcium (calcium-set) tofu would add more calcium than this week needs.

name: Baked whole wheat rigatoni with tempeh and lentil ragù and herby tofu ricotta
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian baked pasta with ricotta
about: A weekend bake of whole wheat rigatoni in a rich red lentil, tempeh and spinach ragù, topped with lemony whipped tofu ricotta and baked until golden at the edges. It is the project dish of the week and it **makes two portions**, with the second one fitting the freezer. Lentils, tempeh and tofu together make a proper high-protein dinner.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Crumble the tempeh into small pieces. Rinse the tomatoes, spinach and parsley.
Warm half the olive oil in a large pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and oregano for a minute, then the chopped tomatoes. Cook for 10 minutes, until they break down.
Stir in the lentils, tempeh and 200 ml of water. Simmer for 20 minutes, until the lentils are soft and the ragù is thick, then stir in the spinach until wilted and season with half the salt.
Boil the rigatoni in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain.

For the ricotta, drain the silken tofu on a clean towel for 15 minutes, then mash it with the crumbled firm tofu, the lemon juice, the remaining oil, the remaining salt and half the parsley, until thick and slightly rough.

Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes. Toss the pasta with the ragù in a baking dish. Dot with spoonfuls of the tofu ricotta. Bake uncovered for 25 minutes, until the ricotta looks set at the edges. Scatter with the toasted walnuts and the remaining parsley.

Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 1 hour. Refrigerate up to 2 days (silken tofu keeps no longer once opened) or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), covered.
tip: Make the ragù on Saturday and assemble Sunday. Freeze the second portion for a lunch next week; thaw it overnight in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Blueberry hemp smoothie with silken tofu and soy drink
about: A thick, purple smoothie made with silken tofu and fortified soy drink, blueberries and hemp hearts. You cannot taste the tofu, only the berries. It is a **over 20 g of protein** and a glass of fortified soy drink.
steps: Rinse fresh blueberries, then put the soy drink, silken tofu, blueberries, hemp hearts, chia and cinnamon in a blender.
Blend for 45 seconds, until completely smooth and thick. Add a splash of soy drink if it is too thick, or an ice cube if you would like it colder.
Pour and drink right away, or keep it in a sealed jar in the fridge for up to 24 hours and shake well.
tip: Use frozen blueberries and it turns into a thicker, shake-like drink. On a day you also had blueberry oats, blend frozen mango in place of the blueberries.

name: Maple cinnamon roasted soybean, walnut and almond crunch
about: A crunchy mix of roasted soybeans, walnuts and almonds tossed with a little maple and cinnamon and baked until glossy. It is sweet, salty and satisfying and gives you **protein and plant omega-3 in a handful**.
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F). Toss the roasted soybeans, walnuts and almonds with the maple syrup, cinnamon and salt.
Spread on a lined tray and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring once, until glossy and fragrant. Watch the nuts so they do not burn.
Cool completely on the tray; the nuts crisp as they cool. Keep in an airtight container for up to a week.
tip: Make a batch of four portions on Sunday and the snack is ready for the week.
ingredients: ready-to-eat roasted soy nuts, never raw dried soybeans

name: Edamame guacamole with baked tortilla wedges and cucumber
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican guacamole
about: A bright green guacamole where half the avocado is swapped for edamame, with lime, cilantro and a little onion, scooped up with crisp baked corn tortilla wedges and cucumber. It is creamy, fresh and limey, and the edamame bring **protein and iron** to a classic snack.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Place the tortilla wedges on a tray and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until crisp.
Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 4 minutes, then drain and cool.

Rinse the cilantro and cucumber, and wash the avocado skin before cutting. Mash the edamame and avocado with a fork or pulse them in a food processor, then stir in the lime juice, cilantro, onion, cumin and salt.
Serve with the tortilla wedges and cucumber slices. Press plastic wrap onto the surface of leftover guacamole, refrigerate, and eat within 2 days.
tip: A little jalapeño gives it a kick. Keep the stone in the guacamole to slow browning.

name: Mango cardamom soy lassi with silken tofu
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian mango lassi
about: A creamy mango lassi made with soy yogurt, silken tofu and fortified soy drink, scented with cardamom. It is cool and a little sweet and **refreshing after a workout**, and it brings protein and a glass of fortified soy drink.
steps: Put the soy yogurt, silken tofu, soy drink, frozen mango, hemp hearts and cardamom in a blender.
Blend for 45 seconds, until thick and smooth. Add a splash of soy drink if it is stiff.
Pour and drink right away, or keep in a sealed jar in the fridge for up to 24 hours.
tip: A squeeze of lime brightens it.

name: Soy-glazed seitan bites with cucumber and sesame oil
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese teriyaki
about: Chewy seitan cubes seared in a sticky soy, ginger and maple glaze, with cool cucumber. They are salty-sweet and savoury, and they pack **over 20 g of protein** into a small plate.
steps: Rinse the cucumber and slice it. Whisk the soy sauce, maple syrup, lemon juice, ginger and garlic in a small bowl.
Pat the seitan dry. Heat the sesame oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the seitan cubes for 4 minutes, turning, until golden and hot all the way through.
Pour in the glaze and toss for 1 minute, until sticky and glossy.
Serve over the cucumber. Keep leftovers in the fridge up to 3 days and reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Cook a double batch and eat the second portion cold in a wrap.

name: Mango chia pudding with silken tofu and soy drink
about: A spoonable chia pudding thickened overnight in soy drink and blended silken tofu, topped with mango. It is lightly sweet, cool and creamy, with **plant omega-3 from the chia** and a boost of protein from the tofu and soy drink.
steps: Blend the soy drink, silken tofu, maple syrup and cardamom until completely smooth.
Stir in the chia seeds, then stir again after 5 minutes so they do not clump. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight. It keeps up to 2 days.
Spoon the mango on top just before eating.
tip: Make it the night before, and make a fresh jar each time. Once opened, keep silken tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

name: Sticky baked tofu bites with soy and ginger
about: Cubes of firm tofu baked until golden and tossed in a sticky soy, ginger and lemon glaze. They are chewy outside and soft inside, and give **about 14 g of protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Press the tofu between clean towels for 10 minutes, then cut it into cubes.
Toss the tofu with the canola oil, spread on a lined tray and bake for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Warm the soy sauce, lemon juice, maple syrup and ginger in a small pan for 2 minutes, until slightly syrupy. Toss the hot tofu in the glaze.
Scatter with the scallions. Eat warm. Keep leftovers in the fridge up to 3 days and reheat once to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Bake a double batch for the week; they re-crisp in a hot oven. Buy a regular firm tofu with about 10% of the daily value for calcium per serving on the label; a high-calcium (calcium-set) tofu would add more calcium than this week needs.

name: Smoky maple tempeh strips with lime soy-yogurt dip and cucumber
about: Thin tempeh strips seared in smoked paprika and maple until crisp at the edges, with a cool lime and cilantro soy-yogurt dip and cucumber. It tastes smoky-sweet and gives **about 23 g of protein**.
steps: Steam the tempeh strips over simmering water for 8 minutes, then pat dry.
Stir the maple syrup, soy sauce and smoked paprika together and brush over the strips.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and sear the strips for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until crisp.
Stir the soy yogurt with the lime juice and chopped cilantro for the dip, rinse and slice the cucumber, and serve.
tip: These make a good sandwich filling too. Tuck them into a tortilla with cucumber.

name: Chaat masala roasted edamame with lime
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian chaat
about: Edamame roasted until lightly blistered, then tossed with tangy chaat masala, chili and lime. It is salty, sour and a little spicy, and a bowl brings **about 18 g of protein plus iron**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Boil the edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain well and pat dry.
Toss with the canola oil, spread on a tray and roast for 12 minutes, shaking once, until lightly blistered.
Toss with the chaat masala, Kashmiri chili, salt and lime juice. Eat warm.
tip: Roast the edamame in the pod for a chewier snack; shell and discard the pods as you eat.

name: Soy yogurt cup with silken tofu, cinnamon and walnuts
about: Thick soy yogurt whisked with silken tofu, hemp hearts and cinnamon, topped with toasted walnuts. It is cool, nutty and simple, and gives you **protein plus plant omega-3** from the walnuts.
steps: Whisk the silken tofu into the soy yogurt until smooth, then stir in the hemp hearts, maple syrup and cinnamon.
Top with the toasted walnuts just before eating, so they stay crunchy. Use soy yogurt by the date on the tub, and silken tofu within 2 days of opening.
tip: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.

name: Lemony silken tofu and herb dip with crunchy vegetables
about: A cool, creamy dip of silken tofu blended with lemon, garlic, parsley and a little olive oil, scooped up with cucumber and carrot sticks. It is a light, fresh snack with **over 20 g of protein**.
steps: Rinse the cucumber, carrot and parsley, then cut the cucumber and carrot into sticks and chop the parsley.
Drain any liquid from the silken tofu, then blend it with the lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt and pepper until completely smooth and thick.
Stir in most of the parsley and spoon the dip into a bowl. Serve with the vegetable sticks and the rest of the parsley on top.
Keep the dip covered in the fridge and eat it within 2 days.
tip: Add a pinch of smoked paprika or a few chopped chives if you like.

name: Chilled silken tofu with ginger, scallion and soy
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese hiyayakko
about: A block of cold silken tofu with a drizzle of soy sauce and sesame oil, fresh ginger, scallion and a squeeze of lemon. It is cool, silky and savoury, and it gives you **about 20 g of protein** for very little effort.
steps: Rinse the scallion, then slice it thinly. Open the silken tofu and drain off the liquid, then pat the block dry with a clean towel.
Slide the tofu onto a plate and leave it whole, or cut it into cubes. Stir the soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger and lemon juice together and spoon it over.
Scatter with the scallion and eat it cold. Keep any unused silken tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
tip: Add a few drops of chili oil or a pinch of chili flakes if you like heat.

name: Banana bread oatmeal with almonds and Greek yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by banana bread
about: Creamy stovetop oats simmered with mashed banana, ground flax and cinnamon, so the bowl smells like banana bread. Egg whites are whisked in until it turns thick and custardy, then a cold spoonful of Greek yogurt, toasted almonds and a drizzle of honey go on top. It tastes like a treat and brings **a good hit of protein**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until they smell nutty, then tip them out.
Bring the milk and an equal amount of water to a gentle simmer in a small pot. Stir in the oats, flax, cinnamon and salt and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Whisk the egg whites in a cup, then stir them into the hot oats in a thin stream. Cook, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes at a gentle bubble, until the whites turn opaque and firm all the way through.
Stir in the mashed banana for the last minute so it melts into the oats.
Spoon the oatmeal into a bowl and top with the Greek yogurt, almonds and a drizzle of honey.
tip: Pour the whites in slowly while you stir so they do not clump. Overripe bananas are the sweetest.

name: Smoky turkey and sweet potato breakfast skillet with spinach and egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic American breakfast hash
about: Crumbled turkey, diced sweet potato and peppers browned in smoked paprika, with spinach wilted through and egg cooked in the same pan until completely firm. It is a proper hot breakfast that is **high in protein and vitamin A**, and it all happens in one skillet.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Warm the oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the sweet potato and onion for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sweet potato is tender and starting to brown.

Push the vegetables to the side, add the turkey and break it up. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes until no pink is left and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Stir in the pepper, garlic, smoked paprika, cumin and salt and cook for 1 minute, then fold in the spinach until it wilts.
Make a gap in the middle. Beat the egg and egg whites together, pour them in and cook, stirring, until completely set and firm, about 2 minutes. Serve straight from the pan.
tip: Short on time? Cook the turkey and sweet potato the night before while dinner simmers, chill within 1 hour, and reheat them in the pan to 74 °C (165 °F) before you add the egg.

name: Strawberry yogurt bowl with honey-toasted oats and almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by a berry yogurt parfait
about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy strawberries and banana, topped with oats and almonds toasted in honey until crunchy. It takes five minutes and gives you **a good hit of protein** before you leave the house.
steps: Toast the oats and almonds in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden. Stir in half the honey and the cinnamon for the last 30 seconds, then tip onto a plate to cool and crisp.
Stir the ground flax into the yogurt, spoon it into a bowl and top with the strawberries, banana and their juice.
Scatter over the crunchy oats and almonds and drizzle with the rest of the honey.
tip: Toast a few days of oats and almonds at once and keep them in a jar.
ingredients: thawed in the fridge, or fresh and sliced

name: Lemon mustard chicken and broccoli stuffed sweet potato with cottage cheese
inspiredBy: Inspired by the American stuffed baked potato
about: A soft baked sweet potato piled with shredded chicken folded into cottage cheese, lemon and a little mustard, with tender broccoli on top. It is sweet, savoury and tangy all at once, and the sweet potato brings **plenty of vitamin A and potassium**.
steps: Scrub the sweet potatoes and wash the broccoli. Prick the sweet potatoes all over with a fork and microwave for about 5 minutes per potato, turning halfway, until a knife slides in easily. For a crisper skin, finish them in a hot oven for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile cover the chicken with water in a small pot, bring to a simmer and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and no pink is left. Lift it out, rest for 5 minutes, then shred it. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Steam the broccoli for 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Fold the shredded chicken into the cottage cheese with the mustard, lemon juice, parsley, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Split the sweet potatoes, fluff the insides with a fork, and pile on the chicken mix and the broccoli. Warm it for 1 minute in the microwave if you like it hot.
tip: For a packed lunch, carry the chicken mix and the sweet potatoes separately in a cold bag with an ice pack, eat the same day, and assemble when you sit down.

name: Seared steak and warm barley salad with lemon mustard dressing
inspiredBy: Inspired by a steak house plate and warm grain salads
about: Thin slices of seared sirloin on a bowl of chewy barley, chickpeas, sweet grated carrot and tender broccoli, all tossed in a sharp dressing of olive oil, lemon, yellow mustard and parsley. It is a steak house plate turned into a hearty lunch. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, and the barley and chickpeas bring fibre.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Rinse the barley and simmer it in plenty of water for 25 to 30 minutes, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Drain well and let it steam dry for a few minutes. Spread any you are not using right away in a shallow container and chill within 1 hour.

Pat the beef dry and season it with the pepper and a pinch of salt. Sear it in a very hot pan with a little of the oil for 3 minutes a side until browned, then turn the heat to medium and keep turning it every minute until it reaches 71 °C (160 °F) in the middle, then rest it on a clean plate for 5 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling it raw.
Whisk the mustard with the lemon juice, the rest of the oil, parsley and the rest of the salt. Let the onion sit in the dressing for 5 minutes to soften.
Toss the warm barley and broccoli with the chickpeas, dressing and carrot. Slice the steak against the grain, lay it on top, and pour over any resting juices.
tip: Cook the barley on Thursday evening while the cod bakes (cool it within 1 hour and chill), and this lunch takes about 15 minutes. Packing it? Keep the steak and salad in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat them the same day.

name: Lighter butter chicken with chickpeas and spinach over cumin millet
inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi butter chicken, lightened with yogurt and chickpeas
about: Tender chicken simmered in a silky tomato sauce with garam masala, ginger and garlic, thickened with Greek yogurt instead of cream. Chickpeas and spinach soak up the sauce, and fluffy cumin millet takes the place of rice. It makes two portions, and **tastes even better the next day**.
steps: Wash the spinach. Rinse the millet and toast it in a dry pot for 2 minutes with the cumin seeds. Add two and a half times its volume of water, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Rest 5 minutes and fluff. Cool what you are saving in a shallow container within 1 hour.
Toss the chicken with half the yogurt, the turmeric, paprika and half the garam masala. Leave it to marinate in the fridge while you start the sauce.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the tomato paste for another minute.

Add the crushed tomatoes and salt and simmer for 8 minutes. Stir in the chicken and chickpeas, cover and cook for 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then the rest of the yogurt and the remaining garam masala so the yogurt does not split.
Serve over the cumin millet. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: To freeze, cool the curry within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C. Freeze it without the millet.

name: Pan-roasted sockeye salmon with romesco, crispy potatoes and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by Catalan romesco with roasted fish
about: Seared sockeye salmon with golden roasted potatoes and tender broccoli, finished with a quick romesco of roasted pepper, tomato and almonds. The sauce is smoky, tangy and a little sweet. The salmon is a rich source of **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and it makes a second plate for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F) and wash the vegetables. Toss the potatoes with half the oil and a pinch of the salt on a large tray (use two trays if they crowd, so they crisp instead of steam), and put the pepper halves cut side down on another tray. Roast the potatoes for 25 minutes, turning once, and the pepper for 15 to 20 minutes, until blistered and soft. Toast the almonds alongside for the last 4 minutes.
Blitz the roasted pepper, almonds, crushed tomato, half the garlic, smoked paprika, vinegar, a spoonful of the oil and a pinch of the salt into a thick, rustic sauce.

Pat the salmon dry and season with a little salt. Sear it in a hot non-stick pan with the rest of the oil, skin side down if it has skin, for 4 minutes, flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Rest it on a clean plate. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Steam the broccoli with the remaining garlic for 4 minutes, until bright and tender, then dress it with the lemon juice.

Serve the salmon on the potatoes with the broccoli, a spoonful of romesco and the parsley. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Fresh salmon is cooked the day you buy it, or bought frozen and thawed in the fridge. Spoon leftover romesco onto potatoes or eggs; it keeps covered in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Beef stroganoff with mushrooms over millet
inspiredBy: Inspired by Russian beef stroganoff and millet kasha
about: Strips of lean sirloin seared hot, then simmered with mushrooms, onion and paprika in a silky sauce finished with Greek yogurt in place of sour cream. It sits on fluffy millet, a nod to Russian kasha. It makes two portions and **reheats beautifully**.
steps: Wash the mushrooms and onion. Rinse the millet and toast it in a dry pot for 2 minutes. Add two and a half times its volume of water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes and fluff. Cool what you are saving within 1 hour.

Pat the beef dry and season it with the pepper. Sear it in a hot pan with half the oil in two batches, 1 to 2 minutes a side, then move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands and the board after handling it raw.

Lower the heat, add the rest of the oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until they have given up their water and browned. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce and a good splash of water and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon.

Return the beef and its juices to the pan and warm through until the beef reaches 71 °C (160 °F). Take the pan off the heat and stir in the yogurt, mustard and half the dill. Do not boil it again or the yogurt will split.
Spoon over the millet and finish with the rest of the dill. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat gently until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Reheat the leftovers gently, on low, stirring: the yogurt sauce can split if it boils hard.

name: Portuguese-style baked cod with sliced potatoes, peppers, onion and parsley
inspiredBy: Inspired by Portuguese bacalhau no forno and bacalhau com grão, made with fresh cod
about: Thick cod fillets baked over thinly sliced potatoes, chickpeas, sweet red pepper and onion with garlic, smoked paprika and a little tomato, then finished with a handful of parsley and lemon. It is a one-tray dinner with **plenty of lean protein**, inspired by the Portuguese way with salt cod, potatoes and chickpeas.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and wash the vegetables. Toss the potatoes, onion, pepper, garlic, chickpeas, smoked paprika, salt and most of the oil in a large baking dish or on a tray (use two trays if they crowd, so they roast instead of steam). Roast for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once, until the potatoes are just tender at the edges.
Pat the cod dry and season it with pepper. Spoon the crushed tomato over the vegetables, nestle the cod on top and drizzle with the rest of the oil.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes, until the fish flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Finish with the lemon juice and the parsley.
tip: Cod is cooked the day it is bought, or thawed overnight in the fridge. Haddock or pollock work the same way.

name: Chicken adobo with crispy potatoes and garlicky green beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by Filipino chicken adobo
about: The Filipino national dish: chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and bay until the sauce is tangy, salty and a little sweet. Crispy roasted potatoes catch the sauce, as they do in many Filipino homes, and quick green beans keep it fresh. It makes two portions, and the flavour **deepens overnight**.
steps: Heat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F) and wash the vegetables. Toss the potatoes with a little of the oil on a tray (use two trays if they crowd, so they crisp instead of steam) and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan and brown the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes a side, then move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

Add the onion and most of the garlic to the pan for 2 minutes. Pour in the soy sauce, vinegar, honey, bay leaf, pepper and the same amount of water as soy sauce and vinegar together, and bring to a boil, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Take the lid off and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes more, until the sauce is a glossy glaze.
Steam the green beans with the last of the garlic for 5 minutes until bright and tender.
Serve the chicken and sauce with the potatoes and green beans. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Use the vinegar you have; cane, coconut or plain white all work. Reduce the sauce a few minutes longer for a thicker glaze.

name: Turkey and oat meatloaf with garlic sweet potato mash and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by the classic North American meatloaf
about: A juicy turkey meatloaf bound with oats and grated carrot, glazed with a sticky tomato and honey topping and served with creamy garlic sweet potato mash. It is Saturday dinner comfort food with **a big hit of protein**, and it makes a second plate for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and wash the vegetables. Mix the turkey with the oats, egg whites, carrot, onion, half the garlic, parsley, most of the salt and the pepper, using your hands, until just combined. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Shape it into a loaf on a lined tray and wash your hands again. Stir the tomato paste, honey and vinegar into a glaze and brush it over the top.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until the loaf reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle. Rest it for 10 minutes before slicing.

Meanwhile boil the sweet potato in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain, saving a splash of the cooking water. Return to the pot with the olive oil, the remaining garlic, a pinch of salt and enough of the water to loosen it, and mash until fluffy.
Steam the broccoli for 4 minutes until bright and tender.
Serve slices of the loaf with the mash and broccoli. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate, and reheat until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Leftover slices reheat well in the oven or a pan, covered, until steaming hot, to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Baked sockeye salmon with parsley salsa verde, green beans and crisp potatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian salsa verde with baked fish
about: Sockeye salmon baked until just flaky and spooned over with a sharp, herby salsa verde of parsley, lemon, garlic and a little mustard, with golden potatoes and green beans. It is a simple one-tray plate, and the salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and wash the vegetables. Toss the potatoes with a third of the oil and a pinch of the salt on a large tray (use two trays if they crowd, so they crisp instead of steam) and roast for 20 minutes, turning once.

Pat the salmon dry, rub with a little oil, salt and pepper, and add it to the tray. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and the potatoes are golden. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Chop the parsley and garlic finely and stir them into the rest of the oil with the lemon juice and zest, mustard and pepper for the salsa verde.
Steam the green beans for 5 minutes until bright and tender.
Serve the salmon with the potatoes and green beans and a big spoonful of the salsa verde.
tip: Fresh salmon is cooked the day you buy it, or bought frozen and thawed in the fridge.

name: Banana berry yogurt smoothie with flax and milk
about: A thick, cold smoothie blended from Greek yogurt, milk, banana, frozen strawberries and ground flax. It drinks like a milkshake but is built from whole foods, with **a good hit of protein** in the glass.
steps: Put the milk, yogurt, banana, strawberries, flax and cinnamon in a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth and thick. Add a splash of milk if it is too thick to pour.
tip: Freeze the banana in chunks for an even thicker, colder smoothie.

name: Cottage cheese with apple, honey and toasted almonds
about: Creamy cottage cheese topped with juicy apple, a drizzle of honey and crunchy toasted almonds. A simple bowl with **a good hit of protein** that tastes like a treat.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and top with the diced apple and almonds, then drizzle with the honey.

name: Paprika deviled eggs with red pepper strips
about: Firm-boiled eggs filled with a creamy mix of yolk, olive oil, lemon and a little mustard, dusted with smoky paprika and served with sweet red pepper strips. It is a classic party snack with **protein and choline**.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, so the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Halve the eggs, scoop the yolks into a bowl and mash with the olive oil, mustard, lemon juice and pepper until smooth.
Spoon the filling back into the whites and dust with paprika. Serve with the red pepper strips. Keep chilled, put any left over back in the fridge within 2 hours, and eat within 3 days.
ingredients: boiled until the yolks are firm

name: Apple slices with a peanut butter cottage cheese dip
about: Crisp apple slices with a creamy dip of peanut butter blended into cottage cheese with a pinch of cinnamon. Sweet, salty and filling, with **protein from the cottage cheese and peanuts**.
steps: Blend or whisk the peanut butter, cottage cheese and cinnamon until smooth.
Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice and serve with the dip.
ingredients: to keep the apple from browning

name: Tuna, caper and parsley stuffed pepper boats
about: Sweet red pepper halves piled with a creamy mix of tuna, cottage cheese, capers, parsley and lemon. A crunchy no-cook snack with **lots of lean protein**.
steps: Mix the tuna with the cottage cheese, capers, parsley, lemon juice, olive oil and pepper.
Spoon the mix into the pepper boats. Tip any leftover tuna into a covered container, chill it and use it within 2 days.

name: Lemon dill chicken bites with a cucumber yogurt dip
about: Little cubes of chicken breast seared with lemon, garlic and paprika, served with a cool dip of Greek yogurt, grated cucumber and dill. They are warm, juicy and packed with **a good hit of protein** for very few calories.
steps: Toss the chicken with half the lemon juice, half the garlic, the paprika and the pepper.
Sear the chicken in a hot non-stick pan with the oil for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until golden and 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

Mix the yogurt with the cucumber, dill, the rest of the lemon juice and garlic, and the salt. Serve the warm bites with the dip. Chill any leftovers within 2 hours and eat them within 3 days, cold or reheated to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Carrot, pepper and spinach egg white frittata bites
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish tortilla and American egg muffins
about: Fluffy baked bites of whisked egg whites with grated carrot, spinach, red pepper and dill, set until completely firm. They are savoury, filling and easy to eat on the move, with **a good hit of protein** from egg whites and very little fat.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and grease as many cups of a muffin tin as you need with a little of the oil.
Cook the carrot and onion in a small pan with the rest of the oil and a splash of water for 4 to 5 minutes, until the carrot is just tender. Stir in the pepper and spinach until the spinach wilts.
Whisk the egg whites with the dill, salt and pepper, and stir in the vegetables. Divide among the muffin cups, filling each about three-quarters full.

Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the bites are puffed, golden, completely firm and 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle. Cool and chill within 2 hours, and eat within 3 days, cold or reheated to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Make a batch of 6 or more bites on Sunday and eat them cold or warmed through. Do not freeze them.

name: Canned salmon and lemon parsley cucumber rounds
about: Flaked canned salmon mixed with a little cottage cheese, lemon, parsley and mustard, piled onto crisp cucumber rounds. A fridge-cold snack with **omega-3 and calcium from the soft salmon bones**.
steps: Flake the salmon in a bowl, mashing the soft bones in well. Mix in the cottage cheese, parsley, lemon juice, mustard and pepper.
Wash the cucumber, cut it into thick rounds and pile the mix on top. Tip any leftover salmon into a covered container, chill it and use it within 2 days.

name: Shakshuka masri, eggs in garlicky tomato and red pepper with baladi bread
inspiredBy: Egyptian shakshuka, the home version with plenty of sweet red pepper, garlic and cumin
