tip: Use the sardines packed in tomato sauce if you like, and then skip some of the crushed tomatoes.

name: Mushroom, white bean and kale barley risotto
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian mushroom risotto, made with barley
about: Pearl barley stirred slowly in broth with browned mushrooms, thyme and white beans, finished with kale, lemon and a little Parmesan. It is creamy without any cream, makes two portions, and the barley and beans bring **fibre**, with mushrooms for B vitamins.
steps: Wash the mushrooms and kale before slicing. Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat and brown the mushrooms for 6 to 7 minutes, until golden. Remove a third and set aside for the top.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes. Stir in the garlic, thyme and barley for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, add the salt and pepper, and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the barley is tender and the liquid is mostly absorbed.
Stir in the white beans and kale for 3 minutes, until the kale wilts and the beans are hot. Add the lemon juice and Parmesan.

Top with the reserved mushrooms and a spoonful of yogurt. Eat one portion now. Spread the second in a shallow container so it cools within 1 hour, refrigerate it, and reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), within 3 days, adding the yogurt cold.
tip: If it thickens in the fridge, loosen it with a splash of broth or water when you reheat.

name: One-pan trout with lemon-dill potatoes and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian fish and dill potatoes
about: Potato chunks and sliced carrot simmered tender in lemony broth, then topped with broccoli and a trout fillet that steams on top, with a quick dill yogurt sauce. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the potatoes bring potassium, with vitamin A from the carrot.
steps: Wash the potatoes, carrot, broccoli and dill. Warm the oil in a large, lidded skillet over medium heat and soften the onion for 3 minutes, then stir in the garlic.
Add the potatoes, carrot, broth, half the lemon juice, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 12 minutes.

Lay the broccoli over the potatoes and the trout on top. Season the trout lightly, cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and the potatoes are tender. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Stir the yogurt with the rest of the lemon juice and half the dill. Spoon it over the fish and scatter on the remaining dill. Refrigerate any extra within 2 hours.
tip: Salmon or arctic char work too.

name: Orange with walnuts
about: A juicy orange with a few walnuts for crunch. It brings **vitamin C** from the orange and plant omega-3 from the walnuts.
steps: Wash the orange before peeling it. Eat it in segments with the walnuts.

name: Carrot and red pepper sticks with peanut butter
about: Crunchy sticks to dip in a spoonful of peanut butter. It brings **protein, fibre and vitamin C**, and the carrot adds vitamin A.
steps: Wash the carrot and pepper, cut them into sticks, and serve with the peanut butter for dipping.

name: Pear with pumpkin seeds
about: A ripe pear with a small handful of pumpkin seeds. The pear brings **fibre**, and the seeds bring magnesium and zinc.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it, and eat it with the seeds.

name: Apple with walnuts
about: A crisp apple with a few walnuts. The apple brings **fibre**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3 and crunch.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it, and eat it with the walnuts.

name: Kiwi with sunflower seeds
about: Two kiwi with a spoonful of sunflower seeds. The kiwi brings **vitamin C and fibre**, and the seeds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash and peel the kiwi, slice it, and eat it with the seeds.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and chili
about: Steamed edamame tossed with lemon and a pinch of chili. A snack that brings **plant protein and folate**.
steps: Heat the frozen edamame in a pot of simmering water for 4 to 5 minutes, until steaming hot. Drain.
Toss with the lemon juice, chili powder and salt.

name: Greek yogurt with cinnamon and walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt with cinnamon and chopped walnuts. It brings **protein and calcium**, with plant omega-3 from the walnuts.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, dust with cinnamon and scatter the walnuts over.

name: Hard-cooked egg with red pepper strips
about: A hard-cooked egg, yolk completely firm, with crunchy red pepper strips and a pinch of cumin. It brings **protein and choline**, and the pepper adds vitamin C.
steps: Lower the egg into a pot of simmering water and cook for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool it under cold water, peel it, and keep it in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Wash the pepper, cut it into strips, and eat with the halved egg sprinkled with the cumin and salt.
ingredients: hard-cooked until the yolk is firm

name: Pear with walnuts
about: A ripe pear with a few walnuts for crunch. The pear brings **fibre**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it, and eat it with the walnuts.

name: Cinnamon apple slices with lemon
about: Crisp apple slices tossed with a squeeze of lemon and a dusting of cinnamon. They bring **fibre and vitamin C**, and keep well for a snack on the go.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it, and toss with the lemon juice and cinnamon. Eat it right away.

name: Orange and kiwi cup with lemon
about: Orange segments and sliced kiwi with a squeeze of lemon, a bright snack that packs well. It brings **vitamin C and fibre**.
steps: Wash the orange and kiwi. Peel the orange and cut it into segments, then peel and slice the kiwi.
Toss together with the lemon juice and eat right away, or pack it in a lidded tub.

name: Banana nut oatmeal with cinnamon
about: Creamy stovetop oats with sliced banana, cinnamon and a crunchy mix of walnuts and almonds. The oats bring **fibre and magnesium**, the nuts bring vitamin E and plant omega-3, and the milk makes it filling.
steps: Bring the milk and oats to a gentle simmer in a small pot with the cinnamon and salt. Stir and cook until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Stir in half of the banana for the last minute so it softens.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the rest of the banana and the walnuts and almonds.
tip: Make a double batch of the dry mix on Sunday so weekday oatmeal is two minutes of work.

name: Scrambled eggs with tomato and spinach on toast
about: Firm scrambled eggs folded with sweet cherry tomatoes and wilted spinach, piled on whole-wheat toast. **Eggs and spinach** bring choline, iron and folate, and the tomatoes add a bright, juicy edge. A glass of milk on the side adds calcium and protein.
steps: Wash the spinach and tomatoes. Quarter the tomatoes and roughly chop the spinach. Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the tomatoes and cook until they soften, about 2 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until it wilts.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently until they are completely set and no liquid egg remains, about 3 minutes.
Toast the bread and pile the eggs on top. Serve with a glass of milk.

name: Yogurt bowl with raspberries, toasted oats and almonds
about: Thick Greek yogurt with raspberries, lightly toasted oats and almonds. The raspberries bring **fibre and vitamin C**, the yogurt brings protein and calcium, and the toasted oats give it a granola crunch.
steps: Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes. Let them cool.
Wash the raspberries.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the raspberries, toasted oats and almonds, and dust with the cinnamon.

name: Lemony salmon and spinach pita
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic tuna salad sandwich, made with canned salmon
about: Flaked canned salmon with yogurt, lemon and parsley, tucked into a warm whole-wheat pita with baby spinach and cucumber. The salmon brings **omega-3 and some vitamin D**, and the soft bones add calcium.
steps: Wash the spinach, cucumber, parsley and carrot. Slice the cucumber, chop the parsley and cut the carrot into sticks.
Flake the salmon into a bowl and mix in the yogurt, lemon juice, parsley and pepper.
Warm the pita in a dry pan or the toaster and open it up.
Fill with the spinach, cucumber and salmon salad and eat with the carrot sticks. Move any salmon left in the tin to a covered container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
If you are packing it, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
ingredients: drained, bones left in and mashed in

name: Greek-style chickpea salad pita
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Greek village salad
about: Chickpeas tossed with cucumber, tomato, red pepper, onion and parsley in a lemony yogurt and olive-oil dressing, stuffed into a whole-wheat pita. **Chickpeas** bring fibre, iron and folate, and the pepper and lemon add vitamin C to help you absorb the iron.
steps: Wash the cucumber, tomatoes, pepper and parsley. Dice the cucumber and pepper, halve the tomatoes, slice the onion very thinly and chop the parsley.
Whisk the yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, oregano and pepper in a bowl. Toss in the chickpeas, vegetables and parsley.
Warm the pita, open it and spoon in the salad.
If you are packing it, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

name: Tuscan-style salmon and white bean salad on toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan tonno e fagioli, made with salmon
about: Creamy white beans and flaked canned salmon with cherry tomatoes, onion, parsley and a firm-cooked egg, dressed with lemon and olive oil and piled on whole-wheat toast. The salmon brings **omega-3 and some vitamin D**, and the egg and beans add choline, fibre and iron.
steps: Cover the egg with cold water in a small pot, bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool it in cold water, peel and cut it into wedges.
Wash the tomatoes and parsley. Halve the tomatoes, slice the onion very thinly and chop the parsley.
Toss the beans, salmon, tomatoes, onion and parsley with the olive oil, lemon juice and pepper.
Toast the bread, spoon the salad on top and tuck in the egg wedges. Move any salmon left in the tin to a covered container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
If you are packing it, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Rinse the beans well to keep the salt down.
ingredients: drained, bones left in and mashed in
hard-boiled until the yolk is firm

name: Pasta e fagioli with beef and kale
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian pasta e fagioli and the Italian-American version made with ground beef
about: A thick, cozy Italian-American soup of white beans, a little lean ground beef, small whole-wheat pasta, tomato and kale, with rosemary and a little Parmesan. The beans and kale bring **fibre, iron and folate**, and it tastes even better the next day.
steps: Wash the carrot, celery and kale. Dice the onion, carrot and celery, mince the garlic, and chop the kale, discarding the thick stems.

Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the beef, breaking it up, until browned and no pink remains, about 5 minutes, then wash your hands, board and spoon after handling the raw beef. Add the onion, carrot, celery and salt and cook until soft, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, rosemary, pepper flakes and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth, 2 cups of water and half of the beans, and bring to a boil. Mash the remaining beans with a fork and stir them in to thicken the soup.
Stir in the pasta and simmer until it is just tender, about 10 minutes, making sure the beef is at least 71 °C (160 °F). Add the kale for the last 3 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with the Parmesan.

Cool the second portion within 1 hour, in a shallow container, then refrigerate it. The pasta drinks the broth overnight, so loosen it with a splash of water when you reheat it once to 74 °C (165 °F). Eat within 3 days.
tip: To freeze, cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days, never refreezing. Reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).
ingredients: small shape such as ditalini or macaroni

name: Lemon garlic chicken with roasted broccoli and potatoes
about: Chicken thighs roasted on one tray with baby potatoes, broccoli and cherry tomatoes in lemon, garlic and oregano. The broccoli and tomatoes bring **vitamin C**, which helps your body absorb the iron from the chicken and potatoes.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a large tray. Scrub the potatoes and cut them into small chunks so they cook quickly.
Toss the potatoes, onion and half of the oil, salt and oregano on the tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Toss the chicken with the garlic, lemon juice, the rest of the oil, salt, oregano and the pepper, then add it to the tray. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.
Roast for 10 minutes, then add the broccoli and tomatoes and roast another 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part and the potatoes are golden.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Salmon, spinach and lemon pasta
about: Whole-wheat penne tossed with flaked pan-seared salmon, wilted spinach, peas and a bright lemon-garlic olive oil sauce. The salmon brings **omega-3 and some vitamin D**, and the spinach and peas add fibre and folate.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the pasta. Wash the spinach and the lemon. Zest half of the lemon, then juice it.

Pat the salmon dry, season with a pinch of the salt and pepper and cook it in a hot nonstick pan with half of the oil, 3 to 4 minutes a side, until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily. Wash your hands, board and anything that touched the raw fish.
Salt the water lightly and cook the pasta until al dente, scooping out a mug of the cooking water before draining. Add the peas for the last 2 minutes and heat until steaming.
In the pasta pot over low heat, warm the remaining oil with the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the pasta, peas, spinach, lemon zest, lemon juice and a splash of pasta water. Toss until the spinach wilts.
Flake the salmon in, toss gently, and finish with the Parmesan and pepper. Eat it fresh; fish is not kept as a leftover in this plan.
ingredients: from the lemon you zest first

name: Turkey meatballs in white bean tomato sauce with garlic toast
about: Tender turkey and spinach meatballs simmered in a garlicky tomato sauce with white beans, carrot and zucchini, served with a slice of whole-wheat garlic toast. Oats keep the meatballs moist, and the beans and spinach bring **iron, fibre and folate**.
steps: Wash the spinach, carrot and zucchini. Finely chop the spinach, grate the onion and carrot, dice the zucchini and mince the garlic.

Mix the turkey, spinach, onion, oats, half of the garlic, half of the salt, the Parmesan and the pepper with wet hands until just combined. Roll into small balls. Wash your hands, board and bowl after handling the raw turkey.
Warm half of the oil in a deep skillet and brown the meatballs on all sides, about 5 minutes. Add the carrot, zucchini and the rest of the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes, beans, basil and the rest of the salt, plus a splash of water. Cover and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until the meatballs reach 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle.
Toast the bread, rub it with the cut side of a clove of garlic if you like, brush with a few drops of the remaining oil and serve with the meatballs.
Pack the second portion into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: To freeze, cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days, never refreezing. Reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).

name: Baked trout with tomatoes, peppers and chickpeas
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian baked fish
about: A trout fillet baked over sweet cherry tomatoes, red pepper and chickpeas with lemon, garlic and parsley. The trout brings **omega-3 and some vitamin D**, and the chickpeas add fibre and iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the pepper, tomatoes and parsley. Halve the tomatoes, cut the pepper into strips and chop the parsley.
Toss the pepper, onion, tomatoes, chickpeas, garlic, half of the oil and half of the salt in a baking dish. Roast for 12 minutes, until the pepper starts to soften.
Rub the trout with the remaining oil, salt and pepper and nestle it on top of the vegetables. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the trout reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and scatter with the parsley.

name: Lentil and mushroom bolognese with fusilli
inspiredBy: Inspired by Bolognese ragu
about: A rich, meaty-tasting ragu of lentils, browned cremini mushrooms and sweet red pepper simmered with tomato and basil, over whole-wheat fusilli. The lentils and mushrooms bring **fibre, iron, folate and B vitamins** with no meat.
steps: Wash the mushrooms, pepper and kale. Finely chop the mushrooms, dice the pepper and onion, mince the garlic and shred the kale.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms, stirring now and then, until they release their water and turn golden, about 8 minutes. Add the onion, pepper and salt and cook for 4 minutes more.

Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the crushed tomatoes, lentils, basil, pepper and 1 cup of water. Simmer for 15 minutes, until thick, adding the kale for the last 3 minutes. Stir in the lemon juice.
Meanwhile boil the fusilli in lightly salted water until al dente, then drain.
Toss the pasta with the ragu and finish with the Parmesan.
tip: Double the ragu and freeze half: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Boil fresh pasta each time.

name: Tuscan-style beef stew with potatoes and kale
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan beef stews
about: A slow-simmered stew of lean beef, potato, carrot, celery and kale in a tomato-rosemary broth. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, the kale and carrot bring vitamin A, and a squeeze of lemon at the end brightens the pot.
steps: Wash the carrot, celery, potato and kale. Dice the carrot, celery and onion, mince the garlic, cut the potato into chunks and chop the kale.
Warm the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches, then set aside. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw beef.
Lower the heat and cook the onion, carrot, celery and salt for 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, rosemary and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Return the beef with the tomatoes, broth, bay leaf and 1 cup of water. Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, until the beef is nearly tender.
Stir in the potato and simmer 20 minutes more, adding the kale for the last 5 minutes. Check that the beef is tender and at least 71 °C (160 °F).

Remove the bay leaf, stir in the lemon juice and pepper and ladle into bowls. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, refrigerate it and eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: In a pressure cooker, the stew takes about 35 minutes. To freeze, cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days, never refreezing.
ingredients: trimmed and cut into bite-sized cubes

name: Orange with almonds
about: A juicy orange with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange, peel and segment it, and serve with the almonds.

name: Pear with walnuts
about: A juicy pear with a few walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it and serve with the walnuts.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A banana with a few walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3**, and the banana brings potassium.
steps: Peel the banana, slice it and serve with the walnuts and cinnamon.

name: Raspberries with yogurt and walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt over raspberries with a few walnuts. The raspberries bring **fibre and vitamin C**, the yogurt adds protein and calcium, and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the raspberries, spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the berries and walnuts.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and chili
about: Steamed edamame with lemon and a pinch of chili. The edamame brings **protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 to 4 minutes, until steaming hot all the way through. Drain.
Toss with the lemon juice, chili and salt.

name: Italian roasted chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with garlic, oregano and a pinch of pepper flakes. They bring **fibre, iron and protein** and keep for a few days in a jar.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Pat the chickpeas very dry.
Toss with the oil, oregano, garlic powder, pepper flakes and salt on a tray.
Roast, shaking once, for 25 to 28 minutes, until crisp. They crisp more as they cool.

name: Carrot and cucumber sticks with lemony yogurt dip
about: Crunchy carrot and cucumber sticks with a creamy yogurt dip brightened with lemon and parsley. The carrots bring **vitamin A**, and the yogurt adds protein and calcium.
steps: Wash the carrot, cucumber and parsley. Cut the vegetables into sticks and chop the parsley.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice, parsley and pepper and serve with the sticks.

name: Hard-boiled egg with cherry tomatoes and basil
about: A firm hard-boiled egg with juicy cherry tomatoes, basil and black pepper. The egg brings **choline and protein**, and the tomatoes add a little vitamin C.
steps: Cover the egg with cold water in a small pot, bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool it in cold water and peel.
Wash the tomatoes and halve them.
Slice the egg over the tomatoes, add a pinch of basil, the salt and pepper.
ingredients: hard-boiled until the yolk is firm

name: Pear with almonds
about: A ripe pear with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it and serve with the almonds.

name: Orange with walnuts
about: A juicy orange with a few walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange, peel and segment it, and serve with the walnuts.

name: Salmon and dill dip with veg sticks
about: Canned salmon mashed with yogurt, lemon, dill and a pinch of garlic into a creamy dip, with crunchy cucumber and carrot sticks. It brings **omega-3 and some vitamin D**, and it's a good way to finish an opened tin.
steps: Wash the cucumber and carrot and cut them into sticks.
Mash the salmon with the yogurt, lemon juice, dill, garlic powder and pepper until creamy.
Serve with the sticks. Move any salmon left in the tin to a covered container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
ingredients: drained, bones left in and mashed in

name: Thick yogurt with grated apple, walnuts and toasted oats
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek yiaourti me karydia, with a bircher-style grated apple
about: Thick Greek yogurt with a grated apple, cinnamon, chopped walnuts and a handful of toasted oats. It is cool, crunchy and ready in minutes. The **yogurt brings plenty of protein**, and the oats, apple skin and nuts add fibre so the fruit digests slowly.
steps: Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking now and then, until they smell nutty. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Wash the apple and grate it on the large holes of a box grater, skin and all.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and stir in half the apple and the cinnamon. Top with the rest of the apple.
Scatter on the walnuts and the toasted oats.
tip: Toast a jar of oats on Sunday and breakfast takes two minutes.

name: Levantine breakfast plate with eggs, labneh and za'atar
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Lebanese and Palestinian breakfast table of eggs, labneh, olives and fresh vegetables
about: Two hard-boiled eggs with a smear of labneh dusted with za'atar, cucumber, tomato, olives and a small wholewheat pita. It is a proper sit-down breakfast with very little starch. The **eggs and labneh carry protein**, and the fresh vegetables add fibre.
steps: Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolks are completely set. Cool them under cold running water and peel.
Spread the labneh on a plate, make a shallow dip in the middle and spoon in the olive oil. Dust with the za'atar.
Wash the cucumber, tomato and mint. Arrange the cucumber, tomato wedges, olives and mint around it.
Warm the pita in a dry pan or toaster and serve it with the halved eggs.
tip: Boil a few eggs on Sunday and keep them in their shells in the fridge for up to 7 days, and peel them just before eating.

name: Shakshuka with chickpeas and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by shakshuka from across the Levant and North Africa, with chickpeas for body
about: Eggs set in a cumin and paprika tomato and pepper sauce with chickpeas and wilted spinach. It makes two portions of sauce: the eggs go in fresh each morning. The eggs and chickpeas bring **protein and fibre**, and the tomato sauce brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach and parsley. Warm the olive oil in a wide, deep pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper for about 8 minutes, until soft and just starting to colour.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and paprika for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, chickpeas and salt and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick. Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Set aside half the sauce for tomorrow. Make two wells in the rest and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook gently for 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites and the yolks are set.
Scatter with parsley. Chill the saved sauce in a shallow container within 1 hour. Tomorrow, reheat it once to 74C (165F), then cook fresh eggs in it for 6 to 8 minutes until set.
tip: Serve with a spoonful of thick yogurt on the side if you like it cool and tangy.

name: Sardine, chickpea and parsley salad with lemon and sumac
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine chickpea salads and the Spanish and Greek habit of tinned fish with beans
about: Sardines, chickpeas, spinach, carrot, cucumber, tomato and a big handful of parsley under a sharp lemon, olive oil and sumac dressing. It is cool, crunchy and filling without any bread. The **sardines bring omega-3 fats** and the chickpeas bring fibre.
steps: Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, sumac and a pinch of oregano.
Wash the spinach, carrot, cucumber, tomatoes and parsley. Toss the chickpeas, spinach, carrot, cucumber, tomatoes, red onion and parsley in a large bowl.
Break the sardines into chunks over the top and drizzle with the dressing.
Toss gently at the table.
tip: Eat the salad within a day, and pack the dressing separately if you take it to work.

name: Chicken shawarma tray with cauliflower, chickpeas and tahini yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine chicken shawarma, roasted on a tray instead of a spit
about: Chicken thighs rubbed with cumin, coriander, allspice and paprika, roasted with cauliflower, carrot, onion and chickpeas until the edges catch. It is served with a cool tahini and lemon yogurt. It makes two portions, and the chickpeas and cauliflower give you **plenty of fibre alongside the protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C (425F). Mix the cumin, coriander, allspice, paprika, garlic, salt and half the olive oil, and rub it all over the chicken. Cover the chicken and leave it in the fridge for 15 minutes. Wash your hands, the board and the spoon before touching the vegetables.
Wash the cauliflower, carrot and parsley. Toss the cauliflower, carrot, chickpeas and onion with the rest of the oil on a large tray and push them to the sides.
Lay the chicken in the middle and roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning the vegetables once, until the cauliflower is browned and the chicken reads 74C (165F) in the thickest piece.
Stir the yogurt, tahini and lemon juice with a spoon of water until smooth.

Slice the chicken, spoon over the sauce and scatter with parsley. Spread the second portion of chicken and vegetables in a shallow container and keep its sauce in a separate small jar. Refrigerate both within 1 hour, reheat the chicken and vegetables once to 74C (165F) all the way through, and spoon the cold sauce on top.
tip: Keep the second portion up to 3 days in the fridge. Roast a second tray of cauliflower alongside if you like it as a side; it keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge.

name: Roasted salmon with warm lentils, tomato and parsley
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian lenticchie and the Greek love of lentils with fish
about: A salmon fillet roasted over a tray of tomatoes, with warm lentils dressed in olive oil, lemon and plenty of parsley. It is a simple weeknight plate with a bright finish. The **salmon brings omega-3 fats**, and the lentils bring fibre and protein.
steps: Wash the tomatoes, carrot, spinach and parsley. Rinse the lentils and simmer them with the bay leaf in plenty of water for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender but not mushy. Drain and discard the bay leaf.
While they cook, heat the oven to 200C (400F). Spread the tomatoes on a tray with half the oil and a pinch of salt and roast for 10 minutes.
Nestle the salmon among the tomatoes, season, and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and is opaque all the way through (70C / 158F in the thickest part).
Soften the onion, carrot and garlic in the rest of the oil for 6 minutes. Stir in the lentils and spinach until the spinach wilts, then add the lemon juice, parsley and the remaining salt.
Serve the lentils topped with the salmon and the roasted tomatoes.
tip: Cook a double batch of lentils: cool them in a shallow tray, refrigerate within 1 hour, keep 3 to 4 days and reheat to 74C (165F).

name: Lemony lentil and chard soup with yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Lebanese adas bi hamod, the lemony lentil and chard soup
about: A thick, sharp lentil soup with chard, garlic and plenty of lemon, finished with a spoon of thick yogurt. The **lentils and chard bring fibre and folate**.
steps: Wash the chard and parsley. Soften the onion in the olive oil in a pot for 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the rinsed lentils and about 5 times their volume of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils fall apart.
Add the chard and salt and cook for another 8 minutes, until the stems are tender.
Stir in the lemon juice and taste; it should be quite sharp.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the yogurt and parsley.
tip: Double the pot and freeze portions: cool within 1 hour before freezing. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days and reheat to 74C (165F). It keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge.

name: Turkey and parsley kofta with bulgur tabbouleh
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine kofta kebabs and tabbouleh, with more herbs than grain
about: Spiced turkey and parsley kofta, browned in a pan, with a green tabbouleh that is mostly parsley, tomato, cucumber and mint with a little bulgur and chickpeas. A cool yogurt sauce ties it together. It makes two portions, and the **lean turkey keeps it high in protein**.
steps: Pour boiling water over the bulgur in a bowl, just enough to cover, and leave it for 15 minutes until tender. Drain well and squeeze out the excess water. Soaked bulgur is a cooked grain, so chill any portion you save within 1 hour.

Wash the parsley, mint, tomato and cucumber. Mix the turkey with the grated onion (do not squeeze it; its juice keeps lean turkey moist), a third of the parsley, the allspice, cumin and half the salt. Shape into 8 small oval kofta, then wash your hands.
Brown the kofta in half the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned. Stop as soon as a thermometer in a kofta reads 74C (165F).
Toss the bulgur with the chickpeas, tomato, cucumber, the rest of the parsley, the mint, lemon juice, remaining oil and salt.

Stir a pinch of salt and some lemon into the yogurt and serve it alongside. Pack the kofta for the second portion in a shallow container and the tabbouleh and yogurt in separate ones, and refrigerate them all within 1 hour. Tomorrow, reheat only the kofta, once, to 74C (165F) all the way through, and eat the tabbouleh and yogurt cold.
tip: Make the kofta mix the night before, keep it covered in the fridge and cook it the next day.

name: Chicken souvlaki with barley, tomato and cucumber salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek chicken souvlaki, served with a barley salad in place of pita
about: Lemony, oregano-rubbed chicken thigh skewers with a chunky barley, tomato and cucumber salad and a yogurt and garlic sauce. It is the taverna plate, with barley instead of fries. The **barley and vegetables bring fibre**, and the skinless chicken thigh keeps the saturated fat low. It makes two portions.
steps: Cover the pearl barley with plenty of water and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes (hulled barley takes about 45), until tender but still chewy. Drain, spread it on a tray to cool, then refrigerate within 1 hour if you are not using it right away.

Toss the chicken with half the oil, half the lemon juice, the oregano, half the garlic and a pinch of salt. Cover and leave it at least 20 minutes in the fridge, or overnight. Throw away any leftover marinade and never brush it on cooked chicken. Wash your hands and the board.
Thread the chicken onto skewers and grill or pan-sear over medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and the chicken reads 74C (165F).
Wash the tomato, cucumber and parsley. Toss the barley with the tomato, cucumber, red onion, parsley, the remaining oil, lemon and salt.

Stir the rest of the garlic and a pinch of salt into the yogurt. Serve the skewers on the salad with the sauce. Spread the second portion in a shallow container, refrigerate it within 1 hour, and reheat the chicken once to 74C (165F) all the way through.
tip: Marinate the chicken the night before and dinner is half done. The second portion keeps up to 3 days.

name: Roasted mackerel with peppers and white beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish pisto and the Greek and Turkish habit of grilled mackerel with a sharp salad
about: A mackerel fillet with sweet roasted peppers, tomato, and white beans warmed in olive oil and lemon. The fish is rich and the beans are mellow, so it all balances. **Mackerel is rich in omega-3**, and the beans bring fibre.
steps: Wash the pepper, tomatoes, spinach and parsley. Heat the oven to 220C (425F). Toss the pepper strips, onion and tomatoes with half the oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.

Rub the mackerel with a little of the remaining oil, the paprika and a pinch of salt and lay it on the tray. Roast 8 to 10 minutes, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily (70C / 158F in the thickest part).
Meanwhile warm the garlic in the rest of the oil in a pan for 1 minute. Add the beans and spinach with a splash of water and cook for 3 minutes, until the spinach is wilted.
Stir the lemon juice and parsley into the beans.
Serve the fish on the beans with the roasted vegetables.
tip: Sardines work just as well if mackerel is hard to find. Use Atlantic mackerel; king mackerel is high in mercury.

name: Lentils and bulgur with sweet onions and cucumber yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Lebanese mujaddara, with bulgur and more lentils than rice
about: Brown lentils and bulgur cooked with cumin and topped with slow-browned onions, with a cold cucumber yogurt on the side. It is humble and deeply savoury. The **lentils and yogurt give it protein and fibre**, and the onions give it the sweetness.
steps: Wash the cucumber and spinach. Cook the onions in two thirds of the oil (keep the rest for the yogurt) over medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until deep golden brown.

Simmer the rinsed lentils in about 4 times their volume of water for 15 minutes. Stir in the cumin, half the onions, the bulgur and salt, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. If it is still wet, cook uncovered for a few minutes more.
Stir the spinach in at the end until wilted and leave to steam for 5 minutes. Cool any leftover lentils and bulgur within 1 hour.
Mix the yogurt, grated cucumber, garlic, mint and the rest of the oil.
Pile the lentils on a plate, top with the rest of the onions and serve with the yogurt.
tip: Brown a double batch of onions; they keep up to 4 days in the fridge. A cooked portion of lentils and bulgur freezes well: thaw it in the fridge, use within 2 days and reheat to 74C (165F).

name: Lighter moussaka with lentils and lean beef
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek moussaka, with roasted eggplant, a lentil and beef sauce and a yogurt topping
about: Layers of roasted eggplant, a cinnamon-scented tomato sauce of lean beef and lentils, and a golden yogurt and egg topping. It is the Sunday-style bake, with a yogurt and egg topping in place of the béchamel. It makes two portions, and the **lentils stretch the beef** and bring fibre.
steps: Wash the eggplant and parsley. Heat the oven to 220C (425F). Brush the eggplant slices with half the oil, lay them on trays and roast for 20 minutes, turning once, until soft and golden.
Simmer the rinsed lentils in water for 20 minutes, until tender. Drain.

Brown the onion in the rest of the oil for 6 minutes. Add the beef and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains (71C / 160F). Stir in the garlic, cinnamon, oregano, crushed tomatoes, lentils and salt and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick.
Layer half the eggplant, the sauce, and the rest of the eggplant in a baking dish. Beat the yogurt with the egg, nutmeg and a pinch of salt and spread it on top.

Bake at 190C (375F) for 30 minutes, until the topping is set and golden and the centre reads 74C (165F). Rest for 10 minutes and scatter with parsley. Spread the second portion in a shallow container, refrigerate it within 1 hour, and reheat it once to 74C (165F) all the way through.
tip: To make ahead, cool the sauce within 1 hour, assemble cold, refrigerate and bake it within a day. Bake from the fridge, adding about 10 minutes, until the centre reads 74C (165F). The second portion keeps up to 3 days.

name: Roasted trout with fennel, olives and white beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Italian and Greek way with baked fish, fennel and olives
about: A trout fillet roasted over sliced fennel and tomatoes, with white beans and olives. It is fresh and savoury. **Trout carries omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the beans and fennel bring fibre.
steps: Wash the fennel, tomatoes and parsley. Heat the oven to 200C (400F). Toss the fennel, tomatoes, garlic, thyme and half the oil on a tray and roast for 15 minutes, until the fennel softens.
Stir in the white beans and olives and move the vegetables to the edges.

Season the trout with salt and the rest of the oil and lay it in the middle. Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the flesh flakes easily and is opaque all the way through (70C / 158F in the thickest part).
Squeeze over the lemon juice and scatter with parsley.
tip: Use salmon if trout is not available.

name: Lemony hummus with carrot, cucumber and pepper sticks
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine hummus bi tahini
about: Smooth lemony hummus made from chickpeas and tahini, with crunchy raw vegetables. The **chickpeas and tahini bring protein**, so it holds you between meals.
steps: Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt and 2 tablespoons of cold water until very smooth, scraping down the sides.
Wash and cut the carrot, cucumber and pepper into sticks.
Serve the hummus in a bowl with the vegetables for dipping.

name: Pear with a handful of walnuts
about: A crisp pear with skin on and a small handful of walnuts. The **walnuts add omega-3 fats**, so the fruit does not stand alone.
steps: Wash the pear and slice it.
Serve it with the walnuts.

name: Roasted red pepper and walnut dip with fennel and carrot
inspiredBy: Inspired by Syrian muhammara, with less oil and more pepper
about: A sweet-sharp dip of roasted red pepper, walnuts and pomegranate molasses, with a few chickpeas blended in where the classic uses breadcrumbs, served with raw vegetables. The **walnuts add omega-3** and the vegetables add crunch and fibre.
steps: Roast the pepper under a hot broiler, turning, until blackened all over, then cover it for 5 minutes, peel and seed it.
Blend the pepper, walnuts, chickpeas, pomegranate molasses, oil, lemon juice and cumin to a thick, slightly textured dip.
Wash the fennel and carrot, cut them into sticks and serve with the dip.
tip: A jar of roasted peppers works in a pinch; rinse them first.

name: Labneh with za'atar, cucumber and olives
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Levantine labneh plate
about: A spoon of thick labneh dusted with za'atar and drizzled with olive oil, with cucumber and a few olives. The **labneh brings protein and calcium** without much starch.
steps: Spread the labneh on a small plate and make a dip in the middle.
Drizzle in the olive oil and dust with za'atar.
Serve with the cucumber, tomato and olives.

name: Orange with walnuts
about: A juicy orange and a small handful of walnuts. The **walnuts add fat and fibre**, which slows the fruit down.
steps: Peel the orange and break it into segments.
Serve with the walnuts.

name: Pear with almonds and walnuts
about: A crisp pear with the skin on, a few almonds and a few walnuts. The **nuts bring vitamin E and omega-3**, so the fruit does not stand alone.
steps: Wash the pear and slice it.
Serve it with the almonds and walnuts.

name: Thick yogurt with cinnamon and toasted almonds
about: Cool Greek yogurt with cinnamon and a few toasted almonds. The **yogurt brings protein and calcium**, and the almonds add crunch and vitamin E.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until fragrant, then chop roughly.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and dust with cinnamon.
Scatter the almonds on top.

name: Sardines on tomato with lemon and a little pita
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Spanish and Greek bar snack of tinned sardines with tomato
about: Tinned sardines with ripe tomato, parsley and a squeeze of lemon, with a small piece of wholewheat pita. The **sardines bring omega-3 fats and calcium** from the soft bones.
steps: Toast the pita and tear it into pieces.
Wash and slice the tomato and lay the slices on a plate and top with the sardines, broken into chunks.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and scatter with parsley, with the pita alongside.
tip: Keep the rest of the tin in a lidded container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

name: Lupini beans with lemon, parsley and toasted almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Italian and Spanish bar snack of lupini beans
about: Lupini beans tossed with lemon, olive oil and parsley, with a few toasted almonds for crunch. They are a savoury, high-protein bar snack. The **lupini beans carry protein and fibre**, and the almonds add vitamin E.
steps: Rinse the lupini beans well and pat them dry.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until fragrant, then chop roughly.
Toss the lupini with the lemon juice, olive oil, parsley and almonds.
tip: Use jarred lupini only, never dried. Lupin is an allergen and can cross-react with peanut, so skip it if you are allergic to peanuts. Refrigerate an opened jar.

name: Orange with almonds
about: A juicy orange and a small handful of almonds. The **almonds add vitamin E and fibre**, and the orange adds vitamin C.
steps: Peel the orange and break it into segments.
Serve with the almonds.

name: Moong chilla with paneer and spinach, mint yogurt dip
inspiredBy: Punjabi and Gujarati moong dal cheela, filled the way a street stall folds it
about: Thin, golden pancakes of ground yellow moong dal with onion, grated carrot and spinach, folded around a little crumbled paneer and served with a cool mint yogurt dip. Moong dal and paneer together make this a breakfast with **plenty of protein and fibre**.
steps: Drain the soaked dal and blend it with the ginger, half the green chili, the hing, the turmeric, the salt and a few spoonfuls of cold water until smooth. The batter should pour like thin pancake batter.
Stir the spinach, carrot, onion, cumin and half the cilantro into the batter.
Mash the paneer with the chaat masala and the rest of the cilantro. For the dip, blitz or stir the yogurt with the mint, the rest of the green chili and a pinch of salt.

Warm a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe it with a little of the oil. Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it into a thin round. Cook until the top looks set and the underside is golden with brown spots, about 3 minutes.
Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edge, flip and cook for 1 minute more. Spoon some paneer down the middle and fold. Repeat with the rest and serve hot with the dip.
tip: Soak the dal the night before and mornings take about 25 minutes. If a chilla tears, the pan is too cool or the batter too thick.
ingredients: split yellow moong dal, soaked for 4 hours or overnight
half in the batter, half in the dip
half in the batter, half in the paneer

name: Masala egg bhurji with a small whole-wheat roti
inspiredBy: Pakistani and Punjabi anda bhurji with peas
about: Soft, well-set scrambled eggs with onion, tomato, green peas, spinach and ginger, scooped up with a small whole-wheat roti and a bowl of cold yogurt. The eggs and yogurt bring **protein to start the day**, and the roti adds whole grain.
steps: Mix the atta with a pinch of salt and enough warm water to make a soft dough. Cover it and rest while you make the bhurji.
Warm the oil in a pan, add the cumin and let it sizzle, then the onion, ginger and green chili. Cook until the onion is soft and golden, about 6 minutes.
Add the tomato, peas, spinach, turmeric and Kashmiri chili. Cook until the tomato breaks down, the spinach wilts and the peas are tender, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the eggs and the salt. Stir gently over medium-low heat until the eggs are completely set with no runny egg left, about 3 minutes. Stir in the cilantro.
Roll the dough into a thin round and cook it on a hot dry pan, turning once, until it has brown spots and puffs a little. Serve with the bhurji and the yogurt.
tip: Roll and cook two or three extra rotis on Sunday evening and they reheat fine in a dry pan.

name: Foxtail millet and moong pongal with curd
inspiredBy: Tamil ven pongal, made with thinai (foxtail millet) in place of rice
about: A soft, peppery pongal of foxtail millet and split moong dal, tempered with ghee, black pepper, cumin and curry leaves, with carrot and green peas stirred through. A bowl of curd on the side adds **protein and calcium**.
steps: Rinse the millet and dal together. Put them in a pot with the carrot, peas, ginger, the salt and about four times their volume of water.

Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat, stirring now and then, until the millet and dal are very soft and a little porridge-like, about 25 minutes. Add a splash of hot water if it gets too thick.
In a small pan, warm the ghee. Add the cumin, the black pepper, the curry leaves and the hing. Sizzle for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Pour the tempering over the pongal and stir well. Serve hot with the yogurt.
tip: Make a double pot the evening before, chill it within 1 hour, and reheat it with a splash of water to 74 C (165 F) once.
ingredients: plain, with a pinch of cumin

name: Punjabi rajma masala with brown basmati and cucumber raita
inspiredBy: Punjabi rajma chawal, with brown basmati and a big bowl of raita
about: Kidney beans simmered in a thick onion-tomato masala, with a small mound of brown basmati and a cool cucumber raita on the side. The beans and yogurt together carry **protein and fibre**, and the rice soaks up the gravy.
steps: Drain the soaked rajma, cover with fresh water and boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer until the beans are completely soft and mash easily between your fingers, about 45 minutes (20 minutes in a pressure cooker).
Meanwhile, cook the brown basmati in plenty of boiling water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain.
Warm the oil in a pan, add the cumin and bay leaf, then the onion. Cook until deep golden, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, Kashmiri chili, ground coriander and salt. Cook until the tomato collapses and the oil separates, about 6 minutes.
Add the beans with their cooking water. Simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side to thicken the gravy. Stir in the garam masala and half the cilantro.
Stir the grated cucumber and the rest of the cilantro into the yogurt with a pinch of salt. Serve the rajma over the rice with the raita on the side.
tip: Cook the beans in a pressure cooker and the whole dish takes about 40 minutes. Squeeze the grated cucumber first so the raita stays thick.

name: Tandoori chicken tikka with missi roti and kachumber
inspiredBy: Punjabi chicken tikka, baked in the oven, with besan and whole-wheat missi roti
about: Chunks of chicken marinated in yogurt, ginger, garlic and Kashmiri chili, baked until charred at the edges, with a crunchy carrot kachumber and a small missi roti made with chickpea flour. Dinner is **high in protein**, and the second portion becomes tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Mix half the yogurt with most of the lemon juice, grated ginger and garlic, Kashmiri chili, garam masala and half the salt. Spoon a little of the marinade into a small bowl for the cauliflower, then coat the chicken in the rest. Never reuse marinade that touched raw chicken. Cover and marinate the chicken in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight, and wash the board and your hands after.

Heat the oven to 230 C (450 F). Spread the chicken and the cauliflower florets (tossed with the marinade you set aside) on a rack set over a tray and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until the edges are charred and there is no pink inside. Check the thickest piece with a thermometer: it should read 74 C (165 F).

For the missi roti, mix the atta, the besan, the ajwain (rubbed between your palms) and a pinch of salt with a little oil and warm water into a soft dough. Rest for 10 minutes, then roll into thin rounds and cook on a hot dry pan until brown-spotted.

Make the kachumber: toss the tomato, grated carrot and onion with the chaat masala and the rest of the lemon juice. Stir the chopped mint and a pinch of salt into the rest of the yogurt for the raita.

Serve half the chicken with a roti, the kachumber and the raita. Spread the second portion in a shallow dish, cool it, refrigerate it within 1 hour and pack it for tomorrow's lunch. Reheat once, until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through.
tip: Roll and cook all the rotis fresh; they are best warm. The leftover chicken is lovely in a dry pan with a squeeze of lemon.
ingredients: half for the marinade, half for the mint raita

name: Masoor dal with spinach, a small roti and cucumber raita
inspiredBy: Punjabi dal palak with pink lentils
about: Quick-cooking pink lentils simmered with a big pile of spinach and finished with a sizzling garlic and cumin tadka. A small whole-wheat roti and a cool cucumber raita turn it into a lunch with **protein and iron**.
steps: Put the lentils in a pot with the turmeric, tomato and about four times their volume of water. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam. Simmer until completely soft, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and a pinch of salt and cook for 3 minutes more until wilted. Mash the dal lightly with a spoon.
Warm the oil and ghee in a small pan. Add the cumin, then the onion, garlic and ginger. Cook until the onion is golden, about 6 minutes. Add the Kashmiri chili and pour the tadka over the dal.
Mix the atta with a pinch of salt and warm water into a soft dough, rest it for 10 minutes, then roll thin and cook on a hot dry pan until brown-spotted.
Stir the cucumber and a pinch of salt into the yogurt. Serve the dal with the roti and the raita.
tip: Frozen spinach works: use it straight from the freezer and cook a minute longer.

name: Tandoori-style salmon with roasted cauliflower and carrot and chickpea kachumber
inspiredBy: Punjabi and Pakistani tandoori machli, baked in the oven
about: Salmon fillet marinated in yogurt, lemon and Kashmiri chili, baked until it flakes, with roasted cauliflower, carrots and a chickpea kachumber. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas, carrot and cauliflower carry the fibre.
steps: Mix half the yogurt with half the lemon juice, grated ginger and garlic, Kashmiri chili, ajwain and half the salt. Coat the salmon, cover and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F). Toss the cauliflower and carrot with the oil, ground cumin and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 10 minutes.

Add the salmon to the tray, skin side down, and roast for another 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork (70 C / 158 F in the thickest part) and the cauliflower is browned at the edges.
Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, onion and the chaat masala with the rest of the lemon juice for the kachumber.
Stir the chopped mint into the rest of the yogurt with a pinch of salt. Serve the salmon on the kachumber with the roasted vegetables and a spoon of mint yogurt.
tip: Skin-on salmon holds together best. Eat this fresh rather than as a leftover.
ingredients: skin-on fillet, cut into two pieces
half for the marinade, half for the mint drizzle

name: Chicken keema matar with jowar roti
inspiredBy: Punjabi and Pakistani keema matar, with minced chicken and a Gujarati-style jowar roti
about: Minced chicken thigh cooked down with onion, tomato, ginger, finely chopped cauliflower and sweet green peas, with a handful of cilantro to finish and a jowar (sorghum) roti. It is **rich in protein**, the peas add fibre, and the second portion is ready for tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Warm the oil in a wide pan, add the cumin, then the chopped onion. Cook until deep golden, about 8 minutes. Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, turmeric, Kashmiri chili, ground coriander and salt. Cook until the tomato collapses and the oil separates, about 6 minutes.

Add the minced chicken and break it up with a spoon. Cook, stirring, until it is no longer pink, then add the peas, the cauliflower and a splash of water. Cover and simmer for 12 minutes until a thermometer in the meat reads 74 C (165 F) and the peas are tender.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt and the garam masala, and finish with the cilantro.

For the roti, knead the jowar flour with a pinch of salt and hot water into a soft dough while it is warm. Divide it into two balls, one for each portion, and pat them out on a damp cloth or between two sheets of parchment, then lift onto a hot dry pan and cook until brown-spotted. Jowar is delicate, so be gentle.

Toss the sliced onion with the lemon juice and the chaat masala for a quick laccha pyaaz, and serve half the keema with the roti and the onion. Spread the second portion in a shallow dish, cool it, refrigerate it within 1 hour and reheat once tomorrow, until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through. Wrap the second roti in a clean cloth and pack it with the keema.
tip: No jowar flour? Use whole-wheat atta. Keema freezes well for up to 3 months: thaw it in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and reheat it once until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through.
ingredients: skinless, minced by the butcher or pulsed in a food processor
half finely chopped for the keema, half thinly sliced for the side
whisked, stirred in off the heat

name: Vegetable sambar with foxtail millet and curd
inspiredBy: Tamil Nadu sambar with drumstick and brinjal, served over millet
about: A tangy toor dal sambar with drumstick, brinjal and carrot, spooned over foxtail millet with a bowl of curd on the side. The dal and curd give it **protein and fibre**, and the second portion is lunch tomorrow.
steps: Cook the toor dal with the turmeric and about four times its volume of water until completely soft, about 25 minutes (10 minutes in a pressure cooker). Mash lightly.
In another pot, simmer the drumstick, brinjal, carrot, onion and tomato in a little water with the tamarind paste, sambar powder and salt until the vegetables are just tender, about 12 minutes.
Stir the dal into the vegetables and simmer for 8 minutes. Add water if it is too thick, as sambar should be pourable.
Cook the millet in two and a half times its volume of water until fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Warm the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds, and when they pop, the curry leaves and hing. Pour the tempering into the sambar.

Serve the sambar over the millet with the curd on the side. Cool the second portion in a shallow dish, refrigerate it within 1 hour and reheat once tomorrow, until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through.
tip: Drumstick pods are chewed and the tough fibre left on the plate. Frozen drumstick works well.
ingredients: plain, as curd on the side

name: Pepper mackerel fry with cabbage poriyal and millet
inspiredBy: Tamil Nadu milagu meen varuval, with a Tamil-style cabbage poriyal
about: Atlantic mackerel fillet rubbed with crushed black pepper, ginger and curry leaves and pan-fried until crisp, with a quick cabbage poriyal tempered with chana dal and fresh coconut. The mackerel is rich in **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**.
steps: Mix the crushed pepper, grated ginger and garlic, half the lemon juice, turmeric, Kashmiri chili and half the salt into a paste. Rub it over the mackerel and rest for 15 minutes.
Cook the millet in two and a half times its volume of water until fluffy, about 15 minutes.

Warm half the oil in a non-stick pan. Fry the mackerel with half the curry leaves for about 4 minutes on each side, until crisp and golden and the fish flakes easily (70 C / 158 F in the thickest part).
For the poriyal, warm the rest of the oil. Add the mustard seeds, and when they pop, the chana dal and the rest of the curry leaves. Cook until the dal is golden, about 1 minute.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then the cabbage, the rest of the salt and a splash of water. Cover and cook until just tender, about 5 minutes. Stir in the coconut.
Serve the fish with the poriyal and the millet, with the rest of the lemon squeezed over.
tip: Make the poriyal while the fish rests. Use Atlantic mackerel, or Indian mackerel (ayala or bangda), not kingfish, surmai or vanjaram, which are higher in mercury. Thaw frozen fillets in the fridge and cook them within 2 days. Cook the fish fresh and do not keep it as a leftover.

name: Gujarati-style sprouted moong usal with jowar roti and curd
inspiredBy: Gujarati and Maharashtrian usal, with whole moong cooked until completely soft
about: Whole green moong, sprouted for a day and then simmered with onion, tomato and a little coconut, with a small jowar roti and a bowl of curd. Sprouted moong cooks quickly and gives **protein and plenty of fibre**.
steps: Rinse the sprouted moong. Sprouted beans must be cooked thoroughly, so boil them in plenty of water at a rolling boil for 15 to 20 minutes, until completely soft. Drain, keeping a little of the water.
Warm the oil in a pan. Add the mustard seeds and cumin, and when the mustard pops, add the onion, ginger and garlic. Cook until golden, about 7 minutes.

Add the tomato, turmeric, Kashmiri chili and salt and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the moong with a few spoonfuls of the cooking water, the garam masala, the peanuts and the coconut. Simmer for 8 minutes.

Knead the jowar flour with a pinch of salt and hot water into a soft dough while it is warm. Shape it into one ball and pat it into a small round on a damp cloth or between two sheets of parchment, then lift it onto a hot dry pan and cook until brown-spotted on both sides.
Serve the usal with the roti, the sliced cucumber and the curd, scattered with cilantro.
tip: Soak the moong the night before, drain it in a colander, cover with a damp cloth and it sprouts in about a day. Rinse twice. Store-bought moong sprouts also work; the 15 to 20 minute boil in step 1 covers both.
ingredients: whole green moong, soaked overnight and sprouted for a day
plain, as curd on the side

name: Chicken dum biryani with brown basmati and cucumber salad
inspiredBy: Hyderabadi and Pakistani chicken dum biryani, packed with vegetables and made with brown basmati
about: A weekend biryani: chicken marinated in yogurt and spices, layered with brown basmati, cauliflower, peas, mint and golden onions and toasted almonds and steamed on the dum. It is a project, but one pot makes two big portions, so Sunday lunch is done. The rice shares the pot with **lots of chicken and vegetables**.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt with the grated ginger and garlic, Kashmiri chili, turmeric, garam masala, half the mint and cilantro and half the salt. Chill for at least 1 hour.

Fry the sliced onion in the oil over medium heat, stirring often, until deep golden, about 15 minutes. Add the almonds for the last 2 minutes. Set half the onion and all the almonds aside for the top.
Soak the rice for 30 minutes, then boil it in plenty of water with the bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, clove and the rest of the salt until about 80% cooked, about 20 minutes. Drain.
In a heavy pot, cook the marinated chicken with the rest of the onions for 10 minutes. Add the cauliflower and peas.

Spread the half-cooked rice over the chicken. Top with the reserved onion and almonds, most of the rest of the mint and cilantro, the ghee and 3 tablespoons of water. Seal the pot with foil and a tight lid and steam on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.

Rest for 10 minutes. Make sure the chicken reads 74 C (165 F) in the thickest piece and the rice is tender. Toss the cucumber with the last of the mint and a pinch of salt for the salad. Serve half. Spread the second portion in a shallow dish, cool it, refrigerate it within 1 hour and eat it the next day, reheated once until it reaches 74 C (165 F) all the way through.
tip: Brown basmati is chewier than white, so give it the full 80% cook before layering. Cook the rice that morning, cool it in a shallow tray and chill it within 1 hour, and the layering takes 20 minutes.

name: Lahori-style trout tawa fry with chickpea and spinach
inspiredBy: Lahori fried fish (machli), pan-fried in a little oil with ajwain, and a quick chana palak
about: Rainbow trout fillet coated in a spiced chickpea-flour crust and pan-fried until crisp, with a quick sauté of chickpeas and spinach and a small whole-wheat roti. The trout brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas and spinach add fibre and iron.
steps: Mix the chickpea flour, ajwain, Kashmiri chili, half the lemon juice, the grated ginger and garlic and half the salt with a spoonful of water into a thick paste. Smear it over the trout and rest for 15 minutes.
Mix the atta with a pinch of salt and warm water into a soft dough and rest it while you cook.

For the chana palak, warm a little of the oil in a pan. Add the cumin and the onion and cook until golden. Add the tomato and cook until soft, about 4 minutes, then the chickpeas and spinach. Cook until the spinach wilts, about 4 minutes, and finish with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon.

Heat the rest of the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Fry the trout for about 4 minutes on each side, until the coating is crisp and the fish flakes easily with a fork (70 C / 158 F in the thickest part).
Roll and cook the roti on a hot dry pan until brown-spotted. Serve the fish with the chana palak, the roti and lemon wedges, dusted with chaat masala.
tip: Do not move the fish while the coating sets, or it will tear. Cook fresh and eat the same day.

name: Salted jeera chaas
inspiredBy: Punjabi and Pakistani salted chaas, with roasted cumin
about: A thin, cooling glass of yogurt whisked with water, roasted cumin and mint, the kind you would drink after a heavy meal. It is a **high-protein sip** with no added sugar.
steps: Toast the cumin in a dry pan for 30 seconds until fragrant, then grind it.
Whisk the yogurt with about a cup of cold water until smooth and pourable.
Stir in the cumin, the black salt, the salt and the chopped mint. Serve over ice or very cold.
ingredients: roasted in a dry pan and ground

name: Mint and cucumber chaas
inspiredBy: Gujarati and Pakistani cucumber chaas
about: Yogurt blended with cucumber, mint and a pinch of cumin into a green, refreshing drink. It is a light way to add **protein and calcium** between meals.
steps: Roughly chop the cucumber and put it in a blender with the yogurt, mint, cumin, lemon juice, salt and about half a cup of cold water.
Blend until smooth and pour into a glass. Serve cold.

name: Masala almonds with cucumber
inspiredBy: Pakistani and Punjabi spiced nuts, pan-toasted with chaat masala
about: A small handful of almonds tossed with chaat masala, a pinch of chili and lemon, toasted until fragrant, with cool cucumber sticks. Almonds are a good source of **vitamin E and healthy fats**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, shaking often, until fragrant and lightly browned, about 4 minutes.
Toss them with the chaat masala, Kashmiri chili, salt and lemon while warm.
Serve with the cucumber sticks.
tip: Toast a jar of almonds on Sunday and add the spices on the day.

name: Guava and apple chaat with yogurt
inspiredBy: Pakistani fruit chaat, with yogurt and almonds
about: Diced guava and apple tossed with chaat masala and a lemony yogurt, with slivered almonds for crunch. Guava is a good source of **vitamin C and fibre**, and the yogurt means the fruit does not come alone.
steps: Wash the fruit well and dice it with the skin on.
Stir the lemon juice and chaat masala into the yogurt.
Toss the fruit with the yogurt and scatter over the almonds.
tip: No guava? A ripe pear works.
ingredients: diced, ripe but firm, or thawed frozen cubes from an Indian grocer

name: Masala roasted chickpeas
inspiredBy: Punjabi and Pakistani chana, oven-crisped with chaat masala
about: No-salt-added chickpeas roasted until crisp and tossed with chaat masala and lemon. A handful has **fibre and plant protein** and keeps you going until dinner.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 C (400 F). Toss the dry chickpeas with the oil on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and golden.
Toss with the chaat masala, Kashmiri chili, salt and lemon while hot. They crisp up as they cool.
tip: Roast a double batch; they stay crisp in a jar for 3 days.
ingredients: no-salt-added, drained, rinsed and patted very dry

name: Masala egg chaat with tomato and onion
inspiredBy: Pakistani street-style anda chaat
about: A hard-boiled egg, chopped and tossed with tomato, onion, chaat masala, black pepper and lemon, the way a street cart in Lahore or Karachi makes anda chaat. An egg gives a quick hit of **protein and choline**.
steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, so the yolk is fully set. Cool it in cold water and peel.
Chop the egg and toss it with the tomato, onion, chaat masala, pepper and lemon.
Eat straight away, or chill and eat the same day.
ingredients: boiled until the yolk is firm

name: Warm moong sprout chaat
inspiredBy: Pakistani and Gujarati sprout chaat, with the sprouts boiled until soft
about: Moong sprouts boiled until tender and tossed with tomato, onion, lemon, chaat masala and a few roasted peanuts. A bowl brings **fibre and plant protein** with a pleasing crunch.
steps: Bring a small pot of water to a boil, add the sprouts and boil for 5 minutes at a rolling boil until completely soft. Raw sprouts can carry bacteria, so do not skip this. Drain well and eat the same day.
Toss the warm sprouts with the tomato, onion, lemon juice, chaat masala and cilantro.
Top with the peanuts and eat warm.

name: Apple chaat with yogurt and peanuts
inspiredBy: Pakistani fruit chaat, with crisp apple and yogurt
about: Crisp diced apple with yogurt, chaat masala, a squeeze of lemon and a spoonful of roasted peanuts. The peanuts add crunch and **protein**, and the yogurt keeps the fruit from standing alone.
steps: Wash the apple well and dice it with the skin on. Toss it with the lemon juice so it stays bright.
Stir the chaat masala into the yogurt.
Fold the apple into the yogurt and scatter over the peanuts.

name: Menemen with white cheese, Turkish eggs with tomato and pepper
about: Turkey's favourite scramble: tomatoes and green pepper cooked down until jammy, then softly set eggs and a little crumbled white cheese stirred through, with Aleppo pepper. You eat it straight from the pan, scooping it up with warm lavash. The eggs and tomatoes bring **protein, choline and lycopene** for a morning that lasts.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a small, wide pan over medium heat. Add the onion and green pepper and cook until soft but not browned, about 4 minutes.
Add the tomato with the Aleppo pepper, black pepper and salt. Cook, stirring and mashing now and then, until it breaks down into a thick, jammy sauce, about 5 minutes.

Crack the eggs straight into the pan, scatter over the feta and stir it all gently through the tomatoes. Keep stirring until no runny egg is left, then take the pan off the heat. Scatter with the parsley.
Bring the pan to the table with the warm lavash and scoop it up. Mopping the pan with the bread is the whole point.
tip: Turkish cooks argue about whether the onion belongs, so leave it out if you are on the other side. Leave the cheese out for a plain menemen.
ingredients: Turkish sivri or any mild green pepper, sliced

name: Nan-o-panir-o-sabzi with walnuts, a boiled egg and fresh herbs
about: The classic Persian breakfast plate: warm lavash, salty feta, walnut halves and a boiled egg, with a heap of fresh herbs and cucumber to roll up into little bites. Nothing to cook but an egg. The herbs bring **vitamin K and folate**, and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Lower the egg gently into a small pot of boiling water and cook for 10 minutes until the white and the yolk are firm. Cool it under cold water and peel.
Wash the herbs and scallion and shake them dry. Leave the mint and parsley as whole sprigs, which is how they are served.
Slice the cucumber and arrange it on a plate with the herbs and scallion. Sprinkle the cucumber with a pinch of salt.
Put the feta and walnut halves on the side of the plate with the halved egg. Warm the lavash in a dry pan or the toaster.
Tear off a piece of bread, wrap a little feta, a walnut and a few herb leaves inside, and eat it as a small roll (this is called a loghmeh). Keep going until the plate is empty.
tip: Persian breakfast comes with sweet black tea. Boil the egg the night before and this takes 5 minutes. Fresh tarragon or basil on the plate is lovely if you find it.

name: Kuku sabzi, Persian herb frittata with barberries and yogurt
about: A thick, deep-green frittata packed with parsley, cilantro, dill, scallion and spinach, with dried fenugreek and tart barberries running through it. It is a Nowruz classic, and it makes two portions, so tomorrow's breakfast is cold wedges tucked into bread. The herbs bring **vitamin K, folate and iron** in a single sitting.
steps: Chop the parsley, cilantro, dill, scallion and spinach very finely. A few pulses in a food processor does it, and the pile should look like a lot more green than you expect.
Beat the eggs in a big bowl with the fenugreek, turmeric, pepper and salt. Fold in all the herbs and the drained barberries. It should be thick, more green than yellow.

Warm half the olive oil in a 20 to 22 cm non-stick, oven-safe pan over medium heat. Pour in the mixture, flatten the top and cover. Cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes, until the edges pull away from the pan and the top is almost set.
Heat the broiler. Brush the top with the rest of the oil and slide the pan under for 3 to 4 minutes, until the top is set and just golden. You can flip it with a plate instead if you prefer.
Let it cool for 5 minutes, then cut into wedges. Serve one portion warm with the yogurt and lavash.
Wrap the second portion for tomorrow. Cold kuku in lavash with a spoonful of yogurt is a very good breakfast sandwich.
tip: A handful of chopped walnuts folded in is traditional if you like crunch. If you cannot find barberries, a few chopped dried cranberries give a similar tang.
ingredients: green and white parts, finely chopped
rinsed, soaked in water for 5 minutes and drained

name: Antalya-style piyaz, white bean salad with egg and tahini
inspiredBy: Turkish piyaz, the white bean salad served with köfte, here as a lunch with a boiled egg and the tahini-lemon dressing they make in Antalya
about: Creamy white beans, juicy tomato and a lot of parsley under a lemony tahini dressing, with sumac onions and a halved boiled egg on top. It is a Turkish meze turned into lunch, and it is better after it sits for 10 minutes. The beans bring **fibre, folate and iron**, and the egg adds choline.
steps: Lower the egg into a small pot of boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, then cool it under cold water and peel.
Toss the sliced red onion with the sumac and a pinch of the salt, squeezing it with your fingers for a minute until it softens and turns pink. Leave it for 10 minutes.
Mash the garlic with the rest of the salt, then whisk it with the tahini, lemon juice, adding cold water a teaspoon at a time until it is pale and pourable like thin cream. Whisk in the olive oil.
Toss the white beans gently with the dressing and most of the parsley. Spread them on a plate.
Pile the tomato and sumac onions on top, add the halved egg, sprinkle with the Aleppo pepper and the rest of the parsley, and eat with the toasted lavash.
tip: Cooked from dried beans (about 70 g dry), it tastes even better. Flaked tinned tuna instead of the egg is a Turkish favourite too.
ingredients: from a tin, drained and rinsed

name: Mercimek çorbası, Turkish red lentil soup with mint and Aleppo oil
about: The soup every Turkish kitchen starts a meal with: red lentils, carrot, potato and onion blended silky smooth, with a lemon squeeze and a spoonful of sizzling olive oil, dried mint and Aleppo pepper on top. A peppery arugula (roka) salad and toasted bread make it lunch. The lentils bring **iron, folate and plant protein**, and the lemon helps you take up that iron.
steps: Warm half the olive oil in a medium pot over medium heat and soften the onion and carrot for 5 minutes. Stir in the cumin and a pinch of paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils, potato, salt and about 600 ml (2½ cups) of water. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer gently until everything is very soft, about 20 minutes.
Blend the soup smooth with an immersion blender (or in batches in a blender, leaving the lid vent open). If it is too thick, loosen it with hot water. Stir in half the lemon juice and taste for salt.
Warm the rest of the olive oil in a small pan with the dried mint and Aleppo pepper until it sizzles and turns red, 30 seconds. Spoon it over the soup.
Serve with the toasted lavash and the arugula, with the rest of the lemon squeezed over the leaves.
tip: Double or triple the soup and freeze the rest in single portions for up to 3 months.
ingredients: rinsed until the water runs clearer

name: Lahmacun-style flatbread with spiced beef, parsley salad and ayran
inspiredBy: Turkish lahmacun, with a whole-wheat lavash standing in for the thin dough so it takes 25 minutes
about: Whole-wheat lavash spread thin with a spiced beef, tomato and pepper topping and baked until crisp at the edges and still bendy in the middle, then rolled up with a handful of parsley, sumac onions and lemon, with a cold glass of ayran, as it is eaten in Turkey. The beef brings **iron, zinc and vitamin B12**, and the yogurt in the ayran brings calcium.
steps: Cut the beef into small cubes and pulse it in a food processor in short bursts until finely ground, or ask the butcher to grind it. Heat the oven to 230 C.
Chop the tomato, green pepper, onion and garlic, and blend or finely chop with the pepper paste into a thick, rough paste. Drain off any extra liquid so the lavash does not turn soggy.
Mix the paste with the beef, half the parsley (finely chopped), the Aleppo pepper, paprika, cumin, black pepper and most of the salt until it is sticky and well combined.
Cut the lavash in half if it is large, brush the tops lightly with water, then with half the oil, and spread the beef mixture over it in a thin, even layer, right out to the edges.
Bake on a tray for 6 to 8 minutes, until the edges are crisp and the meat is cooked through, but the middle is still bendy enough to roll.

Meanwhile toss the sliced red onion with the sumac, a pinch of salt, the rest of the parsley, the rest of the oil and half the lemon juice. Pile it on the hot lavash, squeeze over the rest of the lemon, roll up and eat with your hands.
Whisk the yogurt with 150 ml of cold water and a pinch of salt for the ayran, and pour it over ice.
tip: Blend the topping on Friday night and keep it covered in the fridge. On Saturday it is 10 minutes in the oven.
ingredients: half for the topping, half for the salad

name: Ghormeh sabzi, Persian herb stew with beef and kidney beans, with brown basmati
about: Iran's national stew: a deep green, savoury-sour pot of parsley, cilantro, scallion and spinach fried until dark with fenugreek (shanbalileh), with tender beef, kidney beans and a dried lime (limoo amani) for the sour note. It makes two portions, and it is even better tomorrow. The herbs and beans bring **iron, folate and vitamin K**, and the lime and lemon help you take up the iron.
steps: Warm a third of the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until golden, about 8 minutes, then stir in the turmeric, add the beef and brown it for 5 minutes.
Pour in enough water to cover the beef by 2 cm (about 3 cups for two portions). Add the pierced dried lime, the salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour.

While the beef simmers, warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat. Fry the parsley, cilantro, scallion and spinach, stirring often, until they turn dark green and smell toasty, about 20 minutes. Stir in the fenugreek for the last 2 minutes. This slow frying is where the flavour comes from.

Tip the fried herbs and the kidney beans into the pot. Simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes, until the beef is very tender and the sauce is thick and glossy. Taste, and add the lemon juice and a little salt until it is pleasantly sour.

For the rice, rinse the brown basmati and simmer it in a big pot of salted boiling water for 25 minutes, like pasta, then drain. Return it to the pot, wrap the lid in a clean tea towel and leave it for 10 minutes to steam and fluff up. Cook enough for both portions.
Serve the stew over the rice. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch. The dried lime stays in the pot, and you can press it with a spoon on the plate for more sourness.
tip: Short on time? In a pressure cooker, cook the beef for 20 minutes, then add the herbs and beans and simmer for 10 minutes. You can also fry the herbs the night before.
ingredients: from a tin, drained and rinsed
one whole dried lime serves two portions, pierced a few times

name: Chicken köfte with bulgur pilav and çoban salatası
inspiredBy: Adana and Urfa köfte, which are lamb, made here with chicken thighs and a little bulgur pilav on the side
