ingredients: peeled, thick half-moons; simmers in the sauce, no pre-boil

name: Chicken and egg rice bowl (oyakodon)
inspiredBy: Japanese oyakodon, with the egg cooked through
about: Tender chicken, onion and edamame simmered in a gently sweet, savoury broth, then topped with egg cooked until set and spooned over rice. Grated apple adds the gentle sweetness. It is a quick lunch with plenty of **protein and choline**.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.

Wash the vegetables. Warm the canola oil in a small, wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion, shiitake and ginger for 3 minutes, until soft. Add about half a cup of water, the soy sauce and the grated apple and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken, spreading it out in a single layer, and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, with no pink. Stir in the edamame for the last 2 minutes.
Pour the beaten egg over in a thin stream, cover and cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until the egg is fully set with no runny parts.
Slide everything over the rice and finish with the scallion and sesame seeds.
tip: Eat it straight away. It's the one dish here that doesn't want to wait.

name: Chicken and daikon soup
inspiredBy: Cantonese lou fo tong, the slow-simmered soup of the home kitchen
about: A clear, comforting Cantonese-style soup of chicken thigh, sweet daikon, carrot, sweet corn and ginger, simmered gently until the chicken is tender, with bok choy stirred in at the end and rice on the side. It is hands-off cooking, and the soup freezes well. The **chicken adds protein and B vitamins**, and the daikon keeps the broth clean and sweet.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Put the chicken in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 3 minutes, until foam rises. Drain, rinse the foam off the chicken and out of the pot, then wipe down the sink and wash your hands and board.
Return the chicken to the clean pot with the daikon, carrot, sweet corn and ginger. Add enough water to cover by about 4 cm and bring to a boil, then skim.

Turn the heat down to a very gentle simmer, partly cover and cook for about 40 minutes, until the chicken is very tender, reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the daikon is soft. In a pressure cooker, cook for about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Skim off any fat from the surface. Add the bok choy and the salt and simmer for 3 minutes. Finish with a few drops of sesame oil, the white pepper and scallion, and serve with the rice.
Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C). The soup freezes on its own for up to 3 months.
tip: Found lotus root? Use 100 g instead of the daikon.
ingredients: cut into large chunks, skin and fat trimmed
peeled, thick coins; goes in raw, no pre-boil
kernels cut off the cob, or frozen

name: Beef and potato simmer (nikujaga)
inspiredBy: Japanese nikujaga, home-style simmered beef and potatoes
about: Thin slices of beef with potato, carrot, onion and spinach, simmered in a light soy broth sweetened with grated apple. The **beef brings iron, zinc and B12**, and the potato makes it a full, filling bowl.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Wash the vegetables. Warm the canola oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the beef and ginger and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until the beef has lost its pink colour.
Add the potato, carrot and onion and stir for 1 minute. Add the grated apple, the soy sauce and about 1 cup of water, then bring to a boil.
Turn the heat down, cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the potato is tender and the beef is cooked through. Stir in the spinach for the last 2 minutes, until wilted.
Uncover and cook for 2 minutes more to thicken the broth a little. Serve in a bowl beside the rice, with any broth spooned over.
tip: Cooked a double batch? Chill it in a shallow container within 2 hours. It's even better the next day, and keeps up to 3 days or a month in the freezer. Reheat until steaming hot (74 °C).

name: Sesame, date and almond bites
about: Soft medjool dates mashed with almonds and rolled oats into sticky little balls rolled in black sesame. They are one-hand food you can eat while holding a baby. The **dates, almonds and sesame** add iron, calcium and vitamin E.
steps: Mash the dates with a fork in a bowl until you have a sticky paste.
Stir in the almonds, oats and cinnamon.
Roll into small balls with damp hands, then roll them in the black sesame and chill for 15 minutes. They keep in the fridge for 4 days.
tip: Make a batch of a dozen on Sunday and keep them in a jar in the fridge.

name: Warm tofu with ginger honey syrup
inspiredBy: Chinese tofu pudding (dou hua), made with a quick ginger syrup
about: Warm cubes of tofu spooned over with a little ginger-honey syrup, black sesame and walnuts, a gentle snack in the spirit of Chinese tofu pudding (dou hua). It takes five minutes. The **tofu brings protein and calcium**.
steps: Simmer the honey, ginger and a splash of water in a small pot for 2 minutes to make a syrup.
Warm the tofu in a bowl in the microwave for about 1 minute, or in a pot of hot water, until steaming hot all the way through.
Spoon the syrup over the tofu and scatter with the sesame and walnuts. Let it cool a minute before eating.

name: Soy-simmered egg with edamame
inspiredBy: Chinese soy-braised egg (lu dan), simplified
about: A hard-cooked egg steeped in a light soy and ginger broth until it takes on a savoury, golden-brown edge, with a handful of warm shelled edamame. It's a protein-rich bite you can eat standing up. The **egg brings choline and B12**, and the edamame add folate.
steps: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Lower the egg in gently (add a second for later in the week if you like) and boil for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely set.
Cool in cold water, then peel.
Simmer the soy sauce, ginger and a few tablespoons of water for 2 minutes. Add the egg and turn it for 2 minutes, until glazed.

Warm the edamame in the microwave for about 1 minute and serve beside the egg. If you boiled a second egg, keep it in its shell in the fridge, glaze it on the day you eat it, and eat it within 3 days.

name: Warm almond and black sesame milk
inspiredBy: Chinese almond and sesame drinks (xing ren zhi ma lu)
about: Milk warmed and blended with ground almonds, black sesame and a little honey, a cozy mug for when baby is down. It is inspired by the almond and sesame drinks of Chinese breakfast stalls, with **calcium from the milk** and vitamin E from the almonds.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for about 1 minute, until they smell nutty, then grind them finely with the almonds.
Warm the milk in a pot until steaming, but not boiling, then let it cool a few minutes until warm, not hot.
Whisk in the almond and sesame mixture and the honey, and sip from a lidded mug with baby set down.

name: Warm walnut and black sesame milk
inspiredBy: Chinese walnut and sesame sweet soups (he tao zhi ma hu)
about: Milk warmed and blended with ground walnuts, black sesame and a little honey, a cozy mug for when baby is down. It is inspired by the walnut and sesame sweet soups of southern China. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3 fat (ALA)**, and the milk brings calcium.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for about 1 minute, until they smell nutty, then grind them finely with the walnuts.
Warm the milk in a pot until steaming, but not boiling, then let it cool a few minutes until warm, not hot.
Whisk in the walnut and sesame mixture and the honey, and sip from a lidded mug with baby set down.

name: Mandarin with walnuts and almonds
about: A juicy mandarin with a handful of walnuts and almonds, a no-cook snack you can eat in the car or on the sofa. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3 fat (ALA)**, the almonds bring vitamin E, and the mandarin brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the mandarin, then peel it and eat it with the nuts.

name: Warm edamame with sesame
about: Shelled edamame warmed through and tossed with a pinch of salt and toasted sesame. Easy finger food that takes two minutes. The **soy beans bring protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Warm the edamame in the microwave or in a pot of hot water until steaming hot, about 2 minutes, then let them cool for a minute.
Toss with the salt and sesame seeds.

name: Mango almond lassi
inspiredBy: North Indian mango lassi, made lighter with Greek yogurt
about: Greek yogurt and milk blended with ripe mango, ground almonds and a pinch of cardamom into a cool, creamy drink. It's one-hand food in a glass, with **protein and calcium** from the yogurt and milk and vitamin E from the almonds.
steps: Blend the yogurt, milk, mango, almonds and cardamom until smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink right away, or chill for up to a day.
ingredients: ripe, fresh or thawed from frozen

name: Masala chickpeas and almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian chana snacks and masala nuts
about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with cumin, garam masala and lemon, tossed with a few almonds, a crunchy, savoury snack for the handbag or the nursing chair. The **chickpeas bring protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss the chickpeas with the oil, cumin, garam masala and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp.
Toss with the almonds and the lemon juice and let cool for 5 minutes. They are best the day they're made.

name: Apple with walnuts and almonds
about: A crisp apple with a small handful of walnuts and almonds, sweet, juicy and crunchy. It is a no-cook snack that eats well with one hand. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3 fat (ALA)**, the almonds bring vitamin E, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it if you like and eat it with the nuts.

name: Banana walnut smoothie with black sesame
about: Milk blended with banana, walnuts and a spoonful of black sesame into a thick, creamy drink. It is easy to sip one-handed, with **calcium from the milk**, plant omega-3 fat from the walnuts and potassium from the banana.
steps: Blend everything until smooth and creamy. Black sesame can leave a few specks, which is fine.
Drink right away or chill for a few hours.

name: Yogurt with mandarin and toasted almonds
about: Thick Greek yogurt topped with juicy mandarin segments and crunchy toasted almonds. It's cool, tangy and takes a minute. The **mandarin brings vitamin C**, the almonds bring vitamin E, and the yogurt brings protein and calcium.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for about 2 minutes, until golden and fragrant. Wash the mandarin before peeling and splitting it into segments.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the mandarin and almonds.

name: Berry and walnut overnight oats
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and yogurt, thick and cold, with blueberries, walnuts and a few pumpkin seeds for crunch. It is **ready the second you wake up**, and you can eat it one-handed from the jar. The yogurt and milk bring calcium and iodine, and the pumpkin seeds bring zinc.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, cinnamon and maple syrup together in a jar until there are no dry pockets.
Fold in half the blueberries, put the lid on and chill overnight, or at least 4 hours.
In the morning, loosen with a splash of milk if it has set firm, then top with the rest of the blueberries, the walnuts and the pumpkin seeds.
tip: Mix the jar the night before and eat it within 2 days. Mix a second jar for another morning only if you will eat it within that time.

name: Carrot cake baked oat squares with yogurt
about: Soft, spiced oat squares with grated carrot, dates and walnuts, baked in one dish and cut cold from the fridge. They taste like carrot cake and eat like a bar, so one hand is plenty. The carrot and egg bring **vitamin A and choline**.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a small baking dish with a little canola oil.
Stir the oats, cinnamon and baking powder together, then stir in the beaten eggs, milk and maple syrup until evenly wet.
Fold in the grated carrot, dates and walnuts and spread the mix in the dish.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the middle is set, the top is golden and a knife comes out clean, so the egg is fully cooked (74°C or 165°F in the centre).
Cool, cover and chill in an airtight container. Cut into squares and serve cold or warmed, with the yogurt and blueberries on the side or spooned on top.
tip: Bake Sunday. Keep day 2's square in the fridge in an airtight container and freeze day 5's wrapped alone. Thaw it in the fridge overnight and eat within 2 days.
ingredients: fresh, or thawed if frozen, to serve

name: Egg muffin breakfast wrap with avocado and clementine
about: A baked spinach and cheddar egg muffin tucked into a warm tortilla with sliced avocado, with a clementine on the side. The muffins are baked ahead, so breakfast is a minute of assembly and one hand. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, cooked all the way through.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a muffin tin well.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper, then stir in the spinach and cheddar.
Pour into the tin, about three-quarters full. Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until puffed and completely set in the middle, with no wet egg, and the centre reaches 74°C (165°F).
Cool, then chill within 2 hours. Keep tomorrow's muffins in the fridge and freeze the rest in single portions.
To serve, reheat the muffins to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot all the way through. Warm the tortilla, lay on the avocado and the muffins, fold and eat. Peel the clementine on the side.
tip: Bake 3 breakfasts on Sunday: day 1 from the fridge, days 4 and 7 from the freezer. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat to 74°C (165°F).

name: Beef and bean chili with tortilla for scooping
inspiredBy: classic North American chili con carne
about: A thick, smoky chili with lean beef, kidney and black beans, carrot and tomato, topped with creamy avocado. Cook it on **Sunday and freeze portions**, so a hot, hearty meal is only a reheat away. The beef brings iron, zinc and B12, and the beans add fibre.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft and starting to colour. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until no pink remains, it is browned all over and it reaches 71°C (160°F).
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, beans, salt and a splash of water. Simmer gently for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and the flavours have come together.

Divide into shallow containers so it cools fast, and chill within 2 hours. Keep one portion in the fridge for up to 3 days and freeze the rest in single portions. Reheat to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot all the way through.
Serve in a bowl with the diced avocado on top and the warm tortilla for scooping.
tip: This pot covers day 1's lunch and day 7's dinner. Double it if you want spare freezer meals. Thaw overnight in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.

name: Red lentil, carrot and tomato soup with cheddar quesadilla wedges
inspiredBy: Middle Eastern shorbat adas
about: A silky orange soup of red lentils, carrots and tomato with warm cumin and a squeeze of lemon, served with crisp cheddar quesadilla wedges for dunking. It is a **freezer-friendly one-pot soup** that blends up thick and creamy. The carrots and spinach bring vitamin A and the lentils bring folate.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 8 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and tomatoes and stir for 1 minute.
Rinse the lentils and add them with the broth and a cup of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes, until the lentils and carrots are completely soft.
Blend with an immersion blender until smooth, or leave it a little chunky. Stir in the washed spinach until it wilts, then the salt and lemon juice.
For the quesadilla, scatter the cheddar over half the tortilla, fold it over and toast in a dry pan for 2 minutes a side, until golden and the cheese has melted. Cut into wedges.
Divide into shallow containers so it cools fast, and chill within 2 hours. Keep one portion in the fridge for up to 3 days and freeze the rest in single portions. Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
tip: Make it Sunday and freeze in single portions with a little room at the top. Thaw overnight in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze. Make the quesadilla fresh each time.

name: Sheet-pan salmon with sweet potato, broccoli and lemon-dill yogurt
about: A whole dinner on one tray: salmon roasted over wedges of sweet potato and broccoli, spooned with a cool lemon-dill yogurt. Salmon is the DHA dinner of the week, and the sweet potato brings **plenty of vitamin A**. There is one pan to wash and nothing to stir.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the sweet potato wedges with half the oil, half the salt and the pepper on a large tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the broccoli to the tray with the rest of the oil and toss. Make room for the salmon in the middle.

Season the salmon with a pinch of salt and lay it on the tray. Roast for 10 to 12 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork, reaches 70°C (158°F) inside, and the sweet potato is tender.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic and dill together in a small bowl.
Serve the salmon and vegetables with the yogurt sauce spooned over.
tip: Salmon is best eaten fresh, so cook only what you will eat tonight.

name: Chicken tinga bowl with sweet potato, black beans and avocado
inspiredBy: Pueblan tinga de pollo
about: Tender shredded chicken in a smoky tomato and chipotle sauce with sweet potato cooked right in, over a little brown rice and black beans with avocado and a squeeze of lemon. It makes **two portions**, and tomorrow's lunch is better for the night in the fridge. The chicken brings protein and choline, the sweet potato brings vitamin A.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of water or per the packet until tender, then drain. Warm the black beans through in a small pot.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and cook 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, chipotle, salt and a splash of water and bring to a simmer. Add the chicken and cover. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the sweet potato cubes, cover again and simmer 15 minutes more, until the sweet potato is tender and the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) on a thermometer, with no pink and the juices running clear.
Shred the chicken with two forks right in the sauce and simmer a few minutes, until thick.
Spoon the chicken and sweet potato over the rice and beans. Top with avocado and a squeeze of lemon.
Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch, spreading any leftover rice thin in a shallow container so it cools fast. Chill within 2 hours and reheat once to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot.
tip: Use less chipotle for a milder sauce. The tinga freezes well without the avocado. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.

name: Turkey meatball and spinach soup with little pasta
inspiredBy: Italian wedding soup
about: A brothy soup of tender baked turkey meatballs, carrot, chickpeas, spinach and a small handful of pasta, with lemon at the end. It is warm, mostly water and easy to eat with a spoon. It makes **tomorrow's lunch**, and freezes well without the pasta.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a tray with parchment. Beat the egg in a large bowl (if the list shows part of an egg, beat a whole one, use about half, and cover, chill and cook the rest within 2 days). Mix in the turkey, oats, half the garlic, half the oregano and a pinch of the salt with your hands. If the mix is too soft to roll, chill it for 10 minutes, then roll into small balls with wet hands and set them on the tray.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until browned and cooked through, with no pink inside and 74°C (165°F) on a thermometer.
Meanwhile, warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the rest of the garlic and oregano, then the tomatoes, broth, chickpeas and a cup of water.
Bring to a simmer, add the broken spaghetti and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until tender.
Add the meatballs and the washed spinach and simmer 3 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the meatballs are hot all the way through. Stir in the lemon juice and the rest of the salt.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container and chill within 2 hours. Reheat to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot, with a splash of water if the pasta has soaked up the broth.
tip: To freeze, leave out the pasta and add fresh spaghetti when you reheat it. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.

name: Haddock and sweet corn chowder
inspiredBy: Maritime fish chowder
about: A creamy, comforting chowder of flaky haddock, potato, carrot and sweet corn in a milky broth with thyme and a handful of spinach stirred in. It is **a good iodine dinner**, since haddock and milk are two of the best food sources, and it reheats well for the next day's lunch. Soft, warm and easy to eat with a spoon.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft but not browned.
Add the potato, broth and thyme with a cup of water. Simmer for 10 minutes, until the potato is nearly tender.
Pour in the milk and add the corn. Warm gently, without letting it boil hard.

Cut the haddock into big pieces and lay them in. Cover and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the fish turns opaque, flakes easily and reaches 70°C (158°F). Stir in the washed spinach until it wilts and season with the salt and pepper.
Crush a few potato pieces against the side of the pot to thicken the chowder.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container and chill within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 days, stir and reheat to 74°C (165°F), steaming hot all the way through.
tip: Cod or pollock work too. Do not freeze the chowder, as the fish and milk turn soft and grainy.

name: Maple-ginger salmon rice bowl with broccoli and cucumber
inspiredBy: a Japanese-style salmon bowl, with Canadian maple
about: Salmon brushed with maple, ginger and a little soy sauce, roasted until just flaky, on brown rice with steamed broccoli, crunchy cucumber and carrot. It is sweet, salty and fresh, and everything comes together in one bowl. The salmon brings **DHA and B12**, and the broccoli brings vitamin C and folate.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of water or per the packet until tender, then drain and keep warm.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Stir the maple syrup, soy sauce and ginger together and brush it over the salmon on a lined tray.
Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily, is opaque all the way through and reaches 70°C (158°F) inside.
Steam the broccoli for 4 to 5 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Toss the cucumber and carrot with the lemon juice and the oil.
Pile the rice in a bowl, add the broccoli and the cucumber-carrot salad and set the salmon on top.
tip: Cook the rice fresh, or cool extra rice fast in a shallow container, use it within 2 days and reheat once to 74°C (165°F).

name: Lemon-herb chicken tray bake with potatoes, carrots and chickpeas
inspiredBy: Greek-style lemon chicken and potatoes
about: Juicy chicken thighs roasted over potatoes, carrots, chickpeas and onion with lemon, garlic and thyme, finished with wilted spinach. It goes in the oven and you leave it alone, and the second portion is **tomorrow's lunch**, eaten cold from the fridge or reheated until steaming. A simple roast dinner without the Sunday effort.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (410°F). Toss the potato and carrot with half the oil, half the salt and the thyme on a large tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Toss the chicken with the rest of the oil, the garlic, smoked paprika, lemon juice and the remaining salt.

Add the chicken, chickpeas and onion to the tray and roast for 25 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) on a thermometer in the thickest piece, with no pink and the juices clear, and the potatoes are golden.
Pile the washed spinach onto the hot tray and toss for a minute, until it wilts, and serve.
Pack the second portion and chill it within 2 hours. Reheat to 74°C (165°F), or eat it cold from the fridge.
tip: Cut the potatoes and carrots the night before and keep them covered in cold water in the fridge. Making Big? Use two trays so it roasts instead of steaming.

name: Almond and date oat bars
about: Chewy bars of rolled oats, dates and chopped almonds pressed into a pan and cut into squares. They are sweet without being sugary and you can eat one in your other hand. They bring **slow-burning oats and vitamin E**.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Soak the dates in hot water for 5 minutes, then drain and mash them with a fork or blitz into a paste.
Mix the date paste with the maple syrup, a splash of water, cinnamon and salt, then stir in the oats and almonds until sticky.
Press firmly into a lined small pan. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until lightly golden around the edges.
Cool completely in the pan, cut into bars and keep in an airtight container in the fridge up to 4 days, or freeze wrapped one by one.
tip: Bars you will not eat within 4 days go in the freezer, wrapped one by one. Move one to the fridge the night before and eat it within 2 days of thawing.

name: Smashed chickpea and cucumber wrap
about: Mashed chickpeas with yogurt and lemon in a soft whole-wheat tortilla with crunchy cucumber and baby spinach. It is cold, crisp and juicy, and you can hold it in one hand. The chickpeas and spinach bring **iron, zinc and folate**.
steps: Mash the chickpeas roughly with a fork, then stir in the yogurt, lemon juice and pepper.
Lay the tortilla flat and spread the chickpea mix over it, leaving a border.
Pile the spinach and cucumber down the middle, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Wrap in parchment or foil so you can eat it one-handed. It keeps in the fridge until the next day.
tip: Roll it in foil and peel as you eat, so nothing falls out while the baby feeds.

name: Canned salmon and cucumber wrap
about: Flaked canned salmon, mashed with its soft bones, with creamy yogurt, lemon and dill in a whole-wheat wrap with cucumber and spinach. It tastes like a fresh salmon salad sandwich. Canned salmon with the bones carries **DHA and calcium**.
steps: Drain the salmon and flake it into a bowl, mashing in the soft bones.
Stir in the yogurt, lemon juice, dill and pepper.
Spread on the tortilla, add the cucumber and spinach, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Eat right away or chill, wrapped, until later in the day.
tip: Open a can once and make two wraps. Keep the extra salmon mixture covered in the fridge up to 2 days.

name: Mango and banana yogurt smoothie
about: A cold, thick smoothie of frozen mango, banana, yogurt and milk that you can drink straight from a water bottle or a tall travel cup. It is sweet, easy and mostly water. Yogurt and milk bring **calcium and iodine**, and the mango adds vitamin A.
steps: Add the milk, yogurt, banana and frozen mango to a blender in that order.
Blend for about a minute, until completely smooth.
Drink right away, or pour into a lidded cup or water bottle (never a baby bottle), keep it cold and drink within a day.
tip: Peel and freeze ripe bananas in chunks so the smoothie is thick and cold without ice.

name: Cottage cheese with mango and almonds
about: Creamy cottage cheese with juicy thawed mango and a few chopped almonds, eaten with a spoon from a cup. It is sweet and savoury, cool and hydrating. It brings **protein, iodine and vitamin E** with plenty of water.
steps: Thaw the mango in the fridge overnight or for a few minutes in a bowl of cold water.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a cup or small bowl and top with the mango and almonds.
Eat it cold with a spoon, or keep it in the fridge until you want it.

name: Smoky roasted chickpeas
about: Crunchy chickpeas roasted until crisp with smoked paprika, cumin and lemon. They are a handful-at-a-time snack you can eat from a bowl on your lap. They bring **plant protein, fibre and zinc**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Pat the chickpeas very dry with a clean towel.
Toss with the oil, smoked paprika, cumin and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until deep golden and crunchy.
Let them cool on the tray, as they crisp up as they cool. Squeeze the lemon over just the portion you are eating. Keep the rest plain in a jar for 3 days at most.
tip: Makes two portions. Keep the second plain and add its lemon when you eat it, so it stays crunchy.

name: Clementines with almonds and walnuts
about: Easy-peel clementines with a small handful of almonds and walnuts, juicy and crunchy together. There is no prep and no mess. Together they bring **vitamin C, vitamin E and plant omega-3**.
steps: Peel the clementines and split into segments.
Eat with a small handful of the almonds and walnuts.

name: Carrot sticks with garlicky yogurt dip
about: Crunchy carrot sticks with a cool, garlicky lemon yogurt dip, easy to dunk and eat with one hand. Mostly water, with a little protein. The carrots bring **vitamin A**.
steps: Stir the yogurt, grated garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper together in a small bowl.
Wash and cut the carrots into sticks and dunk them in the dip.
Keep the dip covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.
tip: Makes enough dip for two snacks. Eat the second portion within 2 days.

name: Paprika yogurt eggs
about: Hard-boiled egg halves filled with a creamy yogurt, lemon and smoked paprika mix, easy to eat in two bites. Make them ahead and keep them in the fridge. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, boiled until the yolks are fully set.
steps: Lower the eggs into a pot of simmering water and boil for 10 minutes, so the yolks are fully set. Cool under cold running water, then peel.
Halve the eggs and scoop the yolks into a bowl. Mash with the yogurt, lemon juice, salt and pepper until creamy.
Spoon the filling back into the whites and dust with the smoked paprika.
Eat them the day you fill them.
tip: Hard-boil the eggs up to a week ahead and keep them in the shell, in the fridge. Fill them the day you eat them.

name: Banana and almond yogurt cup
about: Thick Greek yogurt with sliced banana, a few chopped almonds and a dusting of cinnamon, spooned from a cup. It is cool and creamy with a little crunch. The yogurt brings **calcium and iodine**, and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a cup or small bowl.
Top with the banana slices, almonds and cinnamon.
Eat right away, so the banana stays fresh.

name: Blueberry yogurt bowl with walnuts and maple
about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy blueberries, chopped walnuts and a drizzle of maple syrup, eaten with a spoon. It is cool, creamy and mostly water. It brings **calcium, protein and plant omega-3**, with very little iron, so it suits the bigger sizes.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl or cup.
Top with the blueberries and walnuts and drizzle with the maple syrup.
Eat it cold, right away.

name: Cheddar and clementine plate
about: A small plate of sharp cheddar cubes, clementine segments and a few almonds, all finger food. It is sweet, salty and juicy, and easy to eat one-handed. The cheddar brings **calcium and protein**, and the clementines bring vitamin C.
steps: Peel the clementines and split into segments.
Cut the cheddar into small cubes.
Arrange everything on a plate and eat with your fingers.

name: Apple pie overnight oats
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss bircher muesli
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and yogurt with grated apple, cinnamon and walnuts, like a cold bowl of apple pie. Five minutes the night before and nothing to cook in the morning, and it brings **fibre and protein** to the start of the day.
steps: Wash your hands and the apple. Grate the apple, skin and all, and stir it into a jar with the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon until there are no dry patches.
Put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. The oats soak up the milk and turn creamy.
In the morning, stir it up and loosen it with a splash of milk if it is thick. Scatter the walnuts on just before eating so they stay crunchy.
Keep it in the fridge and eat it within 2 days of making it. Never keep soaked oats longer than 3 days.
tip: Stir up Sunday night's jar for Monday, Tuesday night's for Wednesday and Thursday night's for Friday, so no jar sits more than 2 days. At the Light size, make Monday's and Tuesday's jars together on Sunday night. At the lowest Light setting the oats are a couple of spoonfuls, so it eats like a thick apple and yogurt bircher. At the Big size, use a big bowl or a 1 litre jar.
ingredients: washed and coarsely grated, skin on

name: Banana, blueberry and walnut porridge
about: Creamy rolled oats simmered in milk and topped with sliced banana, blueberries and crunchy walnuts. It is a warm, filling weekday breakfast that takes 10 minutes and brings **fibre, potassium and protein**.
steps: Wash your hands and rinse the blueberries. Stir the oats, milk and cinnamon together in a small pot over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Pour into a bowl and top with the banana, blueberries and walnuts. Eat right away.
tip: No time? Microwave the oats and milk in a big bowl for 2 minutes, stir, then 1 more minute. Watch the bowl, it can bubble over. If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, use fresh blueberries or stir frozen ones into the pot for the last 2 minutes.

name: Potato, white bean and spinach hash with eggs
inspiredBy: Inspired by a diner-style potato hash
about: Crisp-edged diced potatoes in a big skillet with onion, red pepper, white beans and spinach, with eggs cooked right on top until the yolks are firm and a little feta crumbled over. It makes two breakfasts, and the eggs, beans and spinach bring **protein, folate and choline**.
steps: Wash the potatoes, pepper and spinach before cutting. Heat the oil in a large lidded nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the potatoes with the salt, cover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until they are tender and starting to brown.
Add the onion and pepper, turn the heat up a little and cook for 5 minutes, until the onion is soft and the potatoes are crisp at the edges.
Stir in the white beans, paprika and pepper, then fold in the spinach until it wilts, about 1 minute.

Make wells in the hash and crack the eggs into them. Cover and cook for 7 to 8 minutes, until the whites are opaque and the yolks are completely firm. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs, then crumble the feta over the top.
Eat half now. Move the other half to a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate.
Reheat the second portion once, until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and eat it within 3 days.
tip: Break the yolks up into the hash with a fork once they are firm. A few drops of hot sauce are great on top.

name: Sardine, egg, new potato and green bean salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by salade Nicoise, with sardines
about: Warm potatoes and green beans tossed in a mustard-lemon dressing with white beans, cherry tomatoes and onion, topped with chunks of sardine, and a firm hard-cooked egg. It is a Nicoise-style packed lunch, and the sardines and egg bring **omega-3 fats, calcium, vitamin D and choline**.
steps: Put the egg in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 12 minutes so the yolk is completely firm. Cool it in cold water, peel and quarter it, then wash your hands.

Wash the potatoes, green beans, tomatoes and parsley. Cook the potatoes in a pot of cold water with a pinch of the salt, brought to a boil, for 8 minutes. Add the green beans and cook for 4 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the beans are bright green. Drain well.
In a big bowl, whisk the mustard, lemon juice, oil, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Toss the warm potatoes and beans in the dressing so they soak it up.
Fold in the white beans, tomatoes, onion and parsley. Break the sardines into chunks and lay them and the egg on top. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
For a packed lunch, chill the salad, then carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Cook the potatoes, beans and egg the night before: chill them within 2 hours in a shallow container, keep them in the fridge and eat within 3 days. In the morning it is a 3-minute toss. Swap the sardines for canned mackerel.
ingredients: baby or new potatoes, scrubbed and cut in 2 cm pieces

name: Sardine, white bean and green bean salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian tuna and white bean salad, with sardines
about: Green beans and creamy white beans with cherry tomatoes, onion and baby spinach in a mustard-lemon dressing, topped with chunks of sardine and sunflower seeds. It is a potato-free lunch for the day that already has two potato dishes, and the sardines bring **omega-3 fats, calcium and vitamin D**.
steps: Wash the green beans, spinach, tomatoes and parsley. Boil the green beans in salted water for 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender, then drain and cool them under cold water.
In a big bowl, whisk the mustard, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper.
Toss the white beans, green beans, tomatoes, onion and parsley in the dressing so the beans soak it up.
Pile onto the spinach. Break the sardines into chunks and lay them on top, then scatter over the sunflower seeds. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
For a packed lunch, carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Cook the green beans the night before and chill them within 2 hours in a shallow container. Swap the sardines for canned mackerel.

name: Lentil, beet and egg salad with feta and sunflower seeds
inspiredBy: Inspired by a French lentil and beet salad
about: Earthy lentils, sweet cooked beets and firm hard-cooked eggs on baby spinach with crunchy carrot, crumbled feta and sunflower seeds, tossed in a lemon-mustard dressing. It is a filling packed lunch with **iron, folate and choline**, and the lemon helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Put the egg in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil, then cook for 12 minutes so the yolk is completely firm. Cool it in cold water, peel and quarter it. Wash your hands after handling the raw egg.

Wash the spinach and carrot. Whisk the lemon juice, mustard, oil and pepper in a big bowl. Add the lentils, beets and carrot and toss to coat. The lentils soak up the dressing, which is what you want.
Fold in the spinach just before serving, then top with the eggs, feta and sunflower seeds.
For a packed lunch, keep the spinach, eggs, feta and seeds in a separate container, carry it all in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Boil the eggs the night before and this is a 5-minute lunch. Beet juice stains, so use a dark bowl.
ingredients: plain, vacuum-packed, cut in small wedges

name: Turkey and bean chili loaded baked potatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex chili and the classic loaded baked potato
about: Fluffy baked potatoes with crisp skins, piled with a smoky turkey and kidney bean chili with spinach stirred in, and finished with a squeeze of lemon and parsley. It makes two portions, and the beans and potato bring **fibre, potassium and iron**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Scrub the potatoes, prick them all over with a fork and microwave for 8 minutes, turning halfway. Set them straight on the oven rack and bake for 15 minutes, until the skins are crisp and the middles are soft.

Meanwhile, wash the pepper, carrot, spinach and parsley before cutting. Warm the oil in a big pot over medium heat and cook the onion, pepper and carrot for 5 minutes, until soft. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin and paprika for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the turkey and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until there is no pink left. Wash your hands, the board and the spoon with hot soapy water.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, kidney beans, salt and a splash of water. Simmer for 12 minutes, until thick, then stir in the spinach for the last minute. The turkey must reach 74 °C (165 °F).
Split the potatoes, spoon the chili over, and finish with the lemon juice and parsley. Eat half now.

Pack the second portion, with the potato and chili in separate shallow containers, within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
tip: Microwave tomorrow's potato for 2 minutes, then crisp it in a hot oven or an air fryer while the chili heats. Use a wide pot if you cook this at the Big size, so the chili thickens.

name: Jacket potatoes with a ladle of turkey and bean chili
inspiredBy: Inspired by the British jacket potato and Tex-Mex chili
about: A fluffy jacket potato with a crisp skin, topped with a ladle of smoky turkey and kidney bean chili with spinach, lemon and parsley. It is a lighter take on the loaded baked potatoes, with more potato and a little less chili, and it makes two portions with **fibre, potassium and iron**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Scrub the potatoes, prick them all over with a fork and microwave for 6 to 8 minutes, turning halfway, until a knife slides in. Set them straight on the oven rack and bake for 15 minutes, until the skins are crisp and the middles are soft.

Meanwhile, wash the pepper, carrot, spinach and parsley before cutting. Warm the oil in a big pot over medium heat and cook the onion, pepper and carrot for 5 minutes, until soft. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin and paprika for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the turkey and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until there is no pink left. Wash your hands, the board and the spoon with hot soapy water.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, kidney beans, salt and a splash of water. Simmer for 12 minutes, until thick, then stir in the spinach for the last minute. The turkey must reach 74 °C (165 °F).
Split the potatoes, spoon the chili over, and finish with the lemon juice and parsley. Eat half now.

Pack the second portion, with the potato and chili in separate shallow containers, within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
tip: Microwave tomorrow's potato for 2 minutes, then crisp it in a hot oven or an air fryer while the chili heats. Use a wide pot if you cook this at the Big size, so the chili thickens.

name: Sweet potato, chickpea and spinach curry
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian chana aloo masala
about: A creamy, gently spiced curry of sweet potato, chickpeas and lentils in tomato and light coconut milk, with spinach wilted in at the end and lemon and parsley to finish. It makes two portions and is good the next day, with **vitamin A, folate, iron and fibre** all in one pot.
steps: Wash the spinach and parsley. Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the ginger, garlic, curry powder, turmeric and cumin and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Add the sweet potato, crushed tomatoes, coconut milk, salt and enough water to just cover. Bring to a boil, then turn it down, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sweet potato is tender.
Stir in the chickpeas and lentils and cook for 3 minutes, then add the spinach and let it wilt for 1 minute.
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley. Taste and add a pinch more salt if it needs it. Eat half now.

Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F). If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
To freeze, cool within 2 hours and freeze up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: A spoonful of plain yogurt on top cools it down. Add a pinch of chili flakes if you like heat.
ingredients: peeled and cut in 2 cm cubes

name: Salmon potato cakes with crunchy slaw and peas
inspiredBy: Inspired by British fishcakes
about: Golden, oven-baked cakes of canned salmon, mashed potato, egg, onion and mustard, with a crisp cabbage and carrot slaw and sweet peas. The salmon, soft bones and all, brings **omega-3 fats, calcium and vitamin D**, and nothing needs frying.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the potatoes, parsley, cabbage and carrot. Boil the potatoes in salted water for 8 to 10 minutes, until a fork slips in easily. Drain, let them steam dry for 2 minutes, and mash roughly.
While they cook, make the slaw. Toss the cabbage and carrot with the yogurt, half the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and half the parsley. Keep it in the fridge.

Flake the salmon into the mash, mashing the soft bones in. Add the onion, egg, the rest of the parsley and lemon juice, the mustard, pepper, the rest of the salt and the oats, and mix. Wash your hands after handling the raw egg. Shape into 4 cakes and chill them for 5 minutes. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

Line a tray with parchment and brush it with half the oil. Bake the cakes for 10 minutes, flip them, brush with the rest of the oil and bake for 8 to 10 minutes more, until golden and hot through, 74 °C (165 °F).
Heat the peas in a small pot of water or in the microwave until steaming hot, about 3 minutes. Serve the cakes with the slaw and peas.
tip: The cakes firm up if you chill them 30 minutes, so shape them in the morning if you can. Swap the salmon for canned mackerel.
ingredients: peeled and cut in 2 cm cubes

name: Tray-roasted chicken with crushed potatoes and green beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by British roast chicken with crushed potatoes
about: Chicken thighs roasted on one tray with garlicky crushed baby potatoes, green beans and cherry tomatoes, finished with lemon, parsley and a garlic yogurt. The potatoes go crisp on the edges and soak up the chicken juices, and it makes two portions with **protein, vitamin C and potassium**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the potatoes, green beans, tomatoes and parsley. Boil the potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes, until nearly tender, then drain.

Meanwhile, cut the thighs into large pieces and toss them with half the oil, the lemon juice, garlic, thyme, paprika, pepper and half the salt. Wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water.

Tip the potatoes onto a big sheet pan and crush each one lightly with the bottom of a glass. Drizzle with the rest of the oil and salt, push them to the sides, and add the chicken in the middle. Roast for 12 minutes.
Add the green beans and tomatoes to the tray and roast for 10 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece and the potato edges are crisp.
Stir the yogurt with the grated garlic, a squeeze of the lemon and a pinch of salt. Scatter the parsley over the tray, spoon the pan juices over and serve with the garlic yogurt. Eat half now.

Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), with the garlic yogurt added cold. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
tip: If the pan looks crowded, use two so everything roasts instead of steaming. At Standard and Big, roast the chickpeas for Thursday's and Friday's snacks together on the second shelf while the oven is on.
ingredients: most smashed for the tray, a little finely grated for the sauce

name: Turkey meatballs in tomato sauce with white bean mash and peas
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swedish meatballs and mash, with a tomato sauce
about: Tender oven-baked turkey meatballs with roasted carrots, a quick onion and tomato sauce, a creamy mash of potato and white beans and sweet peas. It is meatballs and mash comfort food, and the beans in the mash add **fibre and extra protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a sheet pan. Wash the carrots and parsley. Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes, until very tender.

While they cook, mix the turkey with the egg, oats, the grated onion, garlic, parsley, thyme, half the salt and the pepper. Shape into 6 small balls. Wash your hands and the bowl with hot soapy water.
Put the meatballs and carrot sticks on the tray with a third of the oil and bake for 18 minutes, until the meatballs are browned and reach 74 °C (165 °F) in the middle.
Meanwhile, soften the diced onion in a small pot with a little of the oil for 4 minutes. Add the crushed tomatoes and a pinch of salt and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with the white beans, milk, the rest of the oil and salt. Stir in the peas for the last minute so they heat through until steaming.
Roll the meatballs in the sauce and serve with the mash and carrots.
tip: Mash the white beans in well and nobody will guess they are there.
ingredients: half finely grated, half finely diced
peeled and cut in 3 cm cubes

name: Beef keema aloo with peas and tomato-onion salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi keema aloo
about: Lean ground beef simmered with potatoes, peas and spinach in a tomato, ginger and garam masala sauce, finished with lemon and parsley, with a cool tomato and onion salad on the side. It makes two portions, and the beef and spinach bring **iron and zinc**, with the lemon helping you absorb the iron.
steps: Wash the potatoes, spinach, tomatoes and parsley. Warm the oil in a large lidded pan over medium heat and cook the diced onion for 8 minutes, until soft and golden.

Stir in the ginger, garlic, cumin, turmeric and chili powder for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Add the beef and break it up well. Cook for 6 minutes, until no pink is left. Wash your hands, the board and the spoon with hot soapy water.
Add the crushed tomatoes, potatoes, half the salt and 150 ml of water. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick. The beef must reach 71 °C (160 °F).
Stir in the peas and spinach and cook for 3 minutes, until the peas are steaming hot and the spinach has wilted. Finish with the garam masala, half the lemon juice and half the parsley.
Toss the tomatoes and sliced onion with the rest of the lemon juice, parsley and salt. Serve it alongside, with the yogurt spooned over the keema. Eat half now.

Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), with the salad made fresh and the yogurt added cold. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.
tip: Add a green chili with the ginger if you like it hotter. The flavours deepen overnight, so the leftover is even better.
ingredients: scrubbed and cut in 1.5 cm dice
most finely diced for the sauce, a little thinly sliced for the salad

name: Pan-seared trout with warm mustard potato salad and green beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian trout with potatoes
about: Crisp-skinned rainbow trout on baby spinach with a warm salad of baby potatoes, white beans and green beans in a mustard-lemon dressing. It takes about 35 minutes, and the trout brings **omega-3 fats, vitamin D and B12**.
steps: Wash the potatoes, green beans, spinach and parsley. Put the potatoes in a pot of cold water with a pinch of the salt, bring to a boil and cook for 8 minutes. Add the green beans and cook for 4 minutes more, until both are tender, then drain.
In a big bowl, whisk the mustard, lemon juice, the olive oil, a pinch of salt and the pepper. Toss the warm potatoes and beans in the dressing with the white beans, onion and parsley.

Pat the trout dry and season with the rest of the salt, then wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water. Heat the canola oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat and cook the trout skin-side down for 4 minutes, until the skin is crisp. Flip and cook for 2 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Pile the spinach on a plate, add the potato salad and lay the trout on top.
tip: Swap the trout for Arctic char or salmon. Fish is best eaten the day you cook it. If you cook the potato salad ahead, chill it within 2 hours in a shallow container and eat it within 3 days.

name: Apple and almonds
about: A crisp apple with a handful of almonds. The pair gives you **fibre, healthy fats and vitamin E**, and it keeps in a bag all day.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

name: Hard-cooked egg with hummus and red pepper strips
about: A firm hard-cooked egg with a spoonful of hummus and crunchy red pepper strips. It is a little mezze plate with **protein, choline and vitamin C**.
steps: Put the egg in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil, then cook for 12 minutes so the yolk is completely firm. Cool it in cold water and peel it. Wash your hands after handling the raw egg.
Wash the pepper and cut it into strips. Serve the egg with the hummus and pepper. Keep boiled eggs in the fridge and eat them within 3 days, and use opened hummus within 3 days.

name: Hummus with carrot sticks
about: Creamy hummus with crunchy carrot sticks for dipping. It is **fibre, plant protein and vitamin A** in a few minutes.
steps: Wash and peel the carrot, then cut it into sticks. Serve with the hummus. Keep opened hummus in the fridge and use it within 3 days.

name: Orange and almonds
about: A juicy orange with a handful of almonds. The orange brings **vitamin C**, and the almonds bring vitamin E and some calcium.
steps: Wash the orange, peel it and serve with the almonds.

name: Smoky roasted chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crunchy with smoked paprika and cumin. A handful brings **plant protein, fibre and folate**, and they are good until the end of the day.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Pat the chickpeas very dry with a clean towel and toss them with the oil, paprika, cumin and salt.
Spread them on a small tray and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp. They crisp up more as they cool.
Eat them the same day. For the next day, cool them within 2 hours, keep them covered in the fridge and crisp them in a hot oven or air fryer for 3 to 4 minutes.
ingredients: rinsed, drained and patted very dry

name: Kiwi and sunflower seeds
about: Two sweet-tart kiwis with a spoonful of sunflower seeds. The kiwis bring more **vitamin C** than an orange, and the seeds bring vitamin E and magnesium.
steps: Wash the kiwis, halve them and scoop with a spoon. Eat with the sunflower seeds.
ingredients: washed and halved, eaten with a spoon

name: Greek yogurt with blueberries and sunflower seeds
about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy blueberries and a crunch of sunflower seeds. It is **protein, calcium and vitamin E**, ready in two minutes.
steps: Rinse the blueberries. Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the blueberries and sunflower seeds.
Use fresh blueberries if you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, or boil frozen ones for 1 minute and cool them first.

name: Banana and almonds
about: A banana with a handful of almonds. The banana brings **potassium and vitamin B6**, and the almonds bring protein and vitamin E.
steps: Peel the banana and eat it with the almonds.

name: Creamy oatmeal with blueberries and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian bowl of porridge with maple and berries
about: Rolled oats and a spoonful of iron-fortified instant oats simmered in milk until creamy, topped with blueberries, chopped walnuts and a little maple syrup. It is **plain, warm and easy on a queasy morning**, and the oats bring fibre and iron.
steps: Stir both oats, the milk, a splash of water, cinnamon and a pinch of the iodized salt together in a small pot.
Bring to a gentle bubble over medium heat, then turn it down and cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Rinse the blueberries under cold running water. Spoon the oatmeal into a bowl and top with the blueberries, chopped walnuts and a drizzle of maple syrup.
tip: Too much for a sleepy stomach? Leave off the walnuts and let the oatmeal cool a little. A ripe banana is a good swap for the blueberries.
ingredients: Plain instant oats with iron on the label, such as Quaker Instant Oatmeal, Original. Iron varies by brand, so do not stack other iron-fortified cereal on the same day

name: Firm scrambled eggs and spinach on toast with an orange
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian diner breakfast of eggs and toast
about: Eggs scrambled slowly until fully set, with a handful of wilted spinach, on whole-wheat toast with orange wedges and a glass of milk. It is **simple and filling**, and eggs bring choline, milk brings calcium, and the orange's vitamin C helps your body take up plant iron.
steps: Wash the spinach well and shake it dry. Beat the eggs with the iodized salt and a little pepper, then wash your hands.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Add the spinach and stir for a minute, until it wilts.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently with a spatula. Keep cooking until no liquid egg is left and the eggs are set and fully firm, about 3 minutes.
Toast the bread. Pile the eggs on top and serve with the orange, washed and cut into wedges, and a glass of milk.
tip: Not up for much? Skip the spinach and just have eggs on toast.

name: Yogurt bowl with fruit and toasted oats
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian yogurt parfait
about: Thick Greek yogurt topped with sliced banana, blueberries and a handful of rolled oats toasted with maple and cinnamon. It is **cool, light and easy to eat** when mornings are queasy, and the yogurt brings calcium and iodine.
steps: Warm a dry small pan over medium heat. Add the oats, sunflower seeds and cinnamon and toast, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the maple syrup for 30 seconds, then tip the oats onto a plate to cool and crisp up.
Rinse the blueberries and slice the banana.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, add the fruit and scatter the crunchy oats on top.
tip: Toast a double batch of the oats and keep them in a jar for the next breakfast.

name: Mexican-style tomato eggs with black beans and corn tortillas
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos a la mexicana, with the chili kept mild
about: Eggs scrambled firm with tomato, onion, wilted spinach and a little chili powder, served with warm corn tortillas, black beans and avocado. It is **a bright, savoury breakfast** with folate and iron from the beans, and the eggs bring choline.
steps: Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Rinse the tomato and dice it. Soften the onion with the chili powder for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it breaks down into a thick, saucy mixture. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Wash your hands after cracking the eggs. Add the beaten eggs and the iodized salt and stir gently. Keep cooking until no liquid egg is left and the eggs are set and fully firm, about 3 minutes.
Warm the beans in a small pot and warm the tortillas in a dry pan, about 30 seconds a side.
Serve the eggs with the tortillas, beans and the avocado, its skin rinsed before you slice it.
tip: Want it livelier? Add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the chili powder.

name: Potato, pepper and spinach hash with firm eggs
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian diner breakfast hash
about: Crisp-edged potatoes with sweet red pepper, onion and wilted spinach, topped with eggs cooked until the yolks are set, with a glass of milk. A slow, **weekend diner-style breakfast** with choline from the eggs, calcium from the milk and vitamin C from the pepper.
steps: Wash the potato, pepper and spinach. Cover the diced potato with water in a small pot, bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes, until just tender. Drain well.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Add the potato and cook, turning only now and then, until golden and crisp at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and pepper with the smoked paprika, iodized salt and pepper and cook 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Make two wells in the hash and crack in the eggs, then wash your hands. Break each yolk gently with the tip of a spatula. Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 minutes, until the whites and yolks are fully set and no liquid egg is left. Serve with a glass of milk.
tip: A set yolk feels firm. If it jiggles, cook it longer.

name: Lemon-herb chicken traybake with potatoes, chickpeas and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Canadian Sunday roast chicken, simplified onto one tray
about: Chicken thighs roasted on one tray with potatoes, chickpeas, carrots and broccoli, with lemon, garlic and oregano. It is **one tray and very little washing up**, and the chickpeas add folate and iron. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Heat the oven to 425 F (220 C). Toss the potatoes, carrots and chickpeas on a large tray with half the oil, the oregano, iodized salt and pepper. Roast for 15 minutes.
Scrub the lemon under running water, then zest and juice it. Mix the garlic, lemon zest and juice with the remaining oil and rub it over the chicken.

Push the vegetables aside and nestle the chicken in the middle. Wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken. Roast for 10 minutes, then scatter the washed broccoli florets around it.

Roast 15 to 20 minutes more, until the potatoes are golden and the chicken is cooked through, with no pink left and the juices running clear. A thermometer should read 165 F (74 C) in the thickest part.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
tip: Save a pinch of the zest in step 2 and scatter it over the finished tray for a fresh, bright finish. Reheat the leftover tray in a 350 F (180 C) oven or a pan, not the microwave, so the broccoli stays firm.
ingredients: from a lemon; zest it first

name: Maple-mustard salmon with brown rice and broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by Canadian maple-glazed salmon
about: Salmon fillets baked with a glaze of maple, Dijon and dill, served with nutty brown rice and garlicky lemon broccoli. It is **quick and fresh**, and salmon brings omega-3 DHA, one of the low-mercury fatty fish.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Rinse the rice, then simmer it in plenty of water until tender, about 25 minutes, and drain.
Stir the maple syrup, Dijon, dill and half the garlic together. Place the salmon on a lined tray and spoon the glaze on top with a clean spoon. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the salmon is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. A thermometer should read 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part.
Meanwhile, steam the broccoli for 5 minutes, until tender but still bright green. Toss with the oil, the rest of the garlic, lemon juice, iodized salt and pepper.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the broccoli.
tip: Cook extra rice if you like. Cool it quickly, chill it within 2 hours and use it within a day.

name: Tuscan-style red lentil and spinach soup
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian zuppa di lenticchie, a simple lentil soup
about: Red lentils simmered with carrot, onion, tomato and a little whole-wheat pasta, then finished with spinach, lemon and a sprinkle of Parmesan. **Lentils bring folate and iron**, and the lemon helps your body use the iron. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot with the oregano until soft, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the lentils, tomatoes, broth and 2 cups (500 ml) of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until the pasta and lentils are tender, about 8 more minutes. Stir in the spinach and the iodized salt and cook for 2 minutes, until the spinach is silky.
Finish with the lemon juice and a good grind of pepper. Ladle into bowls and sprinkle with the Parmesan.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
tip: The pasta soaks up broth overnight, so loosen the leftover with a splash of water. Freeze the second portion if you will not eat it tomorrow.

name: Beef and black bean chili with carrots and peppers
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex chili con carne, with extra beans and vegetables
about: A hearty chili of lean ground beef and black beans with onion, carrot, red pepper and tomato, spiced with chili powder and cumin. **Beef and beans are a big iron source**, and the tomatoes and pepper bring vitamin C. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.
steps: Rinse the pepper and carrot before you dice them. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until it is browned all the way through with no pink left, about 6 minutes. Ground beef is done at 160 F (71 C). Wash your hands after handling the raw beef.
Add the onion, pepper and carrot and cook for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin and oregano and stir for a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, beans, iodized salt and 1 cup (250 ml) of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until the chili is thick and the carrot is tender.
Serve with the toast alongside for scooping.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
tip: For a milder pot, use half the chili powder. Reheat leftover chili to 165 F (74 C), steaming hot all the way through.

name: Ginger-soy glazed trout with rice, edamame and soy-dressed spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese teriyaki-style fish, glazed with maple and lemon
about: Trout fillets glazed with ginger, garlic, reduced-sodium soy and maple, served with rice, edamame and a simple soy-dressed spinach. It is **a light Japanese-style dinner** with omega-3 DHA from the trout and folate from the edamame and spinach.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it in plenty of water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain.

Stir the soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, garlic and lemon juice together. Pour a third over the trout and leave a third for the spinach and a third for the pan. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.

Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and cook the trout about 4 minutes a side, until opaque all the way through and flaking easily. A thermometer should read 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part. Tip the last third of the glaze (from a clean spoon) into the pan for the final minute and let it bubble.

Boil the edamame for 5 minutes, until tender. Lift it out, then drop the spinach into the same water for 1 minute, until wilted. Drain the spinach, squeeze out the water and toss it with the middle third of the glaze.
Serve the trout on the rice with the edamame and spinach, drizzling any glaze left in the pan over the top.
tip: This works with salmon too. Tuck in a few slices of cucumber on the side for crunch.

name: Chicken and black bean enchilada bake
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican enchiladas, baked in layers like a casserole
about: Corn tortillas layered with small pieces of chicken, black beans and spinach under a homemade mild red sauce, baked with a little cheddar until bubbling. A **weekend project** that is made once and eaten twice, with iron and folate from the beans and spinach.
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F (190 C). Rinse the pepper before you dice it, and rinse the spinach. Warm the oil in a pan and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, chili powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Spoon half of this mixture into a bowl. Add the tomatoes and iodized salt to the pan and simmer 10 minutes, until thick. This is your sauce.

Cut the chicken into small pieces, then wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water. Cook the chicken in a second pan, stirring, until white all the way through with no pink left (165 F, 74 C), about 8 minutes. Stir in the reserved mixture, the beans, the washed spinach and the lemon juice and cook until the spinach wilts.

Spread a few spoonfuls of sauce over the bottom of a baking dish. Layer in half the tortillas, half the filling and a third of the remaining sauce. Repeat, then top with the last of the sauce and the cheddar.
Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 more minutes, until bubbling and 165 F (74 C) in the middle.

Cool the second portion quickly, pack it into a shallow container and get it into the fridge within 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat it until it reaches 165 F (74 C) and is steaming hot all the way through. Eat it within 2 days.
tip: Warm the tortillas for 20 seconds in the microwave so they do not crack when you layer them.

name: Lemon salmon pasta with broccoli and spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian lemon pasta with greens
about: Whole-wheat pasta tossed with flaked baked salmon, broccoli, spinach, lemon and a little Parmesan. It is **comforting and quick**, and the salmon brings omega-3 DHA while the broccoli and spinach bring folate.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Place the salmon on a lined tray, brush with a little of the oil and season with a pinch of the iodized salt. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until it is opaque all the way through and flakes easily. A thermometer should read 158 F (70 C) at the thickest part. Wash your hands after touching the raw fish.
Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling water until tender, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Save a cup of the pasta water, then drain.

In the empty pot, warm the rest of the oil with the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the spinach and stir until wilted, then add the pasta, broccoli, the zest and juice of the scrubbed lemon and a splash of the pasta water.
Flake the salmon into big pieces and fold it in gently. Season with pepper and the rest of the salt.
Serve with the Parmesan on top.
tip: Want it creamier? Stir in an extra splash of the pasta water and a little more Parmesan.
ingredients: from a lemon; zest it first

name: Light tuna and chickpea sandwich with avocado
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic Canadian tuna salad sandwich
about: Canned light tuna mashed with chickpeas, yogurt, onion, lemon and Dijon open-faced on whole-wheat toast with avocado, with a spinach salad on the side. A quick **no-cook lunch** with some omega-3 from the tuna and fibre from the chickpeas. Light tuna is the low-mercury kind.
steps: Mash the chickpeas with a fork in a bowl until mostly broken down.
Stir in the tuna, yogurt, onion, lemon juice and Dijon. Taste and add pepper.
Toast the bread. Rinse the avocado skin before you cut it. Spread the toast with the mashed avocado and pile on the tuna salad for an open-faced sandwich.
Toss the spinach with a squeeze of the lemon and serve it alongside with the carrot sticks as a quick salad. Keep the filling chilled until you eat it, and refrigerate any extra within 2 hours.
tip: Choose canned light tuna. Skip the albacore (white) tuna here: it is higher in mercury. If you pack it, keep it cold with an ice pack and eat it within 4 hours.

name: Greek-style chickpea and cucumber bowl with lemon yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Greek-style chickpea salad with tzatziki
about: Chickpeas tossed with cucumber, tomato and onion, spooned over a garlicky lemon yogurt with toasted whole-wheat bread alongside. A **fresh, crunchy lunch** that is rich in fibre, folate and iron.
steps: Stir the yogurt with half the lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of the iodized salt.
Rinse the tomato. Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, tomato and onion with the oil, the rest of the lemon juice, the oregano and a little more salt.
Spread the yogurt in a bowl, spoon the chickpea salad on top. Toast the bread and serve it alongside.
tip: Toast the bread and rub it with half a cut garlic clove for extra flavour.

name: Egg salad sandwich with cucumber
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Canadian egg salad sandwich
about: Hard-boiled eggs, cooked until the yolks are fully set, mashed with yogurt and Dijon, on whole-wheat bread with cucumber. A **cool, comforting lunch** that is rich in choline.
steps: Place the eggs in a small pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let them sit for 12 minutes, until the whites and yolks are completely firm.
Cool the eggs in cold water, then peel and chop them.
Stir the eggs with the yogurt, Dijon, onion, lemon juice, iodized salt and pepper.
Pile onto the bread with the cucumber and close the sandwich. Eat it soon and keep any extra chilled.
tip: Make it fresh and don't keep it more than 2 days. Boil an extra egg or two for snacks and keep them in the fridge in their shells.

name: Banana with peanut butter
about: A ripe banana sliced and spread with smooth peanut butter. A **soft, filling snack** with potassium and a little protein.
steps: Peel and slice the banana.
Serve with the peanut butter for dipping or spreading.

name: Orange segments and sunflower seeds
about: Juicy orange segments with a handful of sunflower seeds. A **bright, easy snack** with vitamin C and some vitamin E and magnesium from the seeds.
steps: Wash the orange, peel it and break it into segments.
Serve with the sunflower seeds.

name: Blueberry-ginger yogurt
about: Thick yogurt with fresh blueberries, a little grated fresh ginger and a drizzle of maple syrup. **Cool and soothing**, with calcium and iodine from the yogurt.
steps: Rinse the blueberries.
Stir the ginger into the yogurt and spoon into a bowl. Top with the blueberries and drizzle with maple syrup.

name: Crispy cumin chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crunchy with cumin, paprika and a pinch of salt. A **crunchy, salty snack** with fibre, folate and iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 F (200 C). Pat the chickpeas very dry so they crisp.
Toss them with the oil, cumin, paprika and iodized salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and golden. They crisp further as they cool.
ingredients: rinsed, drained and patted very dry

name: No-bake peanut butter oat bites
about: Iron-fortified instant oats stirred with peanut butter, chopped walnuts and a little maple syrup and rolled into bites. A **sweet little snack** with fibre and some iron from the oats.
steps: Stir the oats, peanut butter, walnuts, maple syrup and cinnamon together in a bowl. Add water a teaspoon at a time, usually 2 or 3, until it holds firmly when pressed.
Press into 3 small balls and chill for 10 minutes. Keep leftovers in the fridge.
tip: Press a few blueberries into the middle of each bite for a juicy surprise.
ingredients: Plain instant oats with iron on the label, such as Quaker Instant Oatmeal, Original. Iron varies by brand, so do not stack other iron-fortified cereal on the same day

name: Maple-roasted walnuts and sunflower seeds
about: Walnuts and sunflower seeds toasted in a pan with a little maple syrup and cinnamon. A **warm, crunchy snack** with omega-3 from the walnuts and vitamin E and magnesium from the seeds.
steps: Toast the walnuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Stir in the maple syrup, cinnamon and iodized salt for 30 seconds, until sticky. Tip onto a plate to cool and crisp.

name: Veggie sticks with lemony yogurt dip
about: Crunchy carrot, cucumber and red pepper sticks with a cool lemon and garlic yogurt dip. **Crisp and refreshing**, with vitamin C from the pepper and calcium from the yogurt.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut them into sticks.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice, garlic and iodized salt. Serve with the vegetables.

name: Blueberry-banana yogurt smoothie
about: A smoothie of milk, banana, blueberries, a handful of spinach and a spoonful of yogurt, blended until smooth. **Cold, sippable and gentle**, with calcium from the milk and yogurt and a little folate from the spinach.
steps: Wash the spinach well.
Blend everything with a few ice cubes until completely smooth, about 1 minute. Drink right away.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and a pinch of salt
about: Shelled edamame boiled until tender and sprinkled with a little iodized salt and lemon. A **fun, protein-rich snack** with folate and iron.
steps: Boil the edamame in a small pot of water until tender, about 5 minutes. Drain.
Sprinkle with the iodized salt and a few drops of lemon juice and serve warm.

name: Egg and tomato toast
about: A hard-boiled egg, cooked until the yolk is fully set, sliced over whole-wheat toast with juicy tomato. A **warm-and-cool little snack** with choline from the egg.
steps: Place the egg in a small pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let it sit for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Rinse and slice the tomato. Toast the bread, top with the tomato slices and the sliced egg, and season with the iodized salt and pepper.

name: Egg and avocado toast
about: Whole-wheat toast with mashed avocado and a hard-boiled egg, cooked until the yolk is fully set. **Creamy and filling**, with choline from the egg and healthy fats from the avocado.
steps: Place the egg in a small pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let it sit for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water and peel.
Rinse the avocado skin before you cut it. Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, iodized salt and a pinch of red pepper flakes.
Toast the bread, spread with the avocado and top with the sliced egg.

name: Gentle lemon poha with moong dal, peas and cashews, and a glass of warm milk
inspiredBy: Inspired by Maharashtrian kanda poha, with moong dal, peas, carrot and cashews and no fried extras
about: Soft flattened rice tossed with mustard seed, turmeric, a little split moong dal, sweet peas and golden cashews, with just enough lemon to wake up a sleepy appetite. It is mild and easy on a queasy morning. The moong dal and the glass of milk on the side add **protein and calcium**.
steps: Rinse the poha in a sieve under cool running water for about 30 seconds, tossing it with your fingers, then leave it to drain and soften. It should feel tender but still hold its shape.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and add the mustard seed. When it pops, add the cashews and curry leaves and stir for a minute until the cashews are pale gold.
Add the ginger, green chili, onion and carrot and cook for about 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the soaked moong dal, peas and turmeric with 100 ml of water, cover and cook for 8 minutes until the dal and peas are tender.
Fold in the drained poha and the salt and warm through for 2 minutes, stirring gently. Finish with the lemon juice and cilantro.
Warm the milk until it is steaming and serve it alongside.
