Spoon the rice into a bowl and arrange the salmon, edamame, cucumber and carrot on top. Squeeze over the rest of the lemon and drizzle with the spicy yogurt.
tip: Not a fan of heat? Leave out the chili. The salmon is never served raw here. Put the rice on first.

name: Smoky turkey and black bean burrito bowl
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex burrito bowls
about: Smoky, cumin-spiced ground turkey and black beans with sweet pepper over brown rice, finished with fresh tomato salsa, creamy avocado and cilantro. The beans and turkey bring **protein, iron and fibre**, and the tomato and pepper bring vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands, board and spoon after handling the raw turkey.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and salt for 1 minute. Add the beans and a splash of water and simmer until hot and the sauce clings, about 4 minutes.
Mix the tomatoes with half of the lemon juice and the cilantro for a quick salsa. Wash the avocado before cutting it.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the turkey and beans, then the salsa and avocado, and squeeze over the rest of the lemon.

Before adding the cold toppings, pack the second portion of rice, turkey and beans into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then add fresh toppings.
tip: The rice, beans and turkey freeze well without the toppings: cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze. Put the rice on first.

name: Ginger chicken, broccoli and edamame stir-fry with walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American chicken and broccoli
about: Tender chicken breast with broccoli, edamame, carrot and mushrooms in a glossy ginger-garlic sauce, over brown rice with a handful of wilted spinach and toasted walnuts. **Broccoli, edamame and spinach** bring vitamin C, folate and iron, and the chicken brings protein.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the soy sauce, ginger, garlic and 3 tablespoons of water together in a small bowl. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes, and set aside.

Heat half of the oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer, turning, until golden and at least 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 6 minutes. Move it to a plate and wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.

Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli, carrot, mushrooms and frozen edamame with a splash of water. Stir-fry until the broccoli is bright green and just tender and the edamame is steaming hot all the way through, about 6 minutes.
Return the chicken and add the spinach, pour in the sauce and stir until the spinach wilts and the sauce is glossy and bubbling, about 1 minute. Finish with the sesame oil.

Spoon over the rice and top with the walnuts. Pack the second portion, without the walnuts, into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Add a splash of water when reheating so the sauce loosens. Put the rice on first.

name: Red lentil and kale dal with brown basmati
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian masoor dal
about: A soft, golden dal of red lentils, tomato and kale with ginger, garlic, cumin and garam masala, served over brown basmati with a cool cucumber side and a spoonful of yogurt. The lentils and kale bring **iron, folate and calcium**, and the lemon helps your body absorb that iron.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds until they sizzle, about 30 seconds, then add the onion and cook until soft and golden, about 7 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and chili for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, lentils, salt and 3 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed into a thick soup, about 15 minutes. Add water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the kale and garam masala and simmer until the kale is tender, about 6 minutes, then finish with the lemon juice. Toss the cucumber with the cilantro.

Serve the dal over the rice with the cucumber and a spoonful of yogurt on the side. Cool the second portion of dal and rice within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep the yogurt and cucumber separate, and refrigerate. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), with a splash of water.
tip: To freeze the dal, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days, never refreezing. Reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Put the rice on first.

name: Turmeric-lemon trout with green herb rice and roast broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by Persian sabzi polo ba mahi, herbed rice with fish
about: A trout fillet rubbed with turmeric and garlic and roasted next to broccoli, served on brown basmati tossed with kale, parsley, cilantro and dill, with plenty of lemon. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the kale and broccoli bring vitamin C, vitamin K and folate.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the kale, broccoli, parsley and cilantro. Finely chop the kale and the herbs and cut the broccoli into florets.

Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, adding the kale for the last 2 minutes. Drain well. Meanwhile, toss the broccoli with a little of the oil and a pinch of the salt on a lined tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Rub the trout with the turmeric, half of the garlic, a little oil, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Push the broccoli to one side, lay the trout on the tray and roast until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), 10 to 12 minutes.
Warm the rest of the oil and garlic in the empty rice pot for 30 seconds, then tip the rice and kale back in with the dill, parsley, cilantro and half of the lemon juice and stir.
Serve the trout on the herb rice with the broccoli, and squeeze over the rest of the lemon.
tip: Put the rice on first. No dried dill? Use a little more parsley.
ingredients: skin on or off, pin bones removed

name: Beef bibimbap-style bowl with sesame vegetables and chili-lemon sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean bibimbap, with a soy-garlic beef and a chili-lemon sauce in place of gochujang
about: Thin soy-garlic beef over brown rice with separate little piles of sesame spinach, carrot, zucchini, mushrooms and edamame, finished with a chili-lemon sauce you stir through at the table. The vegetables bring **vitamin A, folate and fibre** (the edamame adds protein), and the beef brings iron and zinc.
steps: Mix half of the soy sauce, the garlic, half of the sesame oil and a few grinds of pepper with the beef. Marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes, never reusing the marinade for anything else. Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the gochugaru, lemon juice, the rest of the soy sauce and a spoonful of water together for the sauce.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, drain it and squeeze it dry. Toss it with a little of the sesame oil and the salt.
Pour hot water over the frozen edamame until steaming hot all the way through, then drain, and keep it as its own pile.

Warm a little of the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the carrot, zucchini and mushrooms separately, each for 2 to 4 minutes until just tender, with a pinch of salt, keeping the piles apart.

Cook the beef in the rest of the oil over high heat, in two batches, until browned and at least 71 °C (160 °F), about 3 minutes a batch. Wash your hands, board, knife and tongs after handling the raw beef.
Fry the eggs in the nonstick pan with the last of the olive oil, flip them and cook until the whites and yolks are completely firm, about 4 minutes in all.
Put the rice in bowls and arrange the beef, edamame and vegetables on top in separate piles. Top each with a firm egg, finish with the remaining sesame oil and serve with the sauce to stir through.

Pack the second portion without the egg, with the sauce on the side, into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then add the sauce. Fry a fresh firm egg to go on top.
tip: Short on time? Skip the zucchini and use extra spinach. Use less gochugaru for less heat. Put the rice on first.
ingredients: sliced very thinly across the grain

name: Yogurt-spiced salmon with kale and chickpea masala over brown basmati
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian tandoori-style fish and chana masala
about: Salmon fillet marinated in lemony yogurt and warm spices and roasted until flaky, served over brown basmati with a quick tomato, kale and chickpea masala. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas and kale bring fibre, iron and calcium.
steps: Mix the yogurt, half of the lemon juice, half of the garam masala, the turmeric, half of the salt and half of the garlic and ginger. Coat the salmon and marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes, never reusing the marinade. Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray. Lift the salmon onto the tray, leaving the extra marinade behind, and roast until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), 10 to 12 minutes. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds until they sizzle, then the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the rest of the garlic and ginger, the rest of the garam masala and the chili for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, the rest of the salt and a splash of water and simmer until the tomatoes collapse, about 6 minutes. Stir in the kale and simmer until tender, about 5 minutes, then finish with the rest of the lemon juice.
Serve the salmon over the rice with the chickpea masala spooned alongside and the cilantro scattered over.
tip: Leave out the chili for a mild version. Put the rice on first.

name: Apple with almonds
about: A crisp apple with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

name: Pear with walnuts
about: A juicy pear with a few walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the pear brings fibre.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it and serve with the walnuts.

name: Orange with walnuts
about: A juicy orange with a few walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange, peel and segment it, and serve with the walnuts.

name: Apple slices with walnuts and cinnamon
about: Crisp apple slices with a few walnuts and a shake of cinnamon. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it, dust with the cinnamon and serve with the walnuts.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A banana with a few walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the banana brings potassium.
steps: Slice the banana, dust with the cinnamon and serve with the walnuts.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and chili
about: Warm edamame with lemon, a pinch of chili and a little salt. The edamame brings **protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Pour boiling water over the frozen edamame, or microwave them, until steaming hot all the way through, then drain.
Toss with the lemon, chili and salt.

name: Carrot and cucumber sticks with lemony yogurt dip
about: Crunchy carrot and cucumber sticks with a cool lemon-yogurt dip. The yogurt brings **calcium and protein**, and the carrot brings vitamin A.
steps: Wash the carrot and cucumber and cut them into sticks.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, salt and pepper together and serve with the sticks.

name: Lemony sardines with cucumber and cherry tomatoes
about: A small plate of canned sardines with cucumber, cherry tomatoes, lemon and parsley. The sardines bring **omega-3, calcium and vitamin B12**, and the lemon and tomatoes brighten them.
steps: Wash the cucumber, tomatoes and parsley, then slice the cucumber, halve the tomatoes and chop the parsley.
Arrange the vegetables on a plate, lay the sardines alongside, and finish with the lemon juice, parsley and pepper.
tip: Keep an opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

name: Blueberries with walnuts
about: A bowl of blueberries with a few walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3 and vitamin E**, and the blueberries bring vitamin C and fibre.
steps: Rinse the blueberries and serve with the walnuts.

name: Pear with almonds
about: A juicy pear with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the pear brings fibre.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it and serve with the almonds.

name: Orange with almonds
about: A juicy orange with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E, magnesium and a little calcium**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange, peel and segment it, and serve with the almonds.

name: Banana with almonds and cinnamon
about: A banana with a few almonds and a dusting of cinnamon. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the banana brings potassium.
steps: Slice the banana, dust with the cinnamon and serve with the almonds.

name: Savoury brown rice breakfast bowl with kale, mushrooms and firm egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean and Chinese savoury rice breakfasts
about: Warm brown rice stir-fried with mushrooms and kale, topped with firm scrambled egg and a drizzle of sesame oil, with a glass of milk on the side. **Eggs and mushrooms** bring choline and B vitamins, and the kale brings calcium and vitamin K.
steps: Wash the kale and mushrooms, slice the mushrooms and thinly slice the kale. Beat the eggs with a splash of water.
Warm the olive oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms until golden, about 4 minutes, then add the kale and a splash of water and stir until it is tender, about 3 minutes.
Add the rice and soy sauce and stir until it is steaming hot all the way through. Push everything to one side.
Pour the eggs into the empty side and stir until completely set and firm, about 2 minutes, then mix them through.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve with a glass of milk.
tip: Microwave a pouch of rice for 2 minutes. Rice from a previous night must have been cooled within 1 hour in a shallow container and used within 3 days; reheat it until steaming hot.
ingredients: ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

name: Warm cinnamon pear over Greek yogurt with oat and almond crunch
about: Cold Greek yogurt under soft pear simmered with cinnamon and a little ginger, topped with a crunchy toasted oat and almond mix. The yogurt brings **protein and calcium**, and the pear and oats bring fibre.
steps: Toast the oats and almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes. Tip them out to cool.
Wash the pear and dice it. Simmer it in the same pan with the cinnamon, ginger and a splash of water until soft, about 5 minutes.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the warm pear and scatter over the crunch.
tip: Toast a few days' worth of crunch at once and keep it in a jar.

name: Savoury ginger-soy oats with mushrooms, spinach and edamame
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese savoury rice porridge, made with oats
about: Creamy oats cooked in water with ginger and soy, topped with golden mushrooms, wilted spinach and warm edamame and a drizzle of sesame oil, with a glass of milk on the side. The edamame and oats bring **protein and fibre**, and the spinach brings iron and folate.
steps: Wash the mushrooms and spinach and slice the mushrooms. Pour hot water over the frozen edamame until steaming hot all the way through, then drain.
Bring the oats, grated ginger and 250 ml of water to a gentle simmer in a small pot, stirring, until thick and creamy, about 6 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a nonstick pan and cook the mushrooms until golden, about 4 minutes. Add the spinach and soy sauce and stir until the spinach wilts.
Spoon the oats into a bowl, top with the mushrooms, spinach and edamame, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve with a glass of milk.
tip: Add a splash of water if the oats thicken as they stand.

name: Cooked salmon poke-style bowl with spicy yogurt drizzle
inspiredBy: Inspired by Hawaiian poke bowls, with the salmon fully cooked
about: Cubes of soy-ginger salmon, cooked through and served warm over brown rice with cool edamame, cucumber and carrot ribbons. A spicy lemon-yogurt drizzle ties it together. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the edamame brings protein and folate.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, pour hot water over the frozen edamame until steaming hot all the way through, then drain. Wash the cucumber and carrot, slice the cucumber and peel the carrot into ribbons.
Stir the yogurt, chili, half of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt together for the drizzle. Stir the soy sauce, ginger and sesame oil together for the glaze.

Warm a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Add the salmon cubes and cook, turning, until opaque and flaky and at least 70 °C (158 °F) inside, 4 to 5 minutes. Pour in the glaze for the last minute so it coats the fish. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Lay the spinach in a bowl, spoon the rice over it and arrange the salmon, edamame, cucumber and carrot on top. Squeeze over the rest of the lemon and drizzle with the spicy yogurt.
tip: Not a fan of heat? Leave out the chili. The salmon is never served raw here. Put the rice on first.

name: Cumin chicken, lentil and roasted vegetable brown rice bowl with lemon yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern roasted chicken and lentil rice bowls
about: Chicken breast, carrot, zucchini and cherry tomatoes roasted with cumin and paprika, piled on brown rice with warm lentils, wilted spinach, a cool lemon-yogurt sauce and parsley. The lentils and spinach bring **iron, folate and fibre**, and the lemon helps your body absorb that iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the carrot, zucchini, tomatoes, spinach and parsley. Slice the carrot thinly so it cooks quickly.

Toss the chicken, carrot, zucchini, onion and tomatoes on a tray with the oil, cumin, paprika and most of the salt. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken. Roast until the carrot is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir the yogurt, half of the lemon juice, the rest of the salt and a spoonful of water together. Heat the rice and the lentils separately, until steaming hot.
Stir the spinach into the hot tray for a minute, until it wilts.
Spoon the rice into a bowl, top with the lentils and the roasted chicken and vegetables, and drizzle with the yogurt sauce. Squeeze over the rest of the lemon and finish with the parsley.
tip: Packing it? Cook it the night before, cool the chicken, vegetables, rice and lentils in a shallow container in the fridge within 1 hour and keep the yogurt sauce apart. Carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack, reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), add the sauce and eat it the same day.
ingredients: ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

name: Warm ginger-soy chickpeas with kale, red pepper and egg over brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-style soy-ginger stir-fried greens and beans
about: Chickpeas, red pepper and wilted kale stir-fried with ginger, soy sauce and a drizzle of sesame oil, spooned over brown rice with a firm hard-boiled egg, lemon, cilantro and toasted walnuts. The chickpeas and kale bring **iron, folate and calcium**, and the lemon and pepper bring vitamin C to help absorb the iron.
steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and boil it for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it under cold water and peel it. Wash the kale, pepper and cilantro, slice the pepper and onion, grate the ginger and chop the kale, discarding the thick stems.
Warm the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft and starting to brown, about 8 minutes. Stir in the ginger and soy sauce for 30 seconds.
Add the kale and a splash of water, cover and cook until the kale is tender, about 4 minutes. Stir in the chickpeas and salt and heat until steaming hot. Heat the rice until steaming.
Season with the lemon juice. Spoon over the rice, halve the egg and set it on top, and finish with the cilantro, walnuts and a drizzle of sesame oil.
tip: Packing it? Make it the night before and cool it in a shallow container in the fridge within 1 hour. Carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack, reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and eat it the same day.
ingredients: boiled until the yolk is firm, as in the steps
ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

name: Smoky turkey and black bean burrito bowl
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex burrito bowls
about: Smoky, cumin-spiced ground turkey and black beans with sweet pepper over brown rice, finished with fresh tomato salsa, creamy avocado and cilantro. The beans and turkey bring **protein, iron and fibre**, and the tomato and pepper bring vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands, board and spoon after handling the raw turkey.

Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and salt for 1 minute. Add the beans and a splash of water and simmer until hot and the sauce clings, about 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach for the last minute, until it wilts.
Mix the tomatoes with half of the lemon juice and the cilantro for a quick salsa. Wash the avocado before cutting it.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the turkey and beans, then the salsa and avocado, and squeeze over the rest of the lemon.

Before adding the cold toppings, pack the second portion of rice, turkey and beans into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then add fresh toppings.
tip: The rice, beans and turkey freeze well without the toppings: cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze. Put the rice on first.

name: Ginger chicken, broccoli and edamame stir-fry with walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American chicken and broccoli
about: Tender chicken breast with broccoli, edamame, carrot and mushrooms in a glossy ginger-garlic sauce, over brown rice with a handful of wilted spinach and toasted walnuts. **Broccoli, edamame and spinach** bring vitamin C, folate and iron, and the chicken brings protein.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the soy sauce, ginger, garlic and 3 tablespoons of water together in a small bowl. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant, about 3 minutes, and set aside.

Heat half of the oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer, turning, until golden and at least 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 6 minutes. Move it to a plate and wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.

Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli, carrot, mushrooms and frozen edamame with a splash of water. Stir-fry until the broccoli is bright green and just tender and the edamame is steaming hot all the way through, about 6 minutes.
Return the chicken and add the spinach, pour in the sauce and stir until the spinach wilts and the sauce is glossy and bubbling, about 1 minute. Finish with the sesame oil.

Spoon over the rice and top with the walnuts. Pack the second portion, without the walnuts, into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Add a splash of water when reheating so the sauce loosens. Put the rice on first.

name: Red lentil and kale dal with brown basmati and a firm egg
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian masoor dal
about: A soft, golden dal of red lentils, tomato and kale with ginger, garlic, cumin and garam masala, served over brown basmati with a firm boiled egg, a cool cucumber side and a spoonful of yogurt. The lentils and kale bring **iron, folate and calcium**, the egg adds choline, and the lemon helps your body absorb the iron.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Put the eggs, one for each portion, in a small pot of cold water, bring to a boil and boil 10 minutes, until the yolks are completely firm. Cool them under cold water.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds until they sizzle, about 30 seconds, then add the onion and cook until soft and golden, about 7 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and chili for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, lentils, salt and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed into a thick soup, about 15 minutes. Add water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the kale and garam masala and simmer until the kale is tender, about 6 minutes, then finish with the lemon juice. Toss the cucumber with the cilantro.

Serve the dal over the rice with one egg, peeled and halved, the cucumber and a spoonful of yogurt on the side. Cool the second portion of dal and rice within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep the yogurt and cucumber separate, and refrigerate it with the second egg still in its shell. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), with a splash of water.
tip: To freeze the dal, without the egg, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days, never refreezing. Reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Put the rice on first.
ingredients: boiled until the yolk is firm, as in the steps

name: Lemony sardine, edamame and cucumber brown rice bowl
inspiredBy: Inspired by Portuguese and Greek sardine and rice salads
about: Canned sardines flaked over brown rice with edamame, cucumber and parsley, finished with a lemon-yogurt dressing and a few almonds. The sardines bring **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D**, and the edamame adds fibre and protein.
steps: Pour boiling water over the frozen edamame, or microwave them, until steaming hot all the way through, then drain. Heat the rice until steaming and let it cool a few minutes.
Wash the cucumber and parsley. Slice the cucumber and chop the parsley.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper together.
Pile the rice, edamame and cucumber in a bowl, flake the sardines on top and spoon over the dressing. Finish with the parsley and almonds.
tip: Keep an opened tin covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Packing it? Spread the heated rice in a shallow container and chill it within 1 hour before you build the bowl, then carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
ingredients: ready-cooked pouch or frozen, or rice cooked and chilled earlier

name: Beef bibimbap-style bowl with sesame vegetables and chili-lemon sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean bibimbap, with a soy-garlic beef and a chili-lemon sauce in place of gochujang
about: Thin soy-garlic beef over brown rice with separate little piles of sesame spinach, carrot, zucchini, mushrooms and edamame, finished with a chili-lemon sauce you stir through at the table. The vegetables bring **vitamin A, folate and fibre** (the edamame adds protein), and the beef brings iron and zinc.
steps: Mix half of the soy sauce, the garlic, half of the sesame oil and a few grinds of pepper with the beef. Marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes, never reusing the marinade for anything else. Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the gochugaru, lemon juice, the rest of the soy sauce and a spoonful of water together for the sauce.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, drain it and squeeze it dry. Toss it with a little of the sesame oil and the salt.
Pour hot water over the frozen edamame until steaming hot all the way through, then drain, and keep it as its own pile.

Warm a little of the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the carrot, zucchini and mushrooms separately, each for 2 to 4 minutes until just tender, with a pinch of salt, keeping the piles apart.

Cook the beef in the rest of the oil over high heat, in two batches, until browned and at least 71 °C (160 °F), about 3 minutes a batch. Wash your hands, board, knife and tongs after handling the raw beef.
Fry the eggs in the nonstick pan with the last of the olive oil, flip them and cook until the whites and yolks are completely firm, about 4 minutes in all.
Put the rice in bowls and arrange the beef, edamame and vegetables on top in separate piles. Top each with a firm egg, finish with the remaining sesame oil and serve with the sauce to stir through.

Pack the second portion without the egg, with the sauce on the side, into a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. Eat within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then add the sauce. Fry a fresh firm egg to go on top.
tip: Short on time? Skip the zucchini and use extra spinach. Use less gochugaru for less heat. Put the rice on first.
ingredients: sliced very thinly across the grain

name: Yogurt-spiced salmon with kale and chickpea masala over brown basmati
inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian tandoori-style fish and chana masala
about: Salmon fillet marinated in lemony yogurt and warm spices and roasted until flaky, served over brown basmati with a quick tomato, kale and chickpea masala. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the chickpeas and kale bring fibre, iron and calcium.
steps: Mix the yogurt, half of the lemon juice, half of the garam masala, the turmeric, half of the salt and half of the garlic and ginger. Coat the salmon and marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes, never reusing the marinade. Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain and fluff it.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray. Lift the salmon onto the tray, leaving the extra marinade behind, and roast until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), 10 to 12 minutes. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds until they sizzle, then the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the rest of the garlic and ginger, the rest of the garam masala and the chili for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, the rest of the salt and a splash of water and simmer until the tomatoes collapse, about 6 minutes. Stir in the kale and simmer until tender, about 5 minutes, then finish with the rest of the lemon juice.
Serve the salmon over the rice with the chickpea masala spooned alongside and the cilantro scattered over.
tip: Leave out the chili for a mild version. Put the rice on first.

name: Apple with almonds
about: A crisp apple with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

name: Turmeric-lemon trout with green herb rice and roast broccoli
inspiredBy: Inspired by Persian sabzi polo ba mahi, herbed rice with fish
about: A trout fillet rubbed with turmeric and garlic and roasted next to broccoli, served on brown basmati tossed with kale, parsley, cilantro and dill, with plenty of lemon. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the kale and broccoli bring vitamin C, vitamin K and folate.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the kale, broccoli, parsley and cilantro. Finely chop the kale and the herbs and cut the broccoli into florets.

Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender, 25 to 30 minutes, adding the kale for the last 2 minutes. Drain well. Meanwhile, toss the broccoli with a little of the oil and a pinch of the salt on a lined tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Rub the trout with the turmeric, half of the garlic, a little oil, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Push the broccoli to one side, lay the trout on the tray and roast until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), 10 to 12 minutes.
Warm the rest of the oil and garlic in the empty rice pot for 30 seconds, then tip the rice and kale back in with the dill, parsley, cilantro and half of the lemon juice and stir.
Serve the trout on the herb rice with the broccoli, and squeeze over the rest of the lemon.
tip: Put the rice on first. No dried dill? Use a little more parsley.
ingredients: skin on or off, pin bones removed

name: Orange, banana and blueberry cup
about: Orange segments, sliced banana and blueberries with a squeeze of lemon, a bright snack that packs well. It brings **vitamin C, potassium and fibre**.
steps: Wash the orange and the blueberries. Peel the orange and cut it into segments, and slice the banana.
Toss together with the lemon juice and eat right away, or pack in a lidded tub.

name: Berry and walnut overnight oats
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss bircher muesli
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt until creamy, with frozen berries that thaw into a berry swirl and a crunch of walnuts. Five minutes the night before, nothing to cook in the morning, and it brings **protein and fibre** before you leave the house.
steps: Wash your hands. Stir the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon together in a jar until there are no dry patches.
Spoon the frozen berries on top, put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. They thaw into the oats and turn them pink, which is what you want.
In the morning, stir it up. If it is thick, loosen it with a splash of milk. Scatter the walnuts on just before eating so they stay crisp.
Keep it in the fridge and eat it within 2 days of making it.
tip: Make it Sunday night for Monday and Wednesday night for Thursday. At the Big size, use a big bowl or a 1 litre jar. If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

name: Apple cinnamon overnight oats with pumpkin seeds
inspiredBy: Inspired by apple pie oatmeal
about: Rolled oats soaked in milk and yogurt with grated apple and plenty of cinnamon, topped with toasted pumpkin seeds. It tastes like apple crisp in a jar, and the seeds bring **iron, zinc and magnesium** along with a good crunch.
steps: Wash your hands and the apple. Grate the apple, skin and all, into a jar.
Add the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon and stir until everything is wet and evenly mixed.
Put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. The oats soften and the apple sweetens the whole jar.
In the morning, stir it and loosen with a splash of milk if needed. Top with the pumpkin seeds and eat within 2 days of making it.
tip: Warm it in the microwave for a minute if you like your oats porridge-style, then add the pumpkin seeds.
ingredients: washed and coarsely grated, skin on

name: Banana walnut overnight oats
inspiredBy: Inspired by banana bread, in a jar
about: Overnight oats with mashed banana, cinnamon and walnuts, creamy from Greek yogurt. It tastes like banana bread but gives you **fibre, protein and potassium** to start the day.
steps: Wash your hands. Mash half the banana in a jar until mostly smooth.
Stir in the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon until no dry oats remain.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, stir, loosen with a splash of milk if needed, and top with the rest of the banana, sliced, and the walnuts. Eat within 2 days of making it.
tip: Use a very ripe banana for the sweetest jar.

name: Sheet-pan sweet potato, spinach and feta egg bake
inspiredBy: Inspired by a frittata, baked on one tray
about: A weekend tray of diced sweet potato, red pepper and spinach set in beaten eggs with a little feta and smoked paprika, cut into squares. It makes two breakfasts, and the sweet potato and spinach bring **vitamin A and folate** alongside plenty of protein.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the sweet potato, pepper and spinach before cutting. Toss the sweet potato and pepper on a lined sheet pan with the oil, paprika, salt and pepper.
Roast for 15 minutes, until the sweet potato is just tender when poked with a fork.
Scatter the spinach over the tray and push everything into an even layer. Beat the eggs and pour them evenly over the vegetables, then crumble on the feta.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the eggs are completely set and firm in the centre, with no wet patches. The centre should reach 74 °C (165 °F).
Let it stand for 5 minutes, then cut into squares. Eat half now. Pack the other half in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate.
Reheat the second portion once, until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and eat it within 3 days.
tip: A spoonful of plain yogurt on the side cools it down. Roast the sweet potato and pepper the night before and the bake takes about 15 minutes.
ingredients: scrubbed and cut in small dice

name: Tuna, egg and potato salad with green beans and lemon-parsley dressing
inspiredBy: Inspired by a French Niçoise salad
about: Warm little potatoes, crisp green beans, light tuna and a firm hard-boiled egg tossed in a lemony olive oil dressing with tomatoes and spinach. The tuna, egg and white beans bring **protein, choline and B vitamins**, and the whole thing comes together in one pot.
steps: Wash the potatoes, beans, spinach, tomatoes and parsley. Halve any big potatoes so they cook evenly. Cover them with cold water, add the egg in its shell and bring to a boil.
Boil for 10 minutes so the yolk is completely firm. Add the green beans for the last 4 minutes. Lift the egg into cold water, drain the rest and let it steam dry for a minute.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl. Toss the warm potatoes, beans, white beans and onion through it so they soak up the dressing.
Peel and quarter the egg. Serve everything over the spinach with the tomatoes, parsley and walnuts, and flake the tuna on top.
tip: Boil the potatoes and eggs on Sunday night, with 2 extra eggs for Tuesday's snack, and cool them within 2 hours. The potatoes keep 3 days in the fridge, and the eggs keep in their shells for up to 1 week.

name: Lemon tuna and white bean salad with spinach
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan tonno e fagioli
about: Flaked light tuna and creamy white beans over spinach and tomatoes, tossed in lemon and olive oil with red onion and parsley. No pans to wash, and the beans and tuna bring **protein, fibre and iron**, with lemon to help you absorb it.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomatoes and parsley.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl. Add the onion and let it sit 5 minutes to soften.
Add the beans, tomatoes and parsley and toss to coat. Flake in the tuna and fold it through gently.
Pile onto the spinach and finish with a crack of pepper.
tip: Pack the dressed beans and the spinach separately if you are taking it to work.

name: Sardine and chickpea salad with tomato and lemon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish tinned-fish tapas
about: Warm chickpeas tossed with juicy tomatoes, red onion, parsley and lemon, with canned sardines piled on top over spinach. Sardines with their soft bones bring **omega-3, vitamin D and calcium** for almost no effort.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomatoes and parsley. Warm the chickpeas in a small pan or the microwave until hot, 1 to 2 minutes.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl. Toss in the warm chickpeas, onion and tomatoes and let them sit for 5 minutes.
Fold in the parsley and pile onto the spinach.
Top with the sardines, broken into big pieces, and squeeze on a little more lemon.
tip: The tomatoes burst a little as they sit in the warm chickpeas, which makes its own sauce.

name: Lemon-oregano chicken thighs with chickpeas, squash and red onion
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek-style lemon roast chicken
about: Juicy chicken thighs roasted on one tray with chickpeas, butternut squash and red onion, with garlic, lemon and fresh oregano. The chickpeas crisp at the edges and soak up the pan juices, and the dish brings **protein, fibre and vitamin A**. It makes tomorrow's lunch too.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the squash, onion, spinach and oregano before cutting. Toss the squash, onion and garlic on a big sheet pan with half the oil and a third of the salt. Roast for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut the thighs into large pieces so they cook fast, then toss them with the rest of the oil, the lemon juice, half the oregano, the pepper and half the remaining salt. Wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water.

Push the vegetables aside and add the chicken and the chickpeas to the tray, seasoning the chickpeas with the last of the salt. Roast for 18 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part and the squash is tender.
Scatter the spinach over the hot tray and let it wilt for a minute. Finish with the rest of the oregano and spoon the pan juices over everything.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Cut the squash into even chunks so it finishes with the chicken. A spoonful of plain yogurt on the side is lovely. If the pan looks crowded, use two so everything roasts instead of steaming.
ingredients: peeled and cut in 2 cm chunks

name: Sheet-pan salmon with baby potatoes, white beans, broccoli and lemon-parsley yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian salmon and potatoes
about: Salmon roasted on one tray alongside crisp little potatoes, white beans and broccoli, finished with a cool lemon, garlic and parsley yogurt sauce. It is about 35 minutes start to finish, and the salmon brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, with iron and fibre from the beans.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the potatoes, broccoli, spinach and parsley. Toss the potatoes on a large sheet pan with half the oil and a third of the salt. Roast for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir the yogurt, parsley, garlic, half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt in a small bowl. Keep it in the fridge.
Toss the broccoli with the rest of the oil and push the potatoes to one side. Season the salmon with the rest of the salt and the pepper. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.

Add the salmon, the beans and the broccoli to the tray and roast for 10 minutes, adding the spinach for the last 2 minutes so it wilts, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and the broccoli is charred at the tips.
Squeeze the remaining lemon juice over everything and serve with the yogurt sauce.
tip: Swap the salmon for trout or Arctic char.
ingredients: baby potatoes, scrubbed and cut in 2 cm pieces

name: Harissa cauliflower and lentil tray with baked eggs and feta
inspiredBy: Inspired by North African harissa roasting
about: Cauliflower and carrots roasted in a harissa and cumin rub until sweet and charred, tossed with lentils, topped with baked eggs and finished with feta, parsley and toasted almonds. A vegetarian tray with **iron, folate, choline and fibre**, with lemon to help your body absorb the iron. It makes tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the cauliflower, carrots, onion and parsley before cutting. Whisk the harissa, oil, cumin and half the lemon juice in a big bowl with the salt.
Toss the cauliflower, carrots and onion in the harissa mix and spread them on a sheet pan in a single layer. Roast for 20 minutes, turning once, until the edges are charred.

Scatter the lentils over the tray. Make a well in the vegetables for each egg and crack them in, then roast 10 to 14 minutes more, until the whites are set and the yolks are completely firm all the way through. Scatter the almonds on for the last 3 minutes so they toast.
Crumble over the feta and parsley and squeeze on the remaining lemon. Serve with a dollop of yogurt.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Use less harissa for a milder tray, and taste your jar first, since heat varies a lot. If the pan looks crowded, use two so everything roasts instead of steaming.

name: Fajita chicken tray with peppers, black beans and sweet potato
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex fajitas, without the tortillas
about: Strips of chicken breast, peppers and onion roasted with smoky fajita spices, with black beans and sweet potato wedges on the same tray. Serve with a quick lime yogurt. It brings **protein, fibre and vitamin C**, and makes tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potato, peppers, onion and parsley before cutting. Toss the sweet potato cubes with a third of the oil and a pinch of salt on a large sheet pan and roast for 10 minutes.

Mix the chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder and remaining salt. Toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the rest of the oil and the spice mix. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

Add the chicken, peppers, onion and beans to the tray in a single layer, pushing the sweet potato aside. Roast for 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the edges of the peppers are browned.
Stir the lime juice into the yogurt with a pinch of salt. Squeeze a little lime over the tray too.
Serve with the lime yogurt and the parsley.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Reheat the leftover portion in a hot pan so the edges crisp again.

name: Sheet-pan trout with sweet potato, broccoli and tahini-lemon sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern fish with tahini
about: Rainbow trout roasted on one tray with sweet potato and a big pile of broccoli, drizzled with a nutty lemon and garlic tahini sauce. Trout is a mild, tender fatty fish that brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the tahini sauce adds a nutty richness and a little calcium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potatoes, broccoli, spinach and parsley. Toss the sweet potato cubes on a sheet pan with half the oil and a third of the salt. Roast for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the tahini, half the lemon juice, the garlic, a pinch of salt and 2 to 3 tablespoons of cold water until pourable.
Toss the broccoli with the rest of the oil. Rub the trout with the pepper and a pinch of salt. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Add the broccoli and the trout to the tray and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, adding the spinach for the last 2 minutes so it wilts, until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Squeeze the rest of the lemon over the tray, drizzle with the tahini sauce and scatter with the parsley.
tip: Salmon or Arctic char works here too.

name: Turkey meatball tray with baby potatoes, white beans and cherry tomatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian polpette al forno
about: Oven-baked turkey meatballs with oats, garlic and parsley on a tray of baby potatoes, white beans, sweet red pepper and cherry tomatoes that burst into a sauce, with spinach wilted in at the end. It is a weekend tray that makes two portions, with **protein, fibre and potassium**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the potatoes, pepper, tomatoes, spinach, parsley and oregano before cutting. Mix the turkey, oats, egg, onion, half the garlic, half the parsley, a pinch of salt and the pepper with your hands. Shape into golf-ball sized meatballs, then wash your hands, the board and any utensil with hot soapy water.
On a large sheet pan, stir the potatoes, whole cherry tomatoes, white beans, pepper, the rest of the garlic, the oregano, the oil and the rest of the salt. Nestle the meatballs in on top.
Bake for 30 minutes, stirring the potatoes once, until the meatballs reach 74 °C (165 °F) in the centre, the potatoes are tender and the tomatoes have burst into a thick sauce.
Stir the spinach and lemon juice through the hot tray so the spinach wilts. Scatter with the rest of the parsley.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Freeze the second portion if you will not eat it within 3 days, then thaw it in the fridge and use within 2 days. If the pan looks crowded, use two so everything roasts instead of steaming.
ingredients: baby potatoes, cut in 2 cm pieces

name: Beef kofta tray with cauliflower, chickpeas and tahini yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern kofta and roasted cauliflower
about: Lean beef kofta spiced with cumin, coriander and cinnamon, roasted with cauliflower, tomatoes and chickpeas and drizzled with a cooling tahini yogurt. A Sunday tray with **iron, zinc and protein**, and the lemon and tomatoes help you absorb the iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the cauliflower, tomatoes and parsley before cutting. Toss the cauliflower on a sheet pan with half the oil and a third of the salt. Roast for 12 minutes.

Mix the beef, onion, half the garlic, half the parsley, cumin, coriander, cinnamon and half the remaining salt with your hands. Shape into small fingers or patties, then wash your hands and the board.
Add the kofta, chickpeas and tomatoes to the tray with the rest of the oil and salt. Roast for 12 to 15 minutes, until the kofta reach 71 °C (160 °F) in the centre and the tomatoes have burst.
Whisk the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice and the rest of the garlic with a splash of water. Drizzle over the tray and scatter with the rest of the parsley.
tip: Make double and freeze the uncooked kofta. Thaw it in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.

name: Apple and almonds
about: A crisp apple with a handful of almonds. The pair gives you **fibre, healthy fats and vitamin E**, and it keeps in a bag all day.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

name: Hummus with carrot and pepper sticks
about: Creamy hummus with crunchy carrot and sweet red pepper sticks. It brings **chickpea protein and fibre**, with vitamin C from the pepper, and needs no cooking.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut them into sticks and strips. Serve with the hummus for dipping.
tip: Store-bought or homemade both work.

name: Greek yogurt with berries and almonds
about: Thick yogurt with frozen berries that thaw into a berry sauce and a sprinkle of almonds. It brings **protein and calcium**, and the berries bring vitamin C.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the frozen berries. Leave for 5 minutes so they soften, then scatter on the almonds and dust with cinnamon.
tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

name: Spiced roasted chickpeas
about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with smoked paprika and cumin. A salty, crisp snack with **fibre and plant protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Pat the chickpeas very dry so they crisp.
Toss them on a small sheet pan with the oil, paprika, cumin and salt.
Roast for 25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway, until crisp and golden. Cool a few minutes, since they crisp up as they cool.
Eat the same day. Stored in a sealed jar they soften within a day or two.
tip: Roast them on the second shelf while Wednesday's harissa tray or Thursday's fajita tray is in the oven; both run at 220 °C.

name: Orange and walnuts
about: A juicy orange with a small handful of walnuts. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the walnuts bring healthy fats and a little omega-3.
steps: Wash the orange, then peel and segment it. Serve with the walnuts.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A ripe banana with chopped walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. Sweet, soft and crunchy, with **potassium, fibre and a little omega-3**.
steps: Slice the banana into a bowl, scatter over the walnuts and dust with cinnamon.

name: Hard-boiled eggs with cherry tomatoes
about: Two firm hard-boiled eggs with sweet cherry tomatoes, black pepper and a squeeze of lemon. It brings **protein and choline** in a snack that travels well.
steps: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil and boil for 10 minutes, until the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water, then peel.
Wash the tomatoes and halve them. Quarter the eggs, add the tomatoes, squeeze on the lemon and finish with the pepper.
Boiled eggs keep in the fridge in their shells for up to 1 week, so make a few at once.

name: Pear and cardamom oatmeal with walnuts, almonds and chia
about: Creamy oats simmered in milk with diced pear, cardamom and cinnamon, stirred with a spoonful of chia and topped with walnuts and almonds. The oats and pear bring **fibre**, the walnuts and chia bring plant omega-3 and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the pear, then core and dice it.
Put the oats, milk, chia, pear, cinnamon and cardamom in a small pot with a splash of water. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy and the pear is tender, about 6 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl and scatter the walnuts and almonds over the top.
tip: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes for more crunch.

name: Pepper and spinach scrambled eggs on rye toast
about: Eggs scrambled until fully set with sweet red pepper and wilted spinach, piled on toasted rye with an orange on the side. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, the glass of milk brings calcium, and the orange brings vitamin C to help absorb the iron in the spinach.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach and orange. Dice the pepper and cut the orange into wedges.
Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the pepper until just soft, about 3 minutes, then add the spinach and stir until it wilts, about 1 minute.

Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper and pour them into the pan. Stir gently until the eggs are cooked through with no liquid left and the yolk is firm, about 3 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Toast the rye, top it with the eggs and serve with the orange wedges and a glass of milk.

name: Orange yogurt bowl with toasted oats, walnuts and almonds
about: Thick yogurt with juicy orange segments, toasted oats for a granola crunch, walnuts and almonds. The orange brings **vitamin C**, the yogurt brings calcium and the nuts bring plant omega-3 and vitamin E.
steps: Toast the oats, walnuts and almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes. Let them cool.
Wash the orange, then peel it and cut it into segments.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the orange, oats and nuts, and dust with the cinnamon.
ingredients: washed, peeled and cut into segments

name: Chicken and avocado sandwich with hummus and crunchy slaw
about: Poached chicken, creamy avocado and a thin spread of hummus on whole-grain bread with lemony red cabbage and carrot for crunch. The hummus and slaw make it **more than bread and meat**, and the cucumber on the side keeps it fresh.
steps: Poach the chicken: cover it with water in a small pot, bring to a simmer and cook gently until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part and the juices run clear, about 12 minutes. Cool within 1 hour, then slice and refrigerate. You can do this the night before.
Wash the cabbage, carrot, cucumber, spinach and avocado. Toss the cabbage and carrot with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.

Toast the bread if you like and spread the hummus on it. Layer the spinach, chicken, avocado and slaw on half the bread and close with the rest (at the bigger sizes that makes two sandwiches), or leave it open-face if you have only one slice. Serve with the cucumber sticks.
To pack it: wrap the sandwich, put it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Mash the avocado with a little of the lemon juice so it spreads like butter. At smaller sizes the bread shrinks to about one slice, so eat it open-face.

name: Tomato and white bean soup with an open-face cheddar toastie
about: A velvety tomato soup blended with white beans and a handful of spinach, with a hot open-face cheddar toastie on the side. The beans make it filling and bring **fibre and folate**, and the cheese is a garnish, not a layer.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 6 minutes, then add the garlic and basil for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, the white beans and the broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 12 minutes.
Wash the spinach and stir it in until wilted, about 1 minute. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth, then season with the salt and pepper.
Make the toastie: spread the mustard on the bread, scatter over the cheddar and grill under a hot broiler until bubbling and golden, about 3 minutes. Cut into fingers.

Serve the soup with the toastie. This makes two portions: cool the second portion within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat the soup until steaming hot (74 °C) and make the toastie fresh.
tip: Hold back a few whole beans and add them after blending for some texture.
ingredients: no added salt, with the juice

name: Salmon cake burger with lemon-dill slaw
about: A flaky canned salmon patty, bound with egg, oats and mustard and baked until golden, tucked into a whole-wheat bun with a cool, crunchy slaw. Canned salmon with its soft bones brings **omega-3 and calcium**, and the cucumber and spinach keep the plate fresh.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a tray with parchment. Wash the dill, cabbage, carrot, cucumber and spinach.

Mash the salmon in a bowl with the egg, oats, a third of the yogurt, half the mustard, the onion, half the dill, half the lemon juice and the pepper. Let it sit for 5 minutes so the oats soak up the moisture, then shape into a patty and place on the tray. Wash your hands and the bowl with hot soapy water after handling the raw egg. Brush with the oil.
Bake until golden and cooked through, with the egg set firm and the centre at 74 °C (165 °F), about 16 minutes.
Meanwhile, toss the cabbage and carrot with the rest of the yogurt, mustard, dill and lemon juice, and the salt, for a quick slaw.
Toast the bun (at smaller sizes a half bun is plenty), fill it with the spinach, patty and plenty of slaw, and serve with the cucumber slices.
Move any salmon left in the tin to a covered container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
tip: Chill the shaped patty for 10 minutes if you have time, it holds together better.

name: Tuna, chickpea and celery sandwich with lemon yogurt
about: Flaked light tuna and mashed chickpeas with crunchy celery and onion, bound with lemony yogurt and a little mustard instead of mayonnaise. Piled on whole-grain bread with spinach, it brings **protein, fibre and selenium**, with carrot sticks and cherry tomatoes alongside.
steps: Wash the celery, dill, spinach, carrot and tomatoes. Drain the tuna and chickpeas and rinse the chickpeas.
Mash the chickpeas roughly with a fork, leaving some texture. Fold in the tuna, celery, onion, dill, yogurt, lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper.

Toast the bread if you like. Pile the tuna mixture onto half the bread, top with the spinach and close with the rest (at the bigger sizes that makes two sandwiches), or leave it open-face if you have only one slice. Serve with the carrot sticks and cherry tomatoes.
To pack it: wrap the sandwich, put it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day. Move any tuna left in the tin to a covered container in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
tip: Add a pinch of smoked paprika if you like it punchier. At smaller sizes the bread shrinks to about one slice, so eat it open-face.

name: Curried cauliflower and chickpea soup with garlic toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian-style spiced cauliflower soups
about: A golden, lightly curried soup of cauliflower, chickpeas and carrot, finished with spinach and a spoonful of lemony yogurt, with garlic toast for scooping. The chickpeas bring **protein and fibre**, the carrot brings vitamin A and the cauliflower brings vitamin C.
steps: Warm most of the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 6 minutes, then stir in half the garlic, the curry powder, turmeric and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cauliflower, chickpeas and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, until the cauliflower is very tender, about 15 minutes.
Mash some of the soup roughly with a potato masher, or blend a third of it, so it is thick but still chunky. Wash the spinach, stir it in until wilted and season with the salt.
Toast the bread, rub it with the cut side of the remaining garlic clove and brush with the last of the oil. Stir the lemon juice into the yogurt.

Ladle the soup into bowls, swirl in the lemony yogurt, scatter the toasted almonds and dill and serve with the garlic toast. This makes two portions: cool the second within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate and reheat until steaming hot (74 °C). Use within 3 days.
tip: To freeze: leave out the yogurt, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze and reheat to 74 °C.
ingredients: crushed, plus a cut clove for the toast

name: Beef and lentil sloppy joes with crunchy cabbage slaw
inspiredBy: Inspired by the American diner sloppy joe
about: The diner classic with half the beef swapped for lentils, simmered with onion, pepper and carrot in a tangy tomato sauce and piled onto a whole-wheat bun with a lemony cabbage slaw. The lentils stretch the beef and bring **iron and fibre**, and the vegetables are hidden right in the sauce.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, pepper and carrot until soft, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika and cumin and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the beef and break it up with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains, about 5 minutes. Wash your hands, the board and the spoon with hot soapy water after handling the raw beef.

Stir in the tomatoes with their juice, the lentils, the mustard, half the lemon juice and the salt. Simmer, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy, about 12 minutes. The beef must reach 71 °C (160 °F).
Toss the cabbage with the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt for a quick slaw.

Toast the bun (at smaller sizes a half bun is plenty), spoon on the sloppy joe mixture and top with slaw. This makes two portions: cool the second portion within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat it until steaming hot (74 °C) and use a fresh bun.
tip: Serve the filling in a bowl over the slaw if you want to skip the bun at lunch.
ingredients: no added salt, crushed with a spoon

name: Warm trout and white bean smash on rye with cucumber and dill
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian smørrebrød
about: Open-face rye toasts spread with a lemony garlic white bean smash, topped with flaked pan-seared trout, shaved cucumber and dill, with a mustard-lemon drizzle and a little spinach salad. Fresh trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D** and the beans bring fibre.
steps: Wash the cucumber, dill, spinach and tomatoes. Shave the cucumber into ribbons with a peeler.
Mash the white beans with a fork with half the lemon juice, the garlic, half the oil and the pepper until fairly smooth, adding a spoonful of water if it is stiff.

Pat the trout dry and season with the salt. Warm the rest of the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the trout skin-side down for 4 minutes, then flip and cook until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F), about 3 minutes more. Wash your hands, the board and the plate with hot soapy water after handling the raw fish.
Whisk the mustard with the rest of the lemon juice and a teaspoon of water. Flake the warm trout, discarding the skin and any bones.

Toast the rye. Spread each slice with the bean smash and top with the warm trout and cucumber. Drizzle with the mustard-lemon dressing, scatter with the dill and serve with the spinach and cherry tomatoes.
tip: Salmon fillet works too, cooked to the same 70 °C (158 °F). If the trout is frozen, thaw it in the fridge overnight and cook it within 2 days.

name: Egg and cress sandwich with hummus, tomato and carrot sticks
inspiredBy: Inspired by the English egg and cress sandwich
about: The tea-room classic with a lighter touch: chopped hard-boiled eggs with peppery cress, mustard and lemon, a layer of hummus and juicy tomato on whole-grain bread. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, the hummus adds fibre, and the carrot sticks add crunch.
steps: Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and cook for 12 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are completely firm. Cool them in cold water, then peel.

Wash the cress well (if you are pregnant, over 65 or have a weakened immune system, use watercress or baby spinach instead of the cress), and wash the tomatoes, carrot and cucumber. Chop the eggs and mix with the cress, mustard, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Spread the hummus on the bread, top with the tomato and the egg mixture, and close the sandwich, or leave it open-face if you have only one slice. Serve with the carrot and cucumber sticks.
To pack it: put the sandwich in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
ingredients: whole eggs, hard-boiled until the yolk is firm

name: Split pea and carrot soup with dill, yogurt and rye toast
about: A thick, comforting soup of yellow split peas, carrot, celery and thyme, with a spoonful of yogurt, dill and toasted walnuts and rye toast alongside. Split peas are one of the best **fibre and protein** foods in the pantry, and this pot needs nothing but time.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery until the onion is soft, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic, thyme and bay leaf for 30 seconds.

Add the split peas and the broth with a cup of water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered and stirring now and then, until the peas have broken down and the soup is thick, about 40 minutes. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Remove the bay leaf. Wash the spinach and stir it in until wilted. Blend about a third of the soup for a creamier body, then season with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Toast the rye. Ladle the soup into bowls, top with the yogurt, dill and walnuts, and serve with the toast.
This makes two portions: cool the second within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat it until steaming hot (74 °C), adding a splash of water.
tip: To freeze: leave out the yogurt, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze and reheat to 74 °C. A pressure cooker does the peas in 15 minutes.

name: Turkey and carrot meatball sub with spinach and tomato sauce
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Italian-American meatball sub
about: Tender turkey meatballs with grated carrot and oats, simmered in a quick garlicky tomato sauce and tucked into a whole-wheat bun with spinach and a little cheddar. The carrot keeps the meatballs juicy, and the spinach stirred into the sauce adds **folate and iron**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). In a bowl, mix the turkey, carrot, oats, half the onion, half the garlic, half the oregano, a pinch of the salt and the pepper. Shape into small meatballs. Wash your hands, the bowl and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw turkey.
Bake the meatballs on a lined tray until browned and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, warm the oil in a pan over medium heat and soften the rest of the onion, about 4 minutes. Add the rest of the garlic and oregano, then the tomatoes with their juice and the rest of the salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, crushing the tomatoes. Wash two thirds of the spinach and stir it in until wilted.
Add the cooked meatballs to the sauce and simmer for 3 minutes.
Split and toast the bun, fill with the rest of the spinach, the meatballs and sauce, and finish with the cheddar. Serve with the cucumber and cherry tomatoes.
ingredients: no added salt, crushed with a spoon
washed, halved, as a side salad

name: Apple with walnuts
about: A crisp apple with a few walnut halves. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the walnuts.

name: Pear with walnuts
about: A ripe pear with a few walnut halves. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3**, and the pear brings fibre.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it and serve with the walnuts.

name: Apple with almonds
about: A crisp apple with a small handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

name: Orange with almonds
about: A juicy orange with a handful of almonds. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash and peel the orange and serve in segments with the almonds.

name: Hummus with carrot and pepper sticks
about: Creamy hummus with crunchy carrot and red pepper sticks. The hummus brings **plant protein and fibre**, and the pepper brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the carrot and pepper, cut them into sticks and serve with the hummus.

name: Yogurt with pear and almonds
about: Cool Greek yogurt with diced pear, a few chopped almonds and a pinch of cinnamon. It brings **calcium and protein**, and the almonds add vitamin E.
steps: Wash and dice the pear, spoon it over the yogurt and top with the almonds and cinnamon.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and cumin
about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with lemon, a pinch of cumin and salt. It brings **protein, folate and fibre**.
steps: Cook the frozen edamame in boiling water or in the microwave until steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the lemon juice, cumin and salt.

name: Tuna and cucumber on rye toast
about: Flaked light tuna with lemon and dill on a small slice of rye with cucumber. It brings **lean protein and selenium** and uses up an opened tin.
steps: Wash the cucumber and dill. Toast the rye.
Mash the tuna with the lemon juice, dill and pepper, pile onto the toast and top with the cucumber.
Use tuna from a tin opened within the last 2 days and kept in a covered container in the fridge.

name: Warm edamame with lemon and chili
about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with lemon, a pinch of chili flakes and salt. It brings **protein, folate and fibre**.
steps: Cook the frozen edamame in boiling water or in the microwave until steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the lemon juice, chili flakes and salt.

name: Pepper and spinach scrambled eggs on rye toast
about: Eggs scrambled until fully set with sweet red pepper and wilted spinach, piled on toasted rye with an orange on the side. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, the glass of milk brings calcium, and the orange brings vitamin C to help absorb the iron in the spinach.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach and orange. Dice the pepper and cut the orange into wedges.
Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the pepper until just soft, about 3 minutes, then add the spinach and stir until it wilts, about 1 minute.

Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper and pour them into the pan. Stir gently until the eggs are cooked through with no liquid left and the yolk is firm, about 3 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Toast the rye, top it with the eggs and serve with the orange wedges and a glass of milk.

name: Tomato and white bean soup with an open-face cheddar toastie
about: A velvety tomato soup blended with white beans and a handful of spinach, with a hot open-face cheddar toastie on the side. The beans make it filling and bring **fibre and folate**, and the cheese is a garnish, not a layer.
steps: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 6 minutes, then add the garlic and basil for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, the white beans and the broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 12 minutes.
Wash the spinach and stir it in until wilted, about 1 minute. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth, then season with the salt and pepper.
Make the toastie: spread the mustard on the bread, scatter over the cheddar and grill under a hot broiler until bubbling and golden, about 3 minutes. Cut into fingers.

Serve the soup with the toastie. This makes two portions: cool the second portion within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat the soup until steaming hot (74 °C) and make the toastie fresh.
tip: Hold back a few whole beans and add them after blending for some texture.
ingredients: no added salt, with the juice

name: Curried cauliflower and chickpea soup with garlic toast
inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian-style spiced cauliflower soups
about: A golden, lightly curried soup of cauliflower, chickpeas and carrot, finished with spinach and a spoonful of lemony yogurt, with garlic toast for scooping. The chickpeas bring **protein and fibre**, the carrot brings vitamin A and the cauliflower brings vitamin C.
steps: Warm most of the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 6 minutes, then stir in half the garlic, the curry powder, turmeric and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cauliflower, chickpeas and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, until the cauliflower is very tender, about 15 minutes.
Mash some of the soup roughly with a potato masher, or blend a third of it, so it is thick but still chunky. Wash the spinach, stir it in until wilted and season with the salt.
Toast the bread, rub it with the cut side of the remaining garlic clove and brush with the last of the oil. Stir the lemon juice into the yogurt.

Ladle the soup into bowls, swirl in the lemony yogurt, scatter the toasted almonds and dill and serve with the garlic toast. This makes two portions: cool the second within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate and reheat until steaming hot (74 °C). Use within 3 days.
tip: To freeze: leave out the yogurt, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze and reheat to 74 °C.
ingredients: crushed, plus a cut clove for the toast

name: Split pea and carrot soup with dill, yogurt and rye toast
about: A thick, comforting soup of yellow split peas, carrot, celery and thyme, with a spoonful of yogurt, dill and toasted walnuts and rye toast alongside. Split peas are one of the best **fibre and protein** foods in the pantry, and this pot needs nothing but time.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery until the onion is soft, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic, thyme and bay leaf for 30 seconds.

Add the split peas and the broth with a cup of water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered and stirring now and then, until the peas have broken down and the soup is thick, about 40 minutes. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Remove the bay leaf. Wash the spinach and stir it in until wilted. Blend about a third of the soup for a creamier body, then season with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Toast the rye. Ladle the soup into bowls, top with the yogurt, dill and walnuts, and serve with the toast.
This makes two portions: cool the second within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat it until steaming hot (74 °C), adding a splash of water.
tip: To freeze: leave out the yogurt, cool within 2 hours, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze and reheat to 74 °C. A pressure cooker does the peas in 15 minutes.

name: Beef and lentil sloppy joes with crunchy cabbage slaw
inspiredBy: Inspired by the American diner sloppy joe
about: The diner classic with half the beef swapped for lentils, simmered with onion, pepper and carrot in a tangy tomato sauce and piled onto a whole-wheat bun with a lemony cabbage slaw. The lentils stretch the beef and bring **iron and fibre**, and the vegetables are hidden right in the sauce.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, pepper and carrot until soft, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika and cumin and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the beef and break it up with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains, about 5 minutes. Wash your hands, the board and the spoon with hot soapy water after handling the raw beef.

Stir in the tomatoes with their juice, the lentils, the mustard, half the lemon juice and the salt. Simmer, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy, about 12 minutes. The beef must reach 71 °C (160 °F).
Toss the cabbage with the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt for a quick slaw.

Toast the bun (at smaller sizes a half bun is plenty), spoon on the sloppy joe mixture and top with slaw. This makes two portions: cool the second portion within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate and use within 3 days. Reheat it until steaming hot (74 °C) and use a fresh bun.
tip: Serve the filling in a bowl over the slaw if you want to skip the bun at lunch.
ingredients: no added salt, crushed with a spoon

name: Salmon cake with lemon-dill slaw
about: A flaky canned salmon cake, bound with egg, oats and mustard and baked until golden, piled on a cool, crunchy slaw with spinach and cucumber. Canned salmon with its soft bones brings **omega-3 and calcium**, and the slaw keeps the plate fresh.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and line a tray with parchment. Wash the dill, cabbage, carrot, cucumber and spinach.

Mash the salmon in a bowl with the egg, oats, a third of the yogurt, half the mustard, the onion, half the dill, half the lemon juice and the pepper. Let it sit for 5 minutes so the oats soak up the moisture, then shape into a patty and place on the tray. Wash your hands and the bowl with hot soapy water after handling the raw egg.
