name: Beef and egg lo mein with bok choy, carrot and edamame
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American lo mein, with whole-wheat spaghetti as the noodles
about: Chewy whole-wheat spaghetti, used as the noodles, tossed in a hot wok with strips of lean beef, firm egg ribbons, bok choy, carrot, garlic and a savoury soy and vinegar sauce. The beef, egg and edamame bring **protein, iron and choline**, and a big pile of bok choy and carrot keeps the noodle portion modest.
steps: Boil the whole-wheat spaghetti (the noodles) in plenty of water until just tender, about 10 minutes, adding the frozen edamame for the last 3 minutes so it is steaming hot all the way through. Drain and toss with half of the sesame oil so they do not stick.
Wash the bok choy, spinach, carrot and scallion. Slice the bok choy and scallion and cut the carrot into thin matchsticks. Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar and chili flakes in a small bowl.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.
Pour in the beaten egg and stir until completely set and firm, about 1 minute, then move it to a plate and break it into ribbons.

Add the beef in a single layer and stir-fry until browned and cooked through, with no pink and at least 71 °C (160 °F), about 3 minutes. Move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw beef.
Add the carrot and garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute, then the bok choy and scallion for 2 minutes, until the stems are tender but still have a little crunch, and stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Return the beef and egg, add the noodles and the sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the noodles are steaming hot. Drizzle with the rest of the sesame oil, scatter over the sesame seeds and serve.
tip: Packing it for work? Cook it the night before, cool it within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep it cold with an ice pack and reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
ingredients: whole-wheat spaghetti, used as the noodles
washed and cut into thin matchsticks

name: Kung pao-style tofu and chickpeas with green beans and carrot over brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Sichuan kung pao, with tofu and chickpeas in place of the chicken
about: Golden tofu, hearty chickpeas, crisp-tender green beans, carrot and spinach in a tangy, lightly sweet and chili-spiked sauce, finished with toasted cashews and scallion, over brown rice. The tofu and chickpeas bring **plant protein, iron and calcium**, and the brown rice keeps the portion modest.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.

Meanwhile, wash the vegetables. Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, chili flakes and 3 tablespoons of water together in a small bowl. Toast the cashews in a dry wok or skillet over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes, then tip onto a plate.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.
Add the tofu and fry, turning, until golden on most sides, about 5 minutes. Move it to a plate.

Add a little more oil if the pan is dry, then add the green beans and carrot and stir-fry until blistered in places and crisp-tender, about 6 minutes, adding a splash of water if they start to stick. Add the garlic and scallion and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

Add the chickpeas, tofu and spinach, then stir the sauce and pour it in. Bubble, stirring, until the spinach wilts and the sauce is reduced and glossy, about 3 minutes, and everything is steaming hot.
Spoon over the rice and scatter with the cashews and sesame seeds.
ingredients: extra-firm, patted dry and cut into small cubes
washed, trimmed and cut in thirds
washed and sliced into thin coins

name: Egg and edamame fried brown rice with carrot and kale
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese vegetable fried rice
about: Brown rice stir-fried hot with firm-scrambled egg, edamame, carrot, kale, spinach and garlic, finished with soy and a little sesame oil. The egg and edamame bring **protein, choline and folate**, and the brown rice stays a modest portion.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.
Spread the drained rice on a tray in a thin layer and let it steam dry for 10 minutes. Wash the carrot, kale, spinach and scallion, dice the carrot and slice the kale and scallion.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.
Pour the beaten egg into the hot wok and stir until completely set and firm, about 1 minute, then move it to a plate.

Add the carrot, garlic, ginger and the white part of the scallion and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the frozen edamame straight from the freezer and stir-fry until steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes.
Add the rice and the egg and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, pressing it against the pan, until it is steaming hot and a little toasty.
Add the kale, spinach, soy sauce and chili flakes and toss until the greens wilt, about 2 minutes. Drizzle with the sesame oil and scatter over the rest of the scallion and the sesame seeds.
tip: Best with rice cooked and chilled the night before: cook a little extra with Friday dinner, cool it within 1 hour in a shallow container, and fry it straight from the fridge (use within 3 days) for a quick lunch.

inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese vegetable fried rice

name: Chicken and cashew stir-fry with red pepper, carrot and spinach over brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American cashew chicken
about: Tender chicken, toasted cashews, red pepper, carrot and spinach in a savoury garlic-ginger sauce, spooned over brown rice. The cashews bring **magnesium, zinc and copper**, and the carrot and red pepper bring **vitamin A and C**.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.
Meanwhile, stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar and broth together in a bowl. Toast the cashews in a dry wok or skillet over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes, then tip onto a plate.
Wash the red pepper, carrot, spinach and scallion, then cut them as described in the list. Pat the chicken dry.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.

Add the chicken in a single layer (in two batches if your pan is smaller than 30 cm, so it browns and does not steam) and let it sear for 1 minute, then stir-fry until golden and cooked through, with no pink inside and 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 5 minutes a batch. Move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.
Add the carrot and a splash of water and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then the red pepper, garlic, ginger and scallion for 2 minutes, until crisp-tender.

Return the chicken and add the spinach, then stir the sauce and pour it in. Bubble, stirring, until the spinach wilts and the sauce has bubbled down to a few spoonfuls that coat everything, about 2 minutes. Toss in half of the cashews and the sesame seeds.

Spoon over the rice. Cool the second portion of rice and stir-fry within 1 hour by spreading it in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot all the way through, 74 °C (165 °F). If you take it to work, pack it cold with an ice pack.
tip: Keep the other half of the cashews in a jar and stir them into the second portion when you reheat it, so they stay crunchy.
ingredients: washed and sliced into thin coins

Wash the red pepper, carrot, spinach and scallion, then cut them as described in the list. Pat the chicken dry.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.

Add the chicken in a single layer (in two batches if your pan is smaller than 30 cm, so it browns and does not steam) and let it sear for 1 minute, then stir-fry until golden and cooked through, with no pink inside and 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, about 5 minutes a batch. Move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.
Add the carrot and a splash of water and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then the red pepper, garlic, ginger and scallion for 2 minutes, until crisp-tender.

Return the chicken and add the spinach, then stir the sauce and pour it in. Bubble, stirring, until the spinach wilts and the sauce has bubbled down to a few spoonfuls that coat everything, about 2 minutes. Toss in half of the cashews and the sesame seeds.

Spoon over the rice. Cool the second portion of rice and stir-fry within 1 hour by spreading it in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot all the way through, 74 °C (165 °F). If you take it to work, pack it cold with an ice pack.
tip: Keep the other half of the cashews in a jar and stir them into the second portion when you reheat it, so they stay crunchy.

name: Orange-garlic salmon with stir-fried bok choy, kale and carrot over brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese orange-flavoured fish and greens, pan-seared at home
about: A seared salmon fillet glazed with fresh orange juice, garlic and black pepper, over brown rice with bok choy, kale and carrot stir-fried in garlic. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the greens, carrot and orange bring calcium, vitamin K, vitamin A and vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.

Stir the orange juice, soy sauce, rice vinegar, black pepper and half of the garlic together in a small bowl. Wash the bok choy, kale and carrot, then cut the bok choy into chunks, tear the kale and cut the carrot into thin ribbons or coins. Pat the salmon dry.

Warm half of the canola oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Lay in the salmon skin-side down and cook for 4 minutes until the skin is crisp, then flip and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily and the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F).

Pour the orange mixture into the pan for the last minute, turning the salmon once, until it bubbles down into a sticky glaze. Lift the salmon onto a clean plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish.

Wipe out the pan and heat the rest of the oil over high heat until it shimmers. Stir-fry the carrot for 3 minutes, then add the kale, bok choy and the rest of the garlic and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until the kale has wilted and the stems are crisp-tender.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the greens alongside. Drizzle with the sesame oil and scatter over the sesame seeds.

name: Black pepper beef and broccoli with kale and bok choy over brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese-American beef and broccoli, with a garlicky black pepper sauce
about: Thin slices of lean sirloin, bright broccoli, kale and bok choy in a savoury, garlicky black pepper sauce, over brown rice. The beef and greens bring **iron, zinc and vitamin C** together, so the iron absorbs well, and the kale and bok choy add calcium.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.

Stir the cornstarch into the cold broth until smooth, then stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar and black pepper. Wash the broccoli, kale, bok choy and scallion, then cut them as described in the list.

Pat the beef dry. Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, add half of the oil and swirl until it shimmers, then sear the beef in a single layer (in two batches if your pan is smaller than 30 cm, so it browns and does not steam) for 2 minutes a batch, stirring, until browned and cooked through with no pink and at least 71 °C (160 °F). Move it to a clean plate. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw beef.

Add the rest of the oil, then the scallion and stir-fry until softened and lightly browned, about 2 minutes. Add the broccoli, garlic and a splash of water, cover for 1 minute, then add the kale and bok choy and stir-fry until the broccoli is bright green and crisp-tender and the greens have wilted, about 3 minutes.
Return the beef to the pan, stir the sauce again and pour it in. Bubble for 1 minute, stirring, until glossy. Stir in the sesame oil and scatter over the sesame seeds.

Spoon over the rice. Cool the second portion of rice and stir-fry within 1 hour by spreading it in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot all the way through, 74 °C (165 °F). If you take it to work, pack it cold with an ice pack.

name: Garlic shrimp and snow peas with carrot and bok choy over whole-wheat noodles
inspiredBy: Inspired by Cantonese shrimp with snow peas in a light white garlic sauce
about: Plump shrimp, crisp snow peas, sweet carrot and bok choy in a light, glossy garlic-ginger sauce over whole-wheat spaghetti, used as the noodles. The shrimp bring **lean protein, iodine and selenium**, and the snow peas bring vitamin C.
steps: Boil the whole-wheat spaghetti (the noodles) in plenty of water until just tender, about 10 minutes, then drain and toss with the sesame oil.

Meanwhile, stir the cornstarch into the cold broth until smooth, then stir in the soy sauce. Wash the snow peas, carrot, bok choy and scallion, then cut them as described in the list. Pat the shrimp dry.
Heat a wok or large heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once, then add the oil and swirl it until it shimmers.
Stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes, then add the bok choy and snow peas for 2 minutes. Push the vegetables to the side.

Add the shrimp, garlic and ginger and stir-fry until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through (70 °C / 158 °F), about 3 minutes. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw shrimp.
Stir the sauce again, pour it in and bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until it thickens, turns glossy and coats the shrimp. Fold in the scallion.
Spoon over the noodles, scatter over the sesame seeds and serve straight away.
tip: Shrimp turn rubbery when they sit, so this one is best eaten the day it is cooked.
ingredients: whole-wheat spaghetti, used as the noodles
peeled, deveined, thawed in the fridge if frozen
washed and sliced thinly on the diagonal

name: Garlic-chili tofu with kale, bok choy and carrot over brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Sichuan-style home-cooked tofu with greens
about: Golden pan-crisped tofu and a big pile of kale, bok choy and carrot in a garlicky, lightly spicy sauce, over brown rice. The tofu brings **plant protein, calcium and iron**, and the greens and carrot bring vitamin K, folate and vitamin A.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.

Press the tofu between clean towels for 10 minutes, then cut it into cubes. Stir the cornstarch into 4 tablespoons of cold water until smooth, then stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey and chili flakes.
Wash the kale, bok choy, carrot and scallion, then tear the kale, slice the bok choy and scallion and cut the carrot into thin coins.

Warm half of the oil in a nonstick wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning, until golden and crisp on most sides, about 8 minutes, in two batches if your pan is smaller than 30 cm, so it browns and does not steam. Move it to a plate.

Add the rest of the oil, then the garlic, ginger and scallion and stir for 20 seconds. Add the carrot and kale with a splash of water and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add the bok choy and stir-fry 2 minutes more, until tender with a little crunch.
Return the tofu, stir the sauce again and pour it in. Bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until glossy, clinging to the tofu and hot all the way through. Stir in the sesame oil.

Spoon over the rice. Cool the second portion of rice and stir-fry within 1 hour by spreading it in a shallow container, then refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot all the way through, 74 °C (165 °F). If you take it to work, pack it cold with an ice pack.
tip: The tofu softens as it sits. Give the second portion 2 minutes in a hot skillet to bring back some crispness.
ingredients: extra-firm, patted dry and cut into cubes
washed and sliced into thin coins

name: Sesame-crusted salmon with garlicky green beans over brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by Japanese sesame-crusted fish and garlicky green beans
about: A pan-seared salmon fillet pressed with toasted sesame seeds, served with blistered garlic-ginger green beans in a splash of soy and rice vinegar, over brown rice. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the green beans add fibre and vitamin K.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in plenty of water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew, 25 to 30 minutes, then drain well and fluff it.
Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar and half of the ginger together in a small bowl. Wash the green beans and trim them. Pat the salmon dry and press the sesame seeds onto the flesh side.

Warm half of the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Lay in the salmon seed-side down and cook for 3 minutes until the seeds are golden and toasty, then flip and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until opaque and flaking and the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Lift the salmon onto a clean plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish.

Wipe the pan, add the rest of the oil and heat over high heat until it shimmers. Stir-fry the green beans until blistered in places and crisp-tender, 5 to 6 minutes, adding the garlic and the rest of the ginger for the last minute and a splash of water to steam them through, then pour in the soy mixture for the last 30 seconds.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the green beans and drizzle with the sesame oil.
ingredients: skin-on fillet, fresh and used within a day of buying

name: Apple with almonds

name: Pear with walnuts
about: A juicy pear with a small handful of walnuts. The walnuts bring **omega-3 fats and fibre**, and the pear brings sweetness and more fibre.

name: Carrot and red pepper sticks with ginger-soy yogurt dip
about: Crunchy carrot and red pepper sticks with a quick Greek yogurt dip spiked with ginger and a little soy. The carrot brings **vitamin A**, the pepper vitamin C, and the yogurt protein and calcium.
steps: Stir the yogurt, grated ginger, soy sauce and rice vinegar together in a small bowl.
Wash the carrot and red pepper, cut them into sticks and dip. Keep the dip in the fridge and finish it the same day.

name: Warm edamame with garlic and chili
about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with garlic, a little soy and chili flakes. The edamame brings **protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Heat the edamame in a pan with a splash of water, stirring, until steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the garlic, soy sauce, rice vinegar and chili flakes and eat warm.

name: Warm edamame with sesame and ginger
about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with toasted sesame seeds, fresh ginger and a splash of soy. The edamame brings **protein, folate and iron**, and the sesame adds crunch.
steps: Heat the edamame in a pan with a splash of water, stirring, until steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the grated ginger, soy sauce and sesame seeds and eat warm.

name: Warm edamame with sesame and ginger
about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with toasted sesame seeds, fresh ginger and a splash of soy. The edamame brings **protein, folate and iron**, and the sesame adds crunch.

name: Roasted chili-sesame chickpeas
about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with sesame seeds, a pinch of chili and a little soy. The chickpeas bring **protein, fibre and iron**, and the sesame adds crunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Toss the very dry chickpeas with the oil, soy sauce, sesame seeds and chili flakes on a small baking tray.
Roast, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp, about 25 minutes. Cool for 5 minutes and eat the same day.

name: Pear with pumpkin seeds
about: A juicy pear with a small handful of pumpkin seeds. The seeds bring **iron, magnesium and zinc**, and the pear brings fibre.
steps: Wash the pear, slice it and serve with the pumpkin seeds.

name: Orange with walnuts
about: A sweet orange and a small handful of walnuts. The orange brings **vitamin C**, and the walnuts bring omega-3 fats.
steps: Wash the orange, peel it and cut it into segments, then serve with the walnuts.

name: Firm-boiled egg with soy-ginger dip and red pepper strips
about: A firm-boiled egg with crunchy red pepper strips and a little soy and ginger to dip. The egg brings **protein and choline**, and the red pepper brings vitamin C.
steps: Lower the egg into a small pot of boiling water and cook for 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it under cold running water and peel it.
Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar and grated ginger together for the dip. Wash the red pepper, cut it into strips and serve with the egg.

name: Pineapple and pear with fresh ginger
about: Juicy pineapple and pear tossed with a little grated fresh ginger, a bright, sweet snack with no cooking. It brings **vitamin C and fibre**.
steps: Wash the pear and the pineapple before cutting. Peel, core and cut the pineapple into chunks and slice the pear.
Toss with the grated ginger and eat right away, or pack it in a lidded tub in the fridge and eat it the same day.

name: Blueberry and cherry overnight oats with walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by Swiss bircher muesli, with summer fruit
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt, then topped with blueberries, sweet cherries and crunchy walnuts. A cool, creamy breakfast with **fibre, protein and calcium**, and nothing to cook.
steps: The night before, stir the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon together in a jar or bowl. Cover and keep it in the fridge overnight.
In the morning, wash the blueberries and cherries, then pit and halve the cherries.
Stir the oats, loosening them with a splash of milk or water if they are thick, then top with the blueberries, cherries and walnuts.
Soaked oats keep up to 3 days covered in the fridge, so mix a fresh jar every night or two rather than a whole week at once.
tip: Use frozen cherries or blueberries thawed in the fridge when fresh ones are out of season.

name: Peach yogurt bowl with walnut oat crunch and mint
inspiredBy: Inspired by a fruit and yogurt breakfast plate
about: Thick Greek yogurt with ripe diced peach, fresh mint and a crunch of toasted oats and walnuts. It brings **protein, calcium and plant omega-3**, and it is cold, quick and refreshing.
steps: Toast the oats and walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden and fragrant. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Wash the peach, cut it away from the pit and dice it.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the peach and drizzle with the honey.
Scatter with the toasted oats and walnuts and the torn mint.
tip: Toast a few days of oats and walnuts at once and keep them in a jar.

name: Arugula, tomato and basil scramble with warm potatoes
inspiredBy: Inspired by a summer vegetable frittata
about: Eggs scrambled until firm with arugula, cherry tomatoes and basil, served over diced potato crisped in the same pan. The eggs bring **choline and protein**, the arugula adds calcium and vitamin K, and the potato brings potassium.
steps: Cook the potato cubes in a microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water, covered, for 4 to 5 minutes until tender when poked with a fork, or simmer them for 8 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes and cook for 4 minutes, turning, until golden at the edges.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes until they start to soften. Wash the arugula, stir it in and let it wilt for 30 seconds.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper and pour them over the vegetables. Cook, stirring and folding, for 3 to 4 minutes until the eggs are completely firm with no runny parts.
Tear the basil over the top and serve.
tip: Boil extra potatoes the night before and breakfast is 10 minutes.

name: Watermelon, feta and mint salad with lemon shrimp and chickpeas
inspiredBy: Inspired by the Greek summer pairing of watermelon and feta
about: Cold, juicy watermelon, salty feta and mint over baby spinach, topped with quick lemon shrimp, chickpeas and almonds. The shrimp and chickpeas make it a meal, with **protein, iodine and fibre**.
steps: Scrub the watermelon rind under running water, then cut away the rind and cube the flesh. Wash the spinach, cucumber and mint.

If the shrimp are frozen, thaw them overnight in the fridge. Pat the shrimp dry. Heat half the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes a side, with half the lemon juice and a pinch of the salt, until pink and opaque and firm to the touch, 70 °C (158 °F) in the centre. Tip them onto a clean plate and wash your hands and the board after handling the raw shrimp.
Whisk the rest of the lemon juice and oil with the pepper and a pinch of salt for the dressing, and toss it with the chickpeas, onion, cucumber and spinach.
Pile the greens onto a plate, top with the watermelon, shrimp and crumbled feta, then scatter with the mint and almonds.

Serve right away while the shrimp are still slightly warm and the melon is cold. If you are packing it, chill the shrimp first, keep the watermelon and dressing separate, and carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack to eat the same day.
tip: No time to cook shrimp? Use a drained tin of salmon, and eat it all that day.
ingredients: rind scrubbed and rinsed first, then cubed

name: Niçoise salad with tuna, new potatoes, green beans and firm eggs
inspiredBy: Inspired by the salade niçoise of Nice, with canned light tuna and no anchovies
about: The classic main-course salad: canned light tuna, tender potatoes, crisp green beans, tomatoes, olives and a firm-cooked egg on baby spinach, with a lemon and Dijon dressing. It brings **protein, selenium and vitamin K**, and the second portion is tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Put the potatoes and eggs (in the shell) in a pot, cover with cold water by about 3 cm (1 inch) and bring to a boil. Simmer for 8 minutes, then add the green beans and simmer for 4 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender when poked with a fork. Lift the eggs out into cold water and drain the potatoes and beans.
Peel tonight's eggs once they are cool enough to handle; the yolks should be completely firm. Keep the eggs for the second portion in their shell in the fridge for tomorrow.
Whisk the onion, Dijon, lemon juice, oil and pepper for the dressing. Toss the warm potatoes and green beans with half of it so they soak up the flavour.
Wash the spinach, tomatoes and basil. Arrange the spinach on a plate, then the potatoes, beans, tomatoes, tuna, olives and quartered egg. Spoon over a little more dressing and top with the basil.

Open tins of fish should be used the same day, so use all the tuna now. Spread the second portion of potatoes, beans and tuna in a shallow container, cool within 1 hour, then cover and refrigerate with the tomatoes. Keep the dressing, spinach and egg separate. Assemble it tomorrow and eat it cold.
If you pack tomorrow's lunch, carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Keep the dressing separate and add it when you eat tomorrow's portion so the beans stay bright green.
ingredients: small waxy potatoes, scrubbed, halved or quartered

name: Chicken, peach and quinoa salad with arugula, basil and almonds
inspiredBy: Inspired by summer peach and chicken salads
about: Seared chicken slices over fluffy quinoa with ripe peach, peppery arugula, basil, cucumber, crunchy almonds and a little feta. Quinoa and chicken bring **protein and magnesium**, and the second portion makes a cold lunch tomorrow.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Spread it in a shallow container and cool within 1 hour.
Meanwhile, slice the chicken breast in half horizontally so the pieces are even, and season them with a pinch of the salt and the pepper.

Heat half the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes a side, until golden and a thermometer reads 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part. Rest it on a clean plate, then wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw chicken. Slice the chicken.

Wash the arugula, cucumber and basil. Whisk the lemon juice, honey, the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt for the dressing. Toss half the cooled quinoa with half the dressing, and keep the second portion of quinoa undressed in the fridge.
Wash one peach and slice it. Toss the dressed quinoa with half the arugula, cucumber, onion and basil, then top with half the chicken, the sliced peach and half the almonds and feta.

Cool the rest of the chicken within 1 hour and keep it and the quinoa in separate covered shallow containers in the fridge, with the rest of the arugula, cucumber, onion, basil and dressing kept apart. Tomorrow, slice the second peach, toss everything together just before eating and eat it cold, packed in a cold bag with an ice pack if you take it out.
tip: No peaches? Cherries or a sliced nectarine work well.

name: Cumin-lime salmon with black bean, charred corn and avocado salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex corn and black bean salads
about: A seared salmon fillet over a bright salad of black beans, charred corn, red pepper, tomatoes, avocado and feta with lime and cilantro. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, the beans bring fibre and folate, and the second portion makes a cold lunch tomorrow.
steps: Heat a dry non-stick or cast-iron pan over high heat. Add the frozen corn and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking now and then, until steaming hot and charred in spots. Tip it into a bowl.
Wash the pepper, tomatoes, arugula, cilantro and avocado. Add the beans, pepper, tomatoes, onion, cilantro and half the lime juice to the corn with a pinch of the salt and half the oil, and toss.
Mix the cumin, chili powder and the rest of the salt and rub it over the salmon. Heat the remaining oil in the same pan over medium-high heat.

Lay both fillets skin-side down in the pan (in two batches if it is small), then wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw salmon. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the skin is crisp, then turn and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily. Squeeze the last of the lime juice over them.
Spread half the arugula on a plate, spoon over half the bean and corn salad, add tonight's avocado and feta and set one fillet on top.

Cool the second fillet within 1 hour, flake it off its skin, and keep it, the rest of the bean and corn salad and the rest of the arugula in separate shallow containers in the fridge. Eat it cold the next day, with freshly cut avocado and the rest of the feta. Cook the salmon the day you buy it, or thaw frozen fillets overnight in the fridge. Pack tomorrow's lunch in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Pat the skin dry for a crisper finish.

name: Thai-style beef salad with quinoa, cucumber and herbs
inspiredBy: Inspired by Thai yam nua, with quinoa to make it a full meal
about: Thin-sliced seared sirloin tossed with arugula, cucumber, tomatoes, mint, cilantro and a hot, sour, savoury lime dressing, over quinoa with crunchy peanuts. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, with vitamin C from the lime and tomatoes to help absorb the iron.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Spread it in a shallow container and cool within 1 hour.

Pat the steak dry and season it with a little pepper. Heat a pan over high heat and cook the steak for 4 to 5 minutes a side, until browned and seared to 71 °C (160 °F) with no pink in the centre. Rest it on a clean plate for 3 minutes, then wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw beef.
Whisk the lime juice, soy sauce, honey, garlic and chili flakes for the dressing. Toast the peanuts in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, then chop them roughly.

Slice the steak thinly across the grain. Wash the arugula, cucumber, tomatoes and herbs. Toss half the cooled quinoa with half the arugula, cucumber, tomatoes, onion and herbs and half the dressing, and keep the rest undressed for tomorrow.
Pile the quinoa salad onto a plate, top with half the beef, spoon over a little more of the dressing, keeping the rest for tomorrow, and scatter with half the peanuts.

Chill the second portion of beef, the quinoa, the cut vegetables and herbs and the rest of the dressing in separate covered containers within 1 hour. Toss them together just before eating tomorrow, packed in a cold bag with an ice pack if you take it out, and finish it within 3 days.
tip: Dial the heat down by leaving out the chili flakes, and put them on the table instead.

name: Lentil and sweet potato salad with arugula, egg, feta and lemon
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine and Mediterranean lentil salads, with sweet potato
about: Tender lentils and sweet potato cubes tossed while warm with cumin, lemon, red onion and arugula, topped with a firm-cooked egg, salty feta and almonds. The lentils bring **iron, folate and fibre**, the sweet potato brings vitamin A, and the lemon helps your body absorb the iron.
steps: Put the eggs (in the shell) in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes, then cool them in cold water; the yolks should be completely firm. Meanwhile, simmer the sweet potato cubes in a separate pot of water for 8 to 10 minutes until tender when poked with a fork. Drain and let them steam dry for a minute.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, cumin, salt and pepper in a large bowl. Add the warm sweet potato, the lentils and the onion and toss gently so the sweet potato stays in pieces.
Wash the arugula and mint. Spoon tomorrow's portion of lentils and sweet potato into a shallow container, then fold half the arugula into tonight's.

Peel tonight's eggs and quarter them. Spoon tonight's salad onto a plate, top with the egg, crumble over half the feta and scatter with half the almonds and mint. Keep the second portion's eggs in their shell in the fridge.

Cool tomorrow's portion within 1 hour, cover it and keep it in the fridge. Eat it cold tomorrow, with the rest of the arugula, feta, almonds and mint and the peeled, quartered egg added just before. Pack it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Use a drained, rinsed tin of lentils, or cook your own from dry and cool them in a shallow container. Lentils left in the tin keep 2 days, covered, in the fridge.

name: Curried chicken and chickpea salad with apple, spinach and yogurt dressing
inspiredBy: Inspired by British coronation chicken, with yogurt, apple and chickpeas
about: Seared chicken tossed in a mild curry-yogurt dressing with crisp apple, cucumber and chickpeas, piled over baby spinach with fresh cilantro. The chicken and chickpeas bring **protein and fibre**, and the spinach and lemon add vitamin K and vitamin C.
steps: Cut the chicken breast in half horizontally so the pieces are even and season with the salt and half the curry powder. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes a side, until golden and a thermometer reads 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part. Rest it on a clean plate, then wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw chicken.
Cool the chicken for 10 minutes, then dice it. Meanwhile, stir the yogurt with the rest of the curry powder, the lemon juice and a spoonful of cold water to make the dressing.
Wash the spinach, cucumber and cilantro. Toss the diced chicken, chickpeas and onion with most of the dressing and chill for 10 minutes if you have time.

Wash the apple, then dice half of it and half the cucumber. Spread half the spinach on a plate, spoon over half the curried chicken salad with the apple and cucumber, drizzle with a little of the remaining dressing and top with half the cilantro.

Cool the rest of the curried chicken salad within 1 hour and keep it in a covered shallow container in the fridge, with the spinach, cilantro and the last of the dressing kept apart. Tomorrow, dice the rest of the apple and cucumber, pile everything over the spinach and eat it cold, packed in a cold bag with an ice pack if you take it out. Spoon any chickpeas left in an opened tin into a covered container, refrigerate and use them within 2 days.
tip: Cook the chicken the night before and dinner is just chopping and tossing.

name: Seared salmon with warm potatoes, radishes and lemon-mint yogurt on arugula
inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian salmon with potatoes and cucumber
about: A seared salmon fillet over peppery arugula with tender warm potatoes, crisp radishes, red onion and a lemony mint-yogurt sauce. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the potatoes bring potassium.
steps: Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until tender when poked with a fork, then drain and let them steam dry.
Meanwhile, stir the yogurt with the mint, garlic, half the lemon juice, a pinch of the salt and a spoonful of cold water to make the sauce.
Wash the arugula and radishes. Toss the warm potatoes, radishes and onion with the rest of the lemon juice, half the oil and the pepper.

Pat the salmon dry and season it with the rest of the salt. Heat the remaining oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the salmon skin-side down for 4 to 5 minutes until the skin is crisp.

Turn the fish and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily. Rest it on a clean plate, then wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw fish.

Spread the arugula on a plate, spoon over the potato salad, set the salmon on top and spoon over the mint-yogurt sauce. Cook the salmon the day you buy it, or thaw frozen fillets overnight in the fridge.
tip: Swap the mint for dill if you have it.

name: Cherries with walnuts
about: Sweet fresh cherries with crunchy walnuts. It brings **vitamin C and plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the cherries, remove the pits and eat them with the walnuts.

name: Cherries with almonds
about: Sweet cherries with a handful of almonds. A snack with **vitamin E, fibre and vitamin C**.
steps: Wash the cherries, remove the pits and eat them with the almonds.

name: Blueberries with almonds
about: Blueberries and crunchy almonds in a bowl. A snack with **fibre, vitamin E and manganese**.
steps: Rinse the blueberries and serve them with the almonds.

name: Blueberries with walnuts
about: Blueberries with walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. A snack with **fibre and plant omega-3**.
steps: Rinse the blueberries, top with the walnuts and sprinkle with the cinnamon.

name: Greek yogurt with blueberries and walnuts
about: Thick yogurt with blueberries and crunchy walnuts. It brings **calcium, protein and plant omega-3**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with the blueberries and scatter with the walnuts.

name: Peach with walnuts
about: A ripe peach with a handful of walnuts. It brings **vitamin C, fibre and plant omega-3**, and takes a minute.
steps: Wash the peach, slice it away from the pit and eat it with the walnuts.

name: Watermelon and feta cubes with mint
about: Cold watermelon cubes with salty feta and torn mint. It brings **vitamin C, some calcium and protein**.
steps: Scrub the watermelon rind under running water, cut the flesh into cubes and chill them. Crumble the feta over the cubes and scatter with the mint. Keep it in the fridge until you eat it, and finish it the same day.

name: Lemony chickpeas with cucumber and mint
about: Chickpeas tossed with crunchy cucumber, mint, lemon and a little olive oil. A snack with **plant protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Toss them with the cucumber, mint, lemon juice, olive oil and salt. Keep it in the fridge until you eat it. Spoon any beans left in an opened tin into a covered container, refrigerate and use them within 2 days.

name: Cucumber and pepper sticks with yogurt-mint dip
about: Crunchy cucumber and red pepper sticks with a cool garlicky yogurt and mint dip, and a handful of walnuts. It brings **vitamin C, calcium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the cucumber and pepper and cut them into sticks. Stir the yogurt with the mint, lemon juice and garlic and serve alongside with the walnuts. Keep the dip in the fridge until you eat.

name: Cucumber and cherry tomato cup with feta and mint
about: Juicy cherry tomatoes and cucumber with salty feta, fresh mint and a drizzle of olive oil. A snack with **vitamin C, some calcium and protein**.
steps: Wash the tomatoes, cucumber and mint. Toss the tomatoes and cucumber with the olive oil and lemon juice, crumble over the feta and scatter with the mint. Keep it in the fridge until you eat it.

name: Chilled tomato and cucumber gazpacho with almonds
about: A cold, no-cook blended soup of ripe tomato, cucumber and red pepper with a little olive oil and garlic, topped with toasted almonds. It brings **vitamin C and lycopene**, and is the most refreshing snack of the week.
steps: Wash the tomatoes, cucumber and pepper. Blend them with the garlic, oil, lemon juice and salt until smooth, then chill for at least 30 minutes.
Pour into a glass or bowl and top with the almonds. Serve it cold from the fridge, never leave it out for more than 2 hours, and use leftovers within 2 days.

name: Blueberry banana oatmeal with walnuts and chia
about: Creamy oats cooked in milk with sliced banana, cinnamon and a spoonful of chia, topped with blueberries, walnuts and almonds. The oats and berries bring **fibre**, the walnuts and chia bring plant omega-3 and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the blueberries and slice the banana.
Put the oats, milk, chia, half the banana and the cinnamon in a small pot with a splash of water. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 6 minutes. The banana will melt into the oats.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the blueberries, the rest of the banana, the walnuts and the almonds.
tip: Mix the dry oats, chia and cinnamon in a jar on Sunday and just add the milk.

name: Egg, black bean and pepper breakfast wrap
about: Eggs scrambled until fully set with sweet pepper and black beans, rolled in a toasted whole-wheat tortilla with tomato and spinach, with an orange and a glass of milk on the side. The eggs and beans bring **protein and choline**, the milk brings calcium and the orange helps your body absorb the iron in the beans.
steps: Wash the pepper, tomato, spinach and orange. Dice the pepper and tomato and cut the orange into wedges.
Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the pepper and chili for 3 minutes, then stir in the beans and spinach until the spinach wilts.
Beat the eggs and pour them in. Stir until completely set with no liquid left and the yolk is firm, about 3 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Warm the tortilla for 20 seconds in a dry pan, fill it with the eggs and tomato, roll it up and serve with the orange wedges and a glass of milk.
tip: Taking it to work? Pack the wrap in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day. Keep the milk and orange separate and cold.

name: Mango lassi yogurt bowl with toasted oats, walnuts and chia
about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy mango, a pinch of cardamom and chia, like a spoonable lassi, with a crunchy topping of toasted oats, walnuts and almonds. The yogurt brings **protein and calcium**, and the walnuts and chia bring plant omega-3.
steps: Toast the oats, walnuts and almonds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and smelling nutty, about 3 minutes. Tip onto a plate to cool.
Wash, peel and dice the mango.
Stir the chia and cardamom into the yogurt and spoon it into a bowl.
Pile the mango on top and scatter over the crunchy oats and nuts.

name: Baked falafel-style chickpea patties in a whole-wheat pita with garlic yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by falafel from a Levantine takeout counter, baked instead of fried
about: Chickpeas mashed with oats, onion, cilantro, cumin and coriander, shaped into patties and baked until golden, then tucked into a warm whole-wheat pita with crunchy red cabbage, spinach, tomato, pickles and a garlic yogurt. The chickpeas and pita bring **fibre and plant protein**, and the yogurt brings calcium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray. Mash the chickpeas well with a fork or potato masher until most are broken and the mix is sticky.
Stir in the oats, onion, half the garlic, the cilantro, cumin, coriander, salt and half the oil until the mix holds together when squeezed. Shape into 5 small patties and press them firm.
Lay the patties on the tray, brush with the remaining oil and bake, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash the cabbage, spinach and tomato. Stir the yogurt, remaining garlic and lemon juice together with a splash of water to make a pourable sauce.
Warm the pita, cut it in half and open the pockets. Fill them with the patties, cabbage, spinach, tomato and pickles and drizzle with the garlic yogurt.
tip: Taking it to work? Pack it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day. Bake Thursday's patties with Monday's, cool them within 2 hours and keep them covered in the fridge up to 3 days, then warm them until steaming hot.
ingredients: no salt added, rinsed and patted very dry

name: Chicken souvlaki-style wrap with cucumber yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek souvlaki from a takeout counter, with chicken thigh in a wrap
about: Lemon and oregano chicken thigh pan-seared until golden, rolled in a warm whole-wheat tortilla with tomato, cucumber, carrot, red onion and spinach and a garlicky cucumber yogurt. The chicken brings **protein and B vitamins**, and the carrot and vegetables keep it fresh and crunchy.
steps: Toss the chicken with half the lemon juice, half the garlic, the oregano, salt, pepper and half the oil in a bowl and leave in the fridge while you prep. Never reuse the marinade.
Wash the cucumber, carrot, tomato and spinach. Grate the carrot, and grate half the cucumber, squeeze out the water and stir it into the yogurt with the rest of the garlic and lemon.

Heat the remaining oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds, fill it with the chicken, tomato, sliced cucumber, carrot, onion and spinach, spoon over the cucumber yogurt and roll it up.
tip: Taking it to work? Pack it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
ingredients: whole wheat (two at the bigger sizes)
washed, half grated into the yogurt, half sliced

name: Black bean and egg quesadilla with avocado
about: A crisp whole-wheat tortilla folded around firm scrambled egg, black beans, peppers, carrot and spinach with a measured sprinkle of cheddar, served with sliced avocado and fresh tomato. The beans bring **fibre, iron and folate**, the egg brings choline and the peppers and tomato add vitamin C to help absorb the iron.
steps: Wash the pepper, carrot, tomato, spinach and avocado. Dice the pepper and tomato, grate the carrot and slice the avocado.
Warm half the oil in a non-stick pan and cook the pepper and carrot with the cumin and chili for 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach and beans and cook until the spinach wilts.

Push the filling aside and pour the egg into the pan. Stir until completely set with no liquid left and the yolk is firm, about 2 minutes, then mix it through the filling. Wash your hands after cracking the egg.
Spread the filling over half the tortilla, scatter over the cheese and fold it over.
Wipe the pan, add the remaining oil and cook the quesadilla for 2 minutes a side until golden and crisp. Cut into wedges and serve with the avocado and tomato.
tip: Taking it to work? Pack it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day, and warm it until steaming.
ingredients: whole wheat (two at the bigger sizes)
no salt added, rinsed and lightly mashed

name: Lean beef cheeseburger on a whole-grain bun with sweet potato wedges
inspiredBy: Inspired by a diner cheeseburger and fries, made with lean beef and baked wedges
about: A juicy burger made with lean beef and grated onion, on a toasted whole-wheat bun with one slice of cheddar, a firm fried egg, tomato, pickles, avocado and a crunchy red cabbage slaw, with oven-crisp sweet potato wedges. Beef brings **iron, zinc and B12**, the egg adds choline and the sweet potato brings vitamin A and potassium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potatoes and avocado, then cut the sweet potatoes into wedges, toss with the oil, smoked paprika and a pinch of the salt on a tray and roast, turning once, until golden and tender, about 30 minutes.
Mix the beef with the onion, half the mustard, remaining salt and the pepper using a fork. Shape into a patty a little wider than the bun and press a dip in the middle.

Cook the patty in a hot non-stick pan, about 4 minutes a side, until browned and cooked through to 71 °C (160 °F) on a thermometer with no pink inside. Lay the cheese on in the last minute. Wash your hands, the board and the plate that held the raw beef.

Fry the egg in the same pan with a drop of water and a lid until the white is set and the yolk is firm all the way through, about 4 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the egg. Toast the bun in the pan.
Toss the cabbage with the lemon juice and the remaining mustard. Build the burger with the tomato, pickles, avocado, cabbage and egg and serve with the wedges.
tip: At the bigger sizes, make two smaller patties and use two buns.
ingredients: a whole egg for the top

name: Chicken tikka traybake with broccoli and brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by chicken tikka from an Indian takeout, roasted on a tray instead of in a tandoor
about: Chicken thigh marinated in yogurt, garlic, ginger and garam masala and roasted on a tray with broccoli, carrots, peppers and red onion, served over brown rice with fresh coriander. The chicken brings **protein and B vitamins**, the carrots and peppers bring vitamins A and C, and the broccoli brings vitamin C and folate.
steps: Spoon a third of the yogurt into a small bowl for serving and keep it in the fridge. Stir the rest with the lemon juice, garlic, ginger, garam masala, paprika, turmeric, cumin, chili and salt and coat the chicken. Cover and leave in the fridge while you prep, and never reuse the marinade.
Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Rinse the rice, then boil it in a large pot of water like pasta for about 25 minutes until tender, and drain well.
Wash the broccoli, pepper, carrot and onion, cut them up and toss with the oil on a large tray. Roast for 10 minutes.

Push the vegetables aside, add the chicken in a single layer and roast about 15 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F). Switch the oven to grill for the last 3 minutes so the edges char a little. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.
Stir the spinach and half the coriander into the hot rice. Serve the rice topped with the chicken and vegetables, spoon over the reserved yogurt and scatter the rest of the coriander.

Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch. Cool any rice within 1 hour, spread in a shallow container, and keep it in the fridge up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken and rice together, once only, until steaming hot all the way through, at 74 °C (165 °F).
ingredients: part for the marinade, part for serving

name: Baked salmon tacos with lime slaw and black beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja-style fish tacos
about: Flaky chili-lime baked salmon in warm whole-wheat tortillas with a crunchy cabbage and carrot slaw and a lime avocado crema, with black beans on the side. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the beans and slaw bring fibre and vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the cabbage, carrot, tomato, cilantro and avocado.

Rub the salmon with the oil, chili, cumin and half the salt and lay it on a lined tray. Bake about 12 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Toss the cabbage and carrot with the lime juice, half the cilantro and the remaining salt. Mash the avocado with the rest of the cilantro and a squeeze of lime into a quick crema.
Warm the beans in a small pot until steaming. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or wrapped in foil in the oven.
Flake the salmon into the tortillas with the slaw, tomato and avocado crema, and serve the beans on the side.
tip: Buy the salmon fresh and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight.

name: Turkey and veggie pizza on a crisp whole-wheat pita base with a fresh salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by a pizzeria sausage and pepper pizza, made with lean turkey on a pita
about: A whole-wheat pita crisped in the oven as a thin, sturdy pizza base, spread with tomato sauce, lean turkey seasoned with fennel, peppers, onion, spinach and a little cheddar, and topped with a fried egg cooked until the yolk is firm, with a quick tomato, cucumber and spinach salad. The vegetables bring **fibre and vitamin C**, the egg brings choline and the turkey keeps the saturated fat low.
steps: Heat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F) with a baking tray inside. Wash the pepper, spinach, tomato and cucumber.

Warm half the oil in a pan and cook the turkey with the fennel and the salt, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F), about 5 minutes. Tip it into a bowl. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw turkey.
Prick the pita all over with a fork and crisp it on the hot tray for 2 minutes. Meanwhile stir the garlic and oregano into the tomato sauce.
Spread the sauce over the pita, scatter on the turkey, pepper, onion and half the spinach and finish with the cheddar. Bake 7 to 8 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and the edge is crisp.

While it bakes, crack the egg into the turkey pan with a drop of water, break the yolk, cover and cook until the white is set and the yolk is firm all the way through, about 4 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the egg.
Slide the egg onto the middle of the pizza. Toss the tomato, cucumber and remaining spinach with the lemon juice and remaining oil, slice the pizza and serve with the salad.
tip: The egg is fried in the pan while the pizza bakes: on a thin pita in the oven it would need so long to set firm that the base would burn.
ingredients: whole wheat, one large (or two at the bigger sizes)
washed, half for the pizza and half for the salad

name: Shrimp and veggie fried brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by takeout shrimp fried rice, with brown rice and plenty of vegetables
about: Brown rice stir-fried hot with shrimp, firm scrambled egg, spinach, peas, carrot, cabbage and red onion in garlic, ginger and a little reduced-sodium soy sauce, finished with lemon. The shrimp brings **protein and iodine**, the egg brings choline and the spinach and peas bring iron and folate.
steps: Cook the rice the night before or on Sunday: rinse it, boil it in a large pot of water like pasta for about 25 minutes until tender, drain and spread it in a shallow tray. Cool within 1 hour, then cover and chill. Cold rice fries best.
Wash the vegetables. Dice the carrot and onion and shred the cabbage.

Heat half the oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Cook the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and opaque all the way through, then lift them out. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw shrimp.

Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the carrot, cabbage, onion, garlic and ginger for 3 minutes. Add the rice and peas and fry, breaking up the clumps, until the rice is steaming hot all the way through, about 4 minutes.

Push the rice aside, pour the beaten eggs into the pan and stir until completely set with no liquid left and the yolk is firm, about 2 minutes, then mix them through with the spinach until it wilts. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Return the shrimp, add the soy sauce, pepper and lemon juice and toss.

Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch. Cool any rice within 1 hour, spread in a shallow container, and keep it in the fridge up to 3 days. Reheat the rice, egg and shrimp together, once only, until steaming hot all the way through, at 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Thaw frozen shrimp in the fridge overnight and cook them within a day.

name: Oven-baked haddock and chips with crushed peas
inspiredBy: Inspired by classic fish and chips, baked instead of fried
about: Haddock in a crisp oat and mustard crumb baked in the oven, with thick potato chips roasted in just a little olive oil, crushed lemony peas and a sharp pickle and lemon relish. Haddock brings **lean protein and iodine**, and the peas and potatoes bring fibre and potassium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Scrub the potatoes, cut them into thick chips, toss with half the oil, paprika and half the salt on a tray and roast, turning once, for 35 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges.
Mix the oat crumbs with the rest of the oil, the pepper and a pinch of salt. Mix half the mustard with a spoonful of the oil from the crumbs and brush it over the fish, then press the crumbs on top.

Lay the fish on a lined tray and bake for the last 12 to 15 minutes, until the crumbs are golden and the fish flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and plate after handling the raw fish.
Cook the peas in boiling water until steaming hot, about 3 minutes, drain and crush roughly with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Stir the chopped pickle with the rest of the mustard and a squeeze of lemon for a quick relish. Serve everything with a lemon wedge.
tip: Buy the fish fresh and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight.

name: Cajun salmon with crunchy slaw, garlic broccoli and brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Louisiana-style blackened fish plate with slaw
about: Salmon rubbed with a smoky, peppery Cajun spice mix and baked until it flakes, with a fist of brown rice, garlicky broccoli and a sharp red cabbage slaw dressed with mustard and lemon. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the broccoli and cabbage bring vitamin C, vitamin K and folate.
steps: Rinse the rice and boil it in a large pot of water like pasta for about 25 minutes until tender, then drain.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Rub the salmon with half the oil and the Cajun spice and lay it on a lined tray. Bake about 12 minutes until it flakes and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Wash the cabbage and broccoli. Shred the cabbage and toss it with the mustard, half the lemon juice and the cilantro.
Steam or boil the broccoli for 4 minutes until bright green and just tender. Warm the remaining oil with the garlic for 30 seconds and toss the broccoli in it.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the broccoli and slaw, and squeeze over the rest of the lemon.
tip: Buy the salmon fresh and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight. Use half the spice mix for a milder dish.

about: A bowl of blueberries with a handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the blueberries bring fibre.
steps: Wash the fruit, prepare it as needed and serve with the almonds.

name: Orange and blueberry cup with walnuts
about: Orange segments and blueberries with chopped walnuts. The fruit brings **vitamin C and fibre**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the fruit, cut the orange into segments and mix with the blueberries. Scatter the walnuts over the top.

name: Greek yogurt with mango and walnuts
about: Thick Greek yogurt with diced mango and chopped walnuts. The yogurt brings **protein and calcium**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Peel and dice the mango, spoon it over the yogurt and scatter the walnuts on top.

name: Cumin paprika crunchy chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crunchy with cumin, paprika and a pinch of salt, a savoury takeout-style snack. They bring **fibre, plant protein and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the chickpeas with the oil, cumin, paprika and salt on a tray.
Roast, shaking once, until crisp, about 20 minutes. Cool on the tray, they crisp up as they cool. Keep in a covered container and eat within 3 days.
ingredients: no salt added, rinsed and patted very dry

name: Black bean and avocado dip with cucumber sticks
about: A chunky dip of mashed black beans and avocado with lime and cumin, scooped with crisp cucumber sticks. The beans bring **fibre and folate**, and the avocado and lime make it creamy and fresh.
steps: Mash the beans and avocado with a fork until chunky. Stir in the lime juice, cilantro and cumin.
Serve with the cucumber sticks. The dip keeps covered in the fridge for a day.

name: Egg, black bean and pepper breakfast wrap
about: Eggs scrambled until fully set with sweet pepper and black beans, rolled in a toasted whole-wheat tortilla with tomato and spinach, with an orange and a glass of milk on the side. The eggs and beans bring **protein and choline**, the milk brings calcium and the orange helps your body absorb the iron in the beans.
steps: Wash the pepper, tomato, spinach and orange. Dice the pepper and tomato and cut the orange into wedges.
Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the pepper and chili for 3 minutes, then stir in the beans and spinach until the spinach wilts.
Beat the eggs and pour them in. Stir until completely set with no liquid left and the yolk is firm, about 3 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the eggs.
Warm the tortilla for 20 seconds in a dry pan, fill it with the eggs and tomato, roll it up and serve with the orange wedges and a glass of milk.
tip: Taking it to work? Pack the wrap in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day. Keep the milk and orange separate and cold.

name: Chicken souvlaki-style wrap with cucumber yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek souvlaki from a takeout counter, with chicken thigh in a wrap
about: Lemon and oregano chicken thigh pan-seared until golden, rolled in a warm whole-wheat tortilla with tomato, cucumber, carrot, red onion and spinach and a garlicky cucumber yogurt. The chicken brings **protein and B vitamins**, and the carrot and vegetables keep it fresh and crunchy.
steps: Toss the chicken with half the lemon juice, half the garlic, the oregano, salt, pepper and half the oil in a bowl and leave in the fridge while you prep. Never reuse the marinade.
Wash the cucumber, carrot, tomato and spinach. Grate the carrot, and grate half the cucumber, squeeze out the water and stir it into the yogurt with the rest of the garlic and lemon.

Heat the remaining oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds, fill it with the chicken, tomato, sliced cucumber, carrot, onion and spinach, spoon over the cucumber yogurt and roll it up.
tip: Taking it to work? Pack it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
ingredients: whole wheat (two at the bigger sizes)
washed, half grated into the yogurt, half sliced

name: Shrimp and veggie fried brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by takeout shrimp fried rice, with brown rice and plenty of vegetables

name: Baked salmon tacos with lime slaw and black beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja-style fish tacos
about: Flaky chili-lime baked salmon in warm whole-wheat tortillas with a crunchy cabbage and carrot slaw and a lime avocado crema, with black beans on the side. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the beans and slaw bring fibre and vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the cabbage, carrot, tomato, cilantro and avocado.

Rub the salmon with the oil, chili, cumin and half the salt and lay it on a lined tray. Bake about 12 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Toss the cabbage and carrot with the lime juice, half the cilantro and the remaining salt. Mash the avocado with the rest of the cilantro and a squeeze of lime into a quick crema.
Warm the beans in a small pot until steaming. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or wrapped in foil in the oven.
Flake the salmon into the tortillas with the slaw, tomato and avocado crema, and serve the beans on the side.
tip: Buy the salmon fresh and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight.

name: Black bean and egg quesadilla with avocado
about: A crisp whole-wheat tortilla folded around firm scrambled egg, black beans, peppers, carrot and spinach with a measured sprinkle of cheddar, served with sliced avocado and fresh tomato. The beans bring **fibre, iron and folate**, the egg brings choline and the peppers and tomato add vitamin C to help absorb the iron.
steps: Wash the pepper, carrot, tomato, spinach and avocado. Dice the pepper and tomato, grate the carrot and slice the avocado.
Warm half the oil in a non-stick pan and cook the pepper and carrot with the cumin and chili for 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach and beans and cook until the spinach wilts.

Push the filling aside and pour the egg into the pan. Stir until completely set with no liquid left and the yolk is firm, about 2 minutes, then mix it through the filling. Wash your hands after cracking the egg.
Spread the filling over half the tortilla, scatter over the cheese and fold it over.
Wipe the pan, add the remaining oil and cook the quesadilla for 2 minutes a side until golden and crisp. Cut into wedges and serve with the avocado and tomato.
tip: Taking it to work? Pack it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day, and warm it until steaming.
ingredients: whole wheat (two at the bigger sizes)
no salt added, rinsed and lightly mashed

about: Haddock in a crisp oat and mustard crumb baked in the oven, with thick potato chips roasted in just a little olive oil, crushed lemony peas and a sharp pickle and lemon relish. Haddock brings **lean protein and iodine**, and the peas and potatoes bring fibre and potassium.

name: Baked falafel-style chickpea patties in a whole-wheat pita with garlic yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by falafel from a Levantine takeout counter, baked instead of fried
about: Chickpeas mashed with oats, onion, cilantro, cumin and coriander, shaped into patties and baked until golden, then tucked into a warm whole-wheat pita with crunchy red cabbage, spinach, tomato, pickles and a garlic yogurt. The chickpeas and pita bring **fibre and plant protein**, and the yogurt brings calcium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray. Mash the chickpeas well with a fork or potato masher until most are broken and the mix is sticky.
Stir in the oats, onion, half the garlic, the cilantro, cumin, coriander, salt and half the oil until the mix holds together when squeezed. Shape into 5 small patties and press them firm.
Lay the patties on the tray, brush with the remaining oil and bake, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash the cabbage, spinach and tomato. Stir the yogurt, remaining garlic and lemon juice together with a splash of water to make a pourable sauce.
Warm the pita, cut it in half and open the pockets. Fill them with the patties, cabbage, spinach, tomato and pickles and drizzle with the garlic yogurt.
tip: Taking it to work? Pack it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day. Bake Thursday's patties with Monday's, cool them within 2 hours and keep them covered in the fridge up to 3 days, then warm them until steaming hot.
ingredients: no salt added, rinsed and patted very dry

name: Chicken tikka traybake with broccoli and brown rice
inspiredBy: Inspired by chicken tikka from an Indian takeout, roasted on a tray instead of in a tandoor
about: Chicken thigh marinated in yogurt, garlic, ginger and garam masala and roasted on a tray with broccoli, carrots, peppers and red onion, served over brown rice with fresh coriander. The chicken brings **protein and B vitamins**, the carrots and peppers bring vitamins A and C, and the broccoli brings vitamin C and folate.
steps: Spoon a third of the yogurt into a small bowl for serving and keep it in the fridge. Stir the rest with the lemon juice, garlic, ginger, garam masala, paprika, turmeric, cumin, chili and salt and coat the chicken. Cover and leave in the fridge while you prep, and never reuse the marinade.
Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Rinse the rice, then boil it in a large pot of water like pasta for about 25 minutes until tender, and drain well.
Wash the broccoli, pepper, carrot and onion, cut them up and toss with the oil on a large tray. Roast for 10 minutes.

Push the vegetables aside, add the chicken in a single layer and roast about 15 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F). Switch the oven to grill for the last 3 minutes so the edges char a little. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.
Stir the spinach and half the coriander into the hot rice. Serve the rice topped with the chicken and vegetables, spoon over the reserved yogurt and scatter the rest of the coriander.

Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch. Cool any rice within 1 hour, spread in a shallow container, and keep it in the fridge up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken and rice together, once only, until steaming hot all the way through, at 74 °C (165 °F).
ingredients: part for the marinade, part for serving

name: Lean beef cheeseburger on a whole-grain bun with sweet potato wedges
inspiredBy: Inspired by a diner cheeseburger and fries, made with lean beef and baked wedges
about: A juicy burger made with lean beef and grated onion, on a toasted whole-wheat bun with one slice of cheddar, a firm fried egg, tomato, pickles, avocado and a crunchy red cabbage slaw, with oven-crisp sweet potato wedges. Beef brings **iron, zinc and B12**, the egg adds choline and the sweet potato brings vitamin A and potassium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potatoes and avocado, then cut the sweet potatoes into wedges, toss with the oil, smoked paprika and a pinch of the salt on a tray and roast, turning once, until golden and tender, about 30 minutes.
Mix the beef with the onion, half the mustard, remaining salt and the pepper using a fork. Shape into a patty a little wider than the bun and press a dip in the middle.

Cook the patty in a hot non-stick pan, about 4 minutes a side, until browned and cooked through to 71 °C (160 °F) on a thermometer with no pink inside. Lay the cheese on in the last minute. Wash your hands, the board and the plate that held the raw beef.

Fry the egg in the same pan with a drop of water and a lid until the white is set and the yolk is firm all the way through, about 4 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the egg. Toast the bun in the pan.
Toss the cabbage with the lemon juice and the remaining mustard. Build the burger with the tomato, pickles, avocado, cabbage and egg and serve with the wedges.
tip: At the bigger sizes, make two smaller patties and use two buns.
ingredients: a whole egg for the top

name: Turkey and veggie pizza on a crisp whole-wheat pita base with a fresh salad
inspiredBy: Inspired by a pizzeria sausage and pepper pizza, made with lean turkey on a pita
about: A whole-wheat pita crisped in the oven as a thin, sturdy pizza base, spread with tomato sauce, lean turkey seasoned with fennel, peppers, onion, spinach and a little cheddar, and topped with a fried egg cooked until the yolk is firm, with a quick tomato, cucumber and spinach salad. The vegetables bring **fibre and vitamin C**, the egg brings choline and the turkey keeps the saturated fat low.
steps: Heat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F) with a baking tray inside. Wash the pepper, spinach, tomato and cucumber.

Warm half the oil in a pan and cook the turkey with the fennel and the salt, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 74 °C (165 °F), about 5 minutes. Tip it into a bowl. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw turkey.
Prick the pita all over with a fork and crisp it on the hot tray for 2 minutes. Meanwhile stir the garlic and oregano into the tomato sauce.
Spread the sauce over the pita, scatter on the turkey, pepper, onion and half the spinach and finish with the cheddar. Bake 7 to 8 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and the edge is crisp.

While it bakes, crack the egg into the turkey pan with a drop of water, break the yolk, cover and cook until the white is set and the yolk is firm all the way through, about 4 minutes. Wash your hands after cracking the egg.
Slide the egg onto the middle of the pizza. Toss the tomato, cucumber and remaining spinach with the lemon juice and remaining oil, slice the pizza and serve with the salad.
tip: The egg is fried in the pan while the pizza bakes: on a thin pita in the oven it would need so long to set firm that the base would burn.
ingredients: whole wheat, one large (or two at the bigger sizes)
washed, half for the pizza and half for the salad

name: Blueberry banana oatmeal with walnuts and chia
about: Creamy oats cooked in milk with sliced banana, cinnamon and a spoonful of chia, topped with blueberries, walnuts and almonds. The oats and berries bring **fibre**, the walnuts and chia bring plant omega-3 and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the blueberries and slice the banana.
Put the oats, milk, chia, half the banana and the cinnamon in a small pot with a splash of water. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 6 minutes. The banana will melt into the oats.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the blueberries, the rest of the banana, the walnuts and the almonds.
tip: Mix the dry oats, chia and cinnamon in a jar on Sunday and just add the milk.

name: Mango lassi yogurt bowl with toasted oats, walnuts and chia
about: Thick Greek yogurt with juicy mango, a pinch of cardamom and chia, like a spoonable lassi, with a crunchy topping of toasted oats, walnuts and almonds. The yogurt brings **protein and calcium**, and the walnuts and chia bring plant omega-3.
steps: Toast the oats, walnuts and almonds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and smelling nutty, about 3 minutes. Tip onto a plate to cool.
Wash, peel and dice the mango.
Stir the chia and cardamom into the yogurt and spoon it into a bowl.
Pile the mango on top and scatter over the crunchy oats and nuts.

name: Orange with almonds
about: Orange with a handful of almonds. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the fruit, prepare it as needed and serve with the almonds.

name: Banana with walnuts
about: Banana with a handful of walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3**, and the banana brings potassium.
steps: Wash the fruit, prepare it as needed and serve with the walnuts.

name: Jok gai, Thai chicken and ginger rice porridge with an egg
inspiredBy: Central Thai jok, made with chicken and cooked brown rice
about: A silky rice porridge with tender minced chicken, ginger, an egg and gai lan, topped with crisp shallot, scallion and cilantro. It's a classic Bangkok breakfast, made from the brown rice you cooked on the weekend. The chicken and egg bring **protein and choline**, and the dried shrimp add a little calcium and iodine.
steps: Soak the dried shrimp in warm water for 10 minutes, then chop them finely. Stir the minced chicken with the fish sauce, half the ginger and a pinch of white pepper for about a minute, until it turns tacky, then roll it into marble-sized balls with wet hands. Wash your hands and the board well after handling the raw chicken.
Fry the shallot rings in the oil over medium heat until golden and crisp, about 4 minutes. Lift them out onto a paper towel.

Put the rice, the shrimp, the rest of the ginger and about 3 times as much water as rice by volume in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently, stirring now and then, for 25 to 30 minutes, until the grains have broken down. Mash about a third of the rice against the side of the pot so the porridge turns silky.

Turn the heat down until the porridge is barely simmering and drop in the chicken balls. Cook for 5 minutes, until cooked through and they reach 74 °C (165 °F), then stir in the gai lan and the salt for 1 minute, until the greens are bright.
Crack the egg into the simmering porridge, cover and cook gently for 4 to 5 minutes, until the white and the yolk are firm, then ladle into a bowl.
Top with the crisp shallot, scallion and cilantro.
tip: On weekdays, make the porridge base (the rice, shrimp and ginger) the night before, and roll the chicken balls and fry the shallots then too (keep the raw balls in the fridge). In the morning, reheat the base with a splash of water and add the chicken, greens and egg, which takes about 15 minutes. A few chili slices at the table is how most Thai cooks finish it.

name: Khai jiao, Thai chicken omelette with tomato and brown rice
inspiredBy: Central Thai khai jiao, the street omelette, made here with chicken
about: A golden omelette with a little minced chicken, crisp at the edges and seasoned with fish sauce and lime, over brown rice with juicy tomato wedges and cilantro. It's the breakfast and quick lunch of every Thai street corner. The eggs and chicken bring **protein and choline**, and the tomato adds vitamin C.
steps: Warm the rice if it's cold. Cut the tomato into wedges and put them on a plate with the rice and cilantro.
Beat the eggs in a bowl with the fish sauce, salt, lime juice and scallion until the mixture is frothy.

Heat the oil in a non-stick wok over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 3 minutes, breaking it up, until it's no longer pink and reaches 74 °C (165 °F). Tip the chicken into the beaten egg and leave the oil in the wok.
Turn the heat to high. When a drop of egg sizzles right away, pour in the egg and leave it alone for 1 minute, until the edges bubble and turn golden and crisp.
Flip the omelette, cook for another minute, then slide it onto the rice and serve with the tomato.
tip: A drizzle of sriracha on the omelette is how most people eat it.

name: Xôi black rice with mung beans, dried shrimp and peanut
inspiredBy: Vietnamese xôi đậu xanh, with black sticky rice for the fibre and a little coconut milk
about: Chewy black glutinous rice with soft, smooth mashed mung beans, a hard-boiled egg, crisp fried shallot and a savoury sprinkle of crushed peanuts and dried shrimp, with a little coconut milk drizzled over.
