Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Drop in spoonfuls of batter and fry for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper and eat warm.
ingredients: scotch bonnet or habanero (produce aisle), or another hot red chili

name: Cranberry-orange oatmeal with almonds and walnuts
inspiredBy: Inspired by cranberry-orange scones, turned into a warm bowl of oatmeal
about: Creamy stovetop oats with orange zest and segments, tart cranberries that burst as they cook, and toasted almonds and walnuts on top. The orange brings **vitamin C**, and the oats and nuts keep you full through a cold morning.
steps: Wash the orange. Take a few strips of zest with a peeler, then peel it and cut the flesh into segments.

Put the oats, milk, an equal amount of water, the zest, cranberries, cinnamon and salt in a small pot. Bring to a simmer, then cook over medium-low heat, stirring now and then, for 8 to 10 minutes, until thick and creamy and the cranberries have burst.
Toast the almonds and walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Spoon the oatmeal into a bowl and top with the orange segments and nuts.
tip: For a sweeter bowl, stir half of a mashed banana into the oats while they cook.
ingredients: zest a strip first, then peel and cut into segments

name: Spiced pears and apples with yogurt and oat crunch
inspiredBy: Inspired by the spiced fruit simmered at winter markets, made with orange juice and whole spices only
about: Pears and apples simmered in orange juice with cinnamon, clove, star anise, cardamom and ginger until the kitchen smells like the holidays, then spooned warm over cold yogurt with toasted oats and walnuts. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's breakfast is already done, and the fruit and yogurt bring **fibre and calcium**.
steps: Wash the pears, apples and orange. Core the pears and apples and cut them into chunks about 2 cm across. Juice the orange.

Put the fruit, orange juice, cranberries, ginger, cinnamon, clove, star anise and cardamom in a small pot. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring once, until the fruit is just soft and the juice is syrupy. Lift out the star anise.
While the fruit cooks, toast the oats and walnuts in a dry pan for 3 to 4 minutes until golden.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, top with half of the warm fruit, and scatter over the oat crunch.

Cool the other half of the fruit within 1 hour in a shallow container, cover and refrigerate it. Tomorrow, reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then add the cold yogurt and a fresh oat crunch.
tip: Make the fruit on Monday evening while the bake cooks, cool it within 1 hour, and reheat it each morning, so breakfast takes 5 minutes. It keeps up to 3 days in the fridge, and it is lovely over porridge too.

name: Baked pear and banana oats with sunflower seeds, walnuts and cinnamon
inspiredBy: Inspired by the baked oatmeal of the American Midwest
about: A tray of oats baked with mashed banana, diced pear and cinnamon until golden and spoonable, with crunchy sunflower seeds and walnuts on top. It makes two portions, so Sunday's breakfast is just a reheat, and it brings **fibre and vitamin E**.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and lightly oil a small baking dish.
Wash the pear, core it and dice it. Mash the banana in a bowl, then stir in the oats, milk, cinnamon, salt and the diced pear.
Pour into the dish, scatter over the sunflower seeds and walnuts and bake for 25 minutes, until set and golden at the edges.
Eat one portion warm. Cool the rest within 1 hour in a shallow container, cover and refrigerate it. Tomorrow, reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), with a splash of milk.
tip: Eat the second portion within 2 days. Bake the oats in the morning, then heat the oven to 160 °C again mid-afternoon for the beef stew, so it is hot at dinner time.

name: Warm salmon, egg and potato salad with spinach and lemon-yogurt dressing
inspiredBy: Inspired by a British salmon and new-potato salad
about: Warm potatoes tossed with wilted baby spinach, flaked tinned salmon, a firm egg and a lemony yogurt dressing with parsley. The tinned salmon, bones and all, brings **omega-3 and calcium**, and the potatoes keep it hearty.
steps: Scrub the potatoes and cut them into chunks about 3 cm across. Cover with cold water in a pot, bring to a boil and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Drain.

Meanwhile, boil the egg for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it in cold water, peel and chop it. Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Wash the spinach. Add the warm potatoes, the spinach and the parsley, and toss gently so the spinach wilts. Fold in the salmon in large flakes, taking out any big pieces of skin, and the egg.
Eat it warm or at room temperature. Keep any opened tin of salmon covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
tip: To pack it, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

name: Warm lentil and roasted carrot salad with spinach, a firm egg and pumpkin seeds
inspiredBy: Inspired by French lentil salads
about: Carrots roasted until sweet and a bit caramelised, tossed with lentils, spinach and a sharp lemon-tahini dressing, topped with a firm egg and pumpkin seeds. The lentils bring **iron and folate**, and the lemon helps your body absorb that iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash and scrub the carrots, cut them into thick sticks and toss with half of the oil, the cumin and the salt on a tray. Roast for 22 to 25 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned at the edges.
Meanwhile, boil the egg for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it in cold water, peel and halve it.
Wash the spinach. Warm the lentils in a small pot or the microwave until steaming. Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, vinegar, the remaining oil, the pepper and a splash of water in a bowl until smooth.
Toss the warm lentils, spinach and roasted carrots in the dressing and let the spinach wilt for 2 minutes.
Top with the egg, the parsley and the pumpkin seeds.
tip: To pack it, keep the egg and dressing in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

name: Quinoa, roasted cauliflower and chickpea bowl with shaved sprouts and lemon-tahini yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine tahini sauces over roast cauliflower
about: Roasted cauliflower and nutty quinoa with chickpeas, crunchy shaved raw Brussels sprouts and a lemon-tahini yogurt sauce. The chickpeas bring protein and **folate**, and the tahini and yogurt bring calcium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the cauliflower and Brussels sprouts. Cut the cauliflower into small florets, toss with the oil, cumin and half of the salt on a tray and roast for 20 to 22 minutes, adding the chickpeas for the last 8 minutes, until browned in places.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered, for 15 minutes. Drain if needed and fluff with a fork.
Shave the Brussels sprouts as thinly as you can with a sharp knife. Whisk the tahini, yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, the remaining salt and a splash of cold water until smooth and pourable.
Pile the quinoa in a bowl, top with the cauliflower, chickpeas and shaved sprouts, pour over the sauce and finish with the parsley.
tip: To pack it, keep the sauce in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

name: Chicken and white bean bake with an oat-parsley crumb
inspiredBy: A French-style bean bake, made with chicken thigh and white beans
about: Chicken thigh braised with white beans, leek, carrot and tomato, with thyme, bay and a little smoked paprika, then finished under the grill with a crisp garlicky crumb of oats and parsley. It makes two portions, and the beans and spinach bring **iron, folate and fibre**.
steps: Rinse the leek well, then slice it. Warm half of the oil in a wide oven-safe pot over medium heat and soften the leek, carrot and celery for 5 minutes, with the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, thyme and paprika for 1 minute. Add the chicken and turn it for 3 minutes. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw chicken.

Add the beans, bay leaf, salt, pepper and enough broth to just cover the beans. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 15 to 18 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the sauce is thick. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Meanwhile, toast the oats in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then mix with the parsley, a pinch of salt and the remaining oil. Scatter half over the pot, dish up one portion and grill (broil) that portion for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden.

Cool the other portion, without crumb, within 2 hours in a shallow container and refrigerate it. Tomorrow, reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), then scatter over the rest of the crumb and grill it for 3 minutes.
tip: To freeze it, cool the pot within 2 hours and freeze up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Make the crumb fresh.
ingredients: just enough to cover the beans

name: Roast turkey breast with cranberry-orange sauce, Brussels sprouts and sweet potato
inspiredBy: Inspired by a North American holiday roast dinner, scaled for a Tuesday
about: Thick turkey breast steaks rubbed with sage and thyme and roasted on one tray with sweet potato cubes and Brussels sprouts, with a quick tart cranberry and orange sauce. The sweet potato brings **vitamin A**, the sprouts bring vitamin C and K, and the turkey is lean protein.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Wash the sweet potatoes, sprouts, orange and apple. Toss the sweet potato cubes with half of the oil and a pinch of salt on a large tray and roast for 10 minutes.

Rub the turkey with half of the remaining oil, the sage, thyme, pepper and the rest of the salt. Add the turkey and the sprouts, tossed in the last of the oil, to the tray. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw turkey. Roast for 18 to 20 minutes more, until the turkey reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the sprouts are browned. Rest the turkey for 5 minutes.
While the tray roasts, simmer the cranberries, orange juice and zest, grated apple and cinnamon in a small pot for 8 to 10 minutes, until the berries pop and the sauce thickens.
Slice the turkey, serve with the vegetables and the cranberry sauce, and scatter over the almonds.
ingredients: juiced, plus a strip of zest

name: Slow-roasted salmon with parsnip and potato mash and lemony braised leeks and kale
inspiredBy: Inspired by a bistro plate of salmon with braised leeks and root mash
about: Salmon roasted gently until just flaking, on a creamy mash of parsnip and potato, with leeks and kale braised in broth with lemon. The salmon brings **omega-3 and some vitamin D**, and the parsnip gives the mash a natural sweetness.
steps: Heat the oven to 140 °C (275 °F). Peel the potato and parsnip, cut them into small chunks and put them in a pot of cold water with a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil and simmer for 15 to 18 minutes, until very tender.

Rinse the leeks well. Warm half of the oil in a pan over medium heat, add the leeks and thyme, and turn for 2 minutes. Add the broth, cover and braise for 8 minutes, then add the washed kale for 3 minutes more, until soft. Finish with half of the lemon juice.

Rub the salmon with the remaining oil, salt and pepper and put it on a tray. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw salmon. Roast for 18 to 22 minutes, until the flesh turns opaque and flakes easily and the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Drain the potato and parsnip, return them to the pot with the milk and mash until creamy. Serve the salmon on the mash with the leeks and a squeeze of the remaining lemon.
Buy the salmon and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge. Do not keep leftovers of this dish.
ingredients: halved, rinsed well, cut in lengths

name: Roasted trout with parsnips, carrots and potatoes, wilted spinach and lemon-parsley yogurt
inspiredBy: Inspired by a Scandinavian plate of baked trout and root vegetables
about: Trout fillet roasted over parsnips, carrots and potatoes until just flaking, with wilted spinach and a sharp lemon and parsley yogurt. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the carrots bring vitamin A.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Scrub the parsnips, carrots and potatoes, cut them into sticks and small chunks, toss with two thirds of the oil and a pinch of salt on a large tray, and roast for 15 minutes.

Rub the trout with the remaining oil, salt, pepper and half of the lemon juice. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw trout. Nestle it among the vegetables, skin side down, and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the flesh turns opaque and flakes easily and the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Stir the yogurt, garlic, the remaining lemon juice and the parsley together.
Wash the spinach and wilt it in a hot pan for 1 minute. Serve the trout over the vegetables with the spinach and sauce.
Buy the trout and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge. Do not keep leftovers of this dish.

name: Split pea soup with smoked turkey, leeks and thyme
inspiredBy: Inspired by North American split pea soup, made with smoked turkey
about: Green split peas simmered with leeks, celery, carrot, thyme and a small amount of ready-cooked smoked turkey until thick and almost creamy, with kale, a squeeze of lemon and toasted walnuts. It makes two portions, and the peas bring **fibre, folate and iron**.
steps: Rinse the split peas in cold water. Rinse the leek well, then slice it. Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat and soften the leek, celery and carrot for 6 minutes, with the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the thyme and paprika for 30 seconds. Add the split peas, smoked turkey, bay leaf, pepper and the broth, plus water so the peas are covered by about 3 cm.

Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring now and then and topping up with hot water if it gets too thick, until the peas are completely soft and the soup is thick. The smoked turkey is salty, so taste before adding any salt.
Wash the kale and stir it in for the last 5 minutes. Lift out the bay leaf, stir in the lemon juice and, for a creamier soup, mash a few spoonfuls against the side of the pot.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes and scatter over each bowl.
Eat one portion now. Cool the other within 2 hours in a shallow container and refrigerate it. Tomorrow, reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), adding a splash of water.
tip: In a pressure cooker the peas take about 15 minutes at high pressure. Split peas foam and can block the vent, so fill the cooker no more than half full, keep the oil in, and release the pressure naturally. To freeze it, cool within 2 hours and freeze up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).
ingredients: smoked, ready-cooked, skin removed, finely diced
plus water to keep it covered

name: Slow-braised beef and root vegetable stew with thyme and bay
inspiredBy: Inspired by the British beef casserole, with parsnip alongside the carrot and potato
about: Chunks of beef chuck braised low and slow in the oven with parsnip, carrot and potato in a thyme and tomato gravy, until the beef falls apart with a fork and the vegetables are sweet. It makes two portions, and the beef brings **iron and zinc**, with spinach stirred in at the end.
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F). Pat the beef dry and season it with the salt and pepper. Warm the oil in a heavy oven-safe pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, about 3 minutes a side, then set it on a clean plate. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw beef.
In the same pot, soften the onion for 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic, tomato paste and thyme for 1 minute. Add the vinegar and scrape up the browned bits.

Return the beef to the pot with the bay leaves and broth. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and braise in the oven for 1 hour. Add the parsnip, carrot and potato, cover and braise for 1 hour more, until the beef is fork-tender, well past 71 °C (160 °F), and the vegetables are soft.
Wash the spinach, stir it in with the parsley and cook for the last 3 minutes, until it wilts. Lift out the bay leaves and taste for salt.
Eat one portion now. Cool the other within 1 hour in a shallow container, since it has potato, and refrigerate it. Tomorrow, reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Start it by mid-afternoon, about 3 hours before dinner. In a pressure cooker, braise the browned beef for 25 minutes at high pressure, release, add the vegetables and cook 8 minutes more. To freeze it, cool within 1 hour and freeze up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F).
ingredients: just enough to come two thirds up the meat

name: Apple wedges with almonds
about: Crisp apple wedges with a small handful of almonds. The apple brings fibre, and the almonds bring crunch and **vitamin E**.
steps: Wash the apple, core it and cut it into wedges.
Eat with the almonds.

name: Pear with walnuts
about: A ripe pear with a small handful of walnuts. The walnuts bring **omega-3**, and the pear brings fibre.
steps: Wash the pear and slice it.
Eat with the walnuts.

name: Orange with walnuts
about: A juicy orange with a small handful of walnuts. The orange brings **vitamin C**, and the walnuts bring omega-3.
steps: Wash the orange, peel it and split it into segments.
Eat with the walnuts.

name: Firm-boiled egg with carrot and celery sticks
about: A firm-boiled egg with crunchy carrot and celery sticks and a pinch of smoked paprika. It brings **protein and choline**.
steps: Boil the egg for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm, then cool it in cold water and peel it.
Wash the carrot and celery and cut them into sticks. Serve with the egg, sprinkled with the paprika and salt.

name: Apple wedges with walnuts and cinnamon
about: Crisp apple wedges with a small handful of walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The walnuts bring **omega-3**, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, core it and cut it into wedges.
Eat with the walnuts and dust with the cinnamon.

name: Carrot and celery sticks with lemon-tahini yogurt dip
about: Crunchy carrot and celery sticks with a creamy lemon, garlic and tahini yogurt dip. The dip brings **calcium and protein**.
steps: Wash the carrot and celery, then cut them into sticks.
Stir the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt together with a splash of water until smooth.
Serve the sticks with the dip.

name: Cinnamon-roasted chickpeas
about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with cinnamon, cumin and a pinch of salt. A crunchy snack that brings **fibre, protein and iron**.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Pat the chickpeas completely dry and toss them with the oil, cinnamon, cumin and salt.
Roast on a tray for 22 to 25 minutes, shaking once, until crisp. They crisp more as they cool.

name: Greek yogurt with banana, cinnamon and walnuts
about: Cool Greek yogurt with sliced banana, a dusting of cinnamon and crunchy walnuts. It brings **calcium and protein**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Top with the banana, walnuts and cinnamon.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A banana with a small handful of walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. It brings **potassium and omega-3**.
steps: Peel the banana and eat it with the walnuts.
Dust with the cinnamon.

name: Banana with almonds and cinnamon
about: A banana with a small handful of almonds and a dusting of cinnamon. It brings **potassium and vitamin E**.
steps: Peel the banana and eat it with the almonds.
Dust with the cinnamon.

name: Butternut squash and white bean soup with sage, walnuts and sunflower seeds
inspiredBy: Inspired by the squash soups of North American winters
about: Butternut squash and white beans simmered with onion, garlic and sage, then blended until velvety, with a swirl of cold yogurt and toasted walnuts and sunflower seeds on top. The squash brings **vitamin A**, the seeds bring vitamin E, and the beans make it a filling lunch.
steps: Wash the squash, then peel it and cut it into small cubes. Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes, with the garlic, sage and thyme for the last minute.
Add the squash, the rinsed beans, the broth, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 to 18 minutes, until the squash is completely soft.
Take the pot off the heat, add the milk and blend until smooth with a stick blender, or in a blender with the lid vented and a towel on top. Reheat gently until steaming.
Toast the walnuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Ladle into a bowl, swirl in the cold yogurt and scatter the walnuts and seeds on top.
tip: Make it the evening before: cool it within 2 hours in a shallow container, refrigerate it, and reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), within 3 days. Pack it in a hot flask and add the yogurt, walnuts and seeds when you eat.

name: Chicken braised with mushrooms and onions, over lentils and kale
inspiredBy: Inspired by French bistro braises of chicken with mushrooms and small onions
about: Chicken thighs braised with browned mushrooms, onion, garlic, thyme and bay in a rich, glossy gravy, then served over lentils and kale that soak up the sauce. The lentils and kale bring **iron and folate**, and the mushrooms bring B vitamins.
steps: Wash the kale and parsley, and wipe or quickly rinse the mushrooms. Warm half of the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for about 3 minutes a side, then set it on a clean plate. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw chicken.

Add the rest of the oil, the mushrooms and the onion and cook for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mushrooms are browned and the onion is golden at the edges. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and thyme for 1 minute.

Pour in the broth with the bay leaf, salt and pepper and scrape up the browned bits. Nestle the chicken back in, bring to a simmer, cover and braise gently for 18 to 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the gravy is glossy.
Stir the lentils and kale into the gravy around the chicken for the last 5 minutes, until steaming hot and the kale is soft. Lift out the bay leaf, add the vinegar and taste for salt.
Serve the chicken on the mushrooms, lentils and kale, scattered with the parsley.
tip: Peeled small shallots or pearl onions, left whole, are lovely here instead of the onion wedges.

name: Sweet potato, egg and salsa verde breakfast tacos
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos con papas and breakfast tacos
about: Grated sweet potato crisped with cumin, wilted spinach, black beans and firm scrambled eggs, tucked into warm corn tortillas with salsa verde and sliced avocado, with a glass of milk on the side. The sweet potato brings **vitamin A and fibre**, the eggs and beans bring protein and choline, and the milk brings calcium.
steps: Wash the sweet potato, spinach and avocado. Grate the sweet potato on the coarse side of a grater and slice the avocado.

Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the sweet potato with the cumin, stirring now and then, until tender with golden edges, about 4 minutes. Add the spinach and beans and stir until the spinach wilts and the beans are hot, about 1 minute.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper and pour them in. Stir gently until the eggs are completely set, with no liquid left and the yolks firm, about 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side. Spoon in the eggs and top with the salsa verde and avocado.
tip: Grate the sweet potato the night before and keep it covered in the fridge to save a few minutes.

name: Mixed berry overnight oats with walnuts and sunflower seeds
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt with frozen berries, cinnamon and a scatter of toasted walnuts. The oats bring **fibre**, the berries bring vitamin C, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3, with sunflower seeds for vitamin E.
steps: Stir the oats, yogurt, cinnamon and enough of the milk to cover the oats well in a jar or bowl. Stir in the frozen berries, cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
In the morning, toast the walnuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, about 2 minutes.
Stir the oats, pour over the rest of the milk (or drink it alongside) and scatter the toasted walnuts and seeds over the top. Eat it cold.
tip: Make two jars at once and keep them covered in the fridge. Eat soaked oats within 3 days, and make a fresh batch after that. If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

name: Banana and peanut butter breakfast wrap with orange
inspiredBy: Inspired by a peanut butter and banana sandwich
about: A warm whole-wheat tortilla with peanut butter, sliced banana, a spoonful of Greek yogurt and cinnamon, with an orange and a glass of milk on the side. The peanut butter, yogurt and milk bring **protein and calcium**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Peel and slice the banana.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side so it turns soft and a little toasty.

Spread the peanut butter over the tortilla, lay the banana down the middle, spoon on the yogurt, sprinkle with the sunflower seeds and dust with cinnamon. Roll it up and eat it with the orange and the milk.
tip: Warm the peanut butter for 10 seconds if it is stiff, so it spreads easily.

name: Chipotle salmon salad wrap with black beans and crunchy veg
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic salmon salad sandwich, with chipotle and black beans
about: Canned salmon mashed with Greek yogurt, lime and a little chipotle, rolled in a whole-wheat tortilla with black beans, red pepper, carrot and spinach. Canned salmon with its soft bones brings **omega-3, vitamin D and calcium**, and the red pepper brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the pepper, carrot, spinach and cilantro. Dice the pepper, grate the carrot and chop the cilantro.
In a bowl, mash the salmon with the yogurt, chipotle, lime juice, cilantro and pepper until it holds together. Fold in the beans, pepper and carrot.
Lay the spinach down the middle of the tortilla, spoon the salmon mixture on top, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
If you are packing it, wrap it well and keep it in a cold bag with an ice pack, and eat it the same day. Cover and refrigerate any opened tin and use it within 2 days.
tip: Chipotle varies a lot from tin to tin. Start with half and taste.
ingredients: minced, with a little of the sauce

name: Peanut-lime chicken and crunchy cabbage wrap
inspiredBy: Inspired by Thai peanut salad and Vietnamese rice paper rolls
about: Thin strips of seared chicken breast tossed with shredded cabbage, carrot and cucumber in a peanut, lime and soy dressing, rolled into a whole-wheat tortilla. The chicken brings **lean protein and niacin**, and the lime and crunchy raw vegetables keep it bright.
steps: Wash the cabbage, carrot, cucumber and cilantro. Shred the cabbage, grate the carrot and cut the cucumber into thin sticks.

Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with the cumin and cook, turning now and then, until golden and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Put it on a clean plate, then wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, garlic and chili powder with a spoonful of warm water until smooth and pourable.

Toss the chicken, cabbage, carrot, cucumber and cilantro with the dressing. Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side, pile the filling down the middle, scatter the sunflower seeds over it, fold in the sides and roll up.
If you are packing it, keep it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Slice the chicken across the grain, as thin as you can, so it cooks quickly and stays tender.

name: Smoky black bean and pepper tacos with lime yogurt
about: Black beans mashed lightly with sweet pepper, onion, cumin and smoked paprika, piled into warm corn tortillas with spinach, avocado and a cool lime and cilantro yogurt. The beans bring **fibre, folate and iron**, and the lime yogurt brings calcium.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach, cilantro and avocado. Slice the pepper, onion and avocado.
Warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the pepper and onion until soft and a little charred at the edges, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika for 30 seconds.

Add the beans with a splash of water and the salt. Cook, mashing about a third of them with the back of a spoon, until thick and hot all the way through, about 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Stir the yogurt with the lime juice and cilantro. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill them with the beans, avocado, a spoonful of the yogurt and a little crumbled queso fresco, and scatter the sunflower seeds over the top.
tip: Mash a few more of the beans if you like the filling thicker.

name: Chicken tinga tacos with pinto beans and lime-pickled onion
inspiredBy: Inspired by tinga de pollo from Puebla, with beans stretching the chicken
about: Tender chicken breast simmered in a smoky chipotle and tomato sauce, shredded and stirred with pinto beans and spinach, then piled into warm corn tortillas with lime-pickled onion, grated carrot, cilantro and avocado. The chicken and beans make it **filling, with fibre and folate**, and the tomato, spinach and lime bring vitamin C.
steps: Wash the carrot, spinach, cilantro and avocado. Slice the onion and grate the carrot. Put a small handful of the onion slices in a bowl with half the lime juice and a pinch of the salt to quick-pickle while you cook. Chop the garlic and spinach.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the rest of the onion until soft and golden at the edges, about 7 minutes, then stir in the garlic, oregano and cumin for 30 seconds.

Add the tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon, then the chipotle and the rest of the lime juice. Bring to a simmer and nestle in the chicken. Cover and cook, turning once, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part, about 15 minutes.

Lift the chicken onto a clean plate and shred it with two forks. Wash your hands, the board and the forks after handling the raw chicken. Return the chicken to the pan with the beans, spinach and the rest of the salt and simmer until the spinach wilts and the sauce is thick and spoonable, about 4 minutes.
Toss the carrot with the cilantro. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill them with the tinga, carrot, pickled onion and avocado.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of tinga within 1 hour in a shallow container, then cover and refrigerate it with the carrot, pickled onion and tortillas kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the tinga until steaming, to 74 °C.
tip: The tinga freezes well without the tortillas and toppings: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C. For less heat, use half the chipotle.
ingredients: minced, with a little of the sauce

name: Pan-seared cod tacos with lime-cabbage slaw and black beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja-style fish tacos
about: Chili-and-cumin cod seared in a hot pan and flaked into warm corn tortillas with a crunchy lime and cilantro cabbage slaw and a quick avocado-lime crema, with garlicky black beans on the side. Cod is a **lean, low-fat protein with iodine**, and the beans bring fibre and folate.
steps: Wash the cabbage, carrot, cilantro and avocado. Toss the cabbage, carrot, half the cilantro and half the lime juice with a pinch of the salt and a pinch of chili.
Mash the avocado with the rest of the lime juice and cilantro into a loose crema.

Pat the cod dry and rub it with half the oil, the chili powder, cumin and the rest of the salt. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the cod 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Warm the beans in a small pot with the garlic and the remaining oil and a splash of water until steaming hot. Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Flake the cod into them, top with the slaw, crema, queso fresco and sunflower seeds, and serve the beans on the side.
tip: Buy fresh cod and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight. Haddock or pollock works the same way.

name: Lentil-walnut tacos with lime crema
inspiredBy: Inspired by walnut "taco meat"
about: A smoky, meaty-textured filling of lentils and toasted walnuts, spiced with cumin and paprika and cooked with tomato, spooned into corn tortillas with shredded lettuce and a lime yogurt crema. The lentils bring **fibre, iron and folate**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the lettuce, spinach and cilantro. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes, then chop them finely.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 7 minutes, then stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chili and oregano for 30 seconds.

Add the lentils, tomatoes with their juice and the soy sauce. Cook, mashing about half the lentils with the back of a spoon, until thick and hot all the way through, about 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then the walnuts.
Stir the yogurt with half the lime juice and half the cilantro. Shred the lettuce and toss it with the rest of the lime juice and cilantro.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill them with the lentil mixture, lettuce and crema.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of filling within 1 hour in a shallow container, then cover and refrigerate it with the lettuce, crema and tortillas kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the filling until steaming, to 74 °C.
tip: The filling freezes well without the crema and lettuce: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C.

name: Cumin-lime trout tacos with pineapple salsa
inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja fish tacos and pineapple salsa
about: Cumin and lime-rubbed trout seared until flaky and piled into warm corn tortillas with a juicy pineapple and red pepper salsa, crunchy cabbage and toasted sunflower seeds. Trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the pineapple and pepper bring vitamin C.
steps: Wash the pineapple, pepper, cabbage and cilantro. Toss the pineapple, onion, pepper, cilantro and two thirds of the lime juice with a pinch of the salt.

Pat the trout dry and rub it with the oil, cumin, chili powder, the rest of the lime juice and the remaining salt. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the trout 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side.
Flake the trout into the tortillas with the cabbage, a big spoonful of salsa, the queso fresco and the toasted seeds.
tip: Buy fresh trout and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight. Slice any leftover pineapple for tomorrow's snack.

name: Korean-style beef lettuce and tortilla wraps
inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean ssam and bulgogi flavours
about: Gochujang-glazed lean beef with garlic and wilted spinach, folded into warm corn tortillas with butter lettuce leaves and a crunchy lime-pickled carrot and cucumber. The beef brings **iron and zinc** and the pickled vegetables bring crunch and brightness.
steps: Wash the carrot, cucumber, spinach, lettuce and ginger. Cut the carrot and cucumber into thin sticks and toss them with the lime juice and the pepper. Let them sit while you cook.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, garlic and ginger with a splash of water into a loose paste.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through to 71 °C (160 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Stir in the paste and the spinach and cook until the spinach wilts and the beef is glazed, about 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Lay a lettuce leaf on each, add the beef and top with the pickled vegetables. Fold and eat.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of beef within 1 hour in a shallow container, cover and refrigerate it with the pickles, lettuce and tortilla kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the beef until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Gochujang brands vary in heat and salt, so taste the paste first. Use less for a milder wrap.
ingredients: washed and cut in thin sticks
washed and cut in thin sticks

name: Salmon, pinto bean and spinach enchiladas verdes
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican enchiladas verdes, with canned salmon for the filling
about: Corn tortillas rolled around a filling of flaked canned salmon, pinto beans and wilted spinach, covered in a tangy salsa verde and tomato sauce and baked until bubbling, then finished with avocado and cilantro. The salmon, with its soft bones, brings **omega-3, vitamin D and calcium**, and the beans bring fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Wash the spinach, cilantro and avocado. Chop the onion and spinach.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cumin, then the beans, spinach and salt, and cook until the spinach wilts and the beans are hot, about 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and fold in the salmon, flaking it with a fork.

Stir the salsa verde with the tomatoes, crushed with a spoon, to make the sauce. Spread a thin layer of it over the bottom of a baking dish. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan so they bend without cracking, fill each with some of the salmon mixture, roll them up and set them seam side down in the dish.
Pour the rest of the sauce over the top, cover the dish with foil and bake until bubbling at the edges and hot all the way through, to 74 °C (165 °F), about 25 minutes.

Top with avocado and cilantro. This makes two portions. Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, refrigerate it, and use it within 3 days. Reheat until steaming, to 74 °C. Cover and refrigerate any opened tin and use it within 2 days.
tip: Freeze the baked enchiladas without the avocado: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C.

name: Chili-lime roasted cauliflower and chickpea tacos with caramelized pineapple
inspiredBy: Inspired by the chili and pineapple flavours of Mexico City taco stands
about: Cauliflower and chickpeas roasted in a smoky chili, lime and tomato rub with caramelized pineapple, tucked into corn tortillas with a lime yogurt crema, raw onion and sunflower seeds. The chickpeas and cauliflower bring **fibre, folate and plant protein**, and the pineapple brings vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a tray with parchment. Wash the cauliflower, pineapple and cilantro.

Whisk the tomatoes, half the lime juice, the oil, garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano and salt in a large bowl. Add the cauliflower, chickpeas and half the onion and toss until coated.

Spread everything in a single layer on the tray, using two trays if it is crowded, so the chickpeas roast rather than steam. Roast for 12 minutes. Add the pineapple wedges and roast until the cauliflower is tender and charred at the edges and the pineapple is caramelized, about 10 minutes more.
Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes. Stir the yogurt with the rest of the lime juice.

Chop the roasted cauliflower and pineapple roughly. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill them with the roasted mixture, a spoonful of crema, the remaining raw onion, cilantro and the sunflower seeds.

name: Orange with sunflower seeds
about: A juicy orange with a small handful of sunflower seeds. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the seeds bring vitamin E and magnesium.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Eat it with the sunflower seeds.

name: Apple slices with walnuts
about: Crisp apple slices with a handful of walnuts. The walnuts bring **plant omega-3** and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, core it and cut it into slices. Eat it with the walnuts.

name: Carrot, cucumber and pepper sticks with lime and chili
about: Crunchy raw vegetables with a squeeze of lime and a shake of chili, the way street vendors serve them. They bring **vitamins A and C** and almost no calories.
steps: Wash the carrot, cucumber and pepper and cut them into sticks and strips.
Squeeze the lime over them and shake on the chili powder and salt.

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A banana with a handful of walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The banana brings **potassium** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Peel the banana and eat it with the walnuts, dusted with the cinnamon.

name: Orange with walnuts
about: A juicy orange with a handful of walnuts. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Eat it with the walnuts.

name: Pineapple with lime and walnuts
about: Juicy pineapple chunks with a squeeze of lime and a handful of walnuts. The pineapple brings **vitamin C and manganese** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the pineapple, peel it and cut it into chunks, then squeeze the lime over it.
Scatter the walnuts over the top and eat.

name: Lime-chili roasted chickpeas
about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with lime, chili and cumin. The chickpeas bring **protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Rinse the chickpeas and dry them very well on a clean towel.
Toss them with the oil, chili powder, cumin and salt and roast on a tray, shaking once, until crisp, about 25 minutes. Squeeze the lime over them and let them cool, as they crisp more as they cool.
tip: Roast a double batch and keep them uncovered at room temperature for up to 2 days.

name: Warm edamame with lime and chili
about: Edamame beans warmed through with lime and a pinch of chili. The edamame brings **protein, iron and folate**.
steps: Cook the edamame in boiling water until steaming hot and tender, about 4 minutes, then drain.
Toss with the lime juice, chili powder and salt and eat warm.

name: Banana with peanut butter
about: A banana with a spoonful of peanut butter. The banana brings **potassium** and the peanut butter brings protein and vitamin E.
steps: Peel and slice the banana and eat it with the peanut butter.

name: Black bean and lime dip with pepper and cucumber sticks
about: A smooth black bean dip with lime and cumin, with pepper and cucumber sticks for dipping. The beans bring **fibre, iron and protein**.
steps: Wash the pepper and cucumber and cut them into strips and sticks.
Mash the beans with the lime juice, oil, cumin and salt, adding a spoonful of water until smooth.
Serve the dip with the vegetables. Keep any leftover dip covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Crunchy cumin pinto beans
about: Oven-crisped pinto beans with cumin, smoked paprika and a squeeze of lime. The beans bring **protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Rinse the pinto beans and dry them very well on a clean towel.

Toss them with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika and salt and roast on a tray, shaking once, until crisp at the edges, about 25 minutes. Squeeze the lime over them and let them cool, as they crisp more as they cool.
tip: Roast a double batch and keep them uncovered at room temperature for up to 2 days.

name: Lime and cumin chickpea dip with carrot and cucumber sticks
about: A quick, chunky chickpea dip with lime, garlic and cumin, with carrot and cucumber sticks for dipping. The chickpeas bring **protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Wash the carrot and cucumber and cut them into sticks.
Mash the chickpeas with the lime juice, oil, garlic, cumin and salt, adding a spoonful of water until you have a chunky dip.
Serve the dip with the sticks. Keep any leftover dip covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Sweet potato, egg and salsa verde breakfast tacos
inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos con papas and breakfast tacos
about: Grated sweet potato crisped with cumin, wilted spinach, black beans and firm scrambled eggs, tucked into warm corn tortillas with salsa verde and sliced avocado, with a glass of milk on the side. The sweet potato brings **vitamin A and fibre**, the eggs and beans bring protein and choline, and the milk brings calcium.
steps: Wash the sweet potato, spinach and avocado. Grate the sweet potato on the coarse side of a grater and slice the avocado.

Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the sweet potato with the cumin, stirring now and then, until tender with golden edges, about 4 minutes. Add the spinach and beans and stir until the spinach wilts and the beans are hot, about 1 minute.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper and pour them in. Stir gently until the eggs are completely set, with no liquid left and the yolks firm, about 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side. Spoon in the eggs and top with the salsa verde and avocado.
tip: Grate the sweet potato the night before and keep it covered in the fridge to save a few minutes.

name: Mixed berry overnight oats with walnuts and sunflower seeds
about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt with frozen berries, cinnamon and a scatter of toasted walnuts. The oats bring **fibre**, the berries bring vitamin C, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3, with sunflower seeds for vitamin E.
steps: Stir the oats, yogurt, cinnamon and enough of the milk to cover the oats well in a jar or bowl. Stir in the frozen berries, cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
In the morning, toast the walnuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, about 2 minutes.
Stir the oats, pour over the rest of the milk (or drink it alongside) and scatter the toasted walnuts and seeds over the top. Eat it cold.
tip: Make two jars at once and keep them covered in the fridge. Eat soaked oats within 3 days, and make a fresh batch after that. If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

name: Banana and peanut butter breakfast wrap with orange
inspiredBy: Inspired by a peanut butter and banana sandwich
about: A warm whole-wheat tortilla with peanut butter, sliced banana, a spoonful of Greek yogurt and cinnamon, with an orange and a glass of milk on the side. The peanut butter, yogurt and milk bring **protein and calcium**, and the orange brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the orange and cut it into wedges. Peel and slice the banana.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side so it turns soft and a little toasty.

Spread the peanut butter over the tortilla, lay the banana down the middle, spoon on the yogurt, sprinkle with the sunflower seeds and dust with cinnamon. Roll it up and eat it with the orange and the milk.
tip: Warm the peanut butter for 10 seconds if it is stiff, so it spreads easily.

name: Chipotle salmon salad wrap with black beans and crunchy veg
inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic salmon salad sandwich, with chipotle and black beans
about: Canned salmon mashed with Greek yogurt, lime and a little chipotle, rolled in a whole-wheat tortilla with black beans, red pepper, carrot and spinach. Canned salmon with its soft bones brings **omega-3, vitamin D and calcium**, and the red pepper brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the pepper, carrot, spinach and cilantro. Dice the pepper, grate the carrot and chop the cilantro.
In a bowl, mash the salmon with the yogurt, chipotle, lime juice, cilantro and pepper until it holds together. Fold in the beans, pepper and carrot.
Lay the spinach down the middle of the tortilla, spoon the salmon mixture on top, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
If you are packing it, wrap it well and keep it in a cold bag with an ice pack, and eat it the same day. Cover and refrigerate any opened tin and use it within 2 days.
tip: Chipotle varies a lot from tin to tin. Start with half and taste.
ingredients: minced, with a little of the sauce

name: Peanut-lime chicken and crunchy cabbage wrap
inspiredBy: Inspired by Thai peanut salad and Vietnamese rice paper rolls
about: Thin strips of seared chicken breast tossed with shredded cabbage, carrot and cucumber in a peanut, lime and soy dressing, rolled into a whole-wheat tortilla. The chicken brings **lean protein and niacin**, and the lime and crunchy raw vegetables keep it bright.
steps: Wash the cabbage, carrot, cucumber and cilantro. Shred the cabbage, grate the carrot and cut the cucumber into thin sticks.

Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with the cumin and cook, turning now and then, until golden and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Put it on a clean plate, then wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, garlic and chili powder with a spoonful of warm water until smooth and pourable.

Toss the chicken, cabbage, carrot, cucumber and cilantro with the dressing. Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side, pile the filling down the middle, scatter the sunflower seeds over it, fold in the sides and roll up.
If you are packing it, keep it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
tip: Slice the chicken across the grain, as thin as you can, so it cooks quickly and stays tender.

name: Chicken tinga tacos with pinto beans and lime-pickled onion
inspiredBy: Inspired by tinga de pollo from Puebla, with beans stretching the chicken
about: Tender chicken breast simmered in a smoky chipotle and tomato sauce, shredded and stirred with pinto beans and spinach, then piled into warm corn tortillas with lime-pickled onion, grated carrot, cilantro and avocado. The chicken and beans make it **filling, with fibre and folate**, and the tomato, spinach and lime bring vitamin C.
steps: Wash the carrot, spinach, cilantro and avocado. Slice the onion and grate the carrot. Put a small handful of the onion slices in a bowl with half the lime juice and a pinch of the salt to quick-pickle while you cook. Chop the garlic and spinach.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the rest of the onion until soft and golden at the edges, about 7 minutes, then stir in the garlic, oregano and cumin for 30 seconds.

Add the tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon, then the chipotle and the rest of the lime juice. Bring to a simmer and nestle in the chicken. Cover and cook, turning once, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part, about 15 minutes.

Lift the chicken onto a clean plate and shred it with two forks. Wash your hands, the board and the forks after handling the raw chicken. Return the chicken to the pan with the beans, spinach and the rest of the salt and simmer until the spinach wilts and the sauce is thick and spoonable, about 4 minutes.
Toss the carrot with the cilantro. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill them with the tinga, carrot, pickled onion and avocado.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of tinga within 1 hour in a shallow container, then cover and refrigerate it with the carrot, pickled onion and tortillas kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the tinga until steaming, to 74 °C.
tip: The tinga freezes well without the tortillas and toppings: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C. For less heat, use half the chipotle.
ingredients: minced, with a little of the sauce

name: Pan-seared cod tacos with lime-cabbage slaw and black beans
inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja-style fish tacos
about: Chili-and-cumin cod seared in a hot pan and flaked into warm corn tortillas with a crunchy lime and cilantro cabbage slaw and a quick avocado-lime crema, with garlicky black beans on the side. Cod is a **lean, low-fat protein with iodine**, and the beans bring fibre and folate.
steps: Wash the cabbage, carrot, cilantro and avocado. Toss the cabbage, carrot, half the cilantro and half the lime juice with a pinch of the salt and a pinch of chili.
Mash the avocado with the rest of the lime juice and cilantro into a loose crema.

Pat the cod dry and rub it with half the oil, the chili powder, cumin and the rest of the salt. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the cod 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Warm the beans in a small pot with the garlic and the remaining oil and a splash of water until steaming hot. Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Flake the cod into them, top with the slaw, crema, queso fresco and sunflower seeds, and serve the beans on the side.
tip: Buy fresh cod and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight. Haddock or pollock works the same way.

name: Lentil-walnut tacos with lime crema
inspiredBy: Inspired by walnut "taco meat"
about: A smoky, meaty-textured filling of lentils and toasted walnuts, spiced with cumin and paprika and cooked with tomato, spooned into corn tortillas with shredded lettuce and a lime yogurt crema. The lentils bring **fibre, iron and folate**, and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
steps: Wash the lettuce, spinach and cilantro. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes, then chop them finely.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 7 minutes, then stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chili and oregano for 30 seconds.

Add the lentils, tomatoes with their juice and the soy sauce. Cook, mashing about half the lentils with the back of a spoon, until thick and hot all the way through, about 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then the walnuts.
Stir the yogurt with half the lime juice and half the cilantro. Shred the lettuce and toss it with the rest of the lime juice and cilantro.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill them with the lentil mixture, lettuce and crema.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of filling within 1 hour in a shallow container, then cover and refrigerate it with the lettuce, crema and tortillas kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the filling until steaming, to 74 °C.
tip: The filling freezes well without the crema and lettuce: cool within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge, use within 2 days, never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C.

name: Cumin-lime trout tacos with pineapple salsa
inspiredBy: Inspired by Baja fish tacos and pineapple salsa
about: Cumin and lime-rubbed trout seared until flaky and piled into warm corn tortillas with a juicy pineapple and red pepper salsa, crunchy cabbage and toasted sunflower seeds. Trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the pineapple and pepper bring vitamin C.
steps: Wash the pineapple, pepper, cabbage and cilantro. Toss the pineapple, onion, pepper, cilantro and two thirds of the lime juice with a pinch of the salt.

Pat the trout dry and rub it with the oil, cumin, chili powder, the rest of the lime juice and the remaining salt. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the trout 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until it flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F). Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw fish.
Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden, about 2 minutes. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds on each side.
Flake the trout into the tortillas with the cabbage, a big spoonful of salsa, the queso fresco and the toasted seeds.
tip: Buy fresh trout and cook it within a day, or thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight. Slice any leftover pineapple for tomorrow's snack.

name: Smoky black bean and pepper tacos with lime yogurt
about: Black beans mashed lightly with sweet pepper, onion, cumin and smoked paprika, piled into warm corn tortillas with spinach, avocado and a cool lime and cilantro yogurt. The beans bring **fibre, folate and iron**, and the lime yogurt brings calcium.
steps: Wash the pepper, spinach, cilantro and avocado. Slice the pepper, onion and avocado.
Warm the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the pepper and onion until soft and a little charred at the edges, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika for 30 seconds.

Add the beans with a splash of water and the salt. Cook, mashing about a third of them with the back of a spoon, until thick and hot all the way through, about 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Stir the yogurt with the lime juice and cilantro. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, then fill them with the beans, avocado, a spoonful of the yogurt and a little crumbled queso fresco, and scatter the sunflower seeds over the top.
tip: Mash a few more of the beans if you like the filling thicker.

name: Korean-style beef lettuce and tortilla wraps
inspiredBy: Inspired by Korean ssam and bulgogi flavours
about: Gochujang-glazed lean beef with garlic and wilted spinach, folded into warm corn tortillas with butter lettuce leaves and a crunchy lime-pickled carrot and cucumber. The beef brings **iron and zinc** and the pickled vegetables bring crunch and brightness.
steps: Wash the carrot, cucumber, spinach, lettuce and ginger. Cut the carrot and cucumber into thin sticks and toss them with the lime juice and the pepper. Let them sit while you cook.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, garlic and ginger with a splash of water into a loose paste.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through to 71 °C (160 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Stir in the paste and the spinach and cook until the spinach wilts and the beef is glazed, about 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Lay a lettuce leaf on each, add the beef and top with the pickled vegetables. Fold and eat.

This makes two portions. Cool the second portion of beef within 1 hour in a shallow container, cover and refrigerate it with the pickles, lettuce and tortilla kept separate. Use it within 3 days and reheat the beef until steaming, to 74 °C (165 °F).
tip: Gochujang brands vary in heat and salt, so taste the paste first. Use less for a milder wrap.

washed and cut in thin sticks

name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
about: A banana with a handful of walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. The banana brings **potassium** and the walnuts bring plant omega-3.
